context.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

latestRelease.title: v0.5.17
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*582 PRs from 194 contributors.*

**Kimi K3 day-0 support**: A 2.8T-parameter multimodal LatentMoE (896 experts, top-16, routed in a 3584-dim latent space) with a 1M-token context, 69 KDA linear-attention layers interleaved with 24 MLA layers, and a MoonViT3d vision tower, shipping as a native MXFP4 checkpoint. SGLang serves it from day 0 with DCP, DSpark speculative decoding, chunked-prefill PP with TP decode, KDA-aware prefix caching, HiCache L2 over DCP, LoRA on the quantized weights, and reasoning, tool-call and OpenAI-compatible serving, verified on NVIDIA GB300 and AMD MI35x ([#32541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32541), [#32828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32828), [#32890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32890), [#33025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33025), [#33112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33112), [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607)).

**MiniMax-H3 day-0 support**: MiniMax's video generation model that produces a video and a synchronized stereo audio track in one request, served natively on SGLang-Diffusion across all three public task profiles: text-to-video-and-audio (`t2va`), first/last-frame conditioning (`fl2va`), and image/video/audio reference conditioning (`ref2va`, which also covers video-to-video). Verified on B200 (TP2 + Ulysses4), H100 (TP2 + Ulysses2), AMD MI300X and MI355X (Ulysses1/2/4/8), and 2x RTX 5090 with layerwise offload ([#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3)).

**Other new models added**: [EmbeddingGemma](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma) and [LFM2.5](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM2.5) embedding models, nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, plus cookbook recipes for Poolside's [Laguna-S-2.1](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) family and [Inkling-Small](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-Small).

**Initial support for the Rust frontend**: Migrates the front half of the server, everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler, from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation ([#29799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799)).

**DCP communication backends and q-replicate (Helix)**: The DeepSeek-MLA decode context-parallel path gains pluggable comm backends. `a2a` exchanges packed attention output plus fp32 LSE in a single NCCL collective per layer, with fp8 KV carried as uint8 byte transport; `fi_a2a` delegates the cross-rank exchange to the FlashInfer MNNVL kernel on GB200. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` projects full-head Q locally and skips the per-layer Q head-dim all-gather. Select with `--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}` ([#21637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21637)).

**DWDP for MoE prefill**: A new prefill parallelism strategy that prefetches peer expert weights over NVLink P2P and computes all experts locally, removing EP all-to-all token dispatch. On 4x B200 with gpt-oss-120b, prefill-only, DWDP4 reaches **1.92x over DEP4** at MNT 32K / ISL 32K, and **506K vs 329K tok/s (1.54x)** at saturation (CONC=128, ISL=8K). Enable with `--dwdp-size`; the authors mark it early-development ([#29778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778)).

**Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache**: For agentic and RL-rollout workloads, requests can carry a stable `session_id` so eviction knows which prefixes an active session still references, instead of evicting purely by cache policy. Release the references with `/close_session`. Opt in with `--enable-session-radix-cache` ([#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)).

**SM90 FP8 MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4**: Adds the DeepGEMM MegaMoE A2A path on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro FP8, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel and FP8 expert weight preparation. Guarded behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` ([#29016](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29016)).

**Faster large-MoE model loading**: Oversized or non-contiguous CPU weight views were driving pathological H2D transfers, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 spending 27 to 32 minutes in H2D on some ranks. Copying those views into contiguous storage before H2D cuts full model loading from about **35 minutes to 6m20s (5.6x)**, and GPT-OSS-20B BF16 from **545s to 70s (7.8x)**, with Qwen3.5-397B measured at 1.93x to 2.3x. Opt in with `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D`, off by default ([#32315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32315)).

**Lower DeepSeek-V4 memory on AMD**: Removing unnecessary expert padding drops MI355X FP4 MoE model weights from **159.07 GB to 112.36 GB**, and bringing the HIP compress-state pool into the memory_saver KV_CACHE region lets colocated RL reclaim it, cutting the measured training-phase footprint from about **143 GiB to 87 GiB per GPU** ([#31450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31450), [#31747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31747)).

**Faster engine recovery**: Large-model restarts cost 3 to 6+ minutes today, about 6.5 minutes for Qwen3-235B FP8 on 4 GPUs, because weights reload from storage and CUDA graphs recapture. A weight-cache daemon holds weights per GPU so a restarting engine can recover from cache instead ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)).

**Lower host overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode**: Under spec-v2 overlap scheduling each decode step runs draft, verify and extend CUDA graphs, and the eager seams between them become GPU idle time at low concurrency. This trims that host work so the host stays off the critical path ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219)).

**Dependencies**: flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 ([#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927)), sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1 ([#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345), [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)), helion 1.4 ([#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)), mooncake 0.3.12.post1 ([#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)), dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0 ([#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)). PyTorch stays at 2.11.0 and the CUDA base image at 13.0.1.

*Full release notes by category below; breaking changes and known issues are at the end.*

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **`helion` jumps 0.2.6 to 1.4**, a major-version move for anyone depending on helion-backed kernels: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* **`sglang.jit_kernel` is retired into `sglang.kernels`**, completing RFC [#29630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630). Imports from the old module path must move: [#32072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32072), [#31666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31666), [#32015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32015), [#32045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32045)
* **Breakable prefill CUDA graph is now on by default for DP attention**: [#31682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31682)
* **CuteDSL BF16 GEMM on SM100 is on by default** when the heuristic allows it: [#30567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30567)
* **sgl-kernel AOT `bmm_fp8` is deleted in favor of `flashinfer.bmm_fp8`; the AOT router GEMM and fused A GEMM are also removed**: [#31202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31202), [#30280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30280)
* **The FP8 per-tensor GEMM backend on SM120 switches to cuBLAS**: [#31961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31961)
* **Unfetchable or unparseable multimodal inputs now return HTTP 400 instead of 500**, and text-only models reject media input outright: [#31417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31417), [#32914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32914)
* **Diffusion request-level quality is restricted to two validated tiers**, lossless (default) and high: [#33453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33453)
* **`ServerArgs` is being made read-only** behind namespace config bags. Code that mutated `ServerArgs` at runtime must route through the new accessors: [#31809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31809), [#31811](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31811), [#33334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33334), [#33338](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33338)

## Known Issues

* **The FlashInfer rmsnorm + quant fusion for SM90/SM100/SM120 was landed and reverted** this cycle ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994), [#33455](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33455)). It is not in this release.
* **Breakable CUDA graph is disabled for NemotronH** pending a fix: [#33130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33130)
* **`test_update_weights_from_disk` is skipped on ROCm** pending a reload fix ([#31924](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31924)): [#31925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31925)
* **The SM120 DeepGEMM release-pipeline test is temporarily skipped**: [#32193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32193)

signals.title: [Feature] NSA optimization roadmap
signals.text: ### Attention algorithm [Link to original table](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1u_AaRCEp2xWO3lxBkXJOgzFm4PG9P-88U6M-Dfa-svI/edit?usp=sharing) The parts highlighted in blue is work that has been done or in progress. To summarize: - Use MHA for short context lengths, as suggested in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/DeepSeek_V3_2.pdf - Below context lengths 2K, sparse attention is the same as non-sparse attention and we can skip the logits computation and directly generates the indices for sparse MLA kernel or use MHA when possible - The current flashmla_decode kernel is not well optimized on B200. So a separate dequant kernel + flashmla_sparse_bf16 works better for prefill + fp8 kvcache if the kv cache is not too long compared to the q sequence length. The heuristics will need to be updated after new optimizations to either the prefill or decode kernels, making it a bit hard to use in practice. Detailed analysis is [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1u_AaRCEp2xWO3lxBkXJOgzFm4PG9P-88U6M-Dfa-svI/edit?gid=1552909022#gid=1552909022) ### Kernel optimizations - FP8 per tensor sparse MLA kernel from trtllm - More optimizations to flashmla_decode on B200 - Adaptive MHA attention pathway #11892 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/12788 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/12964 - Layernorm optimization #12044 - quantize_k_cache_fast (curr: 3 kernel, 6us). No need to cat, but pass in two separate tensors. - Optimize `torch.cat([q_nope, q_rope])` by either writing a fast triton/cuda kernel or using torch.compile. It's used for prefill/decode but the prefill one is much bigger and has more room for optimizations. The trtllm kernel supports separate `q_nope` and `q_rope`, but flashmla doesn't. #12215 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13022 - DeepGeMM fp8_mqa_logits optimizations https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13402 ### Indexer optimizations - [Decode] Optimize dual stream in Indexer https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13546 - [Decode] Move deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata to init time, similar to attention kernel metadata compute - [Prefill] Optimize _get_topk_ragged where there are a lot of small kernels. Try multi-stream, torch.compile, and add new kernels when necessary. - [MTP] Enable nextn = 2/4 in deep_gemm.fp8_paged_mqa_logits, which is faster than the current implementation which uses the kernel with nextn = 1 regardless of mtp size. ### Min latency optimizations - Enable TP in Attention

signals.text: # AITER Upgrade Readiness Tracker > AITER Scout Status Tracking https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26890 ## What this issue tracks Per AITER version that's in (or has been in) SGLang main, we track two things: - New Feature: AITER PRs that SGLang features depend on, and whether both the AITER-side and SGLang-side PRs have landed. - Issue: known bugs/regressions in that AITER version, and what's left before it's considered safe. ## How to read this tracker **This tracker is organized by AITER version / commit.** - **New Feature** tracks forward-looking AITER PRs or commits needed by upcoming SGLang features. - **Issue** tracks problems found in the current AITER version and the remaining action needed before the version can be considered safe. **Column meaning:** - **AITER PR/commit**: the upstream AITER PR, issue, or commit related to the item. - **Feature**: the SGLang-facing feature enabled by the AITER change. - **Area / Issue**: the bug, regression, or compatibility issue observed. - **AITER Status**: upstream AITER state, such as merged, not merged, fixed, or unresolved. - **SGLang Status**: downstream SGLang state for new-feature items, such as merged, not merged, validation needed, or workaround status. - **Next Action**: the remaining downstream action for issue items. signals.title: [Roadmap]: SGLang Distributed KVCache System For Agentic Workload
signals.text: ### Motivation As agentic workloads drive rapid growth in KV cache storage and transfer volumes, the existing PD disaggregation + HiCache stack is hitting significant bottlenecks. Meanwhile, HiCache's compatibility with hybrid models and other evolving features remains limited. There is an urgent need for a robust, high-performance distributed KV cache system capable of sustaining the heavy demands of large-scale agentic scenarios. The core objective is to achieve end-to-end integration of PD incremental transfer, HiCache / HiSparse, pipeline parallelism, and Eagle — validated at scale on DeepSeek DSA (V32、GLM5) and Linear model (Qwen35) families. ### Q3 Roadmap - [ ] **Agentic KV Cache Scheduling** - [ ] Support session-aware RadixTree and HiCache ([PR #29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)) - [ ] Build a KV cache orchestrator across the router and engine to detect agentic workflows—including sessions, sub-agents, and tool calls—and provide scheduling hints such as `PREFETCH`, `DEMOTE`, and `PIN`; integrate with the router roadmap for global KV cache scheduling ([Issue #25760](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760)) - [ ] Support direct L3 cache mode to enable a larger globally shared memory pool - [ ] Build a CPU-only KV cache simulator that replays representative agentic workloads without GPUs ([Issue #21891](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21891)) - [ ] Support KVCache Sequence Split Mode to distribute VRAM pressure evenly. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30501 - [ ] Support Unified-KVCache Layout https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651 - [ ] **UnifiedRadixTree Enhancements** - [ ] Decouple the tree core and implement it in Rust to accelerate hot paths such as matching and eviction ([PR #29901](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29901)) 、https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32710 - [ ] Improve Mamba offloading for production HiCache deployments of Qwen and Kimi models - [ ] Integrate with KVCache-Canary to enable debugging capabilities for KV cache correctness. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32476 - [ ] **PD Disaggregation Integration** - [ ] Support an L2 `DecodeRadixTree` to increase transfer batch sizes and reduce GPU memory usage - [ ] Explore a proof of concept for Prefill-as-a-Service - [ ] **HiSparse Production Readiness** - [ ] Improve the reliability and production readiness of HiSparse ([Issue #28874](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28874)) ### Q2 Roadmap The roadmap below is still incomplete and will be expanded with more content related to Agent/SubAgent KVCache. - [x] **HiCache: Support Hybrid Model** (Linear & DSA) @hzh0425 - [x] Hybrid Cache Controller & Support Linear Hybrid Model https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20457 - [x] Mooncake backend support for hybrid model https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21259 @huangtingwei9988 - [ ] Support MLA + Mamba Hybrid model(KeLing) https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22957 - [x] 3FS Backend support for hybrid model https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23241 @kangyifei - [x] HiCache support for Unified Hybrid Radix Cache https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20415 - [x] Support DeepSeekV4 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24691 - [x] Support MiMO-V2 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27378 - [ ] Dedup MLA KV cache in host memory across TP ranks https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26691 - [ ] **PD-Decode Support HiCache** @hzh0425 @huangtingwei9988 - [x] Support Decode Side RadixTree @ishandhanani - [ ] Support Decode Side HybridRadixTree (SWA/Mamba) (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27770) - [x] Storage Prefetch Interface — Expose a prefetch API that allows newly arriving decode requests to query storage hits and initiate Storage→Host→Device prefetch directly - [ ] Support L2 RadixTree to increase cache hit rate - [ ] Storage supports the concept of groups, enabling unified visibility and eviction for groups composed of multiple keys within a page (e.g., key and value, split by rank, etc.). @huangtingwei9988 - [ ] Heterogeneous TP Support For PD With HiCache @huangtingwei9988 - [ ] **PD Disaggregation**：Idea provided by @ShangmingCai @hzh0425 - [x] **Incremental KV Transfer** — Decode queries storage for cached prefix tokens and reports the hit count to Prefill via protocol extension; Prefill only transfers the non-cached (incremental) portion - [x] **PD Host TransferMode** — Prefill transfers the KV cache directly to Decode's DRAM, bypassing the GPU as an intermediary；Helps increase the decode-side batch size in long-context scenarios. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21591 - [ ] **Support for large decode batches:** During decoding, use the L2 and L3 prefix portions cached on the host (hit from prior computations) along with the incremental part transferred from the prefill phase; then load everything back onto the GPU to perform subsequent inference steps. - [ ] **Agent/Rollout KVCache Management** @hzh0425 @stmatengss @ishandhanani - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24656 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574 - [ ] **HiCache Compatibility with Other Features** - [ ] PP × HiCache Consistency Fix — Resolve compatibility issues between PP and HiCache by synchronizing Rank 0's cache events across PP ranks via event numbering, ensuring RadixTree state consistency @hzh0425 @whybeyoung https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22607 - [x] MTP × HiCache https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21125 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30393 - [x] EP & DP × HiCache - [x] CP × HiCache https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20460 - [x] Support CP Layer-Wise Split With HiCache: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29421 ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: [Feature] W4A8 MoE kernel for NVFP4 models on non-Blackwell GPUs (SM90)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ### Background NVFP4 quantized models like **GLM-5 (744B)** and **DeepSeek V3.2 (671B)** are becoming increasingly popular. On Blackwell GPUs with native FP4 hardware support, these models run great. However, on non-Blackwell GPUs like H20 (SM90), SGLang falls back to the **Marlin W4A16 path** — dequantizing FP4 weights to BF16 and using BF16 tensor cores. We've been running GLM-5-NVFP4 on 8×H20 (141GB HBM3, SM90) and did extensive benchmarking and kernel-level profiling. The results suggest there's a significant opportunity to improve decode performance on these GPUs. ### Current Performance: NVFP4 (W4A16) vs FP8 on 8×H20 **Decode (DP Attention, MTP enabled):** | Concurrency | NVFP4 (Marlin W4A16) | FP8 | Gap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 58.6 tok/s | 63.6 tok/s | FP8 9% faster | | 64 | 963 tok/s | 1,228 tok/s | FP8 28% faster | **Prefill:** | | NVFP4 | FP8 | Gap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Peak (32 conc) | 5,300 tok/s | 10,500 tok/s | FP8 ~2× faster | We initially expected NVFP4 decode to be faster than FP8 since FP4 weights are half the size (decode is conventionally considered bandwidth-bound). However, **FP8 is faster across the board**. ### Root Cause: Marlin Kernel Efficiency Our profiling shows the Marlin W4A16 kernel has very low memory bandwidth utilization on MoE workloads: - **Theoretical** (bandwidth-limited): NVFP4 should read ~100MB per layer (8 activated experts), taking ~28μs at 4TB/s. FP8 reads ~200MB, taking ~52μs. NVFP4 should be ~1.8× faster. - **Actual**: Marlin takes ~117μs/layer (24% bandwidth utilization), FP8 Triton takes ~72μs/layer (72% utilization). FP8 ends up **1.6× faster**. Meanwhile, FP8 Triton's fused_moe_kernel achieves much higher efficiency with a simpler pipeline (direct FP8 loads, post-MMA scaling, FP8 tensor cores). ### Why This Matters NVFP4 has a key advantage over FP8 for serving: **much smaller weight footprint → more KV cache space**. On our 8×H20 setup with DP Attention, NVFP4 weights leave ~37GB/GPU for KV cache vs ~17GB/GPU for FP8, enabling significantly more concurrent requests. A W4A8 kernel would let non-Blackwell deployments benefit from both the memory advantage and competitive compute performance. Models that would benefit: any NVFP4 quantized MoE model on SM90 GPUs (H20, H100, H200, etc.), including GLM-5 and DeepSeek V3.2. ### Environment - GPUs: 8× NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 141GB HBM3) - Model: GLM-5-NVFP4 (744B MoE, 256 experts, top-8) - SGLang with DP Attention (tp=8, dp=8) - MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding enabled ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: [RFC] Sglang non-GPU process rust migration
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. **PR** - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799 Refer Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949 Release Roadmap https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0 ### Motivation **Status**: Draft **Author**: @rainj-me **Created**: Apr 20 2026 **Version**: 0.1 # Rust Server Migration Plan **Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation. --- ## 1. Goals & scope **Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle up to scheduler submission. **In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.), large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch. **Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals, quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them. **Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python. --- ## 2. Architecture summary The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context): - **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded, thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer / scheduler boundary — no shared locks. - **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound); (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries. - **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized. - **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msgpack metadata), never tensor bytes; lifetime is the pool's slot-reuse policy — a slot returns to the free list only after both Python's read and any GPU DMA complete, not Rust's `Drop`. - **Cross-rank:** For DP attention, the first rank of each DP group runs the Rust server *without* the api-server; a single api-server then fans **control** messages to every DP group (duplicated, since control must reach all), while **generation** requests are **round-robined** across DP groups for load balancing. - **Streaming:** a single `Streaming` macro state self-loops per chunk; non-streaming is just a stream whose frames are accumulated and emitted in `Finalizing`. See the request-FSM and topology diagrams in the Appendix for detail. --- ## 3. Phase 1 — Rust server (tok/detok manager + HTTP server) **Target: 2026-07-17** Phase 1 delivers the Rust front-half running in front of the **existing Python scheduler + GPU worker**, inside one process via multi-threaded Rust ⇄ Python. ### 3.1 Work breakdown | | Item | Status | Depends on | Notes | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | 1 | Rust frontend \+ scheduler PoC | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#23360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23360) \[Closed\] | | 2 | Architecture design | ✅ Done | — | Pending final approval | | 3 | Pickle → msgpack migration | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#28688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28688) \[Merged\] Followup issue [\#29465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29465) | | 4 | Single-process framework: multi-threaded Rust \+ Python scheduler/GPU worker | ✅ Done | 3 | | | 5 | Tokenizer & detokenizer manager | ✅ Done | 4 | | | 6 | HTTP server: /generate \+ streaming | ✅ Done | 4, 5 | | | 7 | Encoder support | 🟡 WIP | 4, 5 | Work with dynamo team check whether this can export to dynamo crate. | | 8 | PD disaggregation | ✅Done | 4 | Large. Prefill/decode split — see risk note. | | 9 | DP attention \+ cross-node DP controller | ✅ Done | 4 | Large, cross-node. See risk note. | | 10 | Metrics / logging | 🟡 WIP | 4 | Logging Done, Metrics WIP | | 11 | Port existing HTTP APIs other than the listed APIs below | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Full endpoint parity for drop-in replacement. | | 12 | Unified multi-protocol lib (server \+ gateway) | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Shared http(s)/h2/h3/gRPC/WS layer reused by sglang-gateway. | | 13 | Code Refactor | 🟡 WIP | | | | 14 | AuthZ support | | | | | 15 | Parallel Sampling | | | | | 16 | Benchmark\_serving perf optimization | 🟡 WIP | | | | 17 | Embedding request | | | | | 18 | offline Engine API support | | | | | 19 | Other flags in the TokenizedGenerateReqInput | | | | | 20 | cache\_tokens | | | | | 21 | custom\_logit\_processor | | | | | 22 | preferred\_sampling\_params | | | | | 23 | Standalone API-Server for DP Attn | 🟡 WIP | | | | 24 | Anthorpic API support | | | | | 25 | SageMaker API support | | | | | 26 | Vertex AI API support | | | | | 27 | Ollama compatible API support | | | | | 28 | Weight update APIs | | | | | 29 | HiCache APIs | | | | ### 3.2 Sequencing & critical path Items are **not** independent. The dependency spine is: ``` #3 pickle→msgpack ──► #4 single-process framework ──► #5 tok/detok ──► #6 /generate+stream ──► #11 API parity └─► #10 metrics (parallel) └─► #7 encoder (parallel, after #5) ``` **Critical path to a usable July 17 milestone:** 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with 10 landing in parallel and 11 close behind. That subset is what makes the Rust server a working, A/B-testable drop-in for text LLM traffic. **Recommend deferring out of the July 17 milestone** (track as Phase 1.5 / stretch): items **8 (PD disaggregation)** and **9 (DP attention + cross-node DP controller)**. Both are large, both can land after the core path is proven, and bundling them into the July date puts the whole milestone at risk. Item **12 (unified protocol lib)** is valuable but is a refactor that can follow once #6 stabilizes the protocol surface. > **Date reality check.** July 17 is ~4 weeks out and #4 (the foundation) is still > pending-start. The 3→4→5→6+7 path is achievable in that window if #4 starts > immediately and 8/9/12 are explicitly descoped. Carrying all 12 to July 17 is not > realistic; pick the milestone definition deliberately. ### 3.3 Phase 1 exit criteria - Rust server handles `/generate` (streaming + non-streaming) at parity with Python. - Tok/detok managers run in-process; detok is incremental and order-correct. - Encoder path works for at least one multimodal input type. - Metrics + logs at parity; runs behind a flag, A/B-able against Python. - Endpoint parity sufficient to route production text traffic. --- ## 4. Cross-cutting concerns **Rollout / fallback.** Every phase ships behind a flag with the Python path as the live fallback. Migrate by traffic slice (shadow → small % → ramp), not big-bang. keep the Python path runnable as the live fallback until the Rust path reaches parity. **Testing.** Differential testing against Python (same inputs → same tokens/frames) is the primary correctness gate. Add: FSM property tests (every state has a terminal exit; post-terminal events are no-ops/idempotent); streaming order + UTF-8-boundary tests for detok. **Observability.** Metrics/logging (P1 #10) should land *with* the core path, not after — debugging the channel/FSM/threading layers without it is painful. Per-state request counts, queue depths (ring-buffer occupancy = backpressure signal), per-core load, and control-op latencies. **Kernel / environment.** io_uring features used (`MSG_RING` 5.18+, `SEND_ZC` 6.0+, `DEFER_TASKRUN` 6.1+) set a minimum kernel; some hardened/container environments disable io_uring — keep an epoll+eventfd fallback behind the same loop abstraction. --- ## 5. Top risks | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | July 17 scope (all 12 items) | Milestone slips / quality suffers | Descope 8/9/12; define milestone as 3→4→5→6+10. | | #4 framework is the foundation and hasn't started | Blocks 5–7; whole phase waits | Start immediately; treat as the single highest-priority item. | | Rust↔Python boundary in the single-process step | Perf cliffs, GIL contention | Keep the boundary narrow (handles, not data); measure early. | | Detok ordering / UTF-8 under streaming | Corrupt user-visible output | Shard by `hash(req_id)`; stateful decode offsets; boundary tests. | | Slow-client backpressure on egress | GPU stalls / memory growth | Bounded egress buffers; treat persistent slow consumer as disconnect. | --- ## 6. Milestones | Date | Milestone | | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ~Now | #1 PR #23360, #3 merged (PR #28688); #4 started. | | 2026-07-17 | **Phase 1 core:** Rust server with `/generate` + streaming + encoder + metrics, A/B-able vs Python (items 3–7, 10, 11). | | Phase 1.5 | PD disaggregation (#8), DP attention + cross-node controller (#9), unified protocol lib (#12). | ## 7. Appendix 1. [Initial plan](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0) 2. [Architecture Design](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1_DJ_Fjq_tgMTmzWcmm5uacCi9RJGW_lwZGeXiecc6XY/edit?slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0#slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0)

signals.title: [RFC] Agent-Aware KV Cache Phase 1 for Agentic Workloads
signals.text: ## Summary This RFC proposes Phase 1 of agent-aware KV cache support in SGLang. The goal of this phase is to add a minimal, backward-compatible metadata path for agentic workloads so workflow information can flow from the API layer into runtime requests and KV cache nodes, and optionally affect radix cache eviction. This is intentionally a foundation/prototype phase, not a full workflow-aware cache system. ## Motivation Current KV cache eviction policies such as LRU, LFU, and SLRU treat requests mostly independently. That works well for standard chat/completion workloads, but it misses reuse opportunities in agentic workflows, where requests often share: - repeated prompt prefixes across planner/tool/worker steps - parent/child step relationships - short-term reuse after tool calls - workflow-level TTL or reuse intent Without workflow-aware signals, cache entries that are likely to be reused by upcoming steps may be evicted too early. ## Proposal Phase 1 introduces: - an optional `agent_hints` field in OpenAI-compatible requests - propagation of `agent_hints` through the internal request pipeline - lightweight workflow DAG tracking in the scheduler - radix cache node annotation with workflow metadata - a new optional radix eviction policy: `agent_aware` Initial `agent_hints` fields include: - `workflow_id` - `agent_id` - `step_id` - `step_index` - `total_steps` - `parent_step_id` - `children_step_ids` - `tool_name` - `expected_tool_duration_ms` - `cache_ttl_ms` - `shared_prefix_hash` - `reuse_hint` ## Scope Phase 1 is intended to cover: - request schema support - metadata plumbing - scheduler-side workflow tracking - cache node metadata annotation - a prototype workflow-aware eviction strategy Phase 1 does **not** attempt to fully solve: - `shared_prefix_hash`-driven reuse - HiCache / storage-layer metadata inheritance - cross-process workflow coordination - production-tuned scoring for all agent topologies ## Backward Compatibility - `agent_hints` is optional - existing clients do not need to change - existing eviction policies continue to work unchanged - the new behavior is opt-in ## Testing Expected validation for Phase 1: - schema tests for `agent_hints` - propagation tests from API request to internal request objects - workflow DAG tests for step registration and distance computation - radix cache node annotation tests - eviction ordering tests for `agent_aware` - backward-compat tests when `agent_hints` is omitted How to Run Start SGLang with the new eviction policy: ``` curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "default", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}], "agent_hints": { "workflow_id": "wf-1", "agent_id": "planner", "step_id": "step-1", "children_step_ids": ["step-2"], "cache_ttl_ms": 60000, "reuse_hint": "keep" } }' ``` Prototype validation already exists with dedicated unit tests for the metadata path. ## Open Questions - Should `shared_prefix_hash` remain a hint, or become a stronger reuse primitive in a later phase? - Should TTL be a hard protection or only a ranking signal? - How should workflow-aware metadata eventually interact with HiCache and storage backends? - What observability should be added next: workflow hit rate, protected eviction count, step-distance metrics? ## Requested Feedback Feedback is especially useful on: - the proposed `agent_hints` schema - whether scheduler-local DAG tracking is the right Phase 1 boundary - whether `agent_aware` should land as an experimental eviction policy first - what should be included in Phase 2 CC: @hzh0425 @xiezhq-hermann @huangtingwei9988 @ishandhanani REF: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21846

signals.title: [RFC][Refactor] `mem_cache` pool / allocator restructure
signals.text: ## 1. TL;DR Reorganize `mem_cache/` from "a few catch-all files plus cross-feature pollution" into per-family one-file modules: - `allocator.py` → `allocator/` package (5 files + `__init__.py`) - `memory_pool.py` + 5 sibling files → `pool/` package (10 files, one per family) - `memory_pool_host.py` → `pool_host/` package (9 files, mirrors `pool/`) - Untangle DSv4 ↔ HiSparse class misplacement - Naming rule: **remove role affixes that don't differentiate** — keep `_backend` / `_controller` style only when same-directory files have different roles; drop them when all files share the role the directory already names - Add `mem_cache/README.md` (type × scope) index ### Rules: 1. All PRs must indicate whether they are a Mechanical Move. 2. Mechanical Moves must satisfy the mechanical-refactor-verify skill. 3. Preserve git blame as much as possible, with git blame -C -C as a fallback. 4. All PRs must go through detailed discussion and require adequate test coverage. ### Roadmap - [x] `mem_cache/allocator/` - [x] [Mechanical Move] split allocator.py into allocator/ subpackage https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26675 - [x] [Mechanical Move] SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26676 - [x] [Mechanical Move] hisparse https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26678 - [x] [Modify] mamba https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27256 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] MultiEndedAllocator - [ ] `mem_cache/pool_host/` - [x] [Mechanical Move] base pool_host/ subpackage(__init__+base.py+hisparse.py+common.py) https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27273 - [x] [Mechanical Move] MHATokenToKVPoolHost https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30249 - [x] [Mechanical Move] MLATokenToKVPoolHost https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30616 - [x] [Mechanical Move] MambaPoolHost https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31180 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] DSAIndexerPoolHost - [ ] [Mechanical Move] DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool+DeepSeekV4StateHostPool+LogicalHostPool - [ ] [Mechanical Move] HostPoolGroup - [ ] `mem_cache/pool/` - [ ] HybridLinearKVPool - [ ] `mem_cache/hybrid_cache+mem_cache/unified_cache_components` --- ## 2. Motivation `mem_cache/` has four structural problems (per issue #24335 work items): 1. **Blurred type boundaries** — `memory_pool.py` is 2000 lines / 11 classes mixing req-to-slot indexing, KV abc, KV implementations, and SSM state. 2. **Feature-scope leakage** — `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` defines `HiSparseC4DevicePool`; `hisparse_memory_pool.py` defines three DSv4 classes including a host-side one. 3. **Same abstraction scattered** — allocator classes live in `allocator.py` / `swa_memory_pool.py` / `hisparse_memory_pool.py`. 4. **Inconsistent naming** — `hybrid_cache/{hybrid_cache_controller, hybrid_pool_assembler}.py` literally repeats the parent directory name; `unified_cache_components/{full,mamba,swa}_component.py` repeats the role that the plural directory name already states (compare `models/qwen.py` not `qwen_model.py`). --- ## 3. Overall directory structure ### 3.1 Before ``` mem_cache/ ├── allocator.py (3 classes; SWA/HiSparse allocators live elsewhere) ├── memory_pool.py (2000 lines / 11 classes — catch-all) ├── memory_pool_host.py (1900 lines / 8 classes — host-side catch-all) ├── deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py ❌ contains HiSparseC4DevicePool ├── deepseek_v4_compress_state.py (DSv4 sub-module sitting next to its parent file) ├── swa_memory_pool.py ❌ contains SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator ├── base_swa_memory_pool.py (cross-family base, but lives under SWA's own file) ├── hisparse_memory_pool.py ❌ contains DeepSeekV4SingleKVPoolHost │ ❌ contains HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ❌ contains DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator ├── hybrid_cache/ │ ├── hybrid_cache_controller.py ❌ redundant prefix │ └── hybrid_pool_assembler.py ❌ redundant prefix ├── unified_cache_components/ │ ├── full_component.py ❌ `_component` redundant — dir name already says "components" │ ├── mamba_component.py ❌ same │ ├── swa_component.py ❌ same │ └── tree_component.py ❌ misnamed (actually abc + enums, not "a tree component") └── ... (tree-layer etc., out of scope) ``` ### 3.2 After ``` mem_cache/ ├── README.md # (type × scope) index │ ├── allocator/ # allocation strategy layer │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator (abc only) │ ├── token.py # TokenToKVPoolAllocator (page_size=1) │ ├── paged.py # PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── mamba.py # MambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── swa.py # SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ └── hisparse.py # HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ # DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── pool/ # device physical storage │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # KVCache + BaseSWAKVPool (cross-family abc) │ ├── req_to_token.py # ReqToTokenPool + HybridReqToTokenPool │ ├── mha.py # MHA + NoOp + FP4 │ ├── mla.py # MLA + FP4 │ ├── nsa.py # NSATokenToKVPool │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPool │ ├── hybrid.py # HybridKVPool(to replace HybridLinearKVPool) │ ├── swa.py # SWAKVPool │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseC4DevicePool + HiSparseNSATokenToKVPool │ └── deepseek_v4/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── composite.py # DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool │ ├── single.py # DeepSeekV4SingleKVPool │ ├── indexer.py # DeepSeekV4IndexerPool │ └── compress_state.py # KVAndScore + CompressStatePool │ ├── pool_host/ # host-side mirrors for supported device pools │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # HostKVCache (abc) + synchronized decorator │ ├── common.py # HostTensorAllocator + alloc_with_host_register │ # + alloc_with_pin_memory + get_allocator_from_storage │ ├── mha.py # MHATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── nsa.py # NSAIndexerPoolHost │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPoolHost │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseHostPoolMixin │ ├── group.py # PoolEntry + HostPoolGroup │ └── deepseek_v4.py # DeepSeekV4SingleKVPoolHost │ ├── hybrid_cache/ # multi-pool orchestrator (no __init__.py) │ ├── controller.py # HybridCacheController │ └── pool_assembler.py # HybridPoolAssembler │ ├── unified_cache_components/ # tree-layer subpackage (#20415 territory) │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # TreeComponent (abc) + shared enums (was tree_component.py) │ ├── full.py # FullComponent (was full_component.py) │ ├── mamba.py # MambaComponent (was mamba_component.py) │ └── swa.py # SWAComponent (was swa_component.py) │ └── ... (tree-layer etc., unchanged) ``` --- ## 5. Design rationale ### 5.1 Layer responsibilities and orthogonal axes ``` upper layers (scheduler / model_runner / attention backend) │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────┐ │ hybrid_cache/ │ multi-pool router └────────────────────────────┘ │ uses ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocator/ │ indexing: "give me N slots" └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ owns reference to ↓ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ pool/ (device storage) │ ── hicache ───► │ pool_host/ (CPU mirror)│ │ KV / SSM state physical holder │ offload/reload │ host mirror of pool/ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────┘ ``` | Module | Cares about | In → Out | |---|---|---| | `allocator/` | which slots are free | `need_size` → `indices` | | `pool/` | physical KV / SSM state layout | `(layer_id, indices) ↔ tensor` | | `pool_host/` | host mirror + H2D/D2H | `device_indices ↔ host_indices` | | `hybrid_cache/` | per-layer routing across pools | `layer_id → pool` | ### 5.2 Hicache tiers (L1/L2/L3) — flat, not nested ``` orchestrator (HiCacheController, currently in managers/) │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ pool/ pool_host/ storage/ (L1 GPU) (L2 host) (L3 disk/remote) ```

signals.title: [RFC] Disaggregated request preprocessing
signals.text:
### Motivation Before a model runs, the serving system often needs to know what the request will look like to the model: - A router places and sizes work before a request reaches a GPU: how long the request is, whether its prefix is already cached, and whether its media is already processed. - A disaggregated pipeline prepares a request once and hands the model the tokens, instead of re-tokenizing at each hop. For both cases, the prepared request has to match what the model actually runs. When it does not, cache lookups can miss and token counts can be wrong (#26555, #27386, [llm-d-router#1072](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1072)). This proposal exposes that request view before execution, so routing and model servers do not rely on approximations. ### Proposal

The goal is to expose the same preprocessing path used by SGLang inference as a lightweight standalone service that returns the prepared generate request without running the model. In particular, this should: - Run as a CPU-light preprocessing-only server. - Share the exact preprocessing logic used by normal SGLang inference endpoints. - Return a generate request, not just raw token IDs, with the metadata needed for tokens-in/tokens-out. - Include multimodal hashes and related metadata in the tokenize/preprocess output, so encoder-disaggregated setups can route and reuse MM encoder work consistently. **Before and after:** Today, chat and completions requests can be tokenized through one dedicated `/tokenize` endpoint: ``` chat / completions | v /tokenize | v token ids + count - no mm features (no hashes, no positions) - no /responses or /messages support ``` Proposed, the same request becomes the full input the model runs: ``` request (chat / completion / messages / ...) | v preprocessing (same logic used by serving entry points) - chat template, tools, reasoning - tokenization - media identity and token positions | v generate request - token ids - request metadata - multimodal fields needed by the generate path | v model (token ids in -> token ids out) ``` The model accepts this generate request directly, so preprocessing and execution can run in one process or on separate machines. The rest of the request, such as the sampling settings and any cache key, rides along unchanged for the model to run. ### Usage The standalone mode could be exposed either as: ```bash sglang serve renderer ``` or as a dedicated command: ```bash sglang renderer ``` For HTTP APIs, the clearest option is to expose preprocess-specific endpoints that mirror the serving APIs, for example: ``` /v1/chat/completions/render /v1/completions/render /v1/responses/render /v1/messages/render ``` These endpoints would accept the same request format as the corresponding serving endpoint, but return the prepared generate request instead of running the model. ### Phasing 1. **Shared preprocessing path.** Factor preprocessing into one shared path used by the existing serving entry points. This should not change behavior, and is useful on its own. 2. **Standalone preprocessing service.** Expose the same path as an opt-in service that can run without starting the full serving engine or loading the model (following #27606 in spirit). ### QA **Why not just use the current `/tokenize` endpoint?** `/tokenize` is useful, but it only returns token ids and a count. That is enough for simple text cases, but not for precise routing or token-in/token-out execution. For multimodal requests, we also need media identity and positions in the token sequence. `/tokenize` is also not a lightweight standalone service today: it still requires starting the serving engine, loading the model, and it does not cover all request APIs such as `/responses` or `/messages`. **What is a generate request?** A generate request is the prepared input the model runs on: the token ids, the multimodal inputs if any, and the execution settings that should stay attached to the request. It is not part of the standard OpenAI-compatible API. Each backend defines its own version, so vLLM and SGLang may represent it differently. **How is multimodal handled?** For multimodal requests, preprocessing exposes the information needed before execution: the tokenized request, the media identity, and where each media item appears in the token sequence. Whether heavier processed media data is produced in the standalone service or later in the SGLang server is left as an implementation choice. The important part for this RFC is that routing and model execution use the same media view as full inference. **Why does SGLang need this, instead of one shared preprocessing server for all backends?** The output has to match SGLang's internal model input. Tokenization, chat templates, special tokens, multimodal placeholder handling, and the internal generate-request format can vary by backend and model, so a generic preprocessor would only approximate the result. A shared layer can still normalize user requests before they reach SGLang, but it cannot replace the SGLang-specific preprocessing that produces the model input. **Is this only useful for routing?** No. Similar needs have come up for custom frontends and reinforcement learning. SGLang has related requests for server-mode token IDs and token-ids input (#5653, #12145). ### References This RFC is influenced by parallel vllm work on separating preprocessing from model execution and making the prepared request shape explicit: - [vLLM #35213](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35213): discussion around standalone / disaggregated preprocessing. - [vLLM #36102](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36102): adds the command-line entry point for standalone preprocessing. - [vLLM #36166](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36166): implementation work for standalone preprocessing. - [vLLM #35684](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35684): returns the prepared generate request and includes multimodal information. Related SGLang issues: - SGLang #5653, #12145: token IDs / token-in needs for server-mode and RL workflows. - SGLang #27606: early standalone-preprocessing entry point. - SGLang #27386: applying the chat template before cache-aware hashing. - SGLang #26555: retokenization drift for pre-tokenized multimodal requests. ### cc @Jiminator @JustinTong0323 @vMaroon @ahg-g @nilig @rahulgurnani

signals.title: [Perf] Incomplete TF32 n_splits warmup causes runtime JIT stalls on MHC models
signals.text: # Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. # Motivation ## Problem When serving MHC models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3/V4) with speculative decoding, some `TF32_HC_PRENORM_GEMM` kernels are lazily JIT-compiled during inference, causing 13-16s stalls per uncovered `n_splits` value. **Root cause:** `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre(num_tokens, hc_hidden_size)` computes `n_splits` deterministically: ```python n_splits = max(1, min(n_sms // ceil(num_tokens / 64), num_block_k // 4)) ``` The set of reachable `n_splits` values is finite and depends only on `n_sms` (GPU SM count) and `hc_hidden_size` (model config). For example, on H200 (132 SMs) + DeepSeek-V4 (hc_hidden_size=28672), there are exactly 22 possible values. However, CUDA graph capture only exercises batch sizes 1–256, which only covers `n_splits` values corresponding to `num_tokens <= ~1024`. The remaining values (requiring larger `num_tokens` from chunked prefill or high-concurrency decode batching) are left to lazy compilation at runtime. The existing `pp_parallel_deep_gemm_warmup` doesn't help because: 1. It's gated on `pp_size > 1 and not speculative` — inapplicable to single-node speculative setups 2. Its fixed dummy batch sizes only cover a small subset of `n_splits` values ## Impact Each missing `n_splits` compilation blocks ALL concurrent requests for 13-16s (NVCC compilation). The total cumulative stall can reach ~100s in the first minutes of serving, causing: - Severe TTFT spikes on early requests - Throughput degradation until all values are lazily compiled - Repeated impact on every container restart (since `_INITIALIZATION_DICT` is in-process memory) This affects any deployment combining: - MHC models (DeepSeek-V3, V4, or future models with `hc_hidden_size`) - Single-node (PP=1) with speculative decoding - Container restarts (common in production) ## Measured Results Environment: 8×H200, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, EAGLE 1step, TP=8, 8 concurrency, 50K-input / 1K-output multi-turn **Baseline — same container, warmup fully converged:** | Run | Requests | TTFT avg | TPOT avg | Throughput | Runtime JIT | |-----|----------|----------|----------|------------|-------------| | R1 | 605 | 3,661 ms | 25.1 ms | 19,529 tok/s | 0 | | R2 | 575 | 3,783 ms | 24.9 ms | 19,379 tok/s | 0 | **Fresh container restart (`.cubin` cache mounted, `_INITIALIZATION_DICT` lost):** | Run | Requests | TTFT avg | TPOT avg | Throughput | Runtime JIT | |-----|----------|----------|----------|------------|-------------| | R3 | 625 | 6,350 ms | 27.2 ms | 16,666 tok/s | 11 compilations | **With proposed fix (force-warmup all n_splits at startup, fresh container restart with .cubin cache mounted):** | Run | Requests | TTFT avg | TPOT avg | Throughput | Runtime JIT | |-----|----------|----------|----------|------------|-------------| | Patched | 568 | 4,650 ms | 25.3 ms | 18,235 tok/s | 0 | Improvement over unpatched restart: TTFT -26.8%, throughput +9.4%, runtime JIT eliminated. # Proposed Fix Add a generic `force_warmup_all_mhc_n_splits()` in `kernel_warmup()` that: 1. Reads `n_sms` from `torch.cuda.get_device_properties` (adapts to any GPU) 2. Reads `hc_hidden_size` and `hc_mult` from model config (adapts to any MHC model) 3. Enumerates all reachable `n_splits` via `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre` 4. Calls `_maybe_compile_deep_gemm_one_type_all` for each uncovered value Since `_maybe_compile` checks `_INITIALIZATION_DICT`, values already compiled during CUDA graph capture are skipped. Only genuinely missing values get compiled. **Startup cost:** proportional to the number of missing `n_splits` × `_BUILTIN_M_LIST` traversal. With `.cubin` cache: ~2-8s per value (load-only). Without cache: ~13-16s per value (NVCC compile). Zero runtime cost. I have a working patch validated on 8×H200 + DeepSeek-V4-Pro and will open a PR shortly. ## Environment (validation) - SGLang: v0.5.13 - GPU: 8× NVIDIA H200 (132 SMs) - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hc_mult=4, hidden_size=7168, hc_hidden_size=28672) - Config: TP=8, EAGLE 1step, mem_fraction_static=0.88, chunked_prefill=8192 ## Generality The fix is parametric — it derives everything from runtime GPU properties and model config: - Different GPUs (A100 108 SMs, H100 132 SMs, H200 132 SMs, B200 192 SMs) → different `n_splits` sets, all correctly enumerated - Different MHC models (different `hc_hidden_size`, `hc_mult`) → different `num_block_k` upper bound, correctly handled - Non-MHC models → function is a no-op (guard on `hc_hidden_size is not None`) --- Happy Dragon Boat Festival to all the maintainers and contributors! 🐲 Hope you're enjoying some zongzi today.

signals.title: [Feature] Enable LoRA on non-language (audio/vision) encoder towers and connectors
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang applies LoRA only to the **language** model today. A growing number of multimodal adapters also adapt the **audio/vision encoder tower** and the **connector/projector** (the same need that vLLM is addressing in vllm-project/vllm#31479). On SGLang these tower/connector LoRA weights are currently either **silently dropped** or **collide with language-model layers** — so an adapter that targets the encoder simply doesn't take effect (and in some shapes errors at load). This RFC documents the exact structural blockers (with file:line) and proposes a small, contained change to make LoRA bookkeeping *component-aware*, then offers **Qwen3-ASR as a clean reference implementation** because its tower is already built from native LoRA-wrappable linears. ## Current state — why tower/connector LoRA doesn't attach The LoRA *wrapping* infrastructure already supports every native linear class — `get_lora_layer`'s isinstance map (`python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:1184-1194`) handles `QKVParallelLinear` / `MergedColumnParallelLinear` / `ColumnParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` / `ReplicatedLinear`. So a tower built from native linears is most of the way there. What blocks it is the per-layer bookkeeping: **1. Tower layers collide with (and can overflow) language layers.** `LoRAManager.lora_modules` is a flat list sized by the **language** model's depth: ```python # python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:734-735 self.lora_modules: List[Dict[str, BaseLayerWithLoRA]] = [ {} for _ in range(self.base_hf_config.num_hidden_layers) ] ``` and modules are bucketed purely by `get_layer_id`, whose regex only captures `layers.<N>`: ```python # python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/common.py def get_layer_id(weight_name): match = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", weight_name) return int(match.group(1)) if match else None ``` A tower module path like `audio_tower.layers.5.attn.qkv_proj` therefore resolves to `layer_id = 5` and lands in `lora_modules[5]["qkv_proj"]` (`lora_manager.py:824`) — **the same slot** as `...language_model.layers.5...qkv_proj`. One silently overwrites the other. When the tower is deeper than the LM (e.g. an audio encoder with more `encoder_layers` than the text `num_hidden_layers`), the same indexing **IndexErrors**. **2. The connector/projector is dropped entirely.** Connector/projection modules (e.g. Qwen3-Omni's `proj1` / `proj2` / `conv_out`, native `ReplicatedLinear` at `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_omni_moe.py:241-251`) have no `layers.<N>` segment, so `get_layer_id` returns `None` and the loop skips them: ```python # python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:821-823 layer_id = get_layer_id(module_name) if layer_id is None: continue ``` **3. (Context) the `should_apply_lora` / `lora_pattern` gate is dead code.** 13 multimodal models define `should_apply_lora` / `lora_pattern` (e.g. `gemma4_mm.py:1043-1048` anchored on `^language_model\.layers\.`), but it is **never called** — the only non-`def` reference is the comment at `lora_manager.py:776-777`. The effective tower exclusion today is the `get_layer_id` gate in (1)/(2), not this method. Worth resolving as part of this work so intent and behavior match. ## Proposal Make LoRA module bookkeeping **component-aware** rather than a single language-sized list keyed by a bare layer index: - Resolve each LoRA module to a `(component, layer_id)` location, where `component ∈ {language, audio_tower, vision_tower, connector}` — e.g. extend `get_layer_id` into a `get_module_location(name)` that also reports the component from the path prefix (`audio_tower.` / `visual.` / projector names). - Namespace `lora_modules` per component (or key by `(component, layer_id)`), so tower layers neither collide with nor overflow the language list. Keep the existing language path keyed exactly as today to guarantee **no behavior change for the 13 existing language-only LoRA models** (the `test/registered/lora` suite as the regression guard). - Add a non-`layers.N` bucket for the connector. - A model opts in by declaring its tower/connector leaf names in `supported_lora_modules` and providing `get_hidden_dim(module_name, layer_idx)` for those names (the pattern already exists at `gemma4_mm.py:1050-1079`). Gate tower names through `model.supported_lora_modules` rather than broadening the shared `_KNOWN_LORA_TARGET_MODULES` set (`utils.py:338-357`), which currently filters out bare `proj`/`fc1`/`fc2` and is consumed by the `"all"` auto-detect path. The `set_lora_module` / `replace_submodule` wiring (`lora_manager.py:726-730`) needs no change. ## Reference implementation — Qwen3-ASR `Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration` (`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_asr.py`) is the cleanest first model: - Its tower (`Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder`) is **already native-wrappable** — attention via `VisionAttention(use_qkv_parallel=True)` → `QKVParallelLinear` + `RowParallelLinear`, FFN `fc1`/`fc2` as `Column`/`Row`/`Replicated` ParallelLinear (`qwen3_omni_moe.py:95, 107-108`), stacked as `self.layers = nn.ModuleList([...])` (`qwen3_omni_moe.py:215`). So live paths are `audio_tower.layers.{i}.attn.qkv_proj` etc., which the wrapping infra already supports. - It declares no `supports_lora` today, so it's unclaimed. I'd be glad to implement it as **PR1 (tower / in-layer first)**, with the **connector as a follow-up** to keep the diff reviewable — mirroring how a tower-vs-projector split keeps review surface small. Qwen3-Omni Thinker shares the same encoder, so the work transfers there as a natural PR2. ## Questions for maintainers - Is component-namespaced layer-id keying the approach you'd prefer, or is there an existing convention I should follow instead? - Is there appetite for tower/connector (non-language) LoRA in general? If so, I'm happy to drive the bookkeeping change + the Qwen3-ASR reference PR. cc @Fridge003 @jybsuper (lora) — would value your read on the keying approach before I put up the implementation.

signals.title: Question: unit mismatch in evict_from_tree_cache for SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator?
signals.text: ## Potential Issue Looking at the current main branch code in `common.py`: ```python # common.py evict_from_tree_cache if isinstance(allocator, SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator): full_available_size = allocator.full_available_size() # ← what unit? swa_available_size = allocator.swa_available_size() if full_available_size < num_tokens or swa_available_size < num_tokens: full_num_tokens = max(0, num_tokens - full_available_size) swa_num_tokens = max(0, num_tokens - swa_available_size) tree_cache.evict( EvictParams(num_tokens=full_num_tokens, swa_num_tokens=swa_num_tokens) ) ``` `full_available_size()` for DSA (DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool -> Hisparse allocator -> SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator) eventually calls `self.full_attn_allocator.available_size()` which returns `self.free_slots.numel()` — the number of free **pages** (slots) in the C4 pool. However, `num_tokens` from the callers (`alloc_token_slots` -> `batch.extend_num_tokens`) appears to be in **tokens**. For DSA models, the C4 pool has ~4096 physical pages. Each page stores multiple compressed tokens. Even when the C4 allocator reports ~4000 free pages, a prefill batch requesting e.g. 3000 tokens would see `4000 < 3000 = False` — and Full eviction would never trigger. For non-DSA models with smaller `page_size` (e.g. 16), the unit mismatch is less severe because pages and tokens are closer in magnitude, which might explain why this hasn't been noticed before. ## Question Is `full_available_size()` intended to return pages or tokens? Should `num_tokens` be divided by `page_size` before comparison, or should `full_available_size()` be multiplied by `page_size`? Or are we misunderstanding the DSA allocator architecture? Any clarification would be greatly appreciated. Happy to submit a PR if this is indeed a mismatch. ## Environment - SGLang version: v0.5.x - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash - TP=8, H100, page_size=64, max_total_tokens=16384

signals.title: [BUG] EAGLE + DP Attention + PD Disaggregation: Deadlock when `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is enabled for GLM-5.2
signals.text: # EAGLE + DP Attention + PD Disaggregation: Deadlock when `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is enabled ## Summary When running EAGLE speculative decoding with DP attention in PD disaggregation decode mode, the server deadlocks during warmup if the model config has `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True` (e.g., `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`). The deadlock occurs at the GPU level due to asymmetric `can_cuda_graph` decisions between idle and non-idle DP ranks in the `draft()` method, causing NCCL `all_gather` buffer mismatches across ranks. Removing either `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` or `--enable-dp-attention` or setting `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=False` in the model config avoids the deadlock. ## Environment - **Model**: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (DeepseekV2 architecture, MoE, FP8 quantization, `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True`, `index_topk` set) - **GPU**: 8x B30Z (Blackwell, SM100+) - **Config**: TP=8, DP=8, `enable_dp_attention=True`, `disaggregation_mode=decode`, `speculative_algorithm=EAGLE`, `speculative_num_steps=3`, `speculative_eagle_topk=1`, `speculative_num_draft_tokens=4` - **Prefill worker**: Does NOT enable EAGLE (`--speculative-algorithm` not set) ## Reproduction ### Decode worker launch command ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 \ --watchdog-timeout 100 \ ... # other args ``` ### Symptom The server starts, captures CUDA graphs, then enters PD disaggregation warmup. During warmup, a request is sent to one DP rank while the other 7 DP ranks are idle. The server hangs and eventually triggers a watchdog timeout. ### Stack trace (py-spy dump) **The non-idle DP rank (has the request)** — stuck in `draft_forward` via **eager path**: ``` draft_forward (eagle_worker_v2.py:545) draft (eagle_worker_v2.py:544) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1197) run_batch (scheduler.py:3351) ``` The eager forward reaches MoE router computation (`dsv3_router_gemm`) and blocks on the NCCL collective. **The 7 idle DP ranks** — stuck in `verify` via **cuda graph path**: ``` seqlens_expand_triton (pad.py:381) _apply_cuda_graph_metadata (dsa_backend.py:1533) init_forward_metadata_out_graph (dsa_backend.py:750) load_batch (decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1188) eagle_prepare_for_verify (eagle_utils.py:558) run_eagle_verify (eagle_worker_common.py:451) verify (eagle_worker_v2.py:1504) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1200) ``` These ranks have already completed `draft()` via cuda graph replay and are waiting in `verify()` for the non-idle rank to catch up. ## Root Cause ### Background: `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend` When the model config has `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True`, the EAGLE worker sets `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend=True`. This flag enables seeding the DSA (Dynamic Sparse Attention) top-k indices from the draft-extend output, so that subsequent draft-decode iterations can reuse the computed indices instead of recomputing. ### The problematic code In `eagle_worker_v2.py`, the `draft()` method contains: ```python if ( can_cuda_graph and self.seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend and not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and draft_input.dsa_topk_indices is None ): can_cuda_graph = False # ← forces eager path ``` This condition downgrades `can_cuda_graph` to `False` when `dsa_topk_indices is None`, forcing the rank onto the **eager path** instead of the **cuda graph path**. ### How the divergence happens In PD disaggregation decode mode: 1. **Prefill worker does NOT enable EAGLE** — it doesn't run `_draft_extend_for_prefill`, so `req.output_dsa_topk_indices` is never set (remains `None`). 2. **Decode worker** receives the request via PD transfer. In `build_eagle_disagg_draft_input()` (`eagle_disaggregation.py`), `dsa_topk_indices` is assembled from `req.output_dsa_topk_indices`. Since all are `None`, the result is `None`. 3. When a request arrives on **one DP rank** (non-idle) while **other DP ranks are idle**: - **Non-idle rank**: `forward_mode.is_idle()` → `False`, so `not is_idle()` → `True`. Combined with `dsa_topk_indices is None`, the condition triggers → `can_cuda_graph = False` → **eager path**. - **Idle ranks**: `forward_mode.is_idle()` → `True`, so `not is_idle()` → `False`. The entire condition is skipped → `can_cuda_graph` stays `True` → **cuda graph path**. 4. **Path divergence**: non-idle rank runs `draft_forward` via eager (no DP padding), idle ranks run draft via cuda graph replay (with DP padding to `max(global_num_tokens)`). 5. **Deadlock**: The MoE MLP layer requires all DP ranks to synchronize via NCCL `all_gather`. The eager path uses per-rank token counts (no padding), while the cuda graph path pads all ranks to the same `max_len`. The mismatched buffer sizes cause a GPU-level deadlock on the NCCL collective. ### Why disabling `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` fixes it When `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=False`: - `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend = False` - The condition never triggers - All ranks consistently use `can_cuda_graph` as determined by `can_run_graph()` (which accounts for DP via `can_run_dp_cuda_graph`) - No path divergence, no deadlock ## Solution Instead of downgrading to eager path when `dsa_topk_indices is None`, set a dummy zero-filled tensor. This keeps `can_cuda_graph = True` for all ranks, ensuring they all use the cuda graph path consistently. ### Patch ```diff --- a/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py +++ b/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py @@ -513,7 +513,11 @@ and not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and draft_input.dsa_topk_indices is None ): - can_cuda_graph = False + draft_input.dsa_topk_indices = torch.zeros( + (draft_input.hidden_states.shape[0], self.dsa_index_topk), + dtype=torch.int32, + device=draft_input.hidden_states.device, + ) ``` ### Why this works - The dummy zero tensor makes `dsa_topk_indices is not None`, so the condition no longer triggers, and `can_cuda_graph` stays `True` for the non-idle rank. - Inside the cuda graph runner's `execute()` method, when `dsa_topk_indices` is not `None`, it copies the seed into the static buffer (`buffers.dsa_seed_topk[:raw_bs].copy_(seed)`). A zero-filled seed is equivalent to no seed — the `draft_forward()` method detects that the seed is all-zeros (via the `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend and dsa_topk_indices is not None` check at line ~618) and sets `spec_info.dsa_topk_indices = None` to trigger recomputation. - All DP ranks (idle and non-idle) now consistently use the cuda graph path, which includes proper DP padding via `DpPaddingMode.MAX_LEN`, ensuring NCCL `all_gather` buffer sizes match across ranks. ### Verification The fix was tested with the original launch command. PD disaggregation warmup completes successfully: ``` [2026-07-27 20:30:40] Disaggregation warmup requests completed for all 8 DP ranks [2026-07-27 20:30:40] End of disaggregation warmup [2026-07-27 20:30:40] The server is fired up and ready to roll!

signals.title: [RFC] KVCR as a HiCacheStorage backend for peer-to-peer KV reuse
signals.text:
## Summary SGLang's HiCache already supports pluggable L3 storage backends (mooncake, hf3fs, eic, …) behind a stable `HiCacheStorage` interface. This RFC adds KVCR as one more such backend. KVCR is a multi-tier KV cache management solution from NVIDIA. The integration totally follows the integration and design of hicache storage — we register a `"kvcr"` backend and implement the same `batch_set_v2 / batch_get_v2 / batch_exists_v2` contract the other backends already implement. This backend also aligns with the router-initiated hint model in **[#27574 — Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574)**, which defines a provider-neutral hint taxonomy (Share / Prefetch / Demote / Pin / Retain). KVCR fits the **`Share`** intent — *"reuse a prefix that already lives on another worker... pull the prefix from the old one"* — but does not depend on that RFC: it is a self-contained mechanism any router emitting such a hint can drive. Following the Dynamo DEP (ai-dynamo/dynamo#11673), the near term goal is **direct worker-to-worker (host memory) KV reuse**: a prefix computed on one worker is served to another without recomputation or a round-trip through a global pool. When a request lands on a worker lacking a prefix another worker holds, KVCR fetches it **peer-to-peer** — an asymmetric, directed transfer, not a symmetric external store. Selecting *which* peer holds the prefix is a decision only a router can make well. So the router hands the target worker a small piece of per-request metadata — a **hint** — naming the peer. "Router" here means any orchestrator above the engine: the router (flash indexer) is the first target, SGLang's own router a later one, and the same carrier serves both. The rest of this RFC covers (1) that hint and (2) how KVCR plugs into HiCache to act on it. ## Part 1 — Router Hint ### Why a hint is needed HiCache storage is content-addressed: the controller asks `get(block_hash)` and the backend is expected to know where the bytes live. That works for a global pool. It does **not** work for P2P reuse, where the same prefix may sit on any one of N peer workers. The only component that knows which one is the **router** — it made the routing decision that sent this request here in the first place. The hint will directly tell the node where target kvcache sits. ### Why decide this at the router Putting the source-selection decision at the routing stage — rather than probing peers after a request lands — is what makes the hint valuable beyond avoiding a broadcast: - **It enables a routing cost function that can grow over time.** The hint is the input to a decision the router makes; that decision can start *simple* (route on load only, ignoring cache residency) and evolve to *rich* (weigh prefix cache residency, estimated transfer time, distance/topology, and thresholds that decide when a P2P fetch is even worth it versus recomputation). - **It lets us prefetch and shape system behavior.** Because the router decides before the request is admitted, the target can begin fetching the prefix ahead of time, and the router — with its global view — can steer placement to balance load and reuse across the fleet, rather than reacting locally after the fact. ### Carrier We do **not** widen the `HiCacheStorage` signature. Every v2 call already threads a free-form `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info` dict from the controller into the backend. The hint is the `Share` case of #27574's provider-neutral hint envelope and rides in that dict; the key name below is a placeholder pending #27574's envelope: ``` # placeholder key — to be aligned with #27574's KvHintEnvelope extra_info.extra_info["kvcr_router_hint"] = { "source_control_endpoint": "host:port", # ZMQ control endpoint of the peer holding the prefix "block_hashes": [...], # root-aligned block hashes for the shared prefix } ``` ### Propagation path The hint travels from the router down to the backend without widening any interface — it rides the `extra_info` dict every layer already passes through: 1. **router → scheduler.** The router attaches the hint to the request's `extra_info`; the scheduler stashes it into the prefetch request. 2. **scheduler → controller.** `HiCacheController.prefetch(...)` carries it into the daemon `prefetch_io_aux_func` thread (`managers/cache_controller.py`). 3. **controller → backend.** `_page_transfer → page_get_func(op, hashes, host_idx, extra_info)` hands it to `KVCR.batch_get_v2(...)` (`storage/kvcr/kvcr_store.py`). 4. **backend → decision.** `RouterHint.maybe_from_extra_info(extra_info)` (`storage/kvcr/router_hint.py`) parses it: - hint **absent/malformed** → fall back to local-only (deposit/local-get), never raises; - hint **present** → drive a directed P2P fetch from `source_control_endpoint`. The parser is **fail-closed**: a missing or malformed hint degrades to local-only behavior, it never crashes a prefetch, and the backend is safe to ship before the any router side lands (dynamo pr here https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/11695). ## Part 2 — KVCR Integration Architecture ### Where it sits ```mermaid flowchart LR SCH[Scheduler] --- HRC[HiRadixCache] --- HCC[HiCacheController] HCC -->|HiCacheStorage iface| KS[KVCR
thin adapter] subgraph core[KVCR core · vendored] LD[local DRAM tier
deposit / get] CC[control channel
ZMQ peer] PT[progress thread
owns NIXL agent] end KS --> core ``` `KVCR` is a thin adapter. It owns no transfer threads of its own — kvcr's core runs **one** daemon "kvcr-progress" thread that exclusively holds the NIXL agent and control socket. The store advances state only by calling `poll_completed()` from the HiCache controller's existing prefetch thread. No new threading model is introduced into SGLang. ### Get path (with router hint) — sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AUX as prefetch aux thread participant KS as KVCR participant PT as KVCR progress thread participant SRC as source worker participant SCH as scheduler AUX->>KS: batch_get_v2(hashes, host_idx, extra_info) Note over KS: hint = maybe_from_extra_info(...) KS->>PT: submit_hint(source_endpoint, keys) Note over PT: register source peer KS->>PT: h = deliver(blocks) PT->>SRC: START_WRITE (ctrl) Note over SRC: search_and_pin SRC-->>PT: NIXL WRITE (UCX) → host pages (direct DMA) SRC-->>PT: send_notif("write_done") Note over PT: _poll_notifications
_TargetDeliverOp: WAITING→FINISHED PT-->>KS: _completion_queue.append(OpResult) Note over KS: poll_completed(): match r.op_handle == h KS-->>AUX: [per-page success bools] Note over AUX: operation.increment(page_size × hits) SCH->>SCH: check_prefetch_progress(req_id)
polls completed_tokens (hiradix_cache.py) Note over SCH: True → req admitted into batch ``` - **A single KVCR daemon thread owns the whole P2P mechanism.** It handles all KVCR↔KVCR message send/recv, maintains the internal op state machine, and drives the interaction with NIXL transfers. When a transfer finishes it does not push anything — it just appends the result to a completion queue; the store itself spawns no extra thread. - **The KVCR thread never touches the scheduler main thread or the prefetch thread.** It runs entirely on its own, so neither of SGLang's threads is blocked or slowed by how KVCR does its work. - **The existing completion-notification model is unchanged.** A finished transfer sits on that queue until the prefetch daemon thread actively drains it via `poll_completed()` and turns it into `completed_tokens`; the scheduler main thread, one level up, only reads the resulting boolean tick (`check_prefetch_progress`) — the same KVPoll-style poll as today. ### Non-goals - No changes to HiRadixCache or the scheduler cache path. - No new SGLang-side transfer threads. - Shared-HiCache serving (source pins from HiRadixCache via `TreeNode.protect_host`) is a future swap of the pin adapter only — out of scope here.
