signals.title: [Bug] Hybrid Mamba prefill allocation failure kills scheduler instead of returning request to waiting queue
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug occurs on SGLang 0.5.16, build commit `fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`. - [x] Environment information and a reproduction configuration are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, written in English. ### Describe the bug Under sustained Kimi-K3 traffic with hybrid Mamba/radix caching, a prefill allocation failure terminates a scheduler rank and subsequently the whole server instead of leaving the request in the waiting queue, rechunking it, retracting work, or failing only that request. Observed fatal error on every scheduler rank: ```text RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size. Try to allocate 8192 tokens. Available full tokens: 8070656 (full_available_size=7936 + full_evictable_size_=8062720) Available mamba: 760 (available_size=57 + component_evictable_size_=703) ``` The process supervisor then reports that a child failed, sends `SIGQUIT`, and shuts down the complete process tree. There was no host OOM, CUDA Xid, or Docker OOM kill. The surprising part is that the request passes prefill admission but the later real allocation can still fail fatally: 1. `PrefillAdder.rem_total_tokens` for `is_hybrid_ssm_cache` considers the token allocator's `available_size()` plus `tree_cache.full_evictable_size()`. 2. The admitted request is added to `can_run_list` and removed from `waiting_queue` in `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw()`. 3. `new_batch.prepare_for_extend()` subsequently performs the real allocation. 4. `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` raises an uncaught `RuntimeError` when `allocator.alloc_extend()` returns `None`. There is no rollback that places the admitted prefill request back in `waiting_queue`, and no retry with a smaller chunk. Decode has a retraction path, but this late prefill allocation failure does not. Expected behavior: capacity pressure should preserve process availability. The request should remain/return to waiting, be retried with a smaller chunk after eviction, be preempted, or receive a request-scoped OOM response. A single allocation miss should not terminate every scheduler rank. ### Reproduction Serve Kimi-K3 with TP8/DCP4 and hybrid Mamba cache settings: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --served-model-name kimi-k3-dev \ --tp-size 8 \ --dcp-size 4 \ --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --mem-fraction-static 0.93 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --mamba-full-memory-ratio 7.21 \ --max-mamba-cache-size 800 \ --max-running-requests 60 \ --context-length 262144 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 ``` Run concurrent long-context requests until the Mamba/radix cache is under pressure and submit another request requiring an 8192-token prefill chunk. In our run, the allocator reported the values above and the uncaught exception terminated the server. Even if this particular memory split is too aggressive, the requested fix is graceful backpressure/recovery rather than changing the cache sizing defaults. ### Environment ```text Python: 3.12.3 CUDA available: True GPU 0-7: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (275040 MiB each) Compute Capability: 10.3 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: CUDA 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 595.71.05 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.16 sglang build commit: fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.15.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.140.0 huggingface_hub: 1.24.0 uvicorn: 0.51.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 NVIDIA topology: all eight GPUs connected via NV18 ulimit soft: 1024 ```

signals.title: [Bug] [XPU] Qwen3.5 GDN + speculative decode: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window'
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On --device xpu, any speculative-decoding run on a hybrid GDN/linear-attention model (Qwen3.5) crashes in the target-verify path during the server's own warmup generation, before any user request. gdn_backend.py:43-48 binds the XPU kernel as-is: elif is_xpu(): from sgl_kernel import causal_conv1d_fn_xpu, causal_conv1d_update_xpu causal_conv1d_update = causal_conv1d_update_xpu but the is_target_verify branch at gdn_backend.py:539 calls it with five spec-only kwargs that the XPU op schema does not have — intermediate_conv_window, intermediate_state_indices, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, retrieve_parent_token. The XPU signature stops at conv_state_indices / pad_slot_id. File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py", line 539, in forward_extend mixed_qkv_processed = causal_conv1d_update( TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' The scheduler dies, and the client then reports a downstream ConnectionError (secondary noise). Non-spec decode on the same model/backend is unaffected — only TARGET_VERIFY takes this branch. The NPU and CPU bindings a few lines below (gdn_backend.py:49-60) are wired the same way and look exposed to the identical gap; unverified. Issue is induce #31250 fix. ### Reproduction With simple below steps able to reproduce issue ``` python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code \ --device xpu --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --max-running-requests 1 \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 512 --output-len 8 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' ``` Note : #34712 is required to reproduce the above error using shell command. ### Environment Intel Environment - sglang : 0.5.18.dev364+g667e18d99 torch : 2.12.0+xpu | cuda: None | hip: None | xpu: 20250302 python : 3.12.13 | Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 device : 8 x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics driver : 1.14.36300+8 | mem GB: 22.7

signals.title: [Bug] TypeError in set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs during NEXTN TARGET_VERIFY — mamba_next_track_idx is None (hybrid-mamba + speculative decoding + lazy buffer mode)
signals.text: **Env:** SGLang 0.5.14 (pip wheel) · model: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 · GPU: 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB each) · NEXTN speculative decoding enabled **Crash:** \`TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer\` at \`schedule_batch.py:1594\` in \`set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs()\` during TARGET_VERIFY. **Mechanism (from reading v0.5.14 source):** \`Req.mamba_next_track_idx\` initializes to \`None\` (schedule_batch.py:790) and is only assigned in the extend path — an assignment that lazy buffer mode skips (line ~2325, deferring to \`mamba_lazy_prealloc_at_boundary\` in \`prepare_for_decode\`). NEXTN's TARGET_VERIFY builds the track-index tensor (line 1589+) before any decode step has run for a fresh request, so the tensor build receives \`None\`. **Workaround (running stably on my machine):** for req in batch.reqs: if req.mamba_next_track_idx is None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = 0 placed immediately before the torch.tensor build. Zero is the semantically correct initial ping-pong slot per the field's own comment ("0 or 1"). A maintainer may prefer initializing at the source instead. **Context:** the same architectural class (hybrid-recurrent state index reaching a spec-decode kernel unset/unbounded) has three known instances in vLLM (vllm#43559, vllm#50021) — SGLang fails loudly with this TypeError where vLLM's analogues fault in-kernel. Downstream discussion: noonghunna/club-3090#803.

signals.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
signals.text: ## Motivation The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its `> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss. None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike): - Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer. - `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter, no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for truly scattered index sets. - Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`) become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads them back. ## Prior work **Landed** - #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and bookkeeping coupled to real allocations - #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device sync (non-SWA) - #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on) - #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant: every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned) - #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant) - #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len) **Closed** - #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full shape - #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len` - #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned extents remove the need for it) ## In flight - #35396 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor on the second PD decode prealloc path, and drop the fixture that mocked an unaligned tail length - #35401 -- write the `req_to_token` page tail so a row stays valid over every page the allocator handed out; widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every paged config. Prerequisite for page-ceiling `kv_allocated_len`: without it, anything slicing a row by a page-ceiled length reads the previous occupant's indices - #35592 -- decide SWA slot liveness on the host and drop the `> 0` filter in `free_swa`. Callers now declare whether a range's SWA peers are still live, from state they already keep (`node.swa_tombstone`, `req.kv.swa_evicted_seqlen`, the unified tree's `cd.value is None`); `free_full` completes the pool-specific pair so `free(x) == free_full(x) + free_swa(x)` holds for every allocator. At `page_size == 1` this makes the per-decode-step window eviction (`free_swa_out_of_window_slots`) sync-free outright; paged configs still hit the `torch.unique` in `_expand_to_full_pages`, which needs the page-representative read to go with it

signals.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode. - [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration. - [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure. - [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code. - [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters. --- ## Summary Under a long-prefill workload with: - DeepSeek-V4-Pro - TP=8 - DP=8 - DP Attention enabled - chunked prefill enabled - PrefillDelayer enabled - one 8-GPU node an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes: ### Healthy synchronized state - Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s - DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep - `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait` - average running requests is ~8.5 ### Pathological LOW state - Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s - within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks - the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk - `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay` - average running requests collapses to ~0.15 - residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s. Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency: - throughput: ~48–68k tok/s - avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9 - residual batches: ~11–14% Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress. The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898. --- ## Environment ```text SGLang version : 0.5.14 commit : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb git log -1 : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246) git describe : v0.5.14 remote : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git local patches : no tracked-file modifications ``` The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree. Hardware / topology: ```text 1 node 8 × NVIDIA B30Z TP = 8 DP = 8 DP Attention = enabled MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE ``` Relevant server configuration: ```bash --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --chunked-prefill-size 131072 ``` With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is: ```text 131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens ``` Relevant MegaMoE cap: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512 ``` Workload: ```text input length : 60000 output length : 1 max concurrency : 16 num prompts : 160 ignore_eos : true seed : 1 ``` The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as: ```text 16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder ``` The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline. --- ## Reproduction behavior Representative post-reboot runs: | Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% | | LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% | | LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% | | good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% | | mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% | | LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% | The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise. A host reboot did not eliminate the problem. --- ## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence Using the per-rank counter: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"} ``` I computed: ```text progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) ``` Results: | Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k | | LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k | | LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 | The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately: ```text 16384 tokens ``` which is exactly one effective prefill chunk. `realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution. ### Metric-cadence validation I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk. Across all ranks: ```text jump interval p50 = 1.397 s jump interval p95 = 1.535 s min interval = 0.401 s ``` Jump-size distribution: ```text 16384 ×112 (one full chunk) 11264 ×8 (tail chunks) 256 ×3 (small startup fragments) 32768 ×0 (no two-chunk merge observed) ``` Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run. --- ## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload. | Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% | | mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% | | LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% | The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run: ```text 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 ``` All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s. Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state. Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch. --- ## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs From: ```text sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total ``` healthy runs eventually converge to sustained: ```text input_estimation="all" output_reason="no_wait" ``` while LOW runs remain dominated by: ```text input_estimation="mixed" output_reason="delay" ``` In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state. In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime. I use: ```text all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay) ``` only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode. The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model. --- ## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled. | Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s | | 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s | | 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s | | 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s | | 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s | | 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s | Mean throughput: ```text 58,980 tok/s CV = 12.88% ``` The important mechanism difference is: ```text PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5 PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15 PrefillDelayer OFF : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9 ``` Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime. This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above. --- ## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to: ```text 2 requests/s, fixed interval ``` while keeping concurrency=16. This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful. Representative results: ```text burst: 94,630 tok/s ramp : 53,449 tok/s burst: 64,016 tok/s ramp : LOW again ``` The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state. This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase. Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration. --- ## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes. ### 1. #29898 — missing locally The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch: ```python prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0 if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1: ... output_reason="delay" else: ... output_reason="wait_timeout" ``` but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true: ```python if slot_condition or queue_condition: ... next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count() return _NegotiateOutput( output_allow=False, output_reason="delay", ... ) ``` with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound. This confirms that the local tree predates #29898. However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`. Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse. --- ### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths: ```text add_one_req_ignore_eos() -> negotiation after budget/admission checks add_one_req() -> negotiation at the beginning of the function ``` The dispatch condition is: ```python if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True): return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req) ``` This reproduction has: ```text ignore_eos = true radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false ``` so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`. In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with: ```python if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and ( not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill( local_prefillable=True, running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(), max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs, max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests, waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len, ) ): return AddReqResult.OTHER ``` before later request / chunk / admission checks. Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics. This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal. That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger. --- ### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present The local scheduler already contains an early guard: ```python if ( self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0 and self.chunked_req is None ... ): ``` but the later waiting-queue loop still contains: ```python if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs): self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True ``` while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses: ```python min( pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs, req_to_token_pool.available_size(), ) ``` where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`. This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295. I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor. --- ### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization. With the current settings: ```text disable_overlap_schedule = false SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false ``` PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path. Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround. If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further. --- ### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills. The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match. It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior. --- ## Current interpretation The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence: ```text formal workload begins ↓ DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts ↓ within the first few seconds, per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount ↓ PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states ↓ mixed/delay persists ↓ under-filled / residual batches increase ↓ running concurrency collapses ↓ LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining ``` One causal distinction is still unresolved: ### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer: ```text same/similar forward opportunity ↓ one rank completes later ↓ prefill progress diverges ↓ Delayer subsequently observes mixed ``` ### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities: ```text scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges ↓ Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions ↓ those ranks do less forward work ↓ prefill progress diverges ``` I am instrumenting: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"} ``` together with: ```text sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category} ``` using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`. The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state. The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between: ```text Δprefill_progress and Δcompleted_forward_execution_time ``` over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence. Roughly: ```text ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower → rank likely completed less forward work → supports scheduler/readiness-side cause ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher → rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress → supports execution-duration-side cause ``` This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above. --- ## Why I think this deserves a separate issue I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together: ```text DP Attention + PrefillDelayer + chunked long-prefill workload + same deterministic configuration + healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state + LOW dominated by mixed/delay + avg running collapsing near zero + rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk + request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction ``` #29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug. The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode. --- ## Questions for maintainers 1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer? 2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks? 3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state? 4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`? 5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing? --- ## Additional data available I retained: - per-run server logs - per-rank Prefill batch logs - `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces - 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures - per-rank `realtime_tokens_total` - PrefillDelayer outcome counters - queue/running-request counters - host/GPU telemetry - good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

signals.title: [Bug] Quantized lm_head silently produces uninitialized logits with compressed-tensors (ParallelLMHead not dispatched)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. - [x] Please use English. ### Describe the bug A compressed-tensors checkpoint with a quantized `lm_head` loads without error and then emits **uninitialized logits** — every request returns repeated token 0 (`!!!!!!...`). `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` dispatches on two layer types and returns `None` for everything else: ```python if isinstance(layer, LinearBase): ... if isinstance(layer, FusedMoE): ... return None ``` `ParallelLMHead` subclasses `VocabParallelEmbedding`, not `LinearBase`, so it gets `None` and falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. That creates a plain `weight` parameter, while the checkpoint supplies `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` — which nothing reads. The parameter is never filled, so the head multiplies by uninitialized memory. It is silent: the server starts, reports no error, and serves garbage. **vLLM handles this case** (SGLang's file is marked `# Adapted from vLLM`). In `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py`: ```python if isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead): quant_scheme = self.get_scheme(layer=layer, layer_name=prefix) ... return CompressedTensorsLinearMethod(self) # ParallelLMHead subclasses VocabParallelEmbedding but is handled above as # a linear; only true embedding lookups land here. if isinstance(layer, VocabParallelEmbedding): ... ``` The adaptation appears to have dropped that branch. Note `ParallelLMHead` already calls `quant_method.create_weights` with the `LinearMethodBase` signature (`input_size_per_partition=embedding_dim`, `output_partition_sizes=[num_embeddings_per_partition]`), so the linear method works unmodified. This is **not hardware-specific** — the dispatch has no device branching. It reproduces anywhere a compressed-tensors checkpoint quantizes `lm_head`. Secondary point: with the dispatch added, scheme matching also needs `lm_head` in `config_groups.*.targets`, otherwise it raises `ValueError: Unable to find matching target for lm_head in the compressed-tensors config.` That is checkpoint-side and matches what llm-compressor emits. ### Reproduction Any compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `lm_head` is quantized (i.e. not in `ignore`, and listed in `config_groups.*.targets`): ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <compressed-tensors ckpt with quantized lm_head> curl localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"...","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17*23?"}],"max_tokens":30}' # -> "!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" ``` Leaving `lm_head` in the `ignore` list produces correct output, which isolates it to the head. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 GPU 0: Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151) # incidental — the bug is device-independent PyTorch: 2.13.0a0+rocm7.13.0a20260422 sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g3f048c80b.d20260513 sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post1 triton: 3.7.0 transformers: 5.6.0 ```

signals.title: [Bug] Session continuation crashes the engine on M-RoPE models: unguarded partial slice of the mm-input M-RoPE position table
signals.text:
## Summary Extending a session (`/generate` with `session_params: {id, rid}`) on a Qwen3.5-family model kills the whole engine on the second request. The scheduler process raises inside the static buffer loader: ``` File ".../model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py", line 52, in _foreach_copy torch._foreach_copy_(group_dsts, group_srcs) RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1842) must match the size of tensor b (1816) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` All TP schedulers exit (`Scheduler hit an exception` -> SIGQUIT -> `kill_process_tree`), taking every in-flight request down with them. ## Reproduction matrix (4/4 crash) | session mode | prefill CUDA graphs | second request | result | |---|---|---|---| | native | on (default) | text + 2 images | engine dies | | streaming (`--enable-streaming-session`) | on | text + 2 images | engine dies | | native | `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` | text + 2 images | engine dies (same copy, via `eager_runner.load_batch`) | | native | off | **text only** | engine dies | The text-only reproduction rules out multimodal payloads; the eager reproduction rules out the CUDA-graph runners (the failing copy is the shared `cuda_graph_buffer_registry.fill_from`, used by the eager path too). Turn 1 through the session path works normally. Plain stateless traffic on the same pod is completely healthy (we ran 48-request multimodal ladders up to 26 images / 23.6k tokens with the mamba radix cache giving correct prefix reuse). ## Setup - Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid GDN + full-attention, M-RoPE) - sglang 0.5.17 (image `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` pulled 2026-08-18), BF16, tp 4, `--context-length 32768`, `--trust-remote-code` ## Minimal reproduction Run against a server started with `--enable-streaming-session` (or without; native sessions crash identically). One image on turn 1, a text-only rid-chained turn 2, and the engine dies: ```python import base64, json, urllib.request BASE = "http://localhost:30000" def post(path, body): req = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}{path}", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) def gen(sid, rid, text, images=None): sp = {"id": sid} if rid is None else {"id": sid, "rid": rid} body = {"text": text, "session_params": sp, "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 30, "stop": ["<|im_end|>"]}, "stream": True} if images: body["image_data"] = images final, meta = "", {} with post("/generate", body) as r: for raw in r: line = raw.decode().strip() if not line.startswith("data:") or line[5:].strip() == "[DONE]": continue ch = json.loads(line[5:].strip()) final = ch.get("text", final) meta = ch.get("meta_info", meta) return final, meta img = "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(open("any.jpg", "rb").read()).decode() sid = json.loads(post("/open_session", {"capacity_of_str_len": 262144}).read()) t1 = ("<|im_start|>user
<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>What is this?<|im_end|>
" "<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

") reply, meta = gen(sid, None, t1, [img]) print("turn 1 ok:", reply[:40]) t2 = ("<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
Say one word.<|im_end|>
" "<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

") gen(sid, meta["id"], t2) # engine dies here; subsequent requests get connection refused ``` ## Diagnosis (instrumented, root cause confirmed) The failing tensor is `ForwardBatch.mrope_positions`. We instrumented `_grouped_foreach_copy_` and `_compute_mrope_positions` on the repro pod and caught the crash batch directly. Text-only continuation of a session whose turn 1 carried one image: ``` [XA-DEBUG] mrope extend_lens=[50] prefix_lens=[896] widths=[(3, 2)] [XA-DEBUG] copy mismatch dst=(3, 50) src=(3, 2) dtype=torch.int64 RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (50) must match the size of tensor b (2) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` The mechanism is in `ForwardBatch._compute_mrope_positions` (extend branch): ```python mrope_positions = mm_input.mrope_positions[ :, extend_prefix_len : extend_prefix_len + extend_seq_len ] if mrope_positions.numel() == 0: mrope_positions = self._expand_mrope_from_input(...) ``` For a session continuation, `mm_input` is the session's original multimodal input, whose precomputed `mrope_positions` table covers only the original prompt (~898 columns here). The continuation's extend window `[896 : 896+50]` runs past the end of that table, and the slice **silently truncates** to the 2 overlapping columns. The `numel() == 0` guard only catches the fully-out-of-range case; a partially-out-of-range window sails through as a wrong-width tensor and explodes in the batch loader, killing the engine. The multimodal variant (turn 2 adds 2 new images, delta = 1816 tokens) is the same misalignment, with a hybrid-model amplifier visible in the logged numbers: ``` [XA-DEBUG] mrope extend_lens=[1843] prefix_lens=[1792] widths=[(3, 1816)] [XA-DEBUG] copy mismatch dst=(3, 1843) src=(3, 1816) dtype=torch.int64 ``` `prefix_lens` snapped down to 1792 = 7 x 256 (`mamba_track_interval`): on a GDN hybrid the continuation resumes from the last mamba state checkpoint, which widens the extend window past the raw delta. The M-RoPE table ends at column 3608, so the slice `[:, 1792 : 1792 + 1843]` truncates to 1816 columns against an 1843-token extend. The checkpoint snap-down makes hybrids especially prone to the overrun, but the unguarded partial slice is the root defect and is reachable by any M-RoPE model served with sessions. Models without M-RoPE never take this path, which matches production experience: the identical session protocol (including rewind) has served a gemma-4 pod for weeks without issue. The bug is the intersection sessions x M-RoPE models, not sessions in general. ## Suggested fix shape In the extend branch, treat a partially-covered window the same as an uncovered one: when `mm_input.mrope_positions.shape[1] < extend_prefix_len + extend_seq_len`, recompute positions for the uncovered span (sequential positions continuing from `mrope_position_delta`, as the existing fallback does) instead of slicing short. Alternatively, extend the session's mm-input position table at continuation enqueue. We have a live repro pod and can validate a patch and follow up with a PR. Secondary observation, likely worth its own issue: a per-request accounting error inside the scheduler takes down the entire engine rather than failing the request.

signals.title: [Bug] Ranks sharing one `ssd_offload_path` collide on Mooncake bucket files → L3 cache broken
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug **Summary.** `MooncakeStore` passes one `ssd_offload_path` to every rank's embedded Mooncake client, but Mooncake's `LOCAL_DISK` (bucket) tier assumes **one client per directory**. A shared directory silently corrupts KV data and makes cross-restart recovery ambiguous. A fix already exists in #31926, but it has no tracking issue and its CI is blocked on the `run-ci` label — this issue is the tracking issue + rationale. **Environment.** SGLang `main`; Mooncake `main`; DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MLA), TP8, HiCache L3 → Mooncake bucket backend. **Root cause** (Mooncake `mooncake-store/src/storage_backend.cpp`): - bucket id = `(time_gen() << 12) | 0`, seeded once at construction (`time_gen()` is whole-second), then plain `fetch_add` — time is never re-read. - filename = `<storage_path>/<bucket_id>.bucket` — no rank/client component; opened `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, no `O_EXCL`. - Two ranks constructed in the same second → identical id sequences → identical filenames → the second `O_TRUNC` silently truncates the first → later reads return wrong KV bytes, no error. - With dp-attention, `tp_rank` is attention-group-local (0 on every DP rank when `attn_tp_size==1`), so `tp_rank` alone collapses ranks onto one dir — `dp_rank` is required. **Impact.** - Silent KV corruption in any shared-path multi-rank deploy. Production repro in #31926: 8 clients, same second, mutual truncation within minutes. - On restart, each rank's Mooncake `Init()` adopts the whole directory (no owner tag), so all ranks re-register all keys; the master keeps an arbitrary first-claim → dangling references when one rank later evicts a shared file. **Fix + coupling.** - #31926 gives each rank `ssd_offload_path/rank_{dp}_{tp}_{pp}/` (unchanged when `storage_config is None`) and adds `dp_rank` to `HiCacheStorageConfig`. Its CI is red only because the `run-ci` gate exits before any test runs. - The per-rank layout is also the precondition for Mooncake's per-directory recovery/ownership model — its restart re-adoption binds identity to a per-`storage_path` marker (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2306) — so the SGLang and Mooncake sides should land jointly. **Ask.** 1. Apply the CI label so #31926 (or equivalent per-rank namespacing) can be tested and merged. 2. Confirm one-storage-location-per-client as the supported model, make the per-rank path the HiCache+Mooncake default, and document it. ### Reproduction See #31926 ### Environment See #31926

signals.title: [Feature] Add a tiered AdaLN cache manager for MiniMax-H3
signals.text: ## Summary MiniMax-H3 can avoid keeping the 24.2 GiB of `adaln_proj` checkpoint weights resident by rebuilding AdaLN outputs online. With TP=2, the resident path uses approximately 12.3 GiB per card for those weights. The current online implementation instead keeps a fixed GPU slab of historical timestep plans. This works well for repeated schedules, but it wastes GPU memory and evicts all plans when the schedule working set changes. This issue proposes a tiered cache manager: 1. Keep only the current request's AdaLN working set on GPU. 2. Keep complete, bounded schedule entries in pinned CPU memory. 3. Use online rebuild for CPU misses and high-churn workloads. 4. Keep precomputed sidecars as the preferred path for fixed production schedules. The design must preserve exact timestep-plan matching and the current numerical contract. Approximate timestep merging is out of scope. ## Motivation The cache key is the exact FP32 timestep plan used by a denoise step. A request can produce a different key when any of the following changes: - `num_inference_steps` - video or audio `sigmas` - `flow_shift` or `audio_flow_shift` - condition noise augmentation - task or reference modality layout In a typical 8-step request, only seven plans are needed. The default rebuild slab reserves 64 plans at the maximum width, even when most of that capacity is unused. When capacity is exceeded, the current implementation resets the slab, so returning to a recently used schedule requires rebuilding it from the checkpoint again. The default 64-plan, width-4 slab is approximately 2.31 GiB per card. The T2VA measurements below used the supported width-2 setting, which reduces that fixed slab to approximately 1.16 GiB per card. ## Measurements Environment: 2 x H200, MiniMax-H3 FL2VA, 1344 x 768, 4 seconds, 8 steps, TP=2/Ulysses=1. ### End-to-end measurements | Configuration | AdaLN prepare | E2E | GPU AdaLN working memory | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 64-plan online slab, warm hit | ~0.2 ms | ~19.0 s | ~1.16 GiB/card | | 7-plan request-sized slab, warm hit | ~0.2 ms | ~19.0 s | ~0.13 GiB/card | | 7-plan slab, new schedule | ~2.4 s | ~21.4 s | ~0.13 GiB/card | | Fixed 8-step sidecar, warm hit | ~0.02 ms | ~19.25 s | ~0.13 GiB/card | | Resident AdaLN weights, warm | N/A | ~19.0 s | +~12.3 GiB/card | The 7-plan slab is a temporary request-sized approximation, not the proposed final dynamic implementation. It demonstrates that reducing the slab capacity does not regress warm-request latency. ### CPU backing transfer cost Pinned host-to-device and device-to-host copies were measured at approximately 51 GiB/s: | Schedule working set | H2D | D2H | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 120 MiB (T2VA) | 2.28 ms | 2.29 ms | | 185 MiB (FL2VA) | 3.51 ms | 3.53 ms | | 231 MiB (widest ref2va) | 4.39 ms | 4.40 ms | This is substantially cheaper than rebuilding a schedule from checkpoint weights, which currently takes roughly 2.4-3.0 seconds. Nsight profiling shows that cold rebuild time is dominated by reading roughly 24.3 GiB of AdaLN checkpoint weights into GPU memory. The projection GEMMs are not the dominant cost. ### Raw request results The following values are taken from the server perf dumps generated during the experiment. The sequence for the online runs was `flow_shift = [12, 12, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 12]`, with `audio_flow_shift=3`, 8 inference steps, and the same prompt, resolution, duration, and seed for every request. The first request includes one-time server/kernel warm-up and is reported separately. | Run | Schedule | AdaLN prepare | Denoising | Decoding | E2E | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Online, 64 plans, request 0 | 12 (cold start) | 3037.0 ms | 21427.9 ms | 3466.6 ms | 25206.1 ms | | Online, 64 plans, request 1 | 12 (GPU hit) | 0.2 ms | 16847.6 ms | 2021.8 ms | 18948.3 ms | | Online, 64 plans, requests 2-10 | 4-13 (new schedules) | 2888.4-3044.2 ms | 19793.6-20209.3 ms | 2021.4-2027.6 ms | 21894.5-22335.3 ms | | Online, 64 plans, request 11 | 12 (GPU hit) | 0.2 ms | 17009.5 ms | 2021.3 ms | 19106.7 ms | | Online, 7 plans, request 0 | 12 (cold start) | 2745.5 ms | 21355.7 ms | 2755.7 ms | 24764.7 ms | | Online, 7 plans, request 1 | 12 (GPU hit) | 0.2 ms | 16859.2 ms | 2022.4 ms | 18966.7 ms | | Online, 7 plans, requests 2-10 | 4-13 (new schedules) | 2309.6-2424.1 ms | 19236.3-19334.9 ms | 2020.1-2122.1 ms | 21350.8-21457.9 ms | | Online, 7 plans, request 11 | 12 (evicted, rebuild) | 2363.5 ms | 19240.2 ms | 2128.2 ms | 21502.3 ms | | Resident AdaLN weights, request 1 | 12 (warm) | 0.02 ms | 16920.2 ms | 2027.9 ms | 19025.7 ms | | Fixed sidecar, request 1 | 12 (sidecar hit) | 0.02 ms | 17136.6 ms | 2029.3 ms | 19246.2 ms | The return-to-12 result is the direct eviction evidence: the 64-plan run still had the original schedule available, while the 7-plan run had replaced its entire GPU working set and paid another rebuild. ### Raw memory observations The perf dumps reported the following allocated-memory checkpoints per card: | Configuration | Before forward | Peak after forward | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Online, 64 plans, warm | 51949.1 MiB | 54888.1 MiB | | Online, 7 plans, warm | 50895.4 MiB | 53834.3 MiB | | Resident weights, warm | 63191.6 MiB | 66131.5 MiB | | Fixed sidecar, warm | 50895.6 MiB | 53834.5 MiB | The 7-plan workspace reduced allocated memory by approximately 1054 MiB per card relative to the 64-plan T2VA run, without a measurable warm-hit regression. The resident-weight comparison was run in a separate server process; its latency is useful as a reference, but the memory values should be interpreted as process-level observations rather than an isolated AdaLN allocation measurement. ### Accuracy and transfer checks - The audited AdaLN comparison checked 470,367,744 output elements at TP1 and TP2 with zero mismatches. - Online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs produced matching MP4 MD5 values for both cold and cached cases at TP1 and TP2. - Pinned CPU/GPU transfer microbenchmarks measured 2.28 ms H2D for 120 MiB, 3.51 ms for 185 MiB, and 4.39 ms for 231 MiB. D2H measured 2.29 ms, 3.53 ms, and 4.40 ms respectively. - The fixed sidecar accepted the exact `flow_shift=12` schedule and rejected `flow_shift=4` with `MiniMax H3 AdaLN cache does not cover the request timestep plan`. ### Nsight cold-rebuild profile A TP1 cold-rebuild capture covered 8455.9 ms. Within that range: | Activity | Count/bytes | GPU or API time | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Host-to-device checkpoint copies | 249 copies, 26,078,740,624 bytes | 7258.2 ms | | Main AdaLN projection GEMM kernel | 2450 launches | 296.9 ms | | BF16 output copy kernels | 2400 launches | 7.9 ms | | `cudaMemcpyAsync` host API calls | 397 calls | 7349.7 ms | The capture confirms that checkpoint movement, rather than AdaLN projection compute, dominates an online cold miss. ## Proposed design ### GPU tier - Allocate stable GPU buffers once per worker, sized for the configured maximum request working set. - Reuse the same tensor pointers across requests to preserve CUDA graph and breakable-CUDA-graph assumptions. - Populate the buffers with the current request's complete schedule only. - Do not retain old schedules in the GPU tier after a request is admitted. The exact dynamic allocation policy still needs to account for graph capture. A first implementation may use a deployment-configured upper bound per task (`t2va`, `fl2va`, or `ref2va`) while keeping the active logical length request local. ### CPU tier - Use the complete schedule, including task/modality and exact FP32 plan bits, as the cache key. - Store the complete projected AdaLN output for that schedule in pinned CPU memory. - Bound the cache by bytes and/or number of schedules. - Use LRU eviction and expose hit, miss, admission, eviction, and transfer counters. - Copy a CPU hit into the GPU working set asynchronously before denoising. The CPU tier should cache complete schedules rather than individual plans. A partial plan hit still causes the current rebuild path to scan all AdaLN layers, so plan-level LRU would retain complexity without avoiding the expensive miss. ### Miss and admission policy - On a CPU miss, rebuild the complete schedule from checkpoint weights. - Optionally admit the resulting schedule into CPU memory only after a second use, or when the configured admission budget allows it. - If the workload has a low CPU hit rate or exceeds the CPU byte budget, fall back to online rebuild without retaining the result. - A fixed schedule can bypass the manager entirely and use a precomputed sidecar. ## Layout considerations The current GPU tensor layout is effectively `[plan, timestep, layer, feature]`. Forward accesses are layer-oriented, so slicing one layer across multiple timesteps is non-contiguous for plans longer than one timestep and can force a materialization during `reshape`. The manager should evaluate a layer-contiguous backing layout, for example `[plan, layer, timestep, feature]`, or pre-materialized request-local views. Any layout change must be checked against: - exact BF16 output equality; - TP1 and TP2 behavior; - CUDA graph pointer stability; - per-step denoising latency; - sidecar compatibility. ## Scope ### In scope - A bounded CPU pinned-memory schedule cache. - Request-local GPU working-set management. - Exact schedule key construction and collision-free lookup. - Metrics and perf-dump visibility for each tier. - TP1/TP2 accuracy and end-to-end benchmarks. ### Out of scope - Approximate timestep matching or schedule interpolation. - Changing timestep embedding math or scheduler semantics. - Changing AdaLN numerical precision or TP sharding. - Replacing the existing fixed-schedule sidecar format in the first phase. ## Acceptance criteria - A repeated schedule served from CPU backing avoids checkpoint rebuild and adds no more than 10 ms to AdaLN preparation for the measured H3 working-set sizes. - A CPU miss has the same numerical output as the existing online rebuild path. - GPU memory for an 8-step T2VA request is within the request working-set size, rather than the default 64-plan slab size. - A schedule that is not present in a sidecar fails closed with an actionable error. - Capacity eviction and failed rebuilds leave no partially published cache hit. - TP1 and TP2 outputs remain bit-identical for the audited AdaLN output set and end-to-end media checks. - CUDA graph and breakable-CUDA-graph replay continue to work with the manager enabled, or the manager explicitly disables graph replay with a documented reason. ## Suggested implementation phases 1. Refactor the cache into a request-local GPU workspace with stable pointers; retain the existing online rebuild path as the miss handler. 2. Add a standalone pinned CPU schedule store and benchmark `A -> B -> A` and high-churn sequences before integrating it into request admission. 3. Integrate CPU hits, asynchronous copies, byte-bounded LRU eviction, and metrics. 4. Benchmark the current layout against a layer-contiguous layout. 5. Add TP1/TP2 accuracy tests, sidecar compatibility tests, reset/retry tests, and end-to-end workload benchmarks. ## Open questions - Should CPU entries be shared across workers or kept per TP replica? - Should a schedule be admitted on first use or only after a second use? - What byte budget is appropriate for H200 and lower-memory deployments? - Which graph modes require a fixed maximum workspace versus an eager fallback? - Should the manager be enabled by default, or initially behind an experimental server flag?

signals.title: [Bug] /v1/responses endpoint does not support PD disaggregation
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Summary The `/v1/responses` endpoint does not support PD disaggregation. The `ResponsesRequest` protocol is missing the bootstrap and DP routing fields that `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` already include, and `serving_responses.py` does not pass these fields when constructing `GenerateReqInput`. As a result, the endpoint cannot function in any PD disaggregated deployment. ### Expected Behavior `/v1/responses` should accept and propagate the same PD disaggregation body parameters as `/v1/chat/completions`, so it can be used in PD disaggregated deployments. ### Reproduction prefill： ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 8 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend=mooncake \ --disaggregation-ib-device xx ``` decode： ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 8 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend=mooncake \ --disaggregation-ib-device xx ``` ``` curl http://<host>:<port>/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "input": "Tell me a three sentence bedtime story about a unicorn." }' ``` ### Environment sglang:v0.5.16

signals.title: [Bug] TP>1 LoRA tensor hot-load reuses one-shot ForkingPickler FDs and crashes schedulers
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug is present in the latest release source (`0.5.12.post1`). - [x] A minimal reproducible demo and environment information are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] This issue is written in English. ### Describe the bug `load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` is not safe with tensor parallelism greater than one when the payload is produced by SGLang's `MultiprocessingSerializer`. The serializer uses `ForkingPickler`, so CPU tensor storages are represented by one-shot `multiprocessing.resource_sharer` file-descriptor handles. SGLang serializes the tensor dictionary once, broadcasts the same request to every TP scheduler, and every TP worker independently deserializes the same string. The first consumer removes each handle from the resource-sharer cache; the remaining consumers raise `EOFError`. Relevant `0.5.12.post1` source: - [`Engine.load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` serializes once](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py#L1100-L1120) - [`Scheduler.recv_requests` broadcasts the same request to the TP group](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L1656-L1765) - [Every TP worker calls `MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L188-L204) - [`MultiprocessingSerializer` uses `ForkingPickler`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py#L2234-L2273) This is not a generic Python `resource_sharer` bug: its server deliberately does `self._cache.pop(key)`, so each registered FD is single-use. The issue is broadcasting one single-consumer payload to multiple consumers. Observed end-to-end with an actual SGLang server: - Qwen3-0.6B, 8x H20, `tp_size=8` - rank-16 q/k/v/o LoRA, 224 bf16 CPU tensors (8.75 MiB) - server and serializer shared the same multiprocessing parent/authkey, matching the SGLang `Engine`/embedded-server topology - the HTTP load disconnected after 222 ms - seven schedulers raised `EOFError` - SGLang then received `SIGQUIT` and the server exited - successful loads: **0/1** Using a plain pickle + base64 payload for the same tensor dictionary succeeded for load, one-token generation with the adapter, and unload: **3/3 at TP8**. At TP1, the multiprocessing path is valid and useful. In the same benchmark its warm serialization + HTTP load time was 46.31 ms versus 96.89 ms for inline pickle, so a fix should ideally preserve the optimization for the single-consumer case. ### Reproduction The following latest-release repro isolates the exact payload property used by the TP broadcast. It requires no model or GPU: ```python import multiprocessing as mp import torch from sglang.srt.utils import MultiprocessingSerializer def consume(index, payload, start, results): start.wait() try: restored = MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize(payload) results.put((index, "ok", restored["w"].numel())) except BaseException as exc: results.put((index, type(exc).__name__, str(exc))) if __name__ == "__main__": ctx = mp.get_context("spawn") tensors = {"w": torch.zeros(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16)} payload = MultiprocessingSerializer.serialize(tensors, output_str=True) start = ctx.Event() results = ctx.Queue() workers = [ ctx.Process(target=consume, args=(i, payload, start, results)) for i in range(8) ] for worker in workers: worker.start() start.set() output = sorted(results.get(timeout=30) for _ in workers) for worker in workers: worker.join() print(output) ``` On `sglang==0.5.12.post1`, the result is one success and seven failures: ```text (one worker) ok (seven workers) EOFError ``` The resource-sharer thread also prints seven instances of: ```text send, close = self._cache.pop(key) KeyError: 1 ``` Expected behavior: all eight TP workers load the adapter and the server remains healthy. Potential fixes: 1. Short-term: use an inline pickle/byte payload when `tp_size > 1`, while retaining `MultiprocessingSerializer` for TP1. 2. Performance-preserving: extend the request to carry one independently serialized payload per TP rank, so every rank receives its own FD handles. 3. Alternatively, deserialize once on the leader and explicitly broadcast/copy the tensor contents to the remaining ranks. A downstream workaround using the first approach is being developed in [Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL#227](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL/pull/227). ### Environment Latest-release serializer reproduction: ```text Python: 3.12.0 CUDA available: True GPU: 8x NVIDIA H20 (compute capability 9.0) CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: 12.9 CUDA driver: 535.247.01 PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu128 sglang: 0.5.12.post1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.1 (not used by the CPU-only reproduction) flashinfer_python: 0.6.7.post3 triton: 3.5.1 transformers: 5.3.0 numpy: 2.3.5 fastapi: 0.141.1 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 pyzmq: 27.1.0 ulimit -n: 1000000 ``` The full TP8 server reproduction used the same machine and Python environment with the image's compatible `sglang==0.5.10.post1`. Inspection of `0.5.12.post1` at commit `5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584` confirms that the serialize-once, TP-broadcast, deserialize-per-rank path remains unchanged.

signals.title: [diffusion] MiniMax H3 full-loop denoise rejects ROCm
signals.text: ## Summary MiniMax H3 full-loop denoising rejects AMD ROCm even though the path previously worked through the PyTorch CUDA-compatible ROCm interface. ## Root cause PR #33880 replaced `torch.cuda.is_available()` with: ```python current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_mps() ``` `current_platform.is_cuda()` is false on ROCm; ROCm is represented by `current_platform.is_hip()` / `is_rocm()`. The full-loop denoising stage therefore raises before generation starts. ## Reproduction The existing `minimax_h3_t2va_2gpu_h100` server E2E case reproduces this deterministically on the ROCm 2-GPU lane: - #33880 CI: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208109155/job/95935281212 - #35481 CI: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32230246742/job/96005063829 Both runs fail with: ```text MiniMax H3 full-loop denoise requires CUDA or MPS ``` The later strict-port errors are secondary failures after the first server process is not fully cleaned up. ## Expected behavior ROCm should remain admitted, matching the behavior before #33880, while MPS remains supported. ## Proposed fix and validation Include `current_platform.is_hip()` in the platform admission check and update the error message. Re-run the existing MiniMax H3 ROCm 2-GPU E2E case to validate end-to-end generation.

signals.title: [Bug] Single request with a NUL byte in `regex` segfaults the server
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug One `POST /v1/chat/completions` whose `regex` starts with a NUL byte kills the server process. The connection drops mid-request (HTTP 000, not a 5xx) and every later request from every client is refused until restart. `dispatch_regex` guards with `except RuntimeError`, which handles ordinary bad patterns — but this is a **SIGSEGV**, an OS signal below the interpreter, so no `except` can catch it. The scheduler dies with `exit code -11`. Root cause is in xgrammar: `RegexConverter`'s constructor guards on `std::string::empty()` but hands `regex_.c_str()` to `ParseUTF8`, which stops at the first NUL. A leading NUL therefore yields an empty codepoint vector and an out-of-bounds read; a later NUL silently truncates the pattern to its prefix. Two details that are easy to get wrong: 1. **Trigger is a leading NUL, not control characters generally.** `\x01`, `\x02`, `\x1f` and non-leading NUL all compile fine — a guard rejecting all control characters would break valid patterns like `[\t\n]+`. 2. **A JSON schema reaches the same converter via `pattern`**, at any nesting depth, where the NUL can be an escape (\u0000) — so the request body holds no NUL byte at all. Checking only the raw `regex` field leaves that path open. No xgrammar release fixes it: 0.2.0-0.2.4 and 0.2.6rc1 all crash on the `regex` path, and `regex_converter.cc` is unchanged from v0.2.5 through tip-of-tree. A pin bump is not a workaround. - Fix: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34679 - Same defect in vLLM, fixed the same way: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51796 - Upstream root-cause fix in xgrammar: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/pull/850 ### Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --port 30000 ``` NUL written as a JSON escape, so the payload is plain ASCII: ```bash M=Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct B='{"model":"'"$M"'","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8,' # 1. valid -> 200 curl -sS -X POST localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$B"'"regex":"[0-9]+"}' # 2. printable-invalid -> 400, server alive curl -sS -X POST localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$B"'"regex":"([a-z"}' # 3. leading NUL -> connection dropped, server dead curl -sS -X POST localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$B"'"regex":"\u0000"}' ``` Isolated to xgrammar — no GPU, model or server: ```bash python3 -c 'import xgrammar; xgrammar.Grammar.from_regex(chr(0))' # SIGSEGV ``` ### Environment Reproduced on GB200-NVL4 and GB300 (aarch64) on three images, all pinning xgrammar 0.2.1: `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly (`0.0.0.dev1`), NVIDIA DLFW sglang 26.07 (`0.5.14`) and main (`0.5.16`). `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output to be attached.

signals.title: │ DFlash2 selector crashes with quantized target lm_head (NVFP4 W4A4): RuntimeError requires dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head │
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary DFlash2 speculative decoding (`--speculative-algorithm DFLASH`) crashes on the first request when the target model has a **quantized `lm_head` (NVFP4 W4A4)**: ```text RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head. ``` This currently blocks DFlash2 from being used with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`. ## Environment * **SGLang:** main @ `c14312a66420b75ca9a11bf1817c4db1fa26b097` (PR #35371) * **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` * **GPU:** RTX PRO 6000 96GB, SM120, CUDA 13.0.3 * **Target:** `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` * MLP + `lm_head`: dynamic NVFP4 W4A4, group size 16 * Attention weights: FP8 * **Draft:** `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` * **TP:** 1 * **Draft tokens:** 8 ## Reproduction ```bash docker run --gpus all lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \ --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 \ --tp 1 ``` The server starts successfully and the DFlash2 draft runner initializes correctly, but the **first `/v1/chat/completions` request crashes**. ## Root Cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py`, `compute_candidates` directly requires the target `lm_head` to be dense FP16/BF16/FP32. This is separate from `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head`, which already supports quantized heads through: ```python lm_head.quant_method.apply(...) ``` DFlash2's selector does not use that path. This also explains why **DSpark works with the same NVFP4 target**: DSpark has its own dense `lm_head`, while DFlash2 borrows the target model's `lm_head`. So this is not a simple `DSpark → DFlash2` configuration change. ## What I Tried I ported the quantized-head selector approach from: https://github.com/r0b0tlab/qwen38-27b-nvfp4-sm121-sglang Their patch replaces the unconditional `raise` with a chunked `lm_head.quant_method.apply(...)` path. That approach reportedly works with their **W4A16** NVFP4 checkpoint. However, with the **RadixArk W4A4** checkpoint, the patch still fails. The W4A4 activation quantization in the `lm_head` appears to prevent the same `quant_method.apply` path from working, but I have not narrowed down the exact failure yet. ## Questions 1. Is a **W4A4 quantized `lm_head`** intended to be supported by the DFlash2 selector? 2. If yes, does the selector need a dedicated W4A4 dequantization/quantized matmul path? 3. If no, should the RuntimeError explicitly state that DFlash2 requires a dense target `lm_head`? 4. Should the DFlash2 documentation/model compatibility requirements explicitly mention this limitation? ## Related * DFlash2 merge: #35371 * Working W4A16 patch: https://github.com/r0b0tlab/qwen38-27b-nvfp4-sm121-sglang * vLLM DFlash2 PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52816 ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: `batch_is_full` latched during final chunked-prefill pass starves waiting queue until a running request finishes (self-healing variant of #28530 / #22518)
signals.text: ## Summary With `--max-running-requests 4` and chunked prefill enabled, 4 concurrent cold prompts result in only 3 running requests; the 4th waits in the queue until one of the running requests **finishes decoding entirely**, even though all resource pools are nearly empty. Root cause: `running_batch.batch_is_full` is latched `True` during the final chunked-prefill pass and is never re-evaluated on the steady-state decode path. This is the same stale-flag family as #28530 and #22518 (and the ordering issue in #14872), but triggered by a different, much more common path: **normal generation traffic with chunked prefill**. Unlike #28530 it does not permanently deadlock — it self-heals when a running request completes — so it presents as a latency / throughput cliff rather than a hang, which is likely why it hasn't been reported. ## Environment - sglang v0.5.17 (`lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image, pulled 2026-08) - Model: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (hybrid GDN / linear-attention architecture), `--trust-remote-code` - Single GPU, Docker (WSL2 backend) - Relevant flags: ``` --max-running-requests 4 --cuda-graph-max-bs 4 --max-mamba-cache-size 24 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --context-length 262144 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph ``` ## Symptom 4 concurrent requests with unique ~3100-token prompts (staggered 0/0.2/0.4/0.8s): - **Observed**: 3 requests run, the 4th stays in the waiting queue. Decode-phase queue events show it is only admitted after one of the 3 finishes. In the original production-like scenario (longer prompts), the queued request waited **~4.5 minutes** while the server was otherwise idle-capable. - **Resource headroom at the moment of starvation**: KV pool 382,958 tokens with ≤4% used; mamba state pool 16/24 slots used. No limit is anywhere near reached. - **Self-healing**: as soon as one running request completes its decode, the queued request is admitted immediately — no restart needed (unlike #28530). ## Root cause In `Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw()` (v0.5.17, `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`): 1. During the pass where the last chunked-prefill continuation finishes, the in-flight `chunked_req` occupies the last allocatable slot, so one of the admission paths (in our trace L3204: `len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs)`) sets `running_batch.batch_is_full = True`. 2. The batch then transitions to steady-state decode. On the decode path, `batch_is_full` is only reset when the batch shrinks / becomes empty / retracts — none of which happens while all requests are mid-decode. 3. Every subsequent scheduler pass hits the early return (`if (running_batch.batch_is_full or len(self.waiting_queue) == 0) and self.chunked_req is None`), so the waiting queue is starved until a running request finishes and the batch rebuild path finally clears the flag. I diffed v0.5.17 against `main` (fetched 2026-08-19): all 14 read/write sites of `batch_is_full` are equivalent — the bug is still present on main. ## Minimal reproduction ```python import concurrent.futures as cf, random, string, time, urllib.request, json URL = "http://localhost:8004/v1/chat/completions" # server port MODEL = "Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4" # any model + chunked prefill should work def rand_text(n): return "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " ", k=n)) def call(idx, delay): time.sleep(delay) t0 = time.time() prompt = f"[{time.time()}-{idx}] " + rand_text(4200) + "\nSummarize the above." body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": 400, "temperature": 0.7, "stream": False} req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r: resp = json.load(r) print(f"req{idx}: total={time.time()-t0:.1f}s usage={resp.get('usage')}", flush=True) if __name__ == "__main__": with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex: list(ex.map(call, range(4), [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8])) ``` Expected: 4 requests admitted (4 slots available, ~3100-token prompts each needing 2 chunked passes at 2048). Observed: 3 admitted, 1 queued until first completion. ## Proposed fix Re-evaluate fullness at the top of every `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw()` pass: ```python # FIX(qwen38-queue-starvation): batch_is_full can be latched True during # the final chunked-prefill pass (the in-flight chunked continuation # occupies the last allocatable slot) and is never reset on the decode # path, starving waiting requests until a running request finishes. # Re-evaluate fullness every pass; the allocatable-reqs guard below and # the budget gates in add_one_req still protect all real resources. running_batch.batch_is_full = False ``` placed immediately before the early-return check: ```python if ( running_batch.batch_is_full or len(self.waiting_queue) == 0 ) and self.chunked_req is None: ``` Rationale: `batch_is_full` is a per-pass admission hint, but it is persisted on the long-lived `ScheduleBatch` object, so a stale value survives across scheduler passes. The flag is re-derived inside the pass anyway (L3138 / L3204 / L3209 / L3246), and `PrefillAdder` budget gates enforce all real resource limits, so an unconditional reset cannot over-admit. ## Verification (same repro script) - Before: 3 running + 1 queued; 4th request delayed ~4s in the minimal repro (~4.5 min in the original longer-prompt scenario). - After: all 4 requests admitted immediately, completed uniformly in 8.3–9.2s, **zero** decode-phase queue events. - No regression observed in mixed prefill/decode steady state over extended runs. ## Related - #28530 — NO_TOKEN rejection latches `batch_is_full`, permanent deadlock (page_size > 1) - #22518 — embedding server deadlock, stale `batch_is_full` after first full batch - #14872 — NO_TOKEN set after preemption check, preemption never triggers All share the same underlying defect: `batch_is_full` is sticky state with incomplete reset coverage. A per-pass re-evaluation fixes this whole family of triggers; alternatively each set site could be paired with a guaranteed reset, but that is more invasive.
