signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash expert parallelism (DeepEP) crashes on Hopper/SM90 — DeepGEMM MXFP4 MegaMoE is SM100-only; late failure + misleading error
signals.text: ## Summary Serving the **stock (MXFP4-expert) `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`** with **expert parallelism** (`--enable-expert-parallel` / `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`) crashes on **Hopper (SM90)**. It fails late — after a full weight load + MHC prewarm + at **decode CUDA-graph capture** — inside DeepGEMM's MXFP4 grouped GEMM, which asserts SM100: ``` Capture cuda graph failed: Assertion error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:57): ab.scalar_type() == kPackedFP4 and arch_major == 10 ``` `arch_major == 10` is SM100 (Blackwell). On SM90 the scheduler then dies (`Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization`). This is the same failure as the (still-unanswered) discussion #26564 — reported there on H20, sglang 0.5.12 / DeepEP 1.2.1. Filing as an issue because there's clearly standing demand and no tracking issue. ## Environment / reproduce - **Ours:** `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.15.post1`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (stock MXFP4 experts), 4×H100 (SM90), `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Weights load fine (`quant=fp8, fmt=e4m3`), MHC prewarm completes, then the crash above at decode-graph capture. CrashLoops indefinitely. - **#26564:** H20 (SM90), sglang 0.5.12, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto` — identical assertion. Full traceback path: `scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs → tp_worker.init_cuda_graphs → model_runner.init_decode_cuda_graph → decode_cuda_graph_runner.__init__ → capture → DeepGEMM fp8_paged_mqa/MegaMoE layout.hpp:57`. ## Root cause The EP path (DeepEP a2a) routes expert compute to **DeepGEMM's packed-FP4 MegaMoE** grouped GEMM, and that kernel is built for **SM100 only** (Blackwell has native FP4 tensor cores; Hopper does not). The **TP path avoids this** because it resolves MXFP4 experts to **Marlin**, which dequantizes 4-bit → bf16 in-kernel and runs on SM80/SM90 tensor cores — which is exactly why the current DeepSeek-V4 Hopper cookbook recipe is TP-only. So MXFP4 **expert parallelism is implicitly Blackwell-only** today, with no explicit guard. For reference, vLLM's default single-node EP keeps the MXFP4 experts on **Marlin** (all-gather/reduce-scatter around the same Marlin GEMM) and therefore runs this checkpoint under EP on H100. ## Two UX problems 1. **Fails ~8 min in, not at startup.** The incompatibility is knowable from `(device SM) + (MXFP4 experts) + (EP enabled)` before any weights load, but the error only surfaces at graph capture. 2. **The printed remediations are misleading.** "lower `--mem-fraction-static`", "reduce `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`", "disable decode CUDA graph" — none address an *architecture* requirement. Disabling the graph just relocates the same SM100-only kernel to eager decode. ## Working alternatives on Hopper today (for anyone stuck now, incl. #26564) - **EP:** use the FP8-converted checkpoint `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8` with `--enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend deepep`. FP8 grouped GEMM is Hopper-native; we've run TP8/DP8/EP8 + DeepEP-auto on 8×H100 with zero errors. - **Stock MXFP4:** run **TP + Marlin** (no EP) — the documented Hopper cookbook recipe. ## Proposed fixes 1. **Interim — fail fast.** At startup, when `SM < 100` **and** experts are packed-FP4 **and** EP/DeepEP is requested, raise a clear error naming the two alternatives above, instead of crashing at graph capture with arch-agnostic tuning hints. 2. **Real support — Hopper MXFP4 EP.** Route the DeepEP-dispatched grouped expert batches through a Hopper-capable MXFP4 grouped GEMM (**Marlin**, already used on the TP path, or the FlashInfer mxfp4 path from #24816) instead of DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE. Caveat: SM90 has no native FP4, so this is dequant-to-bf16 compute — a memory-footprint win, not FP4 throughput. Happy to contribute the fail-fast guard (#1) and to help wire the Marlin EP path (#2) — would appreciate a pointer on where the MoE-runner / DeepEP dispatch should select the Hopper kernel.

signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Start a server with the llama3 tool-call parser: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \ --tool-call-parser llama3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` Send a `/v1/chat/completions` request that has `tools`. ``` input = '{}' -> content = '' (the message is gone) input = '{"a": 1} is a dict' -> content = 'is a dict' (the leading JSON is gone) ``` **Expected:** if the parser finds no tool call, it must not change the text. The bug shows without a GPU or a server. The bug is in the parser class. ### Reproduction ```python # pip install "sglang[all]==0.5.17" — no GPU or server needed from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="get_weather", parameters={}))] parser = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum["llama3"]() result = parser.detect_and_parse('{"a": 1} is a dict', tools) print(repr(result.normal_text), result.calls) # 'is a dict' [] — {"a": 1} silently deleted assert result.normal_text == '{"a": 1} is a dict', "leading JSON dropped from content" ``` ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:18:55) [Clang 22.1.3 ] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.173.02 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.28.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.4 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.14.0 anthropic: 0.124.0 ```

signals.title: [Bug] deepseekv32/deepseekv4 tool-call parsers drop calls when the streamed output has two chunks
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Use the `deepseekv32` or `deepseekv4` parser with streaming on. ``` deepseekv32 non-streaming: 3 calls {0: search {}, 1: run_query {}, 2: get_weather {"city": -7}} deepseekv32 2-chunk stream: 1 call {2: ['', '{"city": -7}']} # 2 calls and the names are gone deepseekv4 non-streaming: 2 calls {0: get_weather {"city": 42}, 1: get_weather {"city": -7}} deepseekv4 2-chunk stream: 1 call {1: ['', '{"city": -7}']} # 1 call and the name are gone ``` The non-streaming `detect_and_parse` on the same text is correct. Thus streaming clients and non-streaming clients get different tool calls. **Expected:** each division of the same text must give the calls that `detect_and_parse` gives. ### Reproduction
reproduce_deepseek_dsml_two_chunk.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """deepseekv32 / deepseekv4 detectors: splitting the model output into just TWO streaming chunks makes earlier tool calls disappear from the stream. The split point is inside the number "-7" ("-" | "7") — a perfectly normal token boundary — so any real streamed generation can hit it. pip install "sglang[all]==0.5.17" (CPU is enough) python reproduce_deepseek_dsml_two_chunk.py # exit 1 = bug present """ import json import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser def tool(name): return Tool(type="function", function=Function( name=name, parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}})) TOOLS = [tool("get_weather"), tool("search"), tool("run_query")] CASES = { # three calls; the last one has an argument whose value "-7" straddles # the chunk boundary "deepseekv32": ( '<｜DSML｜function_calls>' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="search">' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="run_query">' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">-7' '', 189, ), # two calls; same "-7" straddle in the second one "deepseekv4": ( '<｜DSML｜tool_calls>' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">42' '' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">-7' '', 208, ), } def stream(name, chunks): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() calls = {} for chunk in list(chunks) + ["", ""]: # trailing flushes, as serving does r = d.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, TOOLS) for c in r.calls: e = calls.setdefault(c.tool_index, ["", ""]) if c.name: e[0] = c.name if c.parameters: e[1] += c.parameters return calls bad = 0 for name, (text, cut) in CASES.items(): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() final = {i: [c.name, c.parameters] for i, c in enumerate(d.detect_and_parse(text, TOOLS).calls)} streamed = stream(name, [text[:cut], text[cut:]]) print(f"{name}: split {text[cut-2:cut]!r} | {text[cut:cut+2]!r}") print(f" non-streaming: {len(final)} calls {final}") print(f" 2-chunk stream: {len(streamed)} calls {streamed}") same = len(streamed) == len(final) and all( streamed.get(i, ["", ""])[0] == final[i][0] and json.loads(streamed.get(i, ["", "null"])[1] or "null") == json.loads(final[i][1] or "null") for i in final) if not same: bad += 1 print(" BUG: streaming lost tool calls vs non-streaming\n") raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0) ```
### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:18:55) [Clang 22.1.3 ] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.173.02 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.28.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.4 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.14.0 anthropic: 0.124.0 ```

signals.title: [Bug]  8 tool-call parsers give wrong or missing calls in token-by-token streaming
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Use one of these parsers with streaming on: `cohere_command4, gemma4, glm, glm45, glm47, minimax-m2, mistral, step3`. Let the output have a call with empty `{}` (or very simple) arguments. Give the text to `parse_streaming_increment` one character at a time. Then compare the result with `detect_and_parse` on the same text. The results do not agree. These are the failure modes: ``` minimax-m2 final: {0: get_weather {}} streamed: {} # the call is gone mistral final: {0: gw {}, 1: gw {}} streamed: {0: gw {}} # the 2nd call is gone cohere_command4 / gemma4: the call gets tool_index=1, not 0 # index shift glm / glm45 / glm47: {"get_weather": 123} streams as {"get_weather": "123"} # int -> str step3 final: 1 call with args streamed: one more call, with empty args ``` Each marker is one token in the applicable model vocabulary. Thus real detokenized streaming makes these increments. This is not an unusual mid-marker division. **Expected:** the sum of the streamed deltas must be equal to the `detect_and_parse` result. Note: vLLM had the same bug class in its xlam / hunyuan_a13b parsers. Some of these sglang parsers are ports of vLLM parsers. ### Reproduction
reproduce_streaming_empty_args.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """8 tool-call detectors lose arguments (or whole calls) when the output is streamed token-by-token, whenever a call with empty/simple arguments is involved. Non-streaming detect_and_parse on the same text is correct. pip install "sglang[all]==0.5.17" (CPU is enough) python reproduce_streaming_empty_args.py # exit 1 = bug present """ import json import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser def tool(name): return Tool(type="function", function=Function( name=name, parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}})) TOOLS = [tool("get_weather"), tool("f")] CASES = { "cohere_command4": '<|START_ACTION|>[{"tool_name": "f", "parameters": {}}]<|END_ACTION|>', "gemma4": "<|tool_call>call:f{}", "glm": "get_weather get_weather " "123 ", "glm45": "get_weather get_weather " "123 ", "glm47": "get_weatherget_weather" "123", "minimax-m2": '' "", "mistral": '[TOOL_CALLS] [{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {}}, ' '{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {}}]', "step3": "<｜tool_calls_begin｜><｜tool_call_begin｜>function<｜tool_sep｜>" '' "<｜tool_call_end｜><｜tool_call_begin｜>function<｜tool_sep｜>" '' 'hello' "<｜tool_call_end｜><｜tool_calls_end｜>", } def stream(name, chunks): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() calls = {} for chunk in list(chunks) + ["", ""]: # trailing flushes, as serving does r = d.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, TOOLS) for c in r.calls: e = calls.setdefault(c.tool_index, ["", ""]) if c.name: e[0] = c.name if c.parameters: e[1] += c.parameters return calls def jeq(a, b): try: return json.loads(a or "null") == json.loads(b or "null") except Exception: return a == b bad = 0 for name, text in CASES.items(): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() final = {i: [c.name, c.parameters] for i, c in enumerate(d.detect_and_parse(text, TOOLS).calls)} streamed = stream(name, list(text)) # one character per increment same = len(streamed) == len(final) and all( streamed.get(i, ["", ""])[0] == final[i][0] and jeq(streamed.get(i, ["", ""])[1], final[i][1]) for i in final) tag = "OK " if same else "BUG" print(f"{tag} {name:16s} final={final}") if not same: print(f" streamed={streamed}") bad += 1 raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0) ```
### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:18:55) [Clang 22.1.3 ] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.173.02 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.28.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.4 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.14.0 anthropic: 0.124.0 ```

signals.title: [Bug] 13 tool-call parsers silently delete the message when generation stops at a tool-call open marker
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Set tools on with one of these parsers: `cohere_command4, deepseekv3, deepseekv31, glm, glm45, hermes, hunyuan, lfm2, mimo, mistral, poolside_v1, qwen3_coder, step3p5`. Let the generation stop immediately after the tool-call open marker. This occurs when the output gets to `max_tokens`. Then `detect_and_parse` gives `normal_text=''` and zero calls. The client gets an empty message with `finish_reason='length'`. The client gets no signal about the tool call. The worst case is mistral. It removes `[TOOL_CALLS` — this is only a **part** of the marker. Thus usual text that contains `[TOOL_CALLS` can also become empty: ``` '[TOOL_CALLS' -> '' (mistral — only a part of the marker) '' -> '' (glm, glm45, hermes, mimo, poolside_v1, qwen3_coder, step3p5) '<|START_ACTION|>' -> '' (cohere_command4) '<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>' -> '' (deepseekv3, deepseekv31) '' -> '' (hunyuan) '<|tool_call_start|>' -> '' (lfm2) ``` **Expected:** keep the text in `normal_text`, or show the incomplete-call condition. An empty message with no signal loses data. **Related vLLM issue:** vLLM had the same bug class in its ernie45 parser: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47903. ### Reproduction
reproduce_bare_marker_text_drop.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """13 sglang tool-call detectors silently delete the visible text when the output ends with a bare tool-call open marker and nothing else — exactly what a max_tokens truncation mid-call produces. detect_and_parse returns normal_text='' and no calls. For mistral, even a PARTIAL marker ('[TOOL_CALLS') vanishes. The same bug class is live in vLLM 0.24.0 (glm47, qwen3_coder, qwen3_xml, step3p5) — several of these parsers are ports of the same code. sglang side: pip install "sglang[all]==0.5.17" (CPU is enough) python reproduce_bare_marker_text_drop.py sglang vllm side: pip install "vllm==0.24.0" python reproduce_bare_marker_text_drop.py vllm Exit 1 = bug present. """ import sys import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "sglang" bad = 0 if mode == "sglang": from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser TOOLS = [Tool(type="function", function=Function( name="get_weather", parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}}))] CASES = { "mistral": "[TOOL_CALLS", # note: not even a complete marker "cohere_command4": "<|START_ACTION|>", "deepseekv3": "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>", "deepseekv31": "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>", "glm": "", "glm45": "", "hermes": "", "hunyuan": "", "lfm2": "<|tool_call_start|>", "mimo": "", "poolside_v1": "", "qwen3_coder": "", "step3p5": "", } for name, text in CASES.items(): res = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]().detect_and_parse( text, TOOLS) lost = not res.calls and res.normal_text.strip() != text.strip() tag = "BUG" if lost else "OK " print(f"{tag} {name:16s} input={text!r:26s} -> " f"normal_text={res.normal_text!r} calls={len(res.calls)}") bad += lost else: from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ( ChatCompletionRequest, ) from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") tools = [{"type": "function", "function": { "name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}] req = ChatCompletionRequest( model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], tools=tools) for name in ("glm47", "qwen3_coder", "qwen3_xml", "step3p5"): cls = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser(name) try: parser = cls(tok, req.tools) except TypeError: parser = cls(tok) res = parser.extract_tool_calls("", req) lost = not res.tools_called and (res.content or "") != "" tag = "BUG" if lost else "OK " print(f"{tag} vllm {name:12s} input='' -> " f"content={res.content!r} tools_called={res.tools_called}") bad += lost raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0) ```

signals.title: Qwen-VL: literal vision marker in text is parsed as extra image when request contains an image
signals.text: ### Reproduction A Qwen-VL chat request containing one valid image_url part and ordinary text containing the literal Qwen sequence `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` returns HTTP 500. The text is harmless in a text-only request because the multimodal processor is not invoked. Once any real image exists, `legacy_load_mm_data()` regex-scans the fully rendered prompt and cannot distinguish a marker emitted by the chat template from the same sequence supplied inside a text or tool-result block. ### Expected behavior Text and tool output should be allowed to contain Qwen special-token spellings without being treated as another attachment. At minimum this should be a client error, rather than a 500. ### Environment - SGLang 0.5.16 - Qwen3.8-27B - OpenAI-compatible chat completions I have a minimal local reproduction and am preparing a regression PR.

signals.title: [Bug] ROCm images pin AITER below the FlyDSL MXFP4 MoE kernels, making tuned AITER_CONFIG_FMOE tables unusable on gfx950
signals.text: ### Summary `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` pins `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT=d9e5ef7ce08ee7045d583aed768cff41aa9210fe` (ROCm/aiter, **2026-07-29**) for all four arch stages. That pin predates ROCm/aiter [`db24351e` — "[fmoe][gfx950] Flydsl mxmoe v2" (#4179), **2026-08-04**](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/db24351e), which introduces the `flydsl_mxmoe_*` / `flydsl_moe2_layout_*` FlyDSL MXFP4 fused-MoE kernel families. Consequence on gfx950: **SGLang cannot consume an AITER-tuned MXFP4 fused-MoE table** (`AITER_CONFIG_FMOE`), and cannot produce one either, so the tuned-MoE kernel-selection path is unavailable on published ROCm images. ### Repro Load any `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` table tuned with AITER ≥ `db24351e` (rows naming `flydsl_mxmoe_*` kernels) — the scheduler dies at model load on every TP rank: ``` ValueError: Invalid FlyDSL kernel name: flydsl_mxmoe_g1_a4w4_16x256x256_f16in_nt ``` raised from `aiter/fused_moe.py` after `aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_kernels.get_flydsl_kernel_params()` returns `None`. Probing the registry inside the published images confirms the cause is the pin, not the table. Model GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, gfx950 (MI350X); 4 distinct kernel names in the table: | image | published | bundled AITER | FlyDSL registry size | table's kernels resolved | `--mxfp4-flydsl` tuner mode | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---| | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x` | 2026-07-24 | `9127c94a` (06-25) | 3393 | **0 / 4** | no | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x` | 2026-08-08 | `d9e5ef7c` (07-29) | 4257 | **0 / 4** | no | Both registries contain only the older `flydsl_moe1_*` / `flydsl_moe2_*` families (1057 of them `afp4_wfp4` in v0.5.16) — **zero** entries matching `mxmoe`, `a4w4`, or `layout`. Note v0.5.17's *image* was published four days **after** the floor commit while its *AITER pin* is six days before it, so the image tag date is not a reliable proxy here. Retuning locally is not a workaround: the bundled `csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py` at this pin has no MXFP4-FlyDSL mode (`--grouped-gemm` is gfx1250-only), so `--mxfp4-flydsl` is rejected with `unrecognized arguments`. ### Impact On MI350X/gfx950 with GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (TP4), the tuned MXFP4 MoE table measured **+7.5–12.9% end-to-end output throughput at concurrency 16–64** on an engine that can load it (kernel-level: +21.6% at M=32, +19.1% at M=16, +7.7% at M=1; 6 of 11 shapes improved past a 3% gate). That gain is currently unreachable from any published SGLang ROCm image. ### Suggested fix Bump `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` to a commit ≥ `db24351e` (or current AITER main) — at minimum for the `gfx950` / `gfx950-rocm720` stages. This follows the existing routine-bump precedent (#28248, #28249, #27555, #27376). Users can already work around it today via the documented build arg (thanks to #21949): ```bash docker build -f docker/rocm.Dockerfile --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm720 \ --build-arg AITER_COMMIT=<commit ≥ db24351e> . ``` Happy to submit the bump PR if a maintainer confirms which AITER commit you'd like to land on — I have a gfx950 (MI350X) node and can validate GLM-5.2-MXFP4 TP4 serving plus the tuned-table load before opening it. ### Environment - 8× MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, TP4 - Model: GLM-5.2-MXFP4 - Images as tabled above; probe via `aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_kernels.get_flydsl_kernel_params(name) is not None`

signals.title: [Feature]Introduce DeepEP's Per-Expert-overlap(PEO) capability into SGLang.
signals.text: ## Motivation Current Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models face a bottleneck in large-scale inference due to the sequential execution of communication and computation, especially under small batch sizes where the All-to-All communications in the dispatch and combine phases become performance bottlenecks. To overcome these limitations, we introduce PEO ([Per-Expert-Overlap](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/492) by grouping experts at the DeepEP layer and scheduling communication and computation across multiple rounds, PEO naturally overlaps the communication of some experts with the GEMM computations of others, significantly improving throughput. ## Modifications - Added implementation of per-expert overlap; - Introduced overlap methods 1 through 4; ## Purpose - Achieve communication-computation overlap solely by adjusting the DeepEP scheduling logic, without modifying the GEMM interface; - Support configurable overlap strategies (overlap-1 through overlap-4) to accommodate varying model scales, batch sizes, and deployment environments; ## Implementation Details + **Expert Grouping**: The `num_local_experts` are divided into `num_rounds` groups, each containing `num_local_experts // num_rounds` experts. + **Phased Scheduling**: - _Dispatch Phase_: In each round, tokens are sent to `num_experts // num_rounds` target experts. - _GEMM Phase_: Upon receiving tokens for a given group, the GEMM computation for that expert group is triggered immediately. - _Combine Phase_: Results are aggregated group-by-group and sent back to the corresponding ranks. + **Overlap Strategy Support**: The scheduling mode is dynamically selected via the `overlap_method` parameter: - `overlap-1`: Complete all sends before performing receives and GEMM; - `overlap-2`: Perform receive + GEMM immediately after each round’s send; - `overlap-3`: Enable concurrent internal send/recv within DeepEP on top of `overlap-2`; - `overlap-4`: Disable overlap entirely (used as a baseline for comparison). + **Compatibility**: Only the DeepEP scheduler is modified; the inference engine and DeepGEMM remain untouched, preserving all existing APIs. ## Dependencies + Per-Expert-Overlap, [https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/492](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/492) ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process) ## Accuracy Tests - origin - PEO ## Performance ### Configuration: H20, EP16, QWEN, DPSK, intput=128, output=1536 ## Repro Script ``` export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=128; export SGLANG_LOCAL_IP_NIC=eth0; export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=/sgl-workspace/profiler; export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0 9.0a" python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /sgl-workspace/models/DeepSeek-R1-0528 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 6178 \ --tp 16 \ --dp 16 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --trust-remote-code \ --disable-radix-cache \ --max-running-requests 2048 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --deepep-mode low_latency \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 \ --dist-init-addr 172.18.0.xx:5757 \ --nnodes 2 \ --stream-output \ --node-rank 0 \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --decode-log-interval 2 \ --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \ --context-length 5000 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --ep-dispatch-algorithm fake \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --stream-out \ --cuda-graph-bs 4 8 16 24 32 64 128 \ --enable-per-expert-overlap \ --peo-overlap-method=3 \ --peo-num-rounds=4 \ --peo-deepep-num-sms=14 \ --peo-up-deepgemm-num-sms=70 \ --peo-down-deepgemm-num-sms=78 ```

signals.title: feat: add prefill_data_parallel_rank for external dp dispatch in P/D disaggregation
signals.text: ## Motivation Currently, the `data_parallel_rank` field in the request body sent to the Decode instance is **overloaded with a dual purpose**: 1. It identifies the **Decode instance's own DP group** (Self-Identity). 2. It implicitly specifies the **target Prefill DP group** to connect to for KV cache transfer (Target-Binding). This coupling forces the Prefill and Decode instances to share the exact same DP rank. It makes it impossible to schedule a request to a Decode instance in DP group `i` while fetching KV cache from a Prefill instance in DP group `j` (where `i != j`), limiting the flexibility of external schedulers. ## Modifications - **Interface Protocol**: - Added an optional field `prefill_data_parallel_rank` to the request interface. - **Logic in P/D disaggregation**: - **Decode Dispatch**: The request is still routed to the specific Decode DP group based on the existing `data_parallel_rank`. - **KV Cache Connection**: When running in **Prefill/Decode (P/D) disaggregation mode**, the Decode instance now uses `prefill_data_parallel_rank` to explicitly identify and connect to the target Prefill DP group. ## Accuracy Tests ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signals.title: [Speculative] Add heterogeneous vocabulary support for standalone speculative decoding
signals.text: Enable draft models with different vocabularies in speculative decoding. Implements ICML 2025 paper "Lossless Speculative Decoding for Heterogeneous Vocabularies". ## Motivation Currently, SGLang's speculative decoding requires the draft model and target model to share the same vocabulary. This limits users to using only matched model pairs (e.g., LLaMA draft for LLaMA target). This PR implements the TLI (Token-Level Intersection) algorithm from the ICML 2025 Oral paper ["Lossless Speculative Decoding for Heterogeneous Vocabularies"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05202) to remove this constraint. **Algorithm:** 1. Compute vocabulary intersection between draft and target tokenizers 2. Mask draft logits to restrict sampling to intersection tokens 3. Map draft token IDs to target vocab space during verification ## Modifications - **New file**: `python/sglang/srt/speculative/vocab_intersection.py` - `VocabIntersectionMapper` class for vocabulary intersection management - `create_vocab_mapper()` factory function - **Modified files**: - `server_args.py`: Add `--enable-heterogeneous-vocab` flag - `standalone_worker.py`: Initialize vocab mapper when enabled - `eagle_worker.py`: Apply logits masking in draft forward - `eagle_info.py`: Map draft tokens to target vocab in verification - `multi_layer_eagle_worker.py`: Add vocab_mapper attribute for consistency **Usage:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --speculative-algorithm STANDALONE \ --speculative-draft-model-path Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B \ --enable-heterogeneous-vocab ``` ## Accuracy Tests N/A - This is a compatibility feature. The TLI algorithm is mathematically lossless (output distribution identical to target model). Feature is opt-in and does not affect existing behavior when disabled. ## Benchmarking and Profiling N/A - This enables new use cases (heterogeneous vocab pairs) rather than optimizing existing ones. Performance depends on vocabulary intersection size between chosen model pairs. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## References - Paper: [Lossless Speculative Decoding for Heterogeneous Vocabularies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05202) (ICML 2025 Oral) - HuggingFace: [Universal Assisted Generation](https://huggingface.co/blog/universal_assisted_generation) (Transformers 4.50.0)

signals.title: [smg] Fix Content-Type header for models and server info endpoints (#8887)
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a recurring issue where the router returns `Content-Type: text/plain` for JSON endpoints like `/v1/models`. This causes failures in strict clients, most notably Open WebUI, which fails to parse the model list if the media type is incorrect. See Open WebUI logs below: ``` 2026-01-20 07:39:02.077 | ERROR | open_webui.routers.openai:send_get_request:86 - Connection error: 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: text/plain; charset=utf-8', url='http://10.0.0.136:8000/v1/models' 2026-01-20 07:39:02.077 | INFO | uvicorn.protocols.http.httptools_impl:send:483 - 172.17.0.1:39010 - "GET /api/models HTTP/1.1" 200 ``` Previously, in #9236, the Gateway relied on faithfully forwarding headers from upstream workers to maintain transparency. However, this trust-based approach is insufficient because it cannot guarantee API compliance when upstream behaviors vary. Since the Gateway explicitly defines these API endpoints (`/v1/models`, `/get_model_info`), it bears the ultimate responsibility for enforcing the API specification. Fixes #8887. Related to #3307 #6237 ## Modifications - **New Middleware**: Implemented `ensure_json_content_type` in `sgl-model-gateway/src/middleware.rs`. This middleware checks if a response is successful and forces the `Content-Type` header to `application/json`. - **Router Update**: Applied this middleware in `sgl-model-gateway/src/server.rs` to the following endpoints: - `/v1/models` - `/get_model_info` - `/get_server_info` - **Testing**: - Updated the file `sgl-model-gateway/tests/api/api_endpoints_test.rs`: 1. Added a regression test `test_pd_mode_content_type` to verify that these endpoints correctly return `application/json` headers. 2. Added `test_error_content_type_on_model_and_server_info_endpoints` to verify that error responses from these endpoints also return `application/json`. 3. Updated existing tests for `/v1/models`, `/get_model_info`, and `/get_server_info` to explicitly verify the `Content-Type` header is correct. - Brought the system up and tested the responses with `curl`: 1. Launch the prefill worker: ```bash uv run python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --port 8001 --host 0.0.0.0 ``` 2. Launch the decode worker: ```bash uv run python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --port 8002 --host 0.0.0.0 ``` 4. Launch the router: ```bash uv run python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://localhost:8001 \ --decode http://localhost:8002 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 ``` 5. Verify the Content-Type for the endpoints: ```bash ❯ curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models | grep -i "^Content-Type:" content-type: application/json ❯ curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8000/get_model_info | grep -i "^Content-Type:" content-type: application/json ❯ curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8000/get_server_info | grep -i "^Content-Type:" content-type: application/json ``` 6. Open WebUI correctly identifies the model: ## Accuracy Tests N/A - This change only affects HTTP response metadata (headers) and does not impact model outputs or inference logic. ## Benchmarking and Profiling N/A - The middleware introduces negligible overhead (header insertion) and does not affect the inference critical path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: fix: avoid EOS token exposure by reordering length check
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Fix EOS token exposure caused by max-length check ordering In the current implementation, the **max-length check** is performed before the **EOS token match check**. This leads to a corner case where the EOS token is generated as the final token exactly when the maximum length is reached. In this scenario, the request hits the length check first and its finish reason is incorrectly set to `"length"` instead of `"matched_token"`. As a result, the EOS token is not trimmed by `trim_matched_stop` and is unexpectedly streamed to the caller.

signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Support [NVIDIA Fast-dLLM-v2](https://huggingface.co/Efficient-Large-Model/Fast_dLLM_v2_7B) with HierarchyBlock algorithm. We would like to make the Fast-dLLM-v2 the standard for integrating new dLLMs and their corresponding algorithms, especially to show: - How do we implement the algorithms without aggressively changing the systems? - How do we test the models and decoding algorithms? ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Init NVIDIA Fast-dLLM-v2 with full logits. - Init HierarchyBlock algorithm for parallel generation. - Add two tests for Fast-dLLM-v2 in GSM8k and HierarchyBlock[to improve the accuracy]. - [Todo] support batching when rebase with the newest version after this PR: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14883 Next steps: - Update HF implementation of Fast-dLLM-v2 with standard ModelOutput including logits and hidden for unit tests. @Hills-code - Figure out the logits differences that come from in SGLang Fast-dLLM-v2, compared with the HF implementation. - Support batching for the HierarchyBlock algorithm. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Right now, MoE distribution logs in SGLang capture expert routing information, but they lack a stable identifier that links recorded distributions back to the originating request. ``` ## Root Cause In the function call detector, when the function name and arguments appear together in the first streaming chunk, the `else` condition causes the argument processing logic to be skipped. This results in returning an empty arguments object `{}` instead of the actual parameters. The problematic code flow: 1. First chunk contains both function name and arguments 2. Code enters the "new function call" branch and creates a tool call with empty arguments 3. The `else` block that processes arguments is never reached 4. Subsequent chunks try to append to empty arguments, but the initial data is lost ## Solution Replace the `else` condition with an explicit `if func_args_raw` check. This ensures arguments are processed both when they appear in the first call and in subsequent calls. **Changes:** - `python/sglang/srt/function_call/deepseekv31_detector.py` **After fix:** Streaming mode now correctly returns `{"city": "上海"}` in tool call arguments, matching the non-streaming behavior.

signals.title: perf: reduce JIT overhead by using fixed step size in Triton kernels
signals.text: Hi from [novita.ai](https://novita.ai/)! <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Speculative decoding Triton kernels define `constexpr` parameters based on runtime batch size / seq_len. This causes **JIT recompilation overhead** each time these dimensions change — a frequent occurrence in online inference. This PR switches to fixed step sizes, allowing kernel reuse and eliminating redundant compilations. ## Modifications Refactor speculative decoding Triton kernels to use fixed step sizes instead of dynamic batch-size-dependent constexpr parameters. Key changes: - Add _SPEC_STEP_SIZE and _SPEC_MAX_NUM_LOOPS constants - Refactor kernels to use loop-based accumulation - Keep v1 (original) kernels for AMD backend compatibility - Add v2 suffix for signals.title: [NPU] allgather after qlora for dsv3.2
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In DeepSeek-V3.2, due to the large hidden dimension of the model, performing all-gather on hidden_states before attention introduces a high-dimensional communication operation. The scale of this communication is proportional to hidden_dim × token_num, which can quickly amplify in multi-card TP scenarios, making communication rather than computation the primary performance bottleneck in the attention stage. ## Modifications allgather_after_q_lora addresses this by removing the pre-attention all-gather of hidden_states and moving the communication before the indexer. It performs all-gather only on low-dimensional tensors such as q_lora, k, and weights just before indexer execution. This reduces high-dimensional communication overhead while maintaining equivalence. Since the all-gather communication occurs after layernorm, it effectively reduces the computational overhead of related operators. ## Accuracy Tests 100%|██████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 1319/1319 [15:25<00:00, 1.43it/s] Accuracy: 0.959 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 927.711 s Output throughput: 154.077 token/s ## Benchmarking and Profiling Serving Benchmark Result Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: 7.0 Max request concurrency: 416 Successful requests: 1664 Benchmark duration (s): 276.95 Total input tokens: 3494400 Total input text tokens: 3494400 Total input vision tokens: 0 Total generated tokens: 1497600 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 1497276 Request throughput (req/s): 6.01 Input token throughput (tok/s): 12617.32 Output token throughput (tok/s): 5407.42 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 6835.00 Peak concurrent requests: 265 Total token throughput (tok/s): 18024.74 Concurrency: 196.95 Accept length: 3.23 -----------------End-to-End Latency----------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 32779.85 Median E2E Latency (ms): 32644.49 -----------------Time to First Token----------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 5600.41 Median TTFT (ms): 4935.13 P99 TTFT (ms): 12345.78 -----------------Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)----------------- Mean TPOT (ms): 30.23 Median TPOT (ms): 30.64 P99 TPOT (ms): 38.63 -----------------Inter-Token Latency----------------- Mean ITL (ms): 30.23 Median ITL (ms): 25.18 P95 ITL (ms): 49.39 P99 ITL (ms): 66.04 Max ITL (ms): 521.57 ## Checklist - signals.title: Fix/flashinfer prefix lens cpu sum
signals.text: ## Motivation Addresses the existing TODO in `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_single_wrapper`: avoid a CUDA device sync caused by `prefix_lens.sum().item()` on the ragged prefill path. Calling `.item()` on a CUDA tensor forces synchronization and can reduce CPU–GPU async overlap. ## Modifications - Thread `forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens_cpu` through the prefill updater call chain as `prefix_lens_cpu`. - When available, compute `paged_kernel_lens_sum = int(prefix_lens_cpu.sum())` on CPU, avoiding the CUDA sync. - Retain the original `.sum().item()` fallback when no CPU tensor is provided. - Remove resolved TODO comment. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model outputs. Same value computed, only on CPU instead of GPU. ## Benchmarking and Profiling **Profiling:** In a PyTorch profiler trace, cumulative `Tensor.item()` time on this path dropped from ~1.6s to ~0.32s. **Benchmark (no regression):** Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on RTX 3090, `bench_serving --num-prompts 50`, 5 runs per branch: | Branch | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean ITL (ms) | |--------|-------------|----------------|---------------| | fix | 366.98 ± 0.78 | 156.20 ± 7.48 | 20.11 ± 0.03 | | main | 365.34 ± 0.29 | 162.03 ± 6.92 | 20.20 ± 0.04 | Differences within noise at this scale; primary goal is removing the avoidable sync.

signals.title: fix: normalize module_name in get_hidden_dim fallback
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR makes **LoRA initialization work for Qwen models** (e.g. Qwen2.5 / Qwen3) in the fallback path of `sglang.srt.lora.utils.get_hidden_dim()` when the HF model does **not** implement `base_model.get_hidden_dim()`. Before this change, the fallback only accepted SGLang internal stacked module names (e.g. `qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`) and raised `NotImplementedError` for common HF-style module names like `q_proj/k_proj/v_proj` (including dotted names such as `layers.0.self_attn.q_proj`). This prevented LoRA init for Qwen when `lora_target_modules` used HF-style names. ## Modifications - In `python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:get_hidden_dim()` (fallback branch only), normalize `module_name` via the existing `get_normalized_target_modules()` mapping before applying the default dimension logic. - Preserve the original user-provided name (`orig_module_name`) only for the error message, so `NotImplementedError` still reports the pre-normalization module name (useful for dotted module names). - No behavior change for models that already implement `base_model.get_hidden_dim()` (fast-path). ## Benchmarking and Profiling N/A (this change affects LoRA init fallback logic, not inference hotpath). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: ROCm: Fix AITER attention for Qwen3-Coder-Next hybrid models
signals.text: ## Goal - Fix v_head_dim init for hybrid models (layer0 can be GDN, not full attention). - Add probe-based CK batch_prefill support detection and triton extend fallback for head_dim>128. - Guard CUDA-only CUTLASS/CuTe-DSL imports and keep ROCm on triton causal_conv1d. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Qwen3-Coder-Next is a hybrid model (GDN + attention). On ROCm with AITER attention backend enabled, we hit runtime issues because: 1. `v_head_dim` was inferred from `token_to_kv_pool.get_value_buffer(0)` which can point to a non-attention layer buffer when layer0 is GDN. 2. CK `mha_batch_prefill` availability for `head_dim > 128` depends on the local AITER build. When unsupported, prefill can fail (or be unstable). 3. `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` imported CUDA-only CUTLASS/CuTe-DSL bits unconditionally in the non-CPU path, which breaks ROCm imports. This PR makes Qwen3-Coder-Next runnable and benchmarkable across both `--attention-backend triton` and `--attention-backend aiter` on ROCm. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` - Fix `v_head_dim` initialization by using `model_config.v_head_dim` instead of `token_to_kv_pool.get_value_buffer(0)`. - Add a small probe at backend init to detect whether CK batch-prefill supports the current head shape (non-MLA, `head_dim > 128`). - If probe fails, fall back to triton `extend_attention_fwd` in `forward_extend`. - Skip the probe when `skip_prefill=True` (decode-only backends like speculative draft backends). - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` - Guard CUDA-only `cutedsl_gdn` import behind `is_cuda()`. - On ROCm/HIP, keep using the triton `causal_conv1d_triton` implementation (do not import/override with CUDA-only implementations). - Only enable CuTe-DSL GDN decode when running on CUDA. ## Accuracy Tests ### GSM8K on Qwen3-Coder-Next (TP=8) Rerun: 2026-02-11 (GSM8K test set has 1319 questions; `--num-questions 2000` runs all of them) - Triton attention backend: - Accuracy: **0.947** - Invalid: **0.000** - Latency: **33.062 s** - Output throughput: **5198.031 tok/s** - AITER attention backend: - Accuracy: **0.947** - Invalid: **0.000** - Latency: **32.303 s** - Output throughput: **5264.421 tok/s** Summary: | Backend | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency | Output tok/s | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | triton | 0.947 | 0.000 | 33.062 s | 5198.031 | | aiter | 0.947 | 0.000 | 32.303 s | 5264.421 | Commands: ```bash # Triton MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-Coder-Next SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 PYTHONPATH=python python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --num-questions 2000 --parallel 512 --port 30000 --backend srt # AITER SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend aiter \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 PYTHONPATH=python python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --num-questions 2000 --parallel 512 --port 30000 --backend srt ``` ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Qwen3-Coder-Next Serving Benchmark Matrix on MI355X (TP=1/4/8) Rerun: 2026-02-11 Parameters: random dataset, 50 prompts, input len 512, output len 256, request rate 5 req/s. | Metric | Triton TP=1 | Triton TP=4 | Triton TP=8 | AITER TP=1 | AITER TP=4 | AITER TP=8 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Status | OK | OK | OK | OK | OK | OK | | Successful requests | 50/50 | 50/50 | 50/50 | 50/50 | 50/50 | 50/50 | | Request throughput (req/s) | 3.85 | 4.08 | 4.10 | 3.84 | 4.06 | 4.08 | | Input tok/s | 1,090 | 1,154 | 1,160 | 1,088 | 1,150 | 1,156 | | Output tok/s | 438 | 464 | 466 | 437 | 462 | 464 | | Peak output tok/s | 686 | 752 | 753 | 685 | 773 | 760 | | Total tok/s | 1,528 | 1,617 | 1,626 | 1,525 | 1,611 | 1,621 | | Concurrency | 13.60 | 10.00 | 9.65 | 13.44 | 10.30 | 10.02 | | Mean E2E Latency (ms) | 3,533 | 2,453 | 2,354 | 3,496 | 2,538 | 2,453 | | Median TTFT (ms) | 86.7 | 82.3 | 80.1 | 83.7 | 84.0 | 83.3 | | Median TPOT (ms) | 29.8 | 21.1 | 20.4 | 29.8 | 21.7 | 21.2 | Command: ```bash MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-Coder-Next PORT=30000 # Server python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --tp {1|4|8} \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend {triton|aiter} \ --port "$PORT" # Benchmark python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port "$PORT" \ --model "$MODEL_PATH" \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 \ --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts 50 \ --request-rate 5 ``` ## signals.title: fix(nsa): align max_context_len with req_to_token width
signals.text: # Motivation In NSA backend initialization, `max_context_len` was derived from `model_config.context_len`. However, CUDA-graph page table usage depends on `req_to_token` actual width, which may include speculative headroom beyond configured `context_len`. This mismatch can cause shape/alignment issues in NSA paths. # Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa_backend.py` - Replace `self.max_context_len = model_runner.model_config.context_len` - With `self.max_context_len = self.req_to_token.shape[1]` - Add comments explaining alignment with `req_to_token` width. # Testing - Verified initialization logic and references locally. # Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

signals.title: perf(nsa-indexer): stabilize ragged MQA chunk shapes for DeepGEMM
signals.text: # Motivation On long-context NSA prefill with ragged batches, chunked MQA logits can produce highly dynamic `M` sizes. This can trigger repeated DeepGEMM JIT recompilation and unstable latency. The goal is to stabilize chunk shapes while preserving correctness. # Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa/nsa_indexer.py` - Add `_MQA_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS = 1024` to bound chunk-row variants. - Compute chunk rows using bucketized power-of-two sizing from free memory, then cap by `_MQA_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS`. - For ultra-long KV (`k_offset >= 65536`), further cap chunk rows to `256`. - In chunk loop, pad tail chunk to fixed `max_rows` (`q`, `weights`, `ks`, `ke`) before `fp8_mqa_logits`, then slice logits back to valid rows. - This keeps kernel input shapes more stable and reduces JIT churn. # Testing - Verified code path and tensor-shape handling logic locally. # Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix fp8 KV cache crash with KV-shared layers in triton backend
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #22277 ## What's broken? Running Gemma4 E4B (`num_kv_shared_layers: 18`) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` (or `fp8_e4m3`) crashes on the first request with: ``` triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 264:17: qk = tl.dot(q, k, out_dtype=tl.float32) ^ Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e5 ``` Models with `num_kv_shared_layers: 0` (e.g., Gemma4 31B) work fine with fp8 KV cache. ## Who is affected? Any model using **both** `num_kv_shared_layers > 0` **and** fp8 KV cache. Currently this means: - **Gemma 4 E4B** (`num_kv_shared_layers: 18`) - **Gemma 3n** (also uses KV-shared layers) Models without KV-shared layers are not affected. ## Where is the bug? **`triton_backend.py:865-872`** In `forward_extend()`, when KV-sharing layers set `k=None, v=None`, the backend reads directly from the fp8 KV cache without dequantization: ```python if k is None and v is None: ... k = k_buffer[cache_loc] # <- fp8 tensor from cache v = v_buffer[cache_loc] # <- no dequant to bf16! ``` ## Why does it happen? For **non-shared layers**, the model computes K/V in bf16 and passes them as `K_Extend` (bf16) to the extend kernel, while separately quantizing them to fp8 for cache storage. The extend kernel always receives bf16 **except** for KV-sharing layers. For **KV-sharing layers**, `k=None` signals the backend to fetch from the KV cache of the donor layer. But `get_kv_buffer()` returns raw fp8 data, and the `k is None` branch passes it directly to the kernel without converting to the compute dtype. The extend section of the Triton kernel does `tl.dot(q, k, out_dtype=tl.float32)` assuming both `q` and `k` are bf16 mixed `bf16 x fp8` causes the compilation error. ## How did we fix it? Added dtype check + dequantization + scale restoration after reading from the KV cache in the `k is None` branch of triton backend: ```python if k.dtype != q.dtype: k = k.to(q.dtype) v = v.to(q.dtype) if layer.k_scale_float is not None: k.mul_(layer.k_scale_float) if layer.v_scale_float is not None: v.mul_(layer.v_scale_float) ``` This fix: - Casts fp8 -> compute dtype, then applies scale factors to reverse the `div_(k_scale)` from `set_kv_buffer` - Guarded by `k.dtype != q.dtype` (no-op for non-quantized KV caches) - `k_scale_float is not None` guard handles runtime fp8 (no quant config, scale=None) - Only affects the KV-sharing code path zero impact on models with `num_kv_shared_layers: 0` **Scope**: Triton backend only. FlashInfer backend fix deferred to a separate PR per maintainer request (blocked on flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2959). ## Acknowledgment The root cause analysis and fix approach were identified and verified by @aqweteddy in the [issue discussion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22277#issuecomment-4203710765). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #27853443955](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27853443955)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #27853443894](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27853443894)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Enable num_splits > 1 for FA3 deterministic inference
signals.text: ## Summary SGLang's deterministic inference mode currently forces `num_splits=1` for FA3, which limits prefill throughput. With the `batch_invariant` scheduling fix in flash-attention (sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43), we can safely use `num_splits > 1` while maintaining bit-exact determinism. This PR sets `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, improving prefill throughput by up to **2.1x** on prefill-bound workloads. ## Benchmark Results (Qwen3-8B, H200, `--attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend flashinfer --enable-deterministic-inference`) | Workload | num_splits=1 | num_splits=4 | Speedup | |----------|-------------|-------------|---------| | **Short prefill** (512 in, 128 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 8,614 | 18,101 | **2.10x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 482 | 1,432 | 0.34x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 8,970 | 3,986 | **2.25x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 131 | 40 | **3.3x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 5,875 | 704 | **8.3x** | | **Medium prefill** (2048 in, 256 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 18,533 | 23,371 | **1.26x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,628 | 2,688 | 0.98x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 10,409 | 8,073 | **1.29x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 62 | 34 | **1.8x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 4,397 | 2,068 | **2.1x** | | **Long prefill** (4096 in, 512 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 16,601 | 18,073 | **1.09x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,850 | 1,887 | **1.51x** | | Mean E2E (ms) | 9,233 | 8,910 | **1.04x** | > **TTFT vs ITL tradeoff on short prefill:** With `num_splits=1` at `request-rate=inf`, prefills run serially — early requests get fast TTFT (482ms) but cause massive decode stalls (P99 ITL 5.9s). With `num_splits=4`, prefills complete faster in aggregate, so decode runs smoothly (P99 ITL 704ms, 8x better), but individual TTFT is higher because more prefills are batched concurrently. E2E latency and throughput are the meaningful comparisons. At realistic request rates this TTFT difference disappears. ## Changes - **`flashattention_backend.py`**: Set `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, pass `batch_invariant=True` - **`flash_attention.py`**, **`flash_attention_v3.py`**: Thread `batch_invariant` param through FA3 call chain - **sgl-kernel**: Add `batch_invariant` to fwd op schema, Python wrapper, C++ header - **sgl-kernel/tests**: Add `test_flash_attn_deterministic_num_splits` (128 test cases, all passing) ## Deterministic validation All three sglang deterministic test modes pass with `num_splits=4`: - `test_deterministic --test-mode single` (15 trials, batch 1-15): **PASS** (1 unique output) - `test_deterministic --test-mode prefix` (4 prefix lengths, logprobs): **PASS** (all identical) - `test_deterministic --test-mode radix_cache`: **PASS** (cached == uncached) ## Reproduce benchmark results **1. Launch server (num_splits=4, this PR):** ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 ``` **2. Run benchmarks (in a separate terminal):** ```bash # Short prefill (512 input, 128 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 \ --num-prompts 300 --request-rate inf # Medium prefill (2048 input, 256 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts 200 --request-rate inf # Long prefill (4096 input, 512 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \ --num-prompts 100 --request-rate inf ``` **3. For num_splits=1 baseline**, temporarily change `flashattention_backend.py` line 210 from `self.num_splits = 4` to `self.num_splits = 1`, restart server, and re-run the same benchmarks. ## Reproduce deterministic tests ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 # In a separate terminal: python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode single --n-start 10 --n-trials 15 python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode prefix --n-start 10 --n-trials 10 --return-logprob python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode radix_cache ``` ## Dependencies Requires: sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43 (`batch_invariant` flag) ## Test plan - [x] 128/128 kernel-level batch invariance tests pass (sgl-kernel) - [x] All 3 sglang deterministic test modes pass - [ ] CI passes <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #28138299519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299519)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #28138299333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299333)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [RL] Add Engine.drain() / POST /drain to wait for in-flight requests
signals.text: Implements section 1 of the RL inner-loop discussion in #24119: a minimal `drain` primitive that lets a framework block until no requests are in flight, so a follow-up `update_weights_*` or `release_memory_*` call lands cleanly without racing mid-decode requests. Independent of the section 3 work in #24123 (which surfaces in-flight detection on `release_memory_occupation`); the two compose naturally. ## What this PR adds `Engine.drain(timeout=None)` returns `(success, remaining_requests)` and is the sync entry point. `TokenizerManager.drain` is the async counterpart for in-process callers, and `POST /drain` exposes the same shape over HTTP, returning `{"success": bool, "remaining_requests": int}` with status 200 in either outcome — the operation itself completes successfully even when the wait times out, and the caller distinguishes via the body. Idleness is tracked via ``tokenizer_manager.rid_to_state``, which the existing detokenizer feedback loop populates and clears as requests start and finish. That dictionary is the natural mirror of "what did the caller submit and is still pending" — exactly the question the RL inner loop needs answered before pushing new weights. The same idiom is already used by ``sigterm_watchdog`` for the graceful-shutdown drain; this PR exposes it as a public API. Implementation is a 50ms poll loop with optional timeout, with no scheduler-side communication. ## What this PR does NOT add The ``paused`` / quiesce flag from the RFC. The infrastructure for that flag is already in tree as ``SchedulerInputBlocker`` (used internally behind ``SGLANG_ENABLE_COLOCATED_BATCH_GEN`` for colocated batch generation), but not exposed as a public engine-control API. Whether requests submitted during the drain window should be queued, rejected, or 5xx-ed is the design question that warrants its own discussion. Today the precondition is documented: callers should not submit new requests during the drain window. A follow-up PR can layer the paused flag on top of this drain without changing the drain surface itself. The scheduler-side ``is_fully_idle()`` check is also not consulted directly. In steady state it converges with ``rid_to_state`` — a request stays in ``rid_to_state`` until the detokenizer reports completion, by which point the scheduler has also moved past it. If maintainer feedback wants a stronger guarantee, that is a small extension to the same shape. ## Tests Added ``test/registered/rl/test_engine_drain.py`` (registered for ``stage-b-test-1-gpu-small``): - drain on a fully idle engine returns immediately with ``success=True``, ``remaining_requests=0``, - drain with a short timeout while a long generation is in flight returns ``success=False`` with ``remaining_requests > 0`` and does not wait for the generation to finish, - drain without a timeout blocks until an in-flight request finishes naturally, then reports idle. Tests use ``popen_launch_server`` rather than driving an in-process Engine because ``Engine.drain`` and ``Engine.generate`` both call ``self.loop.run_until_complete`` on the same event loop and cannot be issued concurrently from two threads against a single Engine instance; the HTTP path naturally handles that concurrency.

signals.title: [bugfix] auto-truncate: leave room for max_new_tokens and reserved tokens
signals.text: Closes #21136. ## What is broken When `--allow-auto-truncate` is enabled and the input alone is longer than `context_len`, `_validate_one_request` truncates the input to exactly `context_len`: ```python del input_ids[_max_req_len:] input_token_num = len(input_ids) ``` The very next check is ```python if max_new_tokens + input_token_num >= _max_req_len: obj.sampling_params[\"max_new_tokens\"] = max(0, _max_req_len - input_token_num) ``` With `input_token_num == _max_req_len`, that forces `max_new_tokens` to 0 and the request returns no output — the opposite of what the caller asked for when they enabled auto-truncation. The same path also fails to subtract `num_reserved_tokens` (used by EAGLE speculative decoding to reserve token slots), so the post-truncation total can still exceed the effective usable length. ## Fix Truncate the input to `context_len - max_new_tokens - num_reserved_tokens`, clamped to at least one input token, so the request actually has room to produce `max_new_tokens` of output: ```python target_input_len = max( 1, _max_req_len - (max_new_tokens or 0) - self.num_reserved_tokens, ) del input_ids[target_input_len:] input_token_num = len(input_ids) + self.num_reserved_tokens ``` The existing downstream `(max_new_tokens + input_token_num)` check still runs and tightens `max_new_tokens` further if anything is off-by-one, so the reliability contract of the function is unchanged. ## Tests `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_auto_truncate.py` (CPU unit suite, registered for `stage-a-test-cpu`) covers: - long input leaves room for `max_new_tokens` (the regression in #21136), - reserved tokens are subtracted from the truncation cap, - missing `max_new_tokens` still truncates safely without a `TypeError`, - short input within the limit is unchanged, - truncation disabled still raises `ValueError`, - an oversized `max_new_tokens` clamps the input to one token rather than going negative. ## Relationship to prior PRs #8104 was an earlier attempt to fix `--allow-auto-truncate`. Before it merged, #9391 landed an independent fix that resolved the original "engine raises ValueError" symptom but introduced the residual `max_new_tokens=0` problem above. This PR builds on the #9391 code rather than the #8104 diff. I will close #8104 separately.

signals.title: [Docker][ROCm] Bump ROCm720 base image from 7.2.0 to 7.2.2 to fix hipEventQuery race
signals.text: ## Motivation The current ROCm720 base image ``` rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 ``` points at **ROCm 7.2.0**, which has a known `hipEventQuery` runtime bug — cross-thread calls ignore `THREAD_LOCAL` capture mode, so the NCCL watchdog can invalidate in-flight HIP graph captures. This surfaces as multi-GPU AITER custom all-reduce crashes (sgl-project/sglang#23580, #23581). AITER's `IPCBufferPool` change in v0.1.12.post1 only widened the race window — the bug also exists with SGLang's own `CustomAllreduce`, just narrower. The fix landed upstream in **ROCm 7.2.2** ([pytorch/pytorch#176251](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/176251)), confirmed by the AMD AITER team in [ROCm/aiter#2941](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2941) and [ROCm/aiter#2857](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2857). ## Modifications Bump both `BASE_IMAGE_*_ROCM720` ARGs in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` to the 7.2.2 build: ``` - rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 + rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 ``` Same Ubuntu / Python / PyTorch version, only the ROCm patch level changes. No C++ rebuild requirement, no Python change. ## Result With this change, AITER custom all-reduce is safe to use again on the rebuilt SGLang ROCm720 images. The defensive default `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AR=false` from #23581 remains useful for users stuck on ROCm 7.2.0 environments, but the bug class is gone on this base image. ## Refs - sgl-project/sglang#23580 — original repro of the multi-GPU crash - sgl-project/sglang#23581 — defensive default-off (already merged-pending) - ROCm/aiter#2941, ROCm/aiter#2857 — root cause investigations - pytorch/pytorch#176251 — the upstream THREAD_LOCAL fix cc @sunway513, @TennyWang1223, @HaiShaw
