signals.title: [Perf][DSV4] add ag_gemm and moe_rs overlap kernels for dsv4 prefill
signals.text: ## 1. Motivation We implement communication-computation overlap for DeepSeek V4 Prefill CP by introducing two fused Triton kernels built on `torch.symmetric_memory`: 1. Fused AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM: the CP AllGather is performed on a dedicated stream via Copy Engine (CE) P2P pulls (consuming no SMs), while a fused kernel on the compute stream performs on-the-fly FP8 quantization and shared expert `gate_up_proj` GEMM. The compute kernel poll signals to consume each chunk as soon as the CE delivers it, overlapping the AllGather with computation. 2. Fused MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter: the routed expert output reduction, shared expert addition, and ReduceScatter send are fused into a single kernel, overlapping the ReduceScatter communication with the reduction computation. - Co-auther: @zxdukki ## 2. Modifications - **Environment Variable** - Add `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL` (default `False`) to enable the fused kernels. - **New Triton Kernels (`symm_mem_kernels/`)** - Add allgather_gemm_symm_mem.py: triton kernel for CE-driven AllGather + on-the-fly FP8 quantization and GEMM with signal-based coordination across two streams. - Add moe_reduce_rs_symm_mem.py: fused MoE topk-reduce + shared expert addition + ReduceScatter in a single triton kernel. - **TorchSymmMemCommunicator (torch_symm_mem.py)** - Split `disabled` / `allreduce_disabled` so fused-kernel contexts work without multicast support. - Add lazy-init helpers to cache AG-GEMM and MoE-RS contexts. - Add CP-mode activation via `set_use_cp()` / `get_active_comm()`. - **Model & Layer (parallel_state.py, fused_moe.py, deepseek_v2/v4.py)** - Initialize `TorchSymmMemCommunicator` when the fused-kernel env var is enabled. - Add `no_topk_reduce` option to skip in-kernel reduction (deferred to the fused RS kernel). - Integrate `maybe_fused_ag_shared_experts` and `maybe_fused_shared_add_rs` into the MoE forward path. - Skip the standalone CP AllGather in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` when the fused path is active. ## 3. Evaluation ### 3.1. Experiment Setup - 3 nodes, with 8 × H20 GPUs and 4 dual-port 200Gbps NICs per node. DSV4 Flash uses 1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill. DSV4 Pro uses 3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill. - Input length 16k/32k/64k/128k, output length 1. ### 3.2. Performance Evaluation - DSV4 Flash mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 548.89 | 521.44 | 5.00% | | 32k | 1092.81 | 1034.50 | 5.33% | | 64k | 2200.69 | 2122.33 | 3.56% | | 128k | 4664.76 | 4500.17 | 3.53% | - DSV4 Pro mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 1066.37 | 1028.04 | 3.59% | | 32k | 1641.93 | 1586.49 | 3.37% | | 64k | 2832.55 | 2731.91 | 3.55% | | 128k | 5355.57 | 5173.78 | 3.39% | - Bench Script: ``` # (random-input-len, num-prompts) BENCH_CONFIGS=( "16384 300" "32768 150" "65536 100" "131072 50" ) for cfg in "${BENCH_CONFIGS[@]}"; do read -r INPUT_LEN NUM_PROMPTS <<< "$cfg" python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --host localhost --port 8288 \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path ./ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --num-prompts $NUM_PROMPTS --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len $INPUT_LEN --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf done ``` ### 3.3. Profiling Here we take DSV4 Flash as an example to show profiling before and after optimization. - AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM (476μs->309μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: - MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter (415μs->235μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: ### 3.4. Accuracy Tests - DSV4 Flash: ``` # ----------------------- baseline ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [02:36<00:00, 6.37it/s] Accuracy: 0.950 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 156.981 s Output throughput: 565.851 token/s # ----------------------- overlap ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [02:15<00:00, 7.39it/s] Accuracy: 0.956 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 135.355 s Output throughput: 655.545 token/s ``` - DSV4 Pro: ``` # ----------------------- baseline ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [04:31<00:00, 3.69it/s] Accuracy: 0.957 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 271.137 s Output throughput: 334.259 token/s # ----------------------- overlap ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [04:32<00:00, 3.67it/s] Accuracy: 0.957 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 272.710 s Output throughput: 331.315 token/s ``` ### 3.5. Repro Script - DSV4 Flash (1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill): ``` SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 \ SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./profile \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8288 \ --trust-remote-code --enable-cache-report \ --log-level info --enable-metrics \ --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --tp-size 8 --pp-size 1 --nnodes 1 \ --node-rank 0 \ --dist-init-addr 192.168.0.1:25000 \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --disable-radix-cache \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 ``` - DSV4 Pro (3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill): ``` SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 \ SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./profile \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8288 \ --trust-remote-code --enable-cache-report \ --log-level info --enable-metrics \ --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --tp-size 8 --pp-size 3 --nnodes 3 \ --node-rank ${NODE_ID} \ --dist-init-addr 192.168.0.1:25000 \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --disable-radix-cache \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32233092061](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233092061) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32324714601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324714601)

signals.title: [AMD] Fix Load and Inference of MLA models with Quark PTPC FP8 attention on ROCm
signals.text: ## Motivation Loading and running MLA models (like `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with quark-quantized MXFP4 weights + per-token-per-channel FP8 attention on ROCm/gfx95 fails with multiple errors. The root cause is that the aiter gfx95 `_gfx95_quant_format="fp8"` path fuses RMSNorm + FP8 quantization into a single kernel (`fused_rms_fp8_group_quant`), passing pre-quantized **tuples** instead of plain bf16 tensors downstream. This pattern was already handled for compressed_tensors attention quantization across three prior PRs: - **#12181** added the `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` routing in `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` for pre-quantized tuple inputs - **#21403** added the `isinstance(input, tuple)` branch in `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` itself - **#22258** added the 3-tuple `(fp8, scale, bf16)` passthrough from `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` in `communicator.py`, and the corresponding unwrap in `dsa_indexer._project_and_scale_head_gates` None of these extended to **quark** attention quantization, and this PR closes that gap. ## Modifications **`fp8_utils.py`: `channel_quant_to_tensor_quant`** Reshape 1D per-channel scale `[N]` -> `[N, 1]` before multiplying against the 2D weight. Quark's `kv_b_proj` has a per-channel FP8 weight with a 1D scale vector that failed to broadcast correctly against the `[N, K]` weight. **`fp8_utils.py`: `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`** Unpack pre-quantized input tuple as `input[0], input[1]` instead of destructuring, to tolerate both 2-tuples and 3-tuples (the 3-tuple was introduced in #22258 but the unpack assumed exactly 2 elements). **`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`: `apply_weights`** Mirror the handling that #12181 added to `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.apply_weights`, extended for quark's weight layout and both tuple formats Note: unlike compressed_tensors which stores `shuffle(w)`, quark stores `shuffle(w).t()`, making the weight layout incompatible with `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`/`gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`; So we dequantize to bf16 and use the existing `apply_fp8_linear` path without requiring weight storage changes. **`dsa_indexer.py`: `_get_q_k_bf16` and `_get_k_bf16`** Mirror the unwrap added in #22258 for `_project_and_scale_head_gates`, applied to the two remaining methods that also receive `x` and call `self.wk`. ## Validation Accuracy is evaluated using [lm_eval](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) on MI355X. Model: GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with routed and shared experts quantized to MXFP4 and self-attention projections quantized to PTPC FP8. | Task | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---| | GSM8K | 93.93% ± 0.66% | 93.71% ± 0.67% | ## Reproduction ### Launch server ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 sglang serve \ --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 \ --json-model-override-args '{"qk_rope_head_dim": 64}' \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` ### Accuracy ```bash lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4-AttnFP8,base_url=http://localhost:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,max_retries =10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \ --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32307518401](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307518401)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32307518148](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307518148)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add dense-FP8 for MXFP4 checkpoints with fused silu, mul, activation quant
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Quark MXFP4 checkpoints leave a handful of large dense projections unquantized in bf16 — most notably the Qwen3.5 `shared_expert.down_proj`. On the AMD ROCm/aiter path these leftover bf16 GEMMs are comparatively heavy, and the cost shows up most in prefill-bound regimes where the dense projection is on the critical path. Today there is no way to promote just these excluded layers without re-quantizing the whole checkpoint. This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-dense-fp8` path that promotes only the eligible large bf16 dense layers (which the checkpoint left unquantized) to **online w8a8 FP8**, and fuses the preceding `SiluAndMul` + per-token activation quantization into a single aiter kernel. Instead of running `SiluAndMul`, then a separate activation quant, then the GEMM, the fused kernel emits a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple that feeds straight into `down_proj`. The path is numerically a dynamic per-token FP8 quant of an otherwise bf16 layer, is ROCm/aiter-only, and is fully opt-in, so default behavior is unchanged. ## Modifications - **`server_args.py`**: Add the `--enable-dense-fp8` server arg (AMD/aiter, default **off**). Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER` and `SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN`. - **`quark/quark.py`**: Give `QuarkConfig` a model-registered dense-FP8 policy. `register_dense_fp8_modules(include, exclude, min_output_size)` lets a model declare which excluded (bf16) layers may be promoted — quark itself owns no module names or thresholds. In `get_quant_method`, a layer that would normally fall back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod` is instead routed to an online dynamic `Fp8LinearMethod` (`Fp8Config(is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=False, activation_scheme="dynamic")`) when `--enable-dense-fp8` is set and the layer matches the policy (include substring, not excluded, output size ≥ min). - **`models/qwen3_5.py`**: Register the Qwen3.5 policy — include only `.shared_expert.down_proj`, exclude tiny/routing/embedding layers (`conv1d`, `shared_expert_gate`, `mlp.gate`, `in_proj_*`, `lm_head`, `embed`), and require `N ≥ 2048`. Aiter-only, so the tuned policy lives with the model. - **`models/qwen2_moe.py`**: In the MoE block forward, when `down_proj` is running as online w8a8 FP8 per-token on aiter, fuse `SiluAndMul` + per-token quant into a single `aiter.silu_and_mul_quant` call that produces the `(fp8, scale)` tuple consumed directly by `down_proj`, skipping a separate activation + quant pass. Gated on `use_aiter_fp8_per_token`; default off. - **`layers/quantization/fp8.py`**: Teach `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` to accept a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple input (from the fused kernel) and route it to the aiter PTPC helper `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`, since `apply_fp8_linear` has no tuple path. Weight is transposed `(K, N) → (N, K)` to match the helper's expectation. ## Usage Opt-in via `--enable-dense-fp8`. It is AMD/aiter-only and requires aiter FP8 per-token, so set the two aiter env flags. The same command applies to both Qwen3.5 checkpoints (add `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` for the MXFP4-AttnFP8 checkpoint): ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --enable-dense-fp8 ``` The `SiluAndMul`+per-token-quant fusion is on by default whenever `--enable-dense-fp8` is active on the aiter per-token path; it can be disabled for debugging with `SGLANG_DISABLE_DENSE_FP8_SILU_FUSE=1` (not recommended — fusion is neutral-to-faster and saves the bf16 intermediate round-trip). ## Accuracy Tests The same `--enable-dense-fp8` config (online PTPC FP8 + fused `SiluAndMul`+quant) is applied to **both** Qwen3.5-397B-A17B checkpoints, TP=2, aiter backend. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions. **MXFP4-AttnFP8** (fp8_e4m3 KV cache): | config | accuracy (flexible / strict) | |------------------------------------------|------------------------------| | `dense_off` (baseline, down_proj bf16) | 0.9363 / 0.9409 | | `dense_on` (this PR, down_proj FP8) | 0.9393 / 0.9454 | **Plain MXFP4** (3-seed mean ± per-seed stderr ≈ 0.007): | config | flexible (3 seeds) | strict (3 seeds) | |------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------| | `dense_off` (baseline, down_proj bf16) | 0.9340 / 0.9356 / 0.9295 | 0.9401 / 0.9409 / 0.9371 | | `dense_on` (this PR, down_proj FP8) | 0.9340 / 0.9257 / 0.9325 | 0.9401 / 0.9409 / 0.9416 | Accuracy is unchanged within noise on both checkpoints — the per-seed spread (±0.007) exceeds the dense_off↔dense_on difference, so promoting `down_proj` to FP8 is accuracy-neutral. ## Speed Tests and Profiling TP=2, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--page-size 16`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, allreduce-fusion on, tuned bf16 GEMM present. A = `dense_off` (baseline), B = `dense_on` (this PR); all other knobs identical. **Throughput below is total token throughput (input+output) across the TP=2 group**, i.e. `tok/s = (tok/s/gpu) × 2`. TPOT is the median per-output-token latency. ### MXFP4-AttnFP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) **ISL/OSL = 1024/1024** (decode-bound): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 776 → 774 | −0.3% | 9.96 → 9.97 | +0.1% | | 8 | 1362 → 1372 | +0.7% | 11.39 → 11.31 | −0.7% | | 16 | 2238 → 2240 | +0.1% | 14.10 → 14.09 | −0.1% | | 32 | 3124* → 3140 | +0.5% | 20.06* → 20.00 | −0.3% | | 64 | 4378 → 4360 | −0.4% | 28.97 → 29.11 | +0.5% | \* The captured `dense_off` cc=32 point was a noisy outlier; a repeat baseline run is used here. At 1k/1k the dense projection is too compute-light to move the needle — results are **at parity (no regression)** on both throughput and TPOT. **ISL/OSL = 8192/1024** (prefill-heavy): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3170 → 3182 | +0.4% | 10.76 → 10.68 | −0.7% | | 8 | 5216 → 5338 | +2.3% | 13.05 → 12.74 | −2.4% | | 16 | 7874 → 8008 | +1.7% | 17.46 → 17.14 | −1.8% | | 32 | 10260 → 10462 | +2.0% | 27.07 → 26.34 | −2.7% | | 64 | 12840 → 13120 | +2.2% | 44.06 → 42.88 | −2.7% | In the prefill-heavy 8k/1k regime — where the bf16 `down_proj` GEMM actually matters — the fused FP8-dense path gives a **consistent ~2% total-throughput gain** and a **~2–3% lower TPOT** at every concurrency. Net: neutral at 1k/1k, a clear win for prefill-bound workloads, with no TPOT regression anywhere. ### Plain MXFP4 Node-pinned (single NUMA node, fixed GPU pair) to suppress host/neighbor contention. **ISL/OSL = 8192/1024** (prefill-heavy): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3258 → 3348 | +2.8% | 10.22 → 10.18 | −0.4% | | 8 | 5140 → 5174 | +0.7% | 13.25 → 13.15 | −0.8% | | 16 | 7798 → 7804 | +0.1% | 17.62 → 17.58 | −0.2% | | 32 | 10184 → 10198 | +0.1% | 27.06 → 27.01 | −0.2% | | 64 | 12878 → 12884 | +0.05% | 43.68 → 43.64 | −0.1% | **ISL/OSL = 1024/1024** (decode-bound) — mean of 3 warm sweeps per arm, with a flat `dense_off` control measured in the same window (control spread ≤0.6%, confirming an uncontended measurement): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 819 → 819 | 0.0% | 9.43 → 9.42 | −0.1% | | 8 | 1331 → 1341 | +0.8% | 11.68 → 11.58 | −0.9% | | 16 | 2203 → 2199 | −0.2% | 14.30 → 14.32 | +0.1% | | 32 | 3089 → 3091 | +0.1% | 20.28 → 20.34 | +0.3% | | 64 | 4352 → 4323 | −0.7% | 29.08 → 29.32 | +0.8% | On the plain MXFP4 checkpoint the dense-FP8 path is **at parity (no regression)** on this host — both throughput and TPOT are unchanged within run-to-run noise across all concurrencies, verified at **8k/1k** and **1k/1k** (the latter across 3 warm sweeps against a flat control). The PTPC+fusion config is therefore **safe to enable uniformly on both checkpoints**: a clear prefill-bound win on MXFP4-AttnFP8, and neutral on plain MXFP4. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` is an NCCL-symmetric-memory all-to-all engine with a fixed per-rank capacity. Fixed capacity means static communication shapes, which makes the MoE decode path CUDA-graph capturable under any topology — including multi-node, where legacy `low_latency` is not available as a graphable path. This PR adds it as a standalone backend `deepep_v2` alongside `deepep`; only expert-parallel dispatch/combine is replaced. Validated on Hopper (H20, H200) and Blackwell (B200 `sm_100`, B300 `sm_103`). ## Modifications - **`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** (new): the dispatcher. `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` selects the ElasticBuffer topology — **not** the legacy `normal/low_latency` split. Layout is chosen per batch by inference phase, not by comm mode: decode uses the expanded layout + masked GEMM (static shapes, graph-capturable, available under `hybrid` too), extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout. Single-shot `dispatch()/combine()` with a strict handle lifecycle; the guards run before the DeepEP import check so the module imports cleanly without DeepEP installed. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: masked-slab repack kernels. A fixed per-expert worker pool keeps the grid static (graph-safe); top-k weights are folded in-kernel; the scale copy takes the source pack-dim stride, which is what makes Blackwell's packed-UE8M0 (column-major) layout correct alongside Hopper's row-major fp32. - **`layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the FP8 adapter (masked decode / contiguous prefill, consuming DeepEP's 128-aligned psum directly as group offsets). `deep_gemm` is the only supported runner: deepep_v2 dispatches FP8 activations plus scales, and no other a2a backend targets a different runner family either. `--moe-runner-backend` is checked at startup, but the runner is chosen per layer by the quant method and several hard-select Triton regardless, so `MoeRunner` rejects the mismatch too — otherwise such a model would reach the permute registry and die on a bare assert after the weights are loaded. - **`layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`**: `get_moe_impl_class` resolves `deepep_v2` to `DeepEPMoE` like every other a2a backend — this is what makes the UE8M0 load-time weight requant apply on Blackwell. - **`server_args.py`, `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: the new flags; `ep_size` and `disable_shared_experts_fusion` are declared through the a2a passes, and the runner is validated against `resolved_view(...)` so a model declaration that restores an unsupported runner fails fast. Boot-time capacity check for the chunked-prefill budget. TBO/SBO and enforced shared-expert fusion are rejected at startup. - **`state_capturer/routed_experts.py`**: classify deepep_v2 as a scattered-a2a backend; otherwise `dp_rank > 0` reads unwritten buffer rows under `--enable-return-routed-experts`. - **No CI/Docker changes**: `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` already provides `ElasticBuffer`, so CI can exercise this backend as-is; it stays inert for every other configuration, fails fast when DeepEP is missing, and its unit tests need only Triton. ## Usage DeepEP v2 needs NCCL symmetric memory, which SGLang turns off by default (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` is set to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when the variable is unset), so an otherwise correct launch fails with `nccl.cu:104: Communicator does not support symmetric memory!`. Pass `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` (used for every benchmark here) or `--enable-symm-mem`, which also works but additionally enables NVLS and a 4 GB symmetric-memory prealloc. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` is the fixed per-rank buffer capacity. It must cover the per-rank chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size / dp_size` under DP attention), and that chunk must be a multiple of `page_size` — with `page_size=256, dp_size=8` the smallest usable pair is capacity 256 with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`. Smaller capacity is better for decode; prefill servers size it to their chunk budget and add `--disable-cuda-graph`. No extra install step: the pinned `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ships `ElasticBuffer` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`), so this backend runs on a stock environment. Re-validated on H20 x8 against that wheel with no source build and no code change -- `direct` GSM8K 0.970 / MMLU 0.890, `hybrid` 0.970 / 0.886, three-question gate passing in both modes. Earlier development used a DeepEP source build at `d4f41e4`; the packaged API is a superset of what the dispatcher calls. Multi-node: add `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid --enable-dp-lm-head --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1}`. Blackwell with a BF16 `wo_a` checkpoint: `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0`. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --ep 8 --enable-dp-attention`, `deep_gemm`, kv fp8. | | deepep_v2 `direct` | deepep_v2 `hybrid` | deepep | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 | | H20 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 | | B200 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | — | | B200 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | — | MMLU at 500 examples has a ~1.4pp standard error at this accuracy, which is wider than every gap in the table; repeat runs of one configuration spanned 0.884-0.896. These numbers show the absence of a systematic shift against the same-node `deepep` baseline, not a ranking. The three-question gate passes on every configuration above. Unit tests (CI, no DeepEP required): masked-slab repack including a production packed-UE8M0 scale and CUDA-graph capture/replay, handle-lifecycle guards, server-args resolution, capturer classification, plus a DP>1 routed-experts readback e2e. The three-question gate also passes on the multi-node configuration below. Earlier validation on the same dispatch path: needle retrieval across chunk boundaries and 8-way concurrent requests 24/24; prefill/decode disaggregation functional. ## Speed Tests | | deepep_v2 | deepep | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 | -0.9% | | H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 | +3.2% | | B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 | -2.8% | | B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 | +2.9% | Each backend pair was measured back-to-back on the same node, on torch 2.13 / sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, with the prefill cells interleaved so drift cannot bias one side. H20 prefill averages 4 samples per cell (sd 95 and 72), B200 prefill 2 per cell (sd 132 and 57); decode is one cell per side. Decode reproduces well across nodes -- deepep_v2 measured 8,385 / 8,403 / 8,429 tok/s on three different B200 nodes -- but the `deepep` side moved more, so the decode delta has landed between -0.9% and -2.8% across runs; read it as "a low single-digit percentage behind" rather than a precise figure. Prefill has been consistently ahead by roughly 3%. Multi-node (2x H20x8, TP16/EP16/DP16, `hybrid`, same protocol): **4,610 tok/s** decode with the masked-GEMM + CUDA-graph path over RDMA — a graphable cross-node decode path legacy `low_latency` does not provide — and **20,688 in_tok/s** prefill (two samples: 20,322 / 21,054). There is no same-fabric deepep baseline for this pair: DeepEP's NVSHMEM data plane does not complete across nodes on this RoCE setup, reproduced with DeepEP's own `test_internode.py` outside SGLang. Reproduction (5 rounds per boot, mean of the last 3; prefill flushes the radix cache before each round): ```bash # common: NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1, SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20, capacity 1024 # deepep_v2: --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct # deepep : --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency|normal --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype fp8 # (with SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024) NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --context-length 4096 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 $BACKEND_FLAGS \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 # decode # --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --disable-cuda-graph --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph # prefill # decode python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 128 # prefill (curl -s localhost:30000/flush_cache before each round) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 16 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (separate follow-up PR). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (above). - [x] Code style. ### Notes for reviewers - Prerequisites: none beyond the current pins -- `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` provides `ElasticBuffer`. NCCL symmetric memory must be on (see Usage). - Follow-ups: TBO/SBO comm-compute overlap (a PoC showed the naive two-phase split cannot overlap because `ElasticBuffer.dispatch` is host-blocking; it needs a `return_recv_hook`-style split in DeepEP), adapters for other MoE runners, documentation. Co-authored-by: jianxiongzhang <40026647+jianxiongzhang@users.noreply.github.com> <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32259471892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259471892)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32259470116](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259470116)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [SM120] DeepSeek-V4: DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer +FP4 MoE+ page-split
signals.text: **Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x. It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend. ## Split out of this PR Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have their own PRs: - #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix) - #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent) **This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once it lands. The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread 0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to reproduce them as written. ## What is in it 1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. 2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer. 3. **Page-split dirty mask** — `_split_kv_pages_to_64` re-laid out the whole SWA KV pool (~105 MB/layer) every decode step; now only the pages this step's top-k references are split (CUDA-graph safe, bit-identical). 4. **DeepGEMM FP4 MoE on SM120** — probe the block-scale entry point (DeepGEMM#324) instead of hard-disabling DeepGEMM at `sm==120`, plus the contiguous grouped-GEMM prefill path, the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant fix, and the swiglu-clamp fallback for TP>=2 shapes. 5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory request from the device budget instead of a fixed 128 KB. Non-SM120 architectures are unchanged: every behavioural change is either gated on `is_sm120_supported()` or is a fix that only engages where the previous code was wrong (the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant and the shared-memory cap). ## E2E benefit "main" is marlin MoE + the torch paged-MQA fallback, because that is the only SM120 path on `14bd315d` that starts: the default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` + TileLang indexer) dies in the TileLang JIT for `sm_120a` (TileLang ships nvcc 13.3, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` has CUDA 13.0 headers), and `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` raises `AttributeError: module 'sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper' has no attribute 'get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor'` (SM120 disables `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` while the runner stays selectable). Both sides then run identical server args, only the tree differs: TP4, marlin MoE, CUTLASS FP8, chunked prefill 8192, `--disable-radix-cache`, and no speculative decoding except where the tables say otherwise. 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, OSL 256, `--warmup-requests 0` so every measured request is a real prefill. TTFT is a median. **Single request (BS=1)** — 3 sequential requests, median. TTFT: | ISL | main | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | 8K | 1124 ms | 899 ms | −20% | | 32K | 4540 ms | 3585 ms | −21% | | 128K | 20107 ms | 15481 ms | −23% | TPOT, without and with MTP-2 (EAGLE, 2 steps / 3 draft tokens) on both sides: | ISL | main | this PR | | main + MTP-2 | this PR + MTP-2 | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8K | 36.1 ms | 10.5 ms | **3.4x** | 13.6 ms | 6.0 ms | 2.3x | | 32K | 35.8 ms | 10.7 ms | **3.3x** | 12.6 ms | 5.7 ms | 2.2x | | 128K | 36.1 ms | 11.9 ms | **3.0x** | 13.4 ms | 6.8 ms | 2.0x | Accepted length is within 0.2 of each other on the two sides at every context length, so the MTP gain comes from the decode path itself, not from better speculation. **Concurrent (ISL 8K)** — `--num-prompts BS --max-concurrency BS`: | BS | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | | output tok/s main | output tok/s this PR | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 3574 ms | 2826 ms | −21% | 42.9 ms | 16.8 ms | 2.6x | 71 | 147 | | 8 | 5660 ms | 4530 ms | −20% | 51.9 ms | 24.3 ms | 2.1x | 108 | 191 | | 16 | 10482 ms | 8365 ms | −20% | 71.6 ms | 40.9 ms | 1.8x | 143 | 219 | TTFT holds at −20% across batch sizes; the decode multiple decays with batch (3.4x at BS1, 1.8x at BS16) because what this PR removes is per-step fixed cost, which amortises as the batch grows. Speculative decoding amortises it the same way. GSM8K (50 questions) is 0.980 on main and 0.960 on this PR at 8K — one question apart. All tables are without prefill context parallelism, which is upstream code this PR does not touch. <details> <summary>Recipes</summary> Common to both: `--fp8-gemm-backend cutlass --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32`, plus `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. **Prefill-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`. **Decode-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. </details> ## Dependencies - FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (SM120 sparse-MLA kernels) and sglang-kernel 0.4.5 — both are what `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` currently ships. - DeepGEMM at or after deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#324 for the FP4 MoE backend. The `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` indexer path additionally needs DeepGEMM's attention host-gates to accept SM120 (a 3-line arch gate, not yet upstream in sgl-project/DeepGEMM); without it, keep the TileLang indexer default. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant.py` (9 cases, registered for CI) covers the fused swiglu-clamp + silu_mul + fp8-quant kernel against a reference. GSM8K numbers are from `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`. Reviewed and validated with @ormandj (conflict resolution) and @moxcat (inference-mode buffer fix, now #35116) on 2x and 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Re-validated after the split on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (the pinned version), this tree plus #35116: GSM8K-50 1.000 with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, 0.960 with MTP-2; ISL 8K BS1 TTFT 116/88 ms, TPOT 12.8/7.3 ms. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32228739222](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32228739222)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32228738944](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32228738944)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [MLX] Windowed per-request KV cache for sliding-window layers
signals.text: > Stacked on #30050 (un-merged): the first commit here is that PR's head; > review only the last commit. Will rebase once #30050 merges. ## Motivation Follow-up promised in #30050. That PR ran gpt-oss sliding-window layers by storing **full** KV history and applying the window at read time (banded mask at prefill, trailing-window truncation at decode). Numerically exact, but sliding layers paid full-context memory. This PR makes sliding-window layers keep only the trailing `window` tokens on the per-request KV path (`--disable-radix-cache`, the configuration the gpt-oss e2e tests run) via a new `WindowedAttentionKVCache`. Measured per-request KV for gpt-oss-20b geometry (24 layers, 12 sliding, window=128, 8 KV heads x 64 head_dim, bf16): | sequence | full-history | windowed | saving | |---|---|---|---| | <= 4096 (preallocated) | 192.0 MiB | 102.0 MiB | 46.9% | | 4096 prompt + 4000 decode | 384.0 MiB | 198.0 MiB | 48.4% | | 8192 prompt + 192 decode | 768.0 MiB | 390.0 MiB | 49.2% | (Numbers are decode steady state. While a prefill chunk is in flight a windowed layer's transient buffer is `window + max(chunk, window)` — the kept prefix plus the chunk — so with the default 4096-token chunked prefill the per-layer peak is ~4224 slots regardless of prompt length: no saving while prefilling a <= 4k prompt, roughly half from the second chunk onwards, and the buffer shrinks to `2*window` on the first decode step.) ## Modifications - `WindowedAttentionKVCache` (attention_kv_cache.py): fixed-size, temporal-order buffer. Decode appends in place into a `2*window` buffer and compacts the trailing window into a fresh buffer when full (amortised O(1) per token); prefill chunks normalise the kept prefix to `min(local, window)` on every `update_and_fetch`, so the returned length is deterministic. `offset` stays absolute (RoPE positions, decode bookkeeping); `make_mask` clamps the mask offset to the kept prefix, mirroring mlx_lm `RotatingKVCache.make_mask`, so mask width always equals returned key length. Oversized prefill-chunk buffers shrink back to `2*window` on the first decode step. Requesting a full-context mask after history has been dropped raises. - `MlxModelRunner`: `_new_native_cache` builds windowed caches for layers in `get_layer_window_sizes(model)` **only when `disable_radix_cache` is set**; the pool/radix path keeps #30050's full-history semantics because (a) `_sync_new_kv_to_pool` / `_sync_decode_kv_to_pool` slice per-request caches at absolute offsets, and (b) radix prefix reuse at match point P needs sliding KV for [P-window, P), which windowed storage no longer has. Pool-side memory work is tracked separately. - `_acquire_cache` resets reused caches via a new `reset()` (both cache classes) instead of poking `offset`. - `MLXAttentionWrapper._batched_decode` is unchanged: its trailing-window slice and locally rebuilt padding mask are already correct for both cache kinds (the windowed buffer is temporal, holds >= min(offset, window) tokens, and reports absolute offsets). Docstring updated. ## Test - New `test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/mlx/test_windowed_kv_cache.py` (15 tests): bit-exact equivalence of windowed storage vs the trailing slice of full-history storage across chunk patterns and compaction boundaries (including chunk > 2*window and buffer shrink after oversized chunks); mask width == returned key length on every chunk; clamped mask == trailing columns of the full banded mask; tiny-gpt-oss chunked prefill and 2*window greedy decode produce identical tokens windowed vs full-history; wrapper batched decode over windowed caches matches the full-KV banded reference at 1e-5 for 12 consecutive steps across the compaction boundary; runner wiring (windowed only on the per-request path, all-contiguous otherwise, reset on reuse). - Existing MLX suites stay green: test_sliding_window_attention (24), test_mlx_runner_pool_contract, test_runner_init_contract, test_scheduler_mixin. - Apple Silicon (M-series 24 GB), real weights, all at final code state: - gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8 reference correctness: PASS — token-for-token vs unpatched mlx_lm greedy (>128-token prompts, windowed path active), plus batched-vs-solo decode isolation - gpt-oss serving smoke (--disable-radix-cache): PASS — 3/3 incl. the >128-token needle prompt - gpt-oss steady-state compaction e2e: PASS — 94-token prompt + 420 greedy decode steps crossing the 2*window=256 compaction boundary three times; output character-identical to full-history storage (#30050 head) for all 420 tokens. (Both storage schemes diverge from unpatched mlx_lm at the same token ~150 steps in — a pre-existing batched-wrapper vs container numeric effect, independent of the storage change.) - qwen2_moe (Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B 4bit) serving regression: PASS — 3/3 on the default radix/pool path; windowed path correctly inactive for non-SWA models - qwen3_moe (Qwen3-30B-A3B 4bit) serving regression: PASS — 3/3 cc @yeahdongcn <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #30195520973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30195520973)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #30195520860](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30195520860)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation As per the title. Add INT4 dense linear support for AWQ/GPTQ quantized models on Intel XPU, enabling INT4 inference on this backend. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/quantization/: int4pack_utils.py, awq_kernels.py, gptq_kernels.py` — INT4 checkpoint conversion and native XPU packed-MM helpers. - Wire up scheme routing in `awq/awq.py, awq/schemes/awq_linear.py, gptq/gptq.py, gptq/schemes/gptq_linear.py, and layers/quantization/__init__.py` to dispatch dense INT4 linear to the XPU kernels. - Add unit tests: `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_int4_dense.py`. ## Accuracy Tests Model: `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4` / `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GPTQ-INT4` GSM8K: AWQ `~0.78`; GPTQ `~0.785`. ## Limitations GPTQ + TP>1 is only rejected when a row-parallel shard actually splits a quantization group — i.e. when `act_order` (`desc_act=true`) has permuted `g_idx` so the local channels no longer sort into whole `group_size` blocks. signals.title: [AMD]DSV4 Fix KV pool sizing for the unified_kv backend
signals.text: ## Motivation The DSV4 `unified_kv` backend has a different physical KV layout than the fp8 path, but `DSV4PoolConfigurator` sized both identically. Under `unified_kv` this over-allocates memory (and can OOM), because: - KV is stored in **bf16 over the full latent** (`attn_head_dim * 2` bytes), not the fp8(nope) + bf16(rope) + scale 584-byte cell. - SWA and the c4/c128 compress-states are **fixed per-request rings** (`num_req_slots * ring_size`), independent of `full_token`, so they must be fixed biases rather than per-token terms. ## Modifications All changes are gated on the same `is_unified_kv_triton()` / `_unified_kv` switch the pool itself uses, so sizing and allocation cannot drift apart. **No behavior change on the non-unified (fp8) path.** ### Pool sizing (`pool_configurator.py`) - Use bf16 full-latent bytes for the per-token coeff on the unified path (`_get_bytes_per_full_token`). - Exclude SWA from the per-token coeff and account for it as a fixed bias (`_fixed_swa_bytes`), inflated for the speculative draft worker the same way as the coeff. - Move the **c4 compress-state (attn + indexer)** off the per-token coeff and size it as a request-scoped fixed bias (`_fixed_c4_state_bytes` / `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`), finalized once `max_running_requests` is known — mirroring the c128 state pool. Subtract it from the token budget and log `c4_state_fixed`. - Factor the `max_running_requests`-per-worker resolution into a shared helper (`_resolve_max_running_requests_per_worker`) reused by the c128 state, SWA ring, and c4 state fixed-byte terms. - Log the SWA ring and c4-state fixed biases alongside the existing c128 fixed bias. ### Memory pool (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`) - Clamp `c4_state_pool_size` up to `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size` as a safety net (mirrors the c128 clamp). ### SWA idle accounting on the unified ring - `model_runner`: reconcile `swa_max_total_num_tokens` down to the allocator ring capacity (`swa_available_size`) so the idle pool-leak invariant matches the fixed per-request SWA ring (gated on unified_kv; no real buffer is resized). - `invariant_checker`: skip the SWA token-pool leak invariant on the unified ring — its `available` is non-binding and cached radix prefixes report a spurious `swa_evictable`, so `available + evictable + protected == total` does not hold; ring slots are still covered by the `req_to_token` leak check. - `pool_stats_observer`: zero `swa_evictable` on the unified ring so `swa_num_used` / `swa_token_usage` stay coherent (cached prefixes hold no ring slot). ### Review-fix follow-ups - Detect unified-KV via the canonical `get_kvcache()._unified_kv` (the previous `getattr(alloc, "_unified", ...)` was always `False` on the wrapped allocators — thanks @amd-danli103). Applied consistently in `invariant_checker`, `pool_stats_observer`, and `schedule_batch`. - Unwrap `logical_attn_allocator` in the `_check_kv_page_invariants` sub-allocator probe so the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper reaches its inner full/swa allocators. - `schedule_policy`: align the `add_one_req` SWA admission gate (`>=` -> `>`) with `add_one_req_ignore_eos` so an exact-fit request is admitted. ## Accuracy / Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv` + EAGLE MTP (speculative), TP8 / DP8, ROCm**. <details> <summary>Server launch command</summary> ```bash export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=false export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS=true export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=false export SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS_TRITON=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_OPT_FP4_MOE_K_ALIGN=128 export SGLANG_DSV4_INDEXER_K_CACHE_PRESHUFFLE=1 export SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY=false export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --tp 8 \ --dp 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-cache-report \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --max-running-request 2048 \ --page-size 256 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --port 30001 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --enable-prefill-delayer ``` </details> <details> <summary>Client / bench_serving command</summary> ```bash NUM_PROMPT=2048 INPUT_LEN=50 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --dataset-name random \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompt ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --max-concurrency ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --random-input $((INPUT_LEN * 1024)) \ --random-output 1024 \ --port 30001 ``` </details> ### Pool sizing (startup) `unified=True`, `bytes_per_full_token=9064` (spec-inflated), `c128_state_fixed=7.83 GB`, `swa_ring_fixed=1.99 GB`, `c4_state_fixed=1.21 GB` — matches the bf16 layout + request-scoped fixed rings. Non-unified (fp8) path logs/sizes are unchanged. | full_token | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | capacity | 8, 898, 560 | 12,047,104 | ### Stress (`bench_serving`, random) 1800 prompts × 51200-token input, 500-token output, concurrency 1800 (92.16M input tokens). - **1800 / 1800 requests completed, 0 crashes / 0 pool-leak errors** across the full run. - Peak `full token usage` 0.96 (previously the saturation zone that tripped idle/leak asserts). - Peak concurrent requests 1800. - MTP accept length 3.07; total token throughput 44,415 tok/s. ### Throughput (8k in / 1k out, concurrency 1024) | config | Total token throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before | 4523.21 | 89981.16 | 130.75 | | apply PR | 4559.63 | 90483.00 | 129.75 | ### GSM8K (5-shot,) **accuracy 0.950, invalid 0.000** — confirms the sizing / SWA-accounting changes do not affect correctness. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269389637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269389637)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269389057](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269389057)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Add MiniCPM-SALA support
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add native serving support for MiniCPM-SALA checkpoints, which interleave MiniCPM sparse softmax-attention layers with constant-decay Lightning linear-attention layers. The implementation integrates the model with SGLang's existing attention, linear-attention, CUDA graph, and memory-pool infrastructure. It also replaces the serving-time dependency on the original out-of-tree block-table extension with SGLang JIT kernels. ## Modifications - Add `MiniCPMHybridConfig` and register both `MiniCPMForCausalLM` and `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. - Normalize mixer aliases and repeat mixer patterns to the configured layer count. - Parse both flattened and legacy nested sparse-attention configuration. - Describe Lightning state using the existing `Mamba2CacheParams` and linear-attention model registry. - Extend the MiniCPM model with SALA mixer support. - Add Lightning QKV projection, optional Q/K normalization, RoPE, output normalization and gating, configurable attention scaling, and checkpoint-compatible weight loading. - Reuse the in-tree Lightning backend and `seg_la` kernels instead of introducing a model-specific linear-attention backend or external dependency. - Generalize the shared Lightning backend to read the linear KV-head count, layerwise decay mode, and per-layer attention scale from the model config. - Add `minicpm_flashattn` and `minicpm_flashinfer` sparse-attention backends. - Compose with `FlashAttentionBackend` for dense metadata and CUDA graph state. - Keep FlashInfer support as a composed decode path rather than duplicating its wrapper management. - Select FA4 automatically on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Support dense/sparse prefill and decode, CUDA graph capture/replay, K1/K2 key compression, sparse top-k selection, and optional fused TileLang kernels. - Add JIT-compiled CUDA block-table kernels. - Use v2 for prefill and v3 for the optimized decode layout, with automatic v2 fallback for unsupported v3 shapes. - Cache compiled modules by top-k, head-group count, and block size. - Attach the MiniCPM compressed cache to the existing `ReqToTokenPool`. - Reserve and account for K1/K2 capacity without introducing a model-specific pool subclass. - Route extend/decode allocation, rollback, request release, streaming-session cleanup, allocator reset, and pool statistics through generic no-op auxiliary-cache hooks. - Add MiniCPM model overrides and developer controls. - Default sparse SALA models to `minicpm_flashattn`, or `minicpm_flashinfer` on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Disable radix caching only for configs that actually contain sparse or Lightning layers. - Reject unsupported sparse-attention PD disaggregation early. - Add `SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSE_TOPK`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_SPLIT_STAGE1`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_DENSE_AS_SPARSE`, and `SGLANG_MINICPM_FORCE_DENSE` environment switches. - Add CPU and CUDA coverage for configuration defaults, model overrides, Lightning dispatch, compressed-cache lifecycle, sparse metadata, block-table kernels, and compression kernels. ## Accuracy Tests The following CPU regression suite passes on the final rebased branch: ```text 112 passed, 8 subtests passed ``` It covers: - MiniCPM config parsing, mixer selection, Lightning cache shape, scaling, and idle batches. - Sparse metadata construction, CUDA graph padding, and dense/sparse batch accounting. - K1/K2 allocation boundaries, reuse, rollback, cleanup, and streaming-session release. - Backend defaults, force-dense remapping, radix-cache gating, and unsupported PD disaggregation. CUDA correctness tests are included for: - v2/v3 block-table outputs against a PyTorch reference. - Sparse key compression against a PyTorch reference. End-to-end checkpoint output accuracy has not yet been recorded on the final rebased branch and should be added before merge. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/bench_get_block_table.py` benchmarks the v2 prefill and v3 decode block-table kernels across token counts. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32104040964](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32104040964)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32104040781](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32104040781)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [DSV4] Fix SWA state pool over-allocation by using storage page size instead of model window
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation For DeepSeek-V4 models, DSV4PoolConfigurator sizes the c4 compressed-state pool using the model's SWA window (cfg.window_size = 128), while the runtime addresses that same pool using the pool's SWA storage page size (server_args.page_size = 256). These two values differ by 2x, causing capacity waste. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications Align the state-pool paging to the SWA storage page size (server_args.page_size), consistent with how DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool and CompressStatePool address the pool at runtime: self.swa_storage_page_size = mr.server_args.page_size # 256 c4_state_ratio = self.c4_ring_size / self.swa_storage_page_size c4_state_pool_size = swa_tokens // self.swa_storage_page_size * self.c4_ring_size A comment is added to disambiguate this storage page size from the model's SWA window (cfg.window_size / SWA_WINDOW = 128). This is not a correctness bug — the runtime already divides by 256, so the smaller pool stays within bounds; it purely recovers wasted capacity. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling Validated on GB200 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP4 / DP4, default config, mem-fraction-static unconstrained). signals.title: [Refactor] New EPD
signals.text: ## Motivation The EPD encoder had grown into a single 4464-line `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py` that owned the FastAPI application, the DP launcher, the request scheduler, CPU preprocessing, the GPU forward, and both transfer backends at the same time. That coupling caused three concrete problems: **1. Duplicated orchestration.** HTTP non-DP and DP workers each maintained their own copy of encode scheduling, batch/direct branching, backend detection, metadata publication, embedding staging, send scheduling, error handling, resource release and metrics updates. On top of that: - single-request and batch encode had two separate implementations; - Mooncake, ZMQ-to-scheduler and ZMQ-to-tokenizer each carried near-identical send logic; - `send` and `release` were tightly coupled, and embedding cleanup was scattered across the normal, error and timeout branches. **2. Unsafe resource lifetimes.** Because `send` implicitly released embeddings and cleanup lived in several places, concurrent encode / send / release had no ordering guarantee: a release racing an in-flight forward could tear down state that a pending send still needed, and a failed encode could leave a `send` waiting forever. **3. No layer to build on.** There was no protocol-neutral home for scheduling, so gRPC could not reuse the HTTP backend topology, and neither the CPU preprocessing nor the HTTP layer could be replaced by a Rust implementation. This PR restructures the encoder into a package with explicit layers and unifies everything after `receive` into a single pipeline, while keeping the external HTTP/gRPC surface unchanged. ## Modifications ## 2. One inference lifecycle for every path Everything after `receive` now follows a single chain, identically for HTTP non-DP and for DP workers: ``` receive (protocol-specific entry point) → execute_encode_pipeline → MMEncoder.encode / batch_encode → acquire encode ref → preprocess → publish metadata → model forward → stage embedding → release encode ref → delivery.send → release_request ``` - `encode()` becomes a batch-of-one call into `batch_encode()`, so there is no second encode implementation. `EncoderScheduler` only decides *whether* requests coalesce into a batch. - `execute_encode_pipeline()` owns metrics and tracing, direct-vs-batched dispatch, metadata publication, the `MMEncoder` call, final metadata sync, the ZMQ synchronous send or the Mooncake metadata response, and resource release on the normal, error and timeout paths. - `ReqState` holds the whole per-request lifecycle: `embedding_data`, `embedding_ready`, `active_encodes`, `active_sends`, `release_requested`, `preserve_metadata_on_release`, `lifecycle_condition`, driven by `_acquire_encode_ref()` / `_release_encode_ref()`. The resulting guarantees: - a release issued during encode cannot delete request state early; - a release waits until `active_sends == 0`; - once a release is requested, new sends are rejected; - a shared embedding is freed only after all destinations have finished; - a failed encode still stages the error, so a waiting `send` can never block forever. - `EncoderDelivery` isolates the backend differences. The previous `ZmqSchedulerDelivery` and `ZmqTokenizerDelivery` collapse into one `ZmqDelivery` parameterized by `cleanup_receive_state`; `self.transfer_backend` / `self.use_mooncake` are cached on `MMEncoder` instead of re-reading `server_args.encoder_transfer_backend` all over the code. - `embedding_to_send.pop()`, `discard_embedding()`, handler-`finally` cleanup, the Mooncake callback cleanup and the ZMQ rendezvous cleanup all collapse into `release_request()`. - Mooncake marks an embedding ready **only after the CUDA stream is synchronized**, so an RDMA read can no longer observe a GPU buffer whose write has not landed. Global-cache embeddings keep their existing per-send registration semantics. ### 3. Metadata is published right after preprocess Every backend publishes embedding shape, dtype and size as soon as preprocessing completes — before the forward runs. At that point `ReqState.embedding_data` holds a metadata placeholder; the real embedding is staged and validated afterwards, which is what sets `embedding_ready`. For Mooncake non-DP this lets the receiver call `/scheduler_receive_meta_data`, then allocate and register its landing buffer **in parallel with the encoder forward**; the RDMA transfer itself still waits for `embedding_ready`. ZMQ publishes the same metadata today, but has no early consumer yet. ### 4. Preprocessing metadata consolidated `EncoderPreprocessResult` returns `mm_inputs`, `grid_thw` and `token_counts` together. Grid normalization and patch/token counting move out of `MMEncoder` into `EncoderPreprocessor`, so `process_mm_items` parses the grid exactly once and the direct, cache, Mooncake and batch paths reuse the same result. `slice_embedding` and `_encode_missing` no longer recompute token counts from the grid. ### 5. Receiver: one embedding pool for both backends - `EmbeddingPool` absorbs `MooncakeEmbeddingPool` and gains `try_stage` / `release_on_gc`. When `SGLANG_EMBEDDING_POOL_SIZE_MB` is set explicitly, `zmq_to_scheduler` also keeps received embeddings resident in the GPU pool: zero-copy per-modality views, slot lifetime bound to `mm_inputs` garbage collection, and a `PENDING` retry when the pool is full. **Default behaviour is unchanged** — the 4096 MB default still applies to Mooncake only. - RDMA buffer release becomes an ownership transfer to the receiving thread, which removes an up-to-1800 s `join` block on the scheduler main thread. - `WaitingMMRequestBase` (ABC) unifies `recv_embedding`; the backend differences shrink to three abstract methods — `send_encode_request`, `_extract_embedding_from_buffer`, `_prepare_embedding_buffer`. Seven separate failure paths merge into `_fail_and_release`, and the classes are renamed off "Image" into the `Zmq` / `Grpc` / `RDMA` families. - Dead code on the `zmq_to_tokenizer` path is removed. ## EPD performance results ### Common workload - 4 random 1080p JPEG images per request - Random input length 1024, output length 64 - Temperature 0, request rate `inf` - Radix cache and MM global cache disabled - Paired values below are `main/new_epd` ## Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ### Test setup - One 8×H20 node - Encoder TP1 on GPU 0–1; Language TP1 on GPU 2 - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.60 - `single`: client concurrency 1, scheduler max batch 1, 8 requests per round - `batch`: client concurrency 4, scheduler max batch 4, 16 requests per round - Each case used 2 warmup requests followed by 3 measured rounds - Results are the median of the 3 rounds - `zmq_to_scheduler` used a 4096 MB embedding pool ### Results | Encoder DP | Path | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | single | Tokenizer | 0.288/0.294 | 3058/2976 | 6.774/6.783 | | 1 | single | Scheduler | 0.293/0.362 | 2990/2331 | 6.786/6.775 | | 1 | single | Mooncake | 0.368/0.403 | 2280/2047 | 6.783/6.778 | | 1 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.447/0.448 | 7095/7076 | 19.498/19.452 | | 1 | batch | Scheduler | 0.436/0.519 | 7476/5945 | 19.439/18.077 | | 1 | batch | Mooncake | 0.525/0.566 | 5860/5352 | 19.421/19.429 | | 2 | single | Tokenizer | 0.282/0.297 | 3122/2934 | 6.780/6.776 | | 2 | single | Scheduler* | 0.334/0.362 | 2556/2343 | 6.777/6.776 | | 2 | single | Mooncake | 0.366/0.402 | 2299/2058 | 6.784/6.779 | | 2 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.488/0.487 | 6369/6367 | 28.541/28.516 | | 2 | batch | Scheduler* | 0.478/0.582 | 6708/5121 | 26.301/27.547 | | 2 | batch | Mooncake | 0.591/0.636 | 4975/4574 | 28.569/26.525 | \* For DP2 Scheduler, main used two independent TP1/DP1 Encoders, while new_epd used one internal TP1/DP2 Encoder. ## Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 ### Test setup - Two 8×H20 nodes - Language TP8 and Encoder deployed on separate nodes - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.70 - `DP4`: one TP1/DP4 Encoder process and one Encoder URL - `4×DP1`: four independent TP1/DP1 Encoders and four Encoder URLs - Concurrency 1: 16 warmup and 16 measured requests - Concurrency 8/32: 32 warmup and 64 measured requests - Results below use the second measured round - Scheduler embedding pool: 4096 MB ### Configurations | Client concurrency / scheduler max batch | Encoder layout | Encoder URLs | |---|---|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | 1 | | 8/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | 4 | ### Results | Concurrency / max batch | Layout | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | Tokenizer | 0.555/0.532 | 1438/1444 | 5.227/5.521 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Scheduler | 0.536/0.554 | 1470/1388 | 5.287/5.357 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Mooncake | 0.579/0.634 | 1315/1216 | 5.550/5.468 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.487/1.495 | 4179/4183 | 18.838/18.889 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.543 | —/3864 | —/19.014 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/1.761 | —/3339 | —/19.010 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.568/1.651 | 3398/2815 | 18.652/33.909 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.358/1.464 | 4323/4158 | 19.737/19.054 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 1.865/1.910 | 2965/2718 | 20.067/18.725 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.605/1.687 | 12621/11471 | 85.097/97.416 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.585 | —/13857 | —/96.598 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/2.246 | —/7814 | —/95.164 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.683/1.603 | 11529/12062 | 112.268/122.776 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.341/1.389 | 16667/13518 | 108.282/108.752 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.126/2.310 | 8433/7584 | 109.113/95.207 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.625/1.656 | 12093/11577 | 96.304/93.734 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.551/1.607 | 12602/13285 | 115.445/96.704 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.101/2.112 | 8615/8826 | 100.019/69.134 | `—` denotes an unsupported main DP4 combination. ### Known limitations in `main` - `main` does not support the `zmq_to_scheduler` path with Encoder DP enabled. - On the Mooncake path, enabling Encoder DP while running the Language service with TP greater than 1 causes request routing and embedding-lifecycle errors. These combinations were therefore not included as valid `main/new_epd` performance pairs. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Bugfix][DSA] Fix num_splits (b+1) crash with DP-attention + speculative decode
signals.text: Motivation Fixes [#30296](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30296). Enabling DP-attention (attn_tp_size > 1) together with speculative decode on a DSA model (DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x) crashes in the FlashMLA decode kernel with num_splits must have shape (b+1). Root cause: cal_padded_tokens (which sizes num_splits) only aligns the token count to cp_align_size, missing the attn_tp_size align that prepare_mlp_sync_batch applies to q. On the spec path the DSA metadata is planned pre-pad and not re-planned, so num_splits ends up shorter than the padded q whenever num_draft_tokens * batch_size isn't a multiple of attn_tp_size. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324174466](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324174466)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324173815](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324173815)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation Integrates TRT-LLM attention kernel for DSv4 style attention (CSA, HCA). ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ``` SGLANG_DSV4_ATTN_DECODE_BACKEND=flashmla/trtllm_gen \ python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 32 ``` ### GSM8K Accuracy GSM8K V4-Pro flashmla: 0.965 GSM8K V4-Pro trtllm_gen: 0.985 ### GPQA (add --chat-template to above server command) ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 21000 --eval-name gpqa \ --num-examples 198 --max-tokens 120000 --repeat 8 \ --thinking-mode deepseek-v3 ``` FlashMLA: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.885 Scores: ['0.889', '0.879', '0.889', '0.879', '0.869', '0.899', '0.904', '0.874'] TRTLLM: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.907 Scores: ['0.919', '0.904', '0.894', '0.904', '0.909', '0.919', '0.904', '0.904'] ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Unit Kernel Benchmarking (ran with private benchmarking repo): ``` # prefill (varlen), long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode prefill --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,2 --seq-lens 4096,16384,65536 --graph # decode, low/mid concurrency x long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,4,16,64 --seq-lens 1024,4096,16384,65536,131072 --graph # decode, high concurrency python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 128,256,512,1024 --seq-lens 256,1024,4096,16384 --graph ``` Prefill: ~1.2x faster Decode: ~1.45x faster The performance for TP > 1 scales better on trtllm-gen, since it seems the flashmla variant requires padding the head_dim to 64 or 128. I've attached some sample graphs showing the kernel perf comparison. ### E2E bench-serving ```bash python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 128 \ --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 4 ``` flashmla: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 59.92 Total input tokens: 1048576 Input token throughput (tok/s): 17500.55 Mean E2E Latency (ms): 29950.67 Mean TTFT (ms): 19009.87 (median 19636.34) Mean TPOT (ms): 86.15 Median ITL (ms): 12.12 ``` trtllm_gen: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 60.09 Total input tokens: 1048576 Input token throughput (tok/s): 17448.78 Mean E2E Latency (ms): 30039.27 Mean TTFT (ms): 16808.71 (median 15734.66) Mean TPOT (ms): 104.18 Median ITL (ms): 13.11 ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Benchmark] Add optional steady-state window for serving metrics
signals.text: ## Motivation The serving benchmark currently calculates metrics over the entire benchmark duration. This includes the initial request ramp-up and final drain phases, where request concurrency is lower. As a result, throughput and other aggregate metrics may not accurately represent performance under sustained load. This PR adds an optional continuous steady-state measurement window and applies it consistently across serving benchmark metrics. ## Modifications - Add the `--steady-state-concurrency-ratio` option to `bench_serving`. - Define the steady-state concurrency threshold as: ```text ceil(observed peak concurrency × steady-state-concurrency-ratio) ``` The minimum steady-state concurrency is calculated as: ceil(observed peak concurrency × steady-state-concurrency-ratio) The measurement window: Starts when active request concurrency first reaches the threshold. Ends when concurrency falls below the threshold for the last time. Remains continuous, so temporary concurrency drops inside the window are retained. For example: python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --steady-state-concurrency-ratio 0.8 \ ... The accepted range is (0, 1]. ## Metrics calculated within the window When steady-state measurement is enabled: - Successful requests and request throughput use requests completed within the window. - Input token throughput uses successful requests started within the window. - Output token throughput uses output tokens generated within the window. - Total token throughput combines input and output tokens measured within the window. - TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and E2E latency statistics use requests completed within the window. - Average and peak concurrency are restricted to the window. - Peak output token throughput only uses one-second buckets inside the window. - Cache statistics use requests started within the window. - Throughput plots are restricted to the same window. Output token timestamps are reconstructed using request start time, TTFT, and ITL. Since a streaming chunk may contain multiple tokens, timestamp events are weighted using the server-reported output token count. Output metadata The benchmark output additionally reports: - Steady-state duration (s) - Steady-state min concurrency In JSONL output: - duration represents the actual metric measurement duration. - benchmark_duration preserves the complete benchmark runtime. - steady_state_duration records the steady-state window duration. - steady_state_concurrency_threshold records the calculated concurrency threshold. Backward compatibility Steady-state measurement is disabled by default. When --steady-state-concurrency-ratio is not specified, all metrics retain the original full-benchmark behavior, including: - The original measurement duration. - The original throughput calculations. - The original latency sample selection. - The original peak throughput and concurrency calculations. - The original cache statistics. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32233981401](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233981401)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32233981201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233981201)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
