signals.title: [AMD] Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode (batched bh16bn128).
signals.text: Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode on gfx950 for Kimi-K3 TP8 (12 local heads). If aiter is not updated to the target version, fall back to use the existing zero-pad + mla_decode_fwd. No behavior change on older containers until aiter/Triton are upgraded. below is the dependency: **aiter runtime dependencies** (container/image, not pinned in this repo): - [ROCm/aiter#4480](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4480) (**merged** to `main`, [`fb82bf7`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/fb82bf7e20adaa9918c9d4bc80e4ff91f000823e)): fp8 Gluon `bh16bn128`, batch>1. - [ROCm/aiter#4555](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4555) (on `main`): decode CUDA graph KV-split budget. - Triton >= 3.7: Gluon `cga_layout` on gfx950. ## Motivation Kimi-K3 at TP8 exposes 12 MLA heads/GPU. The fast aiter persist decode ASM wants head counts divisible by 16 and has no native fp8 12-head path, so fp8 serving had to zero-pad to 16 and go through slower kernels — especially painful at long context under decode CUDA graph. aiter already has a Gluon kernel with a native 12-head masked MFMA tile and an fp8 KV regime (bh16bn128). This PR connects it. ## Modifications - **`aiter_mla_gluon.py`**: thin wrapper + runtime probe (import + Triton `cga_layout` >= 3.7). Logs once at init; returns None → caller falls back. - **`aiter_backend.py`**: h12 head validation (zero-pad mode), decode routing (`_forward_mla_decode`), graph-safe `min_kv_seq_len`, disable slow 16-head persist for h12+fp8, prefill zero-pad Q for h12. - **`forward_mla_rocm.py`**: keep bf16 Q on prefill when fp8 KV (Gluon needs it). - **`test_mla_gluon_h12_fp8.py`**: CPU tests for probe gating and fallback. Scope is **decode only** (`max_q_len==1`, h12, fp8 KV). Prefill unchanged aside from zero-pad Q routing. h=12 KV write is already on main (#34837). ## Accuracy Tests Validated on MI355, Kimi-K3, --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3, --attention-backend aiter, decode CUDA graph enabled (rocm720-mi35x-20260811 image + aiter fb82bf7e2 (aiter PR 4480 merged)): GSM8K: 95.5–95.6% accuracy ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### long-context test(ISL>50K)(radix cache ON) — primary win With this PR, output token/s/gpu has 94%-168% improvement compares to baseline. Baseline: triton attention backend, bf16 kv cache. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260805 This PR stack: fp8 kv cache, Gluon decode, aiter prefill. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260811 ### 8k1k (non-Dspark, disable-radix-cache) With this PR, TTT has 4-10% improvement compares to baseline when c=4/8/16/32. Baseline: triton attention backend, bf16 kv cache. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260805 This PR stack: fp8 kv cache, Gluon decode, aiter prefill. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260811 Compare against 0805 rather than 0811 triton because 0811 image regresses ~10% TTT vs 0805 at high concurrency. | Concurrency | TP | TTT (tok/s) | TTT per GPU (tok/s/gpu) | Output Tput (tok/s) | Median E2EL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | vs 0805 TTT/gpu | vs 0805 ITL | |------------:|---:|------------:|------------------------:|--------------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|----------------:|----------------:|------------:| | 2 | 8 | 810.2 | 101.3 | 90.0 | 18,738.8 | 537.5 | 18.9 | 18.4 | 0.92× | 0.95× | | 4 | 8 | 1,654.5 | 206.8 | 182.4 | 19,757.5 | 536.5 | 21.1 | 19.6 | 1.04× | 0.95× | | 8 | 8 | 2,652.2 | 331.5 | 291.5 | 23,603.9 | 537.1 | 25.5 | 22.0 | 1.05× | 0.90× | | 16 | 8 | 4,145.6 | 518.2 | 464.8 | 31,279.1 | 541.1 | 32.6 | 25.2 | 1.07× | 0.87× | | 32 | 8 | 5,928.8 | 741.1 | 654.8 | 43,986.3 | 558.4 | 47.2 | 31.5 | **1.10×** | **0.85×** | ## Checklist - signals.title: Fix guided decoding for channel-framed reasoning
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34631. Channel-framed reasoning formats such as Muse Glimmer emit an answer-channel header after the reasoning end marker. Guided decoding currently resumes as soon as `<|eom|>` is accepted, so the JSON grammar constrains the model-written `<|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>` header instead of starting at the answer body. ## Modifications - Add optional detector-declared markers for the channel-header boundary and for identifying another reasoning channel. - Opt Muse Glimmer into the channel-header transition. - Add an intermediate state that leaves channel headers unconstrained and does not feed them to the inner grammar. - Preserve state correctly across `copy()` and speculative rollback, including rollback that spans thinking, channel-header, and generation states. - Add `SGLANG_MAX_CHANNEL_HEADER_TOKENS` as an opt-in fail-safe (default: unlimited; positive values resume guided decoding when a malformed header never closes). This avoids rearming early for long, valid tool or recipient names. - Keep per-token channel rollback history only for channel-aware detectors; non-channel detectors retain the previous lightweight rollback accounting. - Keep direct transitions unchanged for all other detectors and for requests without reasoning. - Add 15 off-server unit cases covering answer and repeated-reasoning channels, long headers, fail-safe behavior, multi-token markers, direct generation, copy, rollback, and non-channel memory behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable to model forward accuracy. The state-machine regression checks pass in an isolated CPU-only harness, including the reproduction's grammar arming boundary and rollback behavior. The repository pytest module cannot be collected on this macOS development host because SGLang imports Triton at package initialization and Triton is not available on macOS. It fails before any test code executes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change adds only small token-sequence matchers while a detector explicitly waits for a channel header; all existing detectors retain the direct transition. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted the changed files with Black and checked them with Ruff. - [x] Added unit tests for the new behavior and compatibility paths. - [x] Followed the existing reasoning grammar and environment-variable conventions. - [x] Documentation is not required; this is an internal parser boundary and the fail-safe environment variable is documented inline with the existing environment settings. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324890929](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324890929)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324890657](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324890657)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] Support MegaMoE FuseEP mode for Kimi-K3
signals.text: ## Motivation Enable the Ascend MegaMoE fused dispatch/GEMM/combine path for ModelSlim W4A8 Kimi-K3. The existing NPU FuseEP modes cover the W8A8 paths, while the validated W4A8 deployment needs a separate MegaMoE weight ABI and operator backend. ## Modifications - Add `--fuseep-mode 3` and keep the deprecated environment-variable compatibility in sync. - Route mode 3 through `deep_ep.Buffer.fused_deep_moe` with `backend="mega_moe"` and the Kimi-K3 SiTU activation parameters. - Convert ModelSlim W4A8 expert weights, scales, and biases into the per-expert MegaMoE ABI. - Share FuseEP weight processing between the W8A8 and W4A8 MoE quantization methods. - Add NPU unit coverage for CLI parsing, mode-3 operator routing, and W4A8 weight conversion. ## Accuracy Tests - Targeted mocked NPU unit test on this rebased commit: `3 passed`. - Four-node Kimi-K3 validation of the mode-3 implementation: GPQA Diamond `94.95%` (`188/198`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Four-node Kimi-K3, concurrency 1, 128K input with a verified 115,200-token (90%) prefix-cache hit and 1K output: - TTFT: `9952.8 ms` - TPOT: `38.4 ms` - E2EL: `48300.8 ms` - Output throughput: `20.7036 token/s` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: fix(constrained): reject NUL bytes in grammar specs to stop an xgrammar segfault
signals.text: ## Motivations A `regex` beginning with a NUL byte kills the server. xgrammar's regex converter appends its own NUL terminator and indexes past it, raising **SIGSEGV** — an OS signal, so the `except RuntimeError` in `dispatch_regex` cannot catch it. The scheduler dies with `exit code -11` and all later requests are refused. ```python python3 -c 'import xgrammar; xgrammar.Grammar.from_regex(chr(0))' # SIGSEGV ``` Two measured details: - Trigger is a **leading** NUL, not control characters generally — `\x01`, `\x02`, `\x1f` and non-leading NUL all compile fine. Rejecting all control characters would break valid patterns like `[\t\n]+`. - A **JSON schema reaches the same converter via `pattern`**, where the NUL may be an escape (`\u0000`) — no NUL byte in the request body at all. Guarding only `regex` leaves that path open. No release fixes it: 0.2.0-0.2.4 and 0.2.6rc1 all crash on the `regex` path (`regex_converter.cc` is unchanged v0.2.5 through HEAD). ## Modifications - `base_grammar_backend.py`: `_grammar_key_contains_nul()`, called at the top of `_init_value_dispatch` — the choke point for all four grammar types and every backend. Returns `InvalidGrammarObject`, which flows through the existing failure path to the same clean error an invalid pattern already gets. For `json`/`structural_tag` the spec is decoded and walked, so an escaped `\u0000` in a nested `pattern` is caught; malformed JSON falls through to the backend's own error. Placed at the dispatcher, not `xgrammar_backend.py`, because the JSON path reaches the same native code and a segfault cannot be caught after the fact. - `test_base_grammar_backend.py`: `TestNulByteGrammarRejection` — NUL specs rejected without the backend being called (`regex` and JSON `pattern`, raw and escaped, plus a non-leading NUL so the guard can't be narrowed to `startswith()`); valid patterns, non-NUL control characters and malformed JSON still dispatch normally. A NUL has no meaning in a regex, schema or grammar, so no legitimate request is affected. Verified on aarch64/GB200: the file passes **33 tests / 17 subtests** with no regressions; the new cases fail 8/8 without the guard; on a live server the two crashing payloads go from killing the process to **HTTP 400**, `/health` 200, no segfault markers. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no change to kernels or the model forward path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — one substring check per uncached grammar compilation (for JSON, a parse the backend already performs). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing API change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32308365762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32308365762)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32308365506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32308365506)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Speed up Wan2.2 DiT FP8 attention per-tensor quantization
signals.text: ## Motivation When the DiT FP8 attention path is enabled (`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_AITER_FP8_ATTN=1`), the AITER attention backend quantizes q/k/v with `aiter.per_tensor_quant`. That function is a PyTorch reference implementation: it upcasts the activation to fp32 and then runs `abs` / `max` / `div` / `cast` as four more eager kernels. For the Wan2.2 self-attention shape (`[1, 90000, 40, 128]` bf16, 0.9 GB) that is five kernels and ~14 GB of memory traffic per tensor, against a ~2.3 GB floor. Profiling a Wan2.2-T2V-A14B run showed this tail accounting for 9.5% of total GPU time — the second largest block after the FMHA kernel itself. The obvious fix is to switch to one of aiter's fused per-tensor quant kernels, but neither is usable here. `per_tensor_quant_hip` and `per_tensor_quant_triton` are per-token kernels reused for per-tensor: both decompose over rows of `size(-1)` and reduce the amax with a single `atomicMax`. With `head_dim=128` that is one workgroup per 128 elements — 3.6M workgroups contending on one fp32. Measured runtime scales linearly with row count, making the "fused" kernels 12x *slower* than the eager reference at this shape: | view | rows (grid) | HIP | Triton | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `[..., 128]` (natural) | 3,600,000 | 41.9 ms | 42.4 ms | | `[-1, 1024]` | 450,000 | 5.35 ms | 5.42 ms | | `[-1, 16384]` | 28,125 | 0.61 ms | 0.63 ms | The reduction needs to be decomposed over elements, not rows. This PR does that with `torch.aminmax`. ## Modifications - Add `_per_tensor_quant_fp8` to `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`: a `torch.compile`d dynamic per-tensor FP8 E4M3 quantizer. `torch.aminmax` obtains the amax in one reduction without materializing `abs(x)`, and inductor fuses the rescale and the fp8 cast into a single pass, reaching the 2.3 GB traffic floor. - Use it for the q/k/v quantization in `AITerImpl.forward` in place of `aiter.per_tensor_quant`. No other behavior changes; the BF16 path and the shape-eligibility fallback are untouched. - `dynamic=False` is deliberate and load-bearing: with `dynamic=True` the op measured 0.93 ms instead of 0.61 ms *and* stopped being bit-exact. This is noted in the docstring so it is not "cleaned up" later. ## Accuracy Tests The new implementation is **bit-exact** with `aiter.per_tensor_quant` — not merely close. Verified two ways. Standalone, against the aiter reference (`ndiff` = number of differing elements): | shape | layout | ndiff | scale match | |---|---|---:|---| | `[1, 90000, 40, 128]` | contiguous | 0 / 460,800,000 | exact | | `[1, 90000, 40, 128]` | transposed (non-contiguous) | 0 / 460,800,000 | exact | | `[1, 512, 40, 128]` | contiguous | 0 / 10,485,760 | exact | In-pipeline, by instrumenting the backend to run both implementations on the real model activations during a Wan2.2-T2V-A14B request: **480 q/k/v tensors, every one `ndiff=0` with identical scales.** Note on output determinism: the generated mp4 is not byte-reproducible across runs of this pipeline even with no code change (two unmodified baseline runs produced different hashes), so output hashing is not a valid equivalence check here. The tensor-level comparison above is the meaningful one. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Kernel level `[1, 90000, 40, 128]` bf16 -> fp8 on MI355X (gfx950): | implementation | time | vs current | |---|---:|---:| | `aiter.per_tensor_quant` (current) | 3.433 ms | 1.00x | | `aiter.per_tensor_quant_hip` | 41.91 ms | 0.08x | | **this PR** | **0.608 ms** | **5.64x** | ### End to end Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 720p / 193 frames / 8 steps on MI355X, warmup excluded. `A` = main, `B` = `A` + #34424 (ROCm VAE Conv2D spatial-parallel fix), `C` = `B` + this PR. **1 GPU** | config | Encoding (s) | Denoising (s) | Decoding (s) | Total (s) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A: baseline | 0.10 | 88.94 | 12.62 | 101.65 | | B: #34424 | 0.10 | 88.92 | 5.14 | 94.15 | | C: #34424 + this PR | 0.10 | 81.11 | 4.85 | 86.05 | | **C - B** | 0.00 | **-7.81 (-8.8%)** | -0.29 | -8.10 (-8.6%) | **2 GPU (CFG parallel)** | config | Encoding (s) | Denoising (s) | Decoding (s) | Total (s) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | B: #34424 | 0.17 | 45.07 | 8.60 | 53.84 | | C: #34424 + this PR | 0.17 | 41.19 | 4.37 | 45.72 | | **C - B** | 0.00 | **-3.88 (-8.6%)** | -4.23 | -8.12 (-15.1%) | Warmup-included end to end, for reference: 1 GPU A 105.23 s -> B 97.67 s (that delta is #34424's VAE fix, not this PR); 2 GPU C 45.73 s. **Denoising is the column attributable to this PR**, and it is consistent across both configurations: -8.8% on 1 GPU and -8.6% on 2 GPU. This change only touches the DiT attention path, so the 2 GPU Decoding delta (8.60 s -> 4.37 s) is **not** caused by it — the 1 GPU run, with the same patch applied, shows Decoding essentially flat (5.14 s -> 4.85 s). Treat the 2 GPU Total of -15.1% as coincidental; the defensible claim is the -8.6~8.8% on Denoising. Repeatability: three separate runs of configuration `C` at 2 GPU gave Denoising of 41.209 s / 41.217 s / 41.229 s (0.05% spread), against 45.172 s / 45.093 s for `B`. A purpose-built Triton kernel (persistent, one program per CU) was also implemented and measured at 0.507 ms — 1.21x faster than this version at the op level, but only 0.33% of Denoising (41.08 s vs 41.22 s). Once the decomposition is fixed, quant is ~1.3 s of a 41 s stage, so codegen quality stops mattering. The eight-line version was chosen for maintainability. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: [bugfix] [NPU] fix transpose batch matmul K*B exceed 65536.
signals.text: ## Motivation `torch_npu.npu_transpose_batchmatmul` provides the numerically validated path for Kimi-K3, but it does not support shapes where the relevant dimension limit is reached. In particular, `B * K` must be smaller than `65536`. Large-prefill workloads can exceed this limit and fail at runtime. ## Changes - Use `torch_npu.npu_transpose_batchmatmul` when all shape constraints are satisfied, including `B * K < 65536`. - Fall back to the previous `torch.ops.npu.batch_matmul_transpose` implementation for unsupported large shapes. - Preserve the validated `torch_npu` path for normal Kimi-K3 workloads. - Replace the following Kimi-K3 environment variables with `ServerArgs` options: - `SGLANG_K3_SHARED_EXPERTS_ATTN_TP` → `--k3-shared-experts-attn-tp` - `SGLANG_K3_DENSE_MLP_ATTN_TP` → `--k3-dense-mlp-attn-tp` ## Accuracy gsm8k for k3 --98%(200). ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [kernel] One rmsnorm kernel for every hidden size, tuned from Python
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Three rmsnorm kernels (`rmsnorm.cuh`, `fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh`, `rmsnorm_hf.cuh`) with three hand-written dispatches covered a fraction of the hidden sizes SGLang serves. `_is_supported_rmsnorm_hidden_size` admitted only multiples of 256 (512 above 8192); fused-add only multiples of 16 up to 8192. **1536, 2304, 2560 — Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-30B, Gemma — all fell back to `forward_native`.** The HF-semantics variant was a separate file only because the flag could not be threaded through, and reaching it cost a `.contiguous()` copy. ## Modifications **One kernel.** `kFusedAdd` and `kCastXBeforeOutMul` become template flags. A tile may over-cover its row: `in_bound` predicates the surplus lanes and folds away entirely when the row divides the tile, so **any even hidden size up to 16384** works. The launcher takes an arbitrary row stride and checks alignment at runtime, which drops the `.contiguous()`. **Schedule moves to Python.** `(vec_size, num_threads, copy_mode)` are the trailing template arguments; C++ only validates them. Retuning now costs one JIT compile per configuration instead of invalidating every module built from the file. Parameterizing by thread count rather than unroll makes padded tiles expressible, and they sometimes win — 5120 gains 17% at batch 1 from a tile that idles 17% of its lanes. **Weight staging (`CopyMode`)**, the one new idea, is taken from [flashinfer's CuTe DSL rmsnorm](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.15.post1/flashinfer/norm/kernels/rmsnorm.py) — credited in the file header. RMSNorm reads its row twice, so something must survive the reduction; flashinfer parks the *input* tile in smem to keep it out of registers. Applying the same trick to the *weight* tile frees `kUnroll` vectors of register file: | config | unroll | registers | cp.async | TMA | |---|---|---|---|---| | rmsnorm 12288, 256t | 6 | 87 | **64** | **64** | | rmsnorm 16384, 128t | 16 | 254 | 154 | 168 | | fused_add 12288, 256t | 6 | 102 | **64** | **63** | 12288/256t crossing 64 registers doubles occupancy, 2 → 4 blocks/SM. `cp.async` fills the tile on SM80+; a single `cp.async.bulk` under `elect.sync` on SM90+. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_rmsnorm.py` + `test_fused_add_rmsnorm.py`: **2587 passed** - A correctness matrix over both kernels x bf16/fp16 x both semantics x padded and exact tiles x warp and CTA traits x block sizes from 16 to 1024: **2160 comparisons, 0 over tolerance**, and all three copy modes **bit-identical** to each other (1296 tensor pairs via `torch.equal`) - `sm_80` and `sm_90` cross-compiles of every schedule the Python side emits; TMA is correctly rejected below sm90 (`Feature 'elect' requires .target sm_90`) - End to end on B200: **Qwen3-8B gsm8k 0.927** (300 examples, TMA path live at dim=4096), Qwen3-0.6B 0.635 ## Benchmarking and Profiling B200, bf16, vs the best configuration found by an exhaustive sweep of the previous kernel: | dim | bs=1024 | bs=4096 | bs=8192 | |---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 0.97x | **1.04x** | 1.01x | | 8192 | **1.08x** | **1.04x** | **1.03x** | | 12288 | **1.03x** | **1.05x** | **1.03x** | | 16384 | 1.01x | **1.07x** | **1.04x** | 16384 at batch 8192 lands at 83.9 us, **matching flashinfer for the first time** (previously 3.6% behind). Small batches keep the existing lead — 3072 is 1.78x flashinfer at batch 4. Staging is worth 1.29x (cp.async) / 1.31x (TMA) over the register path at dim=12288, batch 8192, and nothing below unroll 4. The win is proportional to **unroll**, not to hidden size: 16384's best shapes use many threads and low unroll, so they gain least. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269415529](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269415529)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269415074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269415074)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signals.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [CI] Surface AMD ROCm 7.2 state in the PR CI-states block
signals.text: ## Motivation `pr-states.yml` maintains the **CI States** block at the bottom of every PR body, but it only queries `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml`. A merge oncall reading the PR description therefore sees the CUDA result and nothing else, even though `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` is a full PR gate that most PRs dispatch. ## Modifications One file, `.github/workflows/pr-states.yml`. - New row `Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2)` with its own `<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720 -->` markers, reusing the existing `runIcon` / `runLink` rendering, plus `"PR Test ROCm 7.2 (AMD)"` in the `workflow_run` subscription so the block refreshes when that run is requested and when it completes. The subscription is also what covers fork PRs, whose `pull_request` token is read-only. - **One AMD-specific state.** That workflow has an `on.pull_request.paths` filter, so "no run for this SHA" legitimately means *nothing ROCm-relevant changed*, and it renders as `:heavy_minus_sign: **Not triggered**` rather than the stale-push warning the Extra row uses. There is deliberately no label branch on this row: without `run-ci` a path-matching PR still produces a run (`call-gate` fails it), so a missing run is always the paths filter. For the same reason the AMD lookup does not spend the retry budget — retrying cannot conjure a run that was never dispatched, and since `requested` is in the subscription, a real dispatch refreshes the block on its own. - **Every lookup is now restricted to `event=pull_request`.** All three workflows also accept `workflow_dispatch`, and for the AMD workflow that is how a single stage is re-run. Such a run on a PR branch *is* PR-associated, so an unfiltered `head_sha` query can render one stage as the whole gate — for example [run 32203488998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203488998), a green single-stage `workflow_dispatch` run attached to a PR. A `workflow_run` trigger whose source run is not a `pull_request` run is likewise ignored instead of rewriting the block. This is a behavior change for the two existing rows, in the same direction: a manually dispatched run is no longer reported as the PR gate. - The three lookups now run concurrently, so the added query costs no wall-clock time. Example rendering with `run-ci` present, CUDA green, and a PR that touches no ROCm-relevant paths — which is exactly this PR: ``` ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): ✅ [Run #1](…) Latest PR Test (Extra): ⚠️ **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in. Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): ➖ **Not triggered** -- no ROCm-relevant paths changed. ``` ## Verification The rendering cannot be tested by a PR: `pull_request_target` always runs the **base branch** copy of the workflow, so this branch's version never executes on its own PR. The inline `actions/github-script` body was therefore extracted from the YAML and driven under Node against a mocked Actions API — including the **base-revision script over identical mocks**, which is what pins down the blast radius: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Base and Extra rows vs. base revision, 5 label/run combinations | byte-identical | | Single-stage `workflow_dispatch` run as the AMD gate | no longer shown; base revision did show it | | `workflow_run` from a non-`pull_request` run | zero lookups, zero PATCH | | Skipped / in-progress / failed / cancelled runs | render as before | | API cost of the new row | exactly one extra call, no retry round | | Re-patching an already-patched body | no duplicate block, no redundant PATCH | `check-yaml`, `codespell`, `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py` and the whitespace hooks pass, as does `actionlint`. ## Notes for reviewers Two things this PR deliberately does **not** do. 1. **It adds no `notify-pr-states` job to the AMD workflow.** An earlier revision did, on the assumption that `workflow_run.completed` fires only for the first attempt. That assumption is wrong — [actions/runner#726](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/726) documents that a re-run emits `check_run.created`, `workflow_run.completed` and `check_run.completed`, and only `workflow_run.requested` is missing. A notifier would therefore duplicate every refresh, and because the two paths land in different `concurrency` groups (`pr-states-<head_sha>` for `workflow_run` versus `pr-states-<pr_number>` for `workflow_dispatch`) the duplicates can run concurrently and race on the body PATCH. Keeping the subscription only means this PR touches one file and costs no extra runner. 2. **It does not fix the "empty run reads as green" problem.** When a non-gating label is added, `pr-test-extra`'s `check-changes` is skipped, every test job is skipped, but the `always()` aggregator succeeds — so the run's conclusion is `success` even though nothing ran ([run 32289143314](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32289143314) has exactly this shape). The `skipped` check in `isReal` does not catch it. That predates this PR and affects the existing rows; fixing it needs either a per-run jobs lookup or making those empty runs end as `skipped`, which is a separate change. Same for the existing ambiguity between "`pr-gate` blocked it" and "tests failed", noted in the file's own comment above `runIcon`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI reporting only, no runtime code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — no change to runner allocation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — n/a, no harness exists for inline workflow scripts; tested as described above. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — n/a. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32318437572](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318437572)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32318437369](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318437369)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix integer created_at in Responses streaming events
signals.text: ## Summary - preserve the SDK's typed event validation while normalizing snapshot `created_at` values at final SSE serialization - share the serializer across Harmony and non-Harmony response streams, including `response.failed` - assert that `response.created`, `response.in_progress`, and `response.completed` carry integer timestamps on the wire ## Why SGLang's non-streaming Responses model declares `created_at` as an integer. Streaming snapshots are wrapped in the OpenAI SDK's typed event models, whose nested `Response.created_at` field is a float, so Pydantic serializes the same timestamp with a trailing `.0`. Strict clients can therefore accept non-streaming responses but reject streaming snapshots. Fixes #34716. ## Validation - exact isolated reproduction with SGLang's pinned `openai==2.6.1`: all four snapshot event types serialize as floats before the helper and integers after it; a non-snapshot delta remains byte-for-byte on the existing fast path - `black --check` on both changed files - `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037` on both changed files - `python3 -m py_compile` on both changed files - `git diff --check` The focused SGLang fixture could not run in the local macOS checkout because the full SGLang runtime dependency set is not installed; the regression is registered in the existing CPU CI suite. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31787385060](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31787385060)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31787384954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31787384954)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Validate MiniMax-H3 quality=high on B300
signals.text: ## 0x0. What this PR does Video generation does not need distillation, a different solver, or model surgery to get fast. Keep the weights and the math untouched, be rigorous about *computing less*, and MiniMax-H3 goes from 41.19 s to 11.16 s for a 5-second 1344x768 clip with audio on 8x B300 — with the quality argument written down, gated, and byte-reproducible. Concretely, this PR: - admits the strict 8x B300 TP1/Ulysses8 deployment for MiniMax-H3 request-scoped `quality="high"` - gives each validated deployment its own audited Cache-DiT schedule: 4xH200 keeps the conservative `(4, 0.04, 1)`; **8xB300 ships `(4, 0.08, 3)`**, selected by a parameter sweep on the sglang-native prompt set and gated on LPIPS plus a consecutive-frame temporal review - makes Sol-Attn dense guard steps use the platform-selected FlashAttention implementation (FA4 on Blackwell) and preserves packed-document boundaries on sparse steps - lets the common BCG fail-closed path run before H3 arms Cache-DiT input preservation - documents the protocol, limitations, results, and comparison figure in the cookbook ![MiniMax-H3 B300 quality and latency comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16f604256169b1e9889a3ab4f297883f3f84c15d/docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/assets/minimax-h3-b300-quality-high.png) ## 0x1. Results first Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (SM103). Workload: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA T2VA, 1344x768, 124 frames @24 fps, 50 sigma points, video/audio flow shifts 12/3, sglang-native prompts (cookbook example + two benchmark presets), seeds 0/1/2. Latency is the median of three requests after one warmup. This air-cooled node sits on its 1100 W power cap and its sustained-clock regime drifts intraday (~20% on step time), so only same-session ratios are comparable — every row below was measured back-to-back in one session: | Arm | Median latency | Speedup vs Diffusers | LPIPS mean / max vs SGLang lossless | Decision | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Diffusers BF16 dense + Ulysses8 | 41.19 s | 1.00x | 0.347 / 0.465 | baseline | | SGLang lossless | 23.03 s | 1.79x | 0.000 / 0.000 | exact default | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.04, 1) | 16.45 s | 2.50x | 0.101 / 0.129 | superseded on B300 | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.08, 3) | **11.16 s** | **3.69x** | 0.293 / 0.399 | **admitted** | The admitted path is 2.06x faster than SGLang lossless, and its LPIPS distance (0.293 / 0.399) sits below the distance that already separates the two reference implementations from each other (0.347 / 0.465). Side-by-side frames match the lossless output in content, staging, and lighting on all three prompts. ## 0x2. Where the speedup comes from The 0.08 residual threshold works as an adaptive brake: it sleeps on easy content and forces full computation the moment the trajectory drifts, leaving 21 of 49 full video-tower steps on this prompt set. The conservative 0.04 is too sensitive here (33 full steps on the same prompt, 16.45 s). The consecutive-cache cap barely binds at this threshold — cap 1 at the same threshold is strictly slower at equal quality (11.60 s, LPIPS 0.289 / 0.401) — so cap 3 is used. The schedule is deterministic: fresh server launches on the real `quality="high"` code path reproduce the audited sweep outputs byte-for-byte (md5-verified on all three prompts), so the quality gate transfers exactly to the shipped code. Measured on top of the admitted schedule but not enabled here: SubBlock sparse attention (#34148) composes with Cache-DiT and reaches 10.37 s, and passed a 6/6 production-style serving validation on six unseen prompts. Its blk64 kernel needed two separate fixes, both now proposed upstream in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4533 (open, not merged): a deterministic SM103 scheduling hang, and an intermittent CTA wedge — roughly 1 request in 25 — that turned out to be a named-barrier id collision in the kernel's correction warpgroup. With both applied, 100 consecutive requests ran clean and per-request output md5s became deterministic. That last result revises this arm's quality numbers rather than confirming them: the pre-fix kernel silently produced a differing output on roughly one request in six, so the LPIPS figures behind the 10.37 s arm were measured on a nondeterministic kernel and need re-taking before sparse can default. Latency is unaffected. NVFP4 was evaluated and rejected (LPIPS 0.53+ under the same-seed gate even MLP-only, for at most 6% latency). ## 0x3. Sweep and rejected candidates Every line below was measured, not guessed: - threshold 0.04 with cap 1 (the H200 schedule): 33 full steps, 16.45 s — superseded - wider thresholds: 0.24 never triggers the brake and reaches LPIPS max 0.596 — rejected - cache cap 4: LPIPS max 0.53+ — rejected - warmup 3: no end-to-end win, quality drops — rejected - cached audio tower: audio drift leaks into the video tower through the dual-tower bridge — rejected - TaylorSeer order 1: no measurable gain — rejected - `--minimax-h3-adaln-online` with Cache-DiT: corrupted outputs — disqualified - generic Sol-Attn on SM103: slower than dense cuDNN-SDPA — rejected - FA4 attention backend: 4-15% slower per kernel than cuDNN-SDPA at H3 shapes, end-to-end tie — not adopted ## 0x4. Quality protocol Two gates, both must pass. Gate one: frame-aligned LPIPS (AlexNet) at 1 fps against the bit-exact SGLang lossless output — LPIPS measures same-seed trajectory drift, not absolute quality, so the yardstick is stated explicitly: the two reference implementations already sit 0.347 / 0.465 apart, and drift below that line is treated as insignificant. Gate two: human review of consecutive 4 fps frames against a temporal-artifact taxonomy (flicker, coherence, boundaries, mosaic/static regions, ghosting, broken motion, major blur). ## 0x5. Reproducibility and validation - benchmark source rebased onto `41cd5a718`; Diffusers baseline `bb56997d4`, BF16 eager dense, lossless ContextParallel Ulysses8 only - `PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` -> `25 passed, 1 skipped` on the current head - pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file - fresh-launch byte-exact smoke on 8x B300: three prompts, md5 match against the audited sweep outputs, no environment overrides ## 0x6. Risk and rollback The high-quality admission stays fail-closed to the exact B300 device name/capability, topology, task, shape, schedule, flow shifts, eager mode, and native dense attention. The per-deployment schedule map only distinguishes between already-admitted profiles; H200 behavior is unchanged. Removing the B300 deployment branch restores the previous H200-only admission without touching the lossless default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31934159311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934159311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31934158406](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934158406)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix NPU Ring Attention varlen dispatch & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
signals.text: ## Motivation Ring Attention on Ascend NPU currently breaks when execution reaches the packed variable-length FlashAttention fallback (added for Minimax-H3 support). The shared Ring Attention path uses `flash_attn_varlen_func` for variable-length packed sequences, but that entry point did not have an NPU implementation. As a result, Ring Attention regressed on NPU in the current `main` branch. This PR implement the NPU path by adding Ascend support for packed variable-length attention and wiring it into both the generic FlashAttention compatibility API and the diffusion Ascend attention backend. The implementation is based on the Ascend varlen attention work from [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569), extracted here as a focused Ring Attention compatibility fix. ### Before ### After This PR fix this behavior by implementing this fallback: ## Modifications ### Ascend packed variable-length attention - Add `ascend_fused_infer_attention_varlen`, backed by `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score`. - Use the Ascend `TND` layout with packed sequence boundaries supplied through `actual_seq_lengths` and `actual_seq_lengths_kv`. - Validate Q/K/V layout, device placement, dtype, head dimensions, and cumulative sequence lengths. - Support optional host-side cumulative sequence lengths to avoid unnecessary device-to-host synchronization when they are already available. - Handle empty packed segments and non-contiguous Q/K/V views. - Support returning softmax LSE when requested. ### `flash_attn_varlen_func` NPU dispatch - Route NPU tensors from the generic `flash_attn_varlen_func` compatibility API to the Ascend packed-attention implementation. - Explicitly reject FlashAttention options that are not supported by the Ascend implementation instead of silently producing incorrect behavior. - Leave the existing CUDA/FlashAttention v3 path unchanged. ### Diffusion Ascend attention backend - Implement `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. - Use the shared fused `TND` implementation for non-causal packed attention. - Preserve sequence boundaries for causal attention by processing each packed segment independently through the existing Ascend attention path. ## Accuracy Tests - **Before this PR:** the packed variable-length fallback used by Ring Attention does not have a working NPU implementation. - **After this PR:** the same Ring Attention path successfully dispatches through the Ascend varlen implementation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR is primarily a correctness and dispatch fix; no standalone end-to-end performance benchmark was collected. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [SM12x] Add b12x MoE runner backend for DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on GB10
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4's MXFP4 experts (`fp4_e8m0_k32`) have no fused MoE path on the SM12x family (GB10 / DGX Spark, RTX PRO 6000 class). This PR adds an opt-in `--moe-runner-backend b12x` that maps them onto the b12x W4A16 fused MoE kernels, making DeepSeek-V4-Flash practical to serve on 2x DGX Spark. ## Modifications - **Exactly one supported b12x generation: 0.15.3** (`b12x.integration.tp_moe`) — the generation the reference dspark deployment ships and the one every number below was measured on. Later generations changed the W4A16 kernels behind the same API (0.20.0) and then replaced the API (1.2.x); they are **rejected at startup** with an install hint, rather than silently producing different numerics. - 0.15.3 was never published to PyPI. It installs from the source commit whose MoE surface matches the released wheel: ``` pip install --no-deps "b12x @ https://github.com/local-inference-lab/b12x/archive/7dc6fb8fcc6446ea093537d1657df81985fa5f43.tar.gz" ``` (`--no-deps`: b12x's metadata pulls a newer torch.) At startup the backend verifies the installed dist-info version is exactly 0.15.3 and fails with this install hint otherwise. - **`mxfp4_b12x_moe.py`** (new): `Mxfp4B12xMoEMethod` — weight prep hands the checkpoint tensors to b12x **in place** (E8M0 scales consumed natively; `reuse_input_storage=True`, so the Parameters stay live and are kept referenced), a frozen scratch plan built from the layer shapes, and a bind-and-run closure matching vLLM's call sequence. - **Warmup ladder**: b12x refuses to compile kernels during CUDA graph capture and falls back to a pinned tile config that does not fit every block size, so every token count a captured graph can present is compiled eagerly first (decode `bs x spec_window` plus a power-of-two ladder for chunked prefill, sized by `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS`). - **`moe_runner/b12x.py`** (new): fused-path runner registration; the quant info carries only the prepared launch closure and an EP guard (with expert parallelism the dispatcher rewrites non-local experts to -1, which b12x would run as garbage rather than skip). - **`mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py`**: register the new method in the `routed_scaling_factor` whitelist (it is silently dropped otherwise, compressing the whole MoE block by the scaling factor). - Env knobs registered in `environ.py` per conventions: `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS` (sizes the scratch arena; must cover `--chunked-prefill-size`), `SGLANG_B12X_WARMUP` (default on; off only defers compilation -- captured decode shapes are still compiled by the graph runner's pre-capture warmup, the prefill ladder then JIT-compiles on the first chunks), and `SGLANG_B12X_CACHE_DIR` (tracks `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`; forwarded to b12x's `B12X_CUTE_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR`, same pattern as `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`). ## Validation 2x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2 cross-node, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with DSPARK speculative decoding (`gamma=5`), chunked prefill 4096: | Metric | Result | |---|---| | GSM8K 1319q (few-shot, parallel 8) | accuracy **0.945**, invalid 0 | | decode (8k ctx, bs=1) | 73-77 ms/step, accept-length 5.4-5.9 | | prefill 30k input | ~1.9k tok/s input throughput | Also boots and passes GSM8K (200q sampled: 0.960) on current main. ## Notes An earlier revision carried dual-generation support (0.15.3 + 1.2.x behind one method). It was dropped once the 0.15.3 source commit was identified: the 1.2.x W4A16 kernel measured ~19% slower per call at the decode working point on this shape (`cute.Tensor` static strides became runtime-rebuilt `cute.Pointer` layouts), and carrying two calling conventions doubled the surface of a backend that only has hardware-attested coverage. Single generation, hard-rejected otherwise, keeps the numerics story exact. Related: #34018 (FP8 wo_a GEMM on sm12x) is complementary and kept separate on purpose. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32309145516](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309145516)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32309145385](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309145385)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix MoE MORI Accuracy Issue
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a bug where MoE models served with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` produce garbage output (0/10 on known-answer accuracy), while the exact same model/config with `--moe-a2a-backend none` is correct (10/10). This reproduces on: - Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8) - Hy3-preview / Hunyuan (`HYV3ForCausalLM`, 192 experts, top-8, with shared experts) It reproduces at single node (where MoRI runs its IntraNode kernel) and at multi-node (InterNode/RDMA kernel), so it is not tied to a specific transport. ### Root Cause After the experts run, `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` / `HYV3MoEFused` apply a post-experts all-reduce (`moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce` / `moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`), gated by `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`. That all-reduce is correct for backends whose experts return a partial result per rank. But MoRI's `combine` already all-to-all-reduces each token's expert outputs back to the source rank — the routed output is already complete and replicated across the group, exactly like the `flashinfer` and `pplx` dispatchers, which are already excluded from the post-experts all-reduce. Because `mori` was not in the skip list, the extra all-reduce re-reduces an already-complete result, summing it `ep_size`/`tp_size`× and destroying the output. We confirmed this directly by dumping per-rank MoE tensors on the failing server: the routed MoE output is identical across all ranks (already reduced by MoRI combine), and the post-experts `final_out` equals `Σ_ranks(routed)` (i.e. `ep_size × routed`), the fingerprint of the erroneous re-reduce. A reference-trajectory comparison against a correct HuggingFace forward on the same prompt showed layer-0 attention matching (cosine ≈ 1.0) but the trajectory diverging starting at the first MoE layer's output — isolating the defect to the post-experts reduce, not to MoRI's dispatch/GEMM/combine (which produce numerically correct values). ### Specific to Hunyuan 3 `HYV3MoEFused` adds a shared expert (`shared_mlp`, built with `reduce_results=False`) to the routed output before the all-reduce. Under MoRI, the routed output is already full/replicated (must not be reduced again), but the shared output is still a TP/EP partial (still needs reducing). So simply skipping the blanket all-reduce fixes the routed part but leaves `shared` at a fraction (`1/group_size`), which still corrupts the sum. The fix reduces only the shared partial over the same group(s) the blanket reduce would have used, then adds it to the already-full routed output. Qwen3 has no shared experts, so it needs only the skip. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py` — `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`: add an `is_mori()` skip alongside the existing `is_flashinfer()` / `is_pplx()` skips (same "combine already reduces to source rank" rationale). This alone fully fixes models without shared experts (e.g. Qwen3). - `python/sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py` — in both `_forward_single_stream` and `_forward_dual_stream`, for the MoRI path only, reduce the shared-expert partial over the EP/TP group before adding it to the already-full routed output; plus the `get_moe_a2a_backend` import. Required for Hunyuan/Hy3 and any MoRI model with shared experts. Both changes are gated on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()`, so `none`, `flashinfer`, `deepep`, and `pplx` behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy = greedy known-answer probe (10 factual prompts, temperature 0). Baseline `mori` is the unpatched image; `none` is the reference-correct control. ### Probe Test | Model | Nodes | Geometry | Backend | Before Fix | After Fix | |-------|:-----:|----------|---------|:--------:|:--------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | - Qwen3: clean PASS at 1/2/4 nodes (0/10 degenerate). - Hy3: all answers correct at 1/2/4 nodes. At multi-node the probe's separate degenerate-tail heuristic flags 3–4/10 (the base model repeats after answering), but the correct `none` reference shows the same 2–4/10 — i.e. it's a base-model/prompt artifact, not a regression from this fix. - Controls: `--moe-a2a-backend none` remains 10/10 (unchanged), confirming the fix is scoped to MoRI. Both single-node (MoRI IntraNode) and multi-node (MoRI InterNode/RDMA) paths verified. ### GSM8K (exact-match, 40 problems, 5-shot) | Model | Nodes | Geometry | none (control) | mori (before fix) | mori (after fix) | |-------|:-----:|----------|:--------------:|:-----------------:|:----------------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 87.5% (35/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 90.0% (36/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 85.0% (34/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 92.5% (37/40) | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 77.5% (31/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 80.0% (32/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 80.0% (32/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 80.0% (32/40) | - Before the fix, mori is broken at every scale (Qwen3 0%, Hy3 0–2.5%), consistent with the garbage output on the known-answer probe. - After the fix, mori tracks the none reference at every scale: Qwen3 lands at or slightly above none (within noise at N=40), and Hy3 matches the reference closely (exactly equal at 1 and 4 nodes: 31/40 and 32/40). - The absolute score reflects each base model's own capability (Hy3-preview is a preview model, so its ceiling is lower); the fix restores reference-equivalent accuracy on the MoRI path rather than changing model quality. - Single-node exercises MoRI's IntraNode kernel; 2-node and 4-node exercise MoRI's InterNode (RDMA) kernel. Scored offline against the staged GSM8K test split via final-integer exact-match. ### Test Environment - Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm700-mi30x-20260728` (SGLang upstream `main` @ `84cdfde`, version `0.5.16.dev20260728`), 8× MI300 per node, pure TP (`tp==ep`), `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. - Hy3 runs also apply an orthogonal, environment-specific workaround for AITER's `biased_grouped_topk` on ROCm (falls back to the reference impl when `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output=True`); this is unrelated to the all-reduce fix. ## Follow Up - Other MoRI models with shared experts (beyond Hunyuan) would need the same shared-expert handling in their model file; consider factoring the "reduce shared partial only" step into a shared helper. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: Split TRTLLM MHA decode batches by KV sequence length
signals.text: ## Motivation TRTLLM-GEN decode attention can pay a large tail-latency tax when requests in the same batch have very different KV sequence lengths. On GB300, a matched mixed-context profile attributed `8.377 ms` of a `9.822 ms` decode-step delta to attention, with `7.601 ms` coming from the main SM100 variable-sequence FMHA kernel. At BS44/rank on a 148-SM GB300, the unsplit launch has only one KV CTA per request and selects the persistent kernel. Long requests then form the tail of the shared wave. Splitting a fixed-query-length batch into length-sorted groups increases CTA parallelism and prevents the longest requests from delaying the short groups. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS`, with default `1` preserving the existing single-call behavior. - For values above one, sort requests by KV length, form equal-count groups, gather their query/page-table/length metadata, invoke TRTLLM MHA per group, and scatter outputs back to request order. - Reuse the same helper for ordinary fixed-query decode and frozen-KV MTP target verification, including NVFP4 KV-cache scaling. - Validate the split count and cap it at the request count. The ragged-query path is unchanged. - Extend two existing TRTLLM-MHA test cases to cover split eager decode and frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph replay; no new test method or module is added. The refreshed commit is rebased onto current upstream `main@f019f0b064`. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation on `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.985** (197/200) | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | Acceptance was generated naturally; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. Targeted GB300 correctness coverage on the refreshed upstream commit: - existing eager dense-decode case with two sequence-length groups; - existing frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph case with two groups; - `2 passed`, covering `5` subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Feature isolation: no split versus two groups Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, TRTLLM MHA, NEXTN draft length 6, BS44/rank on GB300: | Workload | Splits=1 | Splits=2 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mixed ISL decode iteration | 57.485 ms | 51.639 ms | **-10.17%** | | Uniform 92k, exact matched points | 49.907 ms | 50.008 ms | +0.20% | | q_len=1 attention micro | 0.757 ms | 0.637 ms | **-15.9%** | | q_len=6 attention micro | 1.066 ms | 0.711 ms | **-33.3%** | The mixed run held batch size, average context, request count, and draft settings constant. Length splitting closed `75.5%` of the isolated mixed-ISL attention tax without a material steady-state regression on uniform lengths. ### Production split-count tuning AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. Exact-shape matching used each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. | Metric | Split-3 | Split-4 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape output TPS/User | 67.352353 | 70.623070 | **+4.8561%** | | Strict matched TPS/running request | — | — | **+1.82848%** | | ITL | — | — | **-4.0306%** | | Full decode duration | — | — | **-3.6644%** | Both arms had CUDA graph fraction `1.0` and zero retractions. This second table is split-count tuning enabled by the PR, not an additional additive estimate on top of the no-split comparison. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signals.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Recommended `attention-backend-config` For `num_inference_steps=50` (49 denoise updates), use: ```json { "local_cube_size": [4, 4, 4], "topk_ratio_list": [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.35, 0.30, 0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05 ] } ``` Pass this JSON through `--attention-backend-config` alongside the component-scoped backend selection above. ## Implementation Note The Cube sparse attention backend in this PR is a reference implementation built with PyTorch FlexAttention. For higher performance on supported NVIDIA hardware, future work may explore replacing it with cuDNN Frontend's Block Sparse Attention ([cudnn-frontend/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention at main · NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/tree/main/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention)) operator. Broader hardware support and backend-specific optimizations are left to future community contributions. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32294556528](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32294556528)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32294556356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32294556356)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support Intern-S2-Mobius FP8
signals.text: ## Motivation `internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8` is now public, but it does not load on current SGLang. The serialized FP8 config lists `.linear_attn` parents as exact `modules_to_not_convert` entries, while SGLang treats ignored-layer names as prefixes and consequently skips quantized child projections. Strict loading then also needs to map the checkpoint's fused expert scale tensors and allow omitted KV-cache scales. The existing Intern-S2-Mobius cookbook only exposes the BF16 checkpoint. ## Modifications - Preserve FP8 quantization for Mobius linear-attention qkv/z and output projections while retaining the checkpoint's child exclusions. - Load `gate_up_proj_scale_inv` and `down_proj_scale_inv` into the fused expert scale parameters. - Treat Mobius `attn.k_scale` and `attn.v_scale` as optional while still loading them when present. - Add the FP8 checkpoint to the cookbook selector with verified 1xH200 TP=1 high-throughput and NEXTN recipes. B200 recipes remain explicitly unverified. - Separate the existing BF16 benchmark claims from the new FP8 launch verification. No unit test is added: this is a serialized-checkpoint integration path, and a mock loader test would only restate the configured parameter mappings. The real checkpoint path is covered by the end-to-end gate below. ## Accuracy Tests Verified commit `59c8810358` on 1xH200 with checkpoint revision `ea369586a687b1f31d29c8b10868acf2cb8e2889`: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \ --context-length 262144 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \ --model internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-threads 64 ``` | Examples | Accuracy | Stop rate | Truncated | Error | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1319 | **96.82%** | **100.00%** | 0.00% | 0.00% | All 1319 prediction records reported `finish_reason=stop`. The documented NEXTN recipe also passed live smoke tests: - Text: `15% of 240` returned `36`, `finish_reason=stop`. - Vision: the standard tiger image returned `tiger`, `finish_reason=stop`, with 70 image tokens. - A 292-token bounded generation stopped normally; telemetry reported accept length 4.00 and accept rate 1.00 with decode CUDA graphs enabled. Local validation passed: changed-file `pre-commit`, `py_compile`, cookbook config consistency, `git diff --check`, and `mint validate`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No FP8 speed benchmark is claimed in this PR. The cookbook explicitly keeps the existing speed tables scoped to BF16. For capacity context, the high-throughput server loaded 34.22 GB of FP8 model weights. The NEXTN target+draft process used about 94 GB on H200 with the documented settings. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: [Perf] Fuse prefill norm/act quantization for NVFP4 W4A4 hybrid models (Qwen3.5 family)
signals.text: > Rebased onto `main` after #34859 merged: the SiLU+FP4-quant base fusion landed with the model support, so this PR is now a single commit with the three remaining fusions (attention-layer SiLU coverage, post-LN+FP4-quant, gated-norm+FP8-quant). ## Motivation For Qwen3.5-family hybrid (GDN + attention) models served with a mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, prefill spends a measurable share of GPU time in standalone norm / activation / quantization glue kernels: every projection input is normalized, written to HBM in bf16, then re-read and quantized by a separate kernel. Kernel-level tracing against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same model showed the GEMM/attention/GDN families at parity while SGLang lost time exclusively in this glue (vLLM fuses norm+quant and act+quant via torch.compile). This PR removes the extra round-trips with three targeted fusions (all bit-equivalent up to FP4/FP8 rounding ties, each with a kill switch): 1. **SiLU+mul + NVFP4 quant** for dense MLPs: replaces `act_and_mul` + the standalone per-block FP4 quantize with FlashInfer's `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` (single-group form), handing `down_proj` a prequantized `(fp4, swizzled_scale)` tuple through the existing `_accepts_prequantized_fp4` path. Enabled for both GDN-layer and attention-layer MLPs. 2. **Post-attention GemmaRMSNorm + NVFP4 quant**: FlashInfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` fuses the residual-add, the norm, and the `gate_up` input quant into one kernel. Gemma's `(1 + w)` scaling is folded into a precomputed weight; the swizzled block-scale is exposed as the 2D `(m_padded, K/16)` view so the cuDNN mm_fp4 backend's shape validation also passes. 3. **GDN gated RMSNorm + static-FP8 quant**: adds an fp8-store epilogue to the `fla` `layernorm_gated` Triton kernel (skips the bf16 intermediate write entirely) and teaches `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` to accept a prequantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple for `out_proj` (explicit opt-in attribute, mirroring the fp4 path). Kill switches: `SGLANG_DISABLE_SILU_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_POST_LN_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GATED_NORM_FP8_QUANT_FUSION=1`. ## Benchmark RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), Qwen3.5-family 27B hybrid GDN model, mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, TP1, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --disable-radix-cache`, flashinfer 0.6.17. Workload: `bench_serving`, random 8192-in / 1024-out, bs=1, 5 prompts, seed 1234, warmup pass then measured pass; both lanes in one session on the same GPU, base commit 5c9ee86d90. ### TTFT (8k prefill) | | main | main + this PR | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | TTFT mean | 674.8 ms | **640.1 ms** | **−34.7 ms (−5.1%)** | | TTFT median | 665.3 ms | **631.3 ms** | **−34.0 ms (−5.1%)** | ### Decode (unchanged, sanity check) | | main | main + this PR | |---|---|---| | output tok/s (bs=1) | 68.7 | 69.1 | | ITL median | 13.92 ms | 13.86 ms | Per-kernel effect at the 8k prefill step (torch profiler, per forward): the standalone `act_and_mul` (~8.6 ms), the gate_up-input `quantize_with_block_size` pass (~6.7 ms), the down-input `cvt_fp16_to_fp4` pass, and the out_proj `static_quant_fp8` launches (128/forward) are removed or absorbed into the producing kernel; the gated-norm epilogue also skips its 100 MB bf16 intermediate write per layer. The fusions auto-enable only when the touched projections use the matching ModelOpt linear method (NVFP4 W4A4 for 1–2, per-tensor static FP8 for 3), so other checkpoints and quant modes keep their current control flow. ### Accuracy GSM8K via `sglang.test.run_eval` (full test set, 1319 examples, same server flags as above): | | score | |---|---| | fusions **off** (all kill switches set) | 0.9635 | | fusions **on** (this PR default) | 0.9658 | Also verified layer-count wiring at startup (64/64 layers log each fusion) and bit-exact residual propagation (fused kernels update the residual identically to `fused_add_rmsnorm`). ### Data provenance The RTX PRO 6000 tables above were measured with **all three fusions of this PR** applied directly on `main` @ 5c9ee86d90 (commit a452f1ef8c, fusion content byte-equivalent to this branch's net diff), before stacking on #34859. signals.title: [NPU]Ensure tensors allocated by empty_like are contiguous
signals.text: ## Motivation `torch.empty_like(q)` inherits the memory format of `q` by default.
