signals.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signals.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: [KDA] Route Kimi-Linear through native Cake kernels
signals.text: Depends on #34299 for the checkpoint-capable KDA serving surface and on FlashInfer [#4535](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4535) for native `lower_bound=None` kernels. ## Summary - Auto-select BF16 recurrent state and native Cake prefill/decode for Kimi-Linear-48B's D128 equal-head contract at TP-local H4/H8/H16/H32 (TP8/TP4/TP2/TP1). - Feed packed Q/K/V, raw gate, and row-strided beta views directly to FlashInfer without `contiguous()` staging or state gather/scatter copies. - Preserve the native prefill route under breakable CUDA Graph padding by slicing only the live token prefix as storage-sharing row views. - Keep admission fail-closed and retain structured per-layer route events and aggregate counters. Per-event JSON logging remains an explicit diagnostic opt-in. ## Validation - B200 and B300 each pass 85 focused unit tests, 12 GPU decode integrations, and seven GPU prefill integrations, including bounded rows, H4/H8/H16/H32 unbounded routes, checkpoints, packed rows, graph padding, and exact-identity inputs. - The exact final FlashInfer source passes 48 decode and 15 prefill GPU rows per architecture. Six representative launches per target pass warmup, synccheck, and memcheck with zero errors. - A final-source B200 recurrence diagnostic forces old and new decode variants over graph batches 128/136, active batches 1/32/111/128/136, indexed noncompact state, inactive rows, and 256 sequential updates per case. The new two-warp output and recurrent state are bitwise equal to both one-warp variants across all 1,536 updates, with maximum difference `0.0`. - The full-model TP8/local-H4 audit completes every request. Its isolated diagnostic arm records 7,840 prefill and 59,840 decode Cake successes with zero fallback, fatal outcomes, or copied inputs. - Serving performance is faster than FLA, but final inference qualification remains open: Cake scores `0.875` on the 200-example five-shot GSM8K arm and does not clear the strict `>0.88` threshold; FLA scores `0.905`. ## Kimi-Linear-48B TP8/local-H4 serving The performance audit uses one eight-B200 node and independent `Cake, FLA, FLA, Cake` services. Each arm receives 32 workload-shaped warmups followed by 64 measured requests at nominal 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, and cache flush. Values are two-replicate geometric means except peak memory and accuracy. | Metric | Cake | FLA Triton | Cake / FLA or delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Throughput | 27,863.85 token/s | 26,833.37 token/s | `1.0384x` (+3.84%) | | Mean TTFT | 115.913 ms | 134.673 ms | -13.93% | | Median TTFT | 113.900 ms | 137.567 ms | -17.20% | | Mean TPOT | 6.708 ms | 7.035 ms | -4.64% | | Median TPOT | 6.874 ms | 6.730 ms | +2.13% | | Peak memory across 8 GPUs | 1,366,768 MiB | 1,388,112 MiB | -1.54% | | Five-shot GSM8K accuracy | 0.875 (fails `>0.88`) | 0.905 (passes) | -0.030 | The concurrency-32 performance arm reaches at most 28 live requests and replays at padded batch 32, so its throughput delta is not attributed to two-warp grouping. The 128-thread accuracy arm reaches the two-warp band, but the forced-variant trajectory excludes that selector change as the score-miss cause. Cake/FLA stop on configured token `163586` for 197/199 of 200 accuracy responses; the remaining 3/1 responses validly reach the 512-token cap. The Cake accuracy miss remains explicit and is not treated as a passing serving result.

signals.title: [Diffusion] Align MiniMax H3 request RNG with reference
signals.text: ## Summary - use one request-local CPU generator for MiniMax H3 noise - preserve the reference draw order: visual conditions, target video tensor, then target audio rows - precompute condition noise before denoising instead of re-seeding per modality or condition - keep the existing H3-only scope so other diffusion consistency trajectories are unchanged ## Why The previous implementation independently re-seeded video, audio, and condition streams. signals.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signals.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32317861378](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317861378)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32317861217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317861217)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Add is_dummy truth-table wire tests for mooncake and nixl
signals.text: ## Motivation Item 1 from the open-question-3 review on #33861 (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861#issuecomment-5262038350): the `is_dummy` truth table for mooncake and nixl has no coverage of the frames the senders actually write. The two existing nixl cases omit `msg[9]`, so the explicit `is_dummy` frame the sender writes is never parsed in any test, and mooncake's payload inference (kv and aux frames both empty) has no coverage at all. Additive and independent of the hoisting work; part of the Step 0/1 test surface for #34510. ## Modifications - `test_nixl_backend_basic.py`: five `TransferInfo` cases with sender-faithful frames covering the explicit-frame branch — dummy, dummy with a decode-side prefix hit (the case payload inference cannot see, since `decode_prefix_len` is sent unconditionally), full prefix hit, real transfer — plus one fallback case documenting that without `msg[9]` a prefix-hit dummy parses as real, which is the case the explicit frame exists for. - `test_disaggregation_wire.py`: `TestMooncakeTransferInfoIsDummy`, four cases with frames built as mooncake's `KVSender` writes them (kv and aux empty iff dummy, state indices gated on dummy, `decode_prefix_len` and `required_dst_info_num` unconditional): real, full prefix hit, dummy, dummy with prefix hit. Also asserts the dummy branch clears `dst_kv_indices`/`dst_aux_index`/`dst_state_indices`. Both files are already registered in CPU CI (`base-a-test-cpu`); no new files and no new registrations. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable (CPU wire-format unit tests only; no model or kernel changes). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31902864702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902864702)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902864706](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902864706)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Classify PIL decode-time failures as client errors (400)
signals.text: ## Motivation Image bytes that pass PIL's `open()`-time format sniffing can still fail during the eager `img.load()` in `_load_single_item`: - a PNG whose corruption sits **past the first IDAT chunk** raises `SyntaxError("broken PNG file")` — `Image.open` only parses up to the first IDAT, so sniffing succeeds; - a truncated file raises `OSError("image file is truncated")`. Neither type is in `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` (`UnidentifiedImageError` only covers open-time sniffing failures), so these requests return **500** instead of **400**. This was observed in production as repeated 500 responses for the same corrupt screenshot payload. ## Modifications Catch `OSError` and `SyntaxError` only around PIL's eager `img.convert()` / `img.load()` step and translate them to `ValueError`. Keep `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` narrow so the same broad built-in exceptions from non-PIL loaders or system work remain `RuntimeError` / 500. Tests in `test_base_processor_bad_input.py` cover: - zeroed later PNG chunk header → `SyntaxError` → `ValueError`; - truncated PNG → `OSError` → `ValueError`; - mocked non-PIL `OSError` → `RuntimeError`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32086532911](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086532911)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32086532614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086532614)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion][Model] Support MAGI-2-preview
signals.text: ## Motivation Relate #35011 Adds native support for [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview), SandAI's 114B MoE model that generates a video and its synchronized stereo soundtrack in one denoising trajectory. About 6B parameters are active per token. Audio is not a second pass over finished video: video and audio latents share one packed sequence and one denoise loop. Text-to-video and image+text-to-video are both supported. The checkpoint ships two DiTs. A preview model denoises the clip, and a refiner then takes that result to 1920x1088; the words "preview" and "refiner" below always mean those two. Serving it today means standing up a second stack. The reference implementation launches under `torchrun`, depends on SandAI's own kernels ([MagiAttention](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiAttention), [MagiCompiler](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiCompiler), FlashAttention 3) and so ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview), and its checkpoint has no `model_index.json`. This PR builds it against SGLang's own layers so it is served like every other family in `sglang.multimodal_gen`. ## Modifications ### New code Four pieces the tree did not already have. Everything else goes through existing machinery. - **Multi-head MoE** (`runtime/layers/moe_multihead.py`). MAGI-2 routes 12 independent heads over 256 experts each, top-6, where the tree's MoE assumes one routing head. Viewing tokens as `[N * 12, 256]` instead of `[N, 12, 256]` makes it a standard MoE with `hidden_size=256` and `num_experts=3072`, so srt's Triton `fused_experts` runs unmodified. A rank owns `(12 / ep_size) * 256` of those, and `moe_align_block_size` runs 1024 threads while indexing `prefix[num_experts]`, so anything past 1023 takes an illegal memory access; the experts run in balanced head chunks that fit, which is one call at `ep_size >= 4` and is what lets 1, 2 and 3 work at all. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and `gemm1_clamp_limit`. - **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed through, along with `window_size`. - **Block-window local attention** (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. The same mask is also expressed as token-range pairs for MagiAttention's `flex_flash_attn_func`, which is used when that package is importable and is 1.78x faster on the refiner's shape; without it the `flex_attention` path runs unchanged. - **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288, mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly stochastic. ### Reused from the tree Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them: - **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them. - **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. `ep_size` defaults to the world size and can be set below it through `--pipeline-config-path`, which is how 8 ranks run. - **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work without model-specific code. - `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts. ### Structure Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`. Two orderings matter and are easy to break in review: Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs **after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis, and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding. The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile, residency and warmup still come from the base stage. ### Parallelism `--num-gpus` must divide every Ulysses head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA key/value heads. The preview's 12 MoE heads are sharded by `ep_size` instead and are checked against that. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2, 4 or 8 and preview-only also admits 3, 6 and 12. All four axes are checked in `validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a collective. 8 GPUs divides every Ulysses axis but not the preview's 12 MoE heads, so it needs an explicit `ep_size` of 4: two expert-parallel groups of 4 ranks, each holding all 12 heads. The reference instead pads the head axis to 16 and gives the spare ranks zero-weight experts; this PR needs no padding and leaves no rank idle. `--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance. Expert parallelism is also what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. Below 4 ranks the expert weights need `--dit-layerwise-offload` to fit at all. ### Deliberate divergences from the reference Both are marked at the site in the code. **The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length, which the two-stage tier does not have to spare. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the rotary. **Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, and is not needed: an `ep_size` below the world size reaches 8 ranks without it, as described under Parallelism. ### Docs `docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility matrix. ### Known limitations - Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise. 1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16. - 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration. - `--enable-torch-compile` must be paired with `--regional-compile`. On its own it compiles the whole transformer, and inductor autotuning then fails on the multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`). With `--regional-compile` the expert GEMMs stay out of the compiled region and both DiTs compile per block. Compile is also rank-count dependent: it pays at 4 ranks and loses at 8, where the preview pass measures 335s compiled against 184s eager. - 1 GPU passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview DiT, which casts the whole state dict to the device before layerwise offload can take over. - 2 GPUs needs `--dit-layerwise-offload`; the expert weights are 217 GB. - `ep_size` has no CLI flag, so the 8-rank launch needs `--pipeline-config-path` with `{"ep_size": 4}`. - `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below. - FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded. - The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is unset. ## Accuracy Tests ### Side-by-side with the reference implementation Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording. **Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the climax. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67 **Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the conditioning image. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d **Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at his feet — plus its conditioning still. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964 The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. This PR runs SGLang's own attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate divergences. The clips are the thing to look at. ### Prompt coverage Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English: - Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe - Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20 - Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38 - Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc - Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e - 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9 - Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b - Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23 All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps, 249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the lake clip is continuous and low-frequency. ### Unit tests 59 unit tests, 51 of which need no GPU: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder, packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in, sequence bucketing, the expert-axis sharding predicate, and which submodules the regional-compile conditions select. The remaining 8 need CUDA and are skipped without it: the mHC mixing kernel against an FP32 reference, and the block-window mask against a dense `scaled_dot_product_attention` reference. They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up and they run in the existing suite with no CI change: ``` python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit ``` The full 1080p path needs at least two cards and minutes per clip, so it is not in the suite. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative comparisons, not as sizing targets. They are eager-mode figures; the compiled configuration and the comparison against the reference are in Benchmark below. **One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:** text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under 0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to encode — and measures 741s. **Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat, which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in the host page cache. **Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses 124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer, so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup rather than left for a user to discover. **Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text + reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where the first three share a prompt length: - rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s - using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, since dynamo guards a captured int by value and would recompile per prompt length even at a fixed shape. `dynamic=True` is not an alternative; it costs 26s per clip. ## Benchmark Same box, same weights, same seed 42, same 1920x1088 two-stage tier at 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, 4 ranks on each side. This PR runs `--enable-torch-compile --regional-compile`. Nine clips per side, discarding each process's first clip while its graphs are still building. One clip is 249 frames at 25 fps — just under 10 seconds of 1920x1088 video with its synchronized stereo audio, generated together in one denoising trajectory. 10 seconds is the only duration the model was trained for, so the figures below do not scale with a requested length. Weight loading is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. | | reference | this PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | preview denoise (100 steps) | 277.7s | 286.6s | | refiner denoise (5 steps) | 46.1s | 41.9s | | decode (video and audio) | 8.9s | 7.8s | | **one clip, end to end** | **344.9s** | **349.3s** | **At 4 ranks this PR is 1.3% slower** — 4.4s on a 345s clip, which is larger than the spread between runs. The refiner and the decode are faster; preview denoise is 8.9s slower and is where the difference sits. Stage times do not sum to the end-to-end row on either side, because the two implementations synchronize at different points, so the end-to-end row is the one to compare. ### Across topologies Same clip, same seed, each column at that rank count's best configuration. Two steady clips per arm on one 8-GPU box, so this is a narrower measurement than the nine-clip table above; the 4-rank column reproduces its 349.3s within the noise floor, which is what makes the columns comparable: | | 2 ranks | 4 ranks | 8 ranks | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `ep_size` | 2 | 4 (default) | 4 | | compile | regional | regional | **none** | | offload | layerwise | none | none | | preview denoise (100 steps) | 590.4s | 286.9s | 183.9s | | refiner denoise (5 steps) | 79.4s | 41.3s | 31.6s | | decode (video and audio) | 7.1s | 8.8s | 12.2s | | **one clip, end to end** | **689.0s** | **348.2s** | **253.5s** | | peak memory | 132208 MiB | 85274 MiB | 126572 MiB | | GPU-seconds per clip | 1378 | 1393 | 2028 | 8 ranks is 1.37x faster per clip and spends 46% more GPU-time to get there, so it buys latency rather than throughput, and two concurrent 4-rank deployments beat one 8-rank deployment on total output. 2 and 4 ranks cost the same GPU-seconds, so the 2-rank arm trades latency for hardware at no efficiency loss. Decode moves the wrong way with rank count, so every latency gain comes from denoise. The 8-rank arm runs eager deliberately: compiled, its preview pass measures 335.4s against 183.9s, which is the only configuration in this PR where `--regional-compile` is a loss. 1 rank passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview DiT. The reference was not re-run at 8 ranks, so none of these are head-to-head; its published 8-rank timings use head padding and a different step budget. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Scheduler] Add configurable decode interval after prefill
signals.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation With DP attention, each rank schedules attention work locally while all ranks still participate in the same MoE collective. A rank with repeated chunked-prefill continuation work can therefore keep winning SGLang's prefill-first scheduling decision and starve decode work on peer ranks. In the AgentX workload this left requests waiting while the actual decode batch remained small. The DP-attention MLP-sync all-gather already exposes whether any rank selected an EXTEND batch. Use that globally synchronized signal to enforce a rank-consistent decode interval after prefill. ## Modifications - Add `--prefill-decode-interval N`, defaulting to `0` (disabled, so existing behavior is unchanged). - After an EXTEND batch, defer new prefill scheduling for the next `N` scheduler rounds so the running batch can decode. - Under DP attention, arm the interval from the existing globally synchronized `is_extend_in_batch` flag. Under non-DP scheduling, use the local forward mode. - Validate non-negative values and add focused scheduler/server-argument unit tests. No AIPerf source change is required. The benchmark prototype used the existing per-session routing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes batch selection cadence only; it does not change model math or sampling. - Added unit coverage for disabled, non-DP, globally synchronized DP, and decode/non-rearm behavior. - Added server-argument validation coverage. - `python -m py_compile` passed for all modified Python/test files. - The focused pytest command could not collect on the development VM because its base Python environment does not include `torch`/`numpy`; the new tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equivalent scheduler prototype was evaluated with full 3,600-second DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 AgentX runs on 8x B200 using TP8/DP8/EP8, DP attention, MTP3, and an interval of 16: | Concurrency | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | Cache hit | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 56 | 30.75532 | 23,559.05865 | 95.945% | | 84 | 23.24221 | 26,110.24296 | 94.703% | The c84 run completed 7,096 profiled requests with zero request errors. These results validate the equivalent prototype on SGLang v0.5.17; this PR ports the behavior onto current `main` using the existing global DP EXTEND flag. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32217562639](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217562639)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32217562470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217562470)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [DSA] Trim top-k v2 output modes and tighten its PDL waits
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation The DeepSeek-V4 (DSA indexer) top-k v2 kernel carried an optional `raw_indices` output that no production caller ever requests: the c4 indexer routes to the v1 kernel whenever it needs raw indices, so the v2 argument was only ever exercised by a unit test. Everyone else still paid for it with a per-element `raw_out != nullptr` branch inside the page-table transform loop. While removing it, two PDL (programmatic dependent launch) details in the same kernel turned out to be leaving performance on the table or resting on a condition the caller was not told about. ## Modifications **Output modes.** `raw_indices` is gone; `page_tables` becomes optional instead. `None` selects a `TopKMode::INDICES` template that emits the selected positions straight into the output, so the transform pass -- and the 8 KB shared staging buffer it needs -- is compiled out rather than skipped at runtime. Passing a page table keeps the existing behaviour bit for bit. **Output buffer is no longer prefilled with -1.** Every path already writes all `topk` slots of every row: the collect pass fills `[0, above_count)`, `handle_tie` fills `[above_count, topk)` (padding included), and the trivial path fills everything. The per-layer fill kernel was dead work. **Level-3 PDL wait narrowed to the cluster path.** Only rows whose raw indices come from the persistent cluster kernel need that kernel to have retired. The register / streaming / trivial rows were waiting on it too, holding an SM slot until the long-running pool finished and serializing the short items behind it -- which is exactly the mix level 3 exists for. The wait now lives inside the cluster branch (block-uniform, so the following `__syncthreads()` is unaffected). **Small-batch kernel.** Dropped the redundant `PDLWaitPrimary` after `forward()` (`forward()` already waits internally) and added the missing `PDLTriggerSecondary` so dependents can be scheduled without waiting for the whole grid to drain. **PDL prefetch contract.** The kernel reads `seq_lens` and the plan metadata *before* its `griddepcontrol.wait`, which is only legal while neither is produced by the immediately preceding kernel in the stream (per CUDA: the launch trigger "provides no memory visibility guarantee itself"). Production satisfies this -- both are built during per-forward metadata prep -- but two call sites could quietly break it, so: - the DSA backend now asserts `lengths.dtype == torch.int32` instead of calling `.to(torch.int32)`, which would place a cast kernel exactly there; - the unit test no longer launches `plan_topk_v2` back to back with the transform. Also renamed `TopKMode::INDICE` to `INDICES`. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` -- 234/234 pass on B200. The no-page-table mode is validated directly against `torch.topk` across every dispatch template and boundary (`test_topk_v2_output_indices`), and the paged mode is still validated by inverting the output through the page table (`test_topk_v2`, `test_topk_v2_ragged`), so both modes keep full coverage. ## Benchmarking and Profiling No kernel-algorithm change on the paged path, so throughput is unchanged for the common shapes. The wins are structural: one fewer fill kernel per layer, one fewer branch per output element in the transform loop, and short rows in a mixed-length long-context batch no longer sit blocked on the persistent cluster pool. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31958299936](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958299936)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32233055438](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233055438)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation This fixes a regression introduced by #32541. Before that PR, custom all-reduce v2 was enabled by default and eligible TP16 groups reached the topology and allocator capability check. The added TP2-8-specific multinode policy disabled `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` for TP16 before capability detection, forcing an otherwise eligible configuration to fall back. ## Modifications - Remove the separate multinode flag and server-argument policy; `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` remains the single enable and opt-out control. - Select cross-node v2 from the actual topology, VMM allocator capability, and architecture-tuned world sizes. - Let eligible custom all-reduce inputs run before symmetric-memory PyNccl; larger inputs still fall through. - Replace the server-argument policy tests with capability and dispatch tests. ## Original commits - `fb9411abe` ## Accuracy Tests No model math changes. - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py` — 10 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No public speed benchmark was run. The change restores the eligible TP16 custom all-reduce v2 path and preserves fallback for unsupported topology or message sizes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signals.title: [PD] Overlap prefill DP-rank bootstrap queries
signals.text: ## Motivation Decode admission synchronously queried the prefill bootstrap server for DP-rank routing at the result-consumption point. This HTTP round trip was on the scheduler critical path even though pending bootstrap rooms were already known before request intake and while the previous decode graph could still be in flight. This change is functionally independent of #35070 and is based directly on upstream `main`. For production validation, it was tested with #35070 enabled; the performance numbers below are the additional increment over that PREBUILT-enabled baseline, not a code dependency on #35070. ## Modifications - Submit the authoritative batched prefill DP-rank query through the existing KV-manager executor once, at the top of each decode scheduler iteration before request intake. - Consume the future at the original resolution point, preserving same-cycle receiver initialization and bootstrap-server routing authority. - Preserve FIFO behavior and the existing synchronous retry/error fallback. - Cancel owned futures during queue cleanup. - Add one focused case to the existing decode queue cleanup test. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.995** | | Mean speculative acceptance length | 4.519494 | | Acceptance rate | 0.704089 | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | The evaluation used natural model output; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. Removing the redundant second prefetch does not change the authoritative result-consumption, retry, or receiver-initialization path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. The clean PREBUILT A/B uses each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. Output TPS/User is `output_sequence_length / full_decode_duration`, with exact request-shape matching. | Metric | PREBUILT baseline | Top-only prefetch | Additional change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape Output TPS/User | 83.560918 | 84.695096 | **+1.357308%** | Both jobs completed successfully with zero request errors, zero retractions, and no CUDA-graph fallback. The exact-shape comparison contains 7,870 common shapes and 8,088 matched requests. Instrumentation showed that the upper prefetch had a mean `17.35 ms` lead, was ready at the consume point in `69.8%` of observations, and reduced residual synchronous wait from `1.140 ms` to `0.265 ms`. The removed lower call had only about `0.8 ms` of lead and mostly observed futures already submitted by the upper call, so keeping it added control-flow complexity without preserving additional measured throughput. Targeted production-container unit coverage passed before the production A/B. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [AMD] Perf dsv4 enable heterogeneous AITER FHMoE
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4-Pro stores its 384 routed experts as MXFP4/E8M0, but keeps the single shared expert in native FP8 E4M3 with 128x128 E8M0 scales. Converting that shared expert to MXFP4 introduces avoidable quantization error. This PR integrates AITER's heterogeneous fused shared-expert MoE (FHMoE), so routed experts remain MXFP4 while expert 384 remains native FP8 and both execute in one two-stage MoE schedule. ### AITER dependency This PR requires an AITER build containing both merged changes: - [ROCm/aiter#4269](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4269), merge commit [`00cbe979f20cf380548d7d1d9d73136aa359c276`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/00cbe979f20cf380548d7d1d9d73136aa359c276): FHMoE runtime/AOT implementation. - [ROCm/aiter#4314](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4314), merge commit [`334fd72ad6e69d16785efc97cb8b6b4aec3c2a92`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/334fd72ad6e69d16785efc97cb8b6b4aec3c2a92): C1/C2/C32/C64 decode tuning. All results below were validated with AITER [`868ac1f7aa0d403a77c03e941bc5ffa28c7766d5`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/868ac1f7aa0d403a77c03e941bc5ffa28c7766d5). The ROCm image/deployment must provide this revision or a compatible newer build before enabling the feature. ## Modifications - Add an AITER capability probe and forward native shared weights/scales plus `shared_expert_id` through the MoE runner. - Preserve native FP8 shared-expert checkpoint tensors instead of requantizing them into the MXFP4 routed tensor. - TP-shard shared tensors during loading, retain them for hot reloads, and serialize asynchronous weight/scale pairing. - Expand serialized 128x128 E8M0 scales to AITER's per-1x32 layout, pad the TP8 intermediate shard from logical 384 to physical 512, and apply the required shuffle. - Route six normal experts first, then append semantic expert 384 with weight 1 to form internal `E=385`, `top-k=7` geometry. - Support non-power-of-two routed top-k in the shared-expert append Triton kernel. - Add strict enablement guards and preserve the separate shared-MLP fallback for unsupported configurations. - Add focused tests for policy/fallback, top-k append, TP sharding, FP8/E8M0 layout, uint8 scales, asynchronous loading, hot reload, and argument forwarding. - Add a reproducible validation record under `benchmark/fhmoe/VALIDATION.md`. Enable with: ```bash --enforce-shared-experts-fusion --moe-runner-backend aiter ``` The optimized path is restricted to ROCm `gfx950`, TP=8, EP/A2A/EPLB/offload disabled, BF16 SiLU, 384 routed experts, routed top-k=6, one shared expert, MXFP4 routed weights, and serialized 128x128 block-FP8 shared weights. Unsupported configurations log the reason and use the existing unfused path. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, TP=8, EP disabled, temperature 0, concurrency 64, 20-shot GSM8K, all 1,319 questions: | Mode | Strict exact match | Flexible extract | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Unfused shared MLP | 1254/1319 (95.072%) | 1255/1319 (95.148%) | 0 | | AITER FHMoE | 1262/1319 (95.679%) | 1262/1319 (95.679%) | 0 | FHMoE improved strict accuracy by 0.607 percentage point. All requests completed successfully, with no E8M0-scale, worker, ROCm, or graph-replay errors. Focused SGLang tests: ```bash python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_shared_expert_fusion.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_fhmoe.py ``` Result: `10 passed`. AITER validation included the default and exact DSV4 `test_fhmoe.py` profiles, BM16 scale-boundary coverage, DSV4 AOT precompile, C1/C2/C32/C64 kernel selection, MXFP4 sorting, and HIP graph capture/replay. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hardware/model: 8x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, plain TP8, no EP/A2A/TBO. Workload: fixed 8192 input / 1024 output, `conc*2` warmups and `conc*8` measured requests. | Concurrency | Unfused total tok/s | FHMoE total tok/s | Gain | Unfused / FHMoE median TPOT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 1,218 | 1,233 | +1.25% | 14.28 / 14.09 ms | | 4 | 2,294 | 2,329 | +1.52% | 14.73 / 14.48 ms | | 8 | 4,062 | 4,228 | +4.08% | 16.21 / 15.48 ms | | 16 | 6,803 | 6,917 | +1.67% | 18.55 / 18.18 ms | | 32 | 10,321 | 10,546 | +2.17% | 23.07 / 22.46 ms | FHMoE improved TP8 throughput at every tested concurrency and selected the expected tuned kernels, including the BM16 C32 path. ### Known DP-attention limitation At TP8 + DP8 attention, 8k/1k C256, FHMoE completed 2,048/2,048 requests without errors but regressed total throughput: - Unfused: 32,903 total tok/s, median TPOT 52.29 ms. - FHMoE: 29,330 total tok/s, median TPOT 59.05 ms. - Delta: -10.86% throughput, +12.93% median TPOT. FHMoE is therefore not recommended for DP C256 without additional optimization. Full methodology and results are recorded in `benchmark/fhmoe/VALIDATION.md`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (`isort`, `ruff`, `black-jupyter`). - [x] Add focused unit and GPU tests. - [x] Add reproducible validation documentation. - [x] Provide full accuracy and serving-speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Fix] Support Kimi-K3 ModelOpt mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint
signals.text: ## Motivation The official [nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4) checkpoint is a ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint: - routed MoE experts use NVFP4 with SiTU (`beta=4`, `linear_beta=25`); - supported attention projections use weight-only `FP8_PB_WO` with 128x128 block scales. Current `main` cannot serve this checkpoint with the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend. It rejects gated `situ` during startup, and it does not instantiate/load the checkpoint's block-FP8 attention scales. The K3 fused-front also needs to pass its row-strided FP32 router output through the stride-aware precomputed-routing interface. ## Modifications - Add gated `ActivationType.Situ` support to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP4 runner. - Pass the model-provided SiTU coefficients as GEMM1 alpha/beta and keep the W13 up-dequant scale inside the SiTU activation, avoiding double application through `g1_scale_c`. - Route K3 SiTU fused-front output through SGLang's stride-aware FP32 precomputed-routing path while keeping fused-front enabled. - Dispatch ModelOpt `FP8_PB_WO` layers to SGLang's native serialized block-FP8 linear method with dynamic activation quantization and 128x128 weight blocks. - Load ModelOpt's logical 4-D block scales into SGLang's 2-D `weight_scale_inv` parameters, including fused MLA projections and TP-sharded KDA projections. - Dequantize the FP8 MLA `kv_b` weight before K3's post-load absorption. - Dequantize only K3's small `f_a`/`f_b`/`b` projections once after loading into BF16 buffers for the existing fused tiny-GEMM path; the main KDA projections remain on native block-FP8 GEMMs. - Compile the KDA recompute kernel for the BF16 activation/parameter dtype rather than the serialized FP8 weight dtype. - Add regression coverage for the SiTU scale contract, `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch, block-scale dequantization, and the fused B/F_a path. ## Accuracy Tests Validated the released checkpoint on 8x GB300 with TP8: - GSM8K-200: **197/200 = 0.985** - `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` - `trtllm_mla` prefill and decode attention backends - fused-front enabled - K3 all-reduce fusion enabled - prefill CUDA Graph enabled; decode CUDA Graph enabled for batch sizes 1/2/4 - concurrency 4 - no fused-front-disable environment workaround Both raw completion and chat-completion smoke tests produced coherent, correct answers before the evaluation. The validation used the final patch contents in this PR. The branch was then rebased onto `eafbe2cb6f` from `main`; the intervening upstream commits do not touch this PR's files. Targeted checks: - 13/13 ModelOpt NVFP4 SiTU scale tests passed. - The ModelOpt mixed `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch test passed. - The K3 B/F_a fused-path tests passed, including CUDA Graph replay and block-FP8 dequantization. - Black, Python 3.12 `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed on the changed files. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not measured. signals.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Reland: Fuse shared-expert append into aiter grouped-topk
signals.text: ## Summary Relands #31323, which #35105 reverted after it failed `base-a-test-cpu (0)` on main. That failure is fixed here, along with two latent bugs found while re-testing on MI355X, and the optimization finally gets the test coverage it shipped without. ## What the optimization does On GLM-5.2 with the non-EP aiter grouped-topk route, every decoder layer ran a separate kernel to append the shared expert into the top-k ids/weights. Instead, the shared columns are pre-populated **once** in a persistent top-k buffer and the aiter kernel writes only the routed columns via row stride, so the per-layer append kernel disappears (prefill and decode). - **Bit-identical**: the shared column carries the same constant the append kernel used to write. - **Safe fallback**: the buffer is sized to the max prefill batch; larger token counts take the plain append path. - **Auto-enabled** when `moe_ep_size == 1` and `num_fused_shared_experts > 0`. Other archs, EP mode and non-applicable routes are untouched. GSM8K on MI355X TP4 (GLM-5.2-MXFP4): 0.931 → 0.933. Throughput and TPOT move under 1% either way — the gain is one fewer kernel launch per layer, not raw speed. ## Fixes on top of #31323 **1. Read the sizing config through `get_schedule()`** — the actual revert cause. `base-a-test-cpu (0)` failed with `alias-form process-global config field reads grew: 2 > baseline 0`. The ratchet baseline dropped to 0 on Aug 5, after this branch last ran green against a baseline of 12, so the two `ServerArgs` alias reads only became a violation once merged against current main. **2. `biased_grouped_topk_cpu` accepts `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor`.** `select_experts` passes the kwarg unconditionally, so on CPU + AMX the alias raised `TypeError` during argument binding even when the value was `None`. A non-`None` value is rejected, matching how `fused_topk_cpu` handles parameters it cannot serve. ## New test: `TestAiterGroupedTopkSharedFuse` #31323 shipped with nothing exercising the fused path — `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor` had no non-default coverage anywhere in the repo, which is why both latent bugs above had to be found by hand. `test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_remap_per_rank_shared_slots.py` now adds three tests: - **The buffer must equal the plain append, bit for bit.** The same input goes through the pre-populated buffer and through the plain append (forced by patching the token budget to 0), and the ids and weights must compare equal under `torch.equal`, not merely close. Covered over a decode step and three prefill chunk sizes on the DeepSeek-V3 / GLM-5 routing shape, under both `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor` spellings and four routed scaling factors. - **Expert parallelism must not fuse**, since the pre-populated shared ids only hold when the shared experts live on every rank. - **Reaching the path before the MoE EP group exists must fall back**, not raise — a regression test for fix 3. ## Validation On MI355X everything related to this change is green: the new tests (7 passed, 16 subtests) and the ratchet suite. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32087142988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32087142988)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32087142921](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32087142921)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [FlashInfer v0.6.18] add FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 mode
signals.text: ## Motivation @humansand Add an opt-in W4A16 compute mode for FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE and dense linear layers: weights remain NVFP4 while activations and outputs stay BF16. Registered tests cover online-quantized Nemotron MoE accuracy, serialized ModelOpt Qwen3 dense+MoE disk-reload invariance, and the existing dense W4A4 numerical path. Dependency: - This PR depends on **FlashInfer 0.6.18**. Its [`release-v0.6.18`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/tree/release-v0.6.18) branch contains CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE W4A16 support, SiTU support, the invocation-workspace lifetime fix, and the SM100/SM103 dense W4A16 GEMM from [#4466](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4466). - SGLang's pinned FlashInfer package and CI image must be updated to 0.6.18 before merge. This integration intentionally has no compatibility fallback for earlier FlashInfer APIs. - Historical MoE validation used the 20260817 nightly plus the workspace fix. Final dense+MoE reload validation used [`nightly-v0.6.18-20260818`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/nightly-v0.6.18-20260818) source at `0751be928d24187bd39a0dde45ce96418bc03ddf`, which contains #4466. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16` (default `false`). - Select `CuteDslMoEWrapper(quant_mode="w4a16")`, pass raw BF16 activations, and omit GEMM1/GEMM2 activation scales. - Reuse the existing packed NVFP4 weights and CuTe MMA-layout block scales, but construct weight-only decode alphas for both online-quantized and serialized ModelOpt weights. - Keep serialized ModelOpt NVFP4 dense layers in the existing `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod`. When the environment variable and `--fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` are both selected, its registered `fp4_gemm` compiler boundary dispatches to FlashInfer `mm_bf16_fp4`; otherwise the existing W4A4 `mm_fp4` route is unchanged. - Prepare dense W4A16 weights through `prepare_bf16_fp4_weights`, preserve loader-owned source scales for disk reload, and keep stable prepared scale/alpha bindings for decode CUDA graphs. Reuse the existing NVFP4_AWQ pre-scale operation before BF16 GEMM. - Recognize prepared W4A16 state in the generic quantized LM-head guard, and keep DeepSeek's W4A4-only GEMM+SwiGLU fusion disabled for W4A16. - Support the standard CuTe DSL v2 paths with no A2A or FlashInfer A2A on SM100-family GPUs (SM100/SM103). Keep FlashInfer A2A dispatch in BF16 by suppressing automatic NVFP4 dispatch and rejecting an explicit NVFP4-dispatch configuration; the existing DeepEP masked path remains W4A4-only. Both registered accuracy/reload tests exercise FlashInfer A2A, and the serving benchmark compares no A2A with FlashInfer A2A. - Preserve the configured finalize mode for ReLU2. For gated/SwiGLU W4A16, disable fused finalize and use FlashInfer's two-stage finalize path. - Register nightly `4-gpu-b200` end-to-end coverage for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8` with online NVFP4 expert-weight quantization. - Add a separate registered TP4/DP4/EP4 case with DP attention and FlashInfer A2A for serialized `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`: dense and MoE layers use W4A16, and two same-checkpoint disk reloads across weight/CUDA-graph release and resume must preserve deterministic decode text and token IDs exactly, with token logprobs within `1e-4`. This remains alongside the existing per-token NVFP4 CuTe DSL case. ## Accuracy Tests Environment: - MoE accuracy image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682` (`sha256:fa8774dd128600a09fd6d46670b06fb69a55dac8a3881e50ccf0916a45eb39af`) - Dense+MoE reload image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` (`sha256:51e576f02368480c055c7aadb67590d82b172e2392123ce4cf4cc8251b2d8caf`) - Hardware: 4 of 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs, compute capability SM103, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention and FlashInfer A2A - SGLang: MoE accuracy head `d01db73b433ce975ee055fe21499d31d72571098`; final dense+MoE validated head `e48dd823083eebbc66246371544256e10ac2e304`; historical MoE-dispatch benchmark head `508aef6135729ea66db55f3690f0036219145662` - Dense+MoE runtime: Python `3.12.3`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`, FlashInfer `0.6.18.dev20260818` package set with exact tagged source overlay at `0751be928d24187bd39a0dde45ce96418bc03ddf` MoE accuracy command: ```bash export PYTHONPATH=/hai-workspace/flashinfer-runtime-w4a16-fix:/hai-workspace/sglang/python export HF_HOME=/hai-workspace/hf-cache export SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/hai-workspace/sglang-cache-w4a16-a2a-20260817a export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 export SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=0 cd /hai-workspace/sglang/test python3 registered/backends/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_online_moe_backend.py \ TestFlashinferCuteDSLMoeBackendNvFp4OnlineW4A16.test_gsm8k -f ``` Final dense+MoE and W4A4 compatibility commands: ```bash base=/hai-workspace/sglang-w4a16-dense-validation repo="$base/src/sglang-side-by-side" cd "$repo/test" env \ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH="$repo/python" \ HF_HOME=/hai-workspace/.cache/huggingface \ FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE="$base/cache/side-by-side-w4a4-final-001/flashinfer" \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIR="$base/cache/side-by-side-w4a4-final-001/sglang" \ SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=0 \ SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=0 \ TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false \ python3 registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_linear_backends.py \ TestNvFp4LinearBackends.test_flashinfer_cutedsl -v env \ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ PYTHONPATH="$repo/python" \ HF_HOME=/hai-workspace/.cache/huggingface \ FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE="$base/cache/side-by-side-w4a16-final-001/flashinfer" \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIR="$base/cache/side-by-side-w4a16-final-001/sglang" \ SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=0 \ TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false \ python3 registered/rl/test_update_weights_from_disk_blackwell.py \ TestServerUpdateWeightsFromDiskNVFP4W4A16CuteDSL.test_parameterized_update_weights_from_disk \ -v -f ``` Results: ```text # Online FP8 checkpoint with online NVFP4 expert-weight quantization Flashinfer MoE A2A is enabled. Disable prefill CUDA graph because cuda_graph_config resolved prefill.backend='disabled'. Capture target verify CUDA graph end. elapsed=21.37 s Capture draft decode CUDA graph end. elapsed=7.97 s Capture draft extend CUDA graph end. elapsed=3.01 s Decode batch, ... cuda graph: True Total latency: 59.422 s Score: 0.965 Output throughput: 1330.554 token/s avg_spec_accept_length=3.112170753860127 Ran 1 test in 360.547s OK # Existing dense W4A4 CuTe DSL numerical path test_flashinfer_cutedsl (__main__.TestNvFp4LinearBackends.test_flashinfer_cutedsl) ... ok Ran 1 test in 3.050s OK # Serialized ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint: dense + MoE W4A16 Flashinfer MoE A2A is enabled. [MnnvlMemory] creating address with stride=536870912 Capture target decode CUDA graph end. # all 4 ranks, all 52 shapes through bs=512 Decode batch, ... cuda graph: True # Both update variants passed: flush_cache=true and flush_cache=false. # Each variant released weights, then restored weights, KV cache, and CUDA graphs; # the post-reload text, token IDs, and token logprobs matched the baseline. Update weights end. # first reload Update weights end. # second reload Ran 1 test in 295.491s OK elapsed_seconds=310 exit_status=0 ``` The serialized Qwen3 test covers dense and MoE W4A16, deterministic non-fused finalize, decode CUDA graphs, and two reload cycles through FlashInfer A2A. The Nemotron test covers model-quality accuracy, online expert-weight quantization, EAGLE, and target/draft FlashInfer A2A. GPU-validation log SHA-256 values: Nemotron `ced2b8d4f8211bb8c8c59e4656a3420c1b4511bb093bdca1250d83ab4479263a`; final Qwen3 reload `eb8c45b26676fea21b5dd1ba2b6a918995440c33f959b9183e5e238de2f285ae`; W4A4 dense numerical regression `9df0cc4a0727693faa8f156c153d4a405e71770c538282bf99f573f13722f778`. The two registered W4A16 tests use a 4,096-token FlashInfer dispatch capacity per rank, covering the inherited 16,384-token maximum prefill across EP4. The Nemotron DP-attention case follows SGLang's existing upstream exception and disables only target prefill CUDA graphs; target verify, draft decode, draft extend, and runtime decode graphs remain enabled. The Qwen3 reload test disables prefill graphs but captures and reuses full decode graphs. Fresh-cache wall times include source JIT compilation and are not serving-performance measurements. The generic quantized-LM-head guard and NVFP4_AWQ dense route are implemented but not exercised by these checkpoints. Static validation: ```text git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD: PASS git rev-list --merges upstream/main..HEAD: 0 python3 -m py_compile (all changed Python files): PASS pre-commit run --files (all changed files): PASS python3 scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py: PASS ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Four-GPU MoE-dispatch comparison at historical head `508aef613`. That head used W4A16 for MoE and W4A4 for dense linear layers, so these results characterize no-A2A versus FlashInfer A2A only; they are not a performance claim for the final combined dense+MoE W4A16 head. - Model: `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` - Common topology: TP4, DP4, DP attention, DP LM head, BF16 model activations, BF16 KV cache - No-A2A arm: EP1 tensor-parallel MoE - FlashInfer arm: EP4 with `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer` - Workload: 128 simultaneous requests, exactly 8,192 input and 2,048 output tokens each, `request-rate=inf`, concurrency 128, four warmups, cache flush, seed 42 - CUDA graphs: prefill disabled; decode `full` with max batch size 128 in both arms. signals.title: [AMD] [Kimi-K3] Fuse the KDA input projection into a single GEMM on ROCm
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation - KDA input projection on ROCm runs as two GEMMs per layer: a wide `[q, k, v, g]` projection (6144 rows/rank @ TP8) and a tiny `[f_a | b]` tail (128 + 12 rows/rank). - The tail is arithmetically negligible but still costs a full kernel launch and a second activation read every decode step. - Decode is bandwidth bound, so merging into one `N = 6288` GEMM makes the extra output columns nearly free and removes the second launch. - On gfx950 (`H = 7168`, TP8) the merged GEMM costs 0.55–0.73x the split pair for `M ≤ 64`, staying ahead up to a few hundred tokens; beyond that the untuned `N = 6288` shape loses to the tuned `N = 6144` one — so fusion is threshold-gated, not unconditional. - The `kimi_k3.py` comment warning that folding degrades kernel selection still holds for large-`M` prefill; this change reverses it only below the threshold, on ROCm, leaving the generic path untouched. ## Modifications - Merge the `[q, k, v, g]` and `[f_a | b]` projections into a single `N = 6288` GEMM (`_merge_kda_inproj_weights_hip`), gated by `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSE_KDA_INPROJ` and a decode token-count threshold (a few hundred tokens). - Prefill (~1000-token chunks) and the generic, non-ROCm path are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests This is a layout-only change — same weights and values, reached through views — so parity is expected. **Full GSM8K** — n=1319, 5-shot, 8x MI355X TP8, Triton attention backend, fusion on by default: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \ --num-questions 1319 \ --parallel 256 \ --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 512 \ --host http://127.0.0.1 \ --port 30001 ``` | Run | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.952 | 0.001 | | 2 | 0.951 | 0.001 | Both runs fall inside the documented 0.947–0.958 band (well above the 0.90 tripwire), consistent within noise. **Unit test:** `test/registered/amd/test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion.py` — 3 tests passed, 6 subtests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Kimi K3: ISL 8192, OSL 1024, TP 8, MI355X * 8 ### Throughput/GPU | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 131.94 | 132.11 | +0.14% | | 4 | 218.34 | 219.80 | +0.67% | | 8 | 362.23 | 364.64 | +0.67% | | 16 | 550.69 | 561.43 | +1.95% | | 32 | 764.92 | 781.20 | +2.13% | ### Median ITL | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 16.15 | 16.13 | -0.15% | | 4 | 18.73 | 18.54 | -0.99% | | 8 | 20.91 | 20.70 | -1.03% | | 16 | 24.57 | 23.98 | -2.42% | | 32 | 30.75 | 29.94 | -2.62% | ### Median TTFT | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 913.08 | 912.99 | -0.01% | | 4 | 1556.02 | 1552.53 | -0.22% | | 8 | 2640.40 | 2451.79 | -7.14% | | 16 | 4791.64 | 4781.60 | -0.21% | | 32 | 8944.96 | 9081.63 | +1.53% | ### Median TPOT | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 16.15 | 16.13 | -0.14% | | 4 | 19.14 | 18.96 | -0.94% | | 8 | 22.34 | 22.12 | -0.98% | | 16 | 28.12 | 27.48 | -2.28% | | 32 | 38.48 | 37.54 | -2.44% | ## Checklist -
