signals.title: [PD] Stage MLA DCP=8 relayout before Mooncake RDMA for KIMI K3
signals.text: ## Motivation When Prefill uses DCP size 1 and Decode uses DCP size greater than 1, each Decode rank owns a strided subset of the Prefill KV tokens. The existing Mooncake DCP relayout path builds transfer blocks only when both source and destination token addresses are contiguous. The destination offsets are packed, but the source offsets advance by `dcp_size`. As a result, the source is noncontiguous and the transfer is split into one RDMA block per token and KV layer. For Kimi K3 MLA FP8 KV cache, one token row is approximately: ```text (kv_lora_rank 512 + rope dimension 64) × 1 byte = 576 bytes ``` In a 56K-token, DCP=8, 24-MLA-layer deployment, this produces approximately 168K small transfer descriptors per Decode rank. The observed aggregate P-to-D bandwidth was about 1.23 GB/s across eight RDMA devices, despite the available link bandwidth being much higher. This PR adds an opt-in GPU staging path that gathers each Decode rank's strided token rows into contiguous registered memory before issuing Mooncake transfers. ```text Legacy: strided source tokens -> one descriptor per token and layer -> approximately 576-byte RDMA writes Staged: strided source tokens -> Triton byte-preserving gather -> contiguous layer-major staging buffer -> normally one descriptor per layer and destination page -> 64 × 576 bytes = 36 KiB writes for Kimi K3 ``` For the example above, the descriptor count is expected to decrease from approximately 168K to approximately 2.6K per rank. End-to-end post-change bandwidth and latency measurements are still pending on the target RDMA deployment. ## Modifications - Add an opt-in Prefill-side MLA DCP staging path for the Mooncake transfer backend: - `SGLANG_DISAGG_DCP_STAGING_BUFFER=1` - `SGLANG_DISAGG_DCP_STAGING_BUFFER_SIZE_MB=64` - Gather strided DCP-owned token rows into registered GPU memory using a fused Triton kernel. - Preserve KV bytes exactly by operating on `uint8` data, avoiding FP8 conversion or reinterpretation. - Store gathered data in a layer-major layout and build RDMA descriptors from destination-contiguous runs. - Split transfers into page-aligned batches when a relayout is larger than the configured staging buffer. - Support both direct MLA KV pools and hybrid-MLA pools such as Kimi K3's `HybridLinearKVPool`. - Use 64-bit Triton byte offsets so staging buffers larger than 2 GiB do not overflow. - Add a process-level circuit breaker: - If Triton gather compilation or execution fails, disable the staged path and replay the request through the legacy direct relayout path. - Mooncake/RDMA transfer failures are not caught or hidden by this fallback. - Keep the feature disabled by default. The existing direct DCP relayout path remains unchanged unless the environment variable is enabled. - Add environment validation and PD disaggregation documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The staging kernel performs a byte-preserving gather and does not change KV dtype or numerical representation. Added coverage includes: - CUDA byte-parity testing for gathered FP8-compatible KV rows. - CPU tests for: - DCP token ownership and layout. - Destination-contiguous block construction. - Page-aligned batching. - Direct MLA and hybrid-MLA pool detection. - Triton gather failure fallback and process-level disabling. - Verification that Mooncake transfer failures are not swallowed. - The Kimi Linear PD+DCP nightly suite now explicitly enables the staged path and covers: - Deterministic token ID and logprob parity against a monolithic baseline. - Physical-page and chunk-boundary prompts. - 32K long-context needle retrieval. - GSM8K accuracy with 200 examples and a score threshold of 0.88. Local validation completed: - `pre-commit` passed for all modified files. - Python syntax compilation passed. The registered CUDA and 8×B200 Kimi Linear acceptance tests were not run locally and are expected to run in the corresponding CI environments. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Legacy-path observation Kimi K3 deployment configuration: - Prefill DCP: 1 - Decode DCP: 8 - Physical page size: 64 - MLA KV dtype: FP8 - MLA KV token size: approximately 576 bytes per layer - MLA layers transferred: 24 - Input length: approximately 56K tokens Observed legacy behavior: - Approximately 168K transfer descriptors per Decode rank. - Most descriptors represented one token and one layer. - Approximately 576-byte RDMA payloads. - Aggregate P-to-D bandwidth: approximately 1.23 GB/s across eight RDMA devices. ### Expected staged-path behavior - Normally one transfer descriptor per destination page and KV layer. - Approximately 2.6K descriptors per rank for the same 56K-token request. - Approximately 36 KiB per full-page Kimi K3 transfer block. - Approximately 64× fewer descriptors. These figures describe the expected descriptor reduction. End-to-end post-change throughput, TTFT, and CPU profiling results are pending on the target Mooncake/RDMA environment. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with SGLang pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add unit and registered CUDA tests. - [x] Update PD disaggregation and environment-variable documentation. - [ ] Run the registered CUDA byte-parity test in a GPU CI environment. - [x] Run the Kimi Linear PD+DCP accuracy suite on 8×B200. - [ ] Collect post-change Mooncake/RDMA bandwidth, TTFT, and descriptor-count measurements. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32048239255](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32048239255) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32048239217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32048239217)

signals.title: fix(kernel) Fix Helion small-token prefill bug
signals.text: ## Motivation Fix shape handling in the wrapper for Helion KDA for short prefill requests. Also clearly reject non power of 2 head dim in decode. ## Modifications The Helion KDA backend had three issues. - For short prefill, the prefill Q/K/V may contain only the active tokens while gate and beta remain padded to a CUDA-graph bucket. Deriving the token count from the padded gate tensor caused invalid reshapes for short prompts. - Edge case: If the first prefill request had `T=1`, PyTorch could specialize size-one dimensions in the generated Helion trace. This issue only occurs if the first prefill is `T = 1`, `T > 1` is fine. - Decode used padded `hl.arange` lanes without masks when the key or value dimension was not a power of two. We made the following changes. - Validate that gate and beta cover every Q token, then trim their padded rows at the public Helion prefill boundary. This keeps direct callers consistent with the Triton `chunk_kda` contract. - Route only `T=1` prefill through Triton, preventing a size-one trace from poisoning later Helion shapes. The normal `T>1` Helion path is unchanged. - Reject non power of two head dim for decode (both kimi linear and kimi k3 have head dim = 128 so they're fine). ## Accuracy Tests A standalone sweep compared the public Helion and Triton prefill wrappers, including output, intermediate chunk states, and the mutated final state. Gate and beta padding was filled with large values so the comparison could not pass if either backend consumed padded rows. This not only confirms that Helion works now on short seqs, but that the accuracy is preserved. - input lengths `1, 3, 7, 15, 17, 31, 51, 63, 65, 127, 255, 513, 1023, 2047, 2049, 3001, 8191, 16385`; - fixed and two-sequence packed-varlen layouts; - `H=32`, `H=16`, and `H=12`; - FP32 and BF16 state. All **216/216 cases passed** with `atol=0.02, rtol=0.02`. | Compared value | Maximum absolute difference | |---|---:| | Output | 9.77e-4 | | Intermediate state | 7.81e-3 | | Final state | 4.02e-3 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The change does not affect performance. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [HiCache] Support DCP with DSpark
signals.text: ## Motivation DCP + HiCache + DSpark is currently rejected during server argument validation. Removing that guard exposed a draft HiCache sidecar sizing bug: draft indices inherit the target cache's DCP-wide logical index space, while the draft host pool was sized from only the target's physical per-rank rows. Once L1 eviction reached the uncovered range, the draft host transfer failed with `CUDA error: invalid argument`. ## Modifications - Allow DSPARK with HiCache when `--dcp-size > 1`, while retaining the guard for other speculative algorithms. - Size full draft HiCache sidecar pools from the target host pool's logical capacity. - Apply the same logical-capacity sizing to the legacy draft HiCache path. - Add a regression test for DCP-expanded draft sidecar sizing. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on RunPod node 5 with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs using a Kimi-K3 target and RadixArk Kimi-K3 DSpark draft model, TP8/DCP8, A2A, HiCache L2, and the normal CUDA graph path. - Eviction stress test: 64 requests x 16,384 input tokens, concurrency 48. - Result: 64/64 successful; 1,048,576 input tokens and 512 output tokens processed in 52.00 seconds. - Post-run `/health_generate`: HTTP 200. - No scheduler exceptions or CUDA errors after the fix. - `test_server_args.py`: 144 passed, 15 subtests passed. - `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: 4 passed. [TODO] more advanced tests involving DeepSWE ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a capacity/correctness fix rather than a kernel-path performance change. The eviction stress test above observed approximately 20,164 input tokens/s. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors quantized lm_head instead of value-casting it
signals.text: ## Motivation compressed-tensors checkpoints that quantize `lm_head` (e.g. FP8 per-channel weights targeted via `re:.*lm_head`) currently load as gibberish: `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` returns `None` for `ParallelLMHead`, so the head falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` — the packed fp8 weight is value-cast into a bf16 parameter and `lm_head.weight_scale` is silently dropped (`Parameter lm_head.weight_scale not found in params_dict` at load). ## Modifications - `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method`: add a `ParallelLMHead` branch that resolves a linear scheme and returns `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod` (mirroring the existing ModelOpt handling); unquantized heads keep the current embedding default. - New `get_lm_head_scheme`: the head is treated as quantized only when a config target names it by layer name (exact, `re:` regex, or dotted suffix) and it is not in `ignore`. Module-type targets like `Linear` are not consulted, so checkpoints following the common convention (head unquantized and unmentioned) are unaffected. The resolved target is passed through to `get_scheme_dict` so suffix matches are not re-derived by the stricter `find_matched_target`. Block-FP8 heads are rejected with a clear error (the vocab-parallel weight loader cannot shard `vocab/block_n` weight scales). - Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_lm_head.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`). No other changes needed: the vocab-parallel weight loader already shards `output_dim=0` params, the model loader already runs `process_weights_after_loading` on the head, and the logits path already routes through `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method`. Known limits: models that construct `ParallelLMHead` without a `prefix` keep today's unquantized-head behavior (the empty layer name never matches a target); `update_weights_from_disk` with a quantized head is untested; speculative-decoding draft paths that borrow the target head are a separate follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests A/B on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with a Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint (NVFP4 MLPs, FP8 per-channel `lm_head`), identical flags, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`: | | GSM8K | Invalid | |---|---|---| | main | 0.000 | 0.850 | | this PR | 0.955 | 0.000 | On main, greedy decoding degenerates into repetition loops on any prompt; with this PR the head loads through `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` and the `weight_scale` warning is gone. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No impact on unquantized-head checkpoints (resolution happens once at init). A quantized head replaces a bf16 matmul with the standard fp8 linear path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Fix registered HiCache host pointer aliases
signals.text: ## Motivation Registered HiCache host allocations can have different CPU and GPU virtual addresses. This is observable on MI355X, where `hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is false. Passing the CPU VA to a custom kernel causes a GPU memory fault even though runtime copy APIs can still accept that address. The affected paths include AOT/JIT HiCache transfers, Mamba transfers, HiSparse copies, and host-pool pointer tables. CPU-side storage and disaggregation metadata must continue to expose the original CPU VA. ## Modifications - Add a target-device-aware `get_device_accessible_ptr` AOT API using `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` / `hipHostGetDevicePointer`. - Resolve direct registered-host tensor operands at AOT and JIT kernel launch boundaries while preserving the caller's current device. - Build CUDA/ROCm host-pool kernel pointer tables from device-accessible aliases for MHA, MLA, K-only, DSV4 paged/state, and DSA pools. - Keep raw CPU addresses for unregister, contiguous-buffer metadata, page metadata, and storage/disaggregation consumers. - Preserve unpinned, NPU, and MUSA pointer behavior. - Add registered-mmap regressions for pointer domains, AOT/JIT transfers, and CUDA graph capture/replay. ## Accuracy Tests ROCm 7.2 / MI355X (`gfx950`), Docker image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260813`: - Fresh ROCm AOT build: passed. - `test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: `15 passed`. - `test_transfer_mamba.py`: `16 passed`. - `test_hisparse.py`: `16 passed, 2 skipped`. - `test_mem_pool_host.py`: `9 passed`. - Registered-mmap post-rebase regressions: `3 passed`. - Native HIP runtime comparison: alias matches `hipHostGetDevicePointer`; wrong-device input is rejected; current device is restored. - Repository pre-commit hooks over the rebased PR diff: passed. CUDA validation in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130` (compile-only because this host has no NVIDIA GPU): - HiCache, Mamba, and HiSparse JIT modules compiled and loaded for SM90. - Modified AOT `transfer.cu` and `common_extension.cc` translation units compiled for SM90. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This is a correctness fix for registered-host pointer address domains; it does not change kernel bodies or transfer algorithms. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [Fix] Transformers-fallback (GPT-NeoX) + KV pool config (DeepSeek-VL2)
signals.text: ## Summary Three small fixes surfaced by consecutive downstream accuracy runs. All three are one-liners (plus comments); the first two live in the Transformers-fallback layer, the third in `ModelConfig`. ### 1. `hf_to_sglang_mapper` — map `gpt_neox.` and `embed_out.` `GPTNeoXForCausalLM` has no native SGLang impl → falls back to `TransformersForCausalLM`. The fallback calls `AutoModel.from_config(config)`, which returns the bare `GPTNeoXModel` backbone (`embed_in`, `layers`, `final_layer_norm`) as `self.model`; `self.lm_head` is materialized separately by `CausalMixin`. Pythia / NeoX checkpoints were saved from `GPTNeoXForCausalLM.state_dict()`, so keys carry a `gpt_neox.` wrapper prefix for the backbone and a top-level `embed_out.` for the LM head. The base mapper has no rule for either, so the catch-all `""` → `"model."` fires and produces `model.gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` — which the loader can't find (`ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.gpt_neox' ...`). **Fix:** add two prefix rules alongside the existing `"transformer.": "model."` (GPT-2 analogue): - `"gpt_neox.": "model."` — strip the wrapper prefix so backbone keys land under `self.model.*`. - `"embed_out.": "lm_head."` — route the LM head to SGLang's `self.lm_head` slot. ### 2. `skip_substrs` — skip GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` causal-mask buffer Older GPT-NeoX checkpoints include a persistent causal-mask buffer named `gpt_neox.layers.N.attention.bias`. Newer transformers versions register the same buffer with `persistent=False`, so it is absent from the constructed model's tree. `self.skip_substrs` already skips GPT-2-style `.attn.bias` / `.attn.masked_bias` (attention module named `attn`), but not GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` (attention module named `attention`). Result: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.attention.bias' ...`. **Fix:** add `.attention.bias` to the skip list. The already-present `.masked_bias` catches the fill-value counterpart regardless of attention module name. ### 3. `ModelConfig.v_head_dim` — treat `0` as unset (fixes DeepSeek-VL2 non-MLA V-cache) `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s `language_config` sets `use_mla=False` **and** `v_head_dim=0` — the `0` is an MLA-disabled sentinel from the checkpoint's DeepseekV2-flavored config, not a real head dimension. `ModelConfig.__init__` currently substitutes `head_dim` for `v_head_dim` only when the attribute is `None`, so a `getattr` that returns `0` slips through into `self.v_head_dim`. `pool_configurator.py` then reads `model_config.v_head_dim` directly in the non-MLA branch, and per-slot V-buffers get allocated with last dim = 0. The first extend prefill fails: ``` File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 192, in _set_kv_buffer_impl v_cache[indices] = v RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [432, 10, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [432, 10, 0] ``` DeepSeek-VL2 explicitly selects the standard (non-MLA) `DeepseekForCausalLM` language model when `use_mla=False` (`sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py`), which produces real V with the usual `num_kv_heads * head_dim` layout — the attention layer is correct; the pool is what's mis-sized. **Fix:** swap the guard to `if not self.v_head_dim:` so both `None` and `0` fall back to `self.head_dim`. MLA architectures are unaffected — their architecture-specific `elif` branches later in the same block overwrite `self.v_head_dim` with the real value from the text config. ## Test plan - [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for all three files. - [x] `EleutherAI/pythia-12b` (TP=2, triton) — reproduces the missing-mapper failure on `main`; loads through with fix 1. - [x] `EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b` (TP=2, triton) — with fix 1 applied, reproduces the missing-skip failure on `main`; loads through with fix 2, warmup succeeds, first `POST /generate` returns 200. - [x] `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny` (TP=1, triton, `--disable-radix-cache`, mem-fraction 0.55) — reproduces the `_set_kv_buffer_impl` shape-mismatch on `main`; with fix 3, KV cache allocates `K size = V size = 3.38 GB` (previously `V size = 0.00 GB`), text `POST /generate` returns 200 with valid tokens. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32265644409](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265644409)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32265644129](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265644129)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix: abort handling for dispatched requests after client disconnect
signals.text: ## Summary This PR fixes an issue where a request could continue decoding after the client disconnected, wasting GPU resources and repeatedly logging: ```text Received output for rid=... but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager. ``` ## Root Cause When a request handler was cancelled after dispatch, TokenizerManager removed its `rid_to_state` entry immediately. The disconnect abort path checks this state before sending an AbortReq, so the abort was skipped while the request continued running in the scheduler. A related race also existed for chunked-prefill requests: if a request moved out of the chunked-prefill slot before its deferred abort was processed, the abort could be lost. ## Changes - Track whether each request has been dispatched to the scheduler. - Remove undelivered request states locally on handler failure. - Abort dispatched requests and retain their state until scheduler cleanup completes. - Deduplicate abort requests and abort metrics. - Preserve retry behavior when abort dispatch fails. - Track generated request IDs used by parallel sampling. - Retry deferred chunked-prefill aborts after a request moves to another scheduler queue. - Add regression tests for disconnect cleanup, abort deduplication, dispatch failures, parallel sampling, and chunked-prefill transitions. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32225602246](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225602246)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32225602043](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225602043)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [GDN] Validate FlashInfer Cake CP prefill on Blackwell
signals.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer [#4539](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4539) replaces the SM100/SM103 CP-selected GDN prefill implementation with the Cake backend while preserving the public `chunk_gated_delta_rule` API and its `use_cp="auto"` policy. SGLang already calls that public API; this PR makes the auto policy explicit and adds an SGLang-level route/contract test for the new backend. This PR depends on FlashInfer #4539 and a subsequent FlashInfer release. It intentionally does not pin SGLang production dependencies to an unreleased Git commit; the new test skips when the installed FlashInfer build does not yet expose the Cake route. ## Modifications - Pass `use_cp="auto"` explicitly from `FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`. - Add an SM100/SM103 BF16 GQA generic-tail test through the real SGLang fixture and `FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`. - Require the test invocation to enter Cake exactly once and make the legacy SM100 non-CP route fatal. - Compare output and selected final-state rows against the same FlashInfer revision with `use_cp=False` at `atol=rtol=1e-2`. - Verify Q/K/V/gate/beta/cu-seqlens/cache indices and unselected state rows are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.3, driver 580.159.03: - Targeted SGLang pytest: `1 passed, 7 deselected` (Slurm job `3117357`; the test executed rather than skipping). - Candidate route: FlashInfer #4539 Cake path; external/non-CP fallback is fatal. - The SGLang route test compares #4539 Cake against the same candidate revision with `use_cp=False`; output and selected final state match at `atol=rtol=1e-2`. - The benchmark runner independently repeats the same-revision `use_cp=False` output/state check on the dedicated B=1, L=65 generic-tail case. The three performance rows enforce the intended CP routes plus exact input and unselected-state immutability; the #4539 base CP route (`a91f9fa30a7e4752d8febcf108f7f64984858751`) is used only as the timing arm, not as a numerical oracle. - Maximum observed absolute output error: `2.44140625e-4` - Maximum observed absolute selected-state error: `3.90625e-3` - Both candidate and baseline preserve all input tensors and unselected state rows exactly. ### Model-level GSM8K On the same GB300, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` was evaluated on the same 200 GSM8K questions with 5-shot completion prompts, one request at a time, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=512`. Radix caching was disabled in both arms because FlashInfer CP prefill does not yet support the state-checkpoint outputs needed by SGLang's radix state tracking. | Prefill arm | GSM8K exact match | Difference vs. Triton | |---|---:|---:| | FlashInfer #4539 Cake | 0.890 (178/200) | 0.000 | | Triton control | 0.890 (178/200) | — | For the Cake arm, the live dispatcher reported `extend=FlashInferGDNKernel`, a job-unique empty workspace produced seven SM103 Cake cubins, and the server log contained zero non-CP fallback warnings. The Triton arm reported `extend=TritonGDNKernel` and produced no Cake cubins. Both arms exceeded the predeclared 0.80 accuracy threshold. This is an accuracy comparison, not an end-to-end speed claim: decode used Triton in both arms and dominates the sequential evaluation latency. GSM8K Slurm job: `3123124`; evidence SHA-256: `b3d99f0fa31896e52798af3eed4f4d8c35b3877328065b0daaf8152f0adbf5d8`; dataset SHA-256: `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.3, driver 580.159.03. These are SGLang adapter-level prefill calls (`FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`) with BF16 Q/K/V/state, Hq=Hk=2, Hv=8, D=128. Each row below uses an exact shape cell present in the original PR4078 benchmark set. The BF16 SGLang input/state profile is stated separately and is not presented as PR4078's dtype profile; no extra generic rows are included. | Batch | Sequence lengths | #4539 Cake (ms) | #4539 base CP (ms) | Speedup | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | `[2048]` | 0.433250 | 0.485474 | 1.121x | | 1 | `[8192]` | 0.444626 | 0.511026 | 1.149x | | 4 | `[2048, 2048, 2048, 2048]` | 0.420082 | 0.487810 | 1.161x | Geometric-mean speedup: **1.144x**. Method: same-process ABBA paired samples using Cake `bench_gpu_time_interleaved` (`bench_gpu_time`), required CUPTI GPU activity timing, cold-L2 flush before each sample, 20 ms warmup and 100 ms measurement budget per arm, and a steady-state SM clock gate. The three rows collected 310–384 samples per arm at 2070/2070 MHz in Slurm job `3119121`. During the timed rows, both the candidate non-CP path and base-revision non-CP path were fatal, so every measured call used the intended CP route; the dedicated correctness case intentionally invoked the candidate revision's non-CP path as its numerical reference. Commits: - SGLang: `7cd1dcadc8bdd9e7737d6a0dc4c773600119ac77` - FlashInfer candidate: `d32513c6b5ef378f5ecd95511a9f35e7e2f58b19` - FlashInfer #4539 base: `a91f9fa30a7e4752d8febcf108f7f64984858751` - Cake timing implementation: `25536d8f0acd0eb4503d9fd6b46509b9ac76a115` - Evidence SHA-256: `4c618d8bd8f184177e0be138e99ed0d2da7f2c42881bce9ec6089834ab304621` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [formatting guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [testing guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required for this explicit routing/test-only change; this PR body documents the upstream dependency and validation. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process This is opened as a draft until FlashInfer #4539 is merged and available in an SGLang-supported FlashInfer release. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32105664238](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32105664238)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32105664058](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32105664058)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU] Add diffusion server test config for Intel XPU B60
signals.text: ## Motivation **Let the `multimodal_gen` diffusion server tests run on Intel XPU with correct expectations.** The diffusion server tests compare generated images against committed ground-truth images and check stage timings against committed perf baselines. Both sets of reference values are CUDA-derived, and neither is reachable from XPU today: - `get_consistency_platform()` has no XPU branch, so an XPU run silently falls through to the `h100` thresholds. - `BASELINE_CONFIG` composes per-platform perf overrides for Ascend and MUSA, but there is no XPU entry. The image mismatch is not a correctness bug. XPU seeds its initial latent noise from a different RNG stream than CUDA, so the pixels cannot match bit-for-bit: the image stays semantically identical (CLIP remains high) while `ssim` / `psnr` / `mean_abs_diff` degrade. Comparing XPU output against CUDA thresholds therefore fails on a difference that carries no signal. This PR adds XPU as a first-class platform in both registries, following the existing Ascend and MUSA pattern. ## Modifications Purely additive: 4 files, 56 insertions, 0 deletions. - **`test/test_utils.py`** — register `intel_xpu_b60` in `CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD_FILE_BY_PLATFORM`, add the `intelxpub60` alias, and add the `current_platform.is_xpu()` branch to `get_consistency_platform()`. - **`test/server/consistency_thresholds/intel_xpu_b60.json`** — XPU consistency thresholds for `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` and `fsdp-inference`. - **`test/server/xpu/perf_baselines_xpu.json`** — XPU perf baselines for `fsdp-inference`, measured on Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.71 GiB per card). - **`test/server/testcase_configs.py`** — chain the XPU baseline file into `BASELINE_CONFIG`, alongside the existing Ascend and MUSA `.update()` calls. No CUDA path changes: both new files are read only when the resolved platform is XPU, and the two registry additions are new keys. ## Thresholds | case | clip | ssim | psnr | mean_abs_diff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `fsdp-inference` | 0.97 | 0.6 | 11.0 | 37.0 | | `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` | 0.98 | 0.79 | 15.7 | 17.2 | Only these two cases were measured on XPU hardware. Every other case still inherits from `h100.json`; that is called out in the `_comment` field of the threshold file so the remaining cases can be triaged the same way rather than being assumed correct. ## Dependency Blocked on #33320, which adds `CustomOp.forward_xpu`. `dispatch_forward()` already returns `self.forward_xpu` on XPU, but the base-class method does not exist yet, so any `multimodal_gen` `CustomOp` raises `AttributeError` on XPU before these test configs are reached. This PR is the test-configuration half; #33320 is the runtime half. ## Accuracy Tests Verified on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.7 GiB per card): ``` python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_2_gpu.py::TestDiffusionServerTwoGpu::test_diffusion_generation[fsdp-inference] ``` Model `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo`. Passes end to end in ~157 s, including the consistency check against the thresholds above. Measured CLIP 0.9779 (passes); SSIM 0.6609 / PSNR 12.0434 / mean-abs-diff 33.3489, which fail the H100 thresholds and pass the XPU ones. XPU output is deterministic across 4 runs (identical md5). The perf baselines are single-host measurements, not an averaged multi-run distribution, so they are starting reference values rather than tight regression bounds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — no new test case is introduced; this PR adds the platform configuration that existing diffusion server tests read on XPU. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing behaviour change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). cc: @siju-samuel @rbabukv <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32237906482](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237906482)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32237906272](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237906272)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [UnifiedTree] feat: support runtime attach/detach
signals.text: ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache.attach_storage_backend` / `detach_storage_backend` were stubs that always returned `False`, so the `/hicache/storage-backend` admin API only worked with `HiRadixCache`. This implements them for the unified tree. Preceding fix for #35081. Supersedes #35240 (same feature, developed in parallel). ## Modifications **`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py` (new).** `StorageAttachment` owns the storage backend lifecycle: policy validation, extra-config parsing, controller attach, the ordered teardown, and `apply_runtime_config()`. Keeping it beside the tree rather than inside it leaves `UnifiedRadixCache` on cache logic and gives the three entry points — startup, the admin API, and the atexit hook — one implementation. `UnifiedRadixCache` goes from 2764 to 2520 lines. `apply_runtime_config()` is the single point where storage turns on, which is why the hash backfill below lives there rather than in `attach()`. **Hash-chain backfill (correctness).** Page hashes chain off the parent's last hash, and `_add_new_node` only computes them when storage is enabled. A node built before attach therefore has no hash, and hashing its children against it restarts the chain mid-sequence — the resulting L3 keys claim to encode a full prefix but only encode a suffix, so an unrelated request starting with those tokens loads KV computed under a different prefix, silently. Reproduced end-to-end with `--page-size 64` and explicit `input_ids` (P, R, Q are 128 tokens each): request `P+R` with storage off, attach, request `P+R+Q`, flush, then request `Q+S`. | | L3 hit for the `Q`-prefixed request | |---|---| | without backfill | **128 tokens** — loaded KV computed after `P+R` | | with backfill | **0** — correctly misses | | control: same sequence after its own backup | 128 in both, so L3 itself is healthy | `UnifiedTreeCore.backfill_missing_hash_values()` walks parent-before-child so each node hashes against an already-filled parent. **`cache_controller.py`.** The storage control queues are now initialized to `None` in `__init__` instead of only existing after `_start_storage_threads()`, so a detach on a server that never attached is a clean no-op rather than an `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Tests Output stability is asserted throughout: every scenario re-runs fixed prompts and compares them byte-for-byte against a baseline captured before any attach. ## Tests **15-scenario attach/detach state machine**, run in one server process, asserting per step that the HTTP result is as expected, the server stays healthy, output is unchanged, and `GET /hicache/storage-backend` reflects reality: - traffic → attach → traffic → detach → traffic - attach → traffic → detach - attach → attach (same backend → 200, policies updated; different backend → 400, state unchanged) - attach → detach → detach; detach before any attach - attach/detach cycled 5× with traffic in between - interleaved traffic/attach/traffic/attach/traffic/detach/traffic/detach/traffic - L3 actually used when attached (960 tokens) and unused when detached (0) - invalid policies rejected without changing state - attach onto a warm tree, then extend an existing prefix (the backfill path) - **attach/detach hammered under concurrent traffic**: 16 ops → `[200, 400×15]`, every 400 a `not idle` refusal, state never half-applied, no output drift - **8× attach + real L3 traffic + detach**: L3 hit count constant at 960 across rounds, which is the observable proof that host pages come back (the scheduler's invariant checker guards the device pool but not the host pool) Result: **157 PASS / 0 FAIL on 1 GPU and again under `--tp-size 2`** (48 attaches, repeatedly creating and destroying the prefetch gloo groups; no traceback, SIGQUIT, leak or NCCL/gloo anomaly after server ready). **Unit tests** — `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` pins the contract that a backfilled hash chain is identical to one hashed from the start. Verified by mutation: stubbing `backfill_missing_hash_values` to `return 0` turns two cases red; restoring it turns them green. Full file: 1046 passed, 0 failed. **Registered e2e** — `test_hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach.py` now covers both implementations via a subclass, so the existing HiRadixCache coverage is retained rather than switched over. 2 passed. ## Notes `HiRadixCache` has the same unhashed-node issue and the same non-idempotent detach when no backend was ever attached. Both are left alone here to keep this PR scoped to the unified tree. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32210047237](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210047237)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32213695558](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32213695558)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 low concurrency optimizations
signals.text: ## Summary - Vendor selected Kimi-K3 gfx950 FlyDSL kernels in SGLang with a fail-closed source selector. - Add MLA output-gate, KDA group64/B2, 12-head AITER MLA decode-side padding, and optional latent-tail integrations. - Use one cooperative preactivated MoE producer for exact M2/M4 while larger batches retain the existing fallback. - Add the Kimi-K3 M16384 GEMM tuning profile. - Use the AITER revision already pinned by SGLang; no AITER update is required. ## Runtime configuration Base Kimi-K3 AITER configuration: ```bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 export AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=0 export SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=sglang ``` Enable the PR features: ```bash # MLA output-gate fusion export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_GATE=1 # KDA input projection; B2_FUSIONS adds its exact-M2 specialization export SGLANG_K3_AITER_KDA_GROUP64=1 export SGLANG_K3_AITER_B2_FUSIONS=1 # Unified exact-M2/M4 cooperative MoE preroute export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MOE_PREROUTE_FP8=1 export SGLANG_K3_PREROUTE_PREACTIVATED_SHARED=1 # M=16384 GEMM tuning rows export SGLANG_K3_AITER_M16384_PROFILE=1 ``` The latent-tail profile is independent and remains off by default because it reduces token capacity. Enable it only when explicitly evaluating that trade-off: ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_LATENT_TAIL_FP8=1 ``` The 12-head padding path has no feature flag. It is selected automatically for the covered Kimi-K3 shape when using AITER MLA decode, for example: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --decode-attention-backend aiter ``` All integrations are shape/architecture guarded and fail closed to the existing implementation when the runtime contract is not covered. ## Performance - Unified M2 cooperative preroute: `+1.08%` throughput, `-1.11%` TPOT over the prior M2 design. - Unified M4 cooperative preroute: `+3.08%` throughput, `-3.33%` TPOT over the matched M4 baseline. - M16384 profile: approximately `+0.7%` throughput at C8/C16/C32 and `-2.34%` C32 TTFT. ## Accuracy - GSM8K 1319: `0.953` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Test plan - [x] Selected FlyDSL tests against pinned AITER `d9e5ef7`: 35 passed - [x] C2 8192/256 smoke: 8/8 requests succeeded - [x] C4 8192/256 smoke: 8/8 requests succeeded - [x] GSM8K 50: 1.000 - [x] GSM8K 1319: 0.953 - [x] Forbidden listed-PR path audit and `git diff --check` The current container installs a newer FlyDSL than the old AITER pin expects for full-model MoE startup. The vendored focused kernels were tested directly against the exact pin; full-model smoke used the current compatible AITER checkout. signals.title: test: switch the Inkling-Small NVFP4 deterministic suite to DSPARK
signals.text: ## Motivation Roadmap item under #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for the unified radix cache, speculative-decoding row (DSpark / DFlash). `TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact` in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py` was added to cover the spec side of the sconv/mamba checkpoint save. It cannot reach it: `_is_mamba_track_enabled()` is a method of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`, and EAGLE targets disable the prefill CUDA graph outright (`cuda_graph_setup.py`, #28386), so the runner is never constructed. Measured — reverting #34043 leaves that class green: ``` TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact, #34043 reverted → 2 passed, avg_kl_div=0.0 log: "Disable prefill CUDA graph for EAGLE target on tc_piecewise (#28386)" ``` DSPARK and DFlash are not `is_eagle()`, keep the prefill graph, and are the algorithms #34043 actually fixed (that PR measured a DFlash SWEBench subset going 55% → 35% from zeroed sconv state). ## Modifications `TestInklingSmallNvfp4Deterministic` now runs with DSPARK driving decode, and is renamed `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic`. The helpers, the 1e-9 floor, the `extra_buffer` / SWA / mamba-ratio / `KL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` setup and the dedicated server are all unchanged. Two knobs move: `--mem-fraction-static` 0.85 → 0.80 for this class only (see below), and the file's `est_time` 1700 → 2000 for the draft load and graph capture. This replaces rather than adds: the DSPARK config exercises the same NVFP4 weights and the same `flashinfer_trtllm` fp4 GEMM/MoE path, so the FP4-regression coverage the class was written for is retained, and the non-spec cache-restore logic is covered on the shrunken checkpoint in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`. A second no-spec arm here would cost another server launch on a `4-gpu-b200` slot for coverage that is not unique. The trade that buys: a reading here is no longer self-attributing. Inkling-Small is a 256-expert MoE where dropping `--enable-deterministic-inference` alone reads 5.0e-02 — the same order as the bug signal below — so a red case needs a manual re-run without the speculative flags to separate a state-reuse bug from batch variance. That is written into the class docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Revert-then-red against #34043. First measured on the **bf16** `Inkling-Small` checkpoint at tp=4 on GB300 (same server args plus `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, minus the fp4 flags): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **8.05e-02** | | `..._decode_cache_hit` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | no-spec arm (all three) | 0.0 | 0.0 | Eight orders of magnitude above the floor, and the failure lands where the mechanism predicts — the corruption reaches a request that *restores* a prefix, so the flush-both comparison and the decode-side reuse stay clean. The no-spec arm staying green under the same revert is what identified the reading as speculative-state-specific. Sanity of that run: `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, accept len 1.7–3.5, `cuda graph: True`, and `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend` resolves to `full`, so the class reaches the line #34043 changed. Probe sensitivity with `--enable-deterministic-inference` dropped: 5.0e-02 / 4.3e-02 / 5.9e-03. Since re-measured on this file's own config — NVFP4 `Inkling-Small` at tp=4 on 4x GB300 (SM100, same `modelopt_fp4` / `flashinfer_trtllm` path the class already used; there is precedent for that pairing in `test/registered/gb300/test_glm52_nvfp4.py`): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **1.10e-01** | | **`..._decode_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`** | ``` fix in place : 3 passed (650.79s) #34043 revert: 2 failed, 1 passed ``` So both open questions are closed: the bf16 DSPARK draft does pair with the `modelopt_fp4` target, and the exact-0 baseline holds on NVFP4. The signal is stronger here than on bf16 — the revert also drops one prompt out of the decode-cache reuse, which trips the `min_cache_hit_ratio=0.99` this class already asserts. Whole file on 4x GB300: 5 passed in 1093 s. **`--mem-fraction-static` is 0.80 for this class, not the 0.85 the others use.** The first CI run OOMed mid-test on B200: the draft weights and the speculative CUDA graphs (`974.89 MiB allocated in private pools`) left `avail mem=0.40 GB` at 0.85 on a 178 GB card. The GB300 verification could not have caught this — 284 GB per GPU is 60% more headroom. At 0.80 the KV pool still reports ~6.2M tokens against the ~130k this file uses, so the slack costs nothing. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test-only. On 4x GB300 the class runs 650.79 s and the whole file 1093 s; spec roughly doubles this class against the no-spec arm it replaces (360 s → 685 s on the bf16 checkpoint at the same tp). `est_time` 2000 is an estimate for B200 pending a real CI number, which `scripts/ci/update_est_time.py` will correct. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32323829147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32323829147)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32323829021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32323829021)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signals.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32236976842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32236976842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32236976735](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32236976735)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 fuse MLA Q and cache preparation
signals.text: ## Summary - Fuse Kimi-K3 identity-RoPE Q materialization, Q concat, and latent KV-cache write through AITER's per-head MLA cache operator. - Support BF16-Q/BF16-KV, FP8-Q/FP8-KV, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV mixed output for Triton decode. - Dispatch only on gfx950 decode/idle batches with contiguous covered inputs; DCP and unsupported contracts fail closed to the existing split/cat/cache path. ## Runtime configuration ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION=1 ``` Validated FP8-KV configuration: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend triton \ --decode-attention-backend triton ``` BF16 KV is also covered. The larger measured gain is with BF16-Q + FP8-KV. ## AITER dependency This SGLang integration requires AITER #4342 / commit `770790cd` or newer `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` semantics, including the `compute_all_q_rope` behavior used for correct batch-64 execution. The AITER revision currently pinned by main (`d9e5ef7`) is insufficient: its old schema rejects the new argument, and a 14-argument compatibility call produces incorrect token-64 output. This PR intentionally documents rather than changes the AITER pin. ## Accuracy Tests - Focused operator tests: `9 passed` - GSM8K 1319: `0.955` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Historical matched results for the same integration: - BF16 KV: C32 `+0.63%`, C64 `+0.53%` - FP8 KV: C32 `+3.26%`, C64 `+3.57%` - FP8-KV median TPOT: approximately `-4%` ## Test plan - [x] BF16/BF16, FP8/FP8, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV operator tests at token counts 1 and 64 - [x] Negative slot handling - [x] CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs - [x] Narrow support/fallback predicates - [x] Full GSM8K 1319 with Triton prefill/decode and FP8 KV - [ ] Re-run after the target branch updates its AITER pin AITER prefill was not used in the full-model test because 12-head AITER attention-backend enablement is maintained separately; this fusion acts on the decode path. signals.title: [sglang-miles] Fix p2p weight registry: draft worker overwrite, fused indexer mapping, registration retries
signals.text: Fixes found while verifying miles p2p (RDMA) weight updates on GLM-5.2 744B fp8 with MTP enabled. Companion miles PR: radixark/miles#2605. **Worker-keyed engine-info bootstrap registry** (`engine_info_bootstrap_server.py`, `remote_instance_weight_transporter.py`, `model_runner.py`, `http_server.py`) With speculative decoding, the draft worker's `ModelRunner.initialize()` also registers with the EngineInfoBootstrapServer. The registry was keyed by `tp_rank` alone, last write wins, and the draft registers after the target — so the p2p client received the draft model's weight table and RDMA session for every rank: ordinary target params appeared missing on the remote and every write bucket failed. The registry key is now `(worker, tp_rank)` (`worker` in `{"target", "draft"}`), the transporter tags its registrations, and the two query endpoints take an optional `worker` parameter defaulting to `"target"` — existing clients keep their behavior, and a p2p client can address the draft explicitly. Long-running MTP training needs exactly that: the trained nextn layer must reach the draft, or speculative acceptance decays to zero as the target trains away from the frozen draft (observed as `accept rate: 0.00` followed by an out-of-range index assert in decode ~100 steps in). **Fused DSA indexer weights unmappable by ParameterMapper** (`deepseek_v2.py`) With `use_dsa_indexer_fusion`, the model has one bf16 `indexer.wk_weights_proj` per layer and no `indexer.wk` / `indexer.weights_proj` params. The checkpoint loader folds the unfused names via `_load_fused_indexer_wk`, but `ParameterMapper` — built from `stacked_params_mapping` and used by the p2p staging path — had no entry, so every indexer wk/weights_proj tensor sent by the trainer was silently dropped. Added the two stacked entries, gated on the fusion config (not a `named_parameters()` probe: the NextN subclass builds its mappings before its model exists), with dot-anchored patterns so already-fused checkpoint names cannot be rewritten into nonsense. **NextN name mapping for external weight mappers** (`deepseek_nextn.py`) `mutate_weight_preload` maps `model.layers.{num_hidden_layers}.*` to `model.decoder.*` so `ParameterMapper.from_model` on the draft model resolves converter-emitted nextn names the same way the loader does. **Registration was one-shot and swallowed failures** (`remote_instance_weight_transporter.py`) A transient connection failure while PUTting to the bootstrap server was logged and forgotten; the missing rank then surfaced minutes later as a 404 at the first weight update, far from the cause. Both registrations now retry (24 x 5s, timeout 10s) and raise after exhaustion. **Inverse ue8m0 scale transform for non-128-divisible row counts** (`fp8_utils.py`) The weights-checker comparator crashed on params like `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` (mn=2624): the inverse transform assumed the repeated-scale layout's row count is a multiple of the 128 block size. The main blocks and the partial tail block are now de-repeated separately.

signals.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signals.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash Download the tested FP4/FP8 GGUF from [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash). The benchmark used the immutable model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP4-FP8-native.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32232779018](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232779018)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32232778712](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232778712)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.15 (gfx942 / gfx950) stages to the ROCm Dockerfile
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.15 publishes no `rocm/pytorch` base image, so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing ROCm 7.0 / 7.2 stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.15 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The SDK pin is a nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release: the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0. This specific build is the one the gfx1250 7.15 image also pins, so all three arches share a single 7.15 SDK. Note for sequencing with #32754 (`[AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support`): that PR adds its own copy of a 7.15 pip-SDK stage, which could instead reuse the shared `rocm715-base` stage introduced here. Both PRs also introduce the same `rocm_legacy` / `rocm_rock` extras in `python/pyproject_other.toml`. Whichever lands second will need to be reconciled against the first. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm715-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.15 pip stack — `rocm[libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950]==7.15.0a20260712`, `torch==2.11.0`, `torchvision==0.26.0`, `triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6`, from the ROCm nightlies and devreleases indexes. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15`, which only set build flags (`BUILD_VLLM`, `BUILD_TRITON`, `BUILD_LLVM`, `BUILD_AITER_ALL`, `BUILD_MOONCAKE`, `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`). Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skip the apt install for `*rocm7_15*`, since libdrm ships with the pip SDK. - amdsmi: install it for `*rocm7_15*` (same branch as 7.2), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm 7.x images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: remove `libabsl-dev` before configuring, because nixl's meson wants an abseil providing `absl_log` and refuses its bundled subproject while Ubuntu 24.04's older `libabsl-dev` (20220623) is visible. Only `-dev` packages are removed; `libabsl20220623t64` stays so the Mooncake binaries built earlier keep the shared library they linked against. - Second commit: removing `libabsl-dev` also removes `libgrpc-dev` and `libgrpc++-dev`, which depend on it, so all three are reinstalled once nixl is built. The image's own MORI is built before this point and is fine, but the CI install script rebuilds MORI inside the image, and without `libgrpc++-dev` that rebuild configures without gRPC and silently drops symbols the Python side imports — `mori.umbp` then fails on `CacheRemoteAdmission` and `test_umbp_store` errors out. - The SGLang install now selects a `compressed-tensors` extra: `rocm_rock` for `*rocm7_15*`, `rocm_legacy` otherwise. ### `python/pyproject_other.toml` - Moved `compressed-tensors` out of `srt_hip` into two new mutually exclusive extras, `rocm_legacy = ["compressed-tensors==0.15.0"]` and `rocm_rock = ["compressed-tensors==0.16.0"]`. 0.15.0 requires `torch<2.11` and 0.16.0 requires `torch>=2.10`, so the correct pin depends on which torch the ROCm SDK generation ships rather than on the platform. Pinning the wrong one leaves pip trying to replace the image's ROCm torch with a PyPI build, which it cannot do, and the resolve then fails. Neither extra is pulled automatically — the Dockerfile and the CI install script append one. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Detect the ROCm version inside the CI container and append the matching `compressed-tensors` extra (`rocm_rock` for >= 7.15.0, else `rocm_legacy`) to `EXTRAS`. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. - Keep ROCm 7.15's own Triton (`INSTALL_AITER_TRITON=false` for HIP `7.15*`, matching `BUILD_TRITON=0` on the new stages). AITER's `install_triton.sh` resolves its wheel index from `dpkg -l rocm-core`, which does not exist for a pip-installed SDK, so it would fall back to the ROCm 7.2 index and drop a 7.2-built Triton into a 7.15 image. Verified in the built image that `dpkg-query` finds no `rocm-core` and that `torch.version.hip` reports `7.15.0`. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm7_15-nightly.yml` - Added `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15` to the build matrix, and replaced the single-arch `if` with a `case` mapping them to the `rocm7.15-mi30x` and `rocm7.15-mi35x` tags. - Build args: dropped `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` and `SGLANG_VERSION`, neither of which this Dockerfile consumes, and pass `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, which is what the SGLang install actually reads. ## Accuracy Tests All of the following was run on an MI300X host (gfx942). - `gfx942-rocm7_15` builds end to end (46GB image). - In-image smoke test: torch `2.11.0+rocm7.15.0a20260712`, `torch.version.hip` `7.15.0`, `gcnArchName` `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, a bf16 matmul on device returns finite values, and `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi` and `sglang` all import. - The real CI flow was run against the image: `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0, and `test/run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **6/8 passed**. That matches a ROCm 10 image baseline run on the same host on 2026-08-17, which was also 6/8. The two failures are `test_basic_sanity.py` and `test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`, both `huggingface_hub.errors.GatedRepoError: 401` on `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` because this host has no `HF_TOKEN` — identical to the baseline and unrelated to this change. - Known gap: the `gfx950-rocm7_15` stage has **not** been built or run. It shares `rocm715-base` with gfx942 and differs only in the AITER / sgl-kernel compile targets, but it is unverified. The host is MI300X, so gfx950 runtime tests were not possible here. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32132588829](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132588829)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32132588628](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132588628)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(openai): avoid duplicate routed expert in response when `return_meta_info = True`
signals.text: ## Summary Avoid duplicate routed-expert payloads in non-streaming chat completion responses. ## Symptom & Reproduction - **Symptom:** The base64 `routed_experts` payload appeared in both `choices[*].meta_info` and response-level `sglext` when both return flags were enabled. - **Reproduction:** Build and serialize a non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` response with both flags enabled. - **Expected:** Each choice contains its routed experts once in `meta_info`. - **Observed before the fix:** `sglext.routed_experts` repeated the first choice's routed experts. ## Root Cause 1. `_build_chat_response` projected first-choice `routed_experts` into `SglExt`. 2. `choice_meta_info` serialized the same routed payload for every choice. ## Fix When `return_meta_info` is enabled, omit only response-level `sglext.routed_experts` and keep each choice's `meta_info` authoritative for routed experts. Independently requested `cached_tokens_details` and `spec_tokens_details` remain in `sglext`; `return_meta_info=false`, streaming chat, and `/v1/completions` behavior remain unchanged. ## Verification - `env PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-dedupe-chat-meta-sglext/python python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_completions.py`: 130 passed and 55 subtests passed. - `ruff check --ignore E402 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: passed. - `ruff format --check python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: both files already formatted. - `git merge-tree --write-tree 1f87d8f512e09a6fe230da1e6d4ab228f6bbb91c 584a0880b29cbb5fa0db5a67e08ec8b8c8e0ffaf`: merged cleanly against `main@1f87d8f512e09a6fe230da1e6d4ab228f6bbb91c`. ## Review Focus - `_build_chat_response`: dual-flag requests must omit only response-level routed experts. - `SglExt`: cache/spec projections and their `n > 1` ordering must remain intact. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32319826089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32319826089)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32319825822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32319825822)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
