signals.title: [Kimi] Enable GB300 TP4 and GB200/GB300 TP16 SP collectives
signals.text: ## Summary Build on #35061 to enable tuned Kimi K3 sequence-parallel collectives for: - GB300 DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16, where attention TP is a derived node-local subgroup of full TP16. - GB200 and GB300 attention-TP16 / EP16 across four nodes in one NVL72 segment. ## Relationship to #35061 #35061 now provides the generic infrastructure this change previously carried locally: - topology/VMM-based multinode CustomAllReduceV2 admission; - SM100 world-size-16 communicator configuration; - dispatch priority over symmetric-memory PyNccl; and - capability coverage for world-size-16 MNNVL groups. Those overlapping server-policy, environment, and communicator changes have been removed from this PR. This PR still contributes K3-specific functionality not covered by #35061: 1. Derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-AR policy instead of unconditionally setting `use_custom_allreduce=False`. Capability selection still happens independently for each process group, and explicit `--disable-custom-all-reduce` remains respected. 2. K3 SP dispatch admits world size 16 on SM100 and SM103. 3. Correctness-checked, exact-device GB200 and GB300 `world=16,H=7168` RS/AG tuning tables are added. 4. Pull/direct K3 strategies no longer require push-workspace capacity. Larger RS buckets select measured pull candidates, so every push bucket fits the default 256 KiB world-16 workspace without forcing generic TP16 all-reduce thresholds. Ordinary TP16 all-reduce behavior is owned by #35061 and its generic SM100 heuristics; this PR does not override it. ## Changes ### Attention process group - Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy. - Leave final communicator selection to the topology and allocator capability checks from #35061. - Add focused CPU coverage for the derived-group option. ### K3 world-16 support - Enable K3 SP on SM100/SM103 when an exact-device table is available. - Add GB200 and GB300 `world=16,H=7168` reduce-scatter/all-gather tables. - Keep untuned attention-residual fusion entries on the existing `separate` path. - Check push workspace only in the push entry points; pull RS and direct AG use dedicated symmetric tensors. - Add exact-device table lookup and default-workspace-envelope tests. - Add one-time dispatch/fallback diagnostics. ## World-16 tuning and correctness Both devices were tuned on four 4-GPU nodes in one NVL72 segment over global-token buckets 16 through 16384. - Every measured push/pull/direct candidate was checked against NCCL before timing. - BF16 comparison used `rtol=2e-2`, `atol=5e-2` for rank-16 reduction-order differences. - Every selected custom bucket was faster than NCCL. - Attention-residual fusion was not part of the sweep and remains `separate`. - Production selection excludes push candidates above the generic world-16 256 KiB per-rank workspace. ### GB200 (SM100) Tuning run on four GB200 nodes in one NVL72 segment: | Operation | Tokens | NCCL | Selected custom | Strategy | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:| | Reduce-scatter | 512 | 98.892 us | 20.753 us | pull | 4.76x | | All-gather | 512 | 57.287 us | 16.904 us | direct | 3.39x | | Reduce-scatter | 8192 | 271.825 us | 172.092 us | pull | 1.58x | | All-gather | 8192 | 212.818 us | 171.805 us | direct | 1.24x | | Reduce-scatter | 16384 | 371.195 us | 330.806 us | pull | 1.12x | | All-gather | 16384 | 371.271 us | 334.210 us | direct | 1.11x | An independent graph-validation run captured and replayed every production-table RS+AG pair using the default CustomAllReduceV2 workspace. All 11 buckets matched NCCL; no forced workspace environment override was used. ### GB300 (SM103) | Operation | Tokens | NCCL | Selected custom | Strategy | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:| | Reduce-scatter | 512 | 105.371 us | 20.828 us | pull | 5.06x | | All-gather | 512 | 57.081 us | 16.824 us | direct | 3.39x | | Reduce-scatter | 8192 | 265.358 us | 171.723 us | pull | 1.55x | | All-gather | 8192 | 224.534 us | 171.736 us | direct | 1.31x | The original GB300 production table was checked under CUDA graph capture/replay at every bucket. The default-workspace table selects already-measured/correctness-checked pull candidates at 512 and 1024 tokens. ## Nsight dispatch validation ### GB300 DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16 Exactly 92 custom TP4 RS/AG pairs replaced NCCL per decode step: - NCCL RS over ten steps: 930 -> 10. - NCCL AG: 940 -> 20. - Custom RS: 0 -> 920. - Custom AG: 0 -> 920. - RS median: 16.014 -> 6.853 us (`-57.2%`). - AG median: 16.508 -> 7.179 us (`-56.5%`). - Full decode graph: 43.365 -> 40.259 ms (`-7.16%`). ### GB300 attention-TP16 / EP16 Over ten rank-0 decode steps: - 920 custom RS launches. - 920 custom direct AG launches. - Zero NCCL RS launches. - Eight SP collectives in the aligned four-layer window: 369.731 -> 137.872 us (`-62.71%`). ## Serving validation caveat The serving numbers below are matched stock/custom A/B validation using the pinned public SGLang container, public InferenceX commit, and fixed workload, not official cookbook results: - ISL 8192, OSL 1024, concurrency 512, 2048 requests. - Output throughput: 2872.99 -> 3029.28 tok/s (`+5.44%`). - Median TPOT: 117.64 -> 109.69 ms (`-6.76%`). - Median ITL: 55.33 -> 48.60 ms (`-12.16%`). ## Checks - Rebased onto `upstream/main` at `574274660f`. - Changed-file pre-commit suite passed, including clang-format. - Python syntax compilation and JSON parsing passed. - Push-workspace-envelope checks passed for both device tables. - Added CPU tests for derived attention-TP policy and exact GB200/GB300 dispatch lookup. - GB200: all candidates correctness-checked before timing; all 11 production buckets passed CUDA graph capture/replay against NCCL with the default workspace. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32252871443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32252871443)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32252871139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32252871139)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Warmup-calibrated auto residency promotion in performance-mode auto
signals.text: ## Motivation Under `--performance-mode auto`, component placement is decided **before load** from static per-model thresholds (`keep_resident_min_available_gb`). On GPUs with ample free VRAM this leaves components needlessly offloaded — e.g. a layerwise-offloaded text encoder on an 80–140 GB card pays a full H2D reload every request for VRAM nobody else uses — and fixing it by hand requires per-model, per-GPU flag tuning. This PR makes `auto` mode **calibrate residency from the server warmup it already runs**: measure real memory behavior, then promote implicitly offloaded components to GPU-resident when the default workload provably fits, before the server turns ready. Frozen after `/health`; no changes after startup. ## Modifications **Measurement** - Server warmup forwards record `peak_reserved` + a pre-forward baseline on **every rank** (previously output-rank only). - Video warmup (which caps frames to bound startup) adds one extra small-frame **calibration forward**; a two-point affine fit in workload units (`batch × W × H × frames`) separates constant (weights/buffers) from linear (activation) memory and extrapolates the default-workload peak with a 1.2× margin on the linear part only. Image warmup already runs the default shape, so it is a direct measurement, no extrapolation. - The loader now records real weight/buffer sizes alongside the GPU-load delta (`memory_usages` is ≈0 for exactly the offloaded components residency decisions are about). **Decision + promotion (between last warmup req and ready)** - All ranks all-gather `{estimated peak, budget, candidates}` and compute one deterministic plan: candidates are implicitly offloaded, known-size, native CUDA components only; ranked by per-request H2D savings (layerwise DiT counts default denoise steps); promoted greedily while `estimated_peak + promoted_bytes + reserve ≤ budget`, with `reserve = max(10 % budget, 4 GiB)` and `budget = free + torch-reserved` (min across ranks; excludes other processes on shared GPUs). - Promotion reuses existing primitives: component-offload → resident via `require_component_resident`, layerwise via `disable_offload()`; the strategy cache is invalidated explicitly. - A **re-warm forward** after promotion re-establishes compile/kernel caches and proves the promoted layout actually serves; any failure rolls every rank back to the original strategy (only a rollback failure aborts startup). - Excluded paths: explicit placement / `manual` mode, FSDP, diffusers backend, quantized DiT (ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4, SVDQuant), Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graph, realtime/disagg, `batching_max_size > 1`, any warmup failure. Kill switch: `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_AUTO_RESIDENCY=1`. **Fixes and unification along the way** - Warmup frame caps now run the pipeline's `adjust_num_frames`: LongLive2's server warmup was silently a no-op (17 capped frames → 5 latent frames, not divisible by `num_frames_per_block=8`, error swallowed by fail-open). - The post-request residency hint (`get_can_stay_resident_components`) now shares the promotion's candidate collection and H2D ranking — it previously read the ≈0 `memory_usages`, making the recommendation meaningless, and could recommend FSDP/custom-strategy components. - Logs narrate the adjustment: decision summary (`target/measured/estimated_peak/reserve/budget/promoted`), per-component `mode -> resident` with the **equivalent `--component-residency` flags** users can pin, and the kill switch. ``` Server warmup complete; adjusting component residency for the default workload (--performance-mode auto). Auto residency: target=1024x1024x1f steps=9, measured=[1024x1024x1f=17.4GiB], estimated_peak=17.4 GiB, reserve=13.3 GiB, budget=133.5 GiB, promoted=[text_encoder(layerwise-offload, 6.8 GiB)] Auto residency: adjusted text_encoder: layerwise-offload -> resident. Equivalent server args: --component-residency text_encoder=resident. ... ``` The optimization target is the model-default workload (default resolution/frames, batch 1). Larger or batched workloads should pin residency explicitly; the reserve bounds the blast radius. Static model deployment configs remain as the fallback when calibration is skipped. No numerics change for non-promoted paths; promoted components run identical code at a different placement. ## Test - `test/unit/test_auto_residency.py`: estimation (same-shape, single-point, two-point fit, negative-slope fallback, covering measurement), plan (skip propagation, reserve, cumulative fit, ranking), multi-rank worst-casing, promotion/rollback on stub modules, eligibility gates, LongLive2 frame alignment, applied-changes log, hint/promotion ranking consistency. - H200, Z-Image-Turbo serve: text encoder (layerwise, 6.8 GiB) promoted; warmup 9.15 s, decision <1 s, post-promotion re-warm 0.15 s; `/health` stays 503 until after promotion. - 2×H100, Wan2.1-T2V-14B: VAE promoted; text encoder correctly refused (estimated 65.6 GiB + 6.5 GiB TE > 70.2 GiB budget). Single-GPU 14B correctly refuses all promotions (72.6 vs 72.8 GiB). - Steady-state E2E improved on promoted image cases; no OOM observed in any validated case, including the refusal boundaries. ## Post-submission hardening (adversarial review pass) A 10-angle review over the diff surfaced and fixed, in `harden auto residency against review findings`: - **Measurement**: per-forward `empty_cache` + peak reset (allocator-pool carryover flattened the calibration slope → under-estimate → post-ready OOM); calibration forward moved after the main warmup so one-time allocations can only steepen the slope (safe direction); only `is_warmup` requests are measured (compile prewarm ran a different layout); failed warmups are recorded on every exit path; **`--enable-torch-compile` is excluded** — its warmup deliberately runs a stripped memory layout (layerwise DiT + evicted aux components) whose peaks are not serving peaks; unknown default workloads skip instead of trusting the capped peak. - **Distributed/rollback**: everything before the first all-gather is fenced into a skip report (a raise there parked peer ranks in the collective); error gathers filter on `is not None` with never-empty error strings; a failed in-apply rollback now surfaces as `rollback_failed` (aborts startup) instead of masquerading as rolled back; `disable_offload` re-arms hooks when `load_all_layers` fails; mechanism/mode mismatches from the `offload_during_compile` window are excluded and guarded; `_required_resident_components` tracks an owner feature so rollback cannot release loader hard-requirements. - **Startup contract**: apply-RPC failures honor the warmup fail-open contract; the post-rollback restore warmup keeps `--warmup-resolutions`' fail-closed contract; the calibration request shares `auto_residency_skip_reason` (the kill switch and excluded configs no longer pay for a measurement they never consume); warmup records are consumed exactly once (one-shot handler); re-warm passes no longer double-advance the warmup progress bar. - The warmup/target frame contract (cap → `adjust_num_frames` → `num_gpus` latent alignment) is now one shared helper extracted from `SamplingParams._adjust_visual_fields`, used by real requests, warmup requests, and the workload resolver. Known accepted conservatisms (documented in code): the budget check double-counts bytes of a component already partially on GPU at the measured peak (safe direction), and the reserve stays at `max(10 %, 4 GiB)`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32323020307](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32323020307)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32323020186](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32323020186)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU][CI] key persistent JIT kernel cache by image content ID
signals.text: ## Summary Nightly image rebuilds swap the runtime libs that cached JIT `.so` files link against (e.g. `libsycl.so.8` -> `libsycl.so.9`). Triton keys its cache on source hash only, so the previous gpu-mask-only cache path dlopens stale `.so`s from the prior image and every XPU CI job dies with `OSError: libsycl.so.N: cannot open shared object file`. - Include the resolved `docker image inspect` ID in the cache path so a new image gets a fresh cache dir. - Prune sibling caches for the same GPU but a different image ID via a rootful busybox helper (files are root-owned by the CI container, same pattern as the workspace-ownership reset). - Explicit `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR` overrides are still honored verbatim; if `docker image inspect` fails we fall back to the legacy unversioned path with a warning. - Over-cap reset switched from a runner-level `rm -rf` to the same busybox helper for the same root-owned reason. ## Test plan - [ ] XPU CI passes on an image with a torch/SYCL bump (verify no `libsycl.so.*: cannot open shared object` failures). - [ ] Sibling `kernel-cache-gpu*-<oldid>` dirs are pruned on first run after an image rebuild. - [ ] `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/foo` override still lands at `/tmp/foo` with no pruning. - [ ] Over-cap path (>`XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_MAX_MB`) resets cleanly. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32297133498](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32297133498)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32297133385](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32297133385)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][bugfix] Add moe_ep_size/moe_tp_size to the allreduce-fusion gate test stub
signals.text: ## Motivation `TestAiterAllreduceFusionGate` in `test/registered/ops/test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd.py` has been erroring on every AMD run since 2026-08-12. The hybrid EP+TP guard added in #30700 (commit `c7c03ec53`, 2026-08-11) reads two new fields at the very top of `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer`: ```python parallel = get_parallel() if parallel.moe_ep_size > 1 and parallel.moe_tp_size > 1: return False ``` The AMD gate test stubs `get_parallel()` with a `SimpleNamespace` that only carries `tp_size`, so every one of the 7 gate cases now raises: ``` AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'moe_ep_size' ``` Because the guard sits before every other branch, all 7 cases fail; CI's failfast only surfaces the first one (`test_dense_tp_fuses`). This is a test-stub gap only. The aiter fused all-reduce + RMSNorm kernel itself is fine: the three GPU subtests (`test_fused_ar_rms_benchmark`, `test_fused_ar_rms_multi_hidden_dim`, `test_fused_ar_rms_residual_accuracy`) pass. Scheduled ROCm 7.2 runs on `main`, shard 3 — the guard landed at 2026-08-11T23:46Z: | run date | shard 3 | | --- | --- | | 08-09, 08-10, 08-11 17:46 | success | | 08-12 12:21 onward (every run) | failure | ## Modifications Add `moe_ep_size=1` and `moe_tp_size=1` to the `get_parallel()` stub. Both being 1 means no MoE EP and no MoE TP, so the hybrid EP+TP guard stays inactive and the aiter branch is what decides — which is what all 7 existing cases are written to exercise. No existing assertion changes meaning. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — test-only change, no kernel or model forward code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149134311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149134025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134025)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
signals.text: ## Problem Partition 0 of `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x-rocm720` (`test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py`) has failed on every scheduled run since 2026-08-16 12:08 UTC. Example: [job 95552260420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32083881457/job/95552260420). The empty-batch guard added in #34474 reads `hidden_states.shape[0]` immediately after `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs()`. When the fused AR+quant path is active that call returns a tuple — `(bf16, fp8, scale)` in the GatedDeltaNet layer, `(fp8, scale)` in the plain attention layer — so the guard raises during decode CUDA-graph capture and the server dies at startup: ``` File "python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 806, in forward if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` The scheduler child dying takes the process tree with it, which the test surfaces as the less obvious `Server process exited with code -9`. Only the `fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant` variant is affected; the `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control variant stays on the tensor path. ## Fix Read the row count off the tuple's first element, using the same inline form `glm4_moe.py` already uses for this situation. Applied at both guard sites. This is behavior-preserving. `prepare_attn()` returns early on `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0` *before* the fusion branch, so a tuple can only appear when the count is already `> 0`; the tuple path therefore behaves exactly as it did before #34474, while the tensor path keeps the empty-batch guard. Both sites are patched because `keep_bf16=False` still yields a tuple, just the 2-element form. `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.forward_prepare_native()` / `.forward_prepare_fused_gate()` both open with `isinstance(hidden_states, tuple)`, and `_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear()` has a dedicated `len(...) == 2` branch that only this path produces. Supersedes #35250, which diagnosed the same bug but patched the GatedDeltaNet site only. ## Verification Reproduced and fixed end-to-end on an 8x MI350X node following the CI flow exactly — same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`), same `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, same `run_suite.py` invocation. Before, at the failing scheduled-run SHA `91144797c`: the `AttributeError` above, byte-for-byte the CI signature. After: | Variant | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | Threshold | Status | | ------- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------- | ------ | | fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant | 0,1,2,3 | 0.951 | 0.009 | 53.66 | 4067.56 | 0.94 | PASS | | disable-fused-ar-quant-opt-out | 4,5,6,7 | 0.940 | 0.009 | 53.85 | 4010.65 | 0.94 | PASS | On CI, partition 0 is green on both [run 32203488998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203488998) and [run 32227220289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227220289), with accuracy matching the last pre-regression baseline ([run 31916881653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653): 0.949 / 0.943). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No new test: `test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py` already covers this path and is the test that was red. No user-facing behavior change, and no before-number to benchmark since the server did not start.

signals.title: [VLM] Route every multimodal processor through the worker pool's call site
signals.text: ## Motivation `process_and_combine_mm_data` is the function the multimodal processor worker pool actually runs (`MultimodalProcessorExecutor.run(self.process_and_combine_mm_data, ...)`). **33 of the 37 call sites called it directly**, so those models can never use the pool: with `--mm-processor-worker-num > 1` they build the thread pool and its `deepcopy`'d processor clones at startup and then route every request straight past them. The failure is silent — the model just serves at one-worker speed. That is why PaddleOCR-VL preprocessed pages single-threaded from the day it was added: opting it in (#35318) moved 32-way concurrent throughput from 6.7 to 10.9 req/s on an H200, purely by letting an 87 ms/page preprocess overlap. Only `qwen_vl`, `kimi_k25`, `kimi_k3` and `muse_glimmer` were on the right call site. ## Modifications Mechanically rewrite the 33 sync call sites to `await self.process_and_combine_mm_data_async(...)`, and add a test that pins the invariant. **This is an identity transform, not a behavior change:** - `process_and_combine_mm_data_async` delegates straight to the sync function when `self.mm_processor_executor is None`, which is the case for every model that has not opted into concurrency. - Awaiting a coroutine that never itself suspends does not yield to the event loop, so request interleaving is bit-for-bit unchanged. Only `await loop.run_in_executor(...)` — reached solely when an executor exists — introduces a suspension point. So nothing about scheduling moves until a model sets `supports_mm_processor_concurrency`. What this PR buys is that opting a model in becomes a three-line change instead of a call-site migration plus an audit. ## Verification The migration was generated and checked by AST, not by hand: - 33 sync call sites before, **0** after; 37 async call sites after. - Every call site sits inside an `async def`, before and after — so each edit is exactly `await` + `_async`. - Each of the 33 changed lines differs from its original **only** by that rename (0 deviations, checked mechanically against the diff). - Every touched file compiles; `isort` / `black` / `ruff` clean. `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py` re-runs the same scan as a CPU test, so a processor added later cannot quietly opt out of the pool again. It reports 37 call sites on this branch and would have reported 33 offenders before it. ## Notes for reviewers Turning concurrency *on* for a given model is deliberately **not** part of this PR. That decision is per-model and needs measurement, for two reasons: - The executor is a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, so a model only benefits if its preprocessing releases the GIL (PIL / numpy / torch C code does; pure-Python preprocessing would not). - More workers spread request arrivals, which fragments GPU prefill batches — the tradeoff `qwen_vl` documents when it picks 2 workers, and which showed up in measurement as `--mm-processor-worker-num 8` being slower than 4 on PaddleOCR-VL. `muse_glimmer` is already on the async call site but has no capability flag, so it is the one existing model that could opt in for free once measured. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test (`test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py`) - [x] Verify the change is an identity transform rather than benchmarking it (there is nothing to benchmark: behavior is unchanged until a model opts in) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32305751651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32305751651)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32305751526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32305751526)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix fused DeepSeek top-k capability fallback
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently selects FlashInfer's `fused_topk_deepseek` based on shape constraints without checking whether the active GPU architecture is supported by that kernel. On A10G (SM86), FlashInfer raises `BackendSupportedError` during DeepSeek grouped top-k routing instead of allowing SGLang to use its existing fallback. This was observed in the Dynamo nightly SGLang data-parallel test: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/32114902544/job/95672470424 ## Modifications - Read FlashInfer's `is_compute_capability_supported` metadata before selecting `fused_topk_deepseek`. - Preserve compatibility with FlashInfer versions that do not expose capability metadata. ## Accuracy Tests The numerical implementation is unchanged. Unsupported devices now use the existing SGLang fallback instead of entering a kernel that raises before producing output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. Supported devices retain the fused path; the added check is one device-capability lookup during top-k dispatch. ## Validation - `python3 -m compileall -q python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_topk_deepseek.py` - GPU pytest not run locally because the available environment does not include PyTorch/CUDA. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project guidance. - [x] Keep the change limited to the capability-aware dispatch guard; no new unit test is needed. - [x] No documentation update is needed for this internal dispatch fix. - [x] Accuracy and performance impact are described above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32317601183](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317601183)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32317600849](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317600849)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [VLM] Default to two multimodal preprocessing workers
signals.text: Stacked on #35342 (which routes every processor through the worker pool's call site). Review that one first; this PR is the one line that actually turns the pool on. ## Motivation Preprocessing an image costs real CPU time on the tokenizer's event loop, so with a single worker a model's request throughput is capped at `1 / preprocess_time` no matter how much GPU is idle. That cap is why PaddleOCR-VL saturated at 6.7 req/s on an H200 with GPU headroom to spare — and only four processors in tree had opted out of it. ## The benefit generalizes, because the mechanism does Image preprocessing is numpy / torch / PIL underneath, so it releases the GIL. Wall-clock speedup of 4 threads over 1 on the same work, 1080p input, `torch.set_num_threads(1)` so intraop parallelism cannot be mistaken for thread scaling: | image processor | 1 thread | 4 threads | speedup | `deepcopy` | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2VL (fast / slow) | 24.3 / 24.1 ms | 7.1 / 7.0 ms | 3.41x / 3.45x | ok | | Idefics3 | 46.1 ms | 12.7 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Pixtral | 19.0 ms | 5.2 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Llama4 | 27.0 ms | 7.7 ms | 3.52x | ok | | GLM4V | 31.8 ms | 9.0 ms | 3.51x | ok | | PaddleOCR-VL | 28.4 ms | 8.7 ms | 3.27x | ok | | CLIP | 9.1 ms | 2.8 ms | 3.28x | ok | | Gemma3 | 5.7 ms | 1.9 ms | 2.94x | ok | | SigLIP | 5.5 ms | 2.1 ms | 2.69x | ok | | *pure-Python control* | *81.0 ms* | *80.5 ms* | *1.01x* | — | The control validates the probe. `copy.deepcopy` succeeded on all nine, and the executor already falls back to synchronous processing with a warning if cloning ever fails. ## Two workers, and not more Past two, spreading request arrivals fragments the GPU prefill batches faster than the extra overlap pays for itself — the tradeoff `qwen_vl`'s processor already documents. Swept at 32-way concurrency on an H200: | workload | 1 worker | 2 workers | 4 workers | |---|---|---|---| | PaddleOCR-VL 1080p pages, 128-token outputs | 6.72 | **9.55** | 8.92 req/s | | PaddleOCR-VL 360p pages, 512-token outputs | 22.38 | **25.20** | 25.06 req/s | | Qwen2.5-VL 360p images, 512-token outputs | 12.54 | **12.60** | 12.25 req/s | The middle row is the shape that was supposed to break this: light preprocessing, where overlap has little to win, and long outputs, where batch fragmentation has the most to cost. Two workers gained 13% there instead of regressing. Four workers is where the documented regression actually appears (bottom row, −2.3%). Greedy output is unaffected: two workers against one is byte-identical across five page geometries × two task prompts on PaddleOCR-VL. ## Limitation reviewers should weigh All of this is **Hopper**. The regression `qwen_vl` documents was observed on Blackwell, and no B200 was available to me (GB300 is arm64). A Blackwell check on the light-preprocessing / long-output shape would be worth having before this rides a release — that is the one measurement that could still overturn the default. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test pinning the default (`test_default_worker_count_stays_at_the_measured_optimum`), so raising it requires a fresh sweep - [x] Benchmark on real hardware, including the shape most likely to regress - [x] Verify greedy output is unchanged 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32224837223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837223)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32224837024](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837024)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] ComfyUI: add a MiniMax-H3 node and a generic extra-fields passthrough
signals.text: ## Summary The ComfyUI plugin's executors cover flux / qwen_image / zimage — all image models — so there was no route to MiniMax-H3 from ComfyUI. H3 does not fit the executor route. It denoises a packed video+audio sequence in one pass and routes conditioning by task (`t2va` / `fl2va` / `ref2va`), while ComfyUI's KSampler drives a single latent tensor and has no audio branch. Rebuilding that inside ComfyUI would duplicate the visual/audio/reference conditioning stages the server already runs, so this wires H3 through the server route instead. Two changes: - **`generate_video` gains `extra_fields`.** The video request schema already accepts unknown fields, so the client only needed a way to reach a model's own request surface. `extra_fields` is merged last, so a model-specific field wins over a generic default of the same name. No further change to this client is needed for the next model that adds request fields. - **`SGLDiffusionGenerateH3`** builds H3's `task` / `conditions` / `target` shape from ComfyUI-native inputs. Keyframes carry a `frame_index`; references keep request order because the prompt addresses them positionally per modality; local paths become `file://` URIs while remote URLs pass through unchanged. Output dimensions are read from the response, because H3 aligns the canvas server-side and `short_edge` alone cannot reconstruct it. ## Test plan - [x] 9 new tests drive the real node through the real client and mock only HTTP, so a change on either side of the payload contract fails. They cover the three task shapes, keyframe frame-index mapping, modality ordering for prompt tags, remote-URL passthrough, the server-resolved canvas, the task/conditioning validation errors, and `extra_fields` precedence. - [x] Run on a plain checkout and on an H200 box: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/test/test_h3_request.py --import-mode=importlib` **Not covered:** an end-to-end run against a live H3 server. The tests pin the request shape against the documented contract and the shape used by the existing H3 CI case, but nothing here has generated a video through ComfyUI yet. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32221182305](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32221182305)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32221181823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32221181823)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Deferred decode-side KV release for the NIXL backend
signals.text: ## Motivation #35049 added env-gated **deferred decode-side KV release** — on abort, hold an in-flight request's KV pages/req-slot until the prefill confirms its transfer drained (or a timeout fires), so a still-landing write can't corrupt the next request that reuses those pages. It wired the prefill ack for **mooncake only**. Two reasons NIXL needs it: 1. **There is a latent footgun today.** The decode side is backend-agnostic, so enabling `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` on a NIXL deployment *already* holds pages (`NixlKVManager(CommonKVManager)`, `NixlKVReceiver(CommonKVReceiver)` inherit the abort/tracker machinery). But NIXL never sends `ABORT_ACK` and had no path to receive one, so `is_abort_release_safe` is never satisfied and **every abort waits out the full timeout** — safe (holding is the safe direction), but fully degraded, pinning KV and back-pressuring new requests under abort load. 2. **The hazard is arguably worse than mooncake's.** NIXL transfers are inherently asynchronous — `agent.transfer(handle)` posts and returns, and the worker polls `check_xfer_state(handle)` for `DONE` — so there is always a real in-flight window. Mooncake's *default* path is the synchronous `batch_transfer_sync`. `nixl/conn.py::_handle_abort_notification` even carried a `TODO` for exactly this mechanism. ## Modifications **Shared (`common/conn.py`)** — one ack implementation for both backends: - Hoist `_prefill_unique_rank`, `_send_abort_ack`, `_maybe_ack_drained_abort` and the `_deferred_ack_targets` map from `MooncakeKVManager` to `CommonKVManager`; add `register_deferred_ack_target()` documenting the mark-`Failed`-first ordering. Mooncake behavior is unchanged (now inherited). `CommonKVSender.clear()` already drops held targets, so NIXL gets that cleanup for free. **NIXL (`nixl/conn.py`)**: - `_handle_abort_notification`: parse the return address the decode already sends (`_send_abort_notification` has always included ip/port — NIXL just ignored it), register the held ack **after** the status flip for an active room, and ack a concluded room immediately. It never acks an active room from the bootstrap thread: a chunk dequeued but not yet counted would race the ack. - `transfer_worker`: ack at the skip site (nothing was written for the aborted room) and after the existing `while handles: check_xfer_state == DONE` barrier (writes have landed). NIXL's drain point is actually *cleaner* than mooncake's — no sibling-future hazard. Deliberately **no** ack on the exception path: that barrier bails on the first `ERR`, so sibling handles may still be writing; the room falls back to the decode timeout. **Closing two ack-stranding windows (both backends — both were present in #35049):** Previously the ack was driven only by worker visits, so two sequences left a registered target that nobody ever acked, falling back to the decode timeout (safe, but losing the fast path exactly when you want it): 1. the owning worker could pass its `Failed` skip point *between* the status flip and the target registration (ack attempt a no-op, then the target lands and strands); 2. a room whose enqueued chunks had all drained with no further chunk coming (`is_last_chunk` unseen) is never revisited by the worker at all. The root cause was that `outstanding == 0` was not a quiescence predicate: chunks were counted *after* the `Failed` status check, so a chunk could be dequeued and about to write while the counter still read 0 — which is why the ack could not safely be sent from the bootstrap thread. Now chunks are **counted at dequeue, before the status check**, so a chunk either writes (counted) or skips (uncounted), never both, and `Failed and outstanding == 0` genuinely means nothing can still write. With that predicate the abort path attempts the ack once after registering, covering both windows. Counting slightly earlier is strictly more conservative for the existing `poll()` Success hold and teardown condition (increments/decrements still pair). - Decode: generalize the staging-only ZMQ thread into a decode **listener** that also handles `ABORT_ACK`, started when staging *or* deferred release is enabled. A dedicated thread ingests acks even while the decode is idle — NIXL notifs would **not**, since the decode agent runs with `num_threads=0` and only drains notifs inside a live receiver's `poll()`, which early-returns once `conclude_state` is set on abort. Off by default; when disabled, both backends behave exactly as before. ## Tests New `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`: ack held until outstanding drains, fires at most once, unregistered-room no-op, rank formula matches the Success-sync formula, abort-notification registration (active / concluded / feature-off / legacy 2-frame abort / non-ABORT passthrough), and per-rank ack aggregation. Existing NIXL fixtures that build a manager via `object.__new__` now set `enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = False` (they cover the legacy no-ack behavior). Verified in the `lmsysorg/sglang` container on a CPU VM: ``` test_nixl_deferred_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_nixl_backend_basic Ran 43 tests OK test_deferred_decode_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_decode_queue_cleanup Ran 6 tests OK test_nixl_sender_failure_cleanup Ran 1 test OK test_disaggregation_wire Ran 23 tests OK test_kv_transfer_replica_metric Ran 3 tests OK ``` (The mooncake-side suites are included deliberately: the dequeue-counting change touches shared worker logic.) ## Not covered / follow-ups - **No live NIXL PD run.** The state machine and wiring are unit-tested; an end-to-end abort-mid-transfer run on a real NIXL deployment (and the fast-ack-vs-timeout ratio) is not yet measured. Same gap as #35049's, which validated on mooncake. - Multi-node / TP>1 dummy-rank fan-out unvalidated (the `len(bootstrap_infos)` denominator is dummy-proof by construction, but untested where the real multi-queue concurrency lives). - The mamba/state path (`maybe_send_extra`) is not routed through drain-aware waiting on either backend — carried over from #35049. ## Checklist - [x] Format with pre-commit (black/isort) - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A — abort-path correctness; no kernel/throughput impact, no-op when disabled) - [x] Code style Related: #35049, #32564, #27372 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32218714755](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32218714755)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32218714578](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32218714578)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix]: exclude SM120 from attn-res TMA dispatch
signals.text: # [Kimi-K3] Exclude SM120 from the attention-residual TMA path ## Summary The Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatcher previously enabled the TMA fast path for every CUDA architecture with a compute-capability major version greater than or equal to 10. This incorrectly selected the SM100-oriented TMA kernel on SM120 GPUs such as the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, where the required `tcgen05`/TMEM path is not supported. This PR changes the capability gate to: ```python major >= 10 and major != 12 ``` SM12x devices now use the existing Triton fallback. The fast path remains available on SM10x, SM11x, and later non-SM12x architectures. ## Scope This is a standalone Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatch fix. ## Validation - Verified that the modified Python module passes `py_compile`. - Verified that the PR changes only `python/sglang/srt/layers/attn_residual.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32322724028](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322724028)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32322723630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322723630)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Fall back to cpu_tensor when host-pool retraction cannot fit
signals.text: ## Motivation `resolve_decode_retraction_backup`, added in #34801, picks the PD decode retraction backend on capability alone — mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, priority preemption, pool class. Whether the host pool fits never comes up, and it has to: `host_pool` mirrors the device KV pool 1:1 on every scheduler, while the only capacity check sits downstream in `pool_host/base.py`, well past the point of no return. On a GB300 tray that check can never pass. Four Blackwell Ultra GPUs hold 1110 GiB of HBM against 955 GiB of Grace LPDDR5X, so a KV pool sized to fill HBM cannot be mirrored into host RAM — a hybrid-SWA model at TP4 wants 1059.80 GB against ~854 GB free: ``` ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 117.76 GB but only have 98.90 GB free. ``` No workload or freed page cache gets there, and any node whose HBM rivals its DRAM lands the same way. An inferred default that cannot be satisfied should step aside; one asked for by name should still fail loudly. ## Modifications The inferred choice degrades to `cpu_tensor` with a warning naming both figures. Explicit `host_pool` still hard-fails, since the gate sits inside the `backend is None` branch. The budget reads `available` — what `HostKVCache.__init__` itself gates on. `_agree_across_ranks` all-reduces MIN over the world CPU group, shaped after `sync_fixed_hicache_size`, so no rank diverges. Reaching it needs a rank-uniform predicate, which splits the eligibility test: mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, and priority preemption come from the config bags and gate the estimate, while `supports_host_pool` is per-rank and only picks the backend. Prefill, embedding, and non-PD servers skip the estimate entirely. Three sizing fixes: - `_local_scheduler_count` mirrors the launcher's `pp_size_per_node * tp_size_per_node` plus the classic-DP replica factor. `tp_size // nnodes` undercounts past `pp_size > 1` and can reach zero. Reads `configured_tp_size()` / `configured_pp_size()`, which don't assert before process-group init. - MTP/EAGLE draft pools count, since the mirror packs them into its own `layer_num`. - `_kv_pool_bytes` takes both `get_kv_size_bytes` shapes. It tests for the `(k, v)` pair rather than the scalar: MLA returns `numpy.int64`, which `isinstance(size, int)` misses. `hicache_ratio` keys off the pre-fallback verdict, so the gate cannot enlarge the pool it just rejected. Deliberately not keyed off "a host pool gets built anyway", which would cut 2.0 to 1.0 for hierarchical-cache users on the decode-radix-cache path. The gate and the normalisation cover different cases — reverting the normalisation alone on 4×GB300: | Configuration | Normalisation | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | non-PD MLA | reverted | starts — the gate excludes it | | non-PD MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | | PD decode MLA | reverted | crashes in `_kv_pool_bytes` | | PD decode MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | The estimate is a lower bound; the per-rank gate stays authoritative. Page round-up and SIDECAR draft pools are unmodelled, because reproducing host-pool sizing here would go stale quietly. That belongs in a shared sizing helper, along with the scalar/tuple split and the unified pools — they return `(0, 0)` while subclassing MHA/SWA, so they would leave the gate inert rather than loud. Unreachable today: `--enable-unified-memory` with PD is MLA hybrid-Mamba only. ## Accuracy Tests Outputs are untouched — this resolves startup configuration, not the retraction path. `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_capacity.py` is new and CPU-registered, covering the PP and DP rank arithmetic, fits and doesn't-fit, the reserve, draft-pool accounting, both accessor shapes, the scope, and the ratio invariant driven through the resolver itself. Each fix was mutation-checked by reverting it: | Reverted | Result | | --- | --- | | ratio keyed off the post-fallback backend | 1 failure, `AssertionError: 2.0 != 1.0` | | reduction re-gated on the per-rank predicate | 2 failures, `_agree_across_ranks` called 0 times | | shape normalisation | 3 failures | | config-uniform gate | 2 failures | 166 tests pass across that file, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, and `test_server_args.py`; 20/20 under the `unittest` runner; pre-commit clean. On 4×GB300, a hybrid-SWA PD decode server falls back with identical figures on all four ranks and no deadlock, an MLA server starts clean both non-PD and PD decode, and a plain non-PD server never reaches the estimate. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The gate runs once per scheduler at startup, only for a config-eligible decode server, and the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No flag, default, or documented behaviour moves — an inferred default that used to crash now degrades with a warning. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32201835433](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201835433)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32201835245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201835245)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(cake_gemm): add Cake batch DeepGEMM FP8 backend
signals.text: ## Real-weight correctness and E2E performance Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324), all 163 real FP8 safetensors shards. Both modes ran sequentially on the same 4x NVIDIA GB300 node with TP4/EP4 and identical settings. `native` is SGLang's integration-free packed-scale DeepGEMM path; `cake` enables this PR through FlashInfer's public batch DeepGEMM API. | Correctness | Native | Cake | Comparison | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Greedy prompts | 3 | 3 | same prompts | | Output tokens | 48 | 48 | **48/48 token IDs exact** | | Finish reasons | 3 | 3 | **3/3 exact** | | Non-finite output logprobs | 0 | 0 | **pass** | | Maximum output-token logprob absolute difference | — | — | **0.0** | | Round: 64 requests, input 16, output 128, concurrency 8 | Native output tok/s | Cake output tok/s | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0 | 42.407477 | 43.249187 | **1.019849x** | | 1 | 42.596189 | 43.690664 | **1.025694x** | | 2 | 43.402560 | 43.461728 | **1.001363x** | | Three-round median | Native | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Duration | 192.317675 s | 188.487675 s | **1.020320x** | | Request throughput | 0.332783 req/s | 0.339545 req/s | **1.020320x** | | Output throughput | 42.596189 tok/s | 43.461728 tok/s | **1.020320x** | | Total throughput | 47.920712 tok/s | 48.894444 tok/s | **1.020320x** | | Mean E2E latency | 24,036.562 ms | 23,558.187 ms | **1.020306x** | | Median E2E latency | 24,030.345 ms | 23,506.908 ms | **1.022267x** | | Mean TTFT | 484.798 ms | 479.128 ms | **1.011834x** | | Median TTFT | 507.402 ms | 508.436 ms | **0.997966x** | | Mean TPOT | 185.447 ms | 181.402 ms | **1.022301x** | | Median TPOT | 185.522 ms | 181.394 ms | **1.022760x** | | Output-throughput CV | 1.008% | 0.415% | — | Model load, server startup, kernel JIT, and 16 warmup requests are outside the measured request window. The old `1.85x` result was invalid: its reference arm used a slower wrapper route and produced only about `21.7 tok/s`. The corrected no-integration native packed-scale baseline produces `42.5962 tok/s` at the median. The limited model-level gain is expected from GPU attribution. In a profiled real-serving step, the two target native DeepGEMM kernels used `467.127 ms`, versus `415.951 ms` for Cake (`1.12303x`), but represented only `1.9853%` of native GPU kernel time. Amdahl's law predicts `1.00218x` for that isolated share and an infinite-kernel-speedup ceiling of `1.02025x`; the measured `1.02032x` E2E point estimate is therefore at the scale of the workload's maximum leverage and round-to-round variation, not a 1.85x model acceleration. ## Real-weight GSM8K capability The integration-free native route and Cake route were run sequentially on the same 4x GB300 node against all 1,319 questions from the public GSM8K test split. Both used the same real `DeepSeek-V3-0324` checkpoint, five-shot prompts, greedy decoding (`temperature=0`, `top_p=1`), a 512-token cap, and client parallelism 200. Model load, server startup, JIT, and the 8-question warmup are excluded from the reported evaluation latency. | Capability metric | Native packed DeepGEMM | Cake | Comparison | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Last-number exact-match accuracy | 1240/1319 (**94.0106%**) | 1239/1319 (**93.9348%**) | **-1 question / -0.0758 pp** | | Invalid answers | 0 | 0 | **equal** | | Correctness classification agreement | — | — | **1308/1319 (99.1660%)** | | Parsed final-answer agreement | — | — | **1307/1319 (99.0902%)** | | Complete generated-text agreement | — | — | **915/1319 (69.3707%)** | | Native-only correct / Cake-only correct | 6 | 5 | net **-1** for Cake | | Full GSM8K evaluation | Native packed DeepGEMM | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Benchmark latency | 947.236 s | 936.829 s | **1.011109x** | | Output throughput | 141.409 tok/s | 142.630 tok/s | **1.008635x** | | Full client wall time | 967.225 s | 957.133 s | **1.010544x** | The one-question accuracy delta is accompanied by bidirectional answer changes (6 native-only correct, 5 Cake-only correct), zero invalid outputs, and 99.17% agreement on per-question correctness. Complete generated text is not expected to be byte-identical across the two numerical routes, so the capability comparison uses the benchmark's last-number exact-match metric rather than token identity. ## Reproduction ```bash MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V3-0324 CORPUS_PATH=/path/to/fixed-128-row-corpus.json COMMON_SERVER_ARGS=( --trust-remote-code --tp 4 --ep 4 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --disable-shared-experts-fusion --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --disable-flashinfer-autotune --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 256 --context-length 2048 --max-running-requests 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --random-seed 42 --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":32}' ) # Run the modes sequentially on the same 4-GPU node. SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1 \ SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_STANDARD_LAYOUT=masked \ SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_FP8_BACKEND=native \ sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" --port 30000 "${COMMON_SERVER_ARGS[@]}" SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1 \ SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_STANDARD_LAYOUT=masked \ SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_FP8_BACKEND=cake \ sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" --port 32000 "${COMMON_SERVER_ARGS[@]}" # Flush the cache, run 16 warmup requests, flush again, then run this command # three times per mode. Use port 30000 for native and 32000 for Cake. PORT=30000 python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}" \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path "$CORPUS_PATH" \ --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \ --num-prompts 64 \ --random-input-len 16 \ --random-output-len 128 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 8 \ --seed 42 \ --disable-tqdm ``` For the full capability run, start each mode with `--max-running-requests 200`, then run: ```bash MODE=native # repeat with MODE=cake and a separately started server PORT=30000 # use the port assigned to MODE python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port "$PORT" \ --data-path /path/to/gsm8k-test.jsonl \ --num-shots 5 \ --num-questions 1319 \ --max-new-tokens 512 \ --temperature 0.0 \ --top-p 1.0 \ --parallel 200 \ --result-file "results/${MODE}.jsonl" \ --raw-result-file "results/${MODE}-raw.jsonl" ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32247257012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32247257012)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32247256883](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32247256883)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is 135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets the model run on a consumer GPU, so the remaining barriers are the checkpoint download, host memory, and bytes streamed per layer. This adds a pre-quantized GGUF transformer path. The validated Q4_K_M DiT is 17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB. It complements online `kitchen_int8`: GGUF avoids first downloading and pinning the complete BF16 DiT, while `kitchen_int8` remains the faster compute-oriented path. ## Interface `--model-path` continues to provide the pipeline components and `--transformer-weights-path` selects the GGUF DiT. The loader accepts a local file, `owner/repo/path/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` when that suffix matches exactly one file. Repositories containing multiple variants require the full file path. ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --transformer-weights-path \ leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/minimax_h3_fl2va-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --port 30010 ``` `--quantization gguf` is intentionally rejected: quantization is encoded in the checkpoint and the file path is the selector. ## Implementation - Reuses SRT's GGUF file detection, Hub resolver, quantization type sets, and CUDA dequantization helper. Diffusion no longer carries duplicate download resolution, GGML support tables, or dequantization shape logic. - Keeps a small diffusion-specific header reader because model construction needs each tensor's exact logical and packed shape before parameters exist. Packed tensors stay mmap-backed until the generic loader copies their TP shard, which avoids cloning the complete 17.5 GiB checkpoint during load. - Uses dequantization followed by native GEMM for DiT linears. SRT's fused MMVQ/MMQ path is optimized for low-token LLM inference and regresses normal diffusion sequence lengths. - Supports block-aligned tensor parallel row/column/merged linear slicing. Incompatible TP degrees fail during model construction. - Supports both the original MiniMax-H3 timestep MLP and pruned community checkpoints containing an unquantized `adaln_t_table` curve. - Fails before download for conflicting or unsupported configurations: non-CUDA, FSDP for the GGUF component, LoRA, another `--quantization`, SVDQuant, and the separate MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache/online paths. - Keeps `quality=high` fail-closed when replacement transformer weights are supplied. F32/F16/BF16 tensors use the ordinary linear path. Quantized tensors must be 2D `.weight` matrices and have valid GGML block alignment; malformed, corrupt, opposite-endian, or unsupported files fail at load. ## Validation ### Automated - Changed-files pre-commit: passed. - Focused remote NVIDIA suite: **163 passed, 2 subtests passed**. - Coverage includes header corruption/endianness/BF16 handling, Hub resolution and ambiguity, type selection, CPU-offload loading, pre-download guards, quality admission, pruned curve interpolation, and TP row/column/merged slicing. ### Kernel selection On H200 with the real H3 Q4_K QKV matrix `(21504, 5376)`, fused MMVQ is useful only at one or two tokens. At 256 and 2048 tokens, SRT MMQ took 2.60 ms and 20.61 ms versus 0.37 ms and 0.91 ms for dequantize + GEMM. The final diffusion adapter therefore keeps the native-GEMM path. ### End to end 1x H200, FL2VA Q4_K_M, layerwise-offloaded DiT/text encoder, fixed seed, 1344x768, 107 frames, 2 inference steps: | Revision | Warmup | Generation | Peak GPU | Output | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Original PR dense-dequant path | 12.67 s | 10.11 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | | Refactored SRT-reuse path | 12.64 s | 10.13 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | The two MP4 files are byte-identical (same SHA-256; PSNR infinite, SSIM 1.0). The refactored loader constructed the 17.49 GiB DiT in about 1 second versus about 19 seconds in the original PR run because packed values are no longer cloned wholesale during iteration. The pruned `unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF` FL2VA Q4_K checkpoint also completed server warmup and a real 1344x768, 107-frame video + AAC request on H200; its loaded DiT size was 10.72 GiB. The original RTX 5090 measurements remain valid: 39.0 s denoise and 26.3 GiB peak with `dit,text_encoder` offload; adding VAE offload lowered peak to 19.6 GiB and increased VAE decode from 9.5 s to 57.2 s. Not yet validated end to end: `ref2va`, quantization types other than the listed Q4 variants, and multi-GPU GGUF. TP packed slicing is unit-tested, but a requested 2x H100 validation box remained in infrastructure provisioning and is not reported as a successful run. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update CLI, quantization, compatibility, and MiniMax-H3 documentation. - [x] Run real checkpoint and end-to-end NVIDIA validation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32256244219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256244219)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32256243954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256243954)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] Support wider rows in mega_moe_pre_dispatch
signals.text: ## Motivation `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` assigns one thread to each 8-element input chunk, so a single CUDA block can only cover hidden dimensions up to 8192. Wider shapes are rejected before launch. ## Modifications - Cap the block size at the CUDA 1024-thread limit and process wider rows in strided chunks. - Recompute quantization-group indices for each chunk while preserving the UE8M0 scale layout. - Keep a separate single-chunk kernel specialization so existing shapes retain the same instruction path. - Reject wide shapes whose tail would split a warp-level reduction. ## Accuracy Tests - Verified bitwise FP8 output and UE8M0 scale bytes against a reference implementation for hidden dimensions 3584, 5632, 8192, 12288, and 16384. - Verified exact top-k copies and idle-slot padding. - Verified that hidden dimension 8320 fails with the expected full-warp alignment error. - JIT-compiled the ported CUDA header successfully. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - The single-chunk specialization produces the same SASS instruction stream as the previous kernel. - CUDA-event microbenchmarks showed no measurable regression for shapes that already fit in one chunk. ## Original commits - `d7c54c96f5` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). The relevant clang-format, codespell, whitespace, and EOF checks passed; full pre-commit initialization was blocked by local network policy. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing documentation changes are required. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32180304913](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32180304913)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32180304818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32180304818)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] Add H200 MoE configs for Nemotron-3.5
signals.text: > [!WARNING] > **Draft: do not merge.** Forced-Triton real-model validation on one H200 > found that every tested TP1 table reduced or failed to improve normalized > output-token throughput. The isolated kernel numbers below are valid, but > they do not translate into a serving-positive configuration. ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`: - TP1: `E=128,N=1856` - TP2 per rank: `E=128,N=928` Both shapes previously used the generic fallback config. The tuned configs reduce kernel latency by 32.2% to 39.6% across the measured token counts. ## Forced-Triton real-model validation Tested official revision `d468880b6ad3c6e0d21377ce7242adaea4cc884d` with SGLang v0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), Torch 2.11.0, Triton 3.6.0, and `--moe-runner-backend triton` on one H200. Each comparison used ten 200-question GSM8K runs, five shots, parallelism 64, and zero-temperature sampling. | TP1 candidate | Median latency | Median output throughput | Quality | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Original up only vs baseline | +0.79% | -1.70% | up to 0.5% invalid in three runs | | Original up + tuned down vs baseline | +5.78% | -4.68% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up + down vs fresh baseline | -2.23% | -1.69% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up only vs fresh baseline | -0.22% | -1.68% | zero invalid | | Alignment-aware up only vs reverse-order baseline | +3.95% | -2.86% | zero invalid | The decode-aware searches added M=1,4,16,32,64,128 entries, used 100 real routed-expert tensors covering all 128 experts, and matched up/down `BLOCK_SIZE_M`. A conservative follow-up fixed decode `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` to reduce expert padding and route-alignment overhead. Neither approach produced a serving-positive table. A reverse-order baseline recovered its original performance, ruling out simple node drift. **Decision:** keep this PR in draft and do not publish these configs. A future attempt must tune the complete MoE path, including route alignment, padding, and both projections, rather than optimizing isolated projection kernels. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `c2c1c4d3ebc42402264002f6ec57f90fee58c30c` - Token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape ## Results | TP | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256 | 1435.44 | 930.48 | 1.543x | 35.18% | | 1 | 512 | 1550.47 | 967.20 | 1.603x | 37.62% | | 1 | 1024 | 1694.77 | 1023.66 | 1.656x | 39.60% | | 2 | 256 | 734.74 | 493.07 | 1.490x | 32.89% | | 2 | 512 | 780.75 | 529.32 | 1.475x | 32.20% | | 2 | 1024 | 845.91 | 548.78 | 1.541x | 35.13% | The TP2 per-rank config was also run concurrently on both H200s. Both ranks selected the same configs; their measured means were within 0.6% to 1.0%. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODEL=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-model-configs/nemotron35-lightning RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full TP1 and TP2 searches: ```bash mkdir -p "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 1 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 2 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & wait ``` Baseline and tuned validation, repeated three times for each TP size: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" done CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/E=128,N=1856,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/E=128,N=928,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` Concurrent dual-H200 TP2 per-rank validation: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2-dual-rank-gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results/nemotron35-lightning-h200-configs.patch ```
