signals.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly
signals.text: ## Motivation Two related changes to AMD nightly Qwen coverage: add the missing Qwen3.8 job, and stop spending runner time on two Qwen jobs that are redundant or dead. **Add Qwen3.8.** [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD Instinct recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. The model reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (the checkpoint reports `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs today with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing currently guards it. A change to the shared Qwen3.5 hybrid path or to the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade Qwen3.8 output quality or throughput on ROCm with no signal. The new job follows the single-node MI355X cell the cookbook publishes ([`hw=mi355x`, `quant=mxfp4`, `strategy=balanced`, `nodes=single`](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8#hw=mi355x&variant=default&quant=mxfp4&strategy=balanced&nodes=single)). **Stop running the Qwen3-235B jobs.** They duplicate `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` coverage that survives elsewhere, including per-commit. ### Why MXFP4 and not the FP8 checkpoint directly At 2.4T parameters FP8 is ~2.4 TB, against 8 x 288 GB = 2.30 TB on an MI355X node, so the FP8 checkpoint has no single-node AMD recipe at all — the cookbook serves it as MI300X TP8 x PP2 across two nodes, and the AMD nightly runners are single-node. Single-node on AMD therefore means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization **of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`** (~1.2 TB, ~150 GB per GPU). Only the routed experts are quantized — attention, the shared expert, the MoE gate and `lm_head` stay at source precision — so AMD measures the same **97.49** GSM8K as the FP8 baseline (100% recovery). The FP8 checkpoint's quality is what this job is gating; MXFP4 is just the packaging that fits one node. ## Modifications ### New: Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x job **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in one file, registered to the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite (`est_time=14400`, `nightly=True`): - `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` — GSM8K few-shot at TP8, gated at 0.93. - `test_b_serving_perf` — serving benchmark over batch sizes 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out, reported through the shared `generate_simple_markdown_report`. Both phases launch from a single `SERVER_ARGS`, which reproduces the recipe published on the AMD model card: ``` --tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --trust-remote-code --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' ``` with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and the eval runs `run_eval` gsm8k over the test split at 512 threads, `max_tokens=2048`, `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`. **Why accuracy and perf share a suite** rather than splitting into `nightly-amd-accuracy-*` and `nightly-perf-*`: sharing one `SERVER_ARGS` means the throughput numbers describe the exact configuration the accuracy gate covers, and a flag change cannot drift one out from under the other. Perf is also skipped unless accuracy passed (`accuracy_passed` class flag, with ordering from unittest's alphabetical method sort): a server that decodes garbage still benchmarks fine, so publishing its throughput would be worse than publishing nothing. Two flags in `SERVER_ARGS` are load-bearing rather than restatements of a default, and are commented as such in the file: - `--page-size 1` — `_page_size_default` bumps the default to 64 on HIP when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, so the measured geometry only holds if the page size is pinned. - `--attention-backend aiter` — no arg override picks a backend for `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM` on ROCm, so the AITER path has to be named. The server deliberately runs with **no `--reasoning-parser`**: the scorer extracts the last number in the reply, so a `<think>` block still scores when reasoning stays in `message.content`. With a reasoning parser on, it would be split into `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty and scoring 0. The model path is overridable via `QWEN38_MXFP4_MODEL_PATH` for hosts with a local copy. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x, and the model card pins ROCm 7.2.0 for MI350/MI355. There is no MI30x counterpart — gfx942 has no hardware MX matmul, and the FP8 checkpoint it would otherwise serve needs two nodes. It is a single step rather than the usual accuracy/perf pair, because both phases live in the same suite. `timeout-minutes: 420` / `--timeout-per-file 21600` budget two loads of the 1.2 TB checkpoint, one per phase, which dominate wall time well before either the eval or the benchmark starts; `ENABLE_CACHE_HOST: "1"` keeps the weights on the runner cache so steady-state nights are far cheaper than the first. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite under `NIGHTLY_SUITES[HWBackend.AMD]`. **`scripts/ci/amd/ensure_hf_cache_space.sh`** (new) — run before the test step. `/sgl-data/hf-cache` is shared by every AMD job on the runner and nothing evicts from it, so a new ~1.2 TB tenant does not fit and the download dies partway through on ENOSPC. This is not a capacity ceiling — Kimi-K3's ~1.5 TB checkpoint completes on the same pool — the cache simply has no eviction, and the problem has been papered over twice by repointing `CACHE_HOST` at a fresh empty directory ([#26642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26642), [#26905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26905)), which frees space by abandoning the old cache rather than managing it. Stale partial downloads were already handled by `scripts/ci/utils/cleanup_hf_cache.py`, which the script delegates to rather than reimplementing — that script is wired into `scripts/ci/cuda/prepare_runner.sh` but nothing on AMD called it before. On top of that it reports free space unconditionally and, when clearing partial downloads is not enough, evicts whole checkpoints least-recently-used first. That last part is the genuinely new behavior: the ENOSPC here was a cache full of *complete* checkpoints, which `cleanup_hf_cache.py` alone does not address. Anything modified in the last 120 minutes is protected so a job sharing the mount cannot have weights deleted mid-load, and the caller names the checkpoint it is about to fetch so it is never the victim. It never fails the job. The reporting alone earns its place: the ENOSPC failure was only diagnosable by reading 8,500 lines of job log, because free space was never printed anywhere. Evicted checkpoints are re-downloaded by whichever job needs them next, so on a cache too small for every large model at once this trades another job's download time for this one running at all — and if Qwen3.8 and Kimi-K3 end up evicting each other nightly, the fleet needs more cache capacity than a script can conjure. ### Removed: the Qwen3-235B nightly jobs Only the workflow jobs go. No file under `test/` is touched — the tests, their launch recipes and their thresholds stay exactly as they are, so re-enabling is re-adding the job, and `run_suite.py --suite nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` still works by hand in the meantime. (Marking the tests `disabled=` was considered and rejected: on top of removing the job it changes no behavior, and it would make that manual re-run silently skip.) **All three Qwen3-235B jobs** — `test_qwen3_instruct.py` (BF16), `test_qwen3_instruct_fp8.py` (FP8) on an 8-GPU mi300 runner, and `test_qwen3_instruct_mxfp4.py` (`amd/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-mxfp4`, TP4 + EP2) on MI35x, across *both* the ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 nightlies. `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is well covered without them: - **Per-commit, on both ROCm lanes**, `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` runs on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` in the `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite, quantizes `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` with `--quantization mxfp4` and asserts `gsm8k >= 0.89`. That suite is dispatched by `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0 container) *and* `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` (`--rocm-version rocm720`), so the MXFP4 MoE kernels for this architecture's shapes are checked on every PR against both ROCm versions, not once a night against one. This is why the removal applies to the ROCm 7.0 nightly as well as 7.2: neither lane is left without a substitute. - **Nightly**, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` runs TP8 in `test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py` and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` runs in the mi30x GSM8K sweep. - Serialized Quark MXFP4 *checkpoint loading* is covered by the Qwen3.8 job added here plus the DeepSeek-R1, GLM-5 and Kimi-K3 nightlies. What loses its substitute is the combination rather than any single ingredient: a pre-quantized Quark checkpoint on `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` at 235B scale over TP4 + EP2. The per-commit test quantizes online at TP1, and expert parallelism survives nightly only through the MiniMax jobs — no Qwen job exercises EP after this. That is the deliberate trade for four 8-GPU jobs per night — two per nightly, each capped at `timeout-minutes: 120`, two on the `linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang` pool and two on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. The jobs removed are `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b[-rocm720]` and `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen3-235b-mxfp4[-rocm720]`, along with their `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` dependencies in each workflow. Their three test files then join the other registered-but-undispatched AMD nightly tests noted below. ### Out of scope After this change, a scan turns up **36 AMD nightly test files** registered but reachable by neither `--suite` nor direct path — the three Qwen3-235B tests above plus 33 pre-existing ones, mostly dormant mi30x and mi35x DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax evals. Those are left untouched here. One is worth calling out for whoever picks that up: `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` is not merely dormant but unrunnable — `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` has no `setup_profile_directory()` and `run_benchmark_for_model` takes no `enable_profile=`, so `test_b_perf` would `AttributeError` on its first line, and its model paths are runner-local `/data/amd/` directories rather than HuggingFace ids. It is deliberately left unmodified by this PR. ## Accuracy Tests **Validation run:** [Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2) #32313140175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313140175), dispatched on this branch's head with `job_select: nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720`, covering both phases. Two earlier dispatches informed the current state. [#32185767315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32185767315) predated the perf phase and was cancelled. [#32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) got everything right up to the weight download and then died on ENOSPC in the shared runner cache, which is what the `ensure_hf_cache_space.sh` step above exists to prevent. Between them they did confirm the wiring: job selection resolves to this job alone with the rest skipped, no `qwen3-235b` job exists at these SHAs, and `run_suite.py --suite nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` discovers the test rather than reporting an empty suite after the rename. Expect a long run regardless: both nightlies fire at `30 17 * * *` and drain the same `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` pool, so a manual dispatch queues behind their MI35x backlog, and the 1.2 TB fetch dominates once it starts. The gate is `ACCURACY_THRESHOLD = 0.93`, ~5% below AMD's published 0.9749 — the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.yaml` uses `rtol: 0.05` against 0.9704, i.e. a 0.922 floor). The threshold is inherited from AMD's measurement rather than from a run on the CI fleet, so if the dispatch lands materially off 0.9749 on the CI image, the number should be recalibrated to the observed run the way the Kimi-K3 job was. No model or kernel code is touched by this PR, so there is no output-affecting change to validate beyond the job itself. Static checks, run locally without GPUs: both workflows parse and every `check-all-jobs` dependency resolves to a defined job, with no `job_select` option pointing at a removed one; the AST registry parser resolves the new file to `backend=AMD, suite='nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4', nightly=True, est_time=14400` and no file under `test/` other than the new one differs from `main`; the suite string matches across all three files with no stale references to the pre-rename name; and every symbol the new test imports exists in its source module. `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_workflow_job_names.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, isort, black, ruff and codespell all pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The perf phase is the speed coverage this PR adds; it publishes a latency / input-throughput / output-throughput / ITL table to the job summary rather than asserting a threshold, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Batch sizes and sequence lengths are overridable through the usual `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS` environment variables. Net runner impact: one new MI35x job added, four 8-GPU jobs removed (two per nightly, split across the mi300 and mi35x pools). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe; no doc change needed. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: fix(moe): handle bf16 DeepEP low_latency dispatch (a_scales=None) in cutlass W4A8
signals.text: ### Problem `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_ll()` unconditionally calls `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton(x_scale=a_scales, ...)`. Under DeepEP **low_latency**, the cutlass W4A8 backend dispatches in **bf16** (its default; also forced by `--deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype bf16`), so the dispatch returns bf16 tokens with **no per-token fp8 scales** — `a_scales is None`. The unconditional call then dereferences `None`: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size' ``` at decode cuda-graph capture → scheduler dies (exit -3). Hit on Kimi-K3-W4AFP8 with `--deepep-mode auto` (normal prefill + low_latency decode), cuda-graph ON. ### Fix When `a_scales is None`, quantize the bf16 masked tokens to per-tensor fp8 in-place with the static input scale via `per_tensor_quant_fp8(...)` — byte-for-byte the same quantization `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal()` already applies to its bf16 input. Forcing fp8 dispatch instead is not a general fix: the per-token triton kernel asserts `hidden % 1024 == 0`, which fails for models whose routed-expert hidden size isn't 1024-divisible (e.g. Kimi-K3 = 3584). ### Validation mini-K3 (2 nodes, EP16, `--deepep-mode auto`, cuda-graph ON) passes decode capture and serves completions without the crash. Draft pending upstream CI + a full multi-node run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190125293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125293)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190125037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125037)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add a probe that verifies torch.profiler captures HIP-graph kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD/Silo report that on every `lmsysorg/sglang*` ROCm 7.2 image (v0.5.12 through v0.5.17, `*-rocm720-*`), `torch.profiler` traces contain no GPU kernels for work launched through hipGraph, and they have been swapping `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` / `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200` for the 7.2.4 versions to work around it. The cause is upstream and already fixed: - ROCTracer can fail to report kernel operations: [ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), closed with "Resolved in ROCm 7.2.2". - ROCm 7.2.0's HIP runtime also has a wrong doorbell index in `dispatchGenericAqlPacketBatch` (the graph batch-dispatch path) plus an InterceptQueue ring-buffer heap corruption, both fixed in 7.2.1 ([pytorch/pytorch#177873](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177873)). That matches the `CUDAGraph::replay` deadlock inside `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` seen in our own CI (#34452) — the same bug class surfacing as a hang instead of a gap. - The 7.2.4 bases carry the fixed libraries: `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_*` ships `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204` and `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204` (`hip-runtime-amd` 7.2.26015.70200 -> 7.2.53211.70204, `roctracer` 4.1.70200 -> 4.1.70204). #30984 has since landed the `rocm724` flavors, so images with the fixed runtime are being published. What is missing is a way to confirm that claim, for those images and for any future base bump. Nothing in CI can currently tell a working profiler from a broken one: `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts that the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it, and since #34452 the profiling suite runs without CUDA graphs on ROCm, so it never exercises the replay path at all. ## Modifications ### `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` Captures a graph, replays it under `torch.profiler`, and counts the device events that reach the exported trace. An eager control run separates "this runtime cannot trace graph replay" from "this runtime cannot trace anything", and each phase runs in its own process under a timeout because ROCm 7.2.0 can wedge inside `hipGraphLaunch` rather than merely lose events. It also prints the ROCm version, the mapped HIP and tracing sonames, and warns when the device reports no marketing name, which is the symptom of a base image without libdrm-amdgpu. It depends on nothing but torch and the HIP runtime, so it qualifies any image or base image: ``` torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4 (hip 7.2.41134), rocm 7.2.4 device: 'AMD Instinct MI355X' (gfx950) hip/tracing libs: libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204, libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0 eager launch: 32 kernel events, 1180 us device time, 921 trace events graph replay: 32 kernel events, 1174 us device time, 918 trace events VERDICT: PASS -- graph-replay kernels reach the trace. ``` Not registered in the AMD suites here: on a rocm720 image it is expected to fail and, per #34452, can take the process down with it. #35398 runs it against the published rocm724 images instead. ### `test/registered/unit/ci/test_hip_graph_profiling_probe.py` The probe's value is that a red run says *which* failure happened: nothing traceable at all, a wedged `hipGraphLaunch`, or kernels lost under graph replay. A GPU job can only ever exercise whichever case its image is in, so the mapping is driven on CPU with canned phase results instead — every verdict, the exit codes, the ROCm/ROCm#6102 citation appearing only for the untraced-graph case, the marketing-name warning, and the trace parser, where counting a host-only trace as device work would turn the whole check into a false pass. Registered as `base-a-test-cpu`, 9 tests, no GPU. ### `docs/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.mdx` Document the gap for users on the current images, how to check an image, that the `rocm724` tags carry the ROCm fix, and the `--disable-cuda-graph` fallback for anyone who has to stay on a 7.2.0 runtime, with the caveat that decode numbers collected that way exclude the replay path. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to the change itself; it measures whether profiling works rather than changing performance. ## Test plan Verified locally without a GPU: - The new unit test passes (9 tests): every verdict path, the exit codes, and the trace parser. - Trace parsing additionally checked against a real `export_chrome_trace` output, including a capitalized `Kernel` category. - The timeout path's process-group kill verified against a wedged child. - On a host with no GPU the probe reports `environment: unusable -- no GPU visible to torch` and exits 1. - `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, black, isort and codespell all pass. Needs a GPU host — the decisive measurement, and it needs no SGLang build: ```bash GPU="--device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --security-opt seccomp=unconfined" # ROCm 7.2.0 runtime: expected FAIL (reproduces the report) docker run --rm $GPU -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w \ rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 \ python3 scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py # ROCm 7.2.4 runtime: expected PASS docker run --rm $GPU -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w \ rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 \ python3 scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py ``` Same torch 2.9.1, same probe, only the ROCm patch level differs. Then run it in a published `*-rocm724-*` image (expected PASS) and a `*-rocm720-*` image (expected FAIL). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- The probe is the test; registering it in the AMD suites requires images on a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime. --> - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [AMD] Verify the nightly ROCm 7.2.4 images trace HIP-graph kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation #30984 landed the `rocm724` flavors and the nightly now publishes them to `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. Those flavors exist because ROCm 7.2.0 drops kernel-dispatch events for work submitted through `hipGraphLaunch` ([ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), fixed in 7.2.2), which is what AMD/Silo hit when profiling SGLang decoding on every `*-rocm720-*` image. Nothing verifies that the published images actually restore it. A trace with no GPU kernels in it still looks like a successful profile, `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts the trace directory is non-empty, and since #34452 the profiling suite runs without CUDA graphs on ROCm, so CI never exercises the replay path at all. A future base bump could quietly take the fix away again. ## Modifications One job in `release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml`. After publish, each `rocm724` flavor is probed on the GPU it targets — gfx942 on MI300X, gfx950 on MI355X — because the behaviour lives in the HIP runtime rather than in SGLang, so it is worth confirming per device generation. The job pulls the tag the publish job recorded in its artifact, starts the standard CI container against it, and runs `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` inside the image. No dependency install: the point is to exercise the image's own torch and HIP runtime. The `rocm720` legs are deliberately excluded, since they are expected to fail; a dispatch that selects a single `rocm720` arch skips the job entirely. This verifies after publish rather than gating it, so the daily images are not held behind a GPU runner queue. A red leg means the day's `rocm724` image traces nothing under graph replay and should not be recommended for profiling. Turning it into a real gate means splitting the publish job's `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg` pushes, which is worth doing separately if you want that. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes; this adds a verification job to a release workflow. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The job measures whether profiling works on the published image. ## Test plan - `actionlint` reports nothing on the new job; the only findings in the file are the pre-existing self-hosted runner labels and `docker/login-action@v2` in the publish and mirror jobs. - Job names pass `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`. - The probe itself is validated in #35390 (trace parsing, all verdict paths, timeout handling, no-GPU behaviour). To exercise it, dispatch the nightly with `gpu_arch=gfx950-rocm724` after #35390 merges: publish builds that flavor and the new job probes it on MI355X. Expected `VERDICT: PASS`, against the same probe failing on a `*-rocm720-*` image. ## Notes for reviewers - Depends on #35390, which adds the probe script this job runs. Merge that first. - This PR previously proposed its own `rocm724` stages, nightly workflow, release-matrix entry, and torch Triton-pin patch. #30984 landed all four, so only the verification remains. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- CI workflow change --> - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). <!-- Documented in #35390 --> - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32194584123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194584123)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194583932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194583932)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [GDN] Route Qwen TP4 decode and verify rows through Cake
signals.text: ## Summary - lazily load the optional public FlashInfer Cake GDN decode package on SM100/SM103 - fail closed on unsupported dtype, layout, shape, stride, state-pool, or graph-capture combinations - preserve caller-stream and CUDA graph semantics with preallocated workspace/state and cached FP32 dt bias - route the actual Qwen3-Next TP4 BF16 decode and verify rows through the promoted tile16 full-warp kernels ## Qualification - rebased onto current SGLang main b814a7e812fb9367d994af307085bd30de329f96 - B200/SM100, job 3752127 on umbriel-b200-037: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including actual TP4 eager and CUDA Graph paths - GB300/SM103, job 510532 on nvl72d093-T03: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including the same paths - exact route IDs: cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_t1.tile16_fullwarp and cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_verify_t4.tile16_fullwarp - exact TP4 shapes: B=4,T=1,H=4,HV=8 and B=2/3/5/8,T=4,H=4,HV=8; adjacent B=4,T=4 and every unmeasured layout fail closed - same-environment cold-L2 CUPTI kernel A/B versus live FlashInfer 8044d94bf9: - B200 T1 0.003296 vs 0.003472 ms (1.053x), T4 0.006400 vs 0.006944 ms (1.085x), geometric mean 1.069x - GB300 T1 0.003040 vs 0.003296 ms (1.084x), T4 0.006304 vs 0.006736 ms (1.069x), geometric mean 1.076x - correctness uses fixed BF16 atol=rtol=1e-2; dual-arch public ABI/stream/graph and sanitizer gates pass - exact Qwen3-Next 80B FP8 TP4/MTP model replay, four GB300s, job 3137824: 4/4 tests pass; cache-hit KL 0.0007701/0.0017106 versus the fixed 0.0035 ceiling; all four TP ranks record the Cake T4 route during CUDA Graph capture - attributed serving ABBA, four GB300s, job 3137849: all eight measured 128-request rounds complete; four-round median output/total throughput 1.000280x, mean/median TPOT 1.003214x/1.005037x, and mean TTFT 0.987693x versus FlashInfer (the ~1.25% TTFT regression is retained explicitly) Current-head real-model evidence is recorded below. Review and merge are intentionally deferred in this evidence-only phase. ## Current-head decision evidence This replay uses FlashInfer #4581 head `4215a24cb` and supersedes the earlier `45b60f98` jobs/comment. Review and merge are intentionally deferred. ### Environment and attribution - real Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 weights, revision `c5f5f263bdd5cc134092897864e8905d8fe7b928` - four NVIDIA GB300 CC 10.3 GPUs on healthy replacement nodes; SGLang `ee8378ad4`, Torch `2.13.0a0+nv26.07`, CUDA 13.3 - `sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1+cu130`, `sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post3`, `apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11` - source-matched FlashInfer JIT in both arms; the released image AOT package is removed equally. Candidate phases route all four TP ranks through Cake; baseline phases route none ### Accuracy and model behavior Both arm orders run the full 1,319-row GSM8K file with five fixed exemplars, so 1,314 answers are scored, plus decode/prefill cache-hit KL and prefix-cache branching: | Job / order | FlashInfer | Cake | Paired delta | FlashInfer KL | Cake KL | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---| | `516222`, baseline → Cake | 1256/1314 (0.955860) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -8 / -0.608828 pp | 0.00136385 / 0.00157485 | 0.00134804 / 0.00159145 | | `516345`, Cake → baseline | 1249/1314 (0.950533) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -1 / -0.076104 pp | 0.00078810 / 0.00255420 | 0.00073162 / 0.00252816 | All four tests pass in every arm, all scores exceed the fixed `0.93` gate, and every KL value is below `0.0035`. Cake's exact score reproduces across node and order, but exact no-drop is false. The baseline itself varies by seven answers, so the first paired eight-answer delta cannot be assigned wholly to Cake. ### Uninstrumented E2E A/B Job `516223` uses baseline/Cake/Cake/baseline order, counterbalanced workload order, eight rounds per arm/workload, and 20,000 deterministic round-bootstrap resamples. Every request completes. | Workload | Metric | FlashInfer | Cake | Speedup (95% CI) | Decision | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | 128 prompts, 512 in / 256 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1231.754012 tok/s | 1237.596662 tok/s | 1.004743x [0.998292, 1.020776] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 839.608126 ms | 832.389779 ms | 1.008672x [0.999705, 1.020929] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 6.216159 ms | 6.113625 ms | 1.016771x [1.001588, 1.026764] | speedup | | 64 prompts, 128 in / 1024 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1403.321505 tok/s | 1412.172752 tok/s | 1.006307x [0.994657, 1.042125] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 2834.498442 ms | 2840.753832 ms | 0.997798x [0.986704, 1.034864] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 5.561249 ms | 5.532944 ms | 1.005116x [0.993362, 1.016897] | indistinguishable | Dynamic B2/B3/B5 coverage removes the former statistically resolved decode-heavy throughput regression. Balanced mean TPOT has a resolved gain, and both aggregate-throughput point estimates are positive, but both throughput confidence intervals cross 1.0. Therefore this head passes the fixed model correctness gates but does not establish exact GSM8K no-drop or a general statistically resolved E2E throughput speedup. ## Dependencies - FlashInfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4581 Supersedes #35328 because repository rules prohibit force-pushing its protected head branch after rebase. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32210997206](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210997206)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32210997060](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210997060)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Write the req_to_token page tail so rows stay valid over whole pages
signals.text: The paged allocator hands out whole pages, but the row write only covers the requested tokens, so `req_to_token[:, seq_len : ceil(seq_len)]` keeps the previous occupant's indices. Fill that tail (slots inside a page are consecutive) and widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every `page_size > 1` config, not just speculative ones. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32304945912](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304945912)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32304945576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304945576)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Kimi-K3: fix vision-DP rank-local indexing into global grid_thws_host
signals.text: ## Motivation Serving Kimi-K3 with vision-DP sharding (observed on `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8` with DSPARK speculative decoding, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`), the first `/v1/chat/completions` request that carries **two or more images with different geometries** kills the scheduler: ``` ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids ``` The request returns 500 and the server never recovers — every subsequent request fails until the container is restarted. Single-image requests, and multi-image requests whose images share one NaViT grid, are unaffected — which is how this survives typical smoke tests. ## Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`, `materialize_item_features(image_indices)` receives the **global** image indices assigned to this vision-DP rank, but the deferred-preprocessing block indexes `grid_thws_host` — a global tensor with one row per image in the batch — with the rank-**local** enumerate positions: ```python expected_grids = grid_thws_host[indices] # local idx into global tensor ... patch_counts = [int(grid_thws_host[index].prod().item()) for index in indices] # same bug ``` On any rank whose assigned images are not the global prefix `[0..k)`, the expected grids and patch split counts are read from the wrong rows. If the wrongly-read row happens to hold a different grid, the `torch.equal` sanity check fires and raises, taking the scheduler down. (The non-DP path passes `list(range(len(items)))`, where local == global, so it never triggers.) ## Fix Translate the local enumerate positions through the closure's `image_indices` before indexing `grid_thws_host`, in both the expected-grid comparison and the `patch_counts` split. No numeric effect on correct batches — the check now compares each produced grid against the row it was actually produced from. ## Accuracy Tests Deterministic repro: one chat completion with two images, 504×504 and 1344×756 (different NaViT grids), against a TP8/DCP8 B300 deployment. - **Before:** request returns 500, scheduler dead (`/health` times out until restart) — reproduced 2/2. - **After:** request returns 200 (14.8s cold) with a correct description of both images; `/health` stays 200; subsequent multimodal and text traffic unaffected. Model outputs for previously-working requests are unchanged: the patch only affects index bookkeeping inside a validation check, not any computed feature. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — two list-indexing expressions inside the deferred-preprocessing validation branch; no hot-path change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black/codespell clean; ruff `F401,F821,UP037` and isort report zero *new* findings vs the base revision of this file) - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (The fixed code is a closure inside `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`'s image-feature path, so it cannot be exercised without constructing the model; the failure mode — call sites passing rank-local indices — is only reachable under multi-GPU vision-DP. Validated with the deterministic E2E repro above instead. There is currently no registered NVIDIA K3 e2e suite to extend (`test_kimi_k25.py` uses `kimi_k25.py`, not this file); if maintainers want a registered regression, I'm happy to contribute an `8-gpu-models` K3 case that sends one two-image heterogeneous-grid chat completion and asserts the server survives — pending confirmation the CI runners can host K3 weights.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## CI First-time external contribution from a fork, so I cannot initiate CI myself — could a maintainer or authorized contributor kick it off with `/tag-and-rerun-ci`? I'll follow up with `/rerun-failed-ci` on any flaky stages after that. Happy to address review feedback quickly. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32229955738](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32229955738)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32229955253](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32229955253)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NVIDIA] Fix SM107 MXFP8 activation prep
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Fix MXFP8 activation preparation for the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend on SM107. GPT-OSS on SM107 can reach the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernel without a pre-quantized route handoff. Previously, SGLang used the Triton per-token-group quantizer in this case. This does not reliably produce the activation representation expected by the FlashInfer SM107 path. The quantizer producing the activations must follow the same MXFP8 and UE8M0 layout contract as the FlashInfer MoE kernel consuming them. Using FlashInfer for both operations on SM107 avoids the incompatible producer/consumer path. The fake custom-op implementation also needs the real scale-buffer shape. Returning a placeholder one-element tensor can produce incorrect metadata during `torch.compile`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantizer on SM107 when no route/quant handoff is available. - Preserve Kimi K3's existing fused route/quant handoff. - Preserve the existing Triton activation-quantization path on other SM10x architectures. - Preserve FlashInfer quantization for padded hidden dimensions. - Correct the FlashInfer custom-op fake scale-buffer size for both linear and swizzled layouts so `torch.compile` metadata matches the real quantizer. - Add CPU regression tests covering dispatch behavior, padded inputs, route handoff, and fake output shapes. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> * Validated GPT-OSS with real weights on SM107 with 4 focused regression tests passed on SM107. * Verified the fake quantizer reports the expected scale shape. * Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signals.title: [CI] Trim the base-c 4-gpu-h100 stage from 5 shards to 4
signals.text: `base-c-test-4-gpu-h100` runs its shards serially (`max_parallel = 5 // 3 = 1`), so cutting `est_time` is a linear wall-clock win. **5470s / 16 files -> 3572s / 13 files, 5 shards -> 3.** Nothing is dropped from CI. Most of it is placement: several tests sat on the 4-GPU runner without needing four GPUs. - `test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` -> `base-b`/`1-gpu-small`, dropping its `4-gpu-b200` and `4-gpu-gb300` registrations. Collectives are faked and every arch branch is `patch.object`-mocked, so the three runners ran identical mocks. - `test_hicache_storage_3fs_backend.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Max `--tp-size` is 2 and both configs are H100. - `test_disaggregation_unified_memory.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Its two classes are prefill tp1 on GPU 0 plus decode at `decode_base_gpu_id=1`, i.e. two GPUs; the two classes left in `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py` need three (prefill tp2/pp2 plus `decode_base_gpu_id=2`). The shared parity base class stays in the latter and is imported. Four PD tests already run on `2-gpu-large` with the same `PDDisaggregationServerBase` fixture. - `test_pp_gemma4.py` (new) -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`, taking `TestGemma4PPAccuracy` and `TestGemma4PLEPPAccuracy` out of `test_pp_single_node.py`. Both are tp1/pp2; the four classes left behind are tp2/pp2. Both already carry `@unittest.skipIf(is_in_amd_ci())`, so no AMD registration moves. - The two `*AllocFail` classes and three DeepEP crossings move to new `*_extra.py` files on `extra-b`. Dead code removed (594 lines, no CI time since none of it ran): - `test_deepep_small.py::TestNoGatherdBuffer`, skipped as "covered in test_deepep_large.py" -- verified: `test_deepep_large.py::TestDeepseek` runs the same dp-attention + DeepEP + `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` + `--enable-dp-lm-head` combination. - `test_deepep_small.py::TestMTP`, skipped as "covered in TestMTPWithTBO". That claim was inaccurate -- it is tp4/dp2 while `TestMTPWithTBO` is tp4/dp4 -- so removing it does drop the dp2 + MTP combination rather than a duplicate. - `test/registered/rl/test_release_memory_occupation.py`, carrying `disabled="Temporarily disabled - needs investigation"` since 2026-05-26. Nothing imports it, and the sibling `test_multi_instance_release_memory_occupation.py` is self-contained. All moved classes keep their bodies byte-for-byte; the only edit is renaming the PD parity base class so it can be imported. `base-b-test-2-gpu-large` absorbs the three moves at 6701s -> 8121s, which raises it from 5 shards to 7 and its `max_parallel` from 1 to 2, cutting its serial waves from 5 to 4. `base-b-test-1-gpu-small` stays at 8 shards. Reviewer note: the DeepEP split takes **attention-TP + TBO off the per-commit path**; every other dimension there keeps a representative. The two new `2-gpu-large` `est_time` values (900s, 220s) are estimates split from the parent files -- the live partition model will correct them. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208152940](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208152940)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208152857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208152857)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
signals.text: ## Motivation A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output. #34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`, and scoped itself explicitly: > Only the prefill donation depth changes here. Decode tracking keeps its own `--mamba-track-interval` grid. That decode grid does not land on the tree page. `--mamba-track-interval` has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page — and is never resolved anywhere (`grep` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty). Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant. The insert-time guard that would have caught this was deferred to #34760 and #34780 — **both closed, never merged** — and there is no mamba depth check on the insert in `main` today, so the misalignment stays silent. **Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`. | page | dcp | tree page | interval | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok | | 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** | | 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken | | 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken | Two shipped recipes are on the broken row today, both in `test_kimi_k3_b300.py`: `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) and `TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` (`--dcp-size 8` + DSPARK — spec is only rejected under DCP *with* HiCache, so the mamba grid is live there too). Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries. Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this. ## Modifications `mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well: ```python def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int: return math.lcm( mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval ) ``` Read where a checkpoint depth is picked: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed. The tree page is a process constant, so each site only needs a live handle to the tree. `prepare_for_decode` and the spec paths take it off the batch, as the extend path already does. The batch-result processor takes it off **its own** `tree_cache`: the batch it is handed is the result-queue `copy()`, whose field list is scoped to what `process_batch_result` needs and does not carry one. Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there. Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask and Inkling's `sconv` (which holds only a `ForwardBatch`). `lcm` makes the derived grid a multiple of the raw interval, so every snapshot step is still a flush step and the flush mask's invariant survives. Note the comment at `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:403` says the two "fire on the same steps"; after this change they fire on nested sets of steps. `test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py` is a pre-existing test (#33477) whose hand-built `ScheduleBatch` and processor double now need a `tree_cache`, since `prepare_for_decode` did not read one before this change. Same edit #34808 made to its own double. Page and chunk are set to the interval already under test, so the derived grid stays 4 and every existing boundary expectation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests **Not yet measured — this is why the PR is a draft.** #34808 shipped a cold-vs-warm teacher-forced logprob comparison on a live Kimi-Linear dcp8 server for the prefill half; the decode half deserves the same evidence, and this PR currently argues from page alignment alone. An 8×B300 run on the `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` recipe, before and after, is the next step. What is verified statically: - **Cache reuse is unchanged.** The insert floors the donated depth to the tree page, so the node it lands on is `floor(min(N, floor(N/grid)·grid) / 512) · 512` — which collapses to the same `512q` under both grids (checked for every request length in [0, 4096): zero differ). Same number of cached checkpoints, same node depths, same KV prefix. What changes is *which state* is attached: previously a state that had already consumed 256 more tokens than the node it hung on. Snapshot writes into the ping-pong buffer halve on the affected recipes — less decode work, not fewer cache entries. - **Grid unchanged everywhere else:** page 64 × dcp 4, page 32 × dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config. New CPU unit case in `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`, beside #34808's extend cases since it is the same invariant from the other end. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32304189342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189342)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32304189109](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189109)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Speculative] Fix DSpark base logits for quantized target lm_head
signals.text: ## Motivation Serving a **quantized** target model with a DSpark draft fails at startup (both eager and CUDA-graph capture) with: ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (7x5120 and 2560x248320) ``` Reproduced on `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` drafting `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (RTX 5090, sglang 0.5.17 and current main). **Root cause**: DSpark dense drafts share the target's `lm_head` (`attach_shared_modules`). When the target is quantized, `lm_head.weight` is stored in a packed layout — e.g. NVFP4 stores `[vocab, 2560]` for a 5120-hidden target (5120 × 4 bit = 2560 bytes/row, with separate per-block `weight_scale`). `compute_base_logits` performs a raw `torch.matmul(hidden, weight.T)` against the packed layout, which is invalid for any quantized packing. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/dspark.py` — `DSparkDraftMixin.compute_base_logits`: - When `weight.shape[1] != hidden.shape[-1]` (packed layout), route through `lm_head.quant_method.apply(lm_head, hidden, bias)` — mirroring `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head` so the quant method's dequantize path applies. - Raise a clear `ValueError` when the lm_head is packed but carries no applicable quant method. - Unquantized targets keep the existing dense matmul path unchanged. ## Tests New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/models/test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py` (3 cases, all passing locally): 1. packed weight routes through `quant_method.apply` (call verified via mock, returns expected logits) 2. unquantized weight still uses the dense matmul path 3. packed weight without a quant method raises `ValueError` ``` test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_packed_weight_routes_to_quant_method PASSED test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_packed_weight_without_quant_method_raises PASSED test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_unquantized_weight_uses_matmul PASSED ``` ## End-to-end validation With this patch, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` + `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` boots to `ready to roll` on an RTX 5090 (previously crashed at CUDA graph capture). Single-stream bench (random ISL 1024 / OSL 512, 20 prompts): 131.41 output tok/s, accept len 2.89/8. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32206503048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206503048)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32206502903](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206502903)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd-rocm720` has fails on and off since Aug-15th (5 / 7 scheduled runs) with `AssertionError: -1 not greater than 200` in `test_bench_one_batch_2gpu.py`. The `-1` means no throughput was measured because the server is died. see [this log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653/job/95090118554), is: ``` [aiter] shape is M:1, N:14336, K:4096 ... not found tuned config in /tmp/aiter_configs/bf16_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config! aiter/tuned_gemm.py:514: bgemm_internal_cublaslt error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR when calling hipblasLtMatmul out = F.linear(inp, weights, bias) RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 900, operation not permitted when stream is capturing torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture [AITER] custom_all_reduce.cuh:3412 fail to call hipIpcOpenMemHandle(...) Fatal Python error: Aborted ``` The benchmarks Llama-3.1-8B and Mixtral-8x7B, and the aiter config merge this image pulled `llama70B`, `dsv3`, `dsv4`, `glm47`, `glm5`, `gptoss`, `kimi*`, `minimax_m3_eagle` and `qwen3_5_397b` — no configs to covere these two models. Thus the M:1 decode shapes have no tuned entry, and aiter takes the `F.linear` fallback. hipBLAS handle on first use. When first use is the fallback inside an active HIP graph triggered, `hipblasCreate` is illegal, it returns `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`. Everything after it is down. This help function _pre_initialize_hipblas_handle(self), "Force hipBLAS handle creation before CUDA graph capture on ROCm Running one tiny matmul here creates the handle on a normal stream such that the fallback inside capture reuses it. it helps to pre-initialize hipblas handle. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32244967520](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244967520)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32244967029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244967029)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Fix gfx950 Triton compiler crash on fp8 KV-cache attention
signals.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` has never passed on `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code ([latest instance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166850277/job/95808413702)): ``` python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed. extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so a model served on MI35x with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` **through the Triton attention backend** hits it, in decode as well as prefill. (Backends that do not route through these kernels, and the two ROCm Triton kernels that cannot take an fp8 pool at all, are out of scope; see Modifications.) ### Root cause Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand *down* to the pool dtype before the dot (`tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k)`, `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 `AccelerateAMDMatmul` promotes an fp8 x fp8 `tl.dot` to the scaled `V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4` family, which is **16x16x128** under the `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` launch hint all of these kernels pass. A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: `AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand` clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and `ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper` then reads `kBase = 32` elements per lane from a register range that only holds `K / 4`. That is the out-of-bounds `SmallVector` access. `P @ V` reduces `BLOCK_N`, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. `Q @ Kpe` reduces `BLOCK_DPE` (32/64) and `Q @ K` reduces `BLOCK_DMODEL`, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64. Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of [triton-lang/triton#8278](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/8278), which dropped the `enforcedNonKDim == 0 &&` escape hatch that had let an explicit `matrix_instr_nonkdim` skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. The Triton 3.4.0 wheels in the ROCm CI images predate that fix, so the guard is skipped and the backend aborts. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py` with `dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width)`: `True` for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction. - Each dot that casts an operand down to the tile it reads gets its own constexpr verdict (`QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE`). When it is `False` the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. This covers `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` (extend), `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (decode), `_verify_mla_prefix_stage1`, and `_verify_prefix_stage1` — including `_fwd_kernel`'s extend-stage `P @ V`, whose V is the caller's current-chunk tensor rather than the pool. - CPU unit test pinning the predicate, the widths the crashing gfx950 tile config actually uses, and the presence of the per-dot flags. Every flag is `True` on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, tile sizes, warp counts, and the `#mma` layout are all untouched. **Non-AMD impact: none, verified rather than argued.** `is_gfx95_supported()` returns `False` for every non-HIP build without touching the device, so `dot_in_kv_dtype` short-circuits to `True` on NVIDIA and the guards select the pre-existing expression. To confirm that costs nothing, I compiled the original kernel body and the guarded one (flags `True`) for five targets with Triton 3.4.0 and diffed the emitted TTGIR and LLIR modulo debug locations: **identical on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16)**. That check is what caught the one real difference — writing the guard as `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)` reorders the P cast against the `acc * re_scale` multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async `warp_group_dot` relative to the accumulator scaling. Keeping `p = p.to(v.dtype)` as its own statement inside the guard restores exact equivalence, which is why it is written that way. NVIDIA fp8 KV keeps casting down to fp8 and keeps its fp8 tensor-core path. The residual cost off gfx950 is one extra Triton compile (the new constexpr parameters change the cache key) and three or four integer / `frozenset` comparisons per launch. Two other ROCm Triton kernels dot against a tile that could in principle be fp8, and deliberately get no verdict: - `prefill_attention.py` never reads a KV pool, its `Q @ K` is uncast (so its operands already share a dtype), and its gfx950 `BLOCK_N` is 128 — which tiles the scaled instruction even if `P @ V` ran in fp8. - `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` does read the pool, but its `Q @ K` is uncast too, so a bf16 query against an fp8 pool fails Triton's frontend with `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv` well before the AMD backend. That is a separate pre-existing gap in that kernel, not this crash, and a per-dot verdict would not make it work. The verify combine kernels compute their draft-draft block with `tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2)`, not `tl.dot`, so no matrix-core promotion applies there. Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising `matrix_instr_nonkdim` for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes `warpsPerTile` for the chain-dot tail from `[8, 1]` to `[4, 2]` and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing `BLOCK_N = 128` (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it). ## Accuracy Tests `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` now passes on MI35x hardware. [Run 32217006660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217006660) is a targeted dispatch of just that stage against this PR's head (ROCm 7.0, since that lane is schedule-only and a PR event never runs it): **9/9 passed**, `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reports `"passed": true` with `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` executing, and the log contains no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()`. ([Run 32212523645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32212523645) is the same result on the first commit.) The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiled before, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path `P` reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; `extend_attention_fwd` and `verify_shared_kv_fwd` widen the same dots, so `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache`'s parity check compares like with like. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput measurement yet — the run above establishes correctness, not perf. The reasoning for expecting no loss: the wide `Q @ K` dot keeps `tt.dot_scaled` (verified in the emitted TTGIR below), and for the narrow dots CDNA4's non-scaled `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8` — what a Triton carrying #8278 would fall back to — reduces the same 32 elements per instruction as `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_BF16`, so bf16 operands run at the same rate. The extra cost is the fp8 -> bf16 converts on the V tile and a larger LDS footprint for it (80 KB total at head_dim 256 versus 128 KB for a bf16 pool, so still well inside the 160 KB budget). ## Verification Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for `hip:gfx950` without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as `extend_attention` at head_dim 256 (`BLOCK_M=128`, `num_warps=8`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`): | KV dtype | `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE` | `BLOCK_N` | Result | |---|---|---|---| | fp8_e4m3 | True (today) | 64 | **`RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False (this PR) | 64 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 32 | **`Assertion 'idx < size()' failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False | 32 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 128 | compiles (128 tiles the instruction) | | bf16 | True | 64 | compiles (unchanged path) | The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for `P @ V`, both under the same `#mma` layout as before: ``` %50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...> %77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> ``` The K3 MLA tile (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=64`), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing `BLOCK_DMODEL` to 64 crashes the `Q @ K` dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming `Q @ K` is always wide enough. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32309784950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309784950)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32309784578](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309784578)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [docs] Add a fused-kernels page for SGLang Diffusion
signals.text: ## Motivation Following the [`ops/diffusion` reorganization](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35114), the fused kernels that replace eager elementwise chains — adaLN modulate, residual gating, QK-norm, RoPE, norm epilogues, VAE layout kernels — have no user-facing page. The package `README.md` added in that PR is a selection matrix aimed at kernel authors, so there is nowhere to point someone who asks what is already fused, whether it changes their output, or how to turn on the parts that do. This adds that page, in the spirit of Sol-Engine's [kernel techniques](https://nvlabs.github.io/Sana/Sol-Engine/docs/techniques/kernel/) page but following this site's conventions. ## Modifications New page `docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx`, registered under **Performance Optimization** and cross-linked from the overview's output-preserving lever table. Contents: - **The two numerical contracts.** Bit-exact fusions mount unconditionally and still verify themselves against the live eager chain on first sight, falling back permanently on mismatch. Fusions that differ from eager at half-precision rounding level mount only for `quality="high"`, at batch boundaries, all-or-nothing per transformer. The page explains why the distinction is not pedantic: multi-step denoising turns a per-step rounding difference into visible quality loss. - **How to opt into the request-gated set** — `--quality high` on the CLI, and the `quality` field on the OpenAI-compatible endpoints — plus the list of families that mount. - **An inventory by operator domain** (normalization, adaLN modulation, RoPE/QK-norm, activation, attention, data movement): what each of the 34 registered operators replaces, on which backend, under which contract. - **Coverage by model**, since these kernels target a specific eager chain in a specific model rather than being general-purpose operators. - **How to query the registry** and pin a backend, and the import contract (import from the package, predicate-plus-kernel pairs, lazy resolution). Docs-only; no code changes. ## Accuracy Every table row is derived from the merged tree rather than written from memory: - the operator list, backends and capability sets come from the registry's `_SPECS` in `ops/diffusion/__init__.py` (34 operator ids across 38 implementations); - the model-coverage table comes from the actual import sites under `multimodal_gen/runtime/models`; - `--quality` and the OpenAI `quality` field were traced to `SamplingParams.quality` / `_runtime_sampling_quality` before being documented; - both Python snippets were executed against the live registry: ``` diffusion ops: 34 KernelBackend.TRITON norm.rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact:fused_scale_residual_rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact [CUDA] KernelBackend.CUTE_DSL norm.scale_residual_norm_cutedsl:fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift [CUDA] KernelBackend.FLYDSL norm.fused_residual_norm_flydsl:flydsl_fused_residual_norm_scale_shift [HIP] select_kernel -> KernelBackend.CUTE_DSL KernelSpec has load(): True ``` Relative links resolve to existing pages, `docs.json` parses, the page is reachable from the navigation, and headings follow the sentence-case rule in `docs/AGENTS.md`. signals.title: feat(mamba): add strict FlashInfer SSD and Cake prefill backends
signals.text: ## Summary - add strict opt-in `flashinfer_ssd` and `cake` Mamba SSD prefill backends while preserving the existing `flashinfer` default - project Nemotron-H logical C256 metadata onto the physical C128 domain supported by both source-level SSDCombined backends - preserve unified Mamba radix caching by inserting logical checkpoint boundaries into packed metadata and storing compact Cake checkpoint states in the main prefill pass - consume Cake checkpoints directly when resuming cached suffixes; retain replay only for the original CuTe route - keep backend routing strict: selecting Cake never falls back to Triton or CuTe ## Radix-cache correctness The packed-boundary unit case uses sequence lengths `[72, 312]` with an absolute checkpoint at token 200. Same-backend split-prefix/suffix output and final-state parity passes, and Cake checkpoint state agrees with the original CuTe prefix at BF16 `atol=rtol=1e-2` with maximum absolute error `0.015625`. `nvidia/Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K` revision `20acad0a529d386e3c7115b8635d482f9023e1b9`, BF16, TP2, 2x GB300, full GSM8K test set (1,319 questions), 8 train-set CoT exemplars, greedy decoding, 512 output-token cap, last-number exact match. Dataset SHA256: `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. | Cache-on run | Backend | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Matched run | Existing `flashinfer` | 785 / 1,319 | 59.5148% | 0 | | Matched run | Original `flashinfer_ssd` / CuTe | 770 / 1,319 | 58.3776% | 1 | | Matched run | Cake | 751 / 1,319 | 56.9371% | 0 | | Independent repeat | Cake | 766 / 1,319 | 58.0743% | 0 | Before checkpoint support, the cache-on CuTe and Cake routes each scored 92 / 1,319 (6.9750%). The repaired Cake repeat is within 4 questions (0.3033 percentage points) of the matched CuTe run and is consistent with the prior cache-off Cake result of 762 / 1,319 (57.7710%). Server state confirms `disable_radix_cache=False`, `uses_mamba_radix_cache=True`, and the unified Mamba cache pool; there is no Cake replay or fallback path. ## Performance Three-run medians after warmup and cache flush, fixed token counts; every reported Cake row is faster: | Baseline | Workload | Baseline | Cake | Speedup | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Existing `flashinfer` | TTFT, input 4096 / output 1 / concurrency 1 | 50.717 ms | 37.159 ms | 1.3648x | | Existing `flashinfer` | Total throughput, input 2048 / output 8 / concurrency 16 | 84,140.9 tok/s | 126,098.0 tok/s | 1.4987x | | Original `flashinfer_ssd` | TTFT, input 4096 / output 1 / concurrency 1 | 40.640 ms | 37.159 ms | 1.0937x | | Original `flashinfer_ssd` | Total throughput, input 2048 / output 8 / concurrency 16 | 121,311.7 tok/s | 126,098.0 tok/s | 1.0395x | The new routes remain opt-in because the established production route still has the highest matched-run task accuracy. This PR restores radix-cache safety; it does not change the default backend. Depends on https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4576 and is tracked by https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254.
