signals.title: [Responses] Fix multimodal Kimi-K3 /v1/responses returning 400 "texts cannot be empty"
signals.text: …mpty' <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation A `/v1/responses` request against a **multimodal Kimi-K3** deployment fails immediately: ```json {"error":{"message":"texts cannot be empty and tokenizer must be initialized","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":400}} ``` The equivalent /v1/chat/completions request with the same messages and tools works, so the bug is specific to the /v1/responses path for multimodal Kimi-K3. ## Why The kimi_k3 custom encoder produces a usable prompt_ids (via apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, ...)) but leaves prompt == "" — the only prompt = decode(prompt_ids) assignment lives in the prompt_ids is None branch, which kimi_k3 never enters. OpenAIServingResponses._make_request forwarded that empty prompt as text on the multimodal branch, producing GenerateReqInput(text=""). In TokenizerManager.generate_request, input_ids is None and input_text is empty, so control reaches _tokenize_texts(""), which raises the error above. serving_chat._convert_to_internal_request already special-cases this (elif is_multimodal and self.chat_encoding_spec == "kimi_k3": prompt_kwargs = {"input_ids": ...}); the responses path was missing the same guard. A text-only Kimi-K3 deployment (is_multimodal == False) takes the else branch and uses prompt_ids, so it is unaffected — which is why the bug only surfaces for multimodal Kimi-K3. Fixes #35460 ## Modifications - python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py: - test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py: add ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel or model-forward change; this only fixes which prompt field the responses path hands to the engine. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32231404454](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231404454)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32231403957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231403957)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(cake_vsa): add Cake Stage-2 backend for FastWan VSA
signals.text: ## Motivation FastWan's video sparse attention currently runs Stage 2 through the `vsa` package only. FlashInfer [#4593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4593) adds a Cake source backend that consumes FastWan's direct per-head top-k metadata on SM100/SM103. This PR makes that backend available as an explicit SGLang opt-in while preserving `vsa` as the default. This is a video-diffusion workload, not an LLM reasoning workload, so GSM8K is not applicable. Validation uses [`FastVideo/FastWan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastWan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers) and the VBench `subject_consistency` prompt `a person swimming in ocean`. ## Modifications - add `stage2_backend` (`vsa` or `cake`) and optional zero-based `cake_step_indices` to the existing VSA backend configuration - preserve the compressed-attention branch and pass its direct per-head `torch.topk` metadata to FlashInfer - sort selected KV block ids to preserve native VSA's traversal and BF16 accumulation order - cache the Cake wrapper and fixed `q2k_num` metadata per transformer layer - fail closed for unsupported devices, dtypes, batches, and head dimensions; selected Cake steps never silently fall back - expose the live generation duration while the generation timer context is active The validated FastWan configuration is: ```json {"VSA_sparsity": 0.8, "stage2_backend": "cake", "cake_step_indices": [1, 2]} ``` ## Accuracy NVIDIA B300, BF16, seed 42, 61 frames at 480x832, three denoising steps, guidance scale 3.0, and VSA sparsity 0.8. Applying Cake to all three denoising steps missed the conservative per-frame SSIM gate (`0.914666 < 0.92`). A four-route accuracy sweep isolated the first step, and the explicit `[1, 2]` route passed every frame without relaxing any threshold. | Check | Cake step indices `[1, 2]` | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | Frames passing all gates | 61/61 | 61/61 | | Minimum per-frame PSNR | 35.466198 dB | >= 24 dB | | Minimum per-frame SSIM | 0.978827 | >= 0.92 | | Maximum per-frame MAE | 1.635058 | <= 10 | | Final latent cosine similarity | 0.999255 | reported | | Final latent MAE | 0.018273 | reported | | Baseline repeat max error | 0 | deterministic | | Cake repeat max error | 0 | deterministic | The real-shape backend smoke also passed BF16 `atol=rtol=1e-2` with maximum absolute error `0.0009765625`, one observed Cake route, and zero generic device, host, or floating-point workspace bytes. ## Performance The full-model test alternates both `vsa, cake, cake, vsa` and `cake, vsa, vsa, cake`. Each block has one warmup and five measured requests, for 20 measured requests per backend. Both order-specific ratios are above `1.0x`; the table reports the geometric mean of the two sequence medians. No fixed overhead is added or subtracted. | FastWan 61x480x832 boundary | Native `vsa==0.0.4` | Cake `[1, 2]` | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Synchronized client generation | 1.478475 s | 1.470300 s | **1.005560x** | | Inference worker before output transport | 1225.263790 ms | 1220.807151 ms | **1.003651x** | The client boundary covers request dispatch through the synchronized response, including 61-frame materialization and transport. The worker boundary ends after model forward and before output transport; it is included to isolate the inference path from frame-return overhead. The narrower public-wrapper replay uses cold-L2 CUPTI timing and includes SGLang tiling/untile, compressed attention, dynamic top-k, Stage 2, gate fusion, and the FlashInfer wrapper call. | Near-E2E VSA workload | Native `vsa==0.0.4` | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Model-card 61x448x832, S=23,296 | 3.906334 ms | 3.799102 ms | **1.028226x** | | SGLang default 61x480x832, real/padded S=24,960/26,624 | 4.516563 ms | 4.393202 ms | **1.028080x** | ## Validation - `ruff format --check`: 4 files formatted - focused unit tests: 7 passed - real B300 FastWan shape smoke: correctness, strict Cake route, and zero generic workspaces passed - full FastWan ABBA/BAAB correctness and performance crossover: passed Depends on https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4593 and is tracked by https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32232671225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232671225)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32232670929](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232670929)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix dummy initialization of inverse weight scales
signals.text: ## Summary - Initialize floating-point `weight_scale_inv` tensors to the neutral value `1.0` when loading dummy weights. - Preserve randomized dummy initialization for regular floating-point weights. ## Problem The dummy loader randomized every floating-point tensor into a small interval around zero. Inverse weight scales must be positive, and DeepGEMM paths that convert them to UE8M0 additionally require power-of-two inputs. DSV4 FP4 expert and FP8 attention post-load processing therefore aborted in `transform_sf_into_required_layout` before the server could start. This complements #33500, which fixed serialized MXFP4 scale placeholders stored as raw integer UE8M0 bytes. The affected DSV4 paths here expose floating-point inverse scales, so the integer-placeholder fix does not cover them. ## Fix Use `1.0` for floating-point state-dict entries whose names end in `weight_scale_inv`. It is a neutral, valid inverse scale for the post-load transforms. Real checkpoint loading is unchanged. ## Validation - Full pre-commit suite passed. - A TP4 DSV4 DSpark dummy startup completed target and draft weight loading and post-processing without the DeepGEMM scale-layout assertion. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32232930988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232930988)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32232930566](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232930566)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [DSV4] unified_kv: isolate C4 compress state per request
signals.text: ## Motivation On the `unified_kv` path the DSV4 **C4 compress state** is addressed through the full→SWA mapping: ``` state_loc = (swa_loc // swa_page_size) * c4_ring_size + swa_loc % c4_ring_size ``` `swa_loc` is derived from `req_to_token`, so **two requests sharing a radix prefix resolve the same prefix positions to the same SWA slot, and therefore to the same C4 state row**. The C4 overlap state is per-request — it carries that request's running compress window — so this aliases one request's state onto another's. The same hazard exists within a single request across a slot reuse: a freshly allocated `req_pool_idx` inherits whatever the previous occupant left in its ring rows. C128 already avoids this by addressing state request-scoped. This PR gives C4 the same contract: ``` state_loc = req_pool_idx * c4_ring_size + position % c4_ring_size ``` a pure function of `(req slot, logical position)`, which cannot alias across requests. > **Stacked on #30315 and #31040.** The first 8 files in this diff belong to those two PRs; this PR's own change is the last 12 files (`+332/-43`, commit `fix(dsv4): isolate unified C4 compress state per request`). It has to be stacked: it rewrites `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`, which #30315 introduces. Will rebase onto `main` once those merge. > > To review this PR alone: > ``` > git diff yuttian1/dsv4-unified-kv-swa-ring...yuttian1/dsv4-unified-c4-per-request-ring > ``` ## Modifications Everything is gated on `compress_ratio == 4 and token_to_kv_pool._unified_kv`. **C128 and the non-unified (full→SWA) C4 path are untouched.** **Sizing and lifecycle** - **`pool_configurator.py`** — `_unified_c4_state_pool_size` becomes exactly `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size`, replacing the page-derived upper bound that the old addressing needed. - **`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`** — new `clear_c4_req_states(req_pool_indices)`, which resets the ring rows of the given slots (kv half → `0`, score half → `-inf`). Also documents why C4 needs no MTP-reject cleanup. - **`allocation.py`, `disaggregation/decode.py`** — call `clear_c4_req_states` for **newly allocated slots only**. A chunked continuation reuses its slot and must keep the state its previous chunk captured, so `newly_allocated` is captured *before* `alloc`. **Addressing** - **`compressor.py`, `compressor_v2.py`** — compute `use_req_ring` and thread it into the plan kwargs. - **`compress_hip.py`** — four `self.ratio == 128` guards in `CompressorHip.compress_extend_paged` / `compress_decode_paged` become `ratio == 128 or (ratio == 4 and _unified_kv)`, taking the existing `translate_from_req_position_to_state_loc` branch. - **`kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/c_plan.cuh`** — `compute_c128_loc` → `compute_req_ring_loc`, now also taken under `use_req_ring` (with `RuntimeCheck(!use_req_ring || compress_ratio == 4)`). Under `use_req_ring` the ring row is `position % ring_size`, so the extra "tail of the SWA page" write the overlap path emitted for full→SWA addressing is dropped. - **`kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/attn.py`, `compress.py`** — plumb `use_req_ring` through the Triton kernel and the plan entry points (XPU signatures unchanged). ## Accuracy Tests This is a correctness fix, not a numerics change: the compressed state values are identical, only the row they live in changes. Two tests pin the new address contract. **New — `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py`** (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): - pool size is the exact request-ring product; - `clear_c4_req_states` resets only the selected rings and leaves C128 alone; - `alloc_req_slots` clears new slots but **not** reused ones. **Extended — `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py`**: new `test_unified_request_ring_plans_ignore_full_to_state` runs the real prefill and decode plan kernels with a deliberately degenerate `full_to_state`, and asserts the emitted read pages / write locs are exactly `req_pool_idx * ring_size + position % ring_size`, and that two requests never land on the same row. Both run green on ROCm (MI355X): ``` test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py 3 passed test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py 35 passed ``` Plus the neighbouring suites, unchanged: ``` test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py, test_pool_configurator.py, test_hisparse_pool_configurator.py, test_prefill_adder.py -> 66 passed, 22 subtests passed ``` No end-to-end serving accuracy run is attached yet — the `unified_kv` path needs DeepSeek-V4-Pro on ROCm, which upstream CI cannot reach. Happy to attach one if a reviewer wants it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected throughput impact: the same number of state rows is written, and `_unified_c4_state_pool_size` gets *smaller* (exact product instead of a page-derived upper bound), so the C4 pool allocation shrinks slightly. ## Notes for reviewers This is the upstream port of an internal fix. Four hunks from the internal version are **intentionally omitted** because they depend on a SWA-HiCache offload line that is not upstream (`_swa_offload_page_stride`, `_restore_state_windows`, `capture_c4_state_windows_unified`): the `swa_component.py` and `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` changes, and the two HiCache capture helpers in `compress_hip.py`. When that line lands, the HiCache-side C4 restore will need a follow-up to use the same request-scoped address contract. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269391591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269391591)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269391311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269391311)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Support quantized target lm_head in the DFlash2 selector
signals.text: ## Motivation DFlash2's selector matmuls draft hiddens against the target `lm_head.weight` directly, so quantized targets (ModelOpt NVFP4, compressed-tensors FP8) fail with `RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head` — on 32GB GPUs those checkpoints are the only way to serve Qwen3.8-27B. #34859 fixed the same problem for DSpark via `quant_method.apply`; this does the same for the DFlash2 selector. Overlaps #35462 (@ryou315, credited as co-author): this PR additionally keeps the quantized logits contiguous by masking the padded tail instead of cropping — a padded local vocab crop otherwise fails flashinfer's radix top-k `CHECK_INPUT` at TP=1 and can hang TP>1, since only the rank holding the tail errors while its peers enter the all-gather. Follow-ups split out of this PR so each stays reviewable on its own: #35580 (degenerate-config guard), #35581 (optional cleanup). ## Modifications - `models/dflash.py`: `_project_candidate_logits` projects draft hiddens through the target head, restricted to the org vocab. When `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` admits the head it runs `quant_method.apply` over the padded local vocab and masks the padded tail to `-inf` (a packed weight cannot be row-sliced like the dense path; masking keeps the logits contiguous with no copy, and does nothing when the vocab is unpadded). Both TP branches call it; their control flow is unchanged. - `speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py` `_maybe_build_draft_sampler`: the selector branch accepts a dense head or one the quant gate admits, so quantized and dense heads take the same graph-folded `_SelectorDraftSampler` path (the captured kernel is the one the target's own logits path already runs under CUDA graphs). The dense-only screen still guards the non-selector static-matmul sampler. ## Accuracy Tests RTX 5090, target `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (NVFP4-packed head), draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, greedy: both arms are byte-deterministic across fresh server boots (8/8 prompts each); spec vs target-only outputs fork only at near-tie tokens and 22/28 completed chains reach the same final answer — a stable numerics offset, not corruption. `sgl-eval run gsm8k` 200q: 95.5% with spec vs 98.0% target-only. `test_dflash_logits.py`: 7/7 pass. The quant-path test asserts `apply()` runs on the packed weight, dominant padded garbage never reaches the candidates, and the logits handed to top-k are contiguous with `sorted`/`deterministic` set — the fake quant method returns a deliberately strided view and the top-k stub mirrors flashinfer's call contract, so an unmaterialized output fails the way the real kernel would. The TP test pins the per-shard org-vocab restriction, the global id offset, and the fp32 cast before the all-gather. A worker test pins the pre-capture screen: a gate-passing packed head is admitted to the folded selector sampler and attached before construction, an unsupported one stays eager. All mutation-verified: dropping the mask, the `.contiguous()`, the top-k flags, the id offset, the fp32 cast, or the worker admission each turns a test red. The dense-rejection test is kept for the negative branch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No effect on dense-head targets (same matmul, same screen outcome). Quantized targets go from refusing to serve to serving. Same cell (RTX 5090, fp8 KV, concurrency 1): - `sglang.benchmark.serving` random 8192/1024: TTFT 746.9 ms, median TPOT 7.10 ms, 129.5 output tok/s, accept 3.01 (DSPARK on the same cell: 7.73 ms, 116.5 tok/s, accept 2.59). - GSM8K 200q: 186.5 output tok/s vs 66.6 target-only, accept length 4.85. - Folded vs eager selector sampler isolated on 1024/1024: 5.58 vs 5.61 ms median TPOT with bit-identical accept lengths — the worker change is path consistency, and the two samplers demonstrably compute the same candidates. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Improve K3 dspark draft attn kernel perf
signals.text: ## Motivation With DSpark on Kimi-K3, every step runs 5 draft attn layers (qwen-style, non-causal). Draft attn dominates their cost. In a trace study, the 5 draft layers took 2.368 ms, of which the 5 attn kernels alone accounted for 1.244 ms (>50%). The reason is that this falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`. This generic extend kernel is a poor fit for a shared-KV shape. > Note that draft attn is a common path. `--attention-backend` only selects the target-verify kernel. `aiter` is not among the draft worker's supported backends, so on ROCm the draft always falls back to `triton`. Both `--attention-backend triton` and `aiter` therefore reach the kernel this PR changes. ## Modifications Route DSpark draft attn to `verify_shared_kv`, and extend that kernel to cover the two cases it previously rejected. - **Non-causal situation**: The prefix loop never applies a causal mask, so only modify the stage-2 kernel. - **`h_kv > 1`**: Both stages add a KV-head offset (`head // kv_group_num * stride_h`). A `HAS_KV_HEADS` constexpr keeps the single-KV-head (MLA/MQA) path free of that arithmetic, so the existing Kimi-K3 target-verify path compiles exactly as before. Also adds a tuning entry for `head_dim=64` (`BLOCK_N=256`, 4 warps) and `is_dspark_draft()` in `model_config.py` for the gate. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 1319: ``` 100%|███████████| 1319/1319 [02:00<00:00, 10.98it/s] Accuracy: 0.955 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 120.085 s Output throughput: 1108.066 token/s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested with docker image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`. Since draft attn is a common code path and this change is independent of other work, the numbers are measured directly on `main`, with no other non-merged PRs applied. Perf (isl=8k/16k/32k, cc=4, 32): - On cc=4, ITL improves by 4-12% and TTT by 2-6%. - On cc=32, ITL improves by 1-5% and TTT by 1-2%. The gain grows with input length, from 8k to 32k, in both cases. signals.title: fix(cache): deduplicate shared SWA slots before free
signals.text: ## Problem `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` allows several full-cache locations to reference the same sliding-window slot. `free_swa()` expands the full locations and forwards every mapped value to the underlying allocator without deduplication. When a shared slot appears more than once, it is returned to the free pool repeatedly. The available count exceeds the pool capacity and hybrid-model generation aborts at the allocator invariant: ```text assert self.swa_attn_allocator.available_size() <= self.swa_attn_allocator.size ``` This reproduced on 4x MI350X with Inkling-Small LoRA after 32/256 responses. ## Fix Deduplicate the positive mapped SWA indices before calling the non-idempotent child allocator. Mapping entries are still cleared for every full location. ## Validation - [x] Added a focused regression where two full locations share one SWA slot; one free restores exactly the configured capacity. - [x] Full `test_swa_unittest.py`: 12 passed, 15 subtests passed. - [x] Pre-commit passed on both changed files. - [x] 4x MI350X Inkling-Small native LoRA completed two rollouts and four train steps when combined with the Miles ROCm launcher/API fallbacks; Ray job succeeded. - [ ] Maintainer-triggered CUDA CI. - [ ] Maintainer-triggered AMD CI. This remains draft pending owner review and independent CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32237348266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237348266)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32237347959](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237347959)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(moe): support Llama4 NVFP4 router input weights on SM120
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34192. Llama 4 constructs its MoE layers with `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. For ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120/SM121, SGLang selects the FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner, which previously rejected this configuration during server warmup. For top-1 routing, the required semantics can be implemented exactly by multiplying each token's hidden states by its router weight before activation quantization and passing unit final scales to CUTLASS. This follows the existing pattern in the AITER MoE runner. The fix remains intentionally restricted to top-1 routing. With top-k greater than one, each selected expert would require a differently scaled copy of the input. ## Modifications - Add top-1 router-weight pre-scaling to the common FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE execution path. - Replace the kernel's output-side router scaling with float32 unit `token_final_scales` when pre-scaling is active. - Normalize all `token_final_scales` passed through this CUTLASS path to float32, as required by the binding. - Remove the ModelOpt NVFP4 and FlashInfer CUTLASS assertions that rejected `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. - Preserve explicit rejection for: - top-k greater than one; - activations already quantized before dispatch, including the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 all-gather path. - Add focused CPU unit tests covering: - top-1 activation pre-scaling; - float32 unit final scales; - preservation of expert IDs; - top-k greater than one rejection; - pre-quantized dispatch rejection. The normal `apply_router_weight_on_input=False` path is unchanged apart from enforcing the CUTLASS binding's float32 scale requirement. ## Accuracy Tests Added: ```text test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py ``` The tests compare the transformed hidden states and final scales against the expected top-1 formulation and verify that unsupported configurations fail explicitly. Local validation: ```text python -m py_compile \ python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py \ python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py \ test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py ``` Result: passed. All commit-time pre-commit checks passed, including Python AST validation, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, and registered-test validation. The focused pytest test could not be executed in the local development environment because PyTorch is not installed. No real-checkpoint accuracy test was run for this checkout. The equivalent patch and its SM120/SM121 validation evidence are documented in #34192. That validation used dummy weights for end-to-end liveness, so it is not claimed as a model-accuracy result. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed test or profiling was run for this checkout. The equivalent patch validation documented in #34192 completed both SM120 scenarios without errors and did not show a decode throughput regression. Those results used dummy weights and a separate validated build, so they are included only as prior evidence, not as performance results for this commit. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [Deepseek-V4] Enable shared-experts fusion on the flashinfer_mxfp4 (trtllm-gen) MoE path
signals.text: ## Summary Enable shared-experts fusion for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the `flashinfer_mxfp4` (trtllm-gen) path: the shared expert is routed as expert slot 256 through the same MoE kernel, so the whole MoE runs on a single stream instead of a separate FP8 MLP on an alternate stream (~4 fewer kernel launches + 2 fewer stream syncs per layer). The machinery already existed (#27349); this PR enables and validates it. Also adds a guard rejecting fusion under EP without per-rank shared slots, which would silently compute wrong results. ## Scope - `deepseek_v4.py`: EP guard in the fusion gate (11 lines). - New CPU unit test for the load-time FP8→MXFP4 shared-expert requant (byte-level packing/scale contract). - Recipes: add `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` to the b200/b300/gb200/gb300 flash-official fp4 low-latency entries. ## Testing - Kernel: verified out-of-tree on GB200 with a standalone test at the fused shape (257 experts / top-k 7, every token hits the shared slot), 12/12 vs a dequantized torch reference; no flashinfer change needed. Test available on request. - Unit: `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_shared_expert_requant.py`. - Profiler: with fusion on, the shared-expert kernels disappear and the MoE runs on a single stream. ## Results GB200 tp4, only variable is the fusion flag. signals.text: ## Summary - gracefully terminate metrics test servers before falling back to a process-tree kill - wait for the fallback kill to reap remaining processes ## Root cause The metrics test used the fire-and-forget `kill_process_tree(process.pid)` cleanup path. signals.title: [Diffusion] Fix multi-group layerwise offload startup memory
signals.text: ## Summary - initialize every non-MPS layer group before moving non-layer parameters to the accelerator - release managed groups in descending parameter-byte order during initialization while preserving declared manager order for runtime behavior - preserve each group’s independent prefetch and forward-hook lifecycle - add regression coverage at the real `configure_layerwise_offload` boundary ## Motivation Models can expose multiple entries in `layer_names`. Previously, each manager moved the entire model immediately after replacing only its own layer group. Earlier managers therefore treated later groups as non-layer parameters and transiently moved them to the accelerator, making startup peak memory depend on `layer_names` ordering. The coordinated initialization now replaces all managed groups first, moves the actual non-layer parameters once, and only then finalizes per-group prefetch and hooks. Processing the largest groups first also releases the most device memory earliest when checkpoint loading has already placed weights on the accelerator. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32245883433](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32245883433)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32245883281](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32245883281)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix inflated row pitch when a CP-v2 interleave shard has a single row
signals.text: ## Motivation `InterleaveCPStrategy._interleave_shard` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/cp/interleave.py` ends with: ```python return input_.view(-1, cp_size, *input_.shape[1:])[:, cp_rank].contiguous() ``` The view is strided: `stride(0) == cp_size * row_numel`. The `.contiguous()` is meant to tighten that back down, but it does not always do so. When a chunk has exactly `cp_size` tokens, each rank's shard is a **single row**. A size-1 outer dimension imposes no contiguity constraint, so `is_contiguous()` is already `True` whatever `stride(0)` happens to be, `.contiguous()` becomes a no-op, and the shard silently keeps the `cp_size`-inflated row pitch. Any kernel that takes its row pitch from `stride(0)` rather than from the shape then walks `cp_size` times the intended distance per row and reads past the end of the tensor, which shows up as a GPU memory-access fault. Reproduced on DeepSeek-V4 geometry (`row_numel = 28672`, `cp_size = 8`): | tokens | rank | `stride(0)` before | `stride(0)` after | `is_contiguous()` before | |---|---|---|---|---| | 8 (`== cp_size`, single row) | 0 / 3 / 7 | **229376** | **28672** | `True` | | 32 (`== 4 * cp_size`, multi-row) | 0 / 3 / 7 | 28672 | 28672 | `True` | i.e. the pitch is inflated exactly 8x in the single-row case, while `is_contiguous()` reports `True` throughout. In the multi-row case the existing `.contiguous()` already behaves correctly, so only the single-row case changes. ### Relationship to #34142 This is a **byte-identical duplicate** of the line that #34142 ("Fix inflated row pitch when a CP round-robin shard has a single row") fixes in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/utils.py::dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data`. #34142 does not touch `interleave.py`, so this second location remains affected after it lands. This PR applies the same fix and the same explanatory comment to the `interleave.py` copy, so the two stay consistent. ### Relationship to #34200 Follow-up to #34200 ("[AMD] Port CP V2 to the DeepSeek-V4 HIP backend"). The `interleave.py` copy lives in the CP-v2 code path, which is gated behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` (default `False`) and is therefore dormant on `main` today. #34200's HIP CP-v2 work is what exercises it, which is how this was found. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/cp/interleave.py` — in `_interleave_shard`, compare the shard's row pitch against the parent's explicitly and copy only when they differ: ```python shard = input_.view(-1, cp_size, *input_.shape[1:])[:, cp_rank] if shard.stride(0) != input_.stride(0): shard = shard.clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format) return shard ``` Comparing pitches makes the copy happen exactly when the shard really is strided — and **not at all when `cp_size == 1`**, where the "shard" is the whole tensor and stays a view (verified by `data_ptr()` identity). **Values are bit-identical; only the memory layout changes.** `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py` — two regression cases: - `test_interleave_shard_row_pitch_is_not_inflated`: for `tokens == cp_size` and `tokens == 4 * cp_size`, over every rank, asserts the shard's `stride(0)` equals the parent's and that the values still equal `x[rank::cp_size]`. - `test_interleave_shard_does_not_copy_for_cp_size_one`: asserts `cp_size == 1` stays a view. ## Accuracy Tests No accuracy impact — the change is layout-only and values are bit-identical, verified elementwise against both the previous implementation and `x[rank::cp_size]` for every rank in both the single-row and multi-row cases. The new tests were confirmed to **fail on the pre-fix source** and pass with it, on exactly the four single-row subtests (`AssertionError: 32 != 8`, the scaled-down `cp_size = 4`, `row_numel = 8` analogue of 229376 vs 28672); the multi-row subtests pass either way, confirming the fix is scoped to the single-row case. Full file, post-fix: ``` $ python -m pytest test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py -q 25 passed, 26 subtests passed in 27.47s ``` (CPU-only unit test, already registered via `register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`.) ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference-speed impact. The added `clone` replaces a `.contiguous()` copy that was already intended to happen; in the multi-row case the copy is unchanged, in the single-row case it copies a single row, and for `cp_size == 1` the fix removes a copy that the old code could perform. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32245153262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32245153262)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32245153062](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32245153062)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Forward unknown InternLM tools when configured
signals.text: ## Motivation `InternlmDetector` checks `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS` before deciding whether to keep an unknown tool call, but the forwarding path still indexes `tool_indices[name]`. When forwarding is enabled, an unknown name therefore raises `KeyError`; the outer error handler then returns the original tagged payload as normal text and drops the call. The same failure affects one-shot and streaming parsing. ## Modifications - Use the established `-1` tool index for opted-in unknown InternLM tool calls, matching `BaseFormatDetector.parse_base_json`. - Add CPU regressions for both one-shot and streaming parsing. The existing default behavior that drops unknown tools remains covered and unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects function-call parsing when unknown-tool forwarding is explicitly enabled. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change replaces a dictionary index with `dict.get` in an existing parsing branch. ## Tests - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/function_call`: 466 passed, 14 subtests passed - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/function_call/test_unknown_tool_name.py`: 4 passed - `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Documentation is not needed for this internal correctness fix. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32318962930](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318962930)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32318962795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318962795)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [mem_cache] SWA radix cache: evict branch tail sliding window last
signals.text: ## Motivation `SWARadixCache.evict()` walks the SWA LRU list without any notion of where a branch ends, so it can tombstone (or delete) a node that sits inside the last `sliding_window_size` tokens of a branch. Because `_match_prefix_helper` can only stop at a node that has `sliding_window_size` **consecutive non-tombstone** tokens in front of it (the `match_len_since_tombstone` check), tombstoning a single node inside that trailing window makes the *entire* branch unmatchable: the reusable prefix collapses from tens of thousands of tokens to 0, while the branch's full KV stays allocated in the full pool until full-side LRU reclaims it. This is a cliff, not a gradual degradation — the tail window is the only part of a branch whose SWA KV is load-bearing for reuse. Idle branches are hit first. `_match_post_processor` uses `reset_node_and_parents_mru`, which makes root-side nodes least-recently-used *within* a branch, but ordering *across* branches is still by last access time. A request that is parked in a tool call has its whole branch older than any active branch, so its tail nodes are evicted before the root-side nodes of busy branches — the opposite of what we want. Impact: agentic / multi-turn tool-calling workloads on SWA models (e.g. window 128) with a small SWA pool re-prefill their whole history when they come back from a tool call, even though (a) their full KV is still cached and (b) decode only needs the last `sliding_window_size` SWA tokens. Reproduction sketch (window = 4, two branches sharing an 8-token prefix): ``` shared(8) -> tail1(4) # branch 1, parked in a tool call shared(8) -> other(8) # branch 2, just matched ``` `evict(swa_num_tokens=4)` picks `tail1` (the LRU node) and deletes it, so `match_prefix(branch1)` can no longer return the branch. Tombstoning the 8-token `shared` internal node instead frees 2x more SWA tokens *and* keeps branch 1 fully matchable, because 4 (== window) non-tombstone tokens still follow the tombstone. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/swa_radix_cache.py`: - The SWA eviction loop now skips a candidate whose nearest branch end is less than one page-aligned window away, and retries those nodes only once no other candidate is left. This is a **deprioritization, not a reservation** — the eviction target is still met when the SWA pool is genuinely exhausted, and `swa_evictable_size_` accounting plus the scheduler contract are unchanged, so there is no new OOM / retract risk. - New `_is_swa_branch_tail()` computes the shortest token distance from a candidate down to the nearest branch end, where a branch end is a leaf **or** the node right before an existing tombstone (both are valid stop points for `_match_prefix_helper`). The walk is pruned by the window size, so it visits at most the tail of the branch rather than the whole subtree, and it is iterative so a long chunked-prefill chain cannot exhaust the recursion limit. - New `_swa_tail_size()` factors out the `ceil(window / page) * page` formula that `_maybe_split_leaf_for_swa_lock()` already used, so both paths agree on page alignment. Cost of the deprioritized set is `#branch_ends * sliding_window_size` (128 tokens per branch for a 128-token window), negligible against a few hundred K SWA slots. ### Scope: legacy `SWARadixCache` only `unified_cache/components/swa_component.py` has a parallel SWA eviction walk with the same shape — `_evict_device_next_node()` scans the SWA LRU from the tail via `get_lru_no_lock()` / `get_prev_no_lock()`, tombstones internal nodes inline and cascade-deletes leaves (see `unified_cache/components/README.md`) — so it has the same blind spot. This PR intentionally changes only the legacy `SWARadixCache` to keep the diff reviewable: the unified walk is cursor-based (`cursor_begin` / `cursor_next`, plus the `enable_session_radix_cache` path), so skipping a candidate there also needs cursor-recovery semantics rather than the plain `get_prev_no_lock` step used here. Happy to port it in a follow-up, or to fold it into this PR if maintainers would rather land both paths together — please say which you prefer. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — this only changes which cache entry is evicted first, not any model output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not included yet. I do not have a GPU environment attached right now, so the SWA unit tests have not been executed and I have no workload numbers to report. Both are being added to this PR: - unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_unittest.py` covering (1) the branch tail surviving and the prefix staying fully reusable, (2) the previous behavior as a regression baseline, (3) the fallback pass still meeting the eviction target when only tails remain, and (4) `page_size` equal to, below and above the window; - cache hit rate / TTFT / SWA eviction counts for a tool-calling workload under SWA pool pressure. Review feedback on the approach in the meantime is very welcome — in particular whether maintainers would prefer this gated behind a `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_*` env flag (as with `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_SPLIT_LEAF_ON_INSERT`) rather than being on by default. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32258596774](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258596774)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32258594151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258594151)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Add Spark3 Model
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds native support for the Spark 3 model architecture in SGLang. The implementation introduces the Spark 3 configuration and causal language model, including sliding-window and full attention, head-wise attention output gating, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and checkpoint weight loading. ## Changes | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/spark3.py` | Adds `Spark3Config`, including model dimensions, attention layout, sliding-window configuration, layer types, RoPE parameters, and tied word embeddings. | | `python/sglang/srt/models/spark3.py` | Implements `Spark3ForCausalLM`, including grouped-query attention, interleaved sliding/full attention, head-wise output gating, gated MLP, parallelism support, split prefill, and checkpoint weight loading. | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` | Exports `Spark3Config` through the SGLang configuration package. | | `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py` | Registers `Spark3Config` in SGLang's Hugging Face configuration registry. | ## Key Technical Details 1. Efficient Architecture：The models adopt an efficiency-oriented architecture with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and other structural optimizations, improving the balance between model quality, memory usage, and inference efficiency. 2. Native 1M Context：Both the 1.7B and 4B models natively support up to 1 million tokens of context, enabling long-document understanding, repository-level coding, and long-horizon agent tasks. 3. Strong Coding & Agent Capabilities：The models deliver leading coding and agent performance among models of comparable size, with strong capabilities in code generation, tool use, multi-step execution, and long-context reasoning. 4. Faster Inference：Through model architecture and inference-stack optimizations, the models achieve higher inference efficiency and throughput than many comparable-size models, especially in long-context scenarios. 5. Strong K–12 and Gaokao Performance：The models achieve leading K–12 question-answering performance at comparable parameter scales, with particularly strong results on challenging Chinese Gaokao-style tasks. 6. Advanced Post-Training：The release applies a comprehensive post-training recipe based on Scaled Reinforcement Learning and MOPD, improving reasoning, coding, instruction following, agentic capabilities, and alignment. 7. Controllable Thinking Budget：The models support configurable reasoning levels — none, low, medium, and high — allowing applications to dynamically trade off reasoning quality, latency, and inference cost. 8. 200+ Languages：Multilingual coverage has been expanded to more than 200 languages, supporting broad cross-lingual understanding, generation, translation, and localized applications. ## Performance We run MMLU-Pro on our internal OAI-server compatible benchmarking suite and the scores match the declared performance. Running on 1xH200 SXM5 ```bash ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max request concurrency: not set Successful requests: 500 Benchmark duration (s): 4.48 Total input tokens: 756489 Total input text tokens: 756489 Total generated tokens: 64000 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 63997 Request throughput (req/s): 111.52 Input token throughput (tok/s): 168733.90 Output token throughput (tok/s): 14275.12 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 27064.00 Peak concurrent requests: 500 Total token throughput (tok/s): 183009.02 Concurrency: 463.05 ----------------End‑to‑End Latency---------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 4152.05 Median E2E Latency (ms): 4387.30 P90 E2E Latency (ms): 4391.62 P95 E2E Latency (ms): 4392.38 P99 E2E Latency (ms): 4393.38 ----------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 2348.20 Median TTFT (ms): 2377.59 P90 TTFT (ms): 2386.19 P95 TTFT (ms): 2387.18 P99 TTFT (ms): 2388.39 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)----- Mean TPOT (ms): 14.20 Median TPOT (ms): 15.81 P90 TPOT (ms): 15.85 P95 TPOT (ms): 15.86 P99 TPOT (ms): 15.87 ----------------Inter‑Token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 14.20 Median ITL (ms): 12.72 P90 ITL (ms): 16.52 P95 ITL (ms): 17.51 P99 ITL (ms): 29.32 Max ITL (ms): 307.79 ================================================== ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324473737](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324473737)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324473553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324473553)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(sgl-kernel): route below-SM90 GPUs to sm90 build in load_utils
signals.text: ## Problem `_load_architecture_specific_ops()` routes only `compute_capability == 90` to the `sm90/` directory; every other GPU falls into the `sm100/` branch. However, the sm90 artifact is the compatibility build: `ENABLE_BELOW_SM90` (default ON on x86_64) appends `compute_80`/`compute_89` gencode (and `compute_87` on aarch64) to the shared `SGL_KERNEL_CUDA_FLAGS` used by `common_ops_sm90_build` (see `python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt`). Below-SM90 GPUs (sm_80/86/87/89, e.g. L40S / RTX 4090) are therefore sent to the wrong directory and fail to `import sgl_kernel` whenever the sm100 artifact does not carry below-SM90 gencode — reproduced on an sm_89 GPU with CUDA 12.1 and sglang-kernel 0.4.5, where import failed until cc=89 was routed to the sm90 directory. This currently happens to work on recent x86_64 wheels only because both builds share the same flags and the sm100 artifact incidentally contains sm_89 cubins; any divergence of the two builds' flag sets (or a wheel built with `ENABLE_BELOW_SM90=OFF`) breaks below-SM90 users immediately. ## Fix Route every GPU with `compute_capability < 100` to the sm90 build. cc >= 100 and the no-GPU path are unchanged. `variant_name` now reports the actual cc instead of hardcoding "SM90". Note: sm_89 is **not** a subset of sm_90 (Ada 8.x vs Hopper 9.x) — this works because the sm90 artifact is compiled with below-SM90 gencode, not because sm90 cubins run on sm89. ## Test - `python -m py_compile` passes. - Verified on an sm_89 GPU: `import sgl_kernel` succeeds with cc=89 routed to the sm90 directory.

signals.title: [AMD] Split-KV verify on gfx942: CU-aware split cap, bidirectional draft blocks
signals.text: ## Motivation `verify_splitkv` was gated to gfx95 only. The kernel is arch-neutral Triton and gfx942 is where the serial-prefix walk in `extend_attention_fwd` hurts most: it walks the prefix under a `(bs, h_q, 1)` grid, so a per-TP-rank speculative draft shard leaves most of the device idle. Two further gaps kept it from serving the draft-side shapes it is fastest on: the flat `MAX_N_SPLITS = 16` was tuned at a base grid that already fills the device, and `_verify_combine_stage2` hard-coded causal masking inside the draft block, which ENCODER_ONLY draft layers (bidirectional) do not want. ## Modifications **Enable on gfx942** alongside gfx95. **CU-aware split cap.** The stage1 grid is `(bs, h_q, N_SPLITS)`, so `bs * h_q` fixes how many workgroups exist before splitting. When that underfills the device, raise the cap by the shortfall instead of leaving it flat — bounded at `HARD_MAX_N_SPLITS = 128`, and again by a scratch budget so a large `max_bs` cannot balloon the stage1 partials (`att_out`/`att_lse` are sized by `max_bs` for graph address stability, so `n_splits` multiplies a `max_bs`-sized allocation even when only `bs=1` is live). `choose_n_splits(avg_seqlen)` with no `base_programs` is unchanged, and the boost factor is 1 whenever the base grid already saturates, so **every previously tuned shape is bit-identical**. The CU count is a host-side property read, so this stays HIP-graph-capture safe. **Bidirectional draft blocks.** The intra-block mask becomes a stage2 constexpr (`INTRA_BLOCK_CAUSAL`) driven by the caller's `is_causal`. It keys `_VK_CACHE`, so the two specializations do not alias; `is_causal=True` is the default and is bit-identical to before. `can_handle` refused every non-causal call; the only thing the kernel genuinely cannot serve is an explicit `custom_mask`, so the check narrows to that. **`DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` routing.** It has the same `[tokens, H_Q, D]` ragged-extend shape as `TARGET_VERIFY`, so route it too. Dispatch still goes through `verify_fwd`, so on gfx95 the grouped-head kernel keeps first refusal and declines non-causal calls in its own `can_handle`, falling through to `extend_attention_fwd` exactly as before. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/attention/test_verify_splitkv.py`, extended and now registered for the gfx942 lane (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`) as well as MI35x: - parity vs `extend_attention_fwd(is_causal=False)` at `l_ext` 2 / 4 / 8; - the causal and bidirectional specializations must not alias in `_VK_CACHE`; - `can_handle`: non-causal without a mask is now accepted, non-causal **with** a mask still falls back (the causal + `custom_mask` case is unchanged — it is gated off in the backend by `topk == 1`, not here); - `choose_n_splits`: the legacy no-`base_programs` call bit-identical, a saturating base grid unchanged, an underfilled one raised within `[MAX, HARD_MAX]` and still a power of two. Verified on gfx942: **14/14**, max abs diff **9.8e-4** vs `extend_attention_fwd` on both the causal and the bidirectional path. The CU-aware cap resolves to 128 splits at `bs=1, h_q=8` and 32 at `bs=8, h_q=8`, and to the tuned 16 once the base grid saturates. Accuracy against an exact fp32 reference is unchanged; the two paths differ only in reduction order. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32254763616](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32254763616)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32254763161](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32254763161)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Enable chunked prefix KV on the aiter backend
signals.text: ## Motivation With a cached prefix, the aiter MHA extend path re-gathers and up-projects the entire prefix through `kv_b_proj` in one shot — `index_select` -> fp8->bf16 upcast -> `contiguous` -> `kv_b_proj` -> `cat(k, k_pe)` — which costs ~13.2 KiB per token per MLA layer. On Kimi-K3 at TP8 that is 5.0 GiB/layer at 400k context and 12.6 GiB/layer at 1M, against ~19.5 GiB free. It aborted the scheduler with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` three times in 45 minutes at 347k–411k context. `AttnForwardMethod.MHA_CHUNKED_KV` already bounds that to one chunk, but was unreachable: `maybe_disable_chunked_prefix_cache()` force-sets `disable_chunked_prefix_cache=True` for any backend absent from `CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_SUPPORTED_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, so `--disable-chunked-prefix-cache` was a silent no-op on ROCm. ## Modifications - **`server_args`**: add `aiter` to the supported-backend list. - **`attention_backend_handler`**: `handle_attention_aiter` returns `MHA_CHUNKED_KV` once the cached prefix passes `chunked_prefix_cache_threshold`. Below it, behaviour is unchanged (plain MHA), so this is additive — aiter's asm MLA extend has gqa/qseqlen gaps and is deliberately still not used for extend. - **`aiter_backend`**: `_forward_extend_mha_chunk()` honours `attn_attend_prefix_cache` (per-chunk indptr, non-causal against a chunk) and `mha_return_lse`, mirroring what the musa flashattention backend already does. aiter returns the softmax LSE heads-first `[num_heads, num_tokens]`, so it is transposed to the `[num_tokens, num_heads]` layout `merge_state` indexes. - **`forward_mha`**: `sgl_kernel` exports a `merge_state_v2` wrapper on ROCm but never registers the op, so the CUDA-gated import left the name undefined and the chunked path died with `NameError`. Fall back to `merge_state`, which already dispatches to the Triton kernel on AMD — the same alias the musa branch uses. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/test_aiter_mha_chunked_kv.py` asserts chunk + merge reproduces a single-shot attention over the whole context at Kimi-K3-at-TP8 shapes (12 heads, qk 192, v 128), including an uneven final chunk. It covers the three things that each have already been a bug: `merge_state` callable on ROCm, the LSE layout, and the per-slice causal flags (causal within the new tokens, NON-causal against a prefix chunk — getting this backwards produces plausible-but-wrong output, not a crash). Tolerance 5e-3 is the bf16 reassociation floor from splitting the KV stream. Registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Kimi-K3 at TP8, 937k-token cold prefill: | | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | free VRAM at peak | 0.02 GiB | 17.90 GiB | | transient | 19.3 GiB | 1.99 GiB | | `kv_b_proj` GEMM M | 394564 | 32768 | Peak becomes context-independent (237.86 GB at 400k vs 237.79 GB at 937k) for +1% prefill latency, which is the per-chunk LSE merges. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32254868228](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32254868228)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32254867908](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32254867908)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] moonmath MLA attention backend: MLA decode and speculative verify on gfx942
signals.text: > Best landed after the chunked-prefix-KV PR — this one adds `moonmath_mla` to > `CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_SUPPORTED_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, which is inert until > `handle_attention_aiter` can return `MHA_CHUNKED_KV`. ## Motivation Speculative decoding for MLA models is unreachable on the aiter backend on CDNA3. aiter's asm MLA selects a kernel from a fixed table, and on gfx942 that table has no entry for the shapes Kimi-K3 needs: - **12 query heads.** Kimi-K3 at TP8 is 96/8 = 12 per rank; aiter requires 4, 8, or a multiple of 16 in [16, 128]. `AiterAttnBackend`'s head padding does not reach it either — `head_repeat_factor = 16 // 12 = 1`, so nothing is repeated and the kernel still sees `gqa=12`. - **Draft windows past 4 with an fp8 KV cache.** Across every fp8 KV row in `hsa/gfx942/mla/mla_asm.csv` the maximum is `qSeqLen=4`. An unmatched shape is a process abort during cuda-graph capture, not a recoverable error. Both gaps are still present on current aiter main. ## Modifications **New attention backend — `--attention-backend moonmath_mla`** (`layers/attention/moonmath_mla_backend.py`). Subclasses `AiterAttnBackend` and takes over absorbed MLA with the moonmath_attention A16W8 kernels (bf16 Q / fp8 KV), which read SGLang's existing fused-576 `MLATokenToKVPool` key buffer directly — page_size 1, device-driven, cuda-graph safe. Two shapes, both H <= 16: | forward mode | kernel | | --- | --- | | decode, q_len 1 | `mla_decode_a16w8_paged_dev` | | TARGET_VERIFY, q_len 4..8 | `mla_decode_a16w8_multiq_paged_dev` | Everything else — prefill, bf16 KV, any unsupported geometry — falls through to `AiterAttnBackend`, so the backend is a strict superset of aiter's behaviour. The multi-query arm keeps the draft window resident per CTA and applies end-aligned causal masking inside it, which is what makes a window past 4 reachable. Q stays bf16 in both arms, so there is no query scale to calibrate and the verify logits are not perturbed. **Head padding for the fallback paths.** `_mla_decode_fwd_with_head_pad` defers to the base class whenever its repeat-interleave already reaches 16 (`16 % num_head == 0`), and only handles the counts it cannot — 12, and 3/5/6/7/9..15. It is unconditional at those counts because the current behaviour there is an abort, so there is no prior result to preserve. The pad is on the query side only, and MLA has no reduction across the head axis: QK, softmax and PV are per (head, query position), the split-KV combine is launched on `grid = (bs, nhead)` and indexes its partials by `cur_head`, and the output write is one disjoint row per head. The first H output rows are therefore bit-identical to an unpadded call. `AiterAttnBackend` gains one hook, `skip_mla_head_count_assert`, so a subclass serving MLA with its own kernel is not rejected at construction; it does not make aiter's MLA work at an unsupported head count. **Graph-safe metadata.** The int32 `seq_lens` the kernel reads were staged inside `forward_decode` — once per MLA layer, and inside the captured graph. They move to the metadata hooks: once per forward, and out-of-graph before every replay, which is where a device buffer a captured kernel reads must be refreshed. The frozen kv-split was planned from the model's context window, which over-splits badly at batch; all requests' KV shares one pool, so `pool_slots // bs` is the mean sequence length at that batch and a much better planning input (`parts` is a performance knob — every value >= 1 is numerically correct). **Environment surface: one new variable.** `SGLANG_MOONMATH_MLA_MULTIQ_VERIFY` (default on) routes TARGET_VERIFY through the multi-query kernel; set it to 0 to force the aiter path for A/B. Serving Kimi-K3 with an fp8 KV cache and DSpark at block size 7 (verify window 8, exactly the multi-query kernel's range): ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --tp 8 --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --attention-backend moonmath_mla --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --trust-remote-code ``` ## Accuracy Tests MLA decode and multi-query verify vs an fp32 reference — per-TP-rank shapes, driving the backend's real `forward_decode` / `forward_extend` (gates, seq_lens staging, kv-split planning and operand splitting included) against an fp32 reference computed on the dequantized fp8 KV pool: | case | shapes | rel L2 | | --- | --- | --- | | Kimi-K3 decode (H=12) | bs 1/4/16/32, S 2k–8k | 2.7e-3 | | Kimi-K3 multi-query verify (H=12) | q_len 4,5,6,7,8 x bs 1/4/8/16 | 2.6e-3 | 2.7e-3 is the fp8 KV quantization floor for these shapes, not kernel error — the reference dequantizes the same fp8 bytes. The gates were separately checked to decline (fall back to aiter) at q_len 3, q_len 9, H = 32, and with the multi-query knob off. 20/20. **Unit tests** — `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_moonmath_mla_backend.py`, 11 tests. The 10 gating tests — eligibility (head count, KV dtype, forward mode, MLA dims, non-MLA) and the multi-query window bounds — are pure Python and run without `moonmath_attention`: the kernel package is stubbed into `sys.modules` for the backend construction, so a CI lane that cannot install it still covers every routing decision. Only the 11th, A16W8 decode vs an fp32 reference, needs a ROCm GPU plus the package, and skips without them. Registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. ## Speed Tests MLA decode at Kimi-K3-at-TP8 geometry (H=12, kv_lora 512, rope 64), fp8 KV, on gfx942: | batch | seq | latency | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 2048 | 10.8 us | | 8 | 2048 | 15.0 us | | 32 | 2048 | 22.6 us | | 1 | 8192 | 13.6 us | | 8 | 8192 | 23.1 us | | 32 | 8192 | 52.8 us | | 1 | 150000 | 38.0 us | | 8 | 150000 | 236.4 us | | 32 | 150000 | 965.9 us | ## Notes for reviewers This backend requires `moonmath-attention`, from [moonmath-ai/amd-kernels](https://github.com/moonmath-ai/amd-kernels), plus `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. It is opt-in via `--attention-backend` and the import is at backend construction, so no other configuration is affected — but `moonmath-attention` is not on PyPI. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32254982682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32254982682)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32254982443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32254982443)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Responses] Fix max_output_tokens overestimate on multimodal requests
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Summary The Responses API pre-computed `default_max_tokens = context_len - prompt_length`. For **multimodal** requests `prompt_length` came from `len(tokenizer.encode(engine_prompt_string))`, which only counts the `<image>` placeholder — not the engine-side **post-expansion** token count. So `default_max_tokens` was overestimated, and `_validate_one_request` then rejected `input + default_max_tokens > context_len` with a spurious 400 (any model on the multimodal arch path, e.g. KimiK2.6 sharing `KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration`). The expanded count isn't available at the `serving_responses` layer (image tokens are only expanded engine-side), which is why a serving-side recompute can't be made accurate. Fixes #29287. ## Fix Mirror the Chat Completions route: stop pre-computing `default_max_tokens` and pass `None`, leaving `max_new_tokens` unset so the **scheduler clamps** the budget against the real post-expansion `input_len` — one source of truth. - `ResponsesRequest.to_sampling_params`: `default_max_tokens: Optional[int] = None`, with `None`-safe handling (`max_output_tokens` is still honored and capped when a concrete default is supplied). - `serving_responses.py`: drop the `prompt_length` / `default_max_tokens` computation and pass `None`. This reuses the exact path Chat already uses for unspecified `max_tokens` (`tokenizer_manager` skips the total check when `max_new_tokens is None`, the scheduler substitutes a sentinel and clamps to the real input/system limits), so text Responses requests behave identically to before. ## Tests `test_responses_protocol.py::ResponsesSamplingParamsTestCase`: `None` default + no `max_output_tokens` leaves `max_new_tokens=None`; `None` default + `max_output_tokens=100` → `98`; an explicit `default_max_tokens=128` still caps to `126` (backwards compatible). Pass locally. Per the issue thread @hhy-seven preferred this (option 2); opening as draft for maintainer confirmation. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32255041742](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255041742)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32255041790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255041790)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] MXFP4 MoE on gfx942 through aiter's Triton kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation MXFP4 MoE cannot run on CDNA3, which is what Kimi-K3 needs. `aiter.fused_moe` has no gfx942 a4w4 path and dies in the activation quantiser with `fused_dynamic_mx_quant_moe_sort_hip: not support output type: fp4x2` — the `fp4x2` branch in `csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu` is behind `#if defined(__Float4_e2m1fn_x2)`, which is not defined on CDNA3, and `hsa/gfx942/f4gemm/*.csv` is empty. There is no non-aiter escape either: the generic Triton MoE runner (`moe_runner/triton.py`, what `MoeRunnerBackend.TRITON` selects when `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is unset) has no MXFP4 support at all. So on gfx942 MXFP4 MoE either aborts or has no path. ## Modifications `moe_runner/aiter_mxfp4_triton.py` routes gfx942 MXFP4 MoE through aiter's *Triton* MXFP4 GEMMs, which lower `tl.dot_scaled` onto the bf16 MFMA CDNA3 has always had. `moe_runner/mxfp4_situ_fused.py` adds a SiTU variant of aiter's fused gated epilogue so the routed experts keep their activation fused into the GEMM; `ACT_SITU=False` is the upstream SwiGLU epilogue unchanged. **No patched aiter is required.** `arch_info.is_fp4_avail()` still excludes gfx942, but it is asserted only in aiter's GEMM entry points, never in `fused_moe_mxfp4`, and it was never a capability probe. The one thing a stock aiter lacks is a tile config — there is no `configs/moe/gfx942-MOE-MX_FP4.json`, and the fallback is a 256x256x64 tile sized for CDNA4's 160 KB LDS that does not compile against CDNA3's 64 KB. `_moe_config()` carries the gfx942 table and defers to aiter's the moment aiter ships one. Everything here is behind `use_triton_mxfp4_moe()`, which is False on every arch but gfx942 and on any build where the Triton kernels do not import, so no other MoE path changes. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/moe/test_aiter_mxfp4_triton_moe.py` checks both new kernels against an fp32 reference that dequantizes the same MXFP4 bytes and runs the MoE in plain torch: | case | coverage | | --- | --- | | both epilogues | SwiGLU (upstream) and SiTU (Kimi-K3), incl. the tanh soft-clips | | both routed-weight placements | `apply_router_weight_on_input` on/off | | expert parallelism | `num_global = 2 x local`; the dropped `-1` rows are what make the fused reduce's masked load load-bearing | | tile shapes | 1 / 16 / 512 tokens — either side of the small/medium config boundary | | gate | `SGLANG_AITER_MXFP4_TRITON` override, no GPU needed | | activation | rel L2 vs fp32 reference | | --- | --- | | SiTU | 2.5e-3 – 2.8e-3 | | SwiGLU | 3.8e-3 – 4.2e-3 | | EP rank 1 (half the experts dropped) | 2.5e-3 | | router weight on input | 2.9e-3 | Tolerance is 1e-2 — the bf16 floor, since the fp4 weights are exact on both sides. 6 tests / 7 subtests green on gfx942 against a stock aiter. Registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (isort / black 26.1.0 / ruff `F401,F821,UP037`) - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32255063349](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255063349)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32255062985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255062985)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(sgl-kernel): route below-SM90 GPUs to sm90 build in load_utils
signals.text: ## Problem `_load_architecture_specific_ops()` routes only `compute_capability == 90` to the `sm90/` directory; every other GPU falls into the `sm100/` branch. However, the sm90 artifact is the compatibility build: `ENABLE_BELOW_SM90` (default ON on x86_64) appends `compute_80`/`compute_89` gencode (and `compute_87` on aarch64) to the shared `SGL_KERNEL_CUDA_FLAGS` used by `common_ops_sm90_build` (see `python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt`). Below-SM90 GPUs (sm_80/86/87/89, e.g. L40S / RTX 4090) are therefore sent to the wrong directory and fail to `import sgl_kernel` whenever the sm100 artifact does not carry below-SM90 gencode — reproduced on an sm_89 GPU with CUDA 12.1 and sglang-kernel 0.4.5, where import failed until cc=89 was routed to the sm90 directory. This currently happens to work on recent x86_64 wheels only because both builds share the same flags and the sm100 artifact incidentally contains sm_89 cubins; any divergence of the two builds' flag sets (or a wheel built with `ENABLE_BELOW_SM90=OFF`) breaks below-SM90 users immediately. ## Fix Route every GPU with `compute_capability < 100` to the sm90 build. cc >= 100 and the no-GPU path are unchanged. `variant_name` now reports the actual cc instead of hardcoding "SM90". Note: sm_89 is **not** a subset of sm_90 (Ada 8.x vs Hopper 9.x) — this works because the sm90 artifact is compiled with below-SM90 gencode, not because sm90 cubins run on sm89. ## Test - `python -m py_compile` passes. - Verified on an sm_89 GPU: `import sgl_kernel` succeeds with cc=89 routed to the sm90 directory. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32255261048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255261048)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32255260792](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255260792)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Guard unsupported quantized component checkpoints
signals.text: ## Summary - add one fail-closed admission boundary for native auxiliary component loaders that only materialize plain state dicts - reject detected top-level, nested text-config, and compressed-tensors quantization metadata before model construction or large weight reads - apply the boundary to connectors/duration heads, bridges, diffusion decoders, sound tokenizers, spatial upsamplers, and vocoders - keep the local PE model on its Transformers `from_pretrained` path, where compatible quantization formats remain model-specific - use one documentation contract across the overview, CLI, compatibility matrix, and quantization guide ## Motivation #35184 makes independent component repository routing generic and safely routes supported quantized VAEs. The remaining raw-state native loaders still had no common quantization admission rule, so a quantized component repo could be interpreted as a dense module or fail only after allocating/loading weights. Path routing and quantized materialization are separate capabilities. This PR does not add a generic per-component quantization knob: such a knob would overstate support until each loader has a matching backend. Existing transformer, native encoder, VAE, PE/Transformers, and upstream AutoModel quantization paths remain unchanged. ## Validation - all pre-commit hooks pass - focused unit coverage added for metadata layouts and early rejection order - runtime tests left to CI <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32258969645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258969645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32258969397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258969397)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
