signals.title: [Model] Add qwen3 bidirectional embedding
signals.text: ## Motivation Add native SGLang support for **`ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-3B-0826`**, a text-embedding model built on the Qwen3 backbone but run with **encoder-style (bidirectional) attention** and mean pooling. Its HF checkpoint declares `architectures=["Qwen3BidirectionalModel"]` with `is_causal=false`; without native support it falls back to the Transformers backend (and, more importantly, SGLang has no bidirectional-attention path wired for Qwen3). This is one of a pair of PRs adding the Giga-Embeddings models; the DeepSeek-V3 sibling (`DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel`) is submitted separately. ## Modifications The whole change is driven by the checkpoint's own `is_causal=False` flag (default `True` keeps the existing causal path byte-for-byte identical). It mirrors the merged `Lfm2BidirectionalModel` / `gemma3_causal.py` patterns. - **`models/qwen3.py`**: thread an `attn_type` through `Qwen3Attention` / `Qwen3DecoderLayer`, selected from `config.is_causal` → `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` when bidirectional, else `AttentionType.DECODER` (unchanged default). - **`models/qwen3_embedding.py`**: add `Qwen3BidirectionalModel` (reuses the existing bare-backbone embedding wrapper; `Pooler(MEAN, normalize=True)`), registered via the `EntryClass` list. - **`configs/model_config.py`**: classify `Qwen3BidirectionalModel` as a non-generation (embedding) architecture. - **`configs/embedding_model_spec.py`**: register it as a bidirectional, mean-pooling embedding architecture (auto-enables embedding mode). - **`server_args.py`**: for this architecture, force `--disable-cuda-graph`, `--disable-radix-cache`, `--chunked-prefill-size -1`. Bidirectional attention over the whole prompt makes prefix/split-prefill reuse invalid, and — verified below — the captured prefill CUDA graph corrupts the non-causal attention. This mirrors the existing HRM-Text / EmbeddingGemma handling. Serving is fully automatic: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-3B-0826 \ --is-embedding --trust-remote-code ``` ## Accuracy Tests Reference = HF `AutoModel` (`trust_remote_code`, `is_causal=False`), mean-pool over non-padding tokens + L2 normalize. SGLang served with the out-of-the-box command above (auto-guards applied). Cosine similarity, per text: | Backend | min cosine vs HF (batched & single) | Result | |---|---|---| | triton | 0.997 | ✅ PASS | | flashinfer | 0.9965 | ✅ PASS | | torch_native | 0.9976 | ✅ PASS | Retrieval sanity (query → documents): `Paris` 0.68 ≫ `mitochondria` 0.10 ≫ `photosynthesis` 0.01. Single-request and batched outputs agree (no cross-sequence leakage). > Note: `fa3` could not be validated on the test GPU (RTX 5090, SM120 — fa3 requires SM 80–90). It is a regular-attention backend that honors `ENCODER_ONLY`, so it is expected to pass on Hopper; a maintainer with Hopper hardware may want to confirm. **Regression caught during testing:** with the prefill CUDA graph enabled, embeddings were wrong and batch-size-dependent (min cosine ~0.18). Disabling CUDA graph (as this PR does) restores parity. A unit test guards the capability adjustment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No changes to existing code paths (the causal Qwen3 path is unchanged). The new path is prefill-only embedding; no decode/CUDA-graph impact on existing models. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_bidirectional_embedding_registration.py`; also updated `test_embedding_model_spec.py` and `test_qwen3_embedding_registration.py` for the extended registry). - [x] Update documentation (`docs/docs/supported-models/embedding_models.mdx`). - [x] Provide accuracy results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32259721331](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259721331)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32259720337](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259720337)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Model] Add deepseek v3 bidirectional embedding
signals.text: ## Motivation Add native SGLang support for **`ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-10B-A1.8B-0826`**, a text-embedding model built on the **DeepSeek-V3 MoE (MLA)** backbone but run with **encoder-style (bidirectional) attention** and mean pooling. Its HF checkpoint declares `architectures=["DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel"]` with `is_causal=false`. DeepSeek uses MLA, whose absorbed attention kernels are causal-only, so bidirectional support requires routing through the non-absorbed MHA prefill path. This is one of a pair of PRs adding the Giga-Embeddings models; the Qwen3 sibling (`Qwen3BidirectionalModel`) is submitted separately. ## Modifications Driven entirely by the checkpoint's own `is_causal=False` (default `True` leaves the causal path unchanged). Since embedding models are **prefill-only**, they are served through `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA`'s non-absorbed MHA prefill path (`attn_mha`), which is a standard `RadixAttention` that honors `attn_type`. - **`models/deepseek_v2.py`**: set `attn_mha` to `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` when `config.is_causal is False` (the absorbed `attn_mqa` decode path stays causal and is unused for embeddings). - **`models/deepseek_v2_embedding.py`** (new): `DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel` subclasses `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` to reuse all MoE/MLA weight loading, replacing the logits path with `Pooler(MEAN, normalize=True)`. - **`configs/model_config.py`**: register the arch as **MLA** (so an MLA KV pool is allocated, not MHA) and as a non-generation embedding model. - **`configs/embedding_model_spec.py`**: register as a bidirectional, mean-pooling embedding architecture (auto-enables embedding mode). - **`server_args.py` / `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: for this architecture, force **`--attention-backend triton`**, `--disable-cuda-graph`, `--disable-radix-cache`, `--chunked-prefill-size -1`. Rationale (all verified below): only Triton honors `ENCODER_ONLY` on the MLA MHA prefill (flashinfer silently runs causal); CUDA-graph capture pins the absorbed causal-only MLA kernel; and prefix/split-prefill reuse is invalid under bidirectional attention. This mirrors the existing HRM-Text handling. Serving is fully automatic: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-10B-A1.8B-0826 \ --is-embedding --trust-remote-code ``` ## Accuracy Tests Reference = HF `AutoModel` (`trust_remote_code`, `is_causal=False`), mean-pool over non-padding tokens + L2 normalize. (The remote checkpoint stores per-expert MoE weights; the reference loads them fused.) SGLang served with the out-of-the-box command above. | Backend | min cosine vs HF (batched & single) | Result | |---|---|---| | triton (default / forced) | 0.996 | ✅ PASS | | flashinfer (auto-overridden → triton) | 0.996 | ✅ PASS (after override) | Retrieval sanity (query → documents): `Paris` 0.68 ≫ `mitochondria` 0.16 ≫ `photosynthesis` 0.05. Single-request and batched outputs agree. **Regressions caught during testing (all fixed in this PR):** - Without the MLA registration, startup crashed (`'MHATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'set_mla_kv_buffer'`) — an MHA KV pool was allocated for an MLA model. - With the `flashinfer` backend, the MLA prefill ran **causal** and produced wrong embeddings (min cosine ~0.35). Forcing Triton restores parity; verified that launching with `--attention-backend flashinfer` logs the override to `triton` and yields min cosine 0.9964. A unit test guards the capability adjustment (triton force + CUDA-graph/radix/chunked disable). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No changes to existing DeepSeek code paths (the bidirectional branch is gated on `is_causal=False`, which no existing checkpoint sets). The new path is prefill-only embedding. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v3_bidirectional_embedding_registration.py`; also updated `test_embedding_model_spec.py`). - [x] Update documentation (`docs/docs/supported-models/embedding_models.mdx`). - [x] Provide accuracy results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32260138562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32260138562)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32260137952](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32260137952)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix replicated (TP1) shared expert being summed by collectives that skip the MoE all-reduce
signals.text: ## Motivation The invariant, stated once: **a replicated (TP1) shared expert must never sit inside a tensor that a collective SUMs.** A TP-sharded shared expert produces a genuine per-rank partial, so reducing over it is correct; a replicated one holds the identical full value on every rank, so any group SUM scales it by the group size — silently, once per layer. `DeepseekV2MoE` encodes this by adding the shared output *after* its own post-experts all-reduce. That guard only covers the reduction it performs itself. `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` lets a caller defer, replace, or absorb that reduction, and **every such caller inherits the invariant**. This PR fixes the two reachable callers that did not honour it: 1. the prefill-CP combine (`mlp_reduce_scatter`), on `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` and `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`; 2. `fuse_mlp_allreduce`, which does not remove the all-reduce but *defers* it into the next layer — a plain TP bug, no CP involved. Under DSA prefill context parallelism with `moe_a2a_backend=none`, a **replicated (TP1) shared expert is counted `cp_size` times instead of once, in every MoE layer**. `dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states` SUMs the MoE output across the CP group. That is correct for the routed experts — their per-rank outputs are genuine partial sums — but wrong for a TP1 shared expert, where every rank holds the identical full value. `DeepseekV2MoE` already guards against exactly this for its own reduction: ```python if self.tp_size > 1 and not should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(is_tp_path=True): final_hidden_states = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(final_hidden_states) # TP1 shared experts are replicated, so add them after all-reduce to # avoid summing the same shared output once per TP rank. if self._shared_expert_tp1: final_hidden_states += shared_output ``` But under CP that internal all-reduce is **skipped** (`mlp_reduce_scatter=True`, see `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce`) and the cross-rank sum happens later in the CP combine — outside the reach of that guard. The existing hoist that would have prevented this, `_do_shared_local`, is gated on `_use_tp_moe_gather`, which is `not _use_cp and ...` — so it never engages on the CP path: ```python _do_shared_local = ( _SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL and _use_tp_moe_gather # == not _use_cp and ... and getattr(self.mlp, "shared_experts", None) is not None and getattr(self.mlp, "_shared_expert_tp1", False) ) ``` Both CP MoE paths are affected: the eager path (`dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states`) and the TBO path (`op_cp_combine_a` → `attn_cp_overlap_reduce_scatter_tensor`). ### When it triggers Only when the shared expert is replicated on the `moe_a2a_backend=none` CP path, i.e. `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1` or `should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`. Neither is the default, which is why CI has not caught it. There is currently no CI coverage for CP-v1 on HIP at all. ### Which CP flavors can actually reach this `_deepseek_family_overrides` forces `moe_a2a_backend=deepep` for the **zigzag** DSA CP strategy and for **MLA CP**, and deepep takes the EP combine branch instead of the CP reduce-scatter. So only **`interleave` DSA CP with `moe_a2a_backend=none`** reaches the bug today, on both the DSv4 layer and the DSv2 layer. The new predicate still admits `mla_use_prefill_cp` so the guard survives if that override is relaxed; that arm is currently dead code and is **not** claimed as tested. ## Modifications - Add `cp_requires_shared_expert_hoist()` to `communicator_dsa_cp.py`, documenting the invariant next to the collective that depends on it. - Extend `_do_shared_local` to the CP path in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`, and make it **unconditional** there — deliberately not gated on `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL`, since correctness must not depend on a perf env var. The shared expert is a per-token MLP, so computing it on this rank's local rows before the gather is identical to computing it on the gathered buffer and keeping this rank's slice. - Apply the same hoist to the TBO CP path (`op_cp_gather_a` / `op_cp_moe` / `op_cp_combine_b`), mirroring what `op_gather_a` / `op_combine_b` already do for DP. - **Extend the hoist to `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`**, which reaches the same CP combine via `DSACPLayerCommunicator.postprocess_layer` -> `dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states`. This covers `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (it subclasses `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`, so it uses this layer) and `deepseek_nextn`. - Close two latent gaps that would have made the hoist itself unsound: - `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal_dual_stream` ignored `skip_shared_experts` entirely, so on the capture-mode path the caller's hoisted add and the MoE's own add would *both* land. - `dsv2_flashinfer_moe_dual_stream_graph` cannot express "skip the shared expert", so `forward` now falls back to `forward_normal` when the caller hoisted it. A perf downgrade, confined to a configuration that would otherwise be numerically wrong. - Unit tests encoding the invariant. The `getattr` in the new helper is kept deliberately: a dense layer's `mlp` has no `shared_experts` attribute, and it cannot simply be pre-initialized to `None` because three sites in `deepseek_v2.py` branch on `hasattr(self, "shared_experts")` (lines 869, 1051, 1533 — the last one gates an early return). ### 2. `fuse_mlp_allreduce` defers the all-reduce past the guard Under fusion the decoder tags its output with `_sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion` and the **next** layer's `prepare_attn` performs the all-reduce as part of its residual+layernorm. By then the replicated shared output is already inside the tensor, so it is summed `tp_size` times. The guard is still there; it just no longer guards anything. Fixed by declining the fusion when the layer's mlp owns a replicated shared expert — a perf downgrade strictly confined to configurations that would otherwise be numerically wrong. Applies to `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` and `LagunaDecoderLayer`, the two decoders that both publish `fuse_mlp_allreduce` and can own a replicated shared expert. `glm4_moe_lite` assigns `_shared_expert_tp1 = False` and never reassigns it, so it is unaffected. Reachable with `moe_a2a_backend=none` (anything else makes `mlp_mode` SCATTERED, which disables fusion) + `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1` + no DP attention + `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` on ROCm or `--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` on sm90/sm100. `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion` is asserted off when `attn_cp_size > 1`, so this is disjoint from the CP path above. `has_replicated_shared_expert()` moves the predicate next to `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` in `layers/moe/utils.py`, where the skip reasons that create the hazard are enumerated; `cp_requires_shared_expert_hoist()` keeps its CP-specific docstring and delegates. It also learns the second attribute spelling — `DeepseekV2MoE` says `shared_experts`, `LagunaMoE` says `shared_expert`. ## Accuracy results MI355X, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark`, TP8, greedy, 53 **token-exact** prompt lengths from 56 to 2052 (sent as `input_ids` so no BOS/template shifts the count). Each arm is compared against its **own** non-CP reference at the same TP. | arm | top-1 match | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | TP4 no CP vs TP8 no CP (noise floor) | 51/53 (96%) | 0.098 | | **cp=4, before** | 16/53 (30%) | **1.524** | | **cp=8, before** | 7/53 (13%) | **2.834** | | cp=8, `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=0` (workaround) | 48/53 (91%) | 0.087 | | **cp=8, after this PR** | **50/53 (94%)** | **0.086** | Mean top-1 logprob: `-0.870` no CP, `-2.394` at cp=4, `-3.705` at cp=8, `-0.893` after the fix. The error growing with `cp_size` (2.83 nats at cp=8 vs 1.52 at cp=4, on a matched TP control that itself differs by only 0.098) is the signature of the per-rank duplication. After the fix, CP sits inside the same noise band as simply changing TP. The 3 remaining mismatches are lengths where the non-CP reference is itself run-to-run unstable. Two hypotheses were tested and excluded before landing on this one: batch padding to `cp_align_size` (CP still diverged at 9/11 lengths needing no padding), and DSA top-k selection (at these lengths `seq_len < index_topk=1024`, so top-k is a no-op). ### CP-v2 (`SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=1`) is cured by the same change CP-v2 goes through the same `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`, so it carries the identical double-count. At n=64, TP8, cp=8 (the only length CP-v2 currently runs at cp=8 on HIP, for unrelated reasons): | arm | top-1 token | logprob | |---|---|---| | non-CP TP8 reference | 566 | -0.908 | | CP-v2, unpatched | 201 | -3.302 | | CP-v2, after this PR | 566 | -1.325 | One fix, both CP implementations. To be precise about what is *not* claimed: after the fix CP-v2 is at 25/32 top-1 / mean |Δlogprob| 0.147, still above the 50/53 / 0.071 non-CP noise floor, whereas CP-v1 lands *at* the noise floor (50/53 / 0.086). That CP-v2 residual is a separate v2-specific defect (the HIP dsv4 backend never calls `apply_cp_reindex` under v2), not a shortfall of this fix. ### `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` coverage (GLM-5.1-FP8, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) 8x MI355X, `GLM-5.1-FP8` (78 layers, `n_shared_experts=1`), TP8, DSA prefill CP `interleave`, `attn_cp_size=8`, `moe_a2a_backend=none`, greedy, the same 53 token-exact prompt lengths. Each arm is compared against a **non-CP arm with the same `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1` setting**. | arm | top-1 match | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | no CP, TP1=1 vs no CP, TP1=0 (sharding-only noise floor) | 47/53 | 0.044 | | **CP, TP1=1, before** | 0/53 | **2.189** | | **CP, TP1=1, after this PR** | 3/53 | **0.926** | | CP, TP1=0 (shared expert TP-sharded, bug unreachable — bisection control) | 2/53 | 1.016 | The shared-expert component of the error goes **2.189 -> 0.926**, landing on the **1.016** of the arm where the shared expert is TP-sharded and this bug cannot occur. That is the whole of this defect. **Honest caveat:** the ~1.0 nat that remains in *both* CP arms is a **separate, pre-existing defect** in DSA prefill CP for this model on ROCm — it is present with a TP-sharded shared expert, so nothing in this PR can explain or fix it. This PR does not address it and does not claim to. (`SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=0` above is a bisection control, not a production setting.) ### `fuse_mlp_allreduce` (GLM-5.1-FP8, no CP) 8x MI355X, TP8, **no CP**, `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1`, `moe_a2a_backend=none`, greedy, the same 53 token-exact prompt lengths, against the same build with fusion off. | arm | top-1 match | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | noise floor (TP1=1 vs TP1=0, no fusion) | 47/53 | 0.044 | | **`fuse_mlp_allreduce` on, before** | 0/53 | **2.591** | | **`fuse_mlp_allreduce` on, after this PR** | 49/53 | **0.060** | The fix lands at the noise floor. On how the arms force fusion: they publish `fuse_mlp_allreduce` through a **test-only env gate** rather than `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, so the deferred reduction lands on the exact `moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` branch of `prepare_attn`. Fused and unfused are then mathematically identical *except* for where the shared output is added, which isolates this defect. Using the real flag was tried first and is unusable as a control: on this model and image the aiter fused AR+RMSNorm kernel in `_gather_hidden_states_and_residual` is independently lossy by ~2.45 nats, which swamps the signal. That is a separate issue and is not touched here. ### End-to-end in the deployment stack (PD-disagg + DSpark + HiCache + CP) DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, 1P1D PD-disaggregation over mori, TP8, prefill CP interleave cp=8, HiCache L2 (dram, ratio 3), unified radix tree on, DSpark speculative decoding, AgentX trace replay, 940 s at concurrency 16. Both arms on the same two nodes, differing only by the `deepseek_v4.py` overlay. | | unpatched | patched | |---|---|---| | requests completed / errors | 418 / **0** | 475 / **0** | | output throughput | 430 tok/s | 508 tok/s | | e2e p50 | 8,993 ms | 6,363 ms | | ITL p50 | 25 ms | 16 ms | | interactivity p50 | 40 tok/s | 61 tok/s | | prefix cache hit | 95.5% | 96.1% | | DSpark accept length | 1.55 – 1.95 | 2.36 – 2.60 | The point of this run is that the fix survives the full deployment stack with zero request errors, not the throughput delta. **Accept length is deliberately not offered as a quality metric here**: DSpark self-drafts, so a degenerate target model can be *easier* to predict from itself — on a different (synthetic-corpus) workload the unpatched CP arm scored the *highest* accept length of all arms. What is worth noting is only that the patched arm's 2.36–2.60 sits inside the known-good non-CP DSpark band (2.16 smoke / 2.45 AgentX) while the unpatched arm's does not. ## Adjacent gap, deliberately not fixed here `mlp_reduce_scatter` on the **DP** path is a third caller of the same invariant: with DP attention + `moe_a2a_backend=none` + reduce-scatterv (or max-len padding), `_scatter_hidden_states` SUMs across the TP group after the MoE's own all-reduce was skipped. `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` does hoist the shared expert there — but only when `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL` is set, i.e. a *perf* env var currently doubles as the correctness guard. `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` has no equivalent hoist at all. Reported rather than patched: I have not been able to validate a fix for it on hardware, and this PR's rule is that nothing lands unmeasured. ## Checklist - [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (black/isort applied to touched files) - [x] `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py` + `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_replicated_shared_expert_invariant.py` — 31 passed, 18 subtests - [x] Accuracy validated end-to-end on 8xMI355X: DSv4 layer on DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark; DSv2 layer and the fusion fix on GLM-5.1-FP8 Related: #34142 (CP-v1 interleave shard-pitch fix, still unmerged) and #35510 (the CP-v2 counterpart — note that one is a hardening change, not a live-bug fix: v2's per-rank padding rounds a one-row shard up to `cp_size` rows and `pad_local_rows`' `torch.cat` launders the stride, so the pitch anomaly is currently unreachable there). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32270851433](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32270851433)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32270851217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32270851217)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] fix: stop reserving NCCL device buffers for single-rank groups
signals.text: ## Motivation On a single GPU, ~5 GiB of VRAM is gone before a single weight is loaded. On a 12 GiB consumer card that is 44% of the device, and it makes VAE decode fail at any resolution. The cause is that a single-GPU run still builds every parallel group — DP, CFG, TP, SP, PP, VAE_DECODE, DIT, VAE, ulysses, ring — each with one rank, and each got an NCCL-backed process group. NCCL sizes its per-channel device buffers when the communicator is created, so every one of those groups reserved ~390 MiB (the first, the world group, ~470 MiB). None of that memory can ever be used. Every collective in `GroupCoordinator` returns early on `world_size == 1` ("Bypass the function if we are using only 1 GPU"), and the device communicator is only constructed when `world_size > 1`. `pynccl` already skips communicator creation for single-rank groups; the underlying `torch.distributed.new_group` did not. Measured on an RTX 3060 12 GiB with a bare `torch.distributed` repro: | | device memory | |---|---| | CUDA context only | 114 MiB | | + world group | 584 MiB | | each additional `new_group([0])` | **+388 MiB** | `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` drops the per-group cost to 10 MiB, which confirms these are per-channel buffers for channels a one-rank communicator can never use. ## Modifications Add `new_device_group()` in `group_coordinator.py`, which gives single-rank groups the gloo backend and leaves multi-rank groups on the requested backend. Route the nine device-group creation sites through it: `GroupCoordinator.__init__`, the `PipelineGroupCoordinator` single-rank branch and its `skip_device_group`, `_DIT` and `_VAE` in `parallel_state.py`, and the four ulysses/ring groups in `parallel_groups.py`. The two-rank `device_group_0_1` / `device_group_1_0` pipeline pair is left alone; it is only reached when the group has exactly two ranks. One consumer needed a matching guard. cache-dit averages its residual-difference statistics across the TP x SP slice using the DIT group, and that all-reduce had no world-size check, so on a single GPU it would now stage device tensors through the host on every cached block of every step. Averaging over one rank returns the input, so the patched `similarity` returns the local value instead of running the collective. Every other consumer of these groups already short-circuits: collectives in `GroupCoordinator` return early on `world_size == 1`, the device communicator is built only above 1, the ulysses/ring groups are reached only under `sp_size > 1` in `attention/layer.py` and behind `world_size <= 1` early returns in `usp.py`, and the VAE group has no consumer outside its getter. ## Accuracy Tests Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234. | | free VRAM after load | peak VRAM | VAE decode | output SHA-256 | |---|---|---|---|---| | before | 6.51 GiB | 11552 MiB | **OOM** | no output produced | | `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` control | 11.31 GiB | 6886 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` | | this PR | 11.06 GiB | 6830 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` | Two-GPU regression on the same box, `--num-gpus 2`: patched and unpatched produce the same output, SHA-256 `361bb915…`, so the multi-rank path is unaffected. New unit test `test_single_rank_device_group.py` covers backend selection for single-rank and multi-rank groups (3 tests, 5 subtests). Existing `test_cache_dit_integration.py` passes with the guard (12 tests together). CI note: `multimodal-gen-test-1-npu-a3` is red here, but every diffusion testcase on that runner is red on unrelated branches too (see #35511, where `ernie_image_t2i_1npu`, `flux_image_t2i_npu`, `flux_2_klein_4b_t2i_1npu`, `z_image_t2i_1npu` and `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_1_npu` all fail and the job ends with `Executing the custom container implementation failed`). The NPU lane cannot vet this change right now. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No change to per-step time — 1.10 s/step before, 1.06 s/step after, within the run-to-run noise band measured across this configuration. The groups involved never carried traffic. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32291208968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291208968)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32291208893](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291208893)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Align deterministic DSpark target verify with Triton decode
signals.text: ## Motivation Addresses #35150. Deterministic top-k-1 DSpark target verification used Triton extend attention, while ordinary decoding used Triton decode attention. This change aligns those attention paths for static linear verification. ## Modifications - Build one causal decode row for each target-verify token. - Reuse Triton decode attention in eager and CUDA Graph target verification. - Restrict the path to CUDA deterministic DSpark target workers with top-k 1 and without custom or ragged masks, MLA, DCP, sliding-window attention, unified KV translation, or encoder-decoder attention. ## Accuracy Tests - `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, Black, and the repository Ruff rules passed. - Focused GPU probe: target-verify output exactly matched sequential decode (`unequal=0`, `max_abs=0.0`); eager and CUDA Graph `kv_indptr`, `kv_indices`, and KV splits matched. - Qwen3.8-27B DSpark, 96-token greedy request: - eager forced reject: `spec_accept_rate=0.0` - full CUDA Graph forced reject: `spec_accept_rate=0.0` - normal DSpark: `spec_accept_rate=0.484375` (31/64 drafts accepted) - all three Candidate B runs produced output-ID SHA256 `5fc99930b4c8f106a1267003582448c2f9bfe1f17c4db52839924cfc8e830fa1` The SHA above compares the three Candidate B runs; it is not a Base-model oracle comparison. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run; this PR targets deterministic correctness.

signals.title: [HiCache] Split the host-memory budget across co-located ranks
signals.text: ## Motivation Every HiCache host-pool sizing guard checks its requested size against `psutil.virtual_memory().available`, which reports machine-wide free memory. Co-located ranks each see the same number, so every rank concludes its pool fits and the host ends up oversubscribed by the number of ranks it holds (8x for single-node TP8). The guard passes, and the pinned-host allocation later OOMs instead of failing fast with the intended `ValueError`. ## Modifications - Add `host_memory_budget_bytes()` in `pool_host/base.py`: subtract `HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES` from available host memory once, then divide by the number of ranks sharing the machine. - Derive that count in `ranks_per_host()` as `world_size // nnodes`: the launcher slices ranks uniformly across nodes (resolution asserts divisibility), so the co-located rank count is a config fact and needs no hostname collective — a collective here would have to be issued the same number of times on every rank, and ranks build different numbers of host pools. - Route all six sizing guards (`HostKVCache` base, `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool`, `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool`, `DSAIndexerPoolHost`, and the mamba/mha pools) through the helper. Single-rank behavior is unchanged. - Unit tests (`test_mem_pool_host.py`): the budget is split across co-located ranks, the reserve is subtracted once before the split rather than per rank, and `ranks_per_host` divides world size by node count. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: this only changes host-pool sizing guards, not model forward paths. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32291671532](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291671532)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32291671297](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291671297)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Preserve deterministic DSpark target-verify parity
signals.text: ## Motivation Addresses #35150. With deterministic inference, ordinary Qwen3.8 decode and linear DSpark `TARGET_VERIFY` differed in two numerically relevant places: - decode rounds the GDN beta value through the activation dtype, while target verify kept it in FP32; - decode uses `decode_attention_fwd`, while target verify used `extend_attention_fwd_unified`. Either difference can perturb the persistent GDN state over repeated reject/commit rounds. A routing-only negative control still diverged from the clean packed-decode Base output at token 13 with all 95 drafts rejected, so attention routing alone is insufficient. ## Modifications - Round target-verify beta through its source activation dtype before accumulating in FP32. - Represent an unmasked linear verify block as independent decode streams with KV lengths `prefix_len + 1, ..., prefix_len + verify_len`. - Route only the deterministic CUDA DSpark target-worker path through the existing Triton decode kernel, in eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. - Preserve the existing path for non-deterministic inference, draft workers, masked/tree or ragged verification, MLA, DCP, sliding-window attention, unified memory, encoder-decoder models, and non-CUDA platforms. ## Validation Status Validation uses one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 with CUDA 13.0, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` and `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`, TP=1, Triton attention, deterministic inference, FP32 SSM state, gamma=1, and the exact 96-token reproduction from #35150. - Clean production Base packed-decode oracle: 96 tokens, SHA256 `3ca7a432820875b0dc7c1f2d2e644664e8b864947592a0e876d00400848b6e72`. - Routing-only negative control: 0/95 drafts accepted and first divergence from the clean Base output at token 13. - The combined beta and attention changes match a sequential/unpacked decode diagnostic, but fail against the clean production packed-decode Base oracle: 0/95 drafts accepted, first divergence at output token 6 (`Base=279`, `DSpark=781`), DSpark SHA256 `5fc99930b4c8f106a1267003582448c2f9bfe1f17c4db52839924cfc8e830fa1`. - This PR remains Draft while the remaining packed GDN decode difference is localized; the current commit does not yet fix #35150. - Focused GQA probe: target-verify attention is bitwise equal to sequential decode (`unequal=0`, `max_abs=0`); eager and CUDA Graph `kv_indptr`, KV indices, and split metadata are identical. - `py_compile`, Black 26.1.0, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed claim. The new path is selected only for explicit deterministic inference, where decode parity is the goal. Default non-deterministic serving is unchanged. ## Related Work - The beta-rounding hunk is also present in #34734 by @qq1060; credit to that PR for identifying this alignment. That broader feature PR adds ragged and checkpoint support but does not route deterministic verification through decode and explicitly leaves greedy equivalence unresolved. If #34734 lands first, the duplicate one-line hunk can be dropped during rebase. - #34597 uses the same decode-kernel routing principle for DeepSeek-V4 MTP. - #34821 changes target-verify causal convolution; it does not align Triton full attention. - #33291 adds an opt-in Decode-Verify-Rollback algorithm; this fix preserves the existing DSpark path. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with the repository's Black version. - [x] Run focused attention metadata tests. - [ ] Verify exact clean packed-decode Base parity in eager and CUDA Graph execution. - [x] Keep documentation unchanged because no public API or option changes.

signals.title: Fix: omit null id/name in streaming tool call deltas
signals.text: ## Problem Streaming `tool_calls` continuation chunks currently emit explicit nulls: ```json // first chunk — OK {"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_abc","index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":""}}]} // continuation chunks — id/name serialized as null {"tool_calls":[{"id":null,"index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":null,"arguments":"{"city":"}}]} ``` `ToolCall`/`FunctionResponse` are built with `id=None`/`name=None` for argument-delta chunks (see `_process_tool_call_stream` and `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` in `serving_chat.py`), and `model_dump_json()` serializes `None` as JSON `null`. ## Why this is wrong The de-facto OpenAI streaming contract is that `id`/`function.name`/`type` appear **only in the first delta** of a tool call; continuation chunks carry just `index` and `function.arguments`: - OpenAI's own wire format omits these fields in continuation chunks (developers observe the fields are absent, not null: https://community.openai.com/t/streaming-with-tools-missing-tool-id-name/997791). The `null` values shown in parts of the docs are SDK object reprs, not wire JSON. - vLLM, the other major OpenAI-compatible server, omits unset delta fields via `model_dump_json(exclude_unset=True)` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py). - The OpenAI streaming reference marks `id`/`function.name` as optional (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/streaming-events), and the established convention is omission. ## Why it breaks clients Delta mergers that treat `null` as an explicit value (e.g. `x !== undefined`, the common OpenAI-SDK-style merge) overwrite the `id`/`function.name` streamed in the first chunk with `null`. The accumulated tool call then has an empty name, failing with errors like `unknown tool ""`. This was observed in production against a DeepSeek-V4 sglang deployment (`tool_call_parser=deepseekv4`), but the bug is in the generic OpenAI adapter and affects every `--tool-call-parser`. The same failure mode was reported against vLLM backends emitting nulls (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/26412). Similar behavior is observed in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/translate.ts#L160 ## Fix Add `model_serializer(mode="wrap")` to `ToolCall` and `FunctionResponse` that drops `None` `id`/`name`/`arguments` from the serialized output. This matches the existing `DeltaMessage` serializer pattern in the same file. Non-streaming responses are unaffected: `id`/`name`/`arguments` are always present there. ## Clarification Fix implemented by codex and reviewed by human ## Tests Added unit tests in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py`: - continuation chunk: `id`/`name` omitted, `index`/`arguments` preserved - first chunk: `id`/`name`/`arguments` kept <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32277387056](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32277387056)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32277386971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32277386971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [GDN] Amortize ReplaySSM checkpoint materialization
signals.text: ## Motivation ReplaySSM speculative decoding currently materializes the full GDN checkpoint state on every target step, even though most speculative iterations only need to append a small amount of history. This repeatedly performs work that can be deferred and makes GDN state handling a material part of the decode critical path. ## Modifications - Commit 1 stores speculative GDN updates in a bounded circular history and amortizes checkpoint materialization. - Commit 2 materializes the ReplaySSM state directly from the compact history representation instead of replaying the full raw history. - Preserve the existing checkpoint and recovery semantics while threading the compact state through the GDN backend, memory pool, and speculative utilities. ## Accuracy Tests - Exact state checks covered checkpoint capacity, cursor movement, radix-tree track snapshots, recovery, and sequential-reference comparisons. - Every production arm completed 112/112 identical requests with HTTP 200, fixed input length 88,786 tokens, exact output length 860 tokens, CUDA graph enabled, zero queueing/retractions/errors, and all four ranks at achieved batch 28 during the measured window. - The compact-history validation observed maximum absolute differences of 0.0078125 for the main state and 0.00390625 for the track state, while the active checkpoint path remained bitwise unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs in DP4, MTP with 6 draft tokens, TRTLLM-MHA split 1, ReplaySSM `extra_buffer`, radix-cache page size 64, and the same frozen 112-request cohort in every arm. - Workload: every request uses the same 88,786-token input and generates exactly 860 output tokens; all requests are prefetched first, no new prefill is admitted during measurement, and throughput is measured only from the pure-generation interval after the final prefill and before the first completion. - Acceptance criteria: all four ranks must report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no request completion inside the selected interval. | Variant | Pure-generation steps | Natural mean acceptance length | Target-step time (ms) | Output tokens/s/GPU | Change vs. baseline | SGL/TRT ratio | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline | 110 | 4.84318 | 33.19895 | 4,084.741 | — | 85.3193% | | Commit 1: circular history | 140 | 4.82857 | 32.64644 | 4,141.340 | +1.385% | 86.5015% | | Commit 2: compact materialization | 120 | 4.80208 | 31.13983 | 4,317.890 | +5.708% | 90.1891% | | TRT-LLM reference | Fixed-B28 reference | 4.8 (forced) | 28.07256 | 4,787.594 | Reference | 100% | - Commit 2 improves output throughput by 4.263% over commit 1 and reduces target-step time by 6.20% versus baseline. - The baseline-to-commit-1 mean context per rank changed from 102,456.7 to 103,394.3 tokens (+0.915%), while natural acceptance length decreased by 0.302%, so the measured gain is not explained by a favorable acceptance shift. - Nsight profiling measured the active GDN union decreasing from 5.40407 ms to 3.48862 ms per target step. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - signals.title: [Qwen3.5][MTP] Preserve online NVFP4 draft quantization for mixed checkpoints
signals.text: ## Motivation When a mixed ModelOpt checkpoint is used with an explicitly configured `nvfp4_online` speculative draft model, checkpoint detection currently overwrites the explicit draft quantization choice with `modelopt_mixed`. This prevents the MTP draft MoE from using the intended load-time NVFP4 conversion and FlashInfer CuTeDSL execution path. ## Modifications - Preserve an explicitly selected `nvfp4_online` draft quantization mode for both `modelopt_fp4` and `modelopt_mixed` checkpoints. - Keep the existing default behavior unchanged: when the user does not explicitly select draft quantization, the draft model still inherits the target model quantization. - Do not change the speculative decoding algorithm or automatically enable online NVFP4 on unsupported configurations. ## Accuracy Tests - The Blackwell production serving validation completed 112/112 identical requests with HTTP 200, fixed input length 88,786 tokens, exact output length 860 tokens, all four ranks at achieved batch 28, all CUDA graph captures enabled, zero queueing/retractions/errors, and natural mean acceptance length 4.79792. - This path is explicitly opt-in and limited by the existing SM100+ and FlashInfer MoE backend checks. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs in DP4, fixed ISL 88,786, exact OSL 860, 112 identical requests, MTP with 6 draft tokens, TRTLLM-MHA split 1, ReplaySSM circular history, and no request replenishment during the pure-generation measurement window. - Patch-level result with the same candidate command: before this change, checkpoint detection overwrites the explicit `nvfp4_online` draft setting with `modelopt_mixed`, which creates an incompatible draft runner/dispatcher combination and fails before serving; after this change, the command completes 112/112 requests. Because the unpatched control does not reach the benchmark, there is no patch-only throughput ratio. - The throughput numbers below compare two valid end-to-end draft backend configurations and are not an apple-to-apple attribution of the three-line compatibility fix. - Valid legacy baseline command; orchestration-only and identical arguments are omitted: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4> --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep ``` - Candidate command enabled by this fix: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4> --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --speculative-moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-quantization nvfp4_online ``` - Full configuration change used by the throughput experiment: ```diff --- baseline +++ candidate - --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep + --speculative-moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --speculative-moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-quantization nvfp4_online ``` | Valid configuration | Natural mean acceptance length | Target-step time (ms) | Output tokens/s/GPU | Configuration-level change | SGL/TRT ratio | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | DeepGEMM + DeepEP draft baseline | 4.80208 | 31.13983 | 4,317.890 | — | 90.1891% | | FlashInfer CuTeDSL + FlashInfer A2A + online-NVFP4 draft | 4.79792 | 30.71904 | 4,373.238 | +1.282% | 91.3452% | | TRT-LLM reference | 4.8 (forced) | 28.07256 | 4,787.594 | Reference | 100% | - Relative to the legacy configuration, profiling of the complete candidate tuple removes approximately 1.3672 ms/target-step of draft DeepGEMM work and 0.4218 ms/target-step of draft DeepEP communication; overlap limits the end-to-end gain, so these times are not added arithmetically. - The measured +1.282% belongs to the full runner, A2A backend, and draft-quantization tuple. This PR only preserves the explicit quantization request so that tuple can start; it does not establish an online-NVFP4-only or same-backend speedup. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is measured only from the all-rank fixed-B28 pure-generation interval after the final prefill and before the first request completion; it is not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [EAGLE] Prune draft-extend logits to selected rows
signals.text: ## Motivation During EAGLE draft extension under CUDA graph execution, the model computes full-vocabulary logits for every draft row even though the speculative worker only consumes selected per-request rows. The unnecessary LM-head rows increase graph time and temporary memory usage on the decode critical path. ## Modifications - Select the rows consumed by the speculative verifier before applying the LM head during draft-extend CUDA graph execution. - Keep the full six-row draft forward unchanged so hidden-state and speculative-state evolution remain identical. - Preserve the eager path and existing output contract while sizing the graph logits buffer for the selected rows. ## Accuracy Tests | Natural-acceptance metric | Baseline | Candidate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Completed requests | 112 / 112 | 112 / 112 | | Output length | 860 | 860 | | Mean acceptance length | 3.684250 | 3.652805 | | Acceptance rate | 0.536375 | 0.530488 | | CUDA graph enabled | Yes | Yes | | Queue / retractions / errors | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM-MHA, FlashInfer CuTeDSL MoE plus FlashInfer A2A for target and draft, NEXTN with 5 speculative steps and 6 draft tokens, online-NVFP4 draft weights, ReplaySSM circular history, Mamba `extra_buffer`, and CUDA graph tiers through batch 32. - Workload: one frozen 88,786-token input repeated as a 112-request cohort, 112 warmup requests with OSL 64, 112 measurement requests with exact OSL 860, temperature 0, fixed AL 4.8, and no request replenishment during the measured pure-generation interval. - Measurement gate: all four ranks must simultaneously report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no completion/drain row inside the selected interval. | Serving metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Stable rank intervals | 17 / 17 / 17 / 17 | 17 / 17 / 17 / 16 | — | | Mean context tokens/rank | 103,367.5 | 102,725.7 | -0.6209% | | Target-step host time | 29.688688 ms | 28.996720 ms | -0.691968 ms / -2.3307% | | Fixed-AL4.8 output tokens/s/GPU | 4,526.977 | 4,635.007 | +2.3864% | - To remove the small context difference, an independent exact-context match paired 40 windows at the same mean context of 102,342.4 tokens/rank and measured 4,542.499 to 4,653.987 output tokens/s/GPU (+2.4543%). - The final zero-resident-context drain row is excluded from both arms. | Nsight metric for draft-extend graph `10658` | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Graph time/GPU-step | 1.113471 ms | 0.974980 ms | -0.138491 ms / -12.44% | | Selected-row projection | 0.371574 ms | 0.296726 ms | -0.074848 ms | | Large output copy | 0.098430 ms | 0.017771 ms | -0.080659 ms | | Graph capture memory | 0.15 GB | 0.07 GB | -0.08 GB / -53.3% | - The Nsight capture contains 40 actual-B28 steps on every rank with CUDA graph enabled and queue depth 0. - Draft-decode graph `10637` still performs four full-vocabulary projections per target step by design; this optimization only owns draft-extend graph `10658`. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. - As a cross-engine diagnostic only, applying the measured within-SGL gain to the fixed-work authority gives 4,608.074 output tokens/s/GPU versus TRT-LLM at 4,791.788, or 96.166% with a 3.834% remaining gap; this does not replace a direct final integration comparison. ## Checklist - signals.text: Hey! We're releasing v1 of the `anthropic` SDK shortly. Your `anthropic` dependency has no upper bound, so your users will start getting 1.0, which would break `sglang`. signals.title: [XPU CI] Guardian bot: auto-disable PR on 2-run XPU regression (draft)
signals.text: ## Summary Draft — putting this up so it can be reviewed / iterated on tomorrow. Adds a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/xpu-ci-guardian.yml`) that watches `PR Test (XPU)` on `main`. When the last two consecutive runs on `main` fail, it opens a **draft** PR that inserts `disabled="..."` on the `register_xpu_ci(...)` marker for each failing test file and pings the XPU CI owner. A separate job auto-closes any open guardian PR once `main` goes green again. ## Design - **Watch** — schedule every 30 min + manual `workflow_dispatch` with a `dry_run` toggle. - **Detect (2-run rule)** — only acts when the last two runs on `main` both failed, so single flakes handled by `enable_retry` in `run_suite.py` don't trigger it. Also filters known infra-flake log patterns (`UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`, `Server failed to start`, `XPU out of memory`). - **Diagnose** — extracts `test/registered/**/*.py` paths from the failing job's `--log-failed`. - **Unblock (scope-limited)** — inserts `disabled="auto-disabled by xpu-ci-guardian: run <id>"` into the file's `register_xpu_ci(...)`. Never touches kernel code, test bodies, `run_suite.py`, or per-method `@unittest.skipIf`. Skips files that are already disabled and files that don't call `register_xpu_ci`. - **Dedup** — at most one open guardian PR at a time via the `xpu-ci-guardian` label. - **PR body** — lists failing files with the last 5 commits on each, so the reviewer can jump straight to the probable culprit (as PR #33431 was in the current fire). - **Sweep** — companion job closes any open guardian PR when the next main run is green. - **Never auto-merges** — PR opens as a draft and only a human can promote / merge it. ## Required secrets on the fork's Actions - `GITHUB_TOKEN` (default; read-only for detection). - `BOT_PR_TOKEN` — fine-grained PAT with `contents:write` on `arathi-hlab/sglang` and `pull-requests:write` on `sgl-project/sglang`. ## Enablement checklist (before turning it on) - [ ] Merge (or land into the fork only, if we decide it shouldn't live upstream). - [ ] Add `BOT_PR_TOKEN` secret on the fork. - [ ] Manually run once with `dry_run=true` and inspect the workflow's outputs. - [ ] Manually run once with `dry_run=false` against a known-failing history to confirm the PR body/format looks right. - [ ] Add the `xpu-ci-guardian` label to the label set on `sgl-project/sglang`. ## Explicitly out of scope for this bot - Auto-generating actual code / kernel fixes (LLM-authored kernel patches are wrong often enough that reviewing them costs more than writing them from scratch). - Deep classification (e.g. distinguishing correctness vs. accuracy assertions). The bot just disables; the human writes the fix. - Alerting for non-XPU CI. This is scoped narrowly on purpose. ## Test plan - [ ] Run the workflow manually with `dry_run=true` — the `detect` job should classify the current XPU state and set `act` correctly without opening any PR. - [ ] Run with `dry_run=false` on a synthetic branch where I forcibly log two failing runs, and confirm the PR opens with the right title / labels / reviewer. - [ ] Trigger `sweep-when-green` manually after a subsequent green run — it should close the previously-opened guardian PR. - [ ] Confirm the guardian PR does NOT open a second time while another is open (dedup by `xpu-ci-guardian` label). ## Not included yet (defer to follow-up) - Slack notification hook — trivial to add via `slackapi/slack-github-action` when a channel + token are chosen. - Nightly weekly-summary email of caught regressions. --- 🤖 Draft raised now so it can be reviewed tomorrow morning; happy to iterate on scope / triggers / notification medium. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32281257858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32281257858)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32281257526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32281257526)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(sgl-router): --default-top-k / --default-top-p to set fleet-wide sampling defaults
signals.text: The router forwards requests to the engine, so sampling defaults are normally the engine's job (`generation_config.json` + `--sampling-defaults model`), which requires editing the checkpoint. These flags let an operator set a fleet-wide default `top_k` / `top_p` **at the router** instead. ## Behavior Mirrors the existing `--max-output-tokens` injection: the value is injected into the forwarded `/v1/chat/completions` body **only when the request omits the field** (absent or explicit `null`), so a **client-supplied `top_k` / `top_p` always wins**. Unset (the default) forwards the body untouched — **no behavior change**. - Per-model config, validated at startup: `top_p` in `(0, 1]`, `top_k >= 1`. - Implemented in `build_outgoing_body` alongside the `rid` / `input_ids` / `max_tokens` injections; `RequestProbe` peeks `top_k`/`top_p` to decide fill-if-absent via the new `default_when_absent` helper. - Scope: the `/v1/chat/completions` handler (the only route the router rewrites). ## Usage ``` --default-top-k 1000 --default-top-p 0.95 ``` ## Tests - `default_when_absent`: fills only when missing; client value wins; `null` treated as absent. - `build_outgoing_body` injects both values. - CLI flags reach `ModelConfig` and reject out-of-range values. Verified on a CPU devbox against the sgl-router CI checks: `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo +nightly fmt -- --check` all clean; full `cargo test` green (lib 955, bin 3, component 57, proxy 118 — 0 failed). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32283354838](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32283354838)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32283354394](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32283354394)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [GDN] Validate FlashInfer Cake CP prefill on Blackwell
signals.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer [#4539](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4539) replaces the SM100/SM103 CP-selected GDN prefill implementation with the Cake backend while preserving the public `chunk_gated_delta_rule` API and its `use_cp="auto"` policy. SGLang already calls that public API; this PR makes the auto policy explicit and adds an SGLang-level route/contract test for the new backend. This PR depends on FlashInfer #4539 and a subsequent FlashInfer release. It intentionally does not pin SGLang production dependencies to an unreleased Git commit; the new test skips when the installed FlashInfer build does not yet expose the Cake route. ## Modifications - Pass `use_cp="auto"` explicitly from `FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`. - Add an SM100/SM103 BF16 GQA generic-tail test through the real SGLang fixture and `FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`. - Require the test invocation to enter Cake exactly once and make the legacy SM100 non-CP route fatal. - Compare output and selected final-state rows against the same FlashInfer revision with `use_cp=False` at `atol=rtol=1e-2`. - Verify Q/K/V/gate/beta/cu-seqlens/cache indices and unselected state rows are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.3, driver 580.167.08: - Targeted SGLang pytest: `1 passed, 7 deselected` (Slurm job `518335`; the test executed rather than skipping). - Candidate route: FlashInfer #4539 Cake path; external/non-CP fallback is fatal. - The SGLang route test compares #4539 Cake against the same candidate revision with `use_cp=False`; output and selected final state match at `atol=rtol=1e-2`. - The benchmark runner independently repeats that numerical comparison on B=1, L=65 and enforces exact input and unselected-state immutability for every timed row. - Maximum observed absolute output error: `2.44140625e-4`. - Maximum observed absolute selected-state error: `3.90625e-3`. - Both candidate and baseline preserve all input tensors and unselected state rows exactly. Adapter evidence JSON SHA-256: `0dfe9da69166585bcfd176f32cadc688aaf7794e29d75d08429ac3c7e1a97c58`; evidence-manifest SHA-256: `df1f8b4d8ab7508e2288fc14a41be1e32a16b8ce5e8f5d8890804b44e200e3ee`. ### Model-level GSM8K On the same GB300, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` was evaluated on the same 200 GSM8K questions with 5-shot completion prompts, one request at a time, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=512`. Radix caching was disabled in both arms because FlashInfer CP prefill does not yet support the state-checkpoint outputs needed by SGLang's radix state tracking. | Prefill arm | GSM8K exact match | Difference vs. Triton | |---|---:|---:| | FlashInfer #4539 Cake | 178/200 (0.890) | 0.000 | | Triton control | 178/200 (0.890) | — | For the Cake arm, the live dispatcher must report `extend=FlashInferGDNKernel`, produce SM103 Cake cubins in a job-unique empty workspace, and contain zero non-CP fallback warnings. The Triton arm must report `extend=TritonGDNKernel` and produce no Cake cubins. Both arms must exceed the predeclared 0.80 accuracy threshold. This is an accuracy comparison, not an end-to-end speed claim: decode uses Triton in both arms and dominates the sequential evaluation latency. GSM8K Slurm job: `518440`; result JSON SHA-256: `82523bca3fd65c13031cb15a53ccd1486d3671c28d46cc8582a37e746ed3570e`; evidence-manifest SHA-256: `3c5d92df3f25c5cbf4fac24c59cc4691eecfd6bd1603010aeff49f5c33060703`; dataset SHA-256: `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.3, driver 580.167.08. These are SGLang adapter-level prefill calls (`FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`) with BF16 Q/K/V/state, Hq=Hk=2, Hv=8, D=128. Each row uses an exact shape cell present in the original PR4078 benchmark set. The BF16 SGLang input/state profile is stated separately and is not presented as PR4078's dtype profile; no additional shape rows are included. | Batch | Sequence lengths | #4539 Cake (ms) | Current upstream CP (ms) | Speedup | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | `[2048]` | 0.442594 | 0.436882 | 0.987x | | 1 | `[8192]` | 0.445762 | 0.463090 | 1.039x | | 4 | `[2048, 2048, 2048, 2048]` | 0.443410 | 0.461602 | 1.041x | Geometric-mean speedup: **1.022x**. The B=1, L=2048 row is a measured 1.3% regression; the other two rows improve by 3.9% and 4.1%, respectively. Method: same-process ABBA paired samples using Cake `bench_gpu_time_interleaved` (`bench_gpu_time`), required CUPTI GPU activity timing, cold-L2 flush before each sample, 20 ms warmup and 100 ms measurement budget per arm, and a steady-state SM clock gate. The rows collected 422, 342, and 392 samples per arm at 2070/2070 MHz in Slurm job `518335`. During timed rows, both candidate and baseline non-CP paths were fatal, so every measured call used the intended CP route; the dedicated correctness case intentionally invoked the candidate revision's non-CP path as its numerical reference. Commits: - SGLang: `5fc7baa6dd458f37fdf50d9ad4817ad17365e05e` - FlashInfer candidate: `59da61dd534f74ea3acf8ada60c4a3935e2a8df9` - Current upstream FlashInfer baseline: `05e5d927399d62a2479c430ad3e167738254d760` - Cake timing harness: `25536d8f0acd0eb4503d9fd6b46509b9ac76a115` ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the [formatting guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add a real SGLang route/contract test. - [x] Provide correctness and paired GPU performance results. - [x] Bind the final model-level GSM8K result. ## Review and Merge Process This remains a draft until FlashInfer #4539 is merged and available in an SGLang-supported FlashInfer release. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32286382201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32286382201)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32286381900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32286381900)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kimi K3] Select FlashInfer MXFP4 for SM107 auto MoE
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 packed-MXFP4 models automatically select the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE runner on SM100 and SM103, but the current exact-architecture gate excludes SM107. Consequently, `--moe-runner-backend auto` can fall through to BF16 weight materialization during model loading and exhaust device memory. This is a policy follow-up to #33997. It remains a draft until SGLang's stock FlashInfer artifacts are qualified for the SM107 SiTU MXFP4 path. ## Modifications - Extend Kimi-K3 packed-MXFP4 auto MoE selection from SM100/SM103 to exact SM107. - Preserve every explicit `--moe-runner-backend` choice. - Add unit coverage for the SM107 positive case, a neighboring-architecture negative case, non-MXFP4 input, registry wiring, and explicit backend choices. ## Accuracy Tests SM107 stock-artifact launch, numerics, and memory qualification is pending. This PR must remain in draft and must not merge until that qualification passes, with the pinned FlashInfer artifact/version updated if required. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Pending the same SM107 stock-artifact qualification. The intended comparison is `auto` against explicit `flashinfer_mxfp4`; this change should make those routes identical. ## Checklist - [x] Format the changed files with the repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add focused CPU unit coverage. - [x] No user-facing documentation change is required for this model-specific auto-selection extension. - [ ] Provide SM107 stock-artifact accuracy, memory, and performance results before marking ready. - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. ## Dependency / merge gate Do not merge until the stock FlashInfer artifacts used by SGLang are qualified for SM107 SiTU MXFP4, updating the pinned artifact/version if required. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32288065413](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32288065413)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32289143314](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32289143314)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation Migrate SGLang's FlashInfer MLA backend to the unified planning and tensor APIs introduced by [FlashInfer #4031](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4031). The legacy positional planning and split-tensor run forms are deprecated by that API. SGLang also needs to retain its sync-free CUDA graph replay paths and capture-stable metadata buffers during the migration. AI assistance was used under human direction to implement and validate this draft. ## Modifications - Use `MLAPlanMetadata.csr` and explicit planning keywords for decode and paged prefill. - Pass split queries and packed KV caches through the unified tensor-first run interface. - Adapt the sync-free decode and prefill planners to structured metadata. - Keep initial target-verify graph capture on CUDA metadata, then use pinned host metadata during replay. - Add focused coverage for fast-prefill buffer refresh and make MLA integration tests reject deprecated API warnings. ## Accuracy Tests Targeted B200 validation against FlashInfer #4031: - `test/registered/attention/unittests/mla/test_flashinfer.py`: 7 passed, 1 skipped, and 15 subtests passed. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_mla_dense_block_table.py`: 15 passed. The coverage includes eager execution, CUDA graph capture/replay, speculative target verification, fast planning, and unified MLA cache layouts. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No standalone speed benchmark was rerun for this API migration. signals.title: Fail fast for MXFP4 MegaMoE/DeepEP on non-SM100 GPUs
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes the late, misleading failure in #35557. Serving the stock MXFP4 `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with expert parallelism (`--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, i.e. MegaMoE) on **SM90 (Hopper)** crashes only at **decode CUDA-graph capture**, after a full weight load + MHC prewarm (~minutes): ``` Capture cuda graph failed: Assertion error (.../heuristics/.../layout.hpp:57): ab.scalar_type() == kPackedFP4 and arch_major == 10 ``` `arch_major == 10` is SM100. MegaMoE routes experts through DeepGEMM's packed-FP4 grouped GEMM, which is SM100-only; Hopper has no native FP4. The printed remedies (lower `--mem-fraction-static`, reduce `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`, disable the decode graph) don't apply to an architecture requirement — disabling the graph just moves the same kernel to eager decode. This has bitten more than one user (see #35557 and discussion #26564). ## Change Raise a clear error at MXFP4 quant-method construction — before weights load — when `use_mega_moe` is selected on a non-SM100 GPU, naming the two paths that **do** work on Hopper: - stock MXFP4 with **tensor parallelism** (Marlin backend; no `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`), or - the **FP8-converted** checkpoint (e.g. `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8`) for DP-attention + DeepEP. The guard is gated on `use_mega_moe`, so it is **inert** for: - the **FP8** MegaMoE path (DeepGEMM FP8 grouped GEMM runs on SM90), and - the non-MegaMoE **Marlin / FlashInfer** MXFP4 backends (which already gate on `is_sm90_supported()`). ## Notes / for review - This is an interim guard. The real fix is Hopper MXFP4 EP support (route the MegaMoE/DeepEP FP4 experts to the existing SM90 Marlin runner); I'm happy to work that separately and it would supersede this guard. Design discussion in #35557. - I could not run this on hardware (no local SM90 build); the change is a construction-time `raise`, and the placement mirrors the existing `is_sm90_supported()` checks in `mxfp4_marlin_moe.py`. A maintainer sanity-check on the hook point is welcome. - Minor: the guard fires for any non-SM100 GPU. SM120 would also fail the `arch_major == 10` assertion, so raising there is correct; if `is_sm100_supported()` is ever broadened to include SM120, this predicate should be revisited. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32291318181](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291318181)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32291317852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291317852)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix: account native Qwen3.5/3.8 MTP KV layers in target pool sizing
signals.text: ## Problem For Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 native in-checkpoint MTP (EAGLE/STANDALONE speculative decoding with **no** `--speculative-draft-model-path`), the target worker never learns the draft layer count: `eagle_draft_num_layers` stays `None` because it is only resolved from the external draft model config. The draft KV pool is then **not budgeted into the target cell size**, so on a 32 GB card the draft pool allocation overruns the static memory envelope and OOMs during initialization. ## Correct accounting The native MTP draft physically allocates one full-context draft K/V layer. With the current FP8 geometry: - target: 16 full-attention layers (64 layers, full attention every 4) × 2048 B/token = **32,768 B/token** - native MTP draft: 1 layer × 2048 B/token = **2,048 B/token** - **total = 34,816 B/token (34 KiB/token)** ## Change `resolve_spec_aux_hidden_state_config` now passes the target `model_config` into `_resolve_eagle_aux_hidden_state`. When EAGLE/STANDALONE is active, no external draft path is set, and the target's text config declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, that value is used as `eagle_draft_num_layers`. ```python mtp_num_hidden_layers = getattr(model_config.hf_text_config, "mtp_num_hidden_layers", None) if mtp_num_hidden_layers is not None and int(mtp_num_hidden_layers) > 0: config.eagle_draft_num_layers = int(mtp_num_hidden_layers) ``` **There is one native MTP hidden layer reused across every draft step, so the count is not multiplied by `speculative_num_steps`.** MTP3 means three speculative steps, not three persistent KV layers. ## Scope / non-behavior-changes - Narrow and architecture-aware: the fallback only fires for native Qwen MTP (no external draft path). It never overrides a user-supplied `--speculative-draft-model-path`. - The EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state resolution stays inside the external-draft branch (it needs the external draft config), so the native-MTP path can never reference an undefined `draft_model_config`. - All other architectures, external EAGLE drafts, and non-speculative runs behave exactly as before (`eagle_draft_num_layers` stays `None` when `mtp_num_hidden_layers` is absent). ## Tests `test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_native_mtp_kv_accounting.py` (CPU, `register_cpu_ci`): 1. native Qwen MTP with `eagle_draft_num_layers=None` and `mtp_num_hidden_layers=1` → resolved to 1; 2. multi-layer checkpoints budget every declared layer; 3. **one-layer draft KV inclusion**: end-to-end through the real pool cell-size math — real `Qwen3_5TextConfig` (64 layers, `full_attention_interval=4` → 16 full-attention layers) resolves as a GDN hybrid, per-layer FP8 KV = 2048 B/token, target 32,768 B/token, `(1 + 1/16)` scale → **34,816 B/token**; 4. external EAGLE draft path precedence (draft's own layer count wins, target `mtp_num_hidden_layers` ignored); 5. no regression for non-MTP models (`mtp_num_hidden_layers` absent → `None`, no-op); 6. draft worker exclusion (never double-counts via the target fallback). ## Validation With this fix plus the standalone pre-draft-KV alias work (separate PR), native-Qwen MTP EAGLE boots at `mem-fraction-static 0.985` and serves 262144-token context on RTX 5090 where the draft KV pool previously OOM'd. This is a correctness fix: the draft KV cost must be part of the memory accounting regardless of hardware. ## Not included - No `--max-total-tokens` policy override. - No early-alias / memory-optimization changes (separate PR). - No hardware-specific hacks or allocator workarounds. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32307465731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307465731)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32307465571](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307465571)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
