signals.title: opt: bind native Qwen MTP embed/lm_head before memory pool allocation
signals.text: ## Problem `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` (the native-Qwen MTP wrapper, `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp`) allocates **BF16 skeleton tensors** for the draft model's `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` during construction: - `model.embed_tokens.weight` `[248320, 5120]` = 2,542,796,800 bytes - `lm_head.weight` `[248320, 5120]` = 2,542,796,800 bytes - **5,085,593,600 bytes nominal (~4.7 GiB)** combined These are **not independent learned MTP weights**: the checkpoint does not ship separate MTP embed/head tensors (only `mtp.*` keys exist), and they are ultimately intended to share the target model's embedding and `lm_head`. `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head()` already deletes them and rebinds the draft to the target via `set_embed_and_head` / `set_lm_head_from_target` — but it only ran **after** `draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool()`, i.e. after both the target and draft KV pools were allocated, so the multi-GiB duplicate residency coexisted with pool construction. ## Initialization-order root cause ``` scheduler.init_model_worker() -> init_tp_model_worker() -> target TpModelWorker.__init__() -> ModelRunner.initialize() -> load_model() # target weights resident -> maybe_init_draft_worker() -> EAGLEWorkerV2.__init__() -> EagleDraftWorker.__init__() -> draft TpModelWorker(is_draft_worker=True) # native-MTP weights resident -> self.draft_runner assigned >>> EARLY NATIVE-QWEN MTP ALIAS (this PR) <<< -> init_memory_pools() -> init_target_memory_pool() # target Mamba / KV alloc -> draft pool allocation ``` The alias previously happened at the end of `EagleDraftWorker.alloc_memory_pool()`. Both the target and draft models are already fully loaded by the time `EagleDraftWorker.__init__` finishes — so the earliest safe point is right after `self.draft_runner = self.draft_worker.model_runner`, **before** the scheduler allocates any memory pools. ## Change - In `EagleDraftWorker.__init__`, immediately after `self.draft_runner` is assigned, run the existing embed/head-sharing logic via `_bind_native_qwen_mtp_before_pool()` and store the result in `self._early_mtp_alias_bound`. - `alloc_memory_pool()` now **consumes** the precomputed flag and skips the original post-pool `init_token_map()` / `init_lm_head()` calls when the early bind ran (the alias is idempotent). - The bind reuses the existing `init_lm_head()` path (`set_embed_and_head` + `set_lm_head_from_target`). ## Safety / guarding - Narrow guard: only `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` from `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp` takes the early path. - **Token-mapped (hot-token) heads bail** (`hot_token_id is not None`) and keep the original post-pool ordering — the early bind is unsafe when the head is cloned/reordered. - EAGLE3 / standalone / external-draft / multi-layer workers are untouched (they never construct this class or keep their own ordering). - Genuine MTP decoder / `fc` / norm parameters are never modified — only the embed/head aliases are rebound. - The bind asserts embed storage is shared, `lm_head` module is shared, and zero duplicate bytes remain before pool allocation. - Startup weight-load overlap (`--startup-weight-load-mode=overlap`) is not supported for speculative decoding / hybrid-GDN configs (rejected in `startup_weight_load.py`), so serial weight load always completes before this code runs. ## Memory impact On an RTX 5090 (32 GB, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + native MTP + ReplaySSM EAGLE): | step | free VRAM | |---|---| | pre-alias (both models loaded) | ~8.9 GiB | | after early bind | ~14.0 GiB | | released before target KV alloc | **5,054,136,320 bytes (~4.707 GiB)** | Target KV allocation now sees the freed headroom (Gittensor checkpoint: 14.04 GiB free at the target pool step vs ~8.9 GiB before; RadixArk checkpoint: ~10.9 GiB). ## Deterministic parity Same prompt + `temperature 0.0`: ```text output_ids: [271, 9419, 271, 248068, 198, 760, 1156, 1018] ``` Bit-identical to the unpatched control and to the previous pre-draft-KV alias patch — the alias rebinds tensors, it never changes logits. ## Before / after real-world initialization evidence | checkpoint | previous alias timing (pre-draft-KV) | this PR (init-time) | |---|---|---| | Gittensor Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 262144 ctx, MTP3, 4 Mamba slots | boot + `/generate` 200 | boot + `/generate` 200 | | RadixArk Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 230k/250k/260k ctx | **OOM during target KV construction** (~220k/230k) | boot + `/generate` 200 at 230k, 250k, 260k | Heavier checkpoints (RadixArk) OOMed during **target** KV allocation with the earlier pre-draft-KV patch because the skeleton duplicates were still resident while the target pool profiled and allocated; moving the alias to `__init__` eliminates them first. These are measured single-hardware cases, not universal guarantees. ## Tests `test/registered/unit/spec/test_native_mtp_early_alias.py` (CPU, `register_cpu_ci`): - guard narrowness: only `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` / `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp` takes the early path; same-name-different-module rejected; - alias timing: `alloc_memory_pool` consumes the precomputed `_early_mtp_alias_bound`, never re-binds, and skips post-pool init when it ran; - fallback ordering preserved: non-MTP drafts still run `init_token_map` + `init_lm_head` after the pool; - storage sharing: draft embed/head share target storage after the bind; - genuine MTP weights untouched. ## Untested (honest) - EAGLE3 with native-Qwen MTP (aux-hidden-state path) — not exercised; the guard excludes it from the early path by construction. - Standalone / external EAGLE draft models — not exercised. - TP/PP configurations — not exercised. - Token-map / hot-token heads — covered by the fallback (bail), but not end-to-end. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32307446680](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307446680)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32307446611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307446611)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [sampling] Fix int32 offset overflow in top-k renorm Triton kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation The top-k renorm Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` compute flattened element offsets as `row * vocab_size + offsets` and `program_id * BLOCK_SIZE + arange(...)`. Both products are computed in int32, so for large `batch x vocab_size` tensors the offsets can silently overflow, corrupting loads/stores. ## Modifications Cast the row / program id to `tl.int64` before the multiplication in `_mask_and_partial_sum_kernel` and `_normalize_kernel`, so offset arithmetic is done in 64-bit. ## Checklist - Ran `pre-commit` on the changed file (passed). - Verified on an internal setup exercising the top-k renorm path. ## Original commits - `49831150a` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32306179456](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32306179456)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32306179103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32306179103)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Fold a quantized-head DFlash2 selector into the draft CUDA graph
signals.text: ## Motivation Depends on #35496 (its commit is included below; review only the second commit). With quantized-head support in the selector, those deployments still lose the draft CUDA graph: `_maybe_build_draft_sampler` rejects a non-dense head before it ever reaches the selector branch, so `_draft_sampler` stays `None` and every decode step runs the eager `_propose_selector_block`. The deployments this affects — quantized targets on small GPUs, low concurrency, latency-sensitive — are exactly the ones that can least afford per-step Python and unfused launches. ## Modifications - `speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py` `_maybe_build_draft_sampler`: the selector branch accepts a dense head or one the quant gate admits, so it is captured into `_SelectorDraftSampler`. Capture safety comes from the head itself: the target's own logits path already runs the same quant kernel under its CUDA graphs. The dense-only screen still guards the non-selector static-matmul sampler below. ## Accuracy Tests RTX 5090, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, greedy: boot log confirms `DFLASH selector decode (greedy + sampling) folded into the draft cuda graph`; output parity with the eager path; `sgl-eval run gsm8k` 200q scores 95.5% (98.0% target-only, near-tie divergence — see #35496). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Isolated A/B on the same cell (RTX 5090, random ISL 1024 / OSL 1024, concurrency 1, fp8 KV), only this worker change swapped: | selector sampler | Median TPOT | output tok/s | accept length | |---|---|---|---| | eager fallback (#35496 alone) | 5.61 ms | 169.7 | 3.5793859649 | | folded (this PR) | 5.58 ms | 170.6 | 3.5793859649 | ~0.5% at bs1: the draft forward is already graph-replayed either way, so the eager path only leaves the selector's sampling ops in Python once per verify round. Accept lengths match to full precision — the two paths compute identical candidates. The win should grow with batch size and verify frequency; treat this PR as consistency (the selector no longer silently degrades to a Python path for the heads #35496 enables) plus a small latency gain, not a headline speedup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [Spec] Fail loudly when the DFlash2 selector top_k exceeds the org vocab
signals.text: ## Motivation Depends on #35496 (its commit is included below; review only the second commit). #35496 masks a quantized head's padded vocab tail to `-inf` rather than cropping it, which keeps the logits contiguous but leaves the padded columns in the tensor. A `selector_top_k` wider than the org vocab would then select those columns and return out-of-vocab candidate ids silently, where the dense path raises from `topk`. Nothing validates `selector_top_k` against the vocab today. Unreachable with current checkpoints — `selector_top_k` is a handful of candidates against a vocab of tens of thousands — so this is a guard against a malformed draft config, not a fix for an observed failure. ## Modifications - `models/dflash.py`: assert `num_org >= top_k` in `_project_candidate_logits`, so both the quantized and dense paths fail the same way. Host-side integer compare: free during graph capture, negligible on the eager path. ## Accuracy Tests `test_dflash_logits.py`: 7/7 pass. The new test drives a padded head with `top_k > org_vocab_size` and asserts the `AssertionError`; mutation-verified (removing the assert turns it red). ## Speed Tests and Profiling None; the check is an integer comparison outside the kernel path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32313659722](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313659722)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32313659600](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313659600)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(spec): allow independent draft model config overrides
signals.text: ## Motivation Independent target and speculative checkpoints can require incompatible Hugging Face configuration overrides. SGLang currently applies `--json-model-override-args` to both, including DFlash block inference and DSpARK draft inspection. A target's long-context or multimodal overrides can therefore corrupt draft configuration loading. ## Modifications - Add `--speculative-draft-model-override-args`. - Fall back to `--json-model-override-args` when the draft-specific option is unset, preserving current behavior. - Use the resolved draft override in `ModelConfig`, DFlash config inference, DSpARK checkpoint inspection, and speculative algorithm alias detection. - Only construct draft configuration kwargs when a draft checkpoint exists, preserving draftless duck-typed custom algorithm hooks. - Document the new option in the speculative-decoding parameter reference. - Add CPU tests for fallback, explicit precedence, and independent target/draft `ModelConfig` construction. ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_model_override_args.py`: passed 4/4 under pytest. - `test/registered/unit/spec/test_spec_registry.py`: passed 28/28, including the draftless custom algorithm handler path. - Coverage includes draft override propagation to Gemma4 assistant architecture detection through an actual mocked promotion to `FROZEN_KV_MTP`, including a decrypted draft configuration file. - Integrated with separate Qwen3.8 target and DFlash2 draft checkpoints using distinct YaRN override structures at 524K context admission. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Configuration-only change; no steady-state performance impact. ## Checklist - [x] Run pinned Black, Ruff, and isort checks. - [x] Add focused unit tests. - [x] Update user-facing documentation. - [x] Preserve backward compatibility. - [ ] Run upstream CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32313060282](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313060282)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32313060078](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313060078)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(jit): pin nvcc to the fingerprinted host compiler
signals.text: ## Motivation The SGLang JIT cache fingerprints `CXX`, and the final host link uses that compiler, but nvcc otherwise selects its own default host compiler. CUDA host code can consequently be compiled with a compiler different from both the JIT cache identity and final linker. ## Modifications - Pass the resolved host compiler to nvcc through `-ccbin`. - Add CPU coverage with a generated CUDA wrapper translation unit, proving the same compiler reaches both the Ninja host command and nvcc `-ccbin` flags. - Leave the HIP flags unchanged. - Quote the `-ccbin` path with the same Ninja/shell rules as the host compiler, including executable paths containing spaces or `$`. ## Accuracy Tests - Focused generated-Ninja CUDA-edge assertion passed. - Path-quoting coverage includes both a space and `$`. - `test/registered/kernels/test_jit_cache.py`: passed 43/43 under pytest. - The active native build and runtime JIT path have been exercised with GCC/G++ 15 on CUDA 13 and SM120. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Build-correctness change only; no inference performance claim. ## Checklist - [x] Run pinned Black, Ruff, and isort checks. - [x] Add focused unit coverage. - [x] Verify that a CUDA compile edge consumes the generated cudaflags. - [x] Run the complete upstream JIT cache test file. - [ ] Run upstream CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32310940208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32310940208)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32310940350](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32310940350)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Return 400 for multimodal token/data mismatches
signals.text: ## Summary Return a `ValueError` as soon as a rendered multimodal placeholder has no corresponding media item. The OpenAI serving layer already maps `ValueError` to HTTP 400. ## Why A Qwen-VL request with a valid image plus ordinary text that happens to contain a Qwen vision marker currently reaches `legacy_load_mm_data()` with more image markers than image data. The previous code logged the mismatch, returned partial work, and later raised an uncaught `RuntimeError`, producing HTTP 500. This PR makes the malformed request a clear client error and adds a regression test. It does not attempt to define a lossless escaping scheme for literal reserved model tokens; that broader design question is tracked in #35582. ## Validation `PYTHONPATH=python:. /home/ozgur/venvs/sglang16/bin/python test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_base_processor_bad_input.py` Result: 9 tests passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32310944848](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32310944848)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32310944781](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32310944781)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(spec): build mRoPE positions for ragged verify
signals.text: ## Motivation Compact speculative verification packs a variable number of tokens per request. `compute_spec_mrope_positions` currently reshapes those positions as a dense `[batch, tokens]` tensor. The reshape fails when request lengths differ; when graph padding makes it divisible, deltas can instead be assigned to the wrong request. ## Modifications - Detect a compact ragged verification layout. - Map packed real tokens through the live ragged offsets and apply each request's mRoPE delta. - Preserve zero delta for invalid graph-tier tail padding. - Preserve the existing dense verification path. - Add CUDA regression coverage using a real bucket-rounded layout with tail padding, plus the unchanged dense path. ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_ragged_mrope_positions.py`: passed 2/2 on local CUDA. It covers the usual `batch_size == layout.bs` bucket-rounded case with a negative final-request delta and verifies tail padding remains zero. - Historical Qwen3.8+DSpARK compact qualification reproduced the original failure when the live batch shrank 4→3 with ten packed verify tokens. - After the correction, ordinary OpenAI-compatible requests completed 4→3→2→1 CUDA-graph transitions and a 454,685-token request recovered all three needles exactly. The historical integrated run used the composite local SM120 runtime branch, which also carried the required XQA/GDN support. It demonstrates the observed failure and corrected behavior, not one-commit standalone runtime deployment. The later DFlash2 qualification is deliberately excluded: DFlash2 did not emit ragged verify layouts and therefore did not exercise this code path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed claim. The patch replaces an invalid dense-layout assumption with fixed-shape device-side offset lookup, gather, and masking during speculative metadata construction. ## Checklist - [x] Run pinned Black, Ruff, and isort checks. - [x] Add a registered CUDA test with real graph-bucket rounding. - [x] Validate the affected DSpARK compact runtime shape on SM120. - [ ] Run upstream CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32311114796](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32311114796)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32311114743](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32311114743)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: docker: fix CUDA-13 build — rename NCCL_VERSION ARG to avoid base image ENV collision
signals.text: ## Problem The CUDA-13 branch in `docker/Dockerfile` runs: ``` pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps "nvidia-nccl-cu13==${NCCL_VERSION}" ``` The `nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-cudnn-devel-ubuntu24.04` base image sets `ENV NCCL_VERSION=2.28.3-1` (Debian/apt format), which **shadows** the Dockerfile's `ARG NCCL_VERSION=2.30.7` at `RUN` time. So pip requests `2.28.3-1`, which is not a valid PyPI version, and the build fails: ``` ERROR: No matching distribution found for nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.28.3-1 ``` ## Fix Rename the ARG to `SGL_NCCL_VERSION` so it no longer collides with the base image's `ENV NCCL_VERSION`; the intended `2.30.7` is used. This matches `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`'s `install_nccl()`, which already hardcodes `2.30.7`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32316009906](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316009906)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316009800](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316009800)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix full prefill CUDA graph padding and EAGLE capture
signals.text: ## Motivation Full prefill CUDA graphs replay fixed token buckets that may be larger than the live batch. Models that mask padded hidden states need the live `num_token_non_padded` boundary even when attention tensors are not gathered. Without it, padded rows can propagate through the captured graph. EAGLE target prefill also consumes the full target hidden-state sequence. FullCG previously captured the configured return-hidden-state mode, which could be insufficient and force target prefill back to eager execution. ## Modifications - Register and populate `num_token_non_padded` for FullCG, including non-gathered execution. - Capture `FULL` hidden states for EAGLE target prefill under FullCG while retaining `LAST` for breakable draft workers. - Keep the EAGLE eager fallback specific to `tc_piecewise`, whose fixed capture ceiling can remain below `FULL`. - Add focused regression tests for the non-gathered token boundary and FullCG EAGLE admission. ## Accuracy Tests No model math or kernels are changed. - 42 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The changes update CUDA graph metadata and capture mode; they do not add work to attention or model kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add focused regression tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this graph-correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32317528205](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317528205)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32317528065](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317528065)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Support 128-aligned hidden sizes in the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant kernel
signals.text: ## Motivation `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` requantizes DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It required the hidden size to fill a whole number of 1024-element blocks: ```python K_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024 assert x.size(2) % K_BLOCK_SIZE == 0 grid = (x.size(2) // K_BLOCK_SIZE, 32, x.size(0)) ``` so it rejected any expert hidden size that is only 128-aligned — 3584, for example. Since `W4AFp8MoEMethod` pins the low-latency wire format to fp8 (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/w4afp8.py:286-295`) and `apply_deepep_ll()` rejects a payload that carries no per-token-group scales (`w4afp8.py:347-351`), such a model has no working low-latency path at all: the fp8 payload it is handed trips the assert during decode CUDA-graph capture. 1024 was the only constraint of its kind on that path. `w1_scale` is `[E, K // 512, N * 8]`, so 512-alignment is genuinely required; DeepEP's low-latency fp8 scales are `[E, M, hidden // 128]` (column-major in the last two dims for TMA), so the payload is always a whole number of 128-wide scale groups. A hidden size of 3584 satisfies both — 7 × 512, 28 groups — and was rejected only by the 1024 block. ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`: - Take the grid from `triton.cdiv` and drop the assert. - Mask the k lanes in `_fp8_per_token_quant_to_per_tensor_quant_kernel`: on the hidden load, on the store, and on the scale load, whose offsets derive from `k_offsets` and would otherwise read past the scale tensor in the tail block. - Put the masked form behind `HAS_K_TAIL: tl.constexpr`, so hidden sizes that fill every block keep the original unmasked loads and the same launch geometry. This mirrors `_silu_and_mul_post_per_tensor_quant_kernel` in the same file, which already pairs a `cdiv` grid with a masked fast axis. Adds `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant.py` (`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`). ## Accuracy Tests The new test checks k ∈ {7168, 3584, 1152} — one exact multiple of 1024 and two tailed, so both specializations compile — against a torch reference, and asserts that rows past `masked_m` are left exactly as the caller wrote them. Inputs are integers in [-8, 8] with power-of-two group scales, so every intermediate is exactly representable in e4m3 and the comparison can be `rtol=0, atol=0`. (The kernel saturates fp8 overflow — `cvt.rn.satfinite`, clamping to 448.0 — where `Tensor.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` produces NaN, so a torch-reference test has to stay inside range deliberately.) One H200, torch 2.11.0+cu130 / triton 3.6.0: ``` test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[7168] PASSED test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[3584] PASSED test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[1152] PASSED 3 passed in 16.75s ``` Swapping this commit's kernel for the current `main` file makes the two tailed cases fail while 7168 still passes, so the test covers the change rather than just passing alongside it. A wider matrix run out of tree — both scale layouts (contiguous and DeepEP's column-major) × `masked_m` ∈ {0, 1, 17, m} × E ∈ {4, 8, 56} × K_BLOCK ∈ {1024, 2048} × num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} — is bit-exact against the reference everywhere, with padding rows untouched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hidden sizes that already worked are unaffected, checked two ways on H200 and B200 (torch 2.11 / triton 3.6; kernel timed inside a CUDA graph so Triton's Python launch cost is excluded; DeepEP scale layout, `K_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, m-grid 32). Codegen: the compiled kernel has the same opcode multiset as before at num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8}, differing only in instruction scheduling order. Access widths are unchanged in the tail path too (warps=2 → `ld/st.global.v4.b32`, warps=4 → `v2.b32`, warps=8 → scalar `b32`), so the mask costs no vectorization. Timing at k=7168, relative to the kernel this replaces: | live rows / expert | H200 w8 | H200 w4 | B200 w8 | B200 w4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 32 | −0.18% | −0.38% | −0.59% | +1.11% | | 256 | −0.65% | −0.10% | −1.66% | +1.46% | | 1024 | +0.09% | +0.20% | −0.32% | 0.00% | For reference, a newly-working shape (no prior number — it asserted): k=3584, 8 experts, 1024 live rows per expert — 25.4 µs on H200, 14.6 µs on B200. Reproduction note: in a CUDA-graph A/B loop the first variant measured reads roughly 10% fast on sub-2 µs shapes; interleave the variants and swap their order before trusting a small gap. Not covered here: a multi-node end-to-end decode run on a model whose routed-expert hidden size isn't 1024-divisible. This change unblocks the fp8 low-latency path for those models at the kernel level; that e2e run is still outstanding. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour or flags change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32324979864](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324979864)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32324979753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324979753)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Multihardware Plugin] Introduce SRTPlatform.build_kv_pool request seam; flatten platform class hooks to Optional
signals.text: ## Motivation This is the KV-management redesign promised on #29445 ("this PR has been sitting as we are considering how we manage this layer for KV... next revision may look different"). The existing platform seam for KV pools — `get_{mha,mla,dsa}_kv_pool_cls()` returning a class that the call site instantiates — has three structural defects that have already produced real bugs: 1. **Ctor kwargs leak into every vendor pool.** The call site instantiates the platform's class with a fixed kwargs set, so every out-of-tree pool `__init__` must track call-site churn. #30568 is exactly this: `index_head_dim` is DSA-only, but the OOT MLA path passes it to every vendor pool, forcing each backend to add a phantom parameter or crash at startup. 2. **Every construction site must remember to consult the hook.** #27679: `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` selects its internal paged allocator with a bare `is_npu()` check and never consults `get_paged_allocator_cls()`, forcing OOT plugins to monkey-patch. 3. **Class-granular hooks can't see layout.** In `HybridLinearKVPool.__init__`, the platform class wins over the caller-selected layout variant (e.g. page-major) through an implicit priority chain — the "we should be careful when overriding in-tree `get_xxx_cls()`" concern raised on #29445. The platform clobbers a layout it never sees. This PR replaces the class-getters with a single request-passing seam and makes the remaining `get_*_cls` hooks explicit about "no platform opinion". It is **platform-neutral**: every in-tree platform returns `None` from every new/changed hook, the in-tree NPU (`_is_npu` / ascend) branches are untouched, and out-of-tree platforms keep working through the deprecated hooks. A follow-up PR (the reworked #29445) moves the in-tree NPU selection onto this seam. ## Modifications **New seam** (`platforms/interface.py`, `mem_cache/kv_pool_request.py`): ```python def build_kv_pool(self, *, request: KVPoolRequest) -> Optional[KVCache]: """None = no platform opinion; the configurator builds the in-tree default.""" ``` `KVPoolRequest` (msgspec.Struct) carries plain scalars — kind (`"mha" | "mla" | "dsa"`), sizes, page size, dtype, layer range, **layout** (`contiguous`/`page_major`), attention backend, `post_capture_active`, and `index_head_dim` set **only** for DSA-indexed models. The platform sees the full request and constructs the pool itself, so pool `__init__` signatures stay private to each platform: new request fields never break a platform that ignores them (fixes the #30568 class of bug by construction), and the platform can make an informed layout decision instead of being ordered above it. **Single resolution point** (`mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`): - `_build_platform_kv_pool`: consulted unconditionally at the former OOT-branch position — platform seam → deprecated OOT class hooks (warn-once) → in-tree builders. - `_build_platform_hybrid_full_kv_pool`: resolves the full-attention leaf of hybrid-linear composites, absorbing the OOT selection that lived inside `HybridLinearKVPool.__init__`; the resolved pool is injected via the existing `full_kv_pool` parameter. - `HybridLinearKVPool.__init__` no longer makes platform decisions (`memory_pool.py`). **Hook flattening** (`raise NotImplementedError` → `return None`, callers get explicit fallbacks): - `get_paged_allocator_cls` — now also consulted inside `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` (the #27679 fix). The top-level OOT preemption keeps its legacy semantics. - `get_graph_runner_cls` (`cuda_graph_setup.py`) and `get_piecewise_backend_cls` (`compilation/backend.py`) — platform hook first, device-keyed in-tree defaults unchanged as fallback. - `get_{mha,mla,dsa}_kv_pool_cls` — deprecated, still honored for OOT platforms when `build_kv_pool` returns None. **One deliberate contract change:** an OOT platform that never overrode a hook now falls back to the in-tree default instead of crashing with `NotImplementedError` ("None = use default", matching the existing `get_quantization_config` convention). **Tests:** `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_platform_seam.py` (CPU CI) pins the resolution order (platform → legacy → in-tree), the mambaish/standalone split, the legacy leaf construction kwargs, and the every-hook-defaults-to-None contract. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — platform-neutral refactor; every in-tree platform returns `None` from every changed hook and all `_is_npu`/ascend branches are untouched, so pool/allocator/runner selection is unchanged on all hardware. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — selection-time only; no kernel or forward-path changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- Related: supersedes the KV-hook design in #29445 (reworked NPU platform follows as a stacked PR); fixes the defect classes reported in #30568 and #27679; direction per the `create_kv_pool` factory sketched in RFC #20372. cc @AgainstEntropy @ssshinigami 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32316436177](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316436177)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316436138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316436138)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [model-gateway] Add opt-in `fips` feature using the AWS-LC FIPS module
signals.text: ## Motivation Some deployments (government and other regulated environments) require all cryptography to come from a FIPS 140-3 validated module. This PR adds an opt-in `fips` cargo feature to sgl-model-gateway so those users can build a compliant gateway. Default builds are not affected. ## Modifications Behind the new `fips` feature (off by default): - rustls uses the AWS-LC FIPS provider instead of ring for all TLS (HTTPS server and the reqwest/kube outbound clients; tonic is built without TLS features and does no TLS itself). - JWT verification uses the jsonwebtoken AWS-LC backend. - The wasm module SHA-256 hash uses AWS-LC. - `aws-lc-fips-sys` uses a normal caret requirement (`0.14`) so builds pick up the latest AWS-LC FIPS release (currently 0.14.1, bundling AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0). AWS-LC FIPS is a CMVP-validated module lineage (see [certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) for the 3.x static module). The exact module version in any given build can be read from the binary with `strings <binary> | grep "AWS-LC FIPS"`. Deployments that need a version literally listed on an issued certificate can pin, for example `=0.13.11` (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, the exact version on #5314). - At startup the gateway asserts the installed rustls provider is FIPS and that the AWS-LC JWT provider was installed. If not, it fails to start. - The Python and Go bindings expose the same `fips` feature. Changes that apply to all builds: - New `src/crypto.rs` with `ensure_crypto_provider_installed()`, which replaces the two previous ad-hoc `ring::default_provider().install_default()` call sites, and a `Sha256Hasher` wrapper used for wasm module hashing. Default builds keep ring and RustCrypto sha2. - `jsonwebtoken` upgraded 9.3 to 10.4 and `smg-auth` 1.0.0 to 1.2.2. jsonwebtoken 9 was hardwired to ring; version 10 has pluggable backends. Default builds use its `rust_crypto` backend. Not changed: blake3/xxhash (used for cache-aware routing and consistent hashing, not security relevant) and the openssl dependency (test cert generation and the optional `vendored-openssl` feature only). Build note: `--features fips` (and therefore `--all-features`, used by `make lint` and the rust CI lint job) needs cmake and Go to compile AWS-LC. The CI lint job passes since GitHub runners include both. <details> <summary>FIPS verification evidence</summary> - The fips binary embeds the AWS-LC FIPS module version string (checked with `strings`, currently `AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0`); the default binary does not. - The fips binary starts cleanly and serves `/liveness` and `/health`. - TLS handshake against the fips build negotiates TLS 1.3 `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Forcing `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (not FIPS approved) fails against the fips build and succeeds against the default build, showing the provider swap is active. - Known residual: ring and the jsonwebtoken RustCrypto backend remain linked (cargo features are additive) but are never selected at runtime, which the startup assertions enforce. smg-auth internally uses RustCrypto sha2 for API key fingerprinting; that code only runs when control plane API keys are configured. </details> ## Accuracy Tests N/A, no model or inference code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A, default builds keep the same crypto stack. The fips path only affects opt-in builds. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32316595584](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316595584)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316595103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316595103)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Default the ROCm 7.2 PR gate to 7.2.4
signals.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30984. That PR landed the rocm724 flavor but deliberately kept the PR gate on rocm720, because no rocm724 nightly image existed yet and `find_latest_image` would have aborted at container start rather than degrading. Its commit message said to flip the default once rocm724 nightlies exist. This is that flip. ## Modifications `.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` — `rocm724` becomes the default for the dispatch input, the call input, the workflow-level `ROCM_VERSION` fallback, and the value forwarded to the extra suite. `.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-extra.yml` — same flip. This one is easy to miss: the extra workflow has its own `pull_request` trigger and runs standalone on every PR (all 100 of its recent runs are `pull_request`), where `inputs` is empty and its inline `|| 'rocm720'` fallbacks pick the flavor. Changing only `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` would have left the extra suite on 7.2.0 while the main suite moved to 7.2.4. Its job-name suffix marks non-default flavors and was keyed on `!= 'rocm720'`; it now reads `!= 'rocm724'`. **No required status check name changes.** On the `pull_request` path `inputs.rocm_version` is empty, so the suffix was empty before and is empty after. An explicit `rocm720` dispatch is now the one that gets marked: | trigger | job name | | --- | --- | | `pull_request` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` (unchanged) | | dispatched `rocm724` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` | | dispatched `rocm720` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720` | rocm720 stays reachable from the dropdown and via `AMD_CI_IMAGE`. ## Merge precondition — please do not merge until this holds `find_latest_image` searches a **7-day** window of dated tags and has **no hard-coded rocm724 fallback**, so it returns 1 and the container start fails outright if no recent image exists. That is deliberate — better a loud failure than silently testing a months-old image — but it means this PR must not land before a rocm724 nightly is inside the window. At the time of writing the newest rocm724 tag in `rocm/sgl-dev` is `v0.5.16-rocm724-mi30x-20260807`, which is 13 days old and therefore outside the window. The first post-#30984 rocm724 nightly builds at 12:00 UTC and takes about 2.5h. Check before merging: ```bash curl -s "https://registry.hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/rocm/sgl-dev/tags?page_size=100&name=rocm724-mi30x" \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([t['name'] for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['results']][:3])" ``` Both `rocm724-mi30x` and `rocm724-mi35x` need a tag dated within the last 7 days. ## Validation The 7.2.4 images were exercised end to end on #30984's head before it merged: all six flavors built, and the full PR and nightly suites ran against them on both 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 with no failure attributable to the change — every failure matched a `main` baseline at test level. Details in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5340700214. ## Note on naming The jobs in this workflow keep their static `-rocm720` suffixes (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720`, ...) even though they now run 7.2.4. Renaming them would break every required status check, so that debt is left for a separate pass. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests <!-- N/A: CI configuration change --> - [ ] Update documentation <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signals.title: [AMD][CI] Run the ROCm 7.2 nightly on both 7.2.4 and 7.2.0
signals.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30984, and a sibling to #35602 which does the same for the PR gate. #30984 added rocm724 to the release matrix, so rocm724 images are now published nightly — but the nightly **test** suite still hardcoded `--rocm-version rocm720` in all 47 container starts and had no way to select a flavor. The new images were going untested. The release workflow also still publishes rocm720 images, so simply switching the nightly to 7.2.4 would leave a shipped flavor with no coverage at all. ## Modifications `.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml` only. **Parameterized**, mirroring what `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` already does: a `rocm_version` input on both `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`, plus a workflow-level `ROCM_VERSION` that carries the default — `inputs` is empty on the `schedule` and `push` triggers, so the default cannot live on the inputs alone. All 47 hardcoded container starts now read `--rocm-version "$ROCM_VERSION"`. **Both flavors covered, via a second cron rather than a matrix.** Adding a `rocm_version` matrix dimension to all 47 jobs would have doubled the concurrent GPU load on a suite that already saturates the runners for roughly three hours. Two schedules cost the same total GPU time but spread it: | cron (UTC) | flavor | image it picks up | | --- | --- | --- | | `30 17 * * *` | rocm724 | same day's, published ~14:30 | | `30 5 * * *` | rocm720 | previous day's | Resolution across every trigger: | trigger | `ROCM_VERSION` | | --- | --- | | schedule 17:30 | `rocm724` | | schedule 05:30 | `rocm720` | | push to `main` (`version.py`) | `rocm724` | | dispatch / call, default | `rocm724` | | dispatch / call, explicit | as given | **Concurrency.** The scheduled group now carries the flavor, so a rocm720 run and a rocm724 run cannot cancel each other if one overruns into the other's slot. The dispatch and caller branches of that expression are untouched. ## Merge precondition The rocm720 leg is safe to land at any time. The **rocm724 leg** needs a rocm724 nightly image inside `find_latest_image`'s 7-day window, or the 17:30 run fails at container start — there is no hard-coded rocm724 fallback, by design. Blast radius is smaller than #35602 (a nightly, not the PR gate), but the same check applies: ```bash curl -s "https://registry.hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/rocm/sgl-dev/tags?page_size=100&name=rocm724-mi30x" \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([t['name'] for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['results']][:3])" ``` At the time of writing the newest rocm724 tag is `v0.5.16-rocm724-mi30x-20260807`, outside the window. The first post-#30984 rocm724 nightly builds at 12:00 UTC. ## Validation The full nightly suite was run against both flavors' staging images on #30984's head before it merged — 36 pass / 11 real failures on each, with every failure matching a `main` baseline at test level. Details in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5340700214. Locally verified here: the YAML parses, all 48 jobs are intact, all 47 container starts resolve through `ROCM_VERSION`, no `--rocm-version rocm720` literal remains, and the expression resolves as tabulated above for each trigger. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests <!-- N/A: CI configuration change --> - [ ] Update documentation <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signals.title: [MUSA] Isolate CI dependencies and validate Triton
signals.text: ## Motivation MUSA self-hosted runners reuse `~/.local`. A prior dependency resolution installed public `torch==2.13.0`, which replaced the MUSA Triton 3.2 wheel with generic `triton==3.7.1`. Later MUSA jobs restored the bundled Torch wheels but did not restore Triton, so nightly jobs inherited the poisoned user site. The current installer also allowed several unpinned resolver entry points: - `torchada` declares an unpinned `torch` dependency; - `xgrammar==0.2.1` declares an unpinned `triton` dependency; - local vendor wheels were installed without the documented `--no-deps` behavior; - `compressed-tensors` needs a different version for the Torch 2.9 and 2.11 MUSA stacks. ## Modification - Isolate each GitHub Actions job with a task-local `PYTHONUSERBASE`. - Install vendor wheels, including a hash-pinned `torchada==0.1.82`, with `--no-deps`. - Reuse an installed Triton only after verifying version 3.2.0, MUSA metadata, and the `mtgpu` backend; otherwise install the hash-pinned MUSA wheel. - Generate constraints from the installed MUSA stack and select `compressed-tensors==0.15.0` for Torch 2.9 or `0.17.0` for Torch 2.11. - Fail closed when Torch/Torch-MUSA versions diverge, the MUSA Triton backend is missing, or the active Triton target is not MUSA. - Add unit tests for constraint generation and make MUSA CI script changes trigger the affected PR lanes. ## Test - `python3 -m unittest scripts/ci/musa/test_musa_python_stack.py` (5 passed) - `bash -n scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` - `shellcheck scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` - Full repository pre-commit on the four changed files - Installer and `dev_musa` resolver dry-run in `registry.mthreads.com/mcconline/inference/vllm:v0.24.0-ph1-5.2.0-torch2.11.0.post1-20260819`; no protected MUSA core package was re-resolved - [MUSA LLM nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32320232429): passed on commit `1de308b00585d664ae28476ae25d88486c34b8a7`; Triton target was `musa/mp_31`, and the DeepSeek server smoke passed 4/4 with an HTTP 200 request - [MUSA diffusion nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32320854404): all three Qwen-Image cases in partition 1 passed. The overall workflow remains red for two unrelated reasons: - partition 0 hit a transient `GnuTLS recv error (-110)` while cloning `MooreThreads/mutlass` during AOT setup; - partition 1 failed only the existing Wan 2.1 performance baseline (`4.872 s` best vs `4.3 s` threshold). - The exact base Qwen-Image case belongs to partition 0 and therefore did not start in this workflow run; it passed a separate one-GPU S5000 smoke before this CI change. ## Checklist - [x] The code is formatted and passes lint checks. - [x] Tests cover the new constraint-selection behavior. - [x] Runtime evidence includes an actual server request, not only startup. - [x] The known non-green diffusion results are documented without expanding this dependency-fix PR into performance or network-retry work.
signals.author: yeahdongcn

signals.title: Enable moe_a2a_backend=mori for DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism rejects `moe_a2a_backend=mori` at startup: ```python if server_args.moe_a2a_backend not in ("none", "deepep", "megamoe"): raise ValueError("DeepSeekV4 CP supports moe_a2a_backend in ('none', 'deepep', 'megamoe'), got ...") ``` with a matching assert in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`. On ROCm this is the binding constraint: neither DeepEP nor megaMoE ships in the ROCm images, so `none` is the only usable value and CP users lose the mori a2a path entirely, falling back to an all-gather → MoE → reduce-scatter. **The exclusion is "untested", not "incompatible".** The original assert (`35870d55ac`) read *"Only DeepEP is tested with CP's per-rank token split"*, and #29569 simply widened the tuple to add megamoe. No incompatibility is documented, and none is present: - mori is in `DeepseekV2MoE._enable_a2a_moe`, so `DeepseekV2MoE.forward` routes it to `forward_deepep` — byte-for-byte the path deepep already takes under CP. - Token ordering already lines up: `cp_round_robin_input_ids` (`layers/utils/cp_utils.py:178`) returns `input_ids[cp_rank::cp_size]` for *every* non-`none` backend, which matches how `dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data` slices `hidden_states`. - `MoriEPDispatcher.combine` truncates to `self._num_tokens` (`moriep.py:1116`), so combine returns complete per-token outputs, not partial sums. ### Interaction with the replicated shared expert `_shared_expert_use_tp1` is forced True by `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()`, and a replicated (TP1) shared expert summed by a cross-rank collective is a real bug — see #35535, where exactly that happens on the CP `a2a=none` path. It is structurally unreachable here. The mori CP branch performs no `dsa_cp_gather_hidden_states` / `dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states`; `forward_deepep` computes the shared expert on local rows and adds it once, with no post-experts all-reduce and nothing downstream to sum it per rank. #35535's hoist is correctly gated on `is_none()`, so it is a no-op for mori either way. ## Modifications Three files, 34 lines, all gating and comments — no change to any compute path: - `arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py` — add `"mori"` to the `validate_deepseek_v4_cp` whitelist, and record why each entry is on the list plus the requirement that the model-side gate stay in sync. - `models/deepseek_v4.py` — allow `is_mori()` in the `_run_moe_ffn_dp_sync` assert, documenting why this branch is shared-expert-safe. - `server_args.py` — docstring only, on `_required_mori_dispatch_tokens_per_rank`. It returns the full `chunked_prefill_size` and must **not** be divided by `attn_cp_size`, even though a CP rank normally dispatches `1/cp_size` of it: `can_dsa_cp_split` falls back to a plain replicated prefill for sequences below the split threshold, and in that fallback every rank does see the full chunk. Comment added so it is not "optimized" later. Users enabling CP + mori consequently need `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK >= chunked_prefill_size`. ## Accuracy results 8x MI355X, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark`, TP8, `attn_cp_size=8` (`ATTN_CP0..7` confirmed in the server log), greedy, token-exact prompts sent as raw `input_ids`. Compared against a **non-CP mori arm at the same TP**, so the a2a backend is held fixed and only CP varies. | comparison | first-token top-1 agreement | mean top-1 logprob delta | |---|---|---| | **CP8+mori vs non-CP mori**, 53-length short sweep | **40/40 (100%)** | **−0.015** | | **CP8+mori vs non-CP mori**, 16-length long sweep (4k–16k) | **15/15 (100%)** | ~0 | | *calibration:* known-broken pre-#35535 CP arm vs non-CP | 6/44 (13.6%) | −2.83 | | *calibration:* fixed `a2a=none` CP arm vs non-CP | 47/48 (97.9%) | −0.022 | Agreement is counted over lengths where **both** arms are self-stable across two identical probes. mori's mxfp4 dispatch / fp8 combine is not bitwise reproducible — non-CP mori is itself nondeterministic at 10/53 lengths, versus 1/53 for `a2a=none` — and every excluded length is one where an arm disagrees with itself, not with the other arm. The known-bad "flatter logprobs" signature is −2.83; this measures −0.015. Validation ran with #35535 applied. That fix is a no-op for mori (`_cp_must_hoist_shared` requires `is_none()`, and `_do_shared_local` requires `_use_tp_moe_gather == (not _use_cp and ...)`, both False here), so the numbers transfer unchanged to this main-based branch. ## Known limitation, not addressed here Two-batch-overlap stays off for CP+mori — `_can_run_tbo`'s CP branch still requires `is_none()`. Enabling it needs the EP op list in `_compute_moe_deepseek_v4_prefill(use_cp=True)` plus a fix to `DeepseekV2MoE.op_select_experts`, which reads `state.forward_batch.input_ids` rather than the CP-sliced `_cp_moe_input_ids` that `_forward_layers_tbo_cp` populates. That is a separate change needing its own accuracy run. ## Unrelated pre-existing bug found while testing (not fixed here) A prefill whose **final chunked-prefill chunk is exactly `cp_size` tokens** kills the server: `Memory access fault by GPU node-*` on all 8 ranks, SIGABRT, stack in the DSA indexer (`indexer.py::_forward_prepare_normal` → `compressor_v2.py::forward_unified` → `compressor.py::compute_kv_score` → `linear_bf16_fp32`). Concretely `n % chunked_prefill_size == 8` at cp_size=8, e.g. n=4104 or 8200 with `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, n=16392 with 16384. **It reproduces identically with `moe_a2a_backend=none`**, so it is a CP-v1 defect at 1-token-per-rank in the attention/indexer path, independent of the a2a backend and independent of this PR. `can_dsa_cp_split` admits the split at `seq_len >= cp_size`. Filing separately rather than band-aiding the threshold here, since the faulting kernel is not yet root-caused. ## Checklist - [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (black applied to touched files) - [x] Accuracy validated end-to-end on 8xMI355X against a matched non-CP arm <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324948588](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324948588)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324948373](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324948373)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Benchmark] Support goodput metric.
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. --> ## Motivation Refer to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/8782 and https://hao-ai-lab.github.io/blogs/distserve/ Almost all popular LLM serving engines like SGLang and vLLM use throughput as the primary metric to compare performance with each other. In reality, downstream applications come in different flavors – they may have different latency requirements for user experience, hence dramatically different service level objectives (SLO) to satisfy.Goodput is defined as the number of completed requests per second that meet certain Service Level Objectives, such as TTFT, TPOT, E2E Latency which could be defined by the users. Goodput aims to benchmark GenAI services from a user’s perspective and will provide insights for service providers to further optimize their serving and inference system for better User Experience. If the user doesn't specify `--goodput`, request goodput will not be shown.Supported service level objectives: `TTFT, TPOT, E2EL` <!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. --> ### Benchmark serving with goodput ``` python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1 --dataset-path ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json --random-input 128 --random-output 128 --random-range-ratio 0.9 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9122 --goodput "ttft:100" "tpot:50" "e2el:790" ``` ### Example Console Output ``` ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max reqeuest concurrency: 1 Successful requests: 10 Benchmark duration (s): 7.94 Total input tokens: 1212 Total generated tokens: 1222 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 1222 Request goodput (req/s): 0.50 Request throughput (req/s): 1.26 Input token throughput (tok/s): 152.68 Output token throughput (tok/s): 153.94 Total token throughput (tok/s): 306.62 Concurrency: 1.00 ----------------End-to-End Latency---------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 792.66 Median E2E Latency (ms): 787.16 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 28.29 Median TTFT (ms): 27.79 P99 TTFT (ms): 32.79 ---------------Inter-Token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 6.31 Median ITL (ms): 6.29 P95 ITL (ms): 6.47 P99 ITL (ms): 6.79 Max ITL (ms): 9.44 ================================================== ``` ## Modifications Goodput metric support for benchserving. <!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. --> ## TODO - [ ] Make the metrics more flexible. For example, use P90 e2e latency as the SLO later. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

signal.title: [AMD][Spec] Pack AITER target-verify GQA for Qwen3.5
signal.text: ## Motivation Merged [#34517](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34517) accelerates EAGLE target-verify on **Triton** by loading the shared TP-local KV head once across a block of query heads. InferenceX / InferenceMAX MI355X MTP **must** use `--attention-backend aiter`. On that path, topk=1 verify already goes through AITER `unified_attention`, so the Triton `verify_shared_kv_fwd` kernel is never selected. Calling that Triton kernel from the AITER backend is the wrong follow-up: it breaks the AITER HIP graph and races a Triton verify kernel against `unified_attention`. The AITER equivalent of #34517 is layout, not a new kernel. `aiter_backend.py` currently `.expand()`s the single TP-local KV head to `tp_q_head_num`. `unified_attention` then computes `num_queries_per_kv = 1` (fake MHA). On gfx950 that also inflates the 2D program count until the wrapper drops off the 3D split-KV kernel onto the 2D kernel at high batch (Qwen3.5 TP2, 16 Q heads, 1 KV head). ## Modifications - Stop expanding K/V on the unified target-verify path (default). Pass the true KV-head count so `num_queries_per_kv = tp_q_head_num` and Q heads share one KV load — the same idea as #34517, implemented inside AITER `unified_attention`. - Gate with `SGLANG_ENABLE_AITER_VERIFY_GQA_PACK` (default **True**). Set `False` to restore the historical expand for A/B. - Do **not** import or call `verify_shared_kv_fwd` from `AiterAttnBackend`. - No extra helper module: the skip lives next to the existing expand in `aiter_backend.py`. - Draft-extend routing is out of scope (that is the second half of [#30105](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30105)). ## Kernel evidence (MI355X, Qwen3.5 TP2 verify shape, Lq=4, page=16, HIP graph) `unified_attention` only, expand vs pack. B/A < 1 means packing is faster. | KV | prefix | bs | expand ms | pack ms | B/A | kernels | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | bf16 | 8k | 4 | 0.064 | 0.056 | 0.87 | both 3D | | bf16 | 8k | 64 | 1.271 | 0.326 | **0.26** | 2D → 3D split-KV | | fp8 | 8k | 64 | 0.497 | 0.236 | 0.47 | 2D → 3D split-KV | | bf16 | 32k | 64 | 5.555 | 1.246 | 0.22 | 2D → 3D split-KV | ## E2E serving (MI355X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, 8k/1k) Same InferenceX prefill32k recipe on both arms: `--attention-backend aiter`, page-size 16, EAGLE 3/1/4, context 9236, `kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode=$CONC`, chunked/max-prefill 32768, tokenizer-worker-num 6. Image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260816`. Client is InferenceX `benchmark_serving.py --use-chat-template`. Metric is **total tok/s per GPU** (dashboard unit: `total_token_throughput / TP`). Δ% = (pack − expand) / expand. | C | expand tok/s/GPU | pack tok/s/GPU | Δ tput | expand TPOT ms | pack TPOT ms | Δ TPOT | expand TTFT ms | pack TTFT ms | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2596 | 2753 | +6.0% | 6.36 | 6.17 | −3.0% | 337 | 336 | | 8 | 3716 | 3885 | +4.5% | 9.16 | 8.76 | −4.3% | 347 | 347 | | 16 | 4893 | 5205 | +6.4% | 14.03 | 13.25 | −5.5% | 356 | 352 | | 32 | 6137 | 6689 | +9.0% | 22.76 | 20.72 | −9.0% | 387 | 370 | | **64** | **6149** | **8101** | **+31.8%** | **46.48** | **35.09** | **−24.5%** | 479 | 503 | | 128 | 9083 | 9637 | +6.1% | 63.10 | 59.39 | −5.9% | 663 | 693 | | 256 | 10187 | 10849 | +6.5% | 112.52 | 105.98 | −5.8% | 1007 | 968 | C32→C64 is the serving stall this PR removes: expand goes flat (6137→6149 tok/s/GPU) while TPOT roughly doubles (22.8→46.5 ms). Packing keeps scaling (6689→8101) because TPOT only goes 20.7→35.1 ms. Packing C64 repeats: 8101 / 8114 / 8182 tok/s/GPU (range ~1%). Independent check with packing still off: InferenceX unofficial run [32241233599](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference?unofficialRun=32241233599) (stock AITER on `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`, same prefill32k knobs) MTP C64 = 5728 tok/s/GPU, TPOT 48.6 ms — same flatten as local expand. ## Relation to #30105 [#30105](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30105) already drops this expand **and** reroutes draft_extend. This PR is the verify-only companion to #34517: smaller, default-on GQA packing, and an opt-out env. Happy to close this if #30105 lands first. ## Tests - Kernel A/B and E2E serving A/B on MI355X as above. - No extra test module: the change is the existing expand gated off by default. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the contribution guide. - [x] Provide accuracy and performance measurements (kernel A/B and E2E serving A/B). - [x] Keep the change scoped to the AITER verify layout (two files: `aiter_backend.py`, `environ.py`). - [x] No user-facing documentation is needed; the opt-out env is documented in `environ.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32265389741](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265389741)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32324991518](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324991518)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [BugFix][Qwen3.8] Support Qwen3.8-MXFP4 DCP by registing Qwen3_5 text-only archs in mamba radix cache whitelists

signal.title: [Fix] Support 128-aligned hidden sizes in the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant kernel
signal.text: ## Motivation `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` requantizes DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It required the hidden size to fill a whole number of 1024-element blocks: ```python K_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024 assert x.size(2) % K_BLOCK_SIZE == 0 grid = (x.size(2) // K_BLOCK_SIZE, 32, x.size(0)) ``` so it rejected any expert hidden size that is only 128-aligned — 3584, for example. Since `W4AFp8MoEMethod` pins the low-latency wire format to fp8 (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/w4afp8.py:286-295`) and `apply_deepep_ll()` rejects a payload that carries no per-token-group scales (`w4afp8.py:347-351`), such a model has no working low-latency path at all: the fp8 payload it is handed trips the assert during decode CUDA-graph capture. 1024 was the only constraint of its kind on that path. `w1_scale` is `[E, K // 512, N * 8]`, so 512-alignment is genuinely required; DeepEP's low-latency fp8 scales are `[E, M, hidden // 128]` (column-major in the last two dims for TMA), so the payload is always a whole number of 128-wide scale groups. A hidden size of 3584 satisfies both — 7 × 512, 28 groups — and was rejected only by the 1024 block. ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`: - Take the grid from `triton.cdiv` and drop the assert. - Mask the k lanes in `_fp8_per_token_quant_to_per_tensor_quant_kernel`: on the hidden load, on the store, and on the scale load, whose offsets derive from `k_offsets` and would otherwise read past the scale tensor in the tail block. - Put the masked form behind `HAS_K_TAIL: tl.constexpr`, so hidden sizes that fill every block keep the original unmasked loads and the same launch geometry. This mirrors `_silu_and_mul_post_per_tensor_quant_kernel` in the same file, which already pairs a `cdiv` grid with a masked fast axis. Adds `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant.py` (`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`). ## Accuracy Tests The new test checks k ∈ {7168, 3584, 1152} — one exact multiple of 1024 and two tailed, so both specializations compile — against a torch reference, and asserts that rows past `masked_m` are left exactly as the caller wrote them. Inputs are integers in [-8, 8] with power-of-two group scales, so every intermediate is exactly representable in e4m3 and the comparison can be `rtol=0, atol=0`. (The kernel saturates fp8 overflow — `cvt.rn.satfinite`, clamping to 448.0 — where `Tensor.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` produces NaN, so a torch-reference test has to stay inside range deliberately.) One H200, torch 2.11.0+cu130 / triton 3.6.0: ``` test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[7168] PASSED test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[3584] PASSED test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[1152] PASSED 3 passed in 16.75s ``` Swapping this commit's kernel for the current `main` file makes the two tailed cases fail while 7168 still passes, so the test covers the change rather than just passing alongside it. A wider matrix run out of tree — both scale layouts (contiguous and DeepEP's column-major) × `masked_m` ∈ {0, 1, 17, m} × E ∈ {4, 8, 56} × K_BLOCK ∈ {1024, 2048} × num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} — is bit-exact against the reference everywhere, with padding rows untouched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hidden sizes that already worked are unaffected, checked two ways on H200 and B200 (torch 2.11 / triton 3.6; kernel timed inside a CUDA graph so Triton's Python launch cost is excluded; DeepEP scale layout, `K_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, m-grid 32). Codegen: the compiled kernel has the same opcode multiset as before at num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8}, differing only in instruction scheduling order. Access widths are unchanged in the tail path too (warps=2 → `ld/st.global.v4.b32`, warps=4 → `v2.b32`, warps=8 → scalar `b32`), so the mask costs no vectorization. Timing at k=7168, relative to the kernel this replaces: | live rows / expert | H200 w8 | H200 w4 | B200 w8 | B200 w4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 32 | −0.18% | −0.38% | −0.59% | +1.11% | | 256 | −0.65% | −0.10% | −1.66% | +1.46% | | 1024 | +0.09% | +0.20% | −0.32% | 0.00% | For reference, a newly-working shape (no prior number — it asserted): k=3584, 8 experts, 1024 live rows per expert — 25.4 µs on H200, 14.6 µs on B200. Reproduction note: in a CUDA-graph A/B loop the first variant measured reads roughly 10% fast on sub-2 µs shapes; interleave the variants and swap their order before trusting a small gap. Not covered here: a multi-node end-to-end decode run on a model whose routed-expert hidden size isn't 1024-divisible. This change unblocks the fp8 low-latency path for those models at the kernel level; that e2e run is still outstanding. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour or flags change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32324979864](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324979864)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32324979753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324979753)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][gfx95] Fill the chunked-prefill compute budget exactly
signal.text: ## Summary * A prefill batch never reaches `chunked_prefill_size`. Two independent page roundings leak tokens out of it: `_update_prefill_budget` charges the **page-ceiled** extend length against `rem_chunk_tokens` / `rem_input_tokens` (which are compute budgets, counted in forward-pass tokens), and `add_one_req` floors the last request's truncation back down to a page. With `page_size=64` and `chunked_prefill_size=16384`, the forward runs 16289–16368 tokens instead of 16384. * **That shortfall is not free on gfx95.** The MLA absorb bmm is an aiter Triton kernel whose `EVEN_MN` heuristic is a compile-time `constexpr` keyed on `M % BLOCK_SIZE_M == 0`, so a misaligned M selects a **different compiled binary** — 3819 instructions against 1562 for identical MFMA work (masked store degenerates into 64 separate 16-bit stores; `% M` expands into a full division sequence the compiler then re-predicates). Load instructions are identical, so this is not a coalescing effect. On that kernel alone: **311.2 us at M=16368 vs 155.8 us at M=16384.** * **Fix:** add a `compute_charge` argument to `_update_prefill_budget` so the compute budgets move in raw tokens, independently of the KV budgets, which stay counted in pages and stay page-ceiled. The last request of a batch then takes the remainder verbatim. Both compute budgets have to switch together — they are typically configured to the same value (`chunked_prefill_size == max_prefill_tokens`), so leaving either one ceiled makes it hit zero first and stop the admission loop while the other still has the rounding slack unspent. * Neither floor is a correctness requirement: `alloc_extend` handles a partial leading/trailing page explicitly, DSA builds its page tables per token, and `add_chunked_req` already commits non-page-aligned continuation chunks. The page granularity only bought conservative KV accounting, which is unchanged here. ## Changes | File | Change | | ---- | ------ | | managers/schedule\_policy.py | `_update_prefill_budget`: new `compute_charge` arg; when passed, `rem_chunk_tokens` / `rem_input_tokens` / `rem_dllm_tokens` and the `log_input_tokens` metrics are charged the raw token count instead of the page-ceiled one. KV reservations below are untouched and stay page-ceiled | | managers/schedule\_policy.py | `add_one_req`: fit test compares the **raw** length against `chunk_tokens_limit` (so a request whose ceiled length would spill is not needlessly split); new exact-fill truncation branch takes `chunk_tokens_limit` verbatim, honouring `truncation_align_size` | | managers/schedule\_policy.py | `_use_exact_chunk_fill()` (lru\_cached, lazy `is_gfx95_supported` import) + `PrefillAdder.exact_chunk_fill`; call sites in `add_chunked_req` / `add_req_state` / `add_one_req` pass `compute_charge` only on the gated path | | environ.py | register `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL` (`EnvBool`, default on) | ## Scope gfx95 (MI355X) chunked prefill, gated on `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL` **and** gfx95 — CUDA and other AMD parts keep upstream behaviour on every path. The dLLM path is excluded. KV accounting is unchanged (still page-ceiled), and an SWA-capped chunk stays capped: the exact-fill path takes `chunk_tokens_limit`, not `rem_chunk_tokens`. One side effect on the gated path, which I think is an improvement: `#new-token` now reports the tokens the forward actually runs, which is the long-standing TODO next to `log_input_tokens`. ## Test plan **Baseline** — `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260714` plus six AMD PRs (#30519, #30575, #30715, #30808, #31323, #31324). **This PR** — that baseline plus this PR plus ROCm/aiter#4453. **End to end** (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X TP4, in8192 / out1024): | Concurrency | Mean TTFT base | this PR | Δ | Median TPOT base | this PR | Δ | | ----------- | -------------- | ------- | - | ---------------- | ------- | - | | 4 | 512.25 | 484.58 | **−5.4%** | 13.04 | 13.00 | −0.3% | | 8 | 727.92 | 681.18 | **−6.4%** | 16.41 | 16.23 | −1.1% | | 16 | 999.91 | 930.41 | **−7.0%** | 21.91 | 21.61 | **−1.4%** | | 32 | 1558.20 | 1442.90 | **−7.4%** | 31.00 | 30.37 | **−2.0%** | | 64 | 2742.82 | 2481.36 | **−9.5%** | 49.83 | 48.39 | **−2.9%** | Mean TTFT improves monotonically with concurrency, which is what a shorter prefill should look like: the saving is per prefill forward, so the deeper the queue, the more of them a request waits behind. **Kernel level** (same config): the trace token annotation goes `toks=16350 → 16384`, dense GEMM total 163.5 → 136.6 ms, EXTEND wall 695.4 → 671.6 ms. 25.8 ms of the 26.9 ms comes from the two absorb bmm calls; Tensile/hipBLASLt GEMMs are nearly indifferent to the alignment (1%) since they have no all-or-nothing `constexpr` branch and just run one extra partial tile. Per-forward attribution from torch-profiler traces (in8192 / concurrency 64, decoder layers only) is single-bucket, which is the result I wanted: dense/linear GEMM −65.97 ms, and every other bucket (sparse-MLA attn, all-reduce, MoE, DSA indexer, rmsnorm/quant/act) moves less than 2.1 ms. The effect stays confined to the kernels the `EVEN_MN` constexpr actually selects. **Accuracy:** GSM8K 0.933 → 0.927, single scoring pass each — within what one pass resolves. **Remaining:** draft until the radix-cache path gets explicit coverage. Long context is uncompared (the in70000/out300 sweep only got through concurrency 4/8/16 on the patched side, with no baseline).
