signal.title: Enable moe_a2a_backend=mori for DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism rejects `moe_a2a_backend=mori` at startup: ```python if server_args.moe_a2a_backend not in ("none", "deepep", "megamoe"): raise ValueError("DeepSeekV4 CP supports moe_a2a_backend in ('none', 'deepep', 'megamoe'), got ...") ``` with a matching assert in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`. On ROCm this is the binding constraint: neither DeepEP nor megaMoE ships in the ROCm images, so `none` is the only usable value and CP users lose the mori a2a path entirely, falling back to an all-gather → MoE → reduce-scatter. **The exclusion is "untested", not "incompatible".** The original assert (`35870d55ac`) read *"Only DeepEP is tested with CP's per-rank token split"*, and #29569 simply widened the tuple to add megamoe. No incompatibility is documented, and none is present: - mori is in `DeepseekV2MoE._enable_a2a_moe`, so `DeepseekV2MoE.forward` routes it to `forward_deepep` — byte-for-byte the path deepep already takes under CP. - Token ordering already lines up: `cp_round_robin_input_ids` (`layers/utils/cp_utils.py:178`) returns `input_ids[cp_rank::cp_size]` for *every* non-`none` backend, which matches how `dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data` slices `hidden_states`. - `MoriEPDispatcher.combine` truncates to `self._num_tokens` (`moriep.py:1116`), so combine returns complete per-token outputs, not partial sums. ### Interaction with the replicated shared expert `_shared_expert_use_tp1` is forced True by `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()`, and a replicated (TP1) shared expert summed by a cross-rank collective is a real bug — see #35535, where exactly that happens on the CP `a2a=none` path. It is structurally unreachable here. The mori CP branch performs no `dsa_cp_gather_hidden_states` / `dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states`; `forward_deepep` computes the shared expert on local rows and adds it once, with no post-experts all-reduce and nothing downstream to sum it per rank. #35535's hoist is correctly gated on `is_none()`, so it is a no-op for mori either way. ## Modifications Three files, 34 lines, all gating and comments — no change to any compute path: - `arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py` — add `"mori"` to the `validate_deepseek_v4_cp` whitelist, and record why each entry is on the list plus the requirement that the model-side gate stay in sync. - `models/deepseek_v4.py` — allow `is_mori()` in the `_run_moe_ffn_dp_sync` assert, documenting why this branch is shared-expert-safe. - `server_args.py` — docstring only, on `_required_mori_dispatch_tokens_per_rank`. It returns the full `chunked_prefill_size` and must **not** be divided by `attn_cp_size`, even though a CP rank normally dispatches `1/cp_size` of it: `can_dsa_cp_split` falls back to a plain replicated prefill for sequences below the split threshold, and in that fallback every rank does see the full chunk. Comment added so it is not "optimized" later. Users enabling CP + mori consequently need `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK >= chunked_prefill_size`. ## Accuracy results 8x MI355X, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark`, TP8, `attn_cp_size=8` (`ATTN_CP0..7` confirmed in the server log), greedy, token-exact prompts sent as raw `input_ids`. Compared against a **non-CP mori arm at the same TP**, so the a2a backend is held fixed and only CP varies. | comparison | first-token top-1 agreement | mean top-1 logprob delta | |---|---|---| | **CP8+mori vs non-CP mori**, 53-length short sweep | **40/40 (100%)** | **−0.015** | | **CP8+mori vs non-CP mori**, 16-length long sweep (4k–16k) | **15/15 (100%)** | ~0 | | *calibration:* known-broken pre-#35535 CP arm vs non-CP | 6/44 (13.6%) | −2.83 | | *calibration:* fixed `a2a=none` CP arm vs non-CP | 47/48 (97.9%) | −0.022 | Agreement is counted over lengths where **both** arms are self-stable across two identical probes. mori's mxfp4 dispatch / fp8 combine is not bitwise reproducible — non-CP mori is itself nondeterministic at 10/53 lengths, versus 1/53 for `a2a=none` — and every excluded length is one where an arm disagrees with itself, not with the other arm. The known-bad "flatter logprobs" signature is −2.83; this measures −0.015. Validation ran with #35535 applied. That fix is a no-op for mori (`_cp_must_hoist_shared` requires `is_none()`, and `_do_shared_local` requires `_use_tp_moe_gather == (not _use_cp and ...)`, both False here), so the numbers transfer unchanged to this main-based branch. ## Known limitation, not addressed here Two-batch-overlap stays off for CP+mori — `_can_run_tbo`'s CP branch still requires `is_none()`. Enabling it needs the EP op list in `_compute_moe_deepseek_v4_prefill(use_cp=True)` plus a fix to `DeepseekV2MoE.op_select_experts`, which reads `state.forward_batch.input_ids` rather than the CP-sliced `_cp_moe_input_ids` that `_forward_layers_tbo_cp` populates. That is a separate change needing its own accuracy run. ## Unrelated pre-existing bug found while testing (not fixed here) A prefill whose **final chunked-prefill chunk is exactly `cp_size` tokens** kills the server: `Memory access fault by GPU node-*` on all 8 ranks, SIGABRT, stack in the DSA indexer (`indexer.py::_forward_prepare_normal` → `compressor_v2.py::forward_unified` → `compressor.py::compute_kv_score` → `linear_bf16_fp32`). Concretely `n % chunked_prefill_size == 8` at cp_size=8, e.g. n=4104 or 8200 with `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, n=16392 with 16384. **It reproduces identically with `moe_a2a_backend=none`**, so it is a CP-v1 defect at 1-token-per-rank in the attention/indexer path, independent of the a2a backend and independent of this PR. `can_dsa_cp_split` admits the split at `seq_len >= cp_size`. Filing separately rather than band-aiding the threshold here, since the faulting kernel is not yet root-caused. ## Checklist - [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (black applied to touched files) - [x] Accuracy validated end-to-end on 8xMI355X against a matched non-CP arm <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324948588](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324948588)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324948373](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324948373)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [dLLM] Don't cache the in-flight denoise block in the radix tree
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35270. With radix cache on, a dLLM run trips the idle pool invariant once the server drains. Every request completes, then `on_idle()` raises: ``` ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=469952, available=96, evictable=470016, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0 ``` `available + evictable` is **160 tokens (5 pages) more** than the pool holds. Reported on Ascend NPU and since reproduced on CUDA/A100 by @TrigonW, so it is not device-specific. Nothing actually leaks. `_check_pool_invariant` compares with `!=`, so it reports both directions as a "leak"; the sign is the tell. This one is an **excess** — the radix tree counts the same pages under two nodes. That makes it distinct from the deficit-shaped FDFO abort leak in #32992 (`-32`), which is a separate fix and does not address this. ## Root cause `ReqDllmMixin._init_fill_ids_for_dllm` rebuilds the fill ids as `settled_prefix + dllm_incomplete_ids`, and `dllm_incomplete_ids` is reassigned **in full on every denoise step**. Since `_dllm_page_size` pins `page_size` to the dLLM `block_size`, that in-flight block is a whole trailing page of the radix key. So `cache_unfinished_req` caches a page whose token ids are not final: 1. Step N inserts `[settled][block_v1]`; the write-back at the end points the request's `req_to_token` row at the **tree's** canonical indices, and `cache_protected_len` covers the block. 2. Step N+1 denoises in place, so the key becomes `[settled][block_v2]` over the same KV slots. The match during `insert` now diverges at the block boundary and returns `prefix_len = len(settled)`, which is **below** `cache_protected_len`. 3. `free_segment(kv_indices[cache_protected_len : new_prefix_len], ...)` is therefore an inverted range. It hits the `numel() == 0` guard and silently frees nothing. 4. The node inserted for `block_v2` takes `kv_indices[prefix_len:]` — which, after step N's write-back, are pages the step-N node still owns. `evictable_size_ += len(key)` counts them a second time. This matches every observation in the issue: pages balance physically, `OVERLAP(tree, free) = 0`, no use-after-free, and autoregressive models are clean because their committed token ids never change retroactively. ## Change Add `ReqDllmMixin.get_cacheable_fill_ids()` — the fill ids a prefix cache may take ownership of — and use it in `RadixCache.cache_unfinished_req`. It drops the in-flight block; for every other request it returns `get_fill_ids()` unchanged. No reuse is lost: the block is inserted on a later step, once it resolves and moves into the committed fill ids. ## Tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_dllm_volatile_block.py` (CPU, no accelerator). It drives the real `RadixCache` over real paged pools across two denoise steps and asserts the tree never accounts more tokens than the pages it owns. Without the fix it fails with `128 > 96` — one page double-counted, the same shape as the reported `+160`. Two existing test doubles stub `get_fill_ids` but not the new accessor, so they are updated: `MockReq` in `test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py` now inherits `ReqDllmMixin` (as the real `Req` does), and the `Mock` in `test_radix_cache_unit.py` stubs the new return value. Full `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` run against a clean-`main` baseline on the same machine: 690 failed / 968 passed before, 690 failed / 971 passed after — identical failure set, the +3 being the new tests. (The 690 are pre-existing environment failures on this macOS/CPU box.) ## Notes for reviewers - Scoped to `RadixCache`. Four other caches (`swa_radix_cache`, `mamba_radix_cache`, `unified_radix_cache`, `radix_cache_cpp`) call `req.get_fill_ids()` in `cache_unfinished_req` and carry the same latent assumption. dLLM does not exercise them today, so I left them alone rather than change paths I cannot test — happy to extend if you'd prefer them consistent. - Separately: `_check_pool_invariant` reporting an over-count as "memory leak detected" is what made this look like #32992. Reporting the signed delta would make the two immediately distinguishable. Left out of this PR to keep it focused. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324870673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324870673)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324870129](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324870129)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSV4] Fix SWA state pool over-allocation by using storage page size instead of model window
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation For DeepSeek-V4 models, DSV4PoolConfigurator sizes the c4 compressed-state pool using the model's SWA window (cfg.window_size = 128), while the runtime addresses that same pool using the pool's SWA storage page size (server_args.page_size = 256). These two values differ by 2x, causing capacity waste. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications Align the state-pool paging to the SWA storage page size (server_args.page_size), consistent with how DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool and CompressStatePool address the pool at runtime: self.swa_storage_page_size = mr.server_args.page_size # 256 c4_state_ratio = self.c4_ring_size / self.swa_storage_page_size c4_state_pool_size = swa_tokens // self.swa_storage_page_size * self.c4_ring_size A comment is added to disambiguate this storage page size from the model's SWA window (cfg.window_size / SWA_WINDOW = 128). This is not a correctness bug — the runtime already divides by 256, so the smaller pool stays within bounds; it purely recovers wasted capacity. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling Validated on GB200 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP4 / DP4, default config, mem-fraction-static unconstrained). signal.title: Fix guided decoding for channel-framed reasoning
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34631. Channel-framed reasoning formats such as Muse Glimmer emit an answer-channel header after the reasoning end marker. Guided decoding currently resumes as soon as `<|eom|>` is accepted, so the JSON grammar constrains the model-written `<|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>` header instead of starting at the answer body. ## Modifications - Add optional detector-declared markers for the channel-header boundary and for identifying another reasoning channel. - Opt Muse Glimmer into the channel-header transition. - Add an intermediate state that leaves channel headers unconstrained and does not feed them to the inner grammar. - Preserve state correctly across `copy()` and speculative rollback, including rollback that spans thinking, channel-header, and generation states. - Add `SGLANG_MAX_CHANNEL_HEADER_TOKENS` as an opt-in fail-safe (default: unlimited; positive values resume guided decoding when a malformed header never closes). This avoids rearming early for long, valid tool or recipient names. - Keep per-token channel rollback history only for channel-aware detectors; non-channel detectors retain the previous lightweight rollback accounting. - Keep direct transitions unchanged for all other detectors and for requests without reasoning. - Add 15 off-server unit cases covering answer and repeated-reasoning channels, long headers, fail-safe behavior, multi-token markers, direct generation, copy, rollback, and non-channel memory behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable to model forward accuracy. The state-machine regression checks pass in an isolated CPU-only harness, including the reproduction's grammar arming boundary and rollback behavior. The repository pytest module cannot be collected on this macOS development host because SGLang imports Triton at package initialization and Triton is not available on macOS. It fails before any test code executes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change adds only small token-sequence matchers while a detector explicitly waits for a channel header; all existing detectors retain the direct transition. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted the changed files with Black and checked them with Ruff. - [x] Added unit tests for the new behavior and compatibility paths. - [x] Followed the existing reasoning grammar and environment-variable conventions. - [x] Documentation is not required; this is an internal parser boundary and the fail-safe environment variable is documented inline with the existing environment settings. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324890929](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324890929)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324890657](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324890657)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] [XPU] Qwen3.5 GDN + speculative decode: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window'
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On --device xpu, any speculative-decoding run on a hybrid GDN/linear-attention model (Qwen3.5) crashes in the target-verify path during the server's own warmup generation, before any user request. gdn_backend.py:43-48 binds the XPU kernel as-is: elif is_xpu(): from sgl_kernel import causal_conv1d_fn_xpu, causal_conv1d_update_xpu causal_conv1d_update = causal_conv1d_update_xpu but the is_target_verify branch at gdn_backend.py:539 calls it with five spec-only kwargs that the XPU op schema does not have — intermediate_conv_window, intermediate_state_indices, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, retrieve_parent_token. The XPU signature stops at conv_state_indices / pad_slot_id. File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py", line 539, in forward_extend mixed_qkv_processed = causal_conv1d_update( TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' The scheduler dies, and the client then reports a downstream ConnectionError (secondary noise). Non-spec decode on the same model/backend is unaffected — only TARGET_VERIFY takes this branch. The NPU and CPU bindings a few lines below (gdn_backend.py:49-60) are wired the same way and look exposed to the identical gap; unverified. Issue is induce #31250 fix. ### Reproduction With simple below steps able to reproduce issue ``` python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code \ --device xpu --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --max-running-requests 1 \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 512 --output-len 8 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' ``` Note : #34712 is required to reproduce the above error using shell command. ### Environment Intel Environment - sglang : 0.5.18.dev364+g667e18d99 torch : 2.12.0+xpu | cuda: None | hip: None | xpu: 20250302 python : 3.12.13 | Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 device : 8 x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics driver : 1.14.36300+8 | mem GB: 22.7

signal.title: [BUG] EAGLE + DP Attention + PD Disaggregation: Deadlock when `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is enabled for GLM-5.2
signal.text: # EAGLE + DP Attention + PD Disaggregation: Deadlock when `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is enabled ## Summary When running EAGLE speculative decoding with DP attention in PD disaggregation decode mode, the server deadlocks during warmup if the model config has `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True` (e.g., `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`). The deadlock occurs at the GPU level due to asymmetric `can_cuda_graph` decisions between idle and non-idle DP ranks in the `draft()` method, causing NCCL `all_gather` buffer mismatches across ranks. Removing either `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` or `--enable-dp-attention` or setting `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=False` in the model config avoids the deadlock. ## Environment - **Model**: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (DeepseekV2 architecture, MoE, FP8 quantization, `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True`, `index_topk` set) - **GPU**: 8x B30Z (Blackwell, SM100+) - **Config**: TP=8, DP=8, `enable_dp_attention=True`, `disaggregation_mode=decode`, `speculative_algorithm=EAGLE`, `speculative_num_steps=3`, `speculative_eagle_topk=1`, `speculative_num_draft_tokens=4` - **Prefill worker**: Does NOT enable EAGLE (`--speculative-algorithm` not set) ## Reproduction ### Decode worker launch command ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 \ --watchdog-timeout 100 \ ... # other args ``` ### Symptom The server starts, captures CUDA graphs, then enters PD disaggregation warmup. During warmup, a request is sent to one DP rank while the other 7 DP ranks are idle. The server hangs and eventually triggers a watchdog timeout. ### Stack trace (py-spy dump) **The non-idle DP rank (has the request)** — stuck in `draft_forward` via **eager path**: ``` draft_forward (eagle_worker_v2.py:545) draft (eagle_worker_v2.py:544) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1197) run_batch (scheduler.py:3351) ``` The eager forward reaches MoE router computation (`dsv3_router_gemm`) and blocks on the NCCL collective. **The 7 idle DP ranks** — stuck in `verify` via **cuda graph path**: ``` seqlens_expand_triton (pad.py:381) _apply_cuda_graph_metadata (dsa_backend.py:1533) init_forward_metadata_out_graph (dsa_backend.py:750) load_batch (decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1188) eagle_prepare_for_verify (eagle_utils.py:558) run_eagle_verify (eagle_worker_common.py:451) verify (eagle_worker_v2.py:1504) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1200) ``` These ranks have already completed `draft()` via cuda graph replay and are waiting in `verify()` for the non-idle rank to catch up. ## Root Cause ### Background: `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend` When the model config has `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True`, the EAGLE worker sets `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend=True`. This flag enables seeding the DSA (Dynamic Sparse Attention) top-k indices from the draft-extend output, so that subsequent draft-decode iterations can reuse the computed indices instead of recomputing. ### The problematic code In `eagle_worker_v2.py`, the `draft()` method contains: ```python if ( can_cuda_graph and self.seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend and not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and draft_input.dsa_topk_indices is None ): can_cuda_graph = False # ← forces eager path ``` This condition downgrades `can_cuda_graph` to `False` when `dsa_topk_indices is None`, forcing the rank onto the **eager path** instead of the **cuda graph path**. ### How the divergence happens In PD disaggregation decode mode: 1. **Prefill worker does NOT enable EAGLE** — it doesn't run `_draft_extend_for_prefill`, so `req.output_dsa_topk_indices` is never set (remains `None`). 2. **Decode worker** receives the request via PD transfer. In `build_eagle_disagg_draft_input()` (`eagle_disaggregation.py`), `dsa_topk_indices` is assembled from `req.output_dsa_topk_indices`. Since all are `None`, the result is `None`. 3. When a request arrives on **one DP rank** (non-idle) while **other DP ranks are idle**: - **Non-idle rank**: `forward_mode.is_idle()` → `False`, so `not is_idle()` → `True`. Combined with `dsa_topk_indices is None`, the condition triggers → `can_cuda_graph = False` → **eager path**. - **Idle ranks**: `forward_mode.is_idle()` → `True`, so `not is_idle()` → `False`. The entire condition is skipped → `can_cuda_graph` stays `True` → **cuda graph path**. 4. **Path divergence**: non-idle rank runs `draft_forward` via eager (no DP padding), idle ranks run draft via cuda graph replay (with DP padding to `max(global_num_tokens)`). 5. **Deadlock**: The MoE MLP layer requires all DP ranks to synchronize via NCCL `all_gather`. The eager path uses per-rank token counts (no padding), while the cuda graph path pads all ranks to the same `max_len`. The mismatched buffer sizes cause a GPU-level deadlock on the NCCL collective. ### Why disabling `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` fixes it When `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=False`: - `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend = False` - The condition never triggers - All ranks consistently use `can_cuda_graph` as determined by `can_run_graph()` (which accounts for DP via `can_run_dp_cuda_graph`) - No path divergence, no deadlock ## Solution Instead of downgrading to eager path when `dsa_topk_indices is None`, set a dummy zero-filled tensor. This keeps `can_cuda_graph = True` for all ranks, ensuring they all use the cuda graph path consistently. ### Patch ```diff --- a/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py +++ b/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py @@ -513,7 +513,11 @@ and not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and draft_input.dsa_topk_indices is None ): - can_cuda_graph = False + draft_input.dsa_topk_indices = torch.zeros( + (draft_input.hidden_states.shape[0], self.dsa_index_topk), + dtype=torch.int32, + device=draft_input.hidden_states.device, + ) ``` ### Why this works - The dummy zero tensor makes `dsa_topk_indices is not None`, so the condition no longer triggers, and `can_cuda_graph` stays `True` for the non-idle rank. - Inside the cuda graph runner's `execute()` method, when `dsa_topk_indices` is not `None`, it copies the seed into the static buffer (`buffers.dsa_seed_topk[:raw_bs].copy_(seed)`). A zero-filled seed is equivalent to no seed — the `draft_forward()` method detects that the seed is all-zeros (via the `seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend and dsa_topk_indices is not None` check at line ~618) and sets `spec_info.dsa_topk_indices = None` to trigger recomputation. - All DP ranks (idle and non-idle) now consistently use the cuda graph path, which includes proper DP padding via `DpPaddingMode.MAX_LEN`, ensuring NCCL `all_gather` buffer sizes match across ranks. ### Verification The fix was tested with the original launch command. PD disaggregation warmup completes successfully: ``` [2026-07-27 20:30:40] Disaggregation warmup requests completed for all 8 DP ranks [2026-07-27 20:30:40] End of disaggregation warmup [2026-07-27 20:30:40] The server is fired up and ready to roll!

signal.title: [Perf][DSV4] add ag_gemm and moe_rs overlap kernels for dsv4 prefill
signal.text: ## 1. Motivation We implement communication-computation overlap for DeepSeek V4 Prefill CP by introducing two fused Triton kernels built on `torch.symmetric_memory`: 1. Fused AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM: the CP AllGather is performed on a dedicated stream via Copy Engine (CE) P2P pulls (consuming no SMs), while a fused kernel on the compute stream performs on-the-fly FP8 quantization and shared expert `gate_up_proj` GEMM. The compute kernel poll signals to consume each chunk as soon as the CE delivers it, overlapping the AllGather with computation. 2. Fused MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter: the routed expert output reduction, shared expert addition, and ReduceScatter send are fused into a single kernel, overlapping the ReduceScatter communication with the reduction computation. - Co-auther: @zxdukki ## 2. Modifications - **Environment Variable** - Add `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL` (default `False`) to enable the fused kernels. - **New Triton Kernels (`symm_mem_kernels/`)** - Add allgather_gemm_symm_mem.py: triton kernel for CE-driven AllGather + on-the-fly FP8 quantization and GEMM with signal-based coordination across two streams. - Add moe_reduce_rs_symm_mem.py: fused MoE topk-reduce + shared expert addition + ReduceScatter in a single triton kernel. - **TorchSymmMemCommunicator (torch_symm_mem.py)** - Split `disabled` / `allreduce_disabled` so fused-kernel contexts work without multicast support. - Add lazy-init helpers to cache AG-GEMM and MoE-RS contexts. - Add CP-mode activation via `set_use_cp()` / `get_active_comm()`. - **Model & Layer (parallel_state.py, fused_moe.py, deepseek_v2/v4.py)** - Initialize `TorchSymmMemCommunicator` when the fused-kernel env var is enabled. - Add `no_topk_reduce` option to skip in-kernel reduction (deferred to the fused RS kernel). - Integrate `maybe_fused_ag_shared_experts` and `maybe_fused_shared_add_rs` into the MoE forward path. - Skip the standalone CP AllGather in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` when the fused path is active. ## 3. Evaluation ### 3.1. Experiment Setup - 3 nodes, with 8 × H20 GPUs and 4 dual-port 200Gbps NICs per node. DSV4 Flash uses 1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill. DSV4 Pro uses 3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill. - Input length 16k/32k/64k/128k, output length 1. ### 3.2. Performance Evaluation - DSV4 Flash mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 548.89 | 521.44 | 5.00% | | 32k | 1092.81 | 1034.50 | 5.33% | | 64k | 2200.69 | 2122.33 | 3.56% | | 128k | 4664.76 | 4500.17 | 3.53% | - DSV4 Pro mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 1066.37 | 1028.04 | 3.59% | | 32k | 1641.93 | 1586.49 | 3.37% | | 64k | 2832.55 | 2731.91 | 3.55% | | 128k | 5355.57 | 5173.78 | 3.39% | - Bench Script: ``` # (random-input-len, num-prompts) BENCH_CONFIGS=( "16384 300" "32768 150" "65536 100" "131072 50" ) for cfg in "${BENCH_CONFIGS[@]}"; do read -r INPUT_LEN NUM_PROMPTS <<< "$cfg" python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --host localhost --port 8288 \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path ./ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --num-prompts $NUM_PROMPTS --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len $INPUT_LEN --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf done ``` ### 3.3. Profiling Here we take DSV4 Flash as an example to show profiling before and after optimization. - AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM (476μs->309μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: - MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter (415μs->235μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: ### 3.4. Accuracy Tests - DSV4 Flash: ``` # ----------------------- baseline ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [02:36<00:00, 6.37it/s] Accuracy: 0.950 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 156.981 s Output throughput: 565.851 token/s # ----------------------- overlap ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [02:15<00:00, 7.39it/s] Accuracy: 0.956 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 135.355 s Output throughput: 655.545 token/s ``` - DSV4 Pro: ``` # ----------------------- baseline ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [04:31<00:00, 3.69it/s] Accuracy: 0.957 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 271.137 s Output throughput: 334.259 token/s # ----------------------- overlap ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [04:32<00:00, 3.67it/s] Accuracy: 0.957 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 272.710 s Output throughput: 331.315 token/s ``` ### 3.5. Repro Script - DSV4 Flash (1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill): ``` SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 \ SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./profile \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8288 \ --trust-remote-code --enable-cache-report \ --log-level info --enable-metrics \ --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --tp-size 8 --pp-size 1 --nnodes 1 \ --node-rank 0 \ --dist-init-addr 192.168.0.1:25000 \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --disable-radix-cache \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 ``` - DSV4 Pro (3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill): ``` SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 \ SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./profile \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8288 \ --trust-remote-code --enable-cache-report \ --log-level info --enable-metrics \ --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --tp-size 8 --pp-size 3 --nnodes 3 \ --node-rank ${NODE_ID} \ --dist-init-addr 192.168.0.1:25000 \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --disable-radix-cache \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32233092061](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233092061) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32324714601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324714601)

signal.title: [XPU][CI] key persistent JIT kernel cache by image content ID
signal.text: ## Summary Nightly image rebuilds swap the runtime libs that cached JIT `.so` files link against (e.g. `libsycl.so.8` -> `libsycl.so.9`). Triton keys its cache on source hash only, so the previous gpu-mask-only cache path dlopens stale `.so`s from the prior image and every XPU CI job dies with `OSError: libsycl.so.N: cannot open shared object file`. - Include the resolved `docker image inspect` ID in the cache path so a new image gets a fresh cache dir. - Prune sibling caches for the same GPU but a different image ID via a rootful busybox helper (files are root-owned by the CI container, same pattern as the workspace-ownership reset). - Explicit `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR` overrides are still honored verbatim; if `docker image inspect` fails we fall back to the legacy unversioned path with a warning. - Over-cap reset switched from a runner-level `rm -rf` to the same busybox helper for the same root-owned reason. ## Test plan - [ ] XPU CI passes on an image with a torch/SYCL bump (verify no `libsycl.so.*: cannot open shared object` failures). - [ ] Sibling `kernel-cache-gpu*-<oldid>` dirs are pruned on first run after an image rebuild. - [ ] `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/foo` override still lands at `/tmp/foo` with no pruning. - [ ] Over-cap path (>`XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_MAX_MB`) resets cleanly. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32297133498](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32297133498)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32297133385](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32297133385)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Introduce runtime role switching between prefill and decode
signal.text: ## [PD] Introduce runtime prefill<->decode role switching (mori backend) ### Motivation SGLang's PD disaggregation currently **pins each instance's role (`prefill` / `decode`) at startup** with no way to change it at runtime — to re-balance the P:D ratio you must tear down and relaunch servers. This PR introduces **runtime P<->D role switching**: an operator/router can convert a prefill instance into a decode instance (or vice versa) live, without restarting the server or reloading weights. It lands as a first PoC on the **mori** transfer backend; the control plane is backend-agnostic. ### Design: in-place role flip Key enabler: **the token KV pool is role-independent** — prefill and decode allocate the same KV memory structure. Only the *role-specific* disaggregation structures differ (prefill: bootstrap queue + KV sender; decode: receiver/poll threads, bootstrap registration, role-specific queues/metadata buffers). A flip therefore does **not** reallocate the KV pool or touch model weights. It only tears down and rebuilds the small role-specific structures, then re-dispatches the scheduler event loop to the new role. Draining to idle before teardown is a correctness requirement (an in-flight decode request's KV is owned by an upstream prefill). ### API ``` POST /pd_role_switch {"new_role": "prefill" | "decode", "decode_cuda_graph_bs": [..]?} ``` Gated by `--enable-pd-role-switch` (default **off**, zero impact on existing PD). ### What's in this PR - **Control plane**: `--enable-pd-role-switch`; `PdRoleSwitchReqInput/Output`; `POST /pd_role_switch`; `handle_pd_role_switch` + teardown/rebuild in a dedicated `disaggregation/role_switch.py`; event-loop re-dispatch on flip. Hardened with an in-progress re-entrancy guard, a fail-fast "unhealthy" state on rebuild failure, and table-driven precondition checks. - **Decode CUDA graph on flip**: enable and capture the decode graph on the flip to decode; the captured batch sizes are queryable via `/get_server_info` and can be passed as `decode_cuda_graph_bs` for a size-matched capture; idempotent. - **Backend opt-in interface**: `BaseKVManager.supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`, so other transfer backends can support role switching (checked up-front in the reject path). - **mori backend**: teardown/rebuild hooks for the KV-transfer manager (worker threads are poll-based so they observe the stop flag; sockets, zmq context, RDMA registrations and the IOEngine are released). - **Radix / hicache compatibility**: release the prefix cache on flip; removes the previous `--disable-radix-cache` requirement (works with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`). - **Plumbing / invariants**: `disagg_service.py` (bootstrap started on role-switch instances), `tokenizer_control_mixin.py`, `model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py` (role-agnostic pre-alloc), `invariant_checker.py` (leak check keyed on the pool, not the role). - **Unit tests** (CPU-only, mocked): `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`. ### Validation **Unit tests** — `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`: **17 passed** (control-plane contract, all reject branches, same-role no-op, successful-flip orchestration, serialization, teardown thread-leak, radix-on prefix-cache release). **E2E accuracy (original)** — DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4, 1P1D on 2×MI355X, mori KV transfer, TP8 (pure-TP MoE), concurrency 128, GSM8K (1319, lm_eval flexible/strict): | stage | flexible-extract | strict-match | |-------|------------------|--------------| | baseline (P=node A, D=node B) | 0.9469 | 0.9462 | | after flip (roles swapped via /pd_role_switch) | 0.9462 | 0.9454 | | after flip back (reverted) | 0.9416 | 0.9447 | **Accuracy + performance with radix cache ON (new)** — Qwen3-32B (dense, TP=8, pure-TP), mori, 1P1D on 2×MI300X; 8k1k = random 8192/1024, 320 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup 64: | state | gsm8k | out tok/s | total tok/s | TTFT med | TPOT med | |-------|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|----------| | ① baseline | 0.840 | 2680 | 24119 | 649 ms | 10.62 ms | | ② flip | 0.850 | 2655 | 23895 | 633 ms | 10.77 ms | | ③ flip-back | 0.840 | 2641 | 23772 | 679 ms | 10.69 ms | **Leak stress (new)** — 25 round-trip cycles = **100 role switches**, run once with the radix cache OFF and once ON, metrics recorded per cycle. `flip_fails=0`; weight / kvcache / graph / GPU-free / thread-count stay flat across cycles 2–25 in both configs ⇒ no resource leak. | metric (radix OFF) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |--------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.09 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=53567 D=53488 | constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2127 D=2047 | constant | | metric (radix ON) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |-------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.07 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=50908 D=50748 | bit-for-bit constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2519 D=2224 | ±16, non-monotonic | ### Limitations / follow-ups - Only the **mori** backend's teardown/rebuild hooks are implemented; other backends opt in via `supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`. - Validated with pure-TP MoE (`--tp-size 8`, no EP / DP-attention / MoE a2a). With `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, the a2a dispatch buffer is sized per-role at startup and is not yet rebuilt on flip — a follow-up. - Flip is driven externally (operator/router); an automatic load-based flip policy is out of scope here. ### How to use ```bash # launch both instances with the flag (add --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache to run with radix on) python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode prefill --enable-pd-role-switch python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode decode --enable-pd-role-switch # (optional) query a decode server's captured decode-graph batch sizes curl http://<decode>:8000/get_server_info # -> internal_states[].decode_cuda_graph_bs # after draining, flip (optionally pass decode_cuda_graph_bs for a size-matched capture) curl http://<inst>:8000/pd_role_switch -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"new_role":"decode"}' ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32324696322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324696322)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324696208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324696208)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Complete dots.note.omni support with native encoders, video preprocessing, and MTP decoding
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Merge dots.note.omni model ## Modifications This PR completes the SGLang integration of dots.note.omni, including: - Native in-process vision and audio encoders - Train-consistent native video preprocessing - Full-sharing MTP/NextN speculative decoding - DP/TP/EP execution support, including overlap scheduling - Correct KV-cache sizing for the hybrid sliding-window draft model ## How dots.note.omni differs from existing models dots.note.omni does not fit several assumptions made by existing multimodal and speculative-decoding paths. ### Multimodal architecture Unlike models that reuse standard Hugging Face vision/audio encoders, dots.note.omni uses: - A custom MoE vision transformer - A Whisper-derived audio encoder with a model-specific convolutional frontend and token-length calculation - Model-specific image and audio placeholder expansion - **A native video pipeline that jointly samples and interleaves frames, timestamps, and audio segments under a token budget** The video representation must match the training-time flattening algorithm. Applying a generic uniform-frame video processor changes the modality ordering, sampling strategy, and token allocation, which causes an inference/training mismatch. ### Language-model attention (**Introduce dots_hybrid_attn_backend**) The dots3 language model combines: - MLA - Full-attention and sliding-window layers with different attention geometry - Optional DSA indexing on full-attention layers - Head-wise or element-wise attention gates Therefore, its full-attention and SWA layers cannot always share the same attention path or KV-cache accounting. ### MTP structure the standard single-layer EAGLE/NextN execution path with an ordinary SWA-capacity, MLA-based draft layer. ## Model-specific changes ### Native vision and audio towers This PR migrates the dots.note.omni encoders into SGLang: - Adds the dots MoE ViT implementation - Adds the dots audio model and Whisper-derived speech encoder - Uses SGLang FA3 and fused MoE kernels - Loads encoder weights directly from the model directory - Removes runtime imports and compatibility shims for mm_encoder_server - Honors --language-only, allowing encoder/LLM disaggregation and text-only deployments without loading the multimodal towers ### Train-consistent video preprocessing This PR vendors the required dots video flattening pipeline and integrates it with the OpenAI chat API. The processor: - Accepts a native video_url - Decodes and processes remote video payloads entirely in memory - Uses the tokenizer loaded from the served model - Produces interleaved timestamp, image, and audio content matching training - Uses a deterministic seed derived from the video and question - Reserving the context budget for each video input - Falls back to visual-only processing if audio would exceed the configured token budget - Records per-request preprocessing latency The following request-scoped controls are added: | Field | Purpose | |-------|---------| | seq | Total sequence budget used by the video flattener | | audio_cap | Maximum fraction of the input budget assigned to audio | | audio_sr | Audio sample rate | | k_mode | Deterministic evaluation/sampling mode | These options are request-scoped because evaluation jobs with different context budgets may share one server. Current native-video limitations: - One video per request - A native video cannot currently be mixed with separate image or audio inputs in the same request ### Full-sharing MTP/NextN A dedicated Dot3NoteForCausalLMNextN draft model is added. For draft-model loading, the dots3 configuration is rewritten before attention shapes and KV-cache geometry are derived: - The draft architecture becomes Dot3NoteForCausalLMNextN - Exactly one recursively shared MTP layer is exposed - The layer uses the dots3 SWA attention geometry - A checkpoint-provided MTP embedding is retained when present - The target LM head is shared with the draft model Target verification and draft extension use the paged, absorbed SWA-MLA path. The expanded SWA-MHA path remains limited to prefill, where its logical-tail metadata is available. ## Shared SGLang changes and why they are needed The changes below are implemented in shared infrastructure because the underlying correctness conditions are not specific to one model name. ### 1. Hybrid SWA draft KV-cache accounting The existing hybrid pool configurator charged all EAGLE/NextN draft layers as full-attention layers. That is incorrect for dots3 because its shared draft layer is an ordinary SWA layer with: - SWA latent-vector geometry - SWA token capacity rather than full-attention capacity The speculative auxiliary configuration now records how many draft layers are SWA layers. The hybrid pool configurator separately accounts for: - Full-capacity full-attention draft layers - Ordinary SWA draft layers using the target SWA capacity - Full-capacity SWA-shaped draft layers, such as the existing Inkling case This prevents both under-allocation and unnecessary loss of target KV-cache capacity. The logic is generic for hybrid-SWA models using EAGLE-family draft models. ### 2. DP dummy-row normalization for overlap MTP With DP attention and overlap scheduling, an idle rank must still participate in MLP and attention collectives. SGLang creates dummy rows for this purpose. For speculative decoding, attention metadata may be planned before DP synchronization adds those rows. This previously left the following structures with inconsistent request dimensions: - GPU and CPU extend-length metadata - Prefix-length metadata - Draft cache locations - Positions and hidden states - Dense attention page tables - Draft logits returned to the speculative worker This PR normalizes speculative dummy rows before draft buffers are allocated, keeps the CPU and GPU metadata aligned, preserves the normalized output rows on idle ranks, and exposes a backend hook to refresh row-dependent attention metadata after DP padding. The backend hook defaults to a no-op. Only backends whose metadata can be safely rebuilt opt in, so pre-planned sparse/DSA schedules remain untouched. ### 3. Attention page-table normalization A shared helper is added to align a pre-planned page table with a DP-normalized batch. It truncates extra rows or appends zero-valued dummy rows. Both the dots hybrid backend and the FA3 SWA-MLA fallback use this helper. This avoids model-name checks and makes the invariant explicit at the attention-backend boundary. ### 4. FA3 SWA-MLA fallback dots3's MTP layer is both SWA-shaped and MLA-based. Target verification and draft extension already have a paged latent KV view, while the existing expanded SWA-MHA path is designed for prefill. FA3 therefore gains an absorbed SWA-MLA fallback that consumes the SWA page table and latent KV cache directly. This is exposed as a backend capability and selected by the model only when available. ### 5. OpenAI request and internal request plumbing The dots video controls and the unrendered user question are propagated through: - ChatCompletionRequest - OpenAI chat serving - GenerateReqInput - The dots multimodal processor The original question is required because the training-consistent adapter uses it for deterministic sampling and cache-key construction. It cannot reliably be recovered from the rendered chat prompt, which also contains template, role, and system tokens. The new fields retain defaults and are only consumed by the dots native-video path. ### 6. Encoder/LLM disaggregation validation Dot3NoteForCausalLM is added to the architectures allowed to use --encoder-only and --language-only. The model itself skips vision and audio tower construction in language-only mode. This avoids consuming memory needed by the language model and enables the standard encoder-disaggregation deployment pattern. ## Tests The PR adds coverage for the shared correctness changes: - The DSA K-only rotary path does not alias query and key inputs - Draft-extend dummy requests keep CPU and GPU length metadata aligned - Idle speculative batches retain normalized dummy logits and hidden states - Hybrid-SWA draft layers use SWA geometry and capacity during KV-cache sizing An EP8/TP8/DP8 launch script is also included for dots.note.omni with: - DeepEP - NEXTN speculative decoding - FA3 draft attention - Optional overlap scheduling - Optional language-only mode - Optional DSA and speculative-decoding switches ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.text: `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd-rocm720` has fails on and off since Aug-15th (5 / 7 scheduled runs) with `AssertionError: -1 not greater than 200` in `test_bench_one_batch_2gpu.py`. The `-1` means no throughput was measured because the server is died. see [this log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653/job/95090118554), is: ``` [aiter] shape is M:1, N:14336, K:4096 ... not found tuned config in /tmp/aiter_configs/bf16_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config! aiter/tuned_gemm.py:514: bgemm_internal_cublaslt error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR when calling hipblasLtMatmul out = F.linear(inp, weights, bias) RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 900, operation not permitted when stream is capturing torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture [AITER] custom_all_reduce.cuh:3412 fail to call hipIpcOpenMemHandle(...) Fatal Python error: Aborted ``` The benchmarks Llama-3.1-8B and Mixtral-8x7B, and the aiter config merge this image pulled `llama70B`, `dsv3`, `dsv4`, `glm47`, `glm5`, `gptoss`, `kimi*`, `minimax_m3_eagle` and `qwen3_5_397b` — no configs to covere these two models. Thus the M:1 decode shapes have no tuned entry, and aiter takes the `F.linear` fallback. hipBLAS handle on first use. When first use is the fallback inside an active HIP graph triggered, `hipblasCreate` is illegal, it returns `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`. Everything after it is down. This help function _pre_initialize_hipblas_handle(self), "Force hipBLAS handle creation before CUDA graph capture on ROCm Running one tiny matmul here creates the handle on a normal stream such that the fallback inside capture reuses it. it helps to pre-initialize hipblas handle. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32244967520](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244967520)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32244967029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244967029)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CPU] Fix NUMA/core binding for DP ranks
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. Under DP, DP rank 0 and DP rank 1 both resolve to tp_rank=0 and get bound to the same NUMA node/cores instead of being spread across the machine. This PR fixes this incorrect binding. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> `init_threads_binding` now takes `numa_index` (the worker's global device id) and `world_size = dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`, instead of `tp_rank` and `tp_size`, so every rank across every DP replica maps to a distinct NUMA node / core group. Removed the `world_size == len(threads_bind_list)` equality assert for the explicit `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` path, replacing it with only the per-rank bounds check. signal.title: test: switch the Inkling-Small NVFP4 deterministic suite to DSPARK
signal.text: ## Motivation Roadmap item under #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for the unified radix cache, speculative-decoding row (DSpark / DFlash). `TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact` in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py` was added to cover the spec side of the sconv/mamba checkpoint save. It cannot reach it: `_is_mamba_track_enabled()` is a method of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`, and EAGLE targets disable the prefill CUDA graph outright (`cuda_graph_setup.py`, #28386), so the runner is never constructed. Measured — reverting #34043 leaves that class green: ``` TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact, #34043 reverted → 2 passed, avg_kl_div=0.0 log: "Disable prefill CUDA graph for EAGLE target on tc_piecewise (#28386)" ``` DSPARK and DFlash are not `is_eagle()`, keep the prefill graph, and are the algorithms #34043 actually fixed (that PR measured a DFlash SWEBench subset going 55% → 35% from zeroed sconv state). ## Modifications `TestInklingSmallNvfp4Deterministic` now runs with DSPARK driving decode, and is renamed `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic`. The helpers, the 1e-9 floor, the `extra_buffer` / SWA / mamba-ratio / `KL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` setup and the dedicated server are all unchanged. Two knobs move: `--mem-fraction-static` 0.85 → 0.80 for this class only (see below), and the file's `est_time` 1700 → 2000 for the draft load and graph capture. This replaces rather than adds: the DSPARK config exercises the same NVFP4 weights and the same `flashinfer_trtllm` fp4 GEMM/MoE path, so the FP4-regression coverage the class was written for is retained, and the non-spec cache-restore logic is covered on the shrunken checkpoint in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`. A second no-spec arm here would cost another server launch on a `4-gpu-b200` slot for coverage that is not unique. The trade that buys: a reading here is no longer self-attributing. Inkling-Small is a 256-expert MoE where dropping `--enable-deterministic-inference` alone reads 5.0e-02 — the same order as the bug signal below — so a red case needs a manual re-run without the speculative flags to separate a state-reuse bug from batch variance. That is written into the class docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Revert-then-red against #34043. First measured on the **bf16** `Inkling-Small` checkpoint at tp=4 on GB300 (same server args plus `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, minus the fp4 flags): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **8.05e-02** | | `..._decode_cache_hit` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | no-spec arm (all three) | 0.0 | 0.0 | Eight orders of magnitude above the floor, and the failure lands where the mechanism predicts — the corruption reaches a request that *restores* a prefix, so the flush-both comparison and the decode-side reuse stay clean. The no-spec arm staying green under the same revert is what identified the reading as speculative-state-specific. Sanity of that run: `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, accept len 1.7–3.5, `cuda graph: True`, and `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend` resolves to `full`, so the class reaches the line #34043 changed. Probe sensitivity with `--enable-deterministic-inference` dropped: 5.0e-02 / 4.3e-02 / 5.9e-03. Since re-measured on this file's own config — NVFP4 `Inkling-Small` at tp=4 on 4x GB300 (SM100, same `modelopt_fp4` / `flashinfer_trtllm` path the class already used; there is precedent for that pairing in `test/registered/gb300/test_glm52_nvfp4.py`): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **1.10e-01** | | **`..._decode_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`** | ``` fix in place : 3 passed (650.79s) #34043 revert: 2 failed, 1 passed ``` So both open questions are closed: the bf16 DSPARK draft does pair with the `modelopt_fp4` target, and the exact-0 baseline holds on NVFP4. The signal is stronger here than on bf16 — the revert also drops one prompt out of the decode-cache reuse, which trips the `min_cache_hit_ratio=0.99` this class already asserts. Whole file on 4x GB300: 5 passed in 1093 s. **`--mem-fraction-static` is 0.80 for this class, not the 0.85 the others use.** The first CI run OOMed mid-test on B200: the draft weights and the speculative CUDA graphs (`974.89 MiB allocated in private pools`) left `avail mem=0.40 GB` at 0.85 on a 178 GB card. The GB300 verification could not have caught this — 284 GB per GPU is 60% more headroom. At 0.80 the KV pool still reports ~6.2M tokens against the ~130k this file uses, so the slack costs nothing. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test-only. On 4x GB300 the class runs 650.79 s and the whole file 1093 s; spec roughly doubles this class against the no-spec arm it replaces (360 s → 685 s on the bf16 checkpoint at the same tp). `est_time` 2000 is an estimate for B200 pending a real CI number, which `scripts/ci/update_est_time.py` will correct. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32323829147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32323829147)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32323829021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32323829021)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MUSA] Isolate CI dependencies and validate Triton
signal.text: ## Motivation MUSA self-hosted runners reuse `~/.local`. A prior dependency resolution installed public `torch==2.13.0`, which replaced the MUSA Triton 3.2 wheel with generic `triton==3.7.1`. Later MUSA jobs restored the bundled Torch wheels but did not restore Triton, so nightly jobs inherited the poisoned user site. The current installer also allowed several unpinned resolver entry points: - `torchada` declares an unpinned `torch` dependency; - `xgrammar==0.2.1` declares an unpinned `triton` dependency; - local vendor wheels were installed without the documented `--no-deps` behavior; - `compressed-tensors` needs a different version for the Torch 2.9 and 2.11 MUSA stacks. ## Modification - Isolate each GitHub Actions job with a task-local `PYTHONUSERBASE`. - Install vendor wheels, including a hash-pinned `torchada==0.1.82`, with `--no-deps`. - Reuse an installed Triton only after verifying version 3.2.0, MUSA metadata, and the `mtgpu` backend; otherwise install the hash-pinned MUSA wheel. - Generate constraints from the installed MUSA stack and select `compressed-tensors==0.15.0` for Torch 2.9 or `0.17.0` for Torch 2.11. - Fail closed when Torch/Torch-MUSA versions diverge, the MUSA Triton backend is missing, or the active Triton target is not MUSA. - Add unit tests for constraint generation and make MUSA CI script changes trigger the affected PR lanes. ## Test - `python3 -m unittest scripts/ci/musa/test_musa_python_stack.py` (5 passed) - `bash -n scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` - `shellcheck scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` - Full repository pre-commit on the four changed files - Installer and `dev_musa` resolver dry-run in `registry.mthreads.com/mcconline/inference/vllm:v0.24.0-ph1-5.2.0-torch2.11.0.post1-20260819`; no protected MUSA core package was re-resolved - [MUSA LLM nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32320232429): passed on commit `1de308b00585d664ae28476ae25d88486c34b8a7`; Triton target was `musa/mp_31`, and the DeepSeek server smoke passed 4/4 with an HTTP 200 request - [MUSA diffusion nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32320854404): all three Qwen-Image cases in partition 1 passed. The overall workflow remains red for two unrelated reasons: - partition 0 hit a transient `GnuTLS recv error (-110)` while cloning `MooreThreads/mutlass` during AOT setup; - partition 1 failed only the existing Wan 2.1 performance baseline (`4.872 s` best vs `4.3 s` threshold). - The exact base Qwen-Image case belongs to partition 0 and therefore did not start in this workflow run; it passed a separate one-GPU S5000 smoke before this CI change. ## Checklist - [x] The code is formatted and passes lint checks. - [x] Tests cover the new constraint-selection behavior. - [x] Runtime evidence includes an actual server request, not only startup. - [x] The known non-green diffusion results are documented without expanding this dependency-fix PR into performance or network-retry work.

signal.title: Add Spark3 Model
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds native support for the Spark 3 model architecture in SGLang. The implementation introduces the Spark 3 configuration and causal language model, including sliding-window and full attention, head-wise attention output gating, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and checkpoint weight loading. ## Changes | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/spark3.py` | Adds `Spark3Config`, including model dimensions, attention layout, sliding-window configuration, layer types, RoPE parameters, and tied word embeddings. | | `python/sglang/srt/models/spark3.py` | Implements `Spark3ForCausalLM`, including grouped-query attention, interleaved sliding/full attention, head-wise output gating, gated MLP, parallelism support, split prefill, and checkpoint weight loading. | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` | Exports `Spark3Config` through the SGLang configuration package. | | `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py` | Registers `Spark3Config` in SGLang's Hugging Face configuration registry. | ## Key Technical Details 1. Efficient Architecture：The models adopt an efficiency-oriented architecture with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and other structural optimizations, improving the balance between model quality, memory usage, and inference efficiency. 2. Native 1M Context：Both the 1.7B and 4B models natively support up to 1 million tokens of context, enabling long-document understanding, repository-level coding, and long-horizon agent tasks. 3. Strong Coding & Agent Capabilities：The models deliver leading coding and agent performance among models of comparable size, with strong capabilities in code generation, tool use, multi-step execution, and long-context reasoning. 4. Faster Inference：Through model architecture and inference-stack optimizations, the models achieve higher inference efficiency and throughput than many comparable-size models, especially in long-context scenarios. 5. Strong K–12 and Gaokao Performance：The models achieve leading K–12 question-answering performance at comparable parameter scales, with particularly strong results on challenging Chinese Gaokao-style tasks. 6. Advanced Post-Training：The release applies a comprehensive post-training recipe based on Scaled Reinforcement Learning and MOPD, improving reasoning, coding, instruction following, agentic capabilities, and alignment. 7. signal.title: [DeepSeek-V4] Add Q8KV8 sparse MLA prefill runtime backend
signal.text: Co-authored-by:@JackChuang ## Summary This PR is part of the roadmap tracked in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25746. This PR ports the Q8KV8 sparse MLA prefill path to the DeepSeek-V4 runtime backend and adds a runtime dispatch path via `--dsv4-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8`. When the KV cache uses `fp8_e4m3`, DeepSeek-V4 can run the FP8 query × FP8 KV sparse MLA kernel during prefill instead of falling back to the existing BF16 sparse prefill path. The runtime side also adds Q-head padding, attention-sink padding, kernel input-contract validation, and regression coverage for a real serving shape that previously caused a DeepSeek-V4 hang. Validation has been completed on DeepSeek-V4-Flash with TP8, FP8 KV cache, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, and CUDA graph default serving. Performance experiments show that Q8KV8 delivers consistent throughput and TTFT gains over the existing `flashmla_sparse` baseline, while GSM8K and LongBench-v2 do not show a material accuracy regression. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 already supports FP8 KV cache, but the existing sparse prefill backend still primarily uses the BF16 sparse MLA prefill path. As a result, even when KV is stored in FP8, the runtime cannot fully benefit from the native FP8 Q8KV8 sparse prefill kernel. This PR adds a DeepSeek-V4 Q8KV8 runtime path so prefill can directly use FP8 tensor-core computation. ## Modifications | file | role | |---|---| | `deepseek_v4_backend.py` | DeepSeek-V4 integration + `flashmla_sparse_q8` routing (`_forward_prefill_sparse_q8kv8`), Q/head-sink padding, FP8 workspace, C0/C4/C128 sparse-prefill dispatch | | `dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py` | Q8KV8 backend selection helper, debug env override, dtype-aware sparse-prefill workspace reuse | | `dsv4/dequant_k_cache.py` | fused paged KV gather + dequant + requant to FP8; padded Q cast for Q8KV8 prefill | | `sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90.py` | fail-fast Python-side input contract validation before launching the SM90 Q8KV8 sparse prefill kernel | | `server_args.py` | `flashmla_sparse_q8` in DeepSeek-V4 prefill backend choices via `--dsv4-prefill-backend` | | `test_q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend.py` | runtime wrapper tests for Q8KV8 DeepSeek-V4 sparse prefill, including C0/C4/C128 behavior | | `test_server_args.py` | CLI tests for `--dsv4-prefill-backend` choices | ## Usage | Variant | `--dsv4-prefill-backend` | Notes | |---|---|---| | Baseline / q16 | `flashmla_sparse` | Existing sparse prefill backend | | Q8KV8 / q8 | `flashmla_sparse_q8` | New Q8KV8 sparse prefill backend | ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Flash> \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --dsv4-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192/16384 \ --port 30000 ``` ## Experimental Results ### Performance(H20) We measured prefill performance with `chunked_prefill_size=8192` and `chunked_prefill_size=16384` under the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash serving setup. For each chunk size, we evaluate both `c=1` and `c=16`, where `c` means request concurrency. `c=1` measures single-request prefill latency and input throughput, while `c=16` measures the saturated serving case with 16 concurrent prefill requests. Q8KV8 consistently improves input throughput and TTFT across all tested input lengths, chunk sizes, and concurrency settings. #### chunk16384 — c=1 single-request latency: | il | q8 tps | q16 tps | Δtps | q8 TTFT | q16 TTFT | ΔTTFT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 3.5k | 11,565 | 11,080 | +4.4% | 303 ms | 316 ms | +4.4% | | 8k | 12,257 | 11,631 | +5.4% | 653 ms | 688 ms | +5.4% | | 16k | 12,498 | 11,815 | +5.8% | 1,280 ms | 1,354 ms | +5.8% | | 32k | 11,967 | 11,292 | +6.0% | 2,674 ms | 2,834 ms | +6.0% | | 64k | 11,074 | 10,394 | +6.5% | 5,779 ms | 6,158 ms | +6.5% | | 120k | 9,746 | 9,097 | +7.1% | 12,312 ms | 13,191 ms | +7.1% | | 160k | 9,018 | 8,390 | +7.5% | 17,743 ms | 19,070 ms | +7.5% | #### chunk16384 — saturated throughput (c=16): | il (c) | q8 tps | q16 tps | Δtps | q8 TTFT | q16 TTFT | ΔTTFT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32k (c16) | 12,336 | 11,580 | +6.5% | 23,217 ms | 24,702 ms | +6.4% | | 64k (c16) | 11,389 | 10,628 | +7.2% | 49,643 ms | 53,189 ms | +7.1% | #### chunk8192 — c=1 single-request latency: | il | q8 tps | q16 tps | Δtps | q8 TTFT | q16 TTFT | ΔTTFT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 3.5k | 11,587 | 11,048 | +4.9% | 302 ms | 317 ms | +4.9% | | 8k | 12,278 | 11,620 | +5.7% | 652 ms | 688 ms | +5.7% | | 16k | 12,117 | 11,447 | +5.9% | 1,320 ms | 1,398 ms | +5.9% | | 32k | 11,658 | 10,982 | +6.2% | 2,745 ms | 2,914 ms | +6.1% | | 64k | 10,784 | 10,088 | +6.9% | 5,934 ms | 6,344 ms | +6.9% | | 120k | 9,578 | 8,848 | +8.2% | 12,529 ms | 13,562 ms | +8.2% | | 160k | 8,860 | 8,165 | +8.5% | 18,058 ms | 19,595 ms | +8.5% | #### chunk8192 — saturated throughput (c=16): | il (c) | q8 tps | q16 tps | Δtps | q8 TTFT | q16 TTFT | ΔTTFT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32k (c16) | 11,974 | 11,269 | +6.3% | 23,672 ms | 25,114 ms | +6.1% | | 64k (c16) | 11,072 | 10,369 | +6.8% | 50,012 ms | 53,361 ms | +6.7% | ### Accuracy For GSM8K, we use the full evaluation set with `--num-examples 1319` and keep the default deterministic evaluation configuration from `sglang.test.run_eval`. GSM8K is a short-context mathematical reasoning benchmark, so it mainly checks whether the Q8KV8 sparse prefill path preserves the model's normal reasoning behavior under the same serving configuration. Both q8 and q16 runs use the same model, tokenizer, TP size, FP8 KV cache, chunked prefill size, and sampling/evaluation settings; the only changed server-side parameter is `--dsv4-prefill-backend`. For LongBench-v2, we use a filtered long-context subset with `--num-examples 120`, `--min-context-length 10000`, and `--max-context-length 200000`. The context-length filter keeps the evaluation focused on long-prefill workloads while avoiding outlier samples that exceed the model/server context limit after tokenization. We follow the stochastic long-context setting with `temperature=0.6`, `top_p=0.95`, and `max_tokens=8192`, matching the style of prior DeepSeek-V4 sparse prefill accuracy checks. Under this setup, the comparison is intended to test whether the Q8KV8 prefill implementation changes long-context answer quality, rather than to report a full LongBench-v2 leaderboard number. | Dataset(chunk8192) | q8 | q16 | Δ (q8 - q16) | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GSM8K | 0.970 | 0.969 | +0.001 | | LongBench-v2 | 0.509 | 0.515 | -0.006 | The GSM8K result is unchanged, with Q8KV8 slightly higher by 0.001 absolute. On the LongBench-v2 filtered subset, Q8KV8 is lower by 0.006 absolute, which is small for this stochastic long-context evaluation setting. Overall, these results do not show a material accuracy regression from switching the sparse prefill path from `flashmla_sparse` to `flashmla_sparse_q8`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
