signal.title: [Fix] Support LSE on the RadixAttention extra-kwargs graph path
signal.text: ## Motivation RadixAttention routes backend-specific arguments such as relative bias and auxiliary tensors through a separate graph-compatible helper. Unlike the standard attention path, that helper assumes a tensor-only backend result and discards log-sum-exp output. As a result, attention calls that require both extra kwargs and LSE cannot use the graph path correctly. ## Modifications - Route return_lse through the extra-kwargs attention path. - Unpack and return backend LSE results while preserving the existing tensor-only behavior. - Pad LSE to the CUDA graph token bucket so captured outputs retain stable shapes during replay. - Add a focused regression test covering real-token values and zeroed padding rows. ## Accuracy Tests The regression test verifies that backend LSE values are preserved for live tokens and that padded graph rows are zero. - 6 focused unit tests passed, including 6 parameterized subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The tensor-only path is unchanged; the added handling is active only when LSE is requested. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32307759632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307759632)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32307759427](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307759427)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Summary GLM-Image requires its generation resolution to be divisible by 32. After the requested resolution is rounded up to the D32 generation grid, the decoded output currently keeps the aligned dimensions instead of the dimensions requested by the user. signal.title: [Weight Cache] Support static DP/EP layouts
signal.text: ## Motivation Weight-cache daemons and engines must construct identical model-parallel layouts before CUDA IPC can safely map a cached MoE shard. The existing daemon launcher rejected `dp_size > 1`, preventing static DP/EP deployments from using the daemon-backed weight cache. This change adds static DP/EP layout support to the CUDA IPC weight-cache path. It is the implementation foundation for the DP/EP roadmap in #33522. ## Modifications - Propagate static DP/EP, MoE DP, attention DP, MoE A2A, and DeepEP-mode configuration from the engine into weight-cache daemons. - Initialize daemon-side model-parallel and MoE state with the same static layout as the engine. - Extend `CacheConfig` with MoE DP/EP shard identity and layout fields, so daemon/client compatibility validation rejects incompatible shards. - Fix static Mooncake EP dispatch to use an all-active rank mask when Elastic EP state is absent. - Route Qwen3 MoE through the existing DeepEP-class backend predicate so Mooncake uses the EP execution path. - Add CPU coverage for MoE shard-rank calculation, extended cache fingerprints, and daemon DeepEP-mode forwarding. The implementation supports static layouts. Dynamic expert placement, EPLB, redundant experts, and recovery lifecycle ownership remain roadmap work. ## Accuracy Tests - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_weight_cache_protocol.py` - `29 passed` - Eight-GPU Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 daemon IPC serving with `TP=DP=EP=8`, Mooncake low-latency A2A, DP attention, and DP LM head. - 8 daemons exported IPC handles. - 8 schedulers logged `Loaded model via IPC`. - A deterministic completion generated `Paris` for `The capital of France is`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. signal.title: [diffusion] feat: overlap declared-parallel pipeline stages
signal.text: ## Motivation Adjacent conditioning stages such as text encoding, image encoding, and image-VAE encoding can be independent, but pipelines currently execute every stage serially. This PR adds an explicit declaration mechanism and safely overlaps eligible stages. ## Implementation - `ComposedPipelineBase.add_parallel_stages()` declares one dependency-free execution level. - `ParallelExecutor` runs eligible replicated stages on the caller stream plus reused side CUDA streams. Every member must opt into `concurrency_safe` and return the same request object. - `PipelineStage.may_use_collectives` independently declares cross-rank communication. Multiple collective members are placed in declaration-ordered epochs; non-collective siblings can overlap the first epoch without risking rank-dependent NCCL ordering. - `ImageVAEEncodingStage` reads an explicit VAE capability. Wan VAE reports an encode collective only when spatial-parallel encode is active. - The residency manager permits a parallel group only when all referenced components are resident. CPU/layerwise offload, non-CUDA execution, unsupported stage paradigms, and `--parallel-stage-execution serial` retain serial execution. - `serial` is the default. `auto` is explicit because overlap can increase the temporary activation/workspace peak. ## Adoption Wan I2V and I2V-DMD, Flux2, Qwen Image Edit, Joy Image Edit, MOVA, LongLive2, and the independent LingBot realtime conditioning branches declare applicable parallel groups. ## Validation - Unit coverage includes execution-level derivation, overlap, ordered collective epochs, payload identity, offload downgrades, grad-mode inheritance, residency contracts, and Wan VAE's SP encode capability. - Prior H200 E2E measurements: Flux2 Klein Base I2I at 512x512 improved by 6.77% at one step on one GPU, 2.45% at four steps on one GPU, and 6.33% at four steps with TP2; the TP2 output was byte-identical. The same model at 50 steps improved 0.45% while increasing per-rank peak memory by about 1.65 GB. LongLive2 I2V at 832x480x61 and four steps showed no material gain (0.01%). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32321535556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32321535556)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32321535429](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32321535429)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Summary - Fuse Kimi-K3 identity-RoPE Q materialization, Q concat, and latent KV-cache write through AITER's per-head MLA cache operator. - Support BF16-Q/BF16-KV, FP8-Q/FP8-KV, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV mixed output for Triton decode. - Dispatch only on gfx950 decode/idle batches with contiguous covered inputs; DCP and unsupported contracts fail closed to the existing split/cat/cache path. ## Runtime configuration ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION=1 ``` Validated FP8-KV configuration: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend triton \ --decode-attention-backend triton ``` BF16 KV is also covered. signal.author: kkHuang-amd

signal.title: [Perf] Keep RadixKey prefix matching on the array('q') memcmp path
signal.text: ### Motivation The radix-tree prefix match (`RadixKey.match`) runs for every request that enters the scheduler (`match_prefix_for_req`) and for every prefill insert traversal (`_insert_helper`). Its inner loop compares exponentially growing slices of the two token-id sequences, so the **container type** of `token_ids` dominates the per-call cost: - `array('q')` slice compare is a C-level `memcmp` (fast); - `list[int]` slice compare copies references and boxes every `PyLong` — measured up to **~15x slower** on long shared prefixes. Two concrete issues motivated this PR: 1. `HiRadixCache._concat_split_chain` (backup/restore path) rebuilds a `RadixKey` from plain lists, dropping the restored key onto the slow slice-compare path; 2. `RadixKey.match` asserted `type(t0) is type(t1)`, so a plain-list query key compared against an array-backed tree node (or vice versa) **crashed** even when the contents were identical. This PR keeps the hot path on `array('q')` and makes mixed container inputs safe. ### Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` — `RadixKey.match`: when the two sides' containers disagree, convert the `list` side to `array('q')` so matching proceeds on the memcmp path and the `type is type` assert no longer trips on a list query key vs an array-backed tree node. An eager convert of *both* sides is deliberately avoided: `array("q", list)` costs O(n) per call and is **more** expensive than the list slice compare it would replace, so the convert is limited to the mixed-type case. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py` — `_concat_split_chain`: rebuild the restored `RadixKey` from `array('q')` segments instead of materializing a plain list (also cheaper than list materialization + re-boxing). - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py` — new `test_match_mixed_container_types` and `test_match_list_input_page_and_bigram`. - `benchmark/scheduler/bench_radix_key_match.py` — new stdlib-only micro-benchmark (no torch) that quantifies the container-type cost difference. ### Accuracy Tests N/A — no model forward / kernel / sampling logic changed. Matching semantics are bit-for-bit identical for identical contents; the change only affects the container used to compare (mixed-type inputs now match instead of asserting). ### Speed Tests and Profiling `benchmark/scheduler/bench_radix_key_match.py`, WSL / 16 GB, mean us per call (divergence right after the shared prefix): ``` shared | array/array | list/list | mixed | list/array 1000 | 4.72 | 17.42 | 1430.51 | 3.7x 10000 | 18.97 | 213.30 | 1475.47 | 11.2x 50000 | 68.78 | 879.17 | 1573.07 | 12.8x 99999 | 105.34 | 1571.35 | 1617.83 | 14.9x ``` - `array/array` stays the fastest path with **no regression**: the added `type(...)` checks are O(1) and never run on same-type inputs. - `list/list` remains backward-compatible but ~3.7x–14.9x slower — this is why array storage should be preferred at the source. - `mixed list/array` now matches instead of asserting. ### Checklist - [x] Add unit tests — `test_radix_cache_unit.py` (+2 cases). WSL validation: radix/hiradix unit tests all pass; full `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/` = 1653 passed with the 10 GiB host-memory reserve temporarily overridden for this 16 GB machine. The 2 default-run failures are host-RAM capacity (`Not enough host memory available`), not this change. - [x] Provide speed benchmark results (above). Accuracy tests: not applicable. - [ ] Format code with pre-commit — follows existing style; not run locally (no dev env), CI will verify. - [ ] Update documentation — N/A beyond the benchmark module docstring. ### Review and Merge - Area: KV Cache — merge oncall / codeowners: @ispobock, @xiezhq-hermann. - CI: please tag the PR (`/tag-and-rerun-ci` or `/tag-run-ci-label`) to run on standard runners (larger memory than the local WSL box). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32322342588](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322342588)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32322341990](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322341990)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(openai): Accept the input_audio content part in chat completions
signal.text: ## Motivation OpenAI's Chat Completions API carries inline audio as an `input_audio` content part, holding base64 data plus a format label. SGLang accepts audio only as `audio_url`, an sglang extension whose payload is a URL or a data URI. A request written against the OpenAI spec therefore fails schema validation with a 400 before it reaches the model, on every audio-capable model served through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Inkling, Gemma 4, MiMo-V2.5, and others). ## Modifications - `ChatCompletionMessageContentAudioPart` becomes an annotated union of two concrete variants: the existing `audio_url` part, and a new `input_audio` part. - An `AfterValidator` rewrites an `input_audio` part into the equivalent `audio_url` data URI as it validates, using the registered media type for the declared format (`wav` → `audio/wav`, `mp3` → `audio/mpeg`). - Nothing downstream changes. The conversation parser, the chat-template parser, and the multimodal loader continue to handle `audio_url` alone, so both spellings share one code path and a client's choice between them stops being visible past validation. - Existing `audio_url` requests are unaffected: the variant passes through untouched, for both HTTP(S) URLs and data URIs. - The cookbook pages that describe the audio content-part format (Inkling, Inkling-Small, Gemma 4) now name `input_audio` alongside `audio_url`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; this is request-schema validation only and does not affect model outputs. Inline audio is rewritten to the data URI form that `audio_url` already accepted, so the decoded waveform and the resulting prompt are identical to those of an equivalent `audio_url` request. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; the added work is one dict lookup and one string concatenation per audio content part, at validation time. ## Test Plan 8 new unit tests: 7 protocol cases covering conversion for both formats, `audio_url` passthrough for a URL and a data URI, rejection of an unsupported format, rejection of a missing payload on either variant, and that the JSON schema advertises both spellings; plus one end-to-end case in the conversation-parser tests, built from raw dicts so the parts go through validation the way a request body does, confirming inline audio arrives as a data URI at a parser that only knows `audio_url`. ``` python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py \ test/registered/unit/parser/test_conversation.py \ test/registered/unit/parser/test_jinja_template_utils.py # 139 passed ``` Both test files are already registered on `base-a-test-cpu`, so the new cases run in CI without registry changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update the documentation: the cookbook pages describing the audio content-part format now name `input_audio`. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32057038950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32057038950)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32057038648](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32057038648)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4 MI355X: eliminate bpreshuffle fp8-scale copies at producer sites (MoE down, MLA o_proj bmm)
signal.text: ## Summary Follow-up to the dense-linear bpreshuffle scale no-copy. Several DeepSeek-V4 sites **pre-quantize** an activation and hand a `(fp8, scale)` tuple to a downstream Linear; those scales are emitted row-major and then relaid out with `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` — a relayout **copy per site, per layer** on MI355X (gfx950). This PR eliminates those copies for the producer quant kernels that honor `transpose_scale`, via a zero-copy `torch.as_strided` reinterpret. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`** — one producer-neutral `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` (+ `_tuple`) helper: the zero-copy stride reinterpret of a scale a quant kernel already emitted with `transpose_scale=True`. This **consolidates** the identical `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` that landed on main in #31727 with this PR's producer helper (both were `as_strided(scale, scale.shape, (1, scale.shape[0]))`) into a single operation, keeping the established #31727 name for consistency. Also adds `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale(m, on_bpreshuffle_gfx95=...)`, centralizing the shared `M >= 2` emit gate. - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** — fused-RMS producer repointed to the consolidated helper. - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`** — MLP down-proj input producer (`fused_clamp_act_mul`): request `transpose_scale=True` and reinterpret instead of copy (gated `M>=2`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla_rocm.py`** — o_proj bmm producers ×2 in `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` (`fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant`): same treatment. (ROCm MLA now dispatches here after the recent `forward_mla_rocm.py` split; the optimization was moved off `forward_mla.py`, which is back to matching upstream, so it lands on the actual MI355X call path.) Sites fed by `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` follow the same helper now (the #31727 fix made that kernel honor `transpose_scale`). ## Tests - **CPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_scale.py`) — helper-level stride/no-copy contract, and the centralized `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale` gate incl. the `M == 1` materialize fallback. - **MI35X GPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_producer_mi35x.py`, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) — invokes **both real producers** (`fused_clamp_act_mul`, `fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant`) with `transpose_scale=True` + no-copy vs `transpose_scale=False` + materialize, asserting bit-identical quantized output, equal scale values, the `(1, M)` column-major stride, and zero-copy storage sharing (M ∈ {1, 2, 8, 16}; M==1 exercises the materialize fallback). This is the direct producer-level equivalence evidence — the invariant the optimization relies on, checked on the real kernels rather than a fabricated layout. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP8. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260731`. Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 2 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.933 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.931 | The patched runs sit ~0.8–0.9 pt below baseline. With only two runs per arm this is consistent with, but does not by itself establish, DeepSeek-V4 fp4-MoE run-to-run noise. The correctness guarantee for this PR comes instead from the **producer-level bit-exact test** above: the converted kernels emit identical quantized output and scale values on both paths, so the reroute cannot change the model result. (Happy to add more GSM8K reps if useful.) ### Perf (random 8k/1k, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, seed 42) — preliminary **Single-shot, one run per arm — treat as preliminary, not an established speedup.** The Δ below (≈ ±0.4–0.8%) is within DeepSeek-V4 decode run-to-run noise at these concurrencies and is not backed by repeated A/B runs, so I'm not claiming it as a confirmed win. The correctness/no-regression guarantee for this PR is the **producer-level bit-exact test** above (identical quantized output + scale values on both paths); the value here is eliminating a per-site/per-layer relayout copy, which these numbers are consistent with but do not by themselves prove. I can add repeated-run A/B (mean/p50/variance) if a throughput claim is wanted. | conc | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | ΔTPOT | baseline total tok/s | patched total tok/s | Δtot | |-----:|:------------------:|:-----------------:|:-----:|:--------------------:|:-------------------:|:----:| | 16 | 19.48 | 19.32 | −0.8% | 6500.2 | 6549.1 | +0.8% | | 32 | 24.63 | 24.50 | −0.5% | 9685.3 | 9728.3 | +0.4% | | 64 | 35.03 | 34.79 | −0.7% | 12819.0 | 12898.1 | +0.6% | Measured under pure TP8. (No DP-attention measurement yet — the earlier "larger under DP-attention" note is removed until that's actually measured.) Coherent, zero dropped requests. Applies on top of the dense-linear PR (different `fp8_utils` region) or standalone. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32272019567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32272019567)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32272018916](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32272018916)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][CI] Run the ROCm 7.2 nightly on both 7.2.4 and 7.2.0
signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30984, and a sibling to #35602 which does the same for the PR gate. #30984 added rocm724 to the release matrix, so rocm724 images are now published nightly — but the nightly **test** suite still hardcoded `--rocm-version rocm720` in all 47 container starts and had no way to select a flavor. The new images were going untested. The release workflow also still publishes rocm720 images, so simply switching the nightly to 7.2.4 would leave a shipped flavor with no coverage at all. ## Modifications `.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml` only. **Parameterized**, mirroring what `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` already does: a `rocm_version` input on both `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`, plus a workflow-level `ROCM_VERSION` that carries the default — `inputs` is empty on the `schedule` and `push` triggers, so the default cannot live on the inputs alone. All 47 hardcoded container starts now read `--rocm-version "$ROCM_VERSION"`. **Both flavors covered, via a second cron rather than a matrix.** Adding a `rocm_version` matrix dimension to all 47 jobs would have doubled the concurrent GPU load on a suite that already saturates the runners for roughly three hours. Two schedules cost the same total GPU time but spread it: | cron (UTC) | flavor | image it picks up | | --- | --- | --- | | `30 17 * * *` | rocm724 | same day's, published ~14:30 | | `30 5 * * *` | rocm720 | previous day's | Resolution across every trigger: | trigger | `ROCM_VERSION` | | --- | --- | | schedule 17:30 | `rocm724` | | schedule 05:30 | `rocm720` | | push to `main` (`version.py`) | `rocm724` | | dispatch / call, default | `rocm724` | | dispatch / call, explicit | as given | **Concurrency.** The scheduled group now carries the flavor, so a rocm720 run and a rocm724 run cannot cancel each other if one overruns into the other's slot. The dispatch and caller branches of that expression are untouched. ## Merge precondition The rocm720 leg is safe to land at any time. The **rocm724 leg** needs a rocm724 nightly image inside `find_latest_image`'s 7-day window, or the 17:30 run fails at container start — there is no hard-coded rocm724 fallback, by design. Blast radius is smaller than #35602 (a nightly, not the PR gate), but the same check applies: ```bash curl -s "https://registry.hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/rocm/sgl-dev/tags?page_size=100&name=rocm724-mi30x" \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([t['name'] for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['results']][:3])" ``` At the time of writing the newest rocm724 tag is `v0.5.16-rocm724-mi30x-20260807`, outside the window. The first post-#30984 rocm724 nightly builds at 12:00 UTC. ## Validation The full nightly suite was run against both flavors' staging images on #30984's head before it merged — 36 pass / 11 real failures on each, with every failure matching a `main` baseline at test level. Details in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5340700214. Locally verified here: the YAML parses, all 48 jobs are intact, all 47 container starts resolve through `ROCM_VERSION`, no `--rocm-version rocm720` literal remains, and the expression resolves as tabulated above for each trigger. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests <!-- N/A: CI configuration change --> - [ ] Update documentation <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signal.title: [AMD][CI] Default the ROCm 7.2 PR gate to 7.2.4
signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30984. That PR landed the rocm724 flavor but deliberately kept the PR gate on rocm720, because no rocm724 nightly image existed yet and `find_latest_image` would have aborted at container start rather than degrading. Its commit message said to flip the default once rocm724 nightlies exist. This is that flip. ## Modifications `.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` — `rocm724` becomes the default for the dispatch input, the call input, the workflow-level `ROCM_VERSION` fallback, and the value forwarded to the extra suite. `.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-extra.yml` — same flip. This one is easy to miss: the extra workflow has its own `pull_request` trigger and runs standalone on every PR (all 100 of its recent runs are `pull_request`), where `inputs` is empty and its inline `|| 'rocm720'` fallbacks pick the flavor. Changing only `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` would have left the extra suite on 7.2.0 while the main suite moved to 7.2.4. Its job-name suffix marks non-default flavors and was keyed on `!= 'rocm720'`; it now reads `!= 'rocm724'`. **No required status check name changes.** On the `pull_request` path `inputs.rocm_version` is empty, so the suffix was empty before and is empty after. An explicit `rocm720` dispatch is now the one that gets marked: | trigger | job name | | --- | --- | | `pull_request` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` (unchanged) | | dispatched `rocm724` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` | | dispatched `rocm720` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720` | rocm720 stays reachable from the dropdown and via `AMD_CI_IMAGE`. ## Merge precondition — please do not merge until this holds `find_latest_image` searches a **7-day** window of dated tags and has **no hard-coded rocm724 fallback**, so it returns 1 and the container start fails outright if no recent image exists. That is deliberate — better a loud failure than silently testing a months-old image — but it means this PR must not land before a rocm724 nightly is inside the window. At the time of writing the newest rocm724 tag in `rocm/sgl-dev` is `v0.5.16-rocm724-mi30x-20260807`, which is 13 days old and therefore outside the window. The first post-#30984 rocm724 nightly builds at 12:00 UTC and takes about 2.5h. Check before merging: ```bash curl -s "https://registry.hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/rocm/sgl-dev/tags?page_size=100&name=rocm724-mi30x" \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([t['name'] for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['results']][:3])" ``` Both `rocm724-mi30x` and `rocm724-mi35x` need a tag dated within the last 7 days. ## Validation The 7.2.4 images were exercised end to end on #30984's head before it merged: all six flavors built, and the full PR and nightly suites ran against them on both 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 with no failure attributable to the change — every failure matched a `main` baseline at test level. Details in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5340700214. ## Note on naming The jobs in this workflow keep their static `-rocm720` suffixes (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720`, ...) even though they now run 7.2.4. Renaming them would break every required status check, so that debt is left for a separate pass. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests <!-- N/A: CI configuration change --> - [ ] Update documentation <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signal.title: [Diffusion] Align MiniMax H3 request RNG with reference
signal.text: ## Summary - use one request-local CPU generator for MiniMax H3 noise - preserve the reference draw order: visual conditions, target video tensor, then target audio rows - precompute condition noise before denoising instead of re-seeding per modality or condition - keep the existing H3-only scope so other diffusion consistency trajectories are unchanged ## Why The previous implementation independently re-seeded video, audio, and condition streams. For T2VA this made the target audio latent diverge immediately; because H3 jointly attends over video and audio rows, video output also drifted. The new contract follows the official Diffusers MiniMax H3 implementation from huggingface/diffusers#14355. ## Validation - focused MiniMax H3 numerical contract: 5 passed on H100 devbox - pre-commit: passed on the exact remote checkout - standard 2-GPU H100 E2E: 1 passed in 176.29s (47.50s generation, 22.5 GiB peak GPU memory) - official GT workflow: [run 31890047128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890047128) succeeded - ci-data GT commit: [81ca8f18](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/81ca8f18d485df4e4bac9a5a40c5b4666f0fa57f) - NVIDIA PR CI: [run 31890556920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890556920) succeeded The GT follow-up is intentionally limited to the affected MiniMax H3 H100 T2VA frames. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32321951129](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32321951129)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32321950979](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32321950979)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: docker: fix CUDA-13 build — rename NCCL_VERSION ARG to avoid base image ENV collision
signal.text: ## Problem The CUDA-13 branch in `docker/Dockerfile` runs: ``` pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps "nvidia-nccl-cu13==${NCCL_VERSION}" ``` The `nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-cudnn-devel-ubuntu24.04` base image sets `ENV NCCL_VERSION=2.28.3-1` (Debian/apt format), which **shadows** the Dockerfile's `ARG NCCL_VERSION=2.30.7` at `RUN` time. So pip requests `2.28.3-1`, which is not a valid PyPI version, and the build fails: ``` ERROR: No matching distribution found for nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.28.3-1 ``` ## Fix Rename the ARG to `SGL_NCCL_VERSION` so it no longer collides with the base image's `ENV NCCL_VERSION`; the intended `2.30.7` is used. This matches `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`'s `install_nccl()`, which already hardcodes `2.30.7`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32316009906](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316009906)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316009800](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316009800)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec] Support quantized target lm_head in DFlash2 selector
signal.text: ## Summary - Route DFlash2 candidate projection through `lm_head.quant_method.apply` when the target head is quantized. - Preserve the existing dense projection and TP-local top-k behavior, including slicing padded vocabulary rows before top-k. - Replace the unit test that rejected packed heads with a correctness test for quantization-aware candidate generation. ## Motivation DFlash2 borrows the target model's `lm_head` to build its selector candidates. A ModelOpt NVFP4 target stores that head as packed weights, so treating `.weight` as a dense FP16/BF16 matrix either fails the dense-head guard or produces a shape mismatch. The DFlash worker already keeps a quantized selector head on the eager path instead of folding its static matrix multiplication into the draft CUDA graph. This change makes that eager fallback functional by using the same `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` dispatch as the target logits path. Dense heads retain the existing sliced matrix multiplication, and TP still communicates only local top-k values and IDs. This is a quantized-head follow-up to #35371. Related fixes use the same dispatch pattern in #30119 and #34742. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_logits.py` - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_logits.py` (`4 passed`) - An equivalent runtime override of this `compute_candidates` path was validated with a ModelOpt NVFP4 Qwen3.8-27B target and Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 draft at TP=2. The server completed target and draft CUDA graph capture, kept the quantized selector head eager as intended, served a smoke request, and completed 1000/1000, 50000/400, and 97000/3000 workloads at concurrency 1, 4, and 8. ## Behavior note This PR adds functional quantized-head support to the DFlash2 selector. It does not fold the quantized selector projection into the draft CUDA graph; that remains a separate optimization opportunity. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32231149827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231149827)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32231149622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231149622)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CI][AMD] Run the profiling suite without CUDA graphs on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation `pr-test-amd-rocm720` job [`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720 (linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang, 4)`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31270030007/job/93134338366) failed because `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` hung for ~9 minutes and then took the server down with it. ### What actually happened `test_start_profile_2` posts `/start_profile` with no `num_steps`, so the profiler session stays open across the following `/generate`. The scheduler served the prefill eagerly, then wedged on the first decode CUDA-graph replay and never came back: ``` Thread 19929 (idle): "MainThread" pthread_mutex_lock (libc.so.6) 0x7d914f698353 (libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200) ... 9 more libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200 frames ... at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay (libtorch_hip.so) replay (torch/cuda/graphs.py:141) replay (runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py:150) execute (runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1328) _forward_raw (model_runner.py:1629) ``` Two py-spy dumps 11 s apart show the identical frame, so it is a real deadlock in the HIP runtime's graph-launch path, not sampling noise. The 300 s scheduler watchdog then fired (soft, then hard), `SIGQUIT` killed the server, and the remaining test methods failed with `Connection refused` — which is what the CI report surfaces, but it is only the downstream symptom. ### The two hypotheses in the CI report are both disconfirmed - **`a1ca76b2` (#34052, "Unify WAR read-done gating behind shared-read boundary declarations")** was flagged as the only in-window commit touching `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`. It cannot change ROCm behaviour: `make_war_read_done_event()` returns `None` unless `is_cuda()`, so on HIP `war_read_done_event` is `None`, `_war_read_done_node_planted` stays `False`, and `_war_read_done_record()` collapses `IN_REPLAY` back to `PRE_REPLAY` — exactly the pre-refactor decode policy. - **The CI image rebuild `20260807 -> 20260808`** changed the tag (`v0.5.16-rocm720-mi30x-20260807` -> `v0.5.17-rocm720-mi30x-20260808`), but both images ship the identical torch build `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.lw.git7e1940d4`, so the profiler and the HIP runtime are unchanged across the pass->fail boundary. The resolved `cuda_graph_config` in the two server-args dumps is identical too. ### What it is A race in the ROCm 7.2.0 HIP runtime when a torch-profiler (rocprofiler-sdk kineto) session is attached across HIP graph replays: - The Aug 7 run of the same shard executed the exact same interleaving — three `Profiling starts` / `Stop profiling` / `Profiling done` cycles, the same `ROCTracer produced duplicate flow start` warning, and `Decode batch ... cuda graph: True` in between — and passed in 67 s. The pattern is not deterministically broken; it is timing-dependent. - Across the whole rocm720 run, this is the only file that hit a `CUDAGraph::replay` hang, and it is the only file in CI that attaches and detaches `torch.profiler` around live decoding. The other watchdog hangs that day sit in different frames (device-to-host `.item()` sync in `aiter_backend.init_forward_metadata`). - The hang lands on the first graph launch after the profiler is re-attached, ~30 ms after the previous session was torn down. - AMD documents this class of problem: the ROCm 7.2.4 notes call out reduced `hipGraphLaunch` latency and improved ROCprofiler-SDK stability "for vLLM workloads traced with PyTorch `torch.profiler`", and pytorch/pytorch#177873 documents ROCm 7.2.0 CLR/ROCR bugs that surface specifically under `torch.profiler`. ## Modifications Launch `TestStartProfile`'s server with `--disable-cuda-graph` on HIP. The suite covers the `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` request surface (`start_step`, `num_steps`, no-arg, trace-file emission), none of which depends on graph replay, so no coverage is lost — and with graphs off there is no `hipGraphLaunch` to deadlock while the profiler is attached. CUDA runners are untouched and keep profiling-with-graphs coverage. The server also skips its ~4.4 s decode-graph capture, so the AMD run should get slightly faster rather than slower. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — test-only change, no runtime code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31758879497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31758879497)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31758879362](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31758879362)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache] Fix PP inconsistency with HiCache L3 (#22607)
signal.text: ## Motivation When deploying HiCache and PP, multiple PP ranks go diverge and eventually cause sglang crash. The detailed reason was discussed in issue #22607. ## Modifications This patch introduces two kinds of synchronization mechanisms to fix the issue. I will illustrate this idea with an example of pp_size=2 and tp_size=1. 1. **pp_sync** across scheduler threads. pp_sync is a new name introduced by this patch. PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the **exact** same number of events from its queues. This prevents divergence. 2. **all_reduce** across prefetch threads. Consider a case that PP0 and PP1 have different lengths on their L3 storage for a given sequence. They have to reach an agreement on the length, by perform all_reduce(MIN). This behavior is consistent with TP. This patch also changes how `check_prefetch_progress` works. Before this patch, it simply does all_reduce(MIN) to determine the final tokens prefetchted. However, this would not work on PP, as we cannot do that in the scheduler thread. This patch adds a new background thread `prefetch_sync_thread`, which does the all_reduce work instead. ## Accuracy Tests Added `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py`. I have also tested SWE-bench verified with DSv4 flash model. I ran two groups: - Group A: The baseline, commit 5747ed3b, without this PR, TP=8, L3 enabled. Resolved 356/500. - Group B: This PR, PP=4, TP=2, L3 enabled. Resolved 353/500. I analyzed the difference, and found 351 cases successful in both group, 5 are successful only in group A, and 2 are successful only in group B. The 7 cases that are successfuly in one group but failed in another, are due to container exits after a long time. Here are commands for anyone has interested in reproducing this test. Hints to make L3 are in-use: - Use large number of workers (128), leading to large number of running requests. - Limit number of tokens in L1 and L2. ```sh # Group A sglang serve \ --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp-size 8 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=500000 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # Group B sglang serve \ --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --pp-size 4 \ --tp-size 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=500000 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # SWE bench agent python -m minisweagent.run.benchmarks.swebench \ --subset verified \ --split test \ -c swebench.yaml -c environment.container_timeout=24h \ -o /root/swe_test/result \ -m "openai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" \ -w 128 # SWE evaluation python -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation \ --predictions_path /root/swe_test/result/preds.json \ --dataset_name princeton-nlp/SWE-Bench_Verified \ --split test \ --max_workers 32 \ --run_id test-mini-swe-agent \ --timeout 1200 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling I tested with L1 only, L1+L2 and L1+L2+L3. The size of L1 and L2 are configured not to hold all tokens. L3 is large enough to hold all tokens. `request-rate` is set to `1` so that L3 prefetch are performed and not limited by budget. ```sh # L1 sglang serve \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=4 \ --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen25 \ --page-size=64 \ --enable-metrics # L2 sglang serve \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=4 \ --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen25 \ --page-size=64 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-mem-layout=page_first # L3 sglang serve \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=4 \ --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen25 \ --page-size=64 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-mem-layout=page_first \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "256gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # Benchmark python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \ --num-clients=128 \ --num-rounds=10 \ --disable-auto-run \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --enable-round-barrier \ --request-rate 1 ``` ``` L1 Per-round metrics: Round signal.title: [NPU]Ensure tensors allocated by empty_like are contiguous
signal.text: ## Motivation `torch.empty_like(q)` inherits the memory format of `q` by default. If `q` is non-contiguous, `attn_output` may also become non-contiguous, which may lead to failures in downstream NPU operations requiring contiguous tensors. ## Modifications - Allocate `attn_output` with `memory_format=torch.contiguous_format` in attention forward paths. - Ensure `attn_output` has a contiguous memory layout for both extend and decode. ## Accuracy Tests gemma-3-4b-it ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [RFC] KVCR as a HiCacheStorage backend for peer-to-peer KV reuse
signal.text:
## Summary SGLang's HiCache already supports pluggable L3 storage backends (mooncake, hf3fs, eic, …) behind a stable `HiCacheStorage` interface. This RFC adds KVCR as one more such backend. KVCR is a multi-tier KV cache management solution from NVIDIA. The integration totally follows the integration and design of hicache storage — we register a `"kvcr"` backend and implement the same `batch_set_v2 / batch_get_v2 / batch_exists_v2` contract the other backends already implement. This backend also aligns with the router-initiated hint model in **[#27574 — Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574)**, which defines a provider-neutral hint taxonomy (Share / Prefetch / Demote / Pin / Retain). KVCR fits the **`Share`** intent — *"reuse a prefix that already lives on another worker... pull the prefix from the old one"* — but does not depend on that RFC: it is a self-contained mechanism any router emitting such a hint can drive. Following the Dynamo DEP (ai-dynamo/dynamo#11673), the near term goal is **direct worker-to-worker (host memory) KV reuse**: a prefix computed on one worker is served to another without recomputation or a round-trip through a global pool. When a request lands on a worker lacking a prefix another worker holds, KVCR fetches it **peer-to-peer** — an asymmetric, directed transfer, not a symmetric external store. Selecting *which* peer holds the prefix is a decision only a router can make well. So the router hands the target worker a small piece of per-request metadata — a **hint** — naming the peer. "Router" here means any orchestrator above the engine: the router (flash indexer) is the first target, SGLang's own router a later one, and the same carrier serves both. The rest of this RFC covers (1) that hint and (2) how KVCR plugs into HiCache to act on it. ## Part 1 — Router Hint ### Why a hint is needed HiCache storage is content-addressed: the controller asks `get(block_hash)` and the backend is expected to know where the bytes live. That works for a global pool. It does **not** work for P2P reuse, where the same prefix may sit on any one of N peer workers. The only component that knows which one is the **router** — it made the routing decision that sent this request here in the first place. The hint will directly tell the node where target kvcache sits. ### Why decide this at the router Putting the source-selection decision at the routing stage — rather than probing peers after a request lands — is what makes the hint valuable beyond avoiding a broadcast: - **It enables a routing cost function that can grow over time.** The hint is the input to a decision the router makes; that decision can start *simple* (route on load only, ignoring cache residency) and evolve to *rich* (weigh prefix cache residency, estimated transfer time, distance/topology, and thresholds that decide when a P2P fetch is even worth it versus recomputation). - **It lets us prefetch and shape system behavior.** Because the router decides before the request is admitted, the target can begin fetching the prefix ahead of time, and the router — with its global view — can steer placement to balance load and reuse across the fleet, rather than reacting locally after the fact. ### Carrier We do **not** widen the `HiCacheStorage` signature. Every v2 call already threads a free-form `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info` dict from the controller into the backend. The hint is the `Share` case of #27574's provider-neutral hint envelope and rides in that dict; the key name below is a placeholder pending #27574's envelope: ``` # placeholder key — to be aligned with #27574's KvHintEnvelope extra_info.extra_info["kvcr_router_hint"] = { "source_control_endpoint": "host:port", # ZMQ control endpoint of the peer holding the prefix "block_hashes": [...], # root-aligned block hashes for the shared prefix } ``` ### Propagation path The hint travels from the router down to the backend without widening any interface — it rides the `extra_info` dict every layer already passes through: 1. **router → scheduler.** The router attaches the hint to the request's `extra_info`; the scheduler stashes it into the prefetch request. 2. **scheduler → controller.** `HiCacheController.prefetch(...)` carries it into the daemon `prefetch_io_aux_func` thread (`managers/cache_controller.py`). 3. **controller → backend.** `_page_transfer → page_get_func(op, hashes, host_idx, extra_info)` hands it to `KVCR.batch_get_v2(...)` (`storage/kvcr/kvcr_store.py`). 4. **backend → decision.** `RouterHint.maybe_from_extra_info(extra_info)` (`storage/kvcr/router_hint.py`) parses it: - hint **absent/malformed** → fall back to local-only (deposit/local-get), never raises; - hint **present** → drive a directed P2P fetch from `source_control_endpoint`. The parser is **fail-closed**: a missing or malformed hint degrades to local-only behavior, it never crashes a prefetch, and the backend is safe to ship before the any router side lands (dynamo pr here https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/11695). ## Part 2 — KVCR Integration Architecture ### Where it sits ```mermaid flowchart LR SCH[Scheduler] --- HRC[HiRadixCache] --- HCC[HiCacheController] HCC -->|HiCacheStorage iface| KS[KVCR
thin adapter] subgraph core[KVCR core · vendored] LD[local DRAM tier
deposit / get] CC[control channel
ZMQ peer] PT[progress thread
owns NIXL agent] end KS --> core ``` `KVCR` is a thin adapter. It owns no transfer threads of its own — kvcr's core runs **one** daemon "kvcr-progress" thread that exclusively holds the NIXL agent and control socket. The store advances state only by calling `poll_completed()` from the HiCache controller's existing prefetch thread. No new threading model is introduced into SGLang. ### Get path (with router hint) — sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AUX as prefetch aux thread participant KS as KVCR participant PT as KVCR progress thread participant SRC as source worker participant SCH as scheduler AUX->>KS: batch_get_v2(hashes, host_idx, extra_info) Note over KS: hint = maybe_from_extra_info(...) KS->>PT: submit_hint(source_endpoint, keys) Note over PT: register source peer KS->>PT: h = deliver(blocks) PT->>SRC: START_WRITE (ctrl) Note over SRC: search_and_pin SRC-->>PT: NIXL WRITE (UCX) → host pages (direct DMA) SRC-->>PT: send_notif("write_done") Note over PT: _poll_notifications
_TargetDeliverOp: WAITING→FINISHED PT-->>KS: _completion_queue.append(OpResult) Note over KS: poll_completed(): match r.op_handle == h KS-->>AUX: [per-page success bools] Note over AUX: operation.increment(page_size × hits) SCH->>SCH: check_prefetch_progress(req_id)
polls completed_tokens (hiradix_cache.py) Note over SCH: True → req admitted into batch ``` - **A single KVCR daemon thread owns the whole P2P mechanism.** It handles all KVCR↔KVCR message send/recv, maintains the internal op state machine, and drives the interaction with NIXL transfers. When a transfer finishes it does not push anything — it just appends the result to a completion queue; the store itself spawns no extra thread. - **The KVCR thread never touches the scheduler main thread or the prefetch thread.** It runs entirely on its own, so neither of SGLang's threads is blocked or slowed by how KVCR does its work. - **The existing completion-notification model is unchanged.** A finished transfer sits on that queue until the prefetch daemon thread actively drains it via `poll_completed()` and turns it into `completed_tokens`; the scheduler main thread, one level up, only reads the resulting boolean tick (`check_prefetch_progress`) — the same KVPoll-style poll as today. ### Non-goals - No changes to HiRadixCache or the scheduler cache path. - No new SGLang-side transfer threads. - Shared-HiCache serving (source pins from HiRadixCache via `TreeNode.protect_host`) is a future swap of the pin adapter only — out of scope here.

signal.title: [AMD] Perf dsv4 enable heterogeneous AITER FHMoE
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4-Pro stores its 384 routed experts as MXFP4/E8M0, but keeps the single shared expert in native FP8 E4M3 with 128x128 E8M0 scales. Converting that shared expert to MXFP4 introduces avoidable quantization error. This PR integrates AITER's heterogeneous fused shared-expert MoE (FHMoE), so routed experts remain MXFP4 while expert 384 remains native FP8 and both execute in one two-stage MoE schedule. ### AITER dependency This PR requires an AITER build containing both merged changes: - [ROCm/aiter#4269](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4269), merge commit [`00cbe979f20cf380548d7d1d9d73136aa359c276`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/00cbe979f20cf380548d7d1d9d73136aa359c276): FHMoE runtime/AOT implementation. - [ROCm/aiter#4314](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4314), merge commit [`334fd72ad6e69d16785efc97cb8b6b4aec3c2a92`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/334fd72ad6e69d16785efc97cb8b6b4aec3c2a92): C1/C2/C32/C64 decode tuning. All results below were validated with AITER [`868ac1f7aa0d403a77c03e941bc5ffa28c7766d5`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/868ac1f7aa0d403a77c03e941bc5ffa28c7766d5). The ROCm image/deployment must provide this revision or a compatible newer build before enabling the feature. ## Modifications - Add an AITER capability probe and forward native shared weights/scales plus `shared_expert_id` through the MoE runner. - Preserve native FP8 shared-expert checkpoint tensors instead of requantizing them into the MXFP4 routed tensor. - TP-shard shared tensors during loading, retain them for hot reloads, and serialize asynchronous weight/scale pairing. - Expand serialized 128x128 E8M0 scales to AITER's per-1x32 layout, pad the TP8 intermediate shard from logical 384 to physical 512, and apply the required shuffle. - Route six normal experts first, then append semantic expert 384 with weight 1 to form internal `E=385`, `top-k=7` geometry. - Support non-power-of-two routed top-k in the shared-expert append Triton kernel. - Add strict enablement guards and preserve the separate shared-MLP fallback for unsupported configurations. - Add focused tests for policy/fallback, top-k append, TP sharding, FP8/E8M0 layout, uint8 scales, asynchronous loading, hot reload, and argument forwarding. - Add a reproducible validation record under `benchmark/fhmoe/VALIDATION.md`. Enable with: ```bash --enforce-shared-experts-fusion --moe-runner-backend aiter ``` The optimized path is restricted to ROCm `gfx950`, TP=8, EP/A2A/EPLB/offload disabled, BF16 SiLU, 384 routed experts, routed top-k=6, one shared expert, MXFP4 routed weights, and serialized 128x128 block-FP8 shared weights. Unsupported configurations log the reason and use the existing unfused path. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, TP=8, EP disabled, temperature 0, concurrency 64, 20-shot GSM8K, all 1,319 questions: | Mode | Strict exact match | Flexible extract | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Unfused shared MLP | 1254/1319 (95.072%) | 1255/1319 (95.148%) | 0 | | AITER FHMoE | 1262/1319 (95.679%) | 1262/1319 (95.679%) | 0 | FHMoE improved strict accuracy by 0.607 percentage point. All requests completed successfully, with no E8M0-scale, worker, ROCm, or graph-replay errors. Focused SGLang tests: ```bash python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_shared_expert_fusion.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_fhmoe.py ``` Result: `10 passed`. AITER validation included the default and exact DSV4 `test_fhmoe.py` profiles, BM16 scale-boundary coverage, DSV4 AOT precompile, C1/C2/C32/C64 kernel selection, MXFP4 sorting, and HIP graph capture/replay. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hardware/model: 8x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, plain TP8, no EP/A2A/TBO. Workload: fixed 8192 input / 1024 output, `conc*2` warmups and `conc*8` measured requests. | Concurrency | Unfused total tok/s | FHMoE total tok/s | Gain | Unfused / FHMoE median TPOT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 1,218 | 1,233 | +1.25% | 14.28 / 14.09 ms | | 4 | 2,294 | 2,329 | +1.52% | 14.73 / 14.48 ms | | 8 | 4,062 | 4,228 | +4.08% | 16.21 / 15.48 ms | | 16 | 6,803 | 6,917 | +1.67% | 18.55 / 18.18 ms | | 32 | 10,321 | 10,546 | +2.17% | 23.07 / 22.46 ms | FHMoE improved TP8 throughput at every tested concurrency and selected the expected tuned kernels, including the BM16 C32 path. ### Known DP-attention limitation At TP8 + DP8 attention, 8k/1k C256, FHMoE completed 2,048/2,048 requests without errors but regressed total throughput: - Unfused: 32,903 total tok/s, median TPOT 52.29 ms. - FHMoE: 29,330 total tok/s, median TPOT 59.05 ms. - Delta: -10.86% throughput, +12.93% median TPOT. FHMoE is therefore not recommended for DP C256 without additional optimization. Full methodology and results are recorded in `benchmark/fhmoe/VALIDATION.md`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (`isort`, `ruff`, `black-jupyter`). - [x] Add focused unit and GPU tests. - [x] Add reproducible validation documentation. - [x] Provide full accuracy and serving-speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix: avoid EOS token exposure by reordering length check
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Fix EOS token exposure caused by max-length check ordering In the current implementation, the **max-length check** is performed before the **EOS token match check**. This leads to a corner case where the EOS token is generated as the final token exactly when the maximum length is reached. In this scenario, the request hits the length check first and its finish reason is incorrectly set to `"length"` instead of `"matched_token"`. As a result, the EOS token is not trimmed by `trim_matched_stop` and is unexpectedly streamed to the caller.

signal.title: ROCm: Fix AITER attention for Qwen3-Coder-Next hybrid models
signal.text: ## Goal - Fix v_head_dim init for hybrid models (layer0 can be GDN, not full attention). - Add probe-based CK batch_prefill support detection and triton extend fallback for head_dim>128. - Guard CUDA-only CUTLASS/CuTe-DSL imports and keep ROCm on triton causal_conv1d. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Qwen3-Coder-Next is a hybrid model (GDN + attention). On ROCm with AITER attention backend enabled, we hit runtime issues because: 1. `v_head_dim` was inferred from `token_to_kv_pool.get_value_buffer(0)` which can point to a non-attention layer buffer when layer0 is GDN. 2. CK `mha_batch_prefill` availability for `head_dim > 128` depends on the local AITER build. When unsupported, prefill can fail (or be unstable). 3. `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` imported CUDA-only CUTLASS/CuTe-DSL bits unconditionally in the non-CPU path, which breaks ROCm imports. This PR makes Qwen3-Coder-Next runnable and benchmarkable across both `--attention-backend triton` and `--attention-backend aiter` on ROCm. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` - Fix `v_head_dim` initialization by using `model_config.v_head_dim` instead of `token_to_kv_pool.get_value_buffer(0)`. - Add a small probe at backend init to detect whether CK batch-prefill supports the current head shape (non-MLA, `head_dim > 128`). - If probe fails, fall back to triton `extend_attention_fwd` in `forward_extend`. - Skip the probe when `skip_prefill=True` (decode-only backends like speculative draft backends). - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` - Guard CUDA-only `cutedsl_gdn` import behind `is_cuda()`. - On ROCm/HIP, keep using the triton `causal_conv1d_triton` implementation (do not import/override with CUDA-only implementations). - Only enable CuTe-DSL GDN decode when running on CUDA. ## Accuracy Tests ### GSM8K on Qwen3-Coder-Next (TP=8) Rerun: 2026-02-11 (GSM8K test set has 1319 questions; `--num-questions 2000` runs all of them) - Triton attention backend: - Accuracy: **0.947** - Invalid: **0.000** - Latency: **33.062 s** - Output throughput: **5198.031 tok/s** - AITER attention backend: - Accuracy: **0.947** - Invalid: **0.000** - Latency: **32.303 s** - Output throughput: **5264.421 tok/s** Summary: | Backend | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency | Output tok/s | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | triton | 0.947 | 0.000 | 33.062 s | 5198.031 | | aiter | 0.947 | 0.000 | 32.303 s | 5264.421 | Commands: ```bash # Triton MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-Coder-Next SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 PYTHONPATH=python python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --num-questions 2000 --parallel 512 --port 30000 --backend srt # AITER SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend aiter \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 PYTHONPATH=python python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --num-questions 2000 --parallel 512 --port 30000 --backend srt ``` ## signal.title: perf(nsa-indexer): stabilize ragged MQA chunk shapes for DeepGEMM
signal.text: # Motivation On long-context NSA prefill with ragged batches, chunked MQA logits can produce highly dynamic `M` sizes. This can trigger repeated DeepGEMM JIT recompilation and unstable latency. The goal is to stabilize chunk shapes while preserving correctness. # Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa/nsa_indexer.py` - Add `_MQA_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS = 1024` to bound chunk-row variants. - Compute chunk rows using bucketized power-of-two sizing from free memory, then cap by `_MQA_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS`. - For ultra-long KV (`k_offset >= 65536`), further cap chunk rows to `256`. - In chunk loop, pad tail chunk to fixed `max_rows` (`q`, `weights`, `ks`, `ke`) before `fp8_mqa_logits`, then slice logits back to valid rows. - This keeps kernel input shapes more stable and reduces JIT churn. # Testing - Verified code path and tensor-shape handling logic locally. # Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

signal.title: fix(nsa): align max_context_len with req_to_token width
signal.text: # Motivation In NSA backend initialization, `max_context_len` was derived from `model_config.context_len`. However, CUDA-graph page table usage depends on `req_to_token` actual width, which may include speculative headroom beyond configured `context_len`. This mismatch can cause shape/alignment issues in NSA paths. # Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa_backend.py` - Replace `self.max_context_len = model_runner.model_config.context_len` - With `self.max_context_len = self.req_to_token.shape[1]` - Add comments explaining alignment with `req_to_token` width. # Testing - Verified initialization logic and references locally. # Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

signal.text: Introducing a request‑ID metadata field, allowing all MoE distribution records belonging to the same request to be grouped cleanly. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Right now, MoE distribution logs in SGLang capture expert routing information, but they lack a stable identifier that links recorded distributions back to the originating request. ``` ## Root Cause In the function call detector, when the function name and arguments appear together in the first streaming chunk, the `else` condition causes the argument processing logic to be skipped. This results in returning an empty arguments object `{}` instead of the actual parameters. The problematic code flow: 1. First chunk contains both function name and arguments 2. Code enters the "new function call" branch and creates a tool call with empty arguments 3. The `else` block that processes arguments is never reached 4. signal.title: [NPU] allgather after qlora for dsv3.2
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In DeepSeek-V3.2, due to the large hidden dimension of the model, performing all-gather on hidden_states before attention introduces a high-dimensional communication operation. The scale of this communication is proportional to hidden_dim × token_num, which can quickly amplify in multi-card TP scenarios, making communication rather than computation the primary performance bottleneck in the attention stage. ## Modifications allgather_after_q_lora addresses this by removing the pre-attention all-gather of hidden_states and moving the communication before the indexer. It performs all-gather only on low-dimensional tensors such as q_lora, k, and weights just before indexer execution. This reduces high-dimensional communication overhead while maintaining equivalence. signal.title: [Speculative] Add heterogeneous vocabulary support for standalone speculative decoding
signal.text: Enable draft models with different vocabularies in speculative decoding. Implements ICML 2025 paper "Lossless Speculative Decoding for Heterogeneous Vocabularies". ## Motivation Currently, SGLang's speculative decoding requires the draft model and target model to share the same vocabulary. This limits users to using only matched model pairs (e.g., LLaMA draft for LLaMA target). This PR implements the TLI (Token-Level Intersection) algorithm from the ICML 2025 Oral paper ["Lossless Speculative Decoding for Heterogeneous Vocabularies"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05202) to remove this constraint. **Algorithm:** 1. Compute vocabulary intersection between draft and target tokenizers 2. Mask draft logits to restrict sampling to intersection tokens 3. Map draft token IDs to target vocab space during verification ## Modifications - **New file**: `python/sglang/srt/speculative/vocab_intersection.py` - `VocabIntersectionMapper` class for vocabulary intersection management - `create_vocab_mapper()` factory function - **Modified files**: - `server_args.py`: Add `--enable-heterogeneous-vocab` flag - `standalone_worker.py`: Initialize vocab mapper when enabled - `eagle_worker.py`: Apply logits masking in draft forward - `eagle_info.py`: Map draft tokens to target vocab in verification - `multi_layer_eagle_worker.py`: Add vocab_mapper attribute for consistency **Usage:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --speculative-algorithm STANDALONE \ --speculative-draft-model-path Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B \ --enable-heterogeneous-vocab ``` ## Accuracy Tests N/A - This is a compatibility feature. The TLI algorithm is mathematically lossless (output distribution identical to target model). Feature is opt-in and does not affect existing behavior when disabled. ## Benchmarking and Profiling N/A - This enables new use cases (heterogeneous vocab pairs) rather than optimizing existing ones. Performance depends on vocabulary intersection size between chosen model pairs. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## References - Paper: [Lossless Speculative Decoding for Heterogeneous Vocabularies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05202) (ICML 2025 Oral) - HuggingFace: [Universal Assisted Generation](https://huggingface.co/blog/universal_assisted_generation) (Transformers 4.50.0)

signal.title: [smg] Fix Content-Type header for models and server info endpoints (#8887)
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a recurring issue where the router returns `Content-Type: text/plain` for JSON endpoints like `/v1/models`. This causes failures in strict clients, most notably Open WebUI, which fails to parse the model list if the media type is incorrect. See Open WebUI logs below: ``` 2026-01-20 07:39:02.077 | ERROR | open_webui.routers.openai:send_get_request:86 - Connection error: 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: text/plain; charset=utf-8', url='http://10.0.0.136:8000/v1/models' 2026-01-20 07:39:02.077 | INFO | uvicorn.protocols.http.httptools_impl:send:483 - 172.17.0.1:39010 - "GET /api/models HTTP/1.1" 200 ``` Previously, in #9236, the Gateway relied on faithfully forwarding headers from upstream workers to maintain transparency. However, this trust-based approach is insufficient because it cannot guarantee API compliance when upstream behaviors vary. Since the Gateway explicitly defines these API endpoints (`/v1/models`, `/get_model_info`), it bears the ultimate responsibility for enforcing the API specification. Fixes #8887. Related to #3307 #6237 ## Modifications - **New Middleware**: Implemented `ensure_json_content_type` in `sgl-model-gateway/src/middleware.rs`. This middleware checks if a response is successful and forces the `Content-Type` header to `application/json`. - **Router Update**: Applied this middleware in `sgl-model-gateway/src/server.rs` to the following endpoints: - `/v1/models` - `/get_model_info` - `/get_server_info` - **Testing**: - Updated the file `sgl-model-gateway/tests/api/api_endpoints_test.rs`: 1. Added a regression test `test_pd_mode_content_type` to verify that these endpoints correctly return `application/json` headers. 2. Added `test_error_content_type_on_model_and_server_info_endpoints` to verify that error responses from these endpoints also return `application/json`. 3. Updated existing tests for `/v1/models`, `/get_model_info`, and `/get_server_info` to explicitly verify the `Content-Type` header is correct. - Brought the system up and tested the responses with `curl`: 1. Launch the prefill worker: ```bash uv run python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --port 8001 --host 0.0.0.0 ``` 2. Launch the decode worker: ```bash uv run python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --port 8002 --host 0.0.0.0 ``` 4. Launch the router: ```bash uv run python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://localhost:8001 \ --decode http://localhost:8002 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 ``` 5. Verify the Content-Type for the endpoints: ```bash ❯ curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models | grep -i "^Content-Type:" content-type: application/json ❯ curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8000/get_model_info | grep -i "^Content-Type:" content-type: application/json ❯ curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8000/get_server_info | grep -i "^Content-Type:" content-type: application/json ``` 6. Open WebUI correctly identifies the model: ## Accuracy Tests N/A - This change only affects HTTP response metadata (headers) and does not impact model outputs or inference logic. ## Benchmarking and Profiling N/A - The middleware introduces negligible overhead (header insertion) and does not affect the inference critical path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: fix: normalize module_name in get_hidden_dim fallback
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR makes **LoRA initialization work for Qwen models** (e.g. Qwen2.5 / Qwen3) in the fallback path of `sglang.srt.lora.utils.get_hidden_dim()` when the HF model does **not** implement `base_model.get_hidden_dim()`. Before this change, the fallback only accepted SGLang internal stacked module names (e.g. `qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`) and raised `NotImplementedError` for common HF-style module names like `q_proj/k_proj/v_proj` (including dotted names such as `layers.0.self_attn.q_proj`). This prevented LoRA init for Qwen when `lora_target_modules` used HF-style names. ## Modifications - In `python/sglang/srt/lora/utils.py:get_hidden_dim()` (fallback branch only), normalize `module_name` via the existing `get_normalized_target_modules()` mapping before applying the default dimension logic. - Preserve the original user-provided name (`orig_module_name`) only for the error message, so `NotImplementedError` still reports the pre-normalization module name (useful for dotted module names). - No behavior change for models that already implement `base_model.get_hidden_dim()` (fast-path). ## Benchmarking and Profiling N/A (this change affects LoRA init fallback logic, not inference hotpath). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1.
