signal.title: [diffusion] fix: stop reserving NCCL device buffers for single-rank groups
signal.text: ## Motivation On a single GPU, ~5 GiB of VRAM is gone before a single weight is loaded. On a 12 GiB consumer card that is 44% of the device, and it makes VAE decode fail at any resolution. The cause is that a single-GPU run still builds every parallel group — DP, CFG, TP, SP, PP, VAE_DECODE, DIT, VAE, ulysses, ring — each with one rank, and each got an NCCL-backed process group. NCCL sizes its per-channel device buffers when the communicator is created, so every one of those groups reserved ~390 MiB (the first, the world group, ~470 MiB). None of that memory can ever be used. Every collective in `GroupCoordinator` returns early on `world_size == 1` ("Bypass the function if we are using only 1 GPU"), and the device communicator is only constructed when `world_size > 1`. `pynccl` already skips communicator creation for single-rank groups; the underlying `torch.distributed.new_group` did not. Measured on an RTX 3060 12 GiB with a bare `torch.distributed` repro: | | device memory | |---|---| | CUDA context only | 114 MiB | | + world group | 584 MiB | | each additional `new_group([0])` | **+388 MiB** | `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` drops the per-group cost to 10 MiB, which confirms these are per-channel buffers for channels a one-rank communicator can never use. ## Modifications Add `new_device_group()` in `group_coordinator.py`, which gives single-rank groups the gloo backend and leaves multi-rank groups on the requested backend. Route the nine device-group creation sites through it: `GroupCoordinator.__init__`, the `PipelineGroupCoordinator` single-rank branch and its `skip_device_group`, `_DIT` and `_VAE` in `parallel_state.py`, and the four ulysses/ring groups in `parallel_groups.py`. The two-rank `device_group_0_1` / `device_group_1_0` pipeline pair is left alone; it is only reached when the group has exactly two ranks. One consumer needed a matching guard. cache-dit averages its residual-difference statistics across the TP x SP slice using the DIT group, and that all-reduce had no world-size check, so on a single GPU it would now stage device tensors through the host on every cached block of every step. Averaging over one rank returns the input, so the patched `similarity` returns the local value instead of running the collective. Every other consumer of these groups already short-circuits: collectives in `GroupCoordinator` return early on `world_size == 1`, the device communicator is built only above 1, the ulysses/ring groups are reached only under `sp_size > 1` in `attention/layer.py` and behind `world_size <= 1` early returns in `usp.py`, and the VAE group has no consumer outside its getter. ## Accuracy Tests Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234. | | free VRAM after load | peak VRAM | VAE decode | output SHA-256 | |---|---|---|---|---| | before | 6.51 GiB | 11552 MiB | **OOM** | no output produced | | `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` control | 11.31 GiB | 6886 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` | | this PR | 11.06 GiB | 6830 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` | Two-GPU regression on the same box, `--num-gpus 2`: patched and unpatched produce the same output, SHA-256 `361bb915…`, so the multi-rank path is unaffected. New unit test `test_single_rank_device_group.py` covers backend selection for single-rank and multi-rank groups (3 tests, 5 subtests). Existing `test_cache_dit_integration.py` passes with the guard (12 tests together). CI note: `multimodal-gen-test-1-npu-a3` is red here, but every diffusion testcase on that runner is red on unrelated branches too (see #35511, where `ernie_image_t2i_1npu`, `flux_image_t2i_npu`, `flux_2_klein_4b_t2i_1npu`, `z_image_t2i_1npu` and `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_1_npu` all fail and the job ends with `Executing the custom container implementation failed`). signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix full prefill CUDA graph padding and EAGLE capture
signal.text: ## Motivation Full prefill CUDA graphs replay fixed token buckets that may be larger than the live batch. Models that mask padded hidden states need the live `num_token_non_padded` boundary even when attention tensors are not gathered. Without it, padded rows can propagate through the captured graph. EAGLE target prefill also consumes the full target hidden-state sequence. FullCG previously captured the configured return-hidden-state mode, which could be insufficient and force target prefill back to eager execution. ## Modifications - Register and populate `num_token_non_padded` for FullCG, including non-gathered execution. - Capture `FULL` hidden states for EAGLE target prefill under FullCG while retaining `LAST` for breakable draft workers. - Keep the EAGLE eager fallback specific to `tc_piecewise`, whose fixed capture ceiling can remain below `FULL`. - Add focused regression tests for the non-gathered token boundary and FullCG EAGLE admission. ## Accuracy Tests No model math or kernels are changed. - 42 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The changes update CUDA graph metadata and capture mode; they do not add work to attention or model kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add focused regression tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this graph-correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32317528205](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317528205)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32317528065](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317528065)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
signal.text: ## Motivation A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output. #34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`, and scoped itself explicitly: > Only the prefill donation depth changes here. Decode tracking keeps its own `--mamba-track-interval` grid. That decode grid does not land on the tree page. `--mamba-track-interval` has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page — and is never resolved anywhere (`grep` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty). Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant. The insert-time guard that would have caught this was deferred to #34760 and #34780 — **both closed, never merged** — and there is no mamba depth check on the insert in `main` today, so the misalignment stays silent. **Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`. | page | dcp | tree page | interval | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok | | 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** | | 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken | | 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken | Two shipped recipes are on the broken row today, both in `test_kimi_k3_b300.py`: `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) and `TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` (`--dcp-size 8` + DSPARK — spec is only rejected under DCP *with* HiCache, so the mamba grid is live there too). Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries. Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this. ## Modifications `mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well: ```python def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int: return math.lcm( mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval ) ``` Read where a checkpoint depth is picked: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed. The tree page is a process constant, so each site only needs a live handle to the tree. `prepare_for_decode` and the spec paths take it off the batch, as the extend path already does. The batch-result processor takes it off **its own** `tree_cache`: the batch it is handed is the result-queue `copy()`, whose field list is scoped to what `process_batch_result` needs and does not carry one. Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there. Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask and Inkling's `sconv` (which holds only a `ForwardBatch`). `lcm` makes the derived grid a multiple of the raw interval, so every snapshot step is still a flush step and the flush mask's invariant survives. Note the comment at `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:403` says the two "fire on the same steps"; after this change they fire on nested sets of steps. `test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py` is a pre-existing test (#33477) whose hand-built `ScheduleBatch` and processor double now need a `tree_cache`, since `prepare_for_decode` did not read one before this change. Same edit #34808 made to its own double. Page and chunk are set to the interval already under test, so the derived grid stays 4 and every existing boundary expectation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests **Not yet measured — this is why the PR is a draft.** #34808 shipped a cold-vs-warm teacher-forced logprob comparison on a live Kimi-Linear dcp8 server for the prefill half; the decode half deserves the same evidence, and this PR currently argues from page alignment alone. An 8×B300 run on the `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` recipe, before and after, is the next step. What is verified statically: - **Cache reuse is unchanged.** The insert floors the donated depth to the tree page, so the node it lands on is `floor(min(N, floor(N/grid)·grid) / 512) · 512` — which collapses to the same `512q` under both grids (checked for every request length in [0, 4096): zero differ). Same number of cached checkpoints, same node depths, same KV prefix. What changes is *which state* is attached: previously a state that had already consumed 256 more tokens than the node it hung on. Snapshot writes into the ping-pong buffer halve on the affected recipes — less decode work, not fewer cache entries. - **Grid unchanged everywhere else:** page 64 × dcp 4, page 32 × dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config. New CPU unit case in `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`, beside #34808's extend cases since it is the same invariant from the other end. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32304189342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189342)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32304189109](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189109)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Forward unknown InternLM tools when configured
signal.text: ## Motivation `InternlmDetector` checks `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS` before deciding whether to keep an unknown tool call, but the forwarding path still indexes `tool_indices[name]`. When forwarding is enabled, an unknown name therefore raises `KeyError`; the outer error handler then returns the original tagged payload as normal text and drops the call. The same failure affects one-shot and streaming parsing. ## Modifications - Use the established `-1` tool index for opted-in unknown InternLM tool calls, matching `BaseFormatDetector.parse_base_json`. - Add CPU regressions for both one-shot and streaming parsing. The existing default behavior that drops unknown tools remains covered and unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects function-call parsing when unknown-tool forwarding is explicitly enabled. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change replaces a dictionary index with `dict.get` in an existing parsing branch. ## Tests - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/function_call`: 466 passed, 14 subtests passed - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/function_call/test_unknown_tool_name.py`: 4 passed - `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Documentation is not needed for this internal correctness fix. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32318962930](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318962930)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32318962795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318962795)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sampling] Fix int32 offset overflow in top-k renorm Triton kernels
signal.text: ## Motivation The top-k renorm Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` compute flattened element offsets as `row * vocab_size + offsets` and `program_id * BLOCK_SIZE + arange(...)`. Both products are computed in int32, so for large `batch x vocab_size` tensors the offsets can silently overflow, corrupting loads/stores. ## Modifications Cast the row / program id to `tl.int64` before the multiplication in `_mask_and_partial_sum_kernel` and `_normalize_kernel`, so offset arithmetic is done in 64-bit. ## Checklist - Ran `pre-commit` on the changed file (passed). - Verified on an internal setup exercising the top-k renorm path. ## Original commits - `49831150a` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32306179456](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32306179456)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32306179103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32306179103)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kernel] Support wider rows in mega_moe_pre_dispatch
signal.text: ## Motivation `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` assigns one thread to each 8-element input chunk, so a single CUDA block can only cover hidden dimensions up to 8192. Wider shapes are rejected before launch. ## Modifications - Cap the block size at the CUDA 1024-thread limit and process wider rows in strided chunks. - Recompute quantization-group indices for each chunk while preserving the UE8M0 scale layout. - Keep a separate single-chunk kernel specialization so existing shapes retain the same instruction path. - Reject wide shapes whose tail would split a warp-level reduction. ## Accuracy Tests - Verified bitwise FP8 output and UE8M0 scale bytes against a reference implementation for hidden dimensions 3584, 5632, 8192, 12288, and 16384. - Verified exact top-k copies and idle-slot padding. - Verified that hidden dimension 8320 fails with the expected full-warp alignment error. - JIT-compiled the ported CUDA header successfully. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - The single-chunk specialization produces the same SASS instruction stream as the previous kernel. - CUDA-event microbenchmarks showed no measurable regression for shapes that already fit in one chunk. ## Original commits - `d7c54c96f5` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). signal.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.15 (gfx942 / gfx950) stages to the ROCm Dockerfile
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.15 publishes no `rocm/pytorch` base image, so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing ROCm 7.0 / 7.2 stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.15 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The SDK pin is a nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release: the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0. This specific build is the one the gfx1250 7.15 image also pins, so all three arches share a single 7.15 SDK. Note for sequencing with #32754 (`[AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support`): that PR adds its own copy of a 7.15 pip-SDK stage, which could instead reuse the shared `rocm715-base` stage introduced here. Both PRs also introduce the same `rocm_legacy` / `rocm_rock` extras in `python/pyproject_other.toml`. Whichever lands second will need to be reconciled against the first. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm715-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.15 pip stack — `rocm[libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950]==7.15.0a20260712`, `torch==2.11.0`, `torchvision==0.26.0`, `triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6`, from the ROCm nightlies and devreleases indexes. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15`, which only set build flags (`BUILD_VLLM`, `BUILD_TRITON`, `BUILD_LLVM`, `BUILD_AITER_ALL`, `BUILD_MOONCAKE`, `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`). Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skip the apt install for `*rocm7_15*`, since libdrm ships with the pip SDK. - amdsmi: install it for `*rocm7_15*` (same branch as 7.2), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm 7.x images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: remove `libabsl-dev` before configuring, because nixl's meson wants an abseil providing `absl_log` and refuses its bundled subproject while Ubuntu 24.04's older `libabsl-dev` (20220623) is visible. Only `-dev` packages are removed; `libabsl20220623t64` stays so the Mooncake binaries built earlier keep the shared library they linked against. - Second commit: removing `libabsl-dev` also removes `libgrpc-dev` and `libgrpc++-dev`, which depend on it, so all three are reinstalled once nixl is built. The image's own MORI is built before this point and is fine, but the CI install script rebuilds MORI inside the image, and without `libgrpc++-dev` that rebuild configures without gRPC and silently drops symbols the Python side imports — `mori.umbp` then fails on `CacheRemoteAdmission` and `test_umbp_store` errors out. - The SGLang install now selects a `compressed-tensors` extra: `rocm_rock` for `*rocm7_15*`, `rocm_legacy` otherwise. ### `python/pyproject_other.toml` - Moved `compressed-tensors` out of `srt_hip` into two new mutually exclusive extras, `rocm_legacy = ["compressed-tensors==0.15.0"]` and `rocm_rock = ["compressed-tensors==0.16.0"]`. 0.15.0 requires `torch<2.11` and 0.16.0 requires `torch>=2.10`, so the correct pin depends on which torch the ROCm SDK generation ships rather than on the platform. Pinning the wrong one leaves pip trying to replace the image's ROCm torch with a PyPI build, which it cannot do, and the resolve then fails. Neither extra is pulled automatically — the Dockerfile and the CI install script append one. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Detect the ROCm version inside the CI container and append the matching `compressed-tensors` extra (`rocm_rock` for >= 7.15.0, else `rocm_legacy`) to `EXTRAS`. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. - Keep ROCm 7.15's own Triton (`INSTALL_AITER_TRITON=false` for HIP `7.15*`, matching `BUILD_TRITON=0` on the new stages). AITER's `install_triton.sh` resolves its wheel index from `dpkg -l rocm-core`, which does not exist for a pip-installed SDK, so it would fall back to the ROCm 7.2 index and drop a 7.2-built Triton into a 7.15 image. Verified in the built image that `dpkg-query` finds no `rocm-core` and that `torch.version.hip` reports `7.15.0`. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm7_15-nightly.yml` - Added `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15` to the build matrix, and replaced the single-arch `if` with a `case` mapping them to the `rocm7.15-mi30x` and `rocm7.15-mi35x` tags. - Build args: dropped `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` and `SGLANG_VERSION`, neither of which this Dockerfile consumes, and pass `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, which is what the SGLang install actually reads. ## Accuracy Tests All of the following was run on an MI300X host (gfx942). - `gfx942-rocm7_15` builds end to end (46GB image). - In-image smoke test: torch `2.11.0+rocm7.15.0a20260712`, `torch.version.hip` `7.15.0`, `gcnArchName` `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, a bf16 matmul on device returns finite values, and `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi` and `sglang` all import. - The real CI flow was run against the image: `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0, and `test/run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **6/8 passed**. That matches a ROCm 10 image baseline run on the same host on 2026-08-17, which was also 6/8. The two failures are `test_basic_sanity.py` and `test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`, both `huggingface_hub.errors.GatedRepoError: 401` on `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` because this host has no `HF_TOKEN` — identical to the baseline and unrelated to this change. - Known gap: the `gfx950-rocm7_15` stage has **not** been built or run. It shares `rocm715-base` with gfx942 and differs only in the AITER / sgl-kernel compile targets, but it is unverified. The host is MI300X, so gfx950 runtime tests were not possible here. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32132588829](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132588829)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32132588628](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132588628)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse compress+norm+rope, emit bpreshuffle scale natively, keep kv_score in bf16
signal.text: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4 decode a good part of each attention layer goes to kernels that only move or re-lay-out data rather than compute anything. Three of them run on every layer of every step: 1. On CSA layers (`compress_ratio` 4) compress, norm and rope are three separate launches. Each is 4-8 us, which is small enough that dispatch rather than the work sets the cost. 2. The fp8 quant path writes its scale tensor in one layout and then a second kernel transposes it into the layout the bpreshuffle GEMM actually wants — 152 extra launches per decode step. 3. The compressor takes fp32, so the bf16 `wkv_gate` output is widened by a separate elementwise copy before it can be consumed — 92 extra launches per decode step. None of these carry information the surrounding kernels don't already have, so each can be folded into its neighbour without changing the math. ## Modifications Three independent optimisations, each behind its own env gate. **`SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE`** — new `fused_compress4_norm_rope.cuh` folds compress, norm and rope into a single kernel for CSA layers. The fused kernel maps one token per 64-lane wavefront rather than two; that takes it from 85 to 47 VGPRs and lifts occupancy from 5 to 8 waves/SIMD, which is what makes the fused kernel actually cheaper than the three it replaces instead of merely equal to them. **`SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE`** — the quant kernel writes the scale tensor directly in the physical layout bpreshuffle wants (column-major in M), so the separate transpose pass is not needed. **`SGLANG_OPT_KV_SCORE_BF16`** — `c4_v2.cuh` and `c128_v2.cuh` gain a `SrcFloat` template parameter, kept separate from the compute dtype so `score_bias` stays fp32. The compressor then widens the `wkv_gate` output as it loads it and the fp32 copy in front of compress is never materialised. `compress_forward()` only widens on the XPU path, and `compressor.py` calls `linear_kv_score` where it previously called `linear_bf16_fp32`. **On the defaults.** All three gates default to on. They are separable on purpose — each can be turned off on its own with `=0` if it regresses a shape I did not measure — but the numbers below are all with the three together, which is the configuration the defaults select. Happy to ship any or all of them off by default instead if maintainers would rather see soak time first. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, on the environment below. | Run | Gates | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---|---| | Baseline | all off | 94.7% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 1 | all on | 94.5% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 2 | all on | 94.8% | 0.001 | Baseline and patched are the same build on the same image, gates flipped by env var only. The patched arm was run twice because temperature 0 is not bit-deterministic here — batching order moves with arrival timing — so a single number cannot separate a real accuracy change from run-to-run noise. The two patched passes differ from each other by 0.3 points and bracket the baseline, which is the most that can be claimed: no accuracy change is visible above run-to-run noise at this sample size. ```bash MODEL= FUSE=1 NATIVE_SCALE=1 KVBF16=1 \ NUM_QUESTIONS=1319 NUM_SHOTS=5 MAX_NEW_TOKENS=512 PARALLEL=1200 \ bash bench/gsm8k_item4_517.sh # FUSE=0 NATIVE_SCALE=0 KVBF16=0 for baseline ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) | | ROCm | 7.2.0 | | Image | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260812` | | Model | DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers | | Shape | 8k in / 1k out, `--random-range-ratio 1.0` | Server: ```bash sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL" --port "$PORT" \ --tensor-parallel-size $TP $DP_ARGS \ --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs "$CONC" --max-running-requests "$CONC" \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --page-size 256 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --context-length 16384 \ --chunked-prefill-size $((ISL * TP)) \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion --watchdog-timeout 1800 # DP_ARGS for the conc-64 shape: # --dp $TP --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --enable-two-batch-overlap ``` Client: ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --model "$MODEL" \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --max-concurrency "$CONC" ``` ### Throughput Each shape is measured A B B A and the pairs averaged, so drift over the sweep cancels instead of being charged to whichever arm happened to run second. | Shape | Baseline (tok/s) | Patched (tok/s) | Gain | |---|---|---|---| | conc 4, TP4 | 174.23, 174.85 -> 174.54 | 180.96, 179.99 -> 180.48 | **+3.40%** | | conc 8, TP4 | 302.63, 302.48 -> 302.56 | 314.70, 314.41 -> 314.56 | **+3.97%** | | conc 64, TP8 + DP8 | 1600.37, 1593.98 -> 1597.17 | 1645.41, 1643.07 -> 1644.24 | **+2.95%** | Within-arm spread is 0.05-0.40% on baseline and 0.09-0.54% on patched, comfortably under the gap between arms, so the gain is not sweep-order drift. ### Profile Decode window, 8k1k conc 64 TP8 + DP8, per layer on rank TP-0: | Per layer | Baseline | Patched | |---|---|---| | CSA kernels | 55 | **48** | | HCA kernels | 43 | **40** | | Elementwise, CSA / HCA | 8x / 6x | **3x / 3x** | | bf16->fp32 copy, CSA / HCA | 2x / 1x | **0x / 0x** | The widening copy that fed compress is gone from both layer types, and the 48 / 40 counts hold on all seven ranks that captured a full decode window. The compress kernels take bf16 directly — the fourth template argument is the source dtype: - CSA `flash_c4_decode_norm_rope<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, 0, false, true>` - HCA `flash_c128_decode<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, false>` The three elementwise launches left per layer are two same-dtype `direct_copy` (bf16->bf16, fp32->fp32) and one bf16 residual add. None is a dtype conversion and none sits in front of compress. One caveat worth stating: CSA layer time drops 6.1% while HCA is flat at -0.07% even though HCA also loses three kernels. A single five-step profiler window carries a few us of per-layer drift, which is the same order as the effect being measured, so the throughput sweep above rather than this table is the measurement of record. ### Unit tests ```bash python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c128_v2.py -q # 110 passed ``` `test_c4_v2.py` and `test_c128_v2.py` are parametrised over a new bf16 source dtype: 55 of the 110 are those new cases. The `SrcFloat` path had no coverage before, and the bf16 arm was confirmed to actually reach the new specialisation (the dispatcher was observed compiling with `dtype_src=torch.bfloat16`) rather than being quietly widened somewhere above the kernel. All four compress specialisations (c4/c128 x fp32/bf16 source) were also checked to compile. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) — no user-facing surface changed; the three gates are internal env switches. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32318336713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318336713) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32318336467](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32318336467)

signal.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signal.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix: abort handling for dispatched requests after client disconnect
signal.text: ## Summary This PR fixes an issue where a request could continue decoding after the client disconnected, wasting GPU resources and repeatedly logging: ```text Received output for rid=... but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager. ``` ## Root Cause When a request handler was cancelled after dispatch, TokenizerManager removed its `rid_to_state` entry immediately. The disconnect abort path checks this state before sending an AbortReq, so the abort was skipped while the request continued running in the scheduler. A related race also existed for chunked-prefill requests: if a request moved out of the chunked-prefill slot before its deferred abort was processed, the abort could be lost. ## Changes - Track whether each request has been dispatched to the scheduler. - Remove undelivered request states locally on handler failure. - Abort dispatched requests and retain their state until scheduler cleanup completes. - Deduplicate abort requests and abort metrics. - Preserve retry behavior when abort dispatch fails. - Track generated request IDs used by parallel sampling. - Retry deferred chunked-prefill aborts after a request moves to another scheduler queue. - Add regression tests for disconnect cleanup, abort deduplication, dispatch failures, parallel sampling, and chunked-prefill transitions. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32225602246](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225602246)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32225602043](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225602043)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signal.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32317861378](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317861378)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32317861217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32317861217)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Fuse the ROCm DSA indexer q/k prep into aiter's single kernel
signal.text:
## Summary On ROCm the DSA indexer spends 11 kernels per decode layer on q/k prep. This PR collapses most of that into one aiter kernel. * `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` does k LayerNorm + RoPE + fp8 quant + paged index-k store, q RoPE + fp8 quant, and the head-gate scale in a single launch — six kernels become one. Like the CUDA fused path it drops the Hadamard rotation, which is logit-preserving and only shifts fp8 quantisation error. Prefill drops it too, since prefill writes the index-K cache decode reads back and the two must agree on basis. * `wk` and `weights_proj` are folded into one `wk_weights_proj` GEMM. This needs only the concatenated weight, no fused kernel, but was gated on CUDA; it now runs on CUDA or HIP and is numerically identical to the split projections. * The aiter kernel is tuned for decode's one-token-per-sequence shape and costs about twice what it replaces at prefill widths, so it is gated to decode. It also requires gfx95x, `SGLANG_USE_AITER`, and an aiter build exporting the symbol — a capability probe, not a preference: anything outside the envelope falls back to the existing path. CUDA and NPU are unchanged. Decode indexer on GLM-5.2 / MI355X: **11 kernels / 70.8 us per layer → 5 kernels / 41.4 us (−41.5%)**, which closes the MI355X-vs-B200 indexer gap from 2.55x to 1.49x. Drive-by fix: define the module-level `_use_dsa_indexer_fusion` that `lora_manager.py` already imports but nothing defined, so an indexer-targeted LoRA adapter raised `ImportError` instead of the intended `ValueError`. ## Test plan MI355X TP4, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, fp8 KV, `chunked_prefill=16384`, DSA backend triton, i8192 / o1024, one run per point. Baseline is the same AMD GLM-5.2 stack without this PR (#30519, #30575, #30715, #30808, #31323, #31324, #32888, plus ROCm/aiter#4453). | conc | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 323.3 → 335.9 (+3.9%) | 10.61 → 10.16 (−4.2%) | 366.7 → 367.6 (+0.2%) | | 8 | 465.3 → 482.3 (+3.6%) | 14.02 → 13.43 (−4.2%) | 379.1 → 379.8 (+0.2%) | | 16 | 731.5 → 762.9 (+4.3%) | 15.73 → 14.86 (−5.5%) | 378.0 → 383.3 (+1.4%) | | 32 | 1044.3 → 1081.1 (+3.5%) | 19.39 → 18.37 (−5.3%) | 393.7 → 389.5 (−1.1%) | | 64 | 1342.4 → 1382.2 (+3.0%) | 25.33 → 24.03 (−5.1%) | 631.6 → 615.6 (−2.5%) | ITL improves −4.2% to −5.5% at every concurrency, matching the 29.4 us/layer the kernel table predicts over the 21 layers that run the indexer (0.62 ms per decode forward). TTFT is flat, which is the check that matters given the kernel is decode-only. GSM8K (1200 questions): 0.928 baseline, 0.934 this PR. The index-K cache is bit-exact against the unfused path across both `preshuffle` and `scale_fmt`; the q fp8 payload differs by 1 ULP on 0.10% of elements, because aiter multiplies by the reciprocal rather than dividing.
Per-layer decode indexer kernels, and why the aiter kernel is decode-only | baseline | us | this PR | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (wk) | 6.59 | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (merged wk_weights_proj) | 6.50 | | `hgemm_16x64x64x6` (weights_proj) | 5.30 | — | — | | `Layernorm2dFwd` | 4.19 | `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` | 5.60 | | `kn_entry_2c_sbhd_cached_indirect` (RoPE) | 8.78 | | | | `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` | 4.43 | | | | `_hadamard_quant_kernel` | 4.55 | | | | `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_kernel` | 4.19 | | | | `triton_poi_fused_mul_unsqueeze_0` | 4.18 | | | | `wv_splitk_small` (q proj) | 5.70 | `wv_splitk_small` | 5.95 | | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.34 | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.46 | | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.60 | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.93 | | **total** | **70.8** | **total** | **41.4** | Of the 29.4 us/layer saved, 5.4 is the merged projection and 21.3 is six kernels becoming one; downstream topk and logits move by 0.1–0.3 us, which is noise. With the aiter kernel enabled for prefill too, the prefill indexer went from 1614.5 up to 1780.5 us/layer: the fused kernel alone costs 300.4 us/layer against the 162.8 of the six it replaces, and drags downstream topk and logits ~8% each. Gating it to decode gives prefill 1519.6 us/layer (−5.9%), since prefill still benefits from the merged projection and from dropping the Hadamard.

signal.title: Fix fused DeepSeek top-k capability fallback
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently selects FlashInfer's `fused_topk_deepseek` based on shape constraints without checking whether the active GPU architecture is supported by that kernel. On A10G (SM86), FlashInfer raises `BackendSupportedError` during DeepSeek grouped top-k routing instead of allowing SGLang to use its existing fallback. This was observed in the Dynamo nightly SGLang data-parallel test: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/32114902544/job/95672470424 ## Modifications - Read FlashInfer's `is_compute_capability_supported` metadata before selecting `fused_topk_deepseek`. - Preserve compatibility with FlashInfer versions that do not expose capability metadata. ## Accuracy Tests The numerical implementation is unchanged. signal.title: [Spec] Add LFM2 and LFM2-MoE DSpark speculative decoding support
signal.text: ### What Adds DSpark speculative-decoding support for the LFM2 hybrid (ShortConv + attention) family: both the dense **LFM2** and MoE **LFM2-MoE** targets. Follow-up to #30261 (DSpark), now that it has landed on `main`. Two commits: 1. **Interleaved RoPE in the fused-KV kernel** - the fused RMSNorm+RoPE materialization only handled neox rotation. Adds an `IS_NEOX` constexpr selecting the pairing (neox: `(i, i+rotary/2)`; interleaved/GPT-J: `(2i, 2i+1)`); no change for existing neox drafts. LFM2 draft exports rotate interleaved and need this. 2. **LFM2 / LFM2-MoE target support** - the draft is a DSpark checkpoint (Qwen3-style GQA backbone, markov + confidence heads) exported with interleaved RoPE. It registers as its own `Lfm2DSparkDraftModel` arch (a thin `DSparkDraftModel` subclass, mirroring `Qwen3DSparkModel`) so the LFM2 draft can gain LFM2-specific layers - e.g. ShortConv/conv1d - later without touching the shared classes. Interleaved RoPE and the confidence head come from the checkpoint config; the kernel change handles the rotation. Only the target side needs code beyond that: aux-hidden capture + ShortConv block verify/rollback in `lfm2.py`/`lfm2_moe.py`, hybrid-state commit after verify in the DSpark worker (mirrors the DFlash worker so decoding stays lossless), routing the draft KV injector through the fused-KV path, and marking the LFM2 archs eligible for the `extra_buffer` mamba radix strategy that spec-v2 rollback needs. Net: 7 files, +422/-23, no changes to existing DSpark behavior. Base LFM2-MoE serving parity (the attention-backend / radix-cache override tables for `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM`) is independent of DSpark and is in its own PR: #30780. Pair with it for the 8B target's serving defaults. ### Speedup 1xH100 80GB, bs=1, temperature 0, block size 7, accept length / speedup vs the same server minus spec flags: | dataset | LFM2.5-1.2B + 5L | LFM2.5-8B-A1B + 3L | |---|---|---| | math500 (chat math) | 4.82 / **2.10x** | 5.42 / **2.21x** | | aime (competition math) | 4.36 / 1.95x | 6.20 / **2.42x** | | humaneval (code) | 4.41 / 1.93x | - | | mbpp (code) | 4.45 / 1.95x | 4.80 / 1.96x | | gsm8k (grade-school math) | 3.73 / 1.49x | 3.51 / 1.24x | | mtbench (multi-turn chat) | 2.35 / 1.05x | 5.87 / **2.32x** | Floor is short chat on the small dense target (~1.05x); ceiling is long reasoning on the MoE (2.3-2.4x, accept near the block-7 limit). Accuracy at parity with baseline on every scoreable bench. Note: interleaved RoPE (commit 1) is not optional for these drafts. Serving them neox collapses accept length to ~1.9 vs ~5.1 interleaved. ### Public draft checkpoints - dense: https://huggingface.co/tugot17/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-DSpark-5L (target `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct`) - MoE: https://huggingface.co/tugot17/LFM2.5-8B-A1B-DSpark-3L (target `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-8B-A1B`) ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path tugot17/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-DSpark-5L \ --speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer ``` ### Testing Validated in serving on 1xH100 across the benches above (dense + MoE, draft depths 2L/3L/5L). The MoE ShortConv decode uses the same CUDA `causal_conv1d_update` kernel as dense (an earlier triton swap was removed after confirming identical accept, 5.936 both ways). Happy to add a gated CI test under `test/registered/spec/dspark/` against the public checkpoints. Supersedes #30776, which was opened against the DSpark PR branch before it merged; rebased onto `main`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32244567354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244567354)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32244567092](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244567092)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [model-gateway] Add opt-in `fips` feature using the AWS-LC FIPS module
signal.text: ## Motivation Some deployments (government and other regulated environments) require all cryptography to come from a FIPS 140-3 validated module. This PR adds an opt-in `fips` cargo feature to sgl-model-gateway so those users can build a compliant gateway. Default builds are not affected. ## Modifications Behind the new `fips` feature (off by default): - rustls uses the AWS-LC FIPS provider instead of ring for all TLS (HTTPS server and the reqwest/kube outbound clients; tonic is built without TLS features and does no TLS itself). - JWT verification uses the jsonwebtoken AWS-LC backend. - The wasm module SHA-256 hash uses AWS-LC. - `aws-lc-fips-sys` uses a normal caret requirement (`0.14`) so builds pick up the latest AWS-LC FIPS release (currently 0.14.1, bundling AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0). AWS-LC FIPS is a CMVP-validated module lineage (see [certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) for the 3.x static module). The exact module version in any given build can be read from the binary with `strings <binary> | grep "AWS-LC FIPS"`. Deployments that need a version literally listed on an issued certificate can pin, for example `=0.13.11` (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, the exact version on #5314). - At startup the gateway asserts the installed rustls provider is FIPS and that the AWS-LC JWT provider was installed. If not, it fails to start. - The Python and Go bindings expose the same `fips` feature. Changes that apply to all builds: - New `src/crypto.rs` with `ensure_crypto_provider_installed()`, which replaces the two previous ad-hoc `ring::default_provider().install_default()` call sites, and a `Sha256Hasher` wrapper used for wasm module hashing. Default builds keep ring and RustCrypto sha2. - `jsonwebtoken` upgraded 9.3 to 10.4 and `smg-auth` 1.0.0 to 1.2.2. jsonwebtoken 9 was hardwired to ring; version 10 has pluggable backends. Default builds use its `rust_crypto` backend. Not changed: blake3/xxhash (used for cache-aware routing and consistent hashing, not security relevant) and the openssl dependency (test cert generation and the optional `vendored-openssl` feature only). Build note: `--features fips` (and therefore `--all-features`, used by `make lint` and the rust CI lint job) needs cmake and Go to compile AWS-LC. The CI lint job passes since GitHub runners include both. <details> <summary>FIPS verification evidence</summary> - The fips binary embeds the AWS-LC FIPS module version string (checked with `strings`, currently `AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0`); the default binary does not. - The fips binary starts cleanly and serves `/liveness` and `/health`. - TLS handshake against the fips build negotiates TLS 1.3 `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Forcing `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (not FIPS approved) fails against the fips build and succeeds against the default build, showing the provider swap is active. - Known residual: ring and the jsonwebtoken RustCrypto backend remain linked (cargo features are additive) but are never selected at runtime, which the startup assertions enforce. smg-auth internally uses RustCrypto sha2 for API key fingerprinting; that code only runs when control plane API keys are configured. </details> ## Accuracy Tests N/A, no model or inference code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A, default builds keep the same crypto stack. The fips path only affects opt-in builds. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32316595584](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316595584)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316595103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316595103)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Multihardware Plugin] Introduce SRTPlatform.build_kv_pool request seam; flatten platform class hooks to Optional
signal.text: ## Motivation This is the KV-management redesign promised on #29445 ("this PR has been sitting as we are considering how we manage this layer for KV... next revision may look different"). The existing platform seam for KV pools — `get_{mha,mla,dsa}_kv_pool_cls()` returning a class that the call site instantiates — has three structural defects that have already produced real bugs: 1. **Ctor kwargs leak into every vendor pool.** The call site instantiates the platform's class with a fixed kwargs set, so every out-of-tree pool `__init__` must track call-site churn. #30568 is exactly this: `index_head_dim` is DSA-only, but the OOT MLA path passes it to every vendor pool, forcing each backend to add a phantom parameter or crash at startup. 2. **Every construction site must remember to consult the hook.** #27679: `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` selects its internal paged allocator with a bare `is_npu()` check and never consults `get_paged_allocator_cls()`, forcing OOT plugins to monkey-patch. 3. **Class-granular hooks can't see layout.** In `HybridLinearKVPool.__init__`, the platform class wins over the caller-selected layout variant (e.g. page-major) through an implicit priority chain — the "we should be careful when overriding in-tree `get_xxx_cls()`" concern raised on #29445. The platform clobbers a layout it never sees. This PR replaces the class-getters with a single request-passing seam and makes the remaining `get_*_cls` hooks explicit about "no platform opinion". It is **platform-neutral**: every in-tree platform returns `None` from every new/changed hook, the in-tree NPU (`_is_npu` / ascend) branches are untouched, and out-of-tree platforms keep working through the deprecated hooks. A follow-up PR (the reworked #29445) moves the in-tree NPU selection onto this seam. ## Modifications **New seam** (`platforms/interface.py`, `mem_cache/kv_pool_request.py`): ```python def build_kv_pool(self, *, request: KVPoolRequest) -> Optional[KVCache]: """None = no platform opinion; the configurator builds the in-tree default.""" ``` `KVPoolRequest` (msgspec.Struct) carries plain scalars — kind (`"mha" | "mla" | "dsa"`), sizes, page size, dtype, layer range, **layout** (`contiguous`/`page_major`), attention backend, `post_capture_active`, and `index_head_dim` set **only** for DSA-indexed models. The platform sees the full request and constructs the pool itself, so pool `__init__` signatures stay private to each platform: new request fields never break a platform that ignores them (fixes the #30568 class of bug by construction), and the platform can make an informed layout decision instead of being ordered above it. **Single resolution point** (`mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`): - `_build_platform_kv_pool`: consulted unconditionally at the former OOT-branch position — platform seam → deprecated OOT class hooks (warn-once) → in-tree builders. - `_build_platform_hybrid_full_kv_pool`: resolves the full-attention leaf of hybrid-linear composites, absorbing the OOT selection that lived inside `HybridLinearKVPool.__init__`; the resolved pool is injected via the existing `full_kv_pool` parameter. - `HybridLinearKVPool.__init__` no longer makes platform decisions (`memory_pool.py`). **Hook flattening** (`raise NotImplementedError` → `return None`, callers get explicit fallbacks): - `get_paged_allocator_cls` — now also consulted inside `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` (the #27679 fix). The top-level OOT preemption keeps its legacy semantics. - `get_graph_runner_cls` (`cuda_graph_setup.py`) and `get_piecewise_backend_cls` (`compilation/backend.py`) — platform hook first, device-keyed in-tree defaults unchanged as fallback. - `get_{mha,mla,dsa}_kv_pool_cls` — deprecated, still honored for OOT platforms when `build_kv_pool` returns None. **One deliberate contract change:** an OOT platform that never overrode a hook now falls back to the in-tree default instead of crashing with `NotImplementedError` ("None = use default", matching the existing `get_quantization_config` convention). **Tests:** `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_platform_seam.py` (CPU CI) pins the resolution order (platform → legacy → in-tree), the mambaish/standalone split, the legacy leaf construction kwargs, and the every-hook-defaults-to-None contract. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — platform-neutral refactor; every in-tree platform returns `None` from every changed hook and all `_is_npu`/ascend branches are untouched, so pool/allocator/runner selection is unchanged on all hardware. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — selection-time only; no kernel or forward-path changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- Related: supersedes the KV-hook design in #29445 (reworked NPU platform follows as a stacked PR); fixes the defect classes reported in #30568 and #27679; direction per the `create_kv_pool` factory sketched in RFC #20372. cc @AgainstEntropy @ssshinigami 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32316436177](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316436177)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316436138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316436138)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Enable LoRA on non-language (audio/vision) encoder towers and connectors
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang applies LoRA only to the **language** model today. A growing number of multimodal adapters also adapt the **audio/vision encoder tower** and the **connector/projector** (the same need that vLLM is addressing in vllm-project/vllm#31479). On SGLang these tower/connector LoRA weights are currently either **silently dropped** or **collide with language-model layers** — so an adapter that targets the encoder simply doesn't take effect (and in some shapes errors at load). This RFC documents the exact structural blockers (with file:line) and proposes a small, contained change to make LoRA bookkeeping *component-aware*, then offers **Qwen3-ASR as a clean reference implementation** because its tower is already built from native LoRA-wrappable linears. ## Current state — why tower/connector LoRA doesn't attach The LoRA *wrapping* infrastructure already supports every native linear class — `get_lora_layer`'s isinstance map (`python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py:1184-1194`) handles `QKVParallelLinear` / `MergedColumnParallelLinear` / `ColumnParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` / `ReplicatedLinear`. So a tower built from native linears is most of the way there. What blocks it is the per-layer bookkeeping: **1. Tower layers collide with (and can overflow) language layers.** `LoRAManager.lora_modules` is a flat list sized by the **language** model's depth: ```python # python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:734-735 self.lora_modules: List[Dict[str, BaseLayerWithLoRA]] = [ {} for _ in range(self.base_hf_config.num_hidden_layers) ] ``` and modules are bucketed purely by `get_layer_id`, whose regex only captures `layers.<N>`: ```python # python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/common.py def get_layer_id(weight_name): match = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", weight_name) return int(match.group(1)) if match else None ``` A tower module path like `audio_tower.layers.5.attn.qkv_proj` therefore resolves to `layer_id = 5` and lands in `lora_modules[5]["qkv_proj"]` (`lora_manager.py:824`) — **the same slot** as `...language_model.layers.5...qkv_proj`. One silently overwrites the other. When the tower is deeper than the LM (e.g. an audio encoder with more `encoder_layers` than the text `num_hidden_layers`), the same indexing **IndexErrors**. **2. The connector/projector is dropped entirely.** Connector/projection modules (e.g. Qwen3-Omni's `proj1` / `proj2` / `conv_out`, native `ReplicatedLinear` at `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_omni_moe.py:241-251`) have no `layers.<N>` segment, so `get_layer_id` returns `None` and the loop skips them: ```python # python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py:821-823 layer_id = get_layer_id(module_name) if layer_id is None: continue ``` **3. (Context) the `should_apply_lora` / `lora_pattern` gate is dead code.** 13 multimodal models define `should_apply_lora` / `lora_pattern` (e.g. `gemma4_mm.py:1043-1048` anchored on `^language_model\.layers\.`), but it is **never called** — the only non-`def` reference is the comment at `lora_manager.py:776-777`. The effective tower exclusion today is the `get_layer_id` gate in (1)/(2), not this method. Worth resolving as part of this work so intent and behavior match. ## Proposal Make LoRA module bookkeeping **component-aware** rather than a single language-sized list keyed by a bare layer index: - Resolve each LoRA module to a `(component, layer_id)` location, where `component ∈ {language, audio_tower, vision_tower, connector}` — e.g. extend `get_layer_id` into a `get_module_location(name)` that also reports the component from the path prefix (`audio_tower.` / `visual.` / projector names). - Namespace `lora_modules` per component (or key by `(component, layer_id)`), so tower layers neither collide with nor overflow the language list. Keep the existing language path keyed exactly as today to guarantee **no behavior change for the 13 existing language-only LoRA models** (the `test/registered/lora` suite as the regression guard). - Add a non-`layers.N` bucket for the connector. - A model opts in by declaring its tower/connector leaf names in `supported_lora_modules` and providing `get_hidden_dim(module_name, layer_idx)` for those names (the pattern already exists at `gemma4_mm.py:1050-1079`). Gate tower names through `model.supported_lora_modules` rather than broadening the shared `_KNOWN_LORA_TARGET_MODULES` set (`utils.py:338-357`), which currently filters out bare `proj`/`fc1`/`fc2` and is consumed by the `"all"` auto-detect path. The `set_lora_module` / `replace_submodule` wiring (`lora_manager.py:726-730`) needs no change. ## Reference implementation — Qwen3-ASR `Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration` (`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_asr.py`) is the cleanest first model: - Its tower (`Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder`) is **already native-wrappable** — attention via `VisionAttention(use_qkv_parallel=True)` → `QKVParallelLinear` + `RowParallelLinear`, FFN `fc1`/`fc2` as `Column`/`Row`/`Replicated` ParallelLinear (`qwen3_omni_moe.py:95, 107-108`), stacked as `self.layers = nn.ModuleList([...])` (`qwen3_omni_moe.py:215`). So live paths are `audio_tower.layers.{i}.attn.qkv_proj` etc., which the wrapping infra already supports. - It declares no `supports_lora` today, so it's unclaimed. I'd be glad to implement it as **PR1 (tower / in-layer first)**, with the **connector as a follow-up** to keep the diff reviewable — mirroring how a tower-vs-projector split keeps review surface small. Qwen3-Omni Thinker shares the same encoder, so the work transfers there as a natural PR2. ## Questions for maintainers - Is component-namespaced layer-id keying the approach you'd prefer, or is there an existing convention I should follow instead? - Is there appetite for tower/connector (non-language) LoRA in general? If so, I'm happy to drive the bookkeeping change + the Qwen3-ASR reference PR. cc @Fridge003 @jybsuper (lora) — would value your read on the keying approach before I put up the implementation.
