signal.title: [Perf] Incomplete TF32 n_splits warmup causes runtime JIT stalls on MHC models
signal.text: # Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. # Motivation ## Problem When serving MHC models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3/V4) with speculative decoding, some `TF32_HC_PRENORM_GEMM` kernels are lazily JIT-compiled during inference, causing 13-16s stalls per uncovered `n_splits` value. **Root cause:** `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre(num_tokens, hc_hidden_size)` computes `n_splits` deterministically: ```python n_splits = max(1, min(n_sms // ceil(num_tokens / 64), num_block_k // 4)) ``` The set of reachable `n_splits` values is finite and depends only on `n_sms` (GPU SM count) and `hc_hidden_size` (model config). For example, on H200 (132 SMs) + DeepSeek-V4 (hc_hidden_size=28672), there are exactly 22 possible values. However, CUDA graph capture only exercises batch sizes 1–256, which only covers `n_splits` values corresponding to `num_tokens <= ~1024`. The remaining values (requiring larger `num_tokens` from chunked prefill or high-concurrency decode batching) are left to lazy compilation at runtime. The existing `pp_parallel_deep_gemm_warmup` doesn't help because: 1. It's gated on `pp_size > 1 and not speculative` — inapplicable to single-node speculative setups 2. Its fixed dummy batch sizes only cover a small subset of `n_splits` values ## Impact Each missing `n_splits` compilation blocks ALL concurrent requests for 13-16s (NVCC compilation). The total cumulative stall can reach ~100s in the first minutes of serving, causing: - Severe TTFT spikes on early requests - Throughput degradation until all values are lazily compiled - Repeated impact on every container restart (since `_INITIALIZATION_DICT` is in-process memory) This affects any deployment combining: - MHC models (DeepSeek-V3, V4, or future models with `hc_hidden_size`) - Single-node (PP=1) with speculative decoding - Container restarts (common in production) ## Measured Results Environment: 8×H200, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, EAGLE 1step, TP=8, 8 concurrency, 50K-input / 1K-output multi-turn **Baseline — same container, warmup fully converged:** | Run | Requests | TTFT avg | TPOT avg | Throughput | Runtime JIT | |-----|----------|----------|----------|------------|-------------| | R1 | 605 | 3,661 ms | 25.1 ms | 19,529 tok/s | 0 | | R2 | 575 | 3,783 ms | 24.9 ms | 19,379 tok/s | 0 | **Fresh container restart (`.cubin` cache mounted, `_INITIALIZATION_DICT` lost):** | Run | Requests | TTFT avg | TPOT avg | Throughput | Runtime JIT | |-----|----------|----------|----------|------------|-------------| | R3 | 625 | 6,350 ms | 27.2 ms | 16,666 tok/s | 11 compilations | **With proposed fix (force-warmup all n_splits at startup, fresh container restart with .cubin cache mounted):** | Run | Requests | TTFT avg | TPOT avg | Throughput | Runtime JIT | |-----|----------|----------|----------|------------|-------------| | Patched | 568 | 4,650 ms | 25.3 ms | 18,235 tok/s | 0 | Improvement over unpatched restart: TTFT -26.8%, throughput +9.4%, runtime JIT eliminated. # Proposed Fix Add a generic `force_warmup_all_mhc_n_splits()` in `kernel_warmup()` that: 1. Reads `n_sms` from `torch.cuda.get_device_properties` (adapts to any GPU) 2. Reads `hc_hidden_size` and `hc_mult` from model config (adapts to any MHC model) 3. Enumerates all reachable `n_splits` via `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre` 4. Calls `_maybe_compile_deep_gemm_one_type_all` for each uncovered value Since `_maybe_compile` checks `_INITIALIZATION_DICT`, values already compiled during CUDA graph capture are skipped. Only genuinely missing values get compiled. **Startup cost:** proportional to the number of missing `n_splits` × `_BUILTIN_M_LIST` traversal. With `.cubin` cache: ~2-8s per value (load-only). Without cache: ~13-16s per value (NVCC compile). Zero runtime cost. I have a working patch validated on 8×H200 + DeepSeek-V4-Pro and will open a PR shortly. ## Environment (validation) - SGLang: v0.5.13 - GPU: 8× NVIDIA H200 (132 SMs) - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hc_mult=4, hidden_size=7168, hc_hidden_size=28672) - Config: TP=8, EAGLE 1step, mem_fraction_static=0.88, chunked_prefill=8192 ## Generality The fix is parametric — it derives everything from runtime GPU properties and model config: - Different GPUs (A100 108 SMs, H100 132 SMs, H200 132 SMs, B200 192 SMs) → different `n_splits` sets, all correctly enumerated - Different MHC models (different `hc_hidden_size`, `hc_mult`) → different `num_block_k` upper bound, correctly handled - Non-MHC models → function is a no-op (guard on `hc_hidden_size is not None`) --- Happy Dragon Boat Festival to all the maintainers and contributors! 🐲 Hope you're enjoying some zongzi today.

signal.title: [DCP][Spec] EAGLE/EAGLE3 support for decode context parallelism — stacked on #21637
signal.text: Makes **EAGLE / EAGLE3** work with decode context parallelism (`--dcp-size > 1`). Stacked on #21637. DFlash × DCP already worked (see #33912, `_dflash_draft_cell_size`); it gets one shared fix here, not new support. **Root cause:** the target KV pool is sharded across DCP ranks, but the draft pool is **replicated**. Draft-side code that reads the DCP topology therefore builds rank-local metadata against a full pool. Every change below follows from that. ## Results 8×B200, K2.5-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 (ns2/topk1/ndt3), `--dcp-comm-backend a2a --dcp-replicate-q-proj`, jobs 1496709–1496996. Accept length is the correctness gate: the DCP arm must match the off arm, since a draft chain fed rank-local metadata degenerates after the first token. | config | off (ms) | DCP=8 (ms) | ratio | AL off → DCP | |---|---|---|---|---| | 50K / cc4 | 4.96 | 5.93 | 0.84× | 2.239 → 2.234 | | 128K / cc16 | 19.58 | 20.44 | 0.96× | 2.160 → 2.150 | | 128K / cc24 | 37.66 | **26.78** | **1.41×** | 2.172 → 2.163 | | 256K / cc8 | 20.63 | 22.19 | 0.93× | 1.756 → 1.781 | | 256K / cc16 | 59.51 | **38.14** | **1.56×** | 1.748 → 1.745 | GSM8K 0.940–0.960 on every arm. Below the KV-pool edge DCP pays the verify addon for no benefit; past it the off arm loses admission first and DCP wins. Attention FLOPs are conserved under context sharding, so there is no headroom to beat the off arm at shallow overcommit — the ~16% cost at 50K/cc4 is the design point, not a regression. ## Tests `test_dcp_draft_guard.py`, `test_dcp_draft_pool_bounds.py`, `test_dcp_spec_topk_guard.py` — all three cover failures that are otherwise **silent**: a guard that stops unsharding draft forwards corrupts the chain with no error, an under-budgeted draft pool OOMs at the first large prefill far from its cause, and a mis-scoped topk validator returns wrong tokens rather than raising. The topk tests pin that DSPARK is *not* gated (`is_dflash_family()` would pull it in and reject the shipping Kimi-Linear + DSPARK + DCP path). Registered DCP/spec suites pass on 8×B200, including main's `test_kimi_linear_dcp4.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32316190645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316190645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32316190500](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32316190500)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
signal.text: ## Motivation The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its `> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss. None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike): - Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer. - `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter, no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for truly scattered index sets. - Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`) become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads them back. ## Prior work **Landed** - #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and bookkeeping coupled to real allocations - #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device sync (non-SWA) - #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on) - #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant: every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned) - #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant) - #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len) **Closed** - #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full shape - #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len` - #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned extents remove the need for it) ## In flight - #35396 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor on the second PD decode prealloc path, and drop the fixture that mocked an unaligned tail length - #35401 -- write the `req_to_token` page tail so a row stays valid over every page the allocator handed out; widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every paged config. Prerequisite for page-ceiling `kv_allocated_len`: without it, anything slicing a row by a page-ceiled length reads the previous occupant's indices - #35592 -- decide SWA slot liveness on the host and drop the `> 0` filter in `free_swa`. Callers now declare whether a range's SWA peers are still live, from state they already keep (`node.swa_tombstone`, `req.kv.swa_evicted_seqlen`, the unified tree's `cd.value is None`); `free_full` completes the pool-specific pair so `free(x) == free_full(x) + free_swa(x)` holds for every allocator. At `page_size == 1` this makes the per-decode-step window eviction (`free_swa_out_of_window_slots`) sync-free outright; paged configs still hit the `torch.unique` in `_expand_to_full_pages`, which needs the page-representative read to go with it

signal.text: ## Motivation This PR adds targeted CPU-only unit coverage for `srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py`. The goal is to lock down HiCache storage behavior that is easy to regress but not always obvious from the implementation alone, especially: - `HiCacheFile` key / path derivation - MLA vs non-MLA `config_suffix` behavior - `batch_exists_v2` prefix-hit semantics across KV and extra pools - v1 / v2 batch I/O helpers ## Modifications This PR adds a new unit test file: - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_unit.py` The new tests cover: - `PoolTransferResult` update semantics - `HiCacheFile.config_suffix` construction - `_get_suffixed_key`, `_get_component_key`, and `_get_component_path` - basic file-backed I/O: `set`, `get`, `exists`, `clear` - v1 batch wrappers: `batch_get`, `batch_set` - `batch_exists_v2` behavior for: - KV-only prefix hits - `ALL_PAGES` - `TRAILING_PAGES` - multi-pool min-prefix behavior - unrelated-file isolation - v2 batch I/O pipeline: - `batch_get_v2` - `batch_set_v2` - `_batch_io_v2` - host index / page size edge cases This PR also improves the test-side documentation inside the new file to make the HiCache key/path pipeline more explicit, including: - what a page hash key represents - why page hash keys are prefix-chained - how `config_suffix`, component keys, and on-disk paths relate - why MLA omits TP fields in the storage suffix Related to #20865. ## Test Plan ``` python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_unit.py ================================================= test session starts ================================================= platform darwin -- Python 3.12.10, pytest-9.0.3, pluggy-1.6.0 rootdir: /Users/varvel/code/github/sglang/test configfile: pytest.ini plugins: cov-7.1.0, anyio-4.13.0 collected 50 items test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_unit.py .................................................. signal.title: Enable num_splits > 1 for FA3 deterministic inference
signal.text: ## Summary SGLang's deterministic inference mode currently forces `num_splits=1` for FA3, which limits prefill throughput. With the `batch_invariant` scheduling fix in flash-attention (sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43), we can safely use `num_splits > 1` while maintaining bit-exact determinism. This PR sets `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, improving prefill throughput by up to **2.1x** on prefill-bound workloads. ## Benchmark Results (Qwen3-8B, H200, `--attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend flashinfer --enable-deterministic-inference`) | Workload | num_splits=1 | num_splits=4 | Speedup | |----------|-------------|-------------|---------| | **Short prefill** (512 in, 128 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 8,614 | 18,101 | **2.10x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 482 | 1,432 | 0.34x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 8,970 | 3,986 | **2.25x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 131 | 40 | **3.3x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 5,875 | 704 | **8.3x** | | **Medium prefill** (2048 in, 256 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 18,533 | 23,371 | **1.26x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,628 | 2,688 | 0.98x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 10,409 | 8,073 | **1.29x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 62 | 34 | **1.8x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 4,397 | 2,068 | **2.1x** | | **Long prefill** (4096 in, 512 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 16,601 | 18,073 | **1.09x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,850 | 1,887 | **1.51x** | | Mean E2E (ms) | 9,233 | 8,910 | **1.04x** | > **TTFT vs ITL tradeoff on short prefill:** With `num_splits=1` at `request-rate=inf`, prefills run serially — early requests get fast TTFT (482ms) but cause massive decode stalls (P99 ITL 5.9s). With `num_splits=4`, prefills complete faster in aggregate, so decode runs smoothly (P99 ITL 704ms, 8x better), but individual TTFT is higher because more prefills are batched concurrently. E2E latency and throughput are the meaningful comparisons. At realistic request rates this TTFT difference disappears. ## Changes - **`flashattention_backend.py`**: Set `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, pass `batch_invariant=True` - **`flash_attention.py`**, **`flash_attention_v3.py`**: Thread `batch_invariant` param through FA3 call chain - **sgl-kernel**: Add `batch_invariant` to fwd op schema, Python wrapper, C++ header - **sgl-kernel/tests**: Add `test_flash_attn_deterministic_num_splits` (128 test cases, all passing) ## Deterministic validation All three sglang deterministic test modes pass with `num_splits=4`: - `test_deterministic --test-mode single` (15 trials, batch 1-15): **PASS** (1 unique output) - `test_deterministic --test-mode prefix` (4 prefix lengths, logprobs): **PASS** (all identical) - `test_deterministic --test-mode radix_cache`: **PASS** (cached == uncached) ## Reproduce benchmark results **1. Launch server (num_splits=4, this PR):** ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 ``` **2. Run benchmarks (in a separate terminal):** ```bash # Short prefill (512 input, 128 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 \ --num-prompts 300 --request-rate inf # Medium prefill (2048 input, 256 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts 200 --request-rate inf # Long prefill (4096 input, 512 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \ --num-prompts 100 --request-rate inf ``` **3. For num_splits=1 baseline**, temporarily change `flashattention_backend.py` line 210 from `self.num_splits = 4` to `self.num_splits = 1`, restart server, and re-run the same benchmarks. ## Reproduce deterministic tests ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 # In a separate terminal: python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode single --n-start 10 --n-trials 15 python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode prefix --n-start 10 --n-trials 10 --return-logprob python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode radix_cache ``` ## Dependencies Requires: sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43 (`batch_invariant` flag) ## Test plan - [x] 128/128 kernel-level batch invariance tests pass (sgl-kernel) - [x] All 3 sglang deterministic test modes pass - [ ] CI passes <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #28138299519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299519)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #28138299333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299333)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Motivation Day-0 support for [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`, `model_type=bailing_hybrid`): a hybrid MoE architecture interleaving KDA linear attention (with a safe-gate lower bound) and MLA, with MTP (NEXTN) and DSPARK speculative decoding support. ## Modifications - `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` model (`bailing_hybrid` config): KDA + MLA hybrid layers, 512-expert MoE, and MTP (NEXTN). - DSPARK support for the KDA hybrid path: graph-folded draft proposal, fused KDA chain-verify kernel, and DSA token-to-KV pool sizing. - KDA safe gate propagation through the Triton decode/target-verify kernels and their call sites, matching fused verification. - `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers. - BF16, FP8, compressed-tensors INT4, and native MXFP4 checkpoint support on Hopper and Blackwell. - Exactness, fusion-gate, quantization, and parser tests. ## Validation All serving runs kept decode CUDA Graph enabled and used the default graph sizing. No run used `--disable-cuda-graph` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. ### Quantized checkpoints Full GSM8K uses 1,319 questions. Performance uses 80 exact-length random requests at ISL/OSL 8192/1024 with concurrency 1 and 16; throughput includes input and output tokens per second per GPU. | GPU | format | GSM8K | stop rate | throughput/GPU (c1 / c16) | P50 TTFT ms (c1 / c16) | P50 TPOT ms (c1 / c16) | default graph range | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | H200 | INT4 | 95.30% | 100% | 1,159 / 7,184 | 205.96 / 1,891.74 | 3.68 / 8.16 | through batch 218 | | H200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 100% | 709 / 5,215 | 305.23 / 2,725.52 | 6.05 / 11.17 | through batch 227 | | B200 | INT4 | 96.74% | 99.70% | 482 / 1,344 | 641.41 / 6,202.62 | 8.72 / 48.01 | through batch 305 | | B200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 99.62% | 785 / 7,933 | 127.97 / 1,117.16 | 5.60 / 7.98 | through batch 314 | INT4 selects Marlin on H200 and the graph-compatible Triton WNA16 path on B200. MXFP4 routed experts use the native FlashInfer runner on both GPUs. The B200 MXFP4 checkpoint also contains block-FP8 dense/shared projections, which use the Triton FP8 GEMM backend to avoid an unsupported FlashInfer FP8 tactic without converting the routed experts. BF16 and FP8 were rerun on H200 and B200 after the quantization changes. All four combinations served with CUDA Graph enabled, completed generation, and passed the 20-example GSM8K regression gate with 100% stop rate. ### Speculative decoding Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x B200 TP4, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, thinking on, full GSM8K, `max_tokens=8192`: | spec decoding | score | stop rate | error rate | |---|---:|---:|---:| | DSPARK | 96.66% | 99.77% | 0.00% | | MTP (NEXTN) | 96.44% | 99.62% | 0.00% | Non-stop finishes are long reasoning outputs reaching `max_tokens`, not repetition loops. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests and register them in CI. - [x] Validate serving correctness, stop rate, and accuracy on H200 and B200. - [x] Publish deployment recipes and benchmark results in #34363. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32252403289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32252403289)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32252403188](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32252403188)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [smg] per-router parsing + structured error envelope on /generate, /v1/chat/completions
signal.text: ## Summary Three commits on the `sgl-model-gateway` request handling path. Together they take `/generate` and `/v1/chat/completions` to a *single* parse per router (no more eager routing-view parse in `server.rs` plus second parse inside PD/gRPC) while preserving the structured-400 contract on SGLang RL extension fields. 1. **Proto-style typed routing view (commit 1).** Introduce `ChatRoutingView` / `GenerateRoutingView` — minimal serde structs that capture only the fields the gateway actually reads (`model`, `stream`, `return_logprob`, `return_routed_experts`, batch hints, optional prompt text). Body bytes ride through verbatim, so SGLang RL extension fields the gateway doesn't branch on flow to the backend without reserialisation. 2. **Structured 400 + tests for `return_routed_experts` (commit 2).** Promote wrong-typed extension fields from a generic `json_parse_error` to `invalid_sglang_extension` (with the offending field named) via the new `ViewSchema` trait + `view_parse_error<V>` / `validate_extensions_in_value<V>` helpers. Mock-worker plumbing (`MockWorkerState` request capture, opt-in `routed_experts_b64` injection) plus mock-based and real-GPU e2e (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`) tests for unified + PD round-tripping. 3. **Per-router parsing + structured error envelope (commit 3, this push).** Drop `view: &…RoutingView` from `RouterTrait::route_generate` / `route_chat`; add `model_id: Option<&str>` (matches `route_completion`'s shape). Each router does the single parse that fits its path: - HTTP unified → `…RoutingView` (single typed parse). - HTTP PD → `serde_json::Value` once + `validate_extensions_in_value::<…>` to keep the structured-400 contract (PD parses `Value` regardless to inject `bootstrap_host/port/room`, so this is genuinely one parse). - gRPC + gRPC PD → `Value` once → `validate_extensions_in_value` → `from_value::<typed>` to materialise the proto request. - OpenAI → typed `ChatCompletionRequest`. - `RouterManager`: in IGW mode parses `Value` once via `extract_body_model` (distinguishes absent / `null` / wrong-typed `model`); non-IGW hands body+model_id straight to the default router with no parse. Also unifies the error envelope: `routers::error::create_error` now emits OpenAI-compat `error.type` (`invalid_request_error` / `authentication_error` / `permission_error` / `not_found_error` / `rate_limit_error` / `server_error`) instead of the canonical reason phrase. Every `(Status, &str).into_response()` site in `RouterManager` and `read_body_bytes` migrated to the structured helpers, and the lone `json_parse_failed` site in the dp_aware path renamed to `json_parse_error` so all routers agree on one code. ## Why - **Per-field error codes** let callers distinguish "your JSON is malformed" from "you sent `return_routed_experts: \"yes\"` and we want a bool" without string-matching. Mirrors the contract the older `body_raw` / `parse_sglang_extensions` design exposed before the proto-pattern refactor. - **Single optimal parse per router**: the original proto-pattern win (zero reserialisation on the unified HTTP path) was being undone for PD and gRPC, which had to reparse to `Value` or to a typed proto on top of the routing-view parse. Each router now pays for exactly one parse. - **IGW model resolution must reach the chosen router.** The first proto-pattern refactor renamed `effective_model_id` → `_effective_model_id`, dropping the resolved id and breaking metrics labels / worker selection / cache-aware policies under k8s service-discovery deployments. Pinned with a regression test. - **Structured error envelope across the gateway.** OpenAI-compat clients classify on `error.type`; returning canonical reason strings (`"Bad Request"`) silently broke their `RateLimitError` / `AuthenticationError` dispatch. ## Test plan - [x] `cargo test --lib` — 384 passed, 0 failed. - [x] `cargo test --tests` — 429 passed, 0 failed (all integration suites: api_tests, routing_tests, reliability_tests, security_tests, spec_test, etc.). - [x] PD `invalid_sglang_extension` 400 contract — `test_pd_chat_rejects_invalid_extension_type`, `test_pd_generate_rejects_invalid_extension_type` pass under the new `Value`-then-validate flow. - [x] HTTP unified `invalid_sglang_extension` 400 contract — `test_unified_chat_rejects_invalid_extension_type`, `test_unified_generate_rejects_invalid_extension_type` pass. - [x] IGW model-resolution regression — new `routers::router_manager::tests::igw_route_generate_propagates_resolved_model` pinning that the resolved id reaches the downstream router via `model_id`. - [x] Cache-aware chat text walker — 8 new `routers::http::pd_router::tests::extract_chat_request_text::*` tests covering user / developer / system / multimodal-parts / missing / empty cases. - [x] Extension validator — 6 new `routers::http::routing_view::tests::validate_extensions::*` tests covering wrong-typed / correctly-typed / absent / `null` / non-object cases. - [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean on all changed files. - [ ] `pytest e2e_test/router/test_routed_experts.py -v` on a 2-GPU host (real DeepSeek-V2-Lite).

signal.title: [Spec] Fix Dspark and Dflash state divergence across TP rank
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Related to: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 To fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 bug, upgrade NCCL to the newest version (2.30.7). When TP > 1, Dspark makes serveral sampling decisions on reach rank: 1. The draft Markov chain samples proposal tokens step by step (with in-graph philox noise introduced since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33298) 2. Target verify derives `correct_len` / `bonus` / `cap_trim_lens` 3. Prefill samples `next_token_ids` In order to maintain the speedup, SGLang skips cross-rank sync of sampled tokens by default (I found the comment here: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L496). So nothing forces these values to agree. Once one rank commits a different token or accept length, sequence lengths and KV state drift apart and a later collective deadlocks (demonstrated by fault injection in the Accuracy Tests section below). ## Modifications Broadcast rank 0's sampling decisions before they affect state. The idea follows the existing `verify_lens` handling in `dspark_planner.py` and the EAGLE proposals in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29003 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31478: 1. Broadcast every Markov proposal token in **both** eager and graph-folded sampling. Sync only at the end of a draft block is too late because each step depends on the previous token. 2. Broadcast `correct_len`, `bonus`, and `cap_trim_lens` in the eager verify path and the captured verify epilogue, before finalization, token output, or KV commit. Separate `all_reduce(MIN)` calls could combine fields from different ranks. 3. Broadcast prefill `next_token_ids` before entering the draft path. `DsparkTpSync` in `dspark_tp.py` (newly added file) uses the TP group's PyNCCL communicator. Process-group collectives cannot be captured in CUDA graphs, and using the model's existing TP communicator preserves collective ordering across eager and captured execution. With DP attention, it uses `attn_tp_group`, matching `verify_lens_broadcast_group` in original `dspark_planner.py`. TP=1 is a no-op. The reason why I don't match RNG seeds is because ranks can still diverge if they consume different numbers of random values, and it does not cover non-RNG differences. In addition, for TP > 1, this add `gamma + 3` broadcasts of a `[bs]` tensor per decode step, all within the captured graphs. ## Accuracy Tests All tests below on following configs: - 2 DGX Sparks - TP=2 - DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with 131k context - Decode CUDA graphs and folded sampling enabled - Add https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33407 code. It fixes an unrelated bug for SM12x sparse-MLA topk dispatch crash at boot. Dspark + DeepSeek V4 Flash cannot start on DGX Sparks without it. - **NCCL 2.30.7** for SGLang's PyNCCL communicator via `SGLANG_NCCL_SO_PATH` (torch's bundled 2.28.9 wedges this workload's graph/eager mix with or without this patch; a separate problem from this fix) For accuracy test, we run`python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200` (temp=0): accuracy 0.965, invalid 0.000. This is expected since there's no mathematical changes. To demonstrate the failure mode this patch addresses, we fault-injected a rank-local accept divergence into both builds: rank 1 lowers every accept length by one (`correct_len = torch.clamp(correct_len - 1, min=0)`, NCCL 2.30.7 in both _runs). **_Note: the fault reproduction code has been removed before submitting PR._** Without the fix, the server deadlocks before finishing startup warmup. With the fix, the same injection is harmless: rank 0's broadcast overwrites the divergent values, the server boots, and a temp=0 request returns the expected output. As a stability check on the fix itself (its broadcasts run inside the captured decode graphs), I sent 42 sequential chat requests with `ignore_eos=true` and `max_tokens=512` (30 at temp=1, then 12 at temp=0) and probed `/health_generate` after every request with a 180s client timeout, so a stuck collective surfaces as a failed request instead of a silent hang. As the result, all 42 returned HTTP 200 with `finish_reason=length`. 21504 tokens generated in total and mean acc_len during the temp=1 run was 2.86 (block_size=4). Same for temp=0, neither of them occur any error. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test on 24 natural prompts, 256 output tokens, concurrency=1, temp=1, same setup as above: | Requests | Output throughput | TTFT mean/median/P90 (ms) | TPOT mean/median/P90 (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | 24 | 31.9 tok/s | 157.6 / 153.7 / 178.6 | 30.8 / 31.7 / 35.5 | Comparing with pre-fix TP baseline is impossible because it cannot survive under such load. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 4. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 5. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 6. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Reuse per-step cuda events uniformly (WAR read_done + copy_done)
signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #31468, several paths construct a fresh cuda `Event()` every decode step: the WAR `read_done` in `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.execute()` (twice per DFlash step: draft + verify runners), the same in `EagleDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner`, and the scheduler's `copy_done` (both the overlap and non-overlap spec paths). Each costs a `cudaEventCreate` + Python object churn (~µs/step) — not a host sync, purely allocation/GC hygiene, so no throughput change is expected; a no-regression A/B is attached below. ## Modifications - New `ReusableEventRing` (`sglang/srt/utils/cuda_event_ring.py`): lazy fixed ring of re-recordable events; a slot is re-recorded only after every consumer of its previous record has waited/synchronized, so depth = max records in flight (+ margin). - `read_done` sites (decode graph runner, eagle draft-extend runner): depth **2** per runner — the WAR barrier `wait_event`s and clears `war_fastpath_read_done_event` right after `run_batch`, so at most one record is outstanding. - Scheduler `copy_done` (overlap + non-overlap spec): depth **3** — `result_queue` momentarily holds the previous result plus the just-appended one (≤2 in flight); every consumer (`batch_result_processor`, disaggregation prefill) synchronizes exactly once before a slot recurs. - **Intentionally out of scope:** the unified-memory `forward_done` event — `MultiEndedAllocator` retains and `query()`s old references, so re-recording would silently change what a retained handle reports; it needs its own lifecycle. Likewise the PP microbatch `d2h_event`s, whose lifetime is the PP async depth, not the decode pipeline. ## Test `test/registered/unit/spec/test_cuda_event_ring.py` (CI-registered): lazy fixed allocation + round-robin ordering, distinct-objects-within-depth, depth validation, and a CUDA record/wait/synchronize cycle across ring wrap-around mimicking both lifecycles. ## Benchmarks No-regression e2e posted in the comments: per-cc deltas within the harness noise band (mean +0.6%), GSM8K 0.955/0.965, AL parity. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-writing-documentation). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-writing-documentation). - signal.title: [Fix] Transformers-fallback (GPT-NeoX) + KV pool config (DeepSeek-VL2)
signal.text: ## Summary Three small fixes surfaced by consecutive downstream accuracy runs. All three are one-liners (plus comments); the first two live in the Transformers-fallback layer, the third in `ModelConfig`. ### 1. `hf_to_sglang_mapper` — map `gpt_neox.` and `embed_out.` `GPTNeoXForCausalLM` has no native SGLang impl → falls back to `TransformersForCausalLM`. The fallback calls `AutoModel.from_config(config)`, which returns the bare `GPTNeoXModel` backbone (`embed_in`, `layers`, `final_layer_norm`) as `self.model`; `self.lm_head` is materialized separately by `CausalMixin`. Pythia / NeoX checkpoints were saved from `GPTNeoXForCausalLM.state_dict()`, so keys carry a `gpt_neox.` wrapper prefix for the backbone and a top-level `embed_out.` for the LM head. The base mapper has no rule for either, so the catch-all `""` → `"model."` fires and produces `model.gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` — which the loader can't find (`ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.gpt_neox' ...`). **Fix:** add two prefix rules alongside the existing `"transformer.": "model."` (GPT-2 analogue): - `"gpt_neox.": "model."` — strip the wrapper prefix so backbone keys land under `self.model.*`. - `"embed_out.": "lm_head."` — route the LM head to SGLang's `self.lm_head` slot. ### 2. `skip_substrs` — skip GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` causal-mask buffer Older GPT-NeoX checkpoints include a persistent causal-mask buffer named `gpt_neox.layers.N.attention.bias`. Newer transformers versions register the same buffer with `persistent=False`, so it is absent from the constructed model's tree. `self.skip_substrs` already skips GPT-2-style `.attn.bias` / `.attn.masked_bias` (attention module named `attn`), but not GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` (attention module named `attention`). Result: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.attention.bias' ...`. **Fix:** add `.attention.bias` to the skip list. The already-present `.masked_bias` catches the fill-value counterpart regardless of attention module name. ### 3. `ModelConfig.v_head_dim` — treat `0` as unset (fixes DeepSeek-VL2 non-MLA V-cache) `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s `language_config` sets `use_mla=False` **and** `v_head_dim=0` — the `0` is an MLA-disabled sentinel from the checkpoint's DeepseekV2-flavored config, not a real head dimension. `ModelConfig.__init__` currently substitutes `head_dim` for `v_head_dim` only when the attribute is `None`, so a `getattr` that returns `0` slips through into `self.v_head_dim`. `pool_configurator.py` then reads `model_config.v_head_dim` directly in the non-MLA branch, and per-slot V-buffers get allocated with last dim = 0. The first extend prefill fails: ``` File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 192, in _set_kv_buffer_impl v_cache[indices] = v RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [432, 10, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [432, 10, 0] ``` DeepSeek-VL2 explicitly selects the standard (non-MLA) `DeepseekForCausalLM` language model when `use_mla=False` (`sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py`), which produces real V with the usual `num_kv_heads * head_dim` layout — the attention layer is correct; the pool is what's mis-sized. **Fix:** swap the guard to `if not self.v_head_dim:` so both `None` and `0` fall back to `self.head_dim`. MLA architectures are unaffected — their architecture-specific `elif` branches later in the same block overwrite `self.v_head_dim` with the real value from the text config. ## Test plan - [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for all three files. - [x] `EleutherAI/pythia-12b` (TP=2, triton) — reproduces the missing-mapper failure on `main`; loads through with fix 1. - [x] `EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b` (TP=2, triton) — with fix 1 applied, reproduces the missing-skip failure on `main`; loads through with fix 2, warmup succeeds, first `POST /generate` returns 200. - [x] `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny` (TP=1, triton, `--disable-radix-cache`, mem-fraction 0.55) — reproduces the `_set_kv_buffer_impl` shape-mismatch on `main`; with fix 3, KV cache allocates `K size = V size = 3.38 GB` (previously `V size = 0.00 GB`), text `POST /generate` returns 200 with valid tokens. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32265644409](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265644409)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32265644129](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265644129)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kernel] Add H200 MoE configs for Nemotron-3.5
signal.text: > [!WARNING] > **Draft: do not merge.** Forced-Triton real-model validation on one H200 > found that every tested TP1 table reduced or failed to improve normalized > output-token throughput. The isolated kernel numbers below are valid, but > they do not translate into a serving-positive configuration. ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`: - TP1: `E=128,N=1856` - TP2 per rank: `E=128,N=928` Both shapes previously used the generic fallback config. The tuned configs reduce kernel latency by 32.2% to 39.6% across the measured token counts. ## Forced-Triton real-model validation Tested official revision `d468880b6ad3c6e0d21377ce7242adaea4cc884d` with SGLang v0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), Torch 2.11.0, Triton 3.6.0, and `--moe-runner-backend triton` on one H200. Each comparison used ten 200-question GSM8K runs, five shots, parallelism 64, and zero-temperature sampling. | TP1 candidate | Median latency | Median output throughput | Quality | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Original up only vs baseline | +0.79% | -1.70% | up to 0.5% invalid in three runs | | Original up + tuned down vs baseline | +5.78% | -4.68% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up + down vs fresh baseline | -2.23% | -1.69% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up only vs fresh baseline | -0.22% | -1.68% | zero invalid | | Alignment-aware up only vs reverse-order baseline | +3.95% | -2.86% | zero invalid | The decode-aware searches added M=1,4,16,32,64,128 entries, used 100 real routed-expert tensors covering all 128 experts, and matched up/down `BLOCK_SIZE_M`. A conservative follow-up fixed decode `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` to reduce expert padding and route-alignment overhead. Neither approach produced a serving-positive table. A reverse-order baseline recovered its original performance, ruling out simple node drift. **Decision:** keep this PR in draft and do not publish these configs. A future attempt must tune the complete MoE path, including route alignment, padding, and both projections, rather than optimizing isolated projection kernels. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `c2c1c4d3ebc42402264002f6ec57f90fee58c30c` - Token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape ## Results | TP | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256 | 1435.44 | 930.48 | 1.543x | 35.18% | | 1 | 512 | 1550.47 | 967.20 | 1.603x | 37.62% | | 1 | 1024 | 1694.77 | 1023.66 | 1.656x | 39.60% | | 2 | 256 | 734.74 | 493.07 | 1.490x | 32.89% | | 2 | 512 | 780.75 | 529.32 | 1.475x | 32.20% | | 2 | 1024 | 845.91 | 548.78 | 1.541x | 35.13% | The TP2 per-rank config was also run concurrently on both H200s. Both ranks selected the same configs; their measured means were within 0.6% to 1.0%. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODEL=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-model-configs/nemotron35-lightning RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full TP1 and TP2 searches: ```bash mkdir -p "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 1 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 2 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & wait ``` Baseline and tuned validation, repeated three times for each TP size: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" done CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/E=128,N=1856,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/E=128,N=928,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` Concurrent dual-H200 TP2 per-rank validation: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2-dual-rank-gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results/nemotron35-lightning-h200-configs.patch ```

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Exact token ids behind a completion cannot reliably be recovered by retokenizing the response. Returning exact prompt and sampled token IDs is currently unsupported for `v1/chat/completions` streaming responses (#30917 added `return_token_ids`, but chat streaming rejects it, and its streaming shape interleaves per-chunk id deltas into every choice). This PR exposes both input and output token IDs on the response-level `sglext` extension, delivered once per response, and is opt-in per request or server-wide. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - `protocol.py`: add `return_input_ids` / `return_output_ids` request flags and `sglext.input_ids` (shared prompt) / `sglext.output_ids` (per choice) response fields. - `server_args.py`: add `--return-input-ids` / `--return-output-ids` to force the behavior for every request; signal.title: [Bug] Hybrid Mamba prefill allocation failure kills scheduler instead of returning request to waiting queue
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug occurs on SGLang 0.5.16, build commit `fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`. - [x] Environment information and a reproduction configuration are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, written in English. ### Describe the bug Under sustained Kimi-K3 traffic with hybrid Mamba/radix caching, a prefill allocation failure terminates a scheduler rank and subsequently the whole server instead of leaving the request in the waiting queue, rechunking it, retracting work, or failing only that request. Observed fatal error on every scheduler rank: ```text RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size. Try to allocate 8192 tokens. Available full tokens: 8070656 (full_available_size=7936 + full_evictable_size_=8062720) Available mamba: 760 (available_size=57 + component_evictable_size_=703) ``` The process supervisor then reports that a child failed, sends `SIGQUIT`, and shuts down the complete process tree. There was no host OOM, CUDA Xid, or Docker OOM kill. The surprising part is that the request passes prefill admission but the later real allocation can still fail fatally: 1. `PrefillAdder.rem_total_tokens` for `is_hybrid_ssm_cache` considers the token allocator's `available_size()` plus `tree_cache.full_evictable_size()`. 2. The admitted request is added to `can_run_list` and removed from `waiting_queue` in `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw()`. 3. `new_batch.prepare_for_extend()` subsequently performs the real allocation. 4. `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` raises an uncaught `RuntimeError` when `allocator.alloc_extend()` returns `None`. There is no rollback that places the admitted prefill request back in `waiting_queue`, and no retry with a smaller chunk. Decode has a retraction path, but this late prefill allocation failure does not. Expected behavior: capacity pressure should preserve process availability. The request should remain/return to waiting, be retried with a smaller chunk after eviction, be preempted, or receive a request-scoped OOM response. A single allocation miss should not terminate every scheduler rank. ### Reproduction Serve Kimi-K3 with TP8/DCP4 and hybrid Mamba cache settings: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --served-model-name kimi-k3-dev \ --tp-size 8 \ --dcp-size 4 \ --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --mem-fraction-static 0.93 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --mamba-full-memory-ratio 7.21 \ --max-mamba-cache-size 800 \ --max-running-requests 60 \ --context-length 262144 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 ``` Run concurrent long-context requests until the Mamba/radix cache is under pressure and submit another request requiring an 8192-token prefill chunk. In our run, the allocator reported the values above and the uncaught exception terminated the server. Even if this particular memory split is too aggressive, the requested fix is graceful backpressure/recovery rather than changing the cache sizing defaults. ### Environment ```text Python: 3.12.3 CUDA available: True GPU 0-7: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (275040 MiB each) Compute Capability: 10.3 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: CUDA 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 595.71.05 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.16 sglang build commit: fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.15.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.140.0 huggingface_hub: 1.24.0 uvicorn: 0.51.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 NVIDIA topology: all eight GPUs connected via NV18 ulimit soft: 1024 ```

signal.title: [AMD] Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode (batched bh16bn128).
signal.text: Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode on gfx950 for Kimi-K3 TP8 (12 local heads). If aiter is not updated to the target version, fall back to use the existing zero-pad + mla_decode_fwd. No behavior change on older containers until aiter/Triton are upgraded. below is the dependency: **aiter runtime dependencies** (container/image, not pinned in this repo): - [ROCm/aiter#4480](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4480) (**merged** to `main`, [`fb82bf7`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/fb82bf7e20adaa9918c9d4bc80e4ff91f000823e)): fp8 Gluon `bh16bn128`, batch>1. - [ROCm/aiter#4555](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4555) (on `main`): decode CUDA graph KV-split budget. - Triton >= 3.7: Gluon `cga_layout` on gfx950. ## Motivation Kimi-K3 at TP8 exposes 12 MLA heads/GPU. The fast aiter persist decode ASM wants head counts divisible by 16 and has no native fp8 12-head path, so fp8 serving had to zero-pad to 16 and go through slower kernels — especially painful at long context under decode CUDA graph. aiter already has a Gluon kernel with a native 12-head masked MFMA tile and an fp8 KV regime (bh16bn128). This PR connects it. ## Modifications - **`aiter_mla_gluon.py`**: thin wrapper + runtime probe (import + Triton `cga_layout` >= 3.7). Logs once at init; returns None → caller falls back. - **`aiter_backend.py`**: h12 head validation (zero-pad mode), decode routing (`_forward_mla_decode`), graph-safe `min_kv_seq_len`, disable slow 16-head persist for h12+fp8, prefill zero-pad Q for h12. - **`forward_mla_rocm.py`**: keep bf16 Q on prefill when fp8 KV (Gluon needs it). - **`test_mla_gluon_h12_fp8.py`**: CPU tests for probe gating and fallback. Scope is **decode only** (`max_q_len==1`, h12, fp8 KV). Prefill unchanged aside from zero-pad Q routing. h=12 KV write is already on main (#34837). ## Accuracy Tests Validated on MI355, Kimi-K3, --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3, --attention-backend aiter, decode CUDA graph enabled (rocm720-mi35x-20260811 image + aiter fb82bf7e2 (aiter PR 4480 merged)): GSM8K: 95.5–95.6% accuracy ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### long-context test(ISL>50K)(radix cache ON) — primary win With this PR, output token/s/gpu has 94%-168% improvement compares to baseline. signal.title: [Spec] Fail loudly when the DFlash2 selector top_k exceeds the org vocab
signal.text: ## Motivation Depends on #35496 (its commit is included below; review only the second commit). #35496 masks a quantized head's padded vocab tail to `-inf` rather than cropping it, which keeps the logits contiguous but leaves the padded columns in the tensor. A `selector_top_k` wider than the org vocab would then select those columns and return out-of-vocab candidate ids silently, where the dense path raises from `topk`. Nothing validates `selector_top_k` against the vocab today. Unreachable with current checkpoints — `selector_top_k` is a handful of candidates against a vocab of tens of thousands — so this is a guard against a malformed draft config, not a fix for an observed failure. ## Modifications - `models/dflash.py`: assert `num_org >= top_k` in `_project_candidate_logits`, so both the quantized and dense paths fail the same way. Host-side integer compare: free during graph capture, negligible on the eager path. ## Accuracy Tests `test_dflash_logits.py`: 7/7 pass. The new test drives a padded head with `top_k > org_vocab_size` and asserts the `AssertionError`; mutation-verified (removing the assert turns it red). ## Speed Tests and Profiling None; the check is an integer comparison outside the kernel path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32313659722](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313659722)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32313659600](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313659600)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Disable PTX-inline-asm diffusion LayerNorm fast path on ROCm (fix FLUX warmup crash)
signal.text: ## Motivation On ROCm (MI300X gfx942), bringing up **FLUX.1-dev** on the native SGLang diffusion backend crashes during warmup: ``` [aiter] import [module_rmsnorm_quant] ... error: couldn't allocate output register for constraint 'f' ``` The server never becomes ready (`ready to roll` never prints, `/health_generate` = 503). In CI this is `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd*` (`flux_image_t2i`) timing out at the 90-min step limit (e.g. run 31327057626, 08/09; run 31415663809, 08/10). Deterministic and chronic. Root-cause detail in #34351. ## Root cause The diffusion fast-path helpers embed **NVIDIA PTX inline asm** with float-register constraints (`"=f"`) via `tl.inline_asm_elementwise`: - `numerics.py`: `rcp.approx.f32`, `div.rn.f32`, `rsqrt.approx.f32` / `mul.rn.f32` (all `constraints="=f,..."`) - `layernorm_modulate.py` `_rcp4`: `rcp.approx.f32 / fma.rn.f32 / sub.ftz.f32` PTX is CUDA-only; the AMDGPU backend can't allocate the `'f'` constraint, so the Triton JIT aborts at the first warmup forward. These helpers exist to reproduce NVIDIA aten LayerNorm **bit-for-bit** (SASS-level), so porting the PTX would break the documented contract. The module already guarantees *bit-exact-or-eager-fallback* (`torch.equal` gate + `can_use_*`), so the correct AMD behavior is to take the eager path. ## Fix Gate the fused fast paths off on ROCm: `_is_bf16_cuda()` (used by both `can_use_fused_layernorm_modulate` and `can_use_fused_qk_head_layernorm`) now returns `False` when `torch.version.hip is not None`, so ROCm falls back to the eager aten LayerNorm. CUDA behavior is unchanged. ## Test plan (offline, real hardware) - HW: MI300X (gfx942), image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi30x-20260809`. - **Before:** `sglang serve --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev --model-type diffusion --num-gpus 1` → `couldn't allocate output register for constraint 'f'` at warmup, health 503, never ready. - **After (this patch):** warmup completes (1024x1024 native FLUX denoise), **"The server is fired up and ready to roll!"**, `/health_generate` = 200. No `allocate output register` error. - CUDA path untouched (guard is ROCm-only). Fixes #34351 cc @BBuf <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31456475803](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31456475803)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31456475694](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31456475694)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Let the diffusion AITer backend take grouped-query K/V (fix Cosmos3-Nano startup)
signal.text:
## Motivation `cosmos3_nano_t2i` errors during server startup on ROCm, failing `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd*` — see run [31519319449](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31519319449/job/93872280540) (`8f3d3a31`), the "Cosmos3" cluster in [bingxche/sglang-ci-bot#164](https://github.com/bingxche/sglang-ci-bot/issues/164). The reported error is a red herring. The full chain is: ``` NotImplementedError: AITer backend does not support Grouped Query Attention yet. ← Cosmos3CrossAttention → USPAttention(num_heads=32, num_kv_heads=8), aiter being the ROCm default → "Error while loading customized transformer, falling back to native version" → AttributeError: module diffusers has no attribute Cosmos3OmniTransformer → Rank 0 scheduler is dead. Exit code: 1 ``` Only the last line reached the daily report, so this was filed as a CI-image dependency gap. It is not: `Cosmos3OmniTransformer` is an SGLang-native modeling class, so the loader's fallback to `AutoModel.from_pretrained` can never succeed no matter which `diffusers` the image ships. The real blocker is the `NotImplementedError` one frame up. `AITerImpl.__init__` refused any `num_kv_heads != num_heads`, but the backend it wraps has supported GQA for a long time. [`aiter.flash_attn_func`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/6e2052b0/aiter/ops/mha.py) and `flash_attn_varlen_func` both document "Supports multi-query and grouped-query attention (MQA/GQA) by passing in KV with fewer heads than Q. Note that the number of heads in Q must be divisible by the number of heads in KV", and aiter's gfx942/gfx950 ASM fast path admits grouped shapes explicitly (`ret = ret and (nhead_q % nhead_k == 0)`). So the guard was rejecting shapes the backend already handles — and rejecting them at construction time, which is why it surfaced as a load failure rather than a kernel error. Cosmos3's UND self-attention is unaffected either way: it calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., enable_gqa=True)` directly, not through a backend. The same 1-GPU job also fails `flux_image_t2i` for an unrelated reason; that fix is #34481. ## Modifications - Replace the blanket `num_kv_heads != num_heads` rejection in `AITerImpl.__init__` with the divisibility check aiter actually requires, raising `ValueError` (a bad head ratio is a misconfiguration, not an unimplemented feature). - `_can_use_fmha_fp8_prefill` already declines grouped shapes and logs a fallback to BF16, so the FP8 ASM path keeps its MHA-only contract and needs no change. - New `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py` covers MHA (32/32), GQA (32/8), MQA (32/1) and the default `None`, plus the rejected 32/5 ratio. It runs on `multimodal-gen-unit-test-amd*` and `importorskip`s elsewhere, since `aiter` ships with ROCm only. ## Accuracy Tests This only affects shapes that previously raised at construction time, so nothing that works today changes numerically. `cosmos3_nano_t2i` runs with `run_consistency_check=True`, so the 1-GPU AMD lane is itself the accuracy check for the newly reachable GQA cross-attention. There is no AMD GPU in the environment this was written in, so what I verified locally was the constructor logic: with `aiter` and the platform module stubbed out, `AITerImpl` builds for 32/32, 32/8, 32/1 and `None` heads, rejects 32/5 with the message the new test matches, and `_can_use_fmha_fp8_prefill(128, 128, 128, 32, 8)` still returns `False`. The fix needs a real gfx942 run of `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd-rocm720` and `multimodal-gen-unit-test-amd`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No change for shapes that already worked — the guard ran once at construction and never touched the forward path. Cosmos3 cross-attention now reaches aiter's native GQA kernels instead of failing to load, and its KV is the short text/image prefix, so no head expansion or extra copy is introduced. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly
signal.text: ## Motivation Two related changes to AMD nightly Qwen coverage: add the missing Qwen3.8 job, and stop spending runner time on two Qwen jobs that are redundant or dead. **Add Qwen3.8.** [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD Instinct recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. The model reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (the checkpoint reports `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs today with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing currently guards it. A change to the shared Qwen3.5 hybrid path or to the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade Qwen3.8 output quality or throughput on ROCm with no signal. The new job follows the single-node MI355X cell the cookbook publishes ([`hw=mi355x`, `quant=mxfp4`, `strategy=balanced`, `nodes=single`](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8#hw=mi355x&variant=default&quant=mxfp4&strategy=balanced&nodes=single)). **Stop running the Qwen3-235B jobs.** They duplicate `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` coverage that survives elsewhere, including per-commit. ### Why MXFP4 and not the FP8 checkpoint directly At 2.4T parameters FP8 is ~2.4 TB, against 8 x 288 GB = 2.30 TB on an MI355X node, so the FP8 checkpoint has no single-node AMD recipe at all — the cookbook serves it as MI300X TP8 x PP2 across two nodes, and the AMD nightly runners are single-node. Single-node on AMD therefore means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization **of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`** (~1.2 TB, ~150 GB per GPU). Only the routed experts are quantized — attention, the shared expert, the MoE gate and `lm_head` stay at source precision — so AMD measures the same **97.49** GSM8K as the FP8 baseline (100% recovery). The FP8 checkpoint's quality is what this job is gating; MXFP4 is just the packaging that fits one node. ## Modifications ### New: Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x job **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in one file, registered to the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite (`est_time=14400`, `nightly=True`): - `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` — GSM8K few-shot at TP8, gated at 0.93. - `test_b_serving_perf` — serving benchmark over batch sizes 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out, reported through the shared `generate_simple_markdown_report`. Both phases launch from a single `SERVER_ARGS`, which reproduces the recipe published on the AMD model card: ``` --tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --trust-remote-code --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' ``` with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and the eval runs `run_eval` gsm8k over the test split at 512 threads, `max_tokens=2048`, `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`. **Why accuracy and perf share a suite** rather than splitting into `nightly-amd-accuracy-*` and `nightly-perf-*`: sharing one `SERVER_ARGS` means the throughput numbers describe the exact configuration the accuracy gate covers, and a flag change cannot drift one out from under the other. Perf is also skipped unless accuracy passed (`accuracy_passed` class flag, with ordering from unittest's alphabetical method sort): a server that decodes garbage still benchmarks fine, so publishing its throughput would be worse than publishing nothing. Two flags in `SERVER_ARGS` are load-bearing rather than restatements of a default, and are commented as such in the file: - `--page-size 1` — `_page_size_default` bumps the default to 64 on HIP when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, so the measured geometry only holds if the page size is pinned. - `--attention-backend aiter` — no arg override picks a backend for `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM` on ROCm, so the AITER path has to be named. The server deliberately runs with **no `--reasoning-parser`**: the scorer extracts the last number in the reply, so a `<think>` block still scores when reasoning stays in `message.content`. With a reasoning parser on, it would be split into `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty and scoring 0. The model path is overridable via `QWEN38_MXFP4_MODEL_PATH` for hosts with a local copy. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x, and the model card pins ROCm 7.2.0 for MI350/MI355. There is no MI30x counterpart — gfx942 has no hardware MX matmul, and the FP8 checkpoint it would otherwise serve needs two nodes. It is a single step rather than the usual accuracy/perf pair, because both phases live in the same suite. `timeout-minutes: 420` / `--timeout-per-file 21600` budget two loads of the 1.2 TB checkpoint, one per phase, which dominate wall time well before either the eval or the benchmark starts; `ENABLE_CACHE_HOST: "1"` keeps the weights on the runner cache so steady-state nights are far cheaper than the first. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite under `NIGHTLY_SUITES[HWBackend.AMD]`. **`scripts/ci/amd/ensure_hf_cache_space.sh`** (new) — run before the test step. `/sgl-data/hf-cache` is shared by every AMD job on the runner and nothing evicts from it, so a new ~1.2 TB tenant does not fit and the download dies partway through on ENOSPC. This is not a capacity ceiling — Kimi-K3's ~1.5 TB checkpoint completes on the same pool — the cache simply has no eviction, and the problem has been papered over twice by repointing `CACHE_HOST` at a fresh empty directory ([#26642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26642), [#26905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26905)), which frees space by abandoning the old cache rather than managing it. Stale partial downloads were already handled by `scripts/ci/utils/cleanup_hf_cache.py`, which the script delegates to rather than reimplementing — that script is wired into `scripts/ci/cuda/prepare_runner.sh` but nothing on AMD called it before. On top of that it reports free space unconditionally and, when clearing partial downloads is not enough, evicts whole checkpoints least-recently-used first. That last part is the genuinely new behavior: the ENOSPC here was a cache full of *complete* checkpoints, which `cleanup_hf_cache.py` alone does not address. Anything modified in the last 120 minutes is protected so a job sharing the mount cannot have weights deleted mid-load, and the caller names the checkpoint it is about to fetch so it is never the victim. It never fails the job. The reporting alone earns its place: the ENOSPC failure was only diagnosable by reading 8,500 lines of job log, because free space was never printed anywhere. Evicted checkpoints are re-downloaded by whichever job needs them next, so on a cache too small for every large model at once this trades another job's download time for this one running at all — and if Qwen3.8 and Kimi-K3 end up evicting each other nightly, the fleet needs more cache capacity than a script can conjure. ### Removed: the Qwen3-235B nightly jobs Only the workflow jobs go. No file under `test/` is touched — the tests, their launch recipes and their thresholds stay exactly as they are, so re-enabling is re-adding the job, and `run_suite.py --suite nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` still works by hand in the meantime. (Marking the tests `disabled=` was considered and rejected: on top of removing the job it changes no behavior, and it would make that manual re-run silently skip.) **All three Qwen3-235B jobs** — `test_qwen3_instruct.py` (BF16), `test_qwen3_instruct_fp8.py` (FP8) on an 8-GPU mi300 runner, and `test_qwen3_instruct_mxfp4.py` (`amd/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-mxfp4`, TP4 + EP2) on MI35x, across *both* the ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 nightlies. `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is well covered without them: - **Per-commit, on both ROCm lanes**, `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` runs on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` in the `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite, quantizes `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` with `--quantization mxfp4` and asserts `gsm8k >= 0.89`. That suite is dispatched by `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0 container) *and* `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` (`--rocm-version rocm720`), so the MXFP4 MoE kernels for this architecture's shapes are checked on every PR against both ROCm versions, not once a night against one. This is why the removal applies to the ROCm 7.0 nightly as well as 7.2: neither lane is left without a substitute. - **Nightly**, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` runs TP8 in `test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py` and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` runs in the mi30x GSM8K sweep. - Serialized Quark MXFP4 *checkpoint loading* is covered by the Qwen3.8 job added here plus the DeepSeek-R1, GLM-5 and Kimi-K3 nightlies. What loses its substitute is the combination rather than any single ingredient: a pre-quantized Quark checkpoint on `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` at 235B scale over TP4 + EP2. The per-commit test quantizes online at TP1, and expert parallelism survives nightly only through the MiniMax jobs — no Qwen job exercises EP after this. That is the deliberate trade for four 8-GPU jobs per night — two per nightly, each capped at `timeout-minutes: 120`, two on the `linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang` pool and two on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. The jobs removed are `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b[-rocm720]` and `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen3-235b-mxfp4[-rocm720]`, along with their `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` dependencies in each workflow. Their three test files then join the other registered-but-undispatched AMD nightly tests noted below. ### Out of scope After this change, a scan turns up **36 AMD nightly test files** registered but reachable by neither `--suite` nor direct path — the three Qwen3-235B tests above plus 33 pre-existing ones, mostly dormant mi30x and mi35x DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax evals. Those are left untouched here. One is worth calling out for whoever picks that up: `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` is not merely dormant but unrunnable — `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` has no `setup_profile_directory()` and `run_benchmark_for_model` takes no `enable_profile=`, so `test_b_perf` would `AttributeError` on its first line, and its model paths are runner-local `/data/amd/` directories rather than HuggingFace ids. It is deliberately left unmodified by this PR. ## Accuracy Tests **Validation run:** [Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2) #32313140175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313140175), dispatched on this branch's head with `job_select: nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720`, covering both phases. Two earlier dispatches informed the current state. [#32185767315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32185767315) predated the perf phase and was cancelled. [#32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) got everything right up to the weight download and then died on ENOSPC in the shared runner cache, which is what the `ensure_hf_cache_space.sh` step above exists to prevent. Between them they did confirm the wiring: job selection resolves to this job alone with the rest skipped, no `qwen3-235b` job exists at these SHAs, and `run_suite.py --suite nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` discovers the test rather than reporting an empty suite after the rename. Expect a long run regardless: both nightlies fire at `30 17 * * *` and drain the same `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` pool, so a manual dispatch queues behind their MI35x backlog, and the 1.2 TB fetch dominates once it starts. The gate is `ACCURACY_THRESHOLD = 0.93`, ~5% below AMD's published 0.9749 — the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.yaml` uses `rtol: 0.05` against 0.9704, i.e. a 0.922 floor). The threshold is inherited from AMD's measurement rather than from a run on the CI fleet, so if the dispatch lands materially off 0.9749 on the CI image, the number should be recalibrated to the observed run the way the Kimi-K3 job was. No model or kernel code is touched by this PR, so there is no output-affecting change to validate beyond the job itself. Static checks, run locally without GPUs: both workflows parse and every `check-all-jobs` dependency resolves to a defined job, with no `job_select` option pointing at a removed one; the AST registry parser resolves the new file to `backend=AMD, suite='nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4', nightly=True, est_time=14400` and no file under `test/` other than the new one differs from `main`; the suite string matches across all three files with no stale references to the pre-rename name; and every symbol the new test imports exists in its source module. `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_workflow_job_names.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, isort, black, ruff and codespell all pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The perf phase is the speed coverage this PR adds; it publishes a latency / input-throughput / output-throughput / ITL table to the job summary rather than asserting a threshold, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Batch sizes and sequence lengths are overridable through the usual `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS` environment variables. Net runner impact: one new MI35x job added, four 8-GPU jobs removed (two per nightly, split across the mi300 and mi35x pools). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe; no doc change needed. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
