signal.author: wenkaidu

signal.title: Publish per-scheduler load on a dedicated socket for load-aware routers
signal.text: ## Motivation The cache-aware-zmq router infers a worker's load from a router-side in-flight counter. That counter measures what *this router* dispatched — it misses traffic from other routers and direct clients, and for streaming responses it stays held for the whole response rather than the time the request occupies the scheduler. The engine already builds the right number: `SchedulerLoadInquirer.get_loads()` produces a `LoadSnapshot` every publish cycle (feeding `/v1/loads` and DP-attention dispatch). This exposes that snapshot to out-of-process consumers so a router can price workers on real queue depth / KV occupancy. Ported to `main` from a production branch; the router-side consumer lands separately. ## Modifications **A dedicated per-scheduler load PUB socket.** `SchedulerLoadPublisher` publishes a compact `LoadStat` gauge (`num_running_reqs`, `num_waiting_reqs`, `num_tokens`, `max_total_num_tokens`) on its own ZMQ PUB socket, independent of KV-cache events. The payload is a tagged subset of `LoadSnapshot` so the router-facing wire contract stays fixed as the internal snapshot grows. Framing matches the KV-event socket (`[b"load", big-endian i64 seq, msgpack LoadStat]`) so one subscriber loop handles both. Transport is a plain synchronous PUB socket — a send just enqueues to ZMQ's IO thread — so there is no background thread or replay buffer, which a gauge does not need. **One resolver for the port, shared by the bind and the advertisement.** `resolve_load_pub_range` decides where the load range lives and returns `((host, base), reason)`. Both `SchedulerLoadPublisher` (which binds `base + rank`) and `/server_info`'s `describe_kv_events_publisher` (which advertises `base` under the `kv_events` block, plus `load_topic`) route through it, so the engine cannot advertise a range it will not bind. With auto, the range packs immediately after the KV-event range, bumping past the replay ROUTER range when the two overlap (with the conventional `replay = kv + 1`, always). **Opt-in via `--load-publish-endpoint` (observability namespace).** **Off by default** — unset (or `off`) reserves no port, so an upgrade of an existing `--kv-events-config` deployment can't collide with a co-hosted neighbor's KV bind. `auto` packs the range after the KV-event range; an explicit wildcard-host `tcp://` address places it outright (a concrete host would be *connected to*, not bound). Also requires `--kv-events-config`, since routers discover the base through `/server_info`. **Cadence.** When enabled, publishing is throttled by call count, and an unchanged gauge is deduped to a ~1s heartbeat while a changed one goes out immediately (transitions are never delayed). When the DP-balancing sink also published this cycle, the scheduler hands its already-computed snapshot to the load publisher rather than walking the queues again. When disabled (the default), the publisher holds no socket or thread and each call is a bound method plus a `None` check. **Load also publishes on stalled no-batch iterations.** `on_idle` now publishes before its fully-idle gate — a stall (queues parked under KV pressure / disagg transfer) has no `process_batch_result` to publish the growing gauge. That path spins without sleeping, so a ~50ms wall-clock floor bounds the `get_loads()` refresh for both the DP-balancing writer and the load socket; the fully-idle publish stays at its original post-flush position so the idle gauge reflects compacted KV. **Failure handling is best-effort.** A publish failure never crashes the loop (routers fall back to their own counter) and is logged once per failure episode (the publish path runs every scheduler loop, so it must not flood). **Startup validation.** `--load-publish-endpoint` set without a `--kv-events-config` publisher, not bindable, or overlapping the KV range fails at the entrypoint (`check_load_publish_args`) rather than only warning from a scheduler subprocess. ## Notes for reviewers - **Breaking change to an override point** (per `large-class-init-style` rule 28): `Scheduler.publish_load_snapshot` now returns the `LoadSnapshot` it published (previously nothing); both call sites feed it to the router-facing publisher to avoid a second queue walk. A downstream override returning `None` stays functionally correct — the publisher falls back to `load_inquirer.get_loads` at its own throttled cadence — but silently loses the shared-snapshot optimization. Return the snapshot you wrote to keep it. - **Intentional user-visible change:** endpoint parsing is now strict (`NetworkAddress.parse`), so a bare unbracketed IPv6 kv endpoint (`tcp://::1:5557`) drops the whole `kv_events` block from `/server_info`, where the old `rfind(":")` split advertised it unusably. - **Port footprint (opt-in only):** with `--load-publish-endpoint auto`, a worker reserves `2 * dp_size` ports from its KV base (`2 * dp_size + 1` with the conventional adjacent replay). Co-hosted workers must space their KV bases at least that far apart, or place the range with an explicit address. This is why it's opt-in rather than default-on — see the server-arguments table. - **Inherited limit:** with DP-attention across `nnodes > 1`, the single advertised base is paired with one worker-URL host, so ranks on other nodes aren't reachable at that host — same constraint as the existing KV-event discovery, noted in the resolver docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model execution or output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No benchmark run. The disabled path (default) is a bound-method call plus a `None` check per batch — no socket, no thread. When enabled, the load socket reuses the DP-balancing snapshot whenever that sink also published this cycle (otherwise it collects its own on the same call throttle), and a stalled no-batch loop is bounded to one `get_loads()` per ~50ms for both sinks. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format Code](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html) guide. - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Test Guide](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html). - [ ] Update documentation as needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32274220697](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274220697)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32274220217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274220217)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors kv_cache_scheme scales
signal.text: ## Motivation compressed-tensors checkpoints that declare a `kv_cache_scheme` ship calibrated per-tensor attention `k_scale` / `v_scale` tensors, but they are silently dropped at load (`Parameter model.layers.N.k_scale not found in params_dict`), so `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` runs the cache unscaled. Three gaps compound: - `CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config` never forwarded `kv_cache_scheme`, leaving it `None` even when declared. - `get_quant_method` had no `RadixAttention` branch, so the `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters were never created (ModelOpt has `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` for this; the compressed-tensors equivalent was missing). - The qwen3_5 weight mapper only knew the ModelOpt-style `.k_proj.k_scale` serialization; compressed-tensors stores the scales on the attention module (`.self_attn.k_scale`). ## Modifications - Forward `kv_cache_scheme` in `from_config`. - New `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod(BaseKVCacheMethod)`, returned for `RadixAttention` when a `kv_cache_scheme` is declared. It accepts only what `BaseKVCacheMethod` can represent — static, symmetric, per-tensor FP8. A declared-but-unsupported scheme is skipped with a warning instead of failing the boot: such checkpoints serve correctly with an unquantized-scale KV cache, so refusing to load them would regress working deployments. - A `kv_cache_quant_algo` property on the config: `configure_kv_cache_dtype` duck-types this field to resolve `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, so a declared supported scheme gets the fp8 pool its scales calibrate (ModelOpt parity). Without this, an auto-resolved bf16 pool would store unscaled entries while the attention backends apply the loaded scales on read. - Two `orig_to_new_substr` entries in `QWEN3_5_KV_SCALE_MAPPER` for the attention-level scale names, and the mapper applied in the Qwen3.5 MTP loader for symmetry. - Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_kv_cache.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`). - The pre-existing `kv_cache_scheme` remap in `apply_weight_name_mapper` (dead until this PR forwarded the scheme) is removed: the scheme holds schema fields, never module names, and `apply_dict` drops keys that match a mapper deletion rule. Checkpoints without a `kv_cache_scheme` are unaffected (`get_quant_method` returns `None` for `RadixAttention` as before), and unloaded scales keep the existing default-to-1.0 behavior in `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading`. ## Accuracy Tests RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint with a declared FP8 `kv_cache_scheme`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`: - Before: 32 `k_scale`/`v_scale` drop warnings at load; GSM8K 0.960 (cache unscaled — accuracy-benign on this checkpoint because the calibrated scales are near 1, but incorrect). - After: zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.965, invalid 0.000. Parity within the script's documented variance — this is a correctness fix for the calibration path, not an accuracy rescue. - With `--kv-cache-dtype` left as `auto`: the pool now auto-resolves to `float8_e4m3fn` (previously bf16, ignoring the checkpoint's declared KV calibration); zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.940 / 0.960 across two runs — statistically identical to the explicit-fp8 lane, as expected since both resolve to the same pool and scales. Note: an MTP draft loaded from the same checkpoint carries the same config, so the draft worker's pool auto-resolves to fp8 as well (its scales default to 1.0; write/read stay symmetric). A standalone bf16 draft export without a `quantization_config` keeps a bf16 pool. Known limit: an explicit bf16 `--kv-cache-dtype` override on a checkpoint with declared scales attaches scales to an unquantized pool — the same pre-existing exposure ModelOpt has today; a shared fix belongs in `BaseKVCacheMethod`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No runtime impact: scale resolution happens once at init; the scales feed the existing fp8 KV cache path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(moe): handle bf16 DeepEP low_latency dispatch (a_scales=None) in cutlass W4A8
signal.text: ### Problem `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_ll()` unconditionally calls `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton(x_scale=a_scales, ...)`. Under DeepEP **low_latency**, the cutlass W4A8 backend dispatches in **bf16** (its default; also forced by `--deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype bf16`), so the dispatch returns bf16 tokens with **no per-token fp8 scales** — `a_scales is None`. The unconditional call then dereferences `None`: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size' ``` at decode cuda-graph capture → scheduler dies (exit -3). Hit on Kimi-K3-W4AFP8 with `--deepep-mode auto` (normal prefill + low_latency decode), cuda-graph ON. ### Fix When `a_scales is None`, quantize the bf16 masked tokens to per-tensor fp8 in-place with the static input scale via `per_tensor_quant_fp8(...)` — byte-for-byte the same quantization `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal()` already applies to its bf16 input. Forcing fp8 dispatch instead is not a general fix: the per-token triton kernel asserts `hidden % 1024 == 0`, which fails for models whose routed-expert hidden size isn't 1024-divisible (e.g. Kimi-K3 = 3584). ### Validation mini-K3 (2 nodes, EP16, `--deepep-mode auto`, cuda-graph ON) passes decode capture and serves completions without the crash. Draft pending upstream CI + a full multi-node run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190125293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125293)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190125037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125037)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] vae: fix silently ignored --vae-tiling for Sana (AutoencoderDC)
signal.text: ### Motivation Fixes #34482. `--vae-tiling` was silently ignored for Sana models: the `AutoencoderDC` wrapper does not proxy `enable_tiling` to the inner diffusers model, so the call raised `AttributeError`, which (at the time this PR was opened) was swallowed by a bare `except` in `DecodingStage`. On 8GB GPUs this turns a would-be-successful generation into a fatal OOM after the full denoising loop has already run. See the issue for the root-cause chain. ### Modifications - `runtime/models/vaes/autoencoder_dc.py`: proxy `enable_tiling` / `disable_tiling` to the inner diffusers `AutoencoderDC`, which already implements them. `enable_tiling` is a no-op (with `warning_once`) when spatial-shard parallel decode is installed on this wrapper, since diffusers' `tiled_decode` running per-rank inside a height-sharded decoder breaks the halo exchange (mismatched collective rounds / wrong neighbours). - `configs/models/vaes/sana.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py`: update the two comments that claimed DC-AE tiling is unsupported. - `test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py`: CPU-only unit test asserting the proxy forwards to the inner model and that the spatial-shard guard is a no-op. ### Scope / decisions - **Default unchanged.** `SanaPipelineConfig.vae_tiling` stays `False`; tiling is opt-in via `--vae-tiling`. DC-AE is a 32x-compression autoencoder and tile seam quality / the benefit of diffusers' default 512 tile have not been validated, so a default flip does not belong in a bugfix. - **`decoding.py` is no longer touched.** The v1 of this PR also replaced the bare `except` around `enable_tiling()` with a warning; main has since fixed that call site independently (specific `AttributeError` handling + warning), so that change is dropped here and the PR is now purely the wrapper-side fix. ### Test / Verification - Before: `sglang generate --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers --prompt "..." --save-output --vae-tiling` — fatal OOM in `DecodingStage` on RTX 4070 Laptop 8GB (3/3 runs). Note: with DC-AE's 32x compression, tiling only engages at ≥1024x1024 (512x512 gives a 16x16 latent == `tile_latent_min`). - After: same command (1024x1024) succeeds end-to-end; output image correct. This PR changes correctness (OOM → success), not performance; timings are not reported. - `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py` passes. - pre-commit clean.

signal.title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors quantized lm_head instead of value-casting it
signal.text: ## Motivation compressed-tensors checkpoints that quantize `lm_head` (e.g. FP8 per-channel weights targeted via `re:.*lm_head`) currently load as gibberish: `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` returns `None` for `ParallelLMHead`, so the head falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` — the packed fp8 weight is value-cast into a bf16 parameter and `lm_head.weight_scale` is silently dropped (`Parameter lm_head.weight_scale not found in params_dict` at load). ## Modifications - `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method`: add a `ParallelLMHead` branch that resolves a linear scheme and returns `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod` (mirroring the existing ModelOpt handling); unquantized heads keep the current embedding default. - New `get_lm_head_scheme`: the head is treated as quantized only when a config target names it by layer name (exact, `re:` regex, or dotted suffix) and it is not in `ignore`. Module-type targets like `Linear` are not consulted, so checkpoints following the common convention (head unquantized and unmentioned) are unaffected. The resolved target is passed through to `get_scheme_dict` so suffix matches are not re-derived by the stricter `find_matched_target`. Block-FP8 heads are rejected with a clear error (the vocab-parallel weight loader cannot shard `vocab/block_n` weight scales). - Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_lm_head.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`). No other changes needed: the vocab-parallel weight loader already shards `output_dim=0` params, the model loader already runs `process_weights_after_loading` on the head, and the logits path already routes through `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method`. Known limits: models that construct `ParallelLMHead` without a `prefix` keep today's unquantized-head behavior (the empty layer name never matches a target); `update_weights_from_disk` with a quantized head is untested; speculative-decoding draft paths that borrow the target head are a separate follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests A/B on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with a Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint (NVFP4 MLPs, FP8 per-channel `lm_head`), identical flags, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`: | | GSM8K | Invalid | |---|---|---| | main | 0.000 | 0.850 | | this PR | 0.955 | 0.000 | On main, greedy decoding degenerates into repetition loops on any prompt; with this PR the head loads through `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` and the `weight_scale` warning is gone. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No impact on unquantized-head checkpoints (resolution happens once at init). A quantized head replaces a bf16 matmul with the standard fp8 linear path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(constrained): reject NUL bytes in grammar specs to stop an xgrammar segfault
signal.text: ## Motivations A `regex` beginning with a NUL byte kills the server. xgrammar's regex converter appends its own NUL terminator and indexes past it, raising **SIGSEGV** — an OS signal, so the `except RuntimeError` in `dispatch_regex` cannot catch it. The scheduler dies with `exit code -11` and all later requests are refused. ```python python3 -c 'import xgrammar; xgrammar.Grammar.from_regex(chr(0))' # SIGSEGV ``` Two measured details: - Trigger is a **leading** NUL, not control characters generally — `\x01`, `\x02`, `\x1f` and non-leading NUL all compile fine. Rejecting all control characters would break valid patterns like `[\t\n]+`. - A **JSON schema reaches the same converter via `pattern`**, where the NUL may be an escape (`\u0000`) — no NUL byte in the request body at all. Guarding only `regex` leaves that path open. No release fixes it: 0.2.0-0.2.4 and 0.2.6rc1 all crash on the `regex` path (`regex_converter.cc` is unchanged v0.2.5 through HEAD). ## Modifications - `base_grammar_backend.py`: `_grammar_key_contains_nul()`, called at the top of `_init_value_dispatch` — the choke point for all four grammar types and every backend. Returns `InvalidGrammarObject`, which flows through the existing failure path to the same clean error an invalid pattern already gets. For `json`/`structural_tag` the spec is decoded and walked, so an escaped `\u0000` in a nested `pattern` is caught; malformed JSON falls through to the backend's own error. Placed at the dispatcher, not `xgrammar_backend.py`, because the JSON path reaches the same native code and a segfault cannot be caught after the fact. - `test_base_grammar_backend.py`: `TestNulByteGrammarRejection` — NUL specs rejected without the backend being called (`regex` and JSON `pattern`, raw and escaped, plus a non-leading NUL so the guard can't be narrowed to `startswith()`); valid patterns, non-NUL control characters and malformed JSON still dispatch normally. A NUL has no meaning in a regex, schema or grammar, so no legitimate request is affected. Verified on aarch64/GB200: the file passes **33 tests / 17 subtests** with no regressions; the new cases fail 8/8 without the guard; on a live server the two crashing payloads go from killing the process to **HTTP 400**, `/health` 200, no segfault markers. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no change to kernels or the model forward path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — one substring check per uncached grammar compilation (for JSON, a parse the backend already performs). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing API change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32308365762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32308365762)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32308365506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32308365506)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [SM12x] Add b12x MoE runner backend for DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on GB10
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4's MXFP4 experts (`fp4_e8m0_k32`) have no fused MoE path on the SM12x family (GB10 / DGX Spark, RTX PRO 6000 class). This PR adds an opt-in `--moe-runner-backend b12x` that maps them onto the b12x W4A16 fused MoE kernels, making DeepSeek-V4-Flash practical to serve on 2x DGX Spark. ## Modifications - **Exactly one supported b12x generation: 0.15.3** (`b12x.integration.tp_moe`) — the generation the reference dspark deployment ships and the one every number below was measured on. Later generations changed the W4A16 kernels behind the same API (0.20.0) and then replaced the API (1.2.x); they are **rejected at startup** with an install hint, rather than silently producing different numerics. - 0.15.3 was never published to PyPI. It installs from the source commit whose MoE surface matches the released wheel: ``` pip install --no-deps "b12x @ https://github.com/local-inference-lab/b12x/archive/7dc6fb8fcc6446ea093537d1657df81985fa5f43.tar.gz" ``` (`--no-deps`: b12x's metadata pulls a newer torch.) At startup the backend verifies the installed dist-info version is exactly 0.15.3 and fails with this install hint otherwise. - **`mxfp4_b12x_moe.py`** (new): `Mxfp4B12xMoEMethod` — weight prep hands the checkpoint tensors to b12x **in place** (E8M0 scales consumed natively; `reuse_input_storage=True`, so the Parameters stay live and are kept referenced), a frozen scratch plan built from the layer shapes, and a bind-and-run closure matching vLLM's call sequence. - **Warmup ladder**: b12x refuses to compile kernels during CUDA graph capture and falls back to a pinned tile config that does not fit every block size, so every token count a captured graph can present is compiled eagerly first (decode `bs x spec_window` plus a power-of-two ladder for chunked prefill, sized by `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS`). - **`moe_runner/b12x.py`** (new): fused-path runner registration; the quant info carries only the prepared launch closure and an EP guard (with expert parallelism the dispatcher rewrites non-local experts to -1, which b12x would run as garbage rather than skip). - **`mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py`**: register the new method in the `routed_scaling_factor` whitelist (it is silently dropped otherwise, compressing the whole MoE block by the scaling factor). - Env knobs registered in `environ.py` per conventions: `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS` (sizes the scratch arena; must cover `--chunked-prefill-size`), `SGLANG_B12X_WARMUP` (default on; off only defers compilation -- captured decode shapes are still compiled by the graph runner's pre-capture warmup, the prefill ladder then JIT-compiles on the first chunks), and `SGLANG_B12X_CACHE_DIR` (tracks `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`; forwarded to b12x's `B12X_CUTE_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR`, same pattern as `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`). ## Validation 2x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2 cross-node, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with DSPARK speculative decoding (`gamma=5`), chunked prefill 4096: | Metric | Result | |---|---| | GSM8K 1319q (few-shot, parallel 8) | accuracy **0.945**, invalid 0 | | decode (8k ctx, bs=1) | 73-77 ms/step, accept-length 5.4-5.9 | | prefill 30k input | ~1.9k tok/s input throughput | Also boots and passes GSM8K (200q sampled: 0.960) on current main. ## Notes An earlier revision carried dual-generation support (0.15.3 + 1.2.x behind one method). It was dropped once the 0.15.3 source commit was identified: the 1.2.x W4A16 kernel measured ~19% slower per call at the decode working point on this shape (`cute.Tensor` static strides became runtime-rebuilt `cute.Pointer` layouts), and carrying two calling conventions doubled the surface of a backend that only has hardware-attested coverage. Single generation, hard-rejected otherwise, keeps the numerics story exact. Related: #34018 (FP8 wo_a GEMM on sm12x) is complementary and kept separate on purpose. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32309145516](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309145516)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32309145385](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309145385)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] ci: cache the CI image on mi30x runners instead of re-pulling it every job
signal.text:
## Motivation Every AMD CI job re-acquires the `rocm/sgl-dev` image from scratch, and the setup that precedes it re-fetches the whole git remote. On the [nightly CI dashboard](https://michaelzhang-ai.github.io/sglang-ci/nightly-ci/) this is the container-start step, and it dominates the wall clock of the AMD nightlies. Measured on the Aug 10 scheduled runs ([Nightly Test (AMD)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31415730698), [ROCm 7.2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31415528605)), summing that step across the 90 container jobs: | Phase | Nightly (AMD) | Nightly ROCm 7.2 | |---|---|---| | container-start total | 23.1 GPU-machine-hours | 25.6 GPU-machine-hours | | ⤷ `git fetch --tags origin` | 13.7 h (p50 4.6 min, p90 54 min, max 64 min) | 12.9 h (p50 0.6 min, p90 57 min, max 62 min) | | ⤷ `docker pull` from Docker Hub | 9.2 h (p50 3.7 min, p90 26 min, max 60 min) | 12.5 h (p50 4.2 min, p90 59 min, max 70 min) | That is ~49 GPU-machine-hours of setup per night before a single test runs, and the p50/p90 spread shows most of it is contention: ~90 jobs hitting github.com and Docker Hub for the same objects at the same time. The runners are docker-in-docker with **ephemeral** storage, and each AMD job starts the container exactly once, so an image pulled by one job is gone before the next begins. That is why all 89 sampled jobs pulled the full ~23 GB image, and why no in-daemon cache logic can help. The only thing that survives between jobs is the volume already mounted at `/home/runner/sglang-data` — and it is genuinely shared and persistent, which I verified rather than assumed: an 8-GPU mi35x DeepSeek job loads its weights from there with zero `Downloading` lines, which is only possible if hundreds of GB of HF cache survived from earlier jobs on other pods. ## Modifications Scope: `scripts/ci/amd/` only, plus one CPU-registered unit test. The nightly release workflows are untouched — the image keeps being published to Docker Hub exactly as today. `amd_ci_start_container_disagg.sh` is untouched too, since it only serves the mi35x-fabric disaggregation job. `scripts/release/get_version_tag.py` is deliberately untouched, since setuptools-scm runs it for every pyproject (CUDA, CPU, NPU, XPU) and the PyPI release workflows shell out to it, so no non-AMD wheel version can move. **Cache the pulled image as a tarball on the persistent volume.** New `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_image_cache.sh`. The first job to miss pulls from Docker Hub and seeds a tarball under `/home/runner/sglang-data/docker-images`; every later job on that volume `docker load`s it instead. This works on mi35x as well as mi30x, which the in-network registry does not. Storage pressure on that volume is exactly what shelved the previous attempt at cache seeding, and what [#26642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26642) had to move the path for, so every operation is best-effort and bounded. A cache that is full, slow, locked or corrupt falls back to pulling and never fails a test job. Specifically it: - seeds under an `mkdir` lock, so dozens of simultaneous jobs cannot all stream tens of GB at once; - writes to a temp path and renames, so a reader never observes a partial tarball; - refuses to seed below 120 GB free (`AMD_CI_IMAGE_CACHE_MIN_FREE_GB`); - prunes tarballs older than a day (`AMD_CI_IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS`), which loses nothing since the tags are date-stamped; - prefers `zstd` so a tarball stays near the image's 23.4 GB compressed size rather than its larger on-disk size, falling back to uncompressed when `zstd` is absent; - verifies the image is actually in the store after a load, and falls through to a pull if not; - is switched off entirely by `AMD_CI_IMAGE_TARBALL_CACHE=0`. **`ls-remote` instead of a full tag fetch.** New `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_latest_release_tag.py` lists tags with `git ls-remote --tags --refs` — refs only, no objects — and falls back to the local ref store when the remote is unreachable. It imports `parse_version_tuple` from the shared helper rather than reimplementing the ordering, so the tag it picks is the one the nightly release workflow published the image under, with stable/post above rc ([#23644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23644)). **Only probe the in-network registry on mi30x.** Probes from every `linux-mi35x-*` pool time out after a flat 15s, while all four MI300 pools answer in ~0s (numbers below). The existing mirror preference is otherwise unchanged; it is simply skipped where it cannot possibly work. `AMD_CI_DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIRROR` overrides either way, so retargeting or disabling it is a variable change rather than a code change. **One log line per job for the dashboard.** The container-start step reported a single duration that mixed both costs, which is why it took log scraping to find the split above. The script now emits: ``` [amd-ci-setup] image=rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi30x-20260819 source=local-tarball version_resolve=1s image_acquire=41s ``` `source` is one of `local-tarball`, `registry-mirror`, `docker-hub`, `custom-image` or `dockerfile-build`, so cache hit rate becomes directly measurable rather than inferred. **Unit test.** `test/registered/unit/tools/test_amd_ci_latest_release_tag.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`, no GPU) pins what the image tag depends on: `ls-remote` keeps the lookup from transferring objects, `--refs` keeps annotated tags from also yielding peeled `^{}` entries, ordering matches the shared release helper, an unreachable remote falls back to local tags, and a failed `git` call is reported without being fatal. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — CI plumbing only, no changes to model or kernel code. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Run: **https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32298963203** (ROCm 7.2 AMD, head `e918de13f3`, in flight). An earlier CI run on this branch ([31636206736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31636206736), 22 container starts) A/B'd against 22 runs of the same workflow on other branches, before the tarball cache existed: | Phase (per job, median) | Without change | With change | |---|---|---| | Tag lookup | 136s (mean 149s, max 371s) | **1s** (mean 1s, max 2s) | | Image pull | 374s | 468s (runner/network variance; identical code path on a miss) | | Whole container-start step | 550s | 472s | The tag lookup is confirmed on real hardware: 136s to 1s, about 50 minutes of runner time saved on a single 22-job run. The nightlies stand to gain more, since the fetch cost scales with concurrency and a nightly is 43–47 jobs rather than 22. The tarball cache has **not** been measured on real hardware yet, and one run cannot do it: the first AMD job against a given volume and tag is always a seed (`source=docker-hub` plus a `Seeding image tarball cache` line), and the hit shows up on the second. Its payoff then depends on the volume's read throughput, which I cannot measure from CI logs — a load has to beat a 210s (mi35x) to 430s (mi30x) Docker Hub pull. The instrumentation makes that self-evident from the first hit: `source=local-tarball` with a small `image_acquire` means it is winning, and if it is not, `AMD_CI_IMAGE_TARBALL_CACHE=0` turns it off without a revert. Verified locally with stubbed `docker`, `hostname` and `df`: - Cold mi30x job pulls from Docker Hub and seeds the tarball; the next job on the same volume loads it and issues **no pull at all**, reporting `source=local-tarball`. - mi35x uses the same mechanism and skips the registry probe entirely. - Guards each exercised: a held lock yields "Another job is seeding"; 10 GB free yields "Not seeding"; a missing tarball reports a miss and falls through; a 5-day-old tarball is pruned; `AMD_CI_IMAGE_TARBALL_CACHE=0` disables the cache. - `amd_ci_latest_release_tag.py` resolves the same `v0.5.17` in 0.55s; 16/16 unit tests pass, including the four pre-existing `test_get_version_tag.py` cases; `pre-commit` clean; `bash -n` clean on all three scripts. One side effect checked rather than assumed: dropping `git fetch --tags origin` does not change the version the editable install gets. It is already `sglang-0.0.0.dev1+g955aab8db.d20260810` **with** the fetch in place, because a depth-1 `actions/checkout` HEAD cannot `git describe` from a tag even once tags are present. ## Why not the in-network registry Worth recording, since it is the obvious alternative and the reason this went to the volume instead. Sampling 60 MI300 jobs across Aug 6–19, every probe of `10.44.14.109:5000` that ran came back `manifest unknown` — a real registry 404, so the host is up and the daemon negotiates plain HTTP fine. But no MI35x pool can reach it at all: | Pool | Reached registry | Failed to reach | |---|---|---| | `linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang` | 9 | 0 | | `linux-mi300-2gpu-sglang` | 7 | 0 | | `linux-mi300-4gpu-sglang` | 2 | 0 | | `linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang` | 24 | 0 | | `linux-mi35x-gpu-1/2/8` | **0** | **22** (`context deadline exceeded`, 15s each) | The nightlies are roughly 40 MI300 jobs against 50 MI35x, so the registry could only ever serve a bit under half the fleet, and it has been empty since [#31436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31436) disabled the job that populated it. The persistent volume covers both halves and needs no release-workflow change, which is why the cache lives there. If the mi35x route to the registry is ever opened, `AMD_CI_DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIRROR` makes using it a variable change. For the record on the July failure: `push_local_registry` died with `server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client`, i.e. the mirror missing from `insecure-registries` on the pool that ran it, not the host being down. That no longer reproduces on MI300. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — `--help` for `amd_ci_start_container.sh` and the header of `amd_ci_image_cache.sh` document the new env vars; no user-facing docs affected. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix min-new-token EOS handling
signal.text: ## Summary - include model-config EOS token IDs in the minimum-new-token penalty mask - ignore missing tokenizer EOS metadata when constructing stop-token tensors - cover model-config EOS handling when tokenizer EOS is absent ## Motivation Requests can carry valid EOS IDs from the model configuration even when the tokenizer does not expose an EOS ID. The minimum-new-token penalizer omitted those IDs and attempted to convert `None` into an integer tensor, crashing batch preparation. signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Fix MXFP8 activation preparation for the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend on SM107. GPT-OSS on SM107 can reach the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernel without a pre-quantized route handoff. Previously, SGLang used the Triton per-token-group quantizer in this case. This does not reliably produce the activation representation expected by the FlashInfer SM107 path. The quantizer producing the activations must follow the same MXFP8 and UE8M0 layout contract as the FlashInfer MoE kernel consuming them. Using FlashInfer for both operations on SM107 avoids the incompatible producer/consumer path. The fake custom-op implementation also needs the real scale-buffer shape. Returning a placeholder one-element tensor can produce incorrect metadata during `torch.compile`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantizer on SM107 when no route/quant handoff is available. - signal.title: [VLM] Reuse Kimi-K3 embeddings before normal-serving preprocessing
signal.text: ## Summary This PR is now limited to **ordinary serving**. EPD reuse is split into #35033; metrics and the agentic benchmark harness are split into #35034. - acquires per-image embedding-cache leases on the request final DP route before processor dispatch - omits a feature only when every required TP rank has pinned the same full feature identity - transfers lease ownership to the admitted request; consume, cancel, abort, flush, timeout, and one internal cold-path retry release pins safely - lets repeated Kimi-K3 images skip processor work, feature transport, and ViT in ordinary serving - keeps CPU, CUDA IPC, and CUDA VMM paths compatible; a featureless hit does not allocate an IPC/VMM proxy or a new fixed HBM pool - uses typed processor contracts rather than model-name branches or dynamic attribute probing - adds the canonical VLM preprocessing-cache guide, API examples, model-support guidance, server arguments, and a concise K3 Cookbook reference ## Correctness boundary False hits fail closed under the default configuration: - media identity covers the exact bytes plus modality, processor configuration, backend, and per-image preprocess options - the artifact identity is bound to the processor-output hash; the compact embedding key only selects a candidate and the full feature identity must still match - K3 namespaces Radix prefix KV by ordered full feature identities, so legacy 30-bit pad-sentinel collisions cannot share language-model KV - mutable paths and URLs are re-read and re-hashed; same path with changed bytes misses - partial TP hits, expired leases, and lost leases fall back once to the feature-carrying cold path - feature-hash disagreement clears the stale processor artifact and rejects reuse - caller-provided legacy `mm_hashes` cannot redirect artifact, lease, embedding-cache, or Radix identity `--trust-mm-content-hashes` is the explicit exception: a trusted hot hit can skip reading the media source, so correctness is delegated to the caller. Without it, SGLang reads the actual media bytes, verifies a supplied SHA-256 digest, and rejects mismatches. ## Normal-serving performance Full real-weight Kimi-K3 (1.56 TB), 2 nodes × 4 NVIDIA GB300, TP8, commit `25eae3c909d7`. Each cell is the median of 3 runs over 32 conversations × 8 turns. The same seeded random image set (512²–2048²) is resent on every turn. Both sides use the same 4096 MiB lazy embedding-cache cap and automatic CUDA VMM/FABRIC feature transport; the A/B switch is K3 auto versus `--mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb 0`. Four random images, concurrency 32, 16 output tokens: | Request rate | Output tok/s off → on | Median TTFT off → on | Median E2E off → on | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 53.29 → 100.14 (+87.9%) | 5846 → 1122 ms (-80.8%) | 6364 → 1479 ms (-76.8%) | | 4 | 53.83 → 109.46 (+103.3%) | 6128 → 1148 ms (-81.3%) | 6721 → 1482 ms (-78.0%) | | 8 | 55.53 → 107.57 (+93.7%) | 5830 → 1174 ms (-79.9%) | 6294 → 1502 ms (-76.1%) | | inf | 54.33 → 106.05 (+95.2%) | 5973 → 1133 ms (-81.0%) | 6366 → 1479 ms (-76.8%) | The saturated A/B was repeated on the same nodes: duration fell from 75.39 s to 38.62 s, and median hot-turn TTFT fell from 5956 to 1147 ms. Across 896 hot images, processor calls, feature transport, and ViT forwards were all skipped. Aggregate preprocess-stage time fell from 194.28 s to 24.56 s (-87.4%). The CPU cache held 128 entries / 62,692 bytes with no eviction. Peak HBM was 257,304 MiB cache-on versus 265,202 MiB cache-off; this feature adds no fixed HBM reservation. These numbers establish the cache A/B, not best absolute production throughput: both sides pinned Marlin because the environment automatic TRT-LLM Gen SiTU path hung after one run. ## Validation - changed Python files compile; changed-file pre-commit, registered-test validation, and documentation checks pass - focused tests cover media mutation, cross-input-form identity, processor/backend/config changes, tensor/PIL metadata, duplicates, reordering, partial hits, single-flight, lease pin/timeout/cancel/flush, partial TP hits, retry, and Radix/pad collisions - full-real-weight 2-node GB300 validation passed 11 ordinary-serving identity cases with zero request errors and matching cold/hot prompt/output tokens, finish reasons, and usage - local macOS pytest collection is blocked by an older Transformers package (`transformers.image_processing_backends` is unavailable); the new Linux CI head runs the focused unit suite ## Stack 1. #34398 — media identity, API, bounded LRU, and single-flight infrastructure 2. #34404 — typed K3 per-image artifacts 3. this PR — ordinary-serving scheduler lease and embedding reuse 4. #35033 — EPD early reuse (draft) 5. #35034 — metrics and agentic benchmark coverage (draft) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32305890372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32305890372)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32305890153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32305890153)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: account native Qwen3.5/3.8 MTP KV layers in target pool sizing
signal.text: ## Problem For Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 native in-checkpoint MTP (EAGLE/STANDALONE speculative decoding with **no** `--speculative-draft-model-path`), the target worker never learns the draft layer count: `eagle_draft_num_layers` stays `None` because it is only resolved from the external draft model config. The draft KV pool is then **not budgeted into the target cell size**, so on a 32 GB card the draft pool allocation overruns the static memory envelope and OOMs during initialization. ## Correct accounting The native MTP draft physically allocates one full-context draft K/V layer. With the current FP8 geometry: - target: 16 full-attention layers (64 layers, full attention every 4) × 2048 B/token = **32,768 B/token** - native MTP draft: 1 layer × 2048 B/token = **2,048 B/token** - **total = 34,816 B/token (34 KiB/token)** ## Change `resolve_spec_aux_hidden_state_config` now passes the target `model_config` into `_resolve_eagle_aux_hidden_state`. When EAGLE/STANDALONE is active, no external draft path is set, and the target's text config declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, that value is used as `eagle_draft_num_layers`. ```python mtp_num_hidden_layers = getattr(model_config.hf_text_config, "mtp_num_hidden_layers", None) if mtp_num_hidden_layers is not None and int(mtp_num_hidden_layers) > 0: config.eagle_draft_num_layers = int(mtp_num_hidden_layers) ``` **There is one native MTP hidden layer reused across every draft step, so the count is not multiplied by `speculative_num_steps`.** MTP3 means three speculative steps, not three persistent KV layers. ## Scope / non-behavior-changes - Narrow and architecture-aware: the fallback only fires for native Qwen MTP (no external draft path). It never overrides a user-supplied `--speculative-draft-model-path`. - The EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state resolution stays inside the external-draft branch (it needs the external draft config), so the native-MTP path can never reference an undefined `draft_model_config`. - All other architectures, external EAGLE drafts, and non-speculative runs behave exactly as before (`eagle_draft_num_layers` stays `None` when `mtp_num_hidden_layers` is absent). ## Tests `test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_native_mtp_kv_accounting.py` (CPU, `register_cpu_ci`): 1. native Qwen MTP with `eagle_draft_num_layers=None` and `mtp_num_hidden_layers=1` → resolved to 1; 2. multi-layer checkpoints budget every declared layer; 3. **one-layer draft KV inclusion**: end-to-end through the real pool cell-size math — real `Qwen3_5TextConfig` (64 layers, `full_attention_interval=4` → 16 full-attention layers) resolves as a GDN hybrid, per-layer FP8 KV = 2048 B/token, target 32,768 B/token, `(1 + 1/16)` scale → **34,816 B/token**; 4. external EAGLE draft path precedence (draft's own layer count wins, target `mtp_num_hidden_layers` ignored); 5. no regression for non-MTP models (`mtp_num_hidden_layers` absent → `None`, no-op); 6. draft worker exclusion (never double-counts via the target fallback). ## Validation With this fix plus the standalone pre-draft-KV alias work (separate PR), native-Qwen MTP EAGLE boots at `mem-fraction-static 0.985` and serves 262144-token context on RTX 5090 where the draft KV pool previously OOM'd. This is a correctness fix: the draft KV cost must be part of the memory accounting regardless of hardware. ## Not included - No `--max-total-tokens` policy override. - No early-alias / memory-optimization changes (separate PR). - No hardware-specific hacks or allocator workarounds. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32307465731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307465731)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32307465571](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307465571)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: opt: bind native Qwen MTP embed/lm_head before memory pool allocation
signal.text: ## Problem `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` (the native-Qwen MTP wrapper, `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp`) allocates **BF16 skeleton tensors** for the draft model's `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` during construction: - `model.embed_tokens.weight` `[248320, 5120]` = 2,542,796,800 bytes - `lm_head.weight` `[248320, 5120]` = 2,542,796,800 bytes - **5,085,593,600 bytes nominal (~4.7 GiB)** combined These are **not independent learned MTP weights**: the checkpoint does not ship separate MTP embed/head tensors (only `mtp.*` keys exist), and they are ultimately intended to share the target model's embedding and `lm_head`. `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head()` already deletes them and rebinds the draft to the target via `set_embed_and_head` / `set_lm_head_from_target` — but it only ran **after** `draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool()`, i.e. after both the target and draft KV pools were allocated, so the multi-GiB duplicate residency coexisted with pool construction. ## Initialization-order root cause ``` scheduler.init_model_worker() -> init_tp_model_worker() -> target TpModelWorker.__init__() -> ModelRunner.initialize() -> load_model() # target weights resident -> maybe_init_draft_worker() -> EAGLEWorkerV2.__init__() -> EagleDraftWorker.__init__() -> draft TpModelWorker(is_draft_worker=True) # native-MTP weights resident -> self.draft_runner assigned >>> EARLY NATIVE-QWEN MTP ALIAS (this PR) <<< -> init_memory_pools() -> init_target_memory_pool() # target Mamba / KV alloc -> draft pool allocation ``` The alias previously happened at the end of `EagleDraftWorker.alloc_memory_pool()`. Both the target and draft models are already fully loaded by the time `EagleDraftWorker.__init__` finishes — so the earliest safe point is right after `self.draft_runner = self.draft_worker.model_runner`, **before** the scheduler allocates any memory pools. ## Change - In `EagleDraftWorker.__init__`, immediately after `self.draft_runner` is assigned, run the existing embed/head-sharing logic via `_bind_native_qwen_mtp_before_pool()` and store the result in `self._early_mtp_alias_bound`. - `alloc_memory_pool()` now **consumes** the precomputed flag and skips the original post-pool `init_token_map()` / `init_lm_head()` calls when the early bind ran (the alias is idempotent). - The bind reuses the existing `init_lm_head()` path (`set_embed_and_head` + `set_lm_head_from_target`). ## Safety / guarding - Narrow guard: only `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` from `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp` takes the early path. - **Token-mapped (hot-token) heads bail** (`hot_token_id is not None`) and keep the original post-pool ordering — the early bind is unsafe when the head is cloned/reordered. - EAGLE3 / standalone / external-draft / multi-layer workers are untouched (they never construct this class or keep their own ordering). - Genuine MTP decoder / `fc` / norm parameters are never modified — only the embed/head aliases are rebound. - The bind asserts embed storage is shared, `lm_head` module is shared, and zero duplicate bytes remain before pool allocation. - Startup weight-load overlap (`--startup-weight-load-mode=overlap`) is not supported for speculative decoding / hybrid-GDN configs (rejected in `startup_weight_load.py`), so serial weight load always completes before this code runs. ## Memory impact On an RTX 5090 (32 GB, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + native MTP + ReplaySSM EAGLE): | step | free VRAM | |---|---| | pre-alias (both models loaded) | ~8.9 GiB | | after early bind | ~14.0 GiB | | released before target KV alloc | **5,054,136,320 bytes (~4.707 GiB)** | Target KV allocation now sees the freed headroom (Gittensor checkpoint: 14.04 GiB free at the target pool step vs ~8.9 GiB before; RadixArk checkpoint: ~10.9 GiB). ## Deterministic parity Same prompt + `temperature 0.0`: ```text output_ids: [271, 9419, 271, 248068, 198, 760, 1156, 1018] ``` Bit-identical to the unpatched control and to the previous pre-draft-KV alias patch — the alias rebinds tensors, it never changes logits. ## Before / after real-world initialization evidence | checkpoint | previous alias timing (pre-draft-KV) | this PR (init-time) | |---|---|---| | Gittensor Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 262144 ctx, MTP3, 4 Mamba slots | boot + `/generate` 200 | boot + `/generate` 200 | | RadixArk Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 230k/250k/260k ctx | **OOM during target KV construction** (~220k/230k) | boot + `/generate` 200 at 230k, 250k, 260k | Heavier checkpoints (RadixArk) OOMed during **target** KV allocation with the earlier pre-draft-KV patch because the skeleton duplicates were still resident while the target pool profiled and allocated; moving the alias to `__init__` eliminates them first. These are measured single-hardware cases, not universal guarantees. ## Tests `test/registered/unit/spec/test_native_mtp_early_alias.py` (CPU, `register_cpu_ci`): - guard narrowness: only `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` / `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp` takes the early path; same-name-different-module rejected; - alias timing: `alloc_memory_pool` consumes the precomputed `_early_mtp_alias_bound`, never re-binds, and skips post-pool init when it ran; - fallback ordering preserved: non-MTP drafts still run `init_token_map` + `init_lm_head` after the pool; - storage sharing: draft embed/head share target storage after the bind; - genuine MTP weights untouched. ## Untested (honest) - EAGLE3 with native-Qwen MTP (aux-hidden-state path) — not exercised; the guard excludes it from the early path by construction. - Standalone / external EAGLE draft models — not exercised. - TP/PP configurations — not exercised. - Token-map / hot-token heads — covered by the fallback (bail), but not end-to-end. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32307446680](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307446680)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32307446611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32307446611)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [FlashInfer MLA] Migrate to unified planning and tensor APIs
signal.text: ## Motivation Migrate SGLang's FlashInfer MLA backend to the unified planning and tensor APIs introduced by [FlashInfer #4031](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4031). The legacy positional planning and split-tensor run forms are deprecated by that API. SGLang also needs to retain its sync-free CUDA graph replay paths and capture-stable metadata buffers during the migration. AI assistance was used under human direction to implement and validate this draft. ## Modifications - Use `MLAPlanMetadata.csr` and explicit planning keywords for decode and paged prefill. - Pass split queries and packed KV caches through the unified tensor-first run interface. - Adapt the sync-free decode and prefill planners to structured metadata. - Keep initial target-verify graph capture on CUDA metadata, then use pinned host metadata during replay. - Add focused coverage for fast-prefill buffer refresh and make MLA integration tests reject deprecated API warnings. ## Accuracy Tests Targeted B200 validation against FlashInfer #4031: - `test/registered/attention/unittests/mla/test_flashinfer.py`: 7 passed, 1 skipped, and 15 subtests passed. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_mla_dense_block_table.py`: 15 passed. The coverage includes eager execution, CUDA graph capture/replay, speculative target verification, fast planning, and unified MLA cache layouts. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No standalone speed benchmark was rerun for this API migration. The existing sync-free fast-plan path, capture-stable buffers, and zero-copy packed KV cache path are preserved; the targeted CUDA graph tests pass. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change is required.) - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Accuracy results are above; standalone speed profiling was not rerun.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signal.title: [RFC] Sglang non-GPU process rust migration
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. **PR** - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799 Refer Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949 Release Roadmap https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0 ### Motivation **Status**: Draft **Author**: @rainj-me **Created**: Apr 20 2026 **Version**: 0.1 # Rust Server Migration Plan **Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation. --- ## 1. Goals & scope **Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle up to scheduler submission. **In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.), large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch. **Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals, quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them. **Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python. --- ## 2. Architecture summary The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context): - **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded, thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer / scheduler boundary — no shared locks. - **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound); (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries. - **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized. - **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msgpack metadata), never tensor bytes; lifetime is the pool's slot-reuse policy — a slot returns to the free list only after both Python's read and any GPU DMA complete, not Rust's `Drop`. - **Cross-rank:** For DP attention, the first rank of each DP group runs the Rust server *without* the api-server; a single api-server then fans **control** messages to every DP group (duplicated, since control must reach all), while **generation** requests are **round-robined** across DP groups for load balancing. - **Streaming:** a single `Streaming` macro state self-loops per chunk; non-streaming is just a stream whose frames are accumulated and emitted in `Finalizing`. See the request-FSM and topology diagrams in the Appendix for detail. --- ## 3. Phase 1 — Rust server (tok/detok manager + HTTP server) **Target: 2026-07-17** Phase 1 delivers the Rust front-half running in front of the **existing Python scheduler + GPU worker**, inside one process via multi-threaded Rust ⇄ Python. ### 3.1 Work breakdown | | Item | Status | Depends on | Notes | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | 1 | Rust frontend \+ scheduler PoC | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#23360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23360) \[Closed\] | | 2 | Architecture design | ✅ Done | — | Pending final approval | | 3 | Pickle → msgpack migration | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#28688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28688) \[Merged\] Followup issue [\#29465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29465) | | 4 | Single-process framework: multi-threaded Rust \+ Python scheduler/GPU worker | ✅ Done | 3 | | | 5 | Tokenizer & detokenizer manager | ✅ Done | 4 | | | 6 | HTTP server: /generate \+ streaming | ✅ Done | 4, 5 | | | 7 | Encoder support | 🟡 WIP | 4, 5 | Work with dynamo team check whether this can export to dynamo crate. | | 8 | PD disaggregation | ✅Done | 4 | Large. Prefill/decode split — see risk note. | | 9 | DP attention \+ cross-node DP controller | ✅ Done | 4 | Large, cross-node. See risk note. | | 10 | Metrics / logging | 🟡 WIP | 4 | Logging Done, Metrics WIP | | 11 | Port existing HTTP APIs other than the listed APIs below | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Full endpoint parity for drop-in replacement. | | 12 | Unified multi-protocol lib (server \+ gateway) | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Shared http(s)/h2/h3/gRPC/WS layer reused by sglang-gateway. | | 13 | Code Refactor | 🟡 WIP | | | | 14 | AuthZ support | | | | | 15 | Parallel Sampling | | | | | 16 | Benchmark\_serving perf optimization | 🟡 WIP | | | | 17 | Embedding request | | | | | 18 | offline Engine API support | | | | | 19 | Other flags in the TokenizedGenerateReqInput | | | | | 20 | cache\_tokens | | | | | 21 | custom\_logit\_processor | | | | | 22 | preferred\_sampling\_params | | | | | 23 | Standalone API-Server for DP Attn | 🟡 WIP | | | | 24 | Anthorpic API support | | | | | 25 | SageMaker API support | | | | | 26 | Vertex AI API support | | | | | 27 | Ollama compatible API support | | | | | 28 | Weight update APIs | | | | | 29 | HiCache APIs | | | | ### 3.2 Sequencing & critical path Items are **not** independent. The dependency spine is: ``` #3 pickle→msgpack ──► #4 single-process framework ──► #5 tok/detok ──► #6 /generate+stream ──► #11 API parity └─► #10 metrics (parallel) └─► #7 encoder (parallel, after #5) ``` **Critical path to a usable July 17 milestone:** 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with 10 landing in parallel and 11 close behind. That subset is what makes the Rust server a working, A/B-testable drop-in for text LLM traffic. **Recommend deferring out of the July 17 milestone** (track as Phase 1.5 / stretch): items **8 (PD disaggregation)** and **9 (DP attention + cross-node DP controller)**. Both are large, both can land after the core path is proven, and bundling them into the July date puts the whole milestone at risk. Item **12 (unified protocol lib)** is valuable but is a refactor that can follow once #6 stabilizes the protocol surface. > **Date reality check.** July 17 is ~4 weeks out and #4 (the foundation) is still > pending-start. The 3→4→5→6+7 path is achievable in that window if #4 starts > immediately and 8/9/12 are explicitly descoped. Carrying all 12 to July 17 is not > realistic; pick the milestone definition deliberately. ### 3.3 Phase 1 exit criteria - Rust server handles `/generate` (streaming + non-streaming) at parity with Python. - Tok/detok managers run in-process; detok is incremental and order-correct. - Encoder path works for at least one multimodal input type. - Metrics + logs at parity; runs behind a flag, A/B-able against Python. - Endpoint parity sufficient to route production text traffic. --- ## 4. Cross-cutting concerns **Rollout / fallback.** Every phase ships behind a flag with the Python path as the live fallback. Migrate by traffic slice (shadow → small % → ramp), not big-bang. keep the Python path runnable as the live fallback until the Rust path reaches parity. **Testing.** Differential testing against Python (same inputs → same tokens/frames) is the primary correctness gate. Add: FSM property tests (every state has a terminal exit; post-terminal events are no-ops/idempotent); streaming order + UTF-8-boundary tests for detok. **Observability.** Metrics/logging (P1 #10) should land *with* the core path, not after — debugging the channel/FSM/threading layers without it is painful. Per-state request counts, queue depths (ring-buffer occupancy = backpressure signal), per-core load, and control-op latencies. **Kernel / environment.** io_uring features used (`MSG_RING` 5.18+, `SEND_ZC` 6.0+, `DEFER_TASKRUN` 6.1+) set a minimum kernel; some hardened/container environments disable io_uring — keep an epoll+eventfd fallback behind the same loop abstraction. --- ## 5. Top risks | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | July 17 scope (all 12 items) | Milestone slips / quality suffers | Descope 8/9/12; define milestone as 3→4→5→6+10. | | #4 framework is the foundation and hasn't started | Blocks 5–7; whole phase waits | Start immediately; treat as the single highest-priority item. | | Rust↔Python boundary in the single-process step | Perf cliffs, GIL contention | Keep the boundary narrow (handles, not data); measure early. | | Detok ordering / UTF-8 under streaming | Corrupt user-visible output | Shard by `hash(req_id)`; stateful decode offsets; boundary tests. | | Slow-client backpressure on egress | GPU stalls / memory growth | Bounded egress buffers; treat persistent slow consumer as disconnect. | --- ## 6. Milestones | Date | Milestone | | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ~Now | #1 PR #23360, #3 merged (PR #28688); #4 started. | | 2026-07-17 | **Phase 1 core:** Rust server with `/generate` + streaming + encoder + metrics, A/B-able vs Python (items 3–7, 10, 11). | | Phase 1.5 | PD disaggregation (#8), DP attention + cross-node controller (#9), unified protocol lib (#12). | ## 7. Appendix 1. [Initial plan](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0) 2. [Architecture Design](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1_DJ_Fjq_tgMTmzWcmm5uacCi9RJGW_lwZGeXiecc6XY/edit?slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0#slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0)

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add SGLang support for GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA models: - GraniteSWA: Granite with per-layer sliding-window attention and a learnable per-head attention sink. - GraniteMoeSWA: GraniteMoeShared-style MoE combined with the SWA/sink attention above (reuses GraniteSWAAttention). Optional shared experts via shared_intermediate_size (disabled by default). Both models support per-layer sliding window vs full attention configs, as well as NoPE and varying RoPE thetas. These model classes were merged into Transformers main yesterday 7/30 (5.15.0.dev0) and we would like to extend support here. Portions of this PR were developed with assistance by Claude Code. I have reviewed and tested all changes myself. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/granite_swa.py` (new): `GraniteSWAForCausalLM`. Reuses `RadixAttention`, passing `sinks=self.sinks` at forward. Sliding window and RoPE base are set per layer via `config.layer_types` and `config.layer_rope_theta` (`theta == 0` for NoPE). - `python/sglang/srt/models/granitemoe_swa.py` (new): `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`. Reuses `GraniteSWAAttention` from `granite_swa.py` and `GraniteMoeMoE` from `granitemoe.py`. Adds an optional shared-expert MLP (`shared_intermediate_size > 0`). Custom `load_weights` remaps HF checkpoint keys to match SGLang conventions and shards attention sinks across TP ranks. - `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`: add these two models to the existing gpt-oss handling of attention sinks, avoiding FlashInfer backend (no sink support). - `docs/supported_models/text_generation/generative_models.md`: adds both models to the supported-models table, referencing the public HF checkpoints. - `test/registered/models/test_generation_models.py`: registers correctness tests for both checkpoints (see below); adds an optional per-`ModelCase` `torch_dtype` override (defaults to the existing global `TORCH_DTYPES` behavior for every other model) used only by the MoE entry. ## Accuracy Tests - Parity established locally against HF implementation (one token deviation out of 15 in teacher-forced bf16 forward pass) - Registered correctness tests for the public HF checkpoints `ibm-granite/granite-swash-2b` (dense) and `ibm-granite/granite-swash-3b-a600m` (MoE with shared experts). MoE checkpoint is pinned to its native bf16, as fp16 deviates at a near-tie token prediction for one of the default prompts. Tolerances have been adjusted to reflect the lower logit precision. - GSM8K scores (5-shot, on H100) similar to published model cards, within sampling noise: 39.5 vs 42.23 for `granite-swash-2b`, 41.5 vs 39.58 for `granite-swash-3b-a600m` ## Speed Tests and Profiling `sglang.bench_serving` on H100: - `granite-swash-2b`: ~397 tok/s output @ concurrency 1; ~19.2k tok/s output @ concurrency 100 - `granite-swash-3b-a600m`: ~405 tok/s output @ concurrency 1; ~14.8k tok/s output @ concurrency 100 ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [VLM] Route every multimodal processor through the worker pool's call site
signal.text: ## Motivation `process_and_combine_mm_data` is the function the multimodal processor worker pool actually runs (`MultimodalProcessorExecutor.run(self.process_and_combine_mm_data, ...)`). **33 of the 37 call sites called it directly**, so those models can never use the pool: with `--mm-processor-worker-num > 1` they build the thread pool and its `deepcopy`'d processor clones at startup and then route every request straight past them. The failure is silent — the model just serves at one-worker speed. That is why PaddleOCR-VL preprocessed pages single-threaded from the day it was added: opting it in (#35318) moved 32-way concurrent throughput from 6.7 to 10.9 req/s on an H200, purely by letting an 87 ms/page preprocess overlap. Only `qwen_vl`, `kimi_k25`, `kimi_k3` and `muse_glimmer` were on the right call site. ## Modifications Mechanically rewrite the 33 sync call sites to `await self.process_and_combine_mm_data_async(...)`, and add a test that pins the invariant. **This is an identity transform, not a behavior change:** - `process_and_combine_mm_data_async` delegates straight to the sync function when `self.mm_processor_executor is None`, which is the case for every model that has not opted into concurrency. - Awaiting a coroutine that never itself suspends does not yield to the event loop, so request interleaving is bit-for-bit unchanged. Only `await loop.run_in_executor(...)` — reached solely when an executor exists — introduces a suspension point. So nothing about scheduling moves until a model sets `supports_mm_processor_concurrency`. What this PR buys is that opting a model in becomes a three-line change instead of a call-site migration plus an audit. ## Verification The migration was generated and checked by AST, not by hand: - 33 sync call sites before, **0** after; 37 async call sites after. - Every call site sits inside an `async def`, before and after — so each edit is exactly `await` + `_async`. - Each of the 33 changed lines differs from its original **only** by that rename (0 deviations, checked mechanically against the diff). - Every touched file compiles; `isort` / `black` / `ruff` clean. `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py` re-runs the same scan as a CPU test, so a processor added later cannot quietly opt out of the pool again. It reports 37 call sites on this branch and would have reported 33 offenders before it. ## Notes for reviewers Turning concurrency *on* for a given model is deliberately **not** part of this PR. That decision is per-model and needs measurement, for two reasons: - The executor is a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, so a model only benefits if its preprocessing releases the GIL (PIL / numpy / torch C code does; pure-Python preprocessing would not). - More workers spread request arrivals, which fragments GPU prefill batches — the tradeoff `qwen_vl` documents when it picks 2 workers, and which showed up in measurement as `--mm-processor-worker-num 8` being slower than 4 on PaddleOCR-VL. `muse_glimmer` is already on the async call site but has no capability flag, so it is the one existing model that could opt in for free once measured. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test (`test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py`) - [x] Verify the change is an identity transform rather than benchmarking it (there is nothing to benchmark: behavior is unchanged until a model opts in) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32305751651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32305751651)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32305751526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32305751526)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
