signal.title: [GDN] Amortize ReplaySSM checkpoint materialization
signal.text: ## Motivation ReplaySSM speculative decoding currently materializes the full GDN checkpoint state on every target step, even though most speculative iterations only need to append a small amount of history. This repeatedly performs work that can be deferred and makes GDN state handling a material part of the decode critical path. ## Modifications - Commit 1 stores speculative GDN updates in a bounded circular history and amortizes checkpoint materialization. - Commit 2 materializes the ReplaySSM state directly from the compact history representation instead of replaying the full raw history. - Preserve the existing checkpoint and recovery semantics while threading the compact state through the GDN backend, memory pool, and speculative utilities. ## Accuracy Tests - Exact state checks covered checkpoint capacity, cursor movement, radix-tree track snapshots, recovery, and sequential-reference comparisons. - Every production arm completed 112/112 identical requests with HTTP 200, fixed input length 88,786 tokens, exact output length 860 tokens, CUDA graph enabled, zero queueing/retractions/errors, and all four ranks at achieved batch 28 during the measured window. - The compact-history validation observed maximum absolute differences of 0.0078125 for the main state and 0.00390625 for the track state, while the active checkpoint path remained bitwise unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs in DP4, MTP with 6 draft tokens, TRTLLM-MHA split 1, ReplaySSM `extra_buffer`, radix-cache page size 64, and the same frozen 112-request cohort in every arm. - Workload: every request uses the same 88,786-token input and generates exactly 860 output tokens; all requests are prefetched first, no new prefill is admitted during measurement, and throughput is measured only from the pure-generation interval after the final prefill and before the first completion. - Acceptance criteria: all four ranks must report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no request completion inside the selected interval. | Variant | Pure-generation steps | Natural mean acceptance length | Target-step time (ms) | Output tokens/s/GPU | Change vs. baseline | SGL/TRT ratio | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline | 110 | 4.84318 | 33.19895 | 4,084.741 | — | 85.3193% | | Commit 1: circular history | 140 | 4.82857 | 32.64644 | 4,141.340 | +1.385% | 86.5015% | | Commit 2: compact materialization | 120 | 4.80208 | 31.13983 | 4,317.890 | +5.708% | 90.1891% | | TRT-LLM reference | Fixed-B28 reference | 4.8 (forced) | 28.07256 | 4,787.594 | Reference | 100% | - Commit 2 improves output throughput by 4.263% over commit 1 and reduces target-step time by 6.20% versus baseline. - The baseline-to-commit-1 mean context per rank changed from 102,456.7 to 103,394.3 tokens (+0.915%), while natural acceptance length decreased by 0.302%, so the measured gain is not explained by a favorable acceptance shift. - Nsight profiling measured the active GDN union decreasing from 5.40407 ms to 3.48862 ms per target step. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. ## Checklist - signal.title: feat(metrics): count waiting-queue request rejections
signal.text: The scheduler drops requests from the waiting queue in three places without recording anything: a full queue, a preemption by a higher-priority request, and a waiting timeout. None are observable. The tokenizer-side sglang:num_aborted_requests_total counter does not cover them, because its only increment site counts aborts the frontend initiates, and these travel the opposite direction. HTTP status codes do not cover them either for streaming requests: the 200 is committed at http.response.start before the scheduler can reject, so the client receives 200 plus an SSE error chunk and the rejection never appears in any status-code metric. Rejected requests also return before set_wait_queue_entry_time(), so they are absent from queue_time_seconds, per_stage_req_latency, TTFT, and e2e_request_latency. On a production deployment running --max-queued-requests, this hid roughly 6% of offered load behind zero recorded 503s. Add sglang:num_queue_rejected_requests_total, labelled by reason. It inherits the SchedulerMetricsCollector label set, so it carries dp_rank and attributes rejections to the individual rank whose queue filled, which matters when a load-balance method concentrates a shared prefix on one rank. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! signal.author: liangjuf

signal.title: [sglang-miles] Fix p2p weight registry: draft worker overwrite, fused indexer mapping, registration retries
signal.text: Fixes found while verifying miles p2p (RDMA) weight updates on GLM-5.2 744B fp8 with MTP enabled. Companion miles PR: radixark/miles#2605. **Worker-keyed engine-info bootstrap registry** (`engine_info_bootstrap_server.py`, `remote_instance_weight_transporter.py`, `model_runner.py`, `http_server.py`) With speculative decoding, the draft worker's `ModelRunner.initialize()` also registers with the EngineInfoBootstrapServer. The registry was keyed by `tp_rank` alone, last write wins, and the draft registers after the target — so the p2p client received the draft model's weight table and RDMA session for every rank: ordinary target params appeared missing on the remote and every write bucket failed. The registry key is now `(worker, tp_rank)` (`worker` in `{"target", "draft"}`), the transporter tags its registrations, and the two query endpoints take an optional `worker` parameter defaulting to `"target"` — existing clients keep their behavior, and a p2p client can address the draft explicitly. Long-running MTP training needs exactly that: the trained nextn layer must reach the draft, or speculative acceptance decays to zero as the target trains away from the frozen draft (observed as `accept rate: 0.00` followed by an out-of-range index assert in decode ~100 steps in). **Fused DSA indexer weights unmappable by ParameterMapper** (`deepseek_v2.py`) With `use_dsa_indexer_fusion`, the model has one bf16 `indexer.wk_weights_proj` per layer and no `indexer.wk` / `indexer.weights_proj` params. The checkpoint loader folds the unfused names via `_load_fused_indexer_wk`, but `ParameterMapper` — built from `stacked_params_mapping` and used by the p2p staging path — had no entry, so every indexer wk/weights_proj tensor sent by the trainer was silently dropped. Added the two stacked entries, gated on the fusion config (not a `named_parameters()` probe: the NextN subclass builds its mappings before its model exists), with dot-anchored patterns so already-fused checkpoint names cannot be rewritten into nonsense. **NextN name mapping for external weight mappers** (`deepseek_nextn.py`) `mutate_weight_preload` maps `model.layers.{num_hidden_layers}.*` to `model.decoder.*` so `ParameterMapper.from_model` on the draft model resolves converter-emitted nextn names the same way the loader does. **Registration was one-shot and swallowed failures** (`remote_instance_weight_transporter.py`) A transient connection failure while PUTting to the bootstrap server was logged and forgotten; the missing rank then surfaced minutes later as a 404 at the first weight update, far from the cause. Both registrations now retry (24 x 5s, timeout 10s) and raise after exhaustion. **Inverse ue8m0 scale transform for non-128-divisible row counts** (`fp8_utils.py`) The weights-checker comparator crashed on params like `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` (mn=2624): the inverse transform assumed the repeated-scale layout's row count is a multiple of the 128 block size. The main blocks and the partial tail block are now de-repeated separately.
signal.author: yueming-yuan

signal.title: moe: add DeepEP V2 ElasticBuffer support to MoE token dispatcher
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepEP V2 ([deepseek-ai/DeepEP#605](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/605), merged 2026-04-29) introduces `ElasticBuffer` alongside the legacy `Buffer`. SGLang's MoE token dispatcher (`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py`) only knows how to build and drive the V1 `Buffer`, so there is currently no way to reach the V2 path from SGLang without monkeypatching `DeepEPBuffer.get_deepep_buffer()` at runtime. The V2 API differs from V1 in ways that touch the whole dispatch/combine contract, not just the constructor: - **MoE-shape ctor.** `ElasticBuffer(group, num_max_tokens_per_rank, hidden, num_topk, ...)` instead of V1's NVL/RDMA byte-pool ctor. - **No `get_dispatch_layout()`.** V2 infers the layout internally from `topk_idx`, so the V1 pre-pass is gone at the call site. - **5-tuple dispatch.** Dispatch returns `(recv_x, recv_topk_idx, recv_topk_weights, EPHandle, event)`; `num_recv_tokens_per_expert_list` now lives on the `EPHandle`, not in the return tuple. - **Typed event.** The pybind requires `deep_ep._C.EventHandle` for `previous_event`; passing a V1 `Buffer.capture()` `EventOverlap` raises `TypeError`. - **`combine` signature.** V2 `combine` drops the V1 `config` kwarg and reuses the dispatch handle's SM count. `deep_ep.__init__` on a V2 install exports **both** `Buffer` (from `buffers/legacy.py`) and `ElasticBuffer` (from `buffers/elastic.py`), so SGLang's existing `from deep_ep import Buffer, Config` surface keeps working unchanged. This PR adds the missing consumer-side plumbing so `ElasticBuffer` is reachable and correct. Parallel upstream work adopts the same `HAVE_DEEP_EP_V2` probe shape, and this PR mirrors it so the frameworks stay consistent: - **Megatron-LM**: [NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#4632](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/4632) — `fused_a2a.py` V2 translation. This PR's dispatch/combine translation mirrors that one. - **vLLM**: [vllm-project/vllm#41183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41183) — WideEP DeepEP V2. ## Modifications All changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py` plus its unit test. The V2 path is **opt-in** behind `SGLANG_DEEPEP_USE_V2=1`; with it unset (or on a pre-V2 `deep_ep` install) the V1 `Buffer` path runs byte-identical to before. 1. **Probe + opt-in buffer build.** A `try: from deep_ep import ElasticBuffer` probe sets `have_deepep_v2`. `get_deepep_buffer()` builds an `ElasticBuffer` when V2 is importable and the env var is set, otherwise the legacy `Buffer`. `clean_buffer()` skips `clean_low_latency_buffer` when the live object is an `ElasticBuffer` (V2 has no equivalent). 2. **Call-site translation in `_dispatch_core` / `_combine_core`** (`b65c871`). Drops the V1 `get_dispatch_layout()` pre-pass; unpacks the 5-tuple and reads `num_recv_tokens_per_expert_list` off the `EPHandle`; re-derives the typed `EventHandle` via the elastic buffer's `capture()` for `previous_event`; drops the V1 `config` kwarg on `combine`. Mirrors the Megatron `fused_a2a` V2 path. 3. **Cache-slot fix** (`0bb2713`). The V2 branch stored the buffer on `cls._buffer`, but the cache guard reads `state.buffer` — so **every** `_get_buffer()` (twice per MoE layer per forward) constructed and tore down a fresh `ElasticBuffer` (NCCL comm split + GIN ring alloc + QP setup, ~0.35 s each). On a 2-node TP16/EP16 run this was **~34 s/token** of pure constructor churn. Caching to `state.buffer` fixes it (this bug ships inside this PR's earlier commit; the fix is in the same PR). 4. **`num_max_tokens_per_rank` sizing** (`b2959be`). `ElasticBuffer` hard-asserts `num_tokens <= num_max_tokens_per_rank` on every dispatch (`csrc/elastic/buffer.hpp:684`). The env default (128) is tuned for the V1 low-latency **decode** batch; in **normal** mode a chunked-prefill batch dispatches up to `chunked_prefill_size` tokens at once. Two layers had to be fixed together: bound the **ctor** capacity by `chunked_prefill_size` / `max_prefill_tokens`, **and** pass `num_max_tokens_per_rank=None` at the dispatch call — because `elastic.py` resolves `value_or(passed, ctor)`, so a passed decode value (128) silently overrides the prefill-sized ctor and re-trips the assert. 5. **Env-gated timing instrumentation** (`0bb2713`, default-off). `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_TIMING=1` wraps dispatch/combine in a cuda-synced `_V2Timer` that logs per-call and cumulative ms. Dead when unset. 6. **Hermetic unit test** (`84fd157`). `test/srt/test_deepep_v2_probe.py` exercises the three probe states. The "neither installed" case now inserts a `sys.modules['deep_ep'] = None` sentinel so `import deep_ep` raises deterministically even on a host where `deep_ep` is genuinely installed (previously it only passed on CPU-only CI). V2 fall-through matrix: - `have_deepep_v2=False` (pre-V2 install) → legacy `Buffer`, byte-identical to pre-patch. - `have_deepep_v2=True`, env unset → legacy `Buffer`, byte-identical. V2 latent. - `have_deepep_v2=True`, `SGLANG_DEEPEP_USE_V2=1` → new `ElasticBuffer` path. - `use_deepep=False` → unchanged; module still imports. ## Accuracy Tests Validated end-to-end on 2× p5en.48xlarge (16× H200), TP16/EP16, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal`, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, cross-node dispatch/combine over the DeepEP V2 `ElasticBuffer` path (`SGLANG_DEEPEP_USE_V2=1` confirmed on all 16 ranks in the server log: `constructing deep_ep.ElasticBuffer`). Coherent generation through the V2 path (greedy, `temperature=0`): ``` prompt : "The capital of France is" output : " Paris. The capital of the United Kingdom is London." ``` `/v1/models` returns 200 on both nodes; the probe unit test passes 3/3 on a pod with `deep_ep` V2 installed (was 2 pass / 1 fail before the hermetic fix), and skips cleanly on CPU-only hosts. > Note on CI hardware: this validation ran on AWS EFA (proxy-GIN transport). SGLang's EP CI runs on NVLink/InfiniBand, where the V2 kernels are exercised by the same `ElasticBuffer` API. The default path is unchanged, so existing EP tests under `test/registered/ep/` and `test/manual/ep/` run on the V1 `Buffer` and are unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling AIPerf sweep on the same 2-node TP16/EP16 serve, ISL 512 / OSL 128, streaming chat completions: | Concurrency | TTFT mean (ms) | ITL mean (ms) | Request latency mean (ms) | Requests | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 308.0 | 143.9 | 18,583 | 8 | | 4 | 402.9 | 146.8 | 19,045 | 32 | | 8 | 478.7 | 146.2 | 19,050 | 64 | ITL is flat across concurrency (decode-bound per user; the all-to-all transport is not the bottleneck at these shapes), and the full sweep runs with 0 buffer asserts and the server alive throughout — the sizing fix (modification #4) is what makes c=8 survive. Kernel-level profiling with the shipped `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_TIMING=1` instrumentation (reproducible from this PR): the V2 dispatch/combine kernels measure **7.2 ms / 6.6 ms p50** at TP16/EP16 cross-node. This is what surfaced the cache-slot bug (modification #3) — before the fix, wall time was ~34 s/token of constructor churn around ~14 ms of actual kernels; after, ~150 ms/token. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py` — black-jupyter applied.) - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test/srt/test_deepep_v2_probe.py`, hermetic across CPU-only and GPU hosts.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing doc change; the path is opt-in and internal. Happy to add a note under EP docs if reviewers prefer.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. (Above — 2-node TP16/EP16 EFA, coherent output + AIPerf matrix + kernel p50.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Related - DeepEP V2: [deepseek-ai/DeepEP#605](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/605) (merged) - Megatron-LM DeepEP V2: [NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#4632](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/4632) - vLLM DeepEP V2: [vllm-project/vllm#41183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41183) - Shared DeepEP V2 + AWS EFA reproduction substrate (public): [`antonai-work/vllm-deepep-v2-efa`](https://github.com/antonai-work/vllm-deepep-v2-efa), [`antonai-work/nemo-rl-deepep-v2-efa`](https://github.com/antonai-work/nemo-rl-deepep-v2-efa) /cc @zhyncs @merrymercy @Ying1123 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32297147893](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32297147893)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32297146926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32297146926)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSA] Trim top-k v2 output modes and tighten its PDL waits
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation The DeepSeek-V4 (DSA indexer) top-k v2 kernel carried an optional `raw_indices` output that no production caller ever requests: the c4 indexer routes to the v1 kernel whenever it needs raw indices, so the v2 argument was only ever exercised by a unit test. Everyone else still paid for it with a per-element `raw_out != nullptr` branch inside the page-table transform loop. While removing it, two PDL (programmatic dependent launch) details in the same kernel turned out to be leaving performance on the table or resting on a condition the caller was not told about. ## Modifications **Output modes.** `raw_indices` is gone; `page_tables` becomes optional instead. `None` selects a `TopKMode::INDICES` template that emits the selected positions straight into the output, so the transform pass -- and the 8 KB shared staging buffer it needs -- is compiled out rather than skipped at runtime. Passing a page table keeps the existing behaviour bit for bit. **Output buffer is no longer prefilled with -1.** Every path already writes all `topk` slots of every row: the collect pass fills `[0, above_count)`, `handle_tie` fills `[above_count, topk)` (padding included), and the trivial path fills everything. The per-layer fill kernel was dead work. **Level-3 PDL wait narrowed to the cluster path.** Only rows whose raw indices come from the persistent cluster kernel need that kernel to have retired. The register / streaming / trivial rows were waiting on it too, holding an SM slot until the long-running pool finished and serializing the short items behind it -- which is exactly the mix level 3 exists for. The wait now lives inside the cluster branch (block-uniform, so the following `__syncthreads()` is unaffected). **Small-batch kernel.** Dropped the redundant `PDLWaitPrimary` after `forward()` (`forward()` already waits internally) and added the missing `PDLTriggerSecondary` so dependents can be scheduled without waiting for the whole grid to drain. **PDL prefetch contract.** The kernel reads `seq_lens` and the plan metadata *before* its `griddepcontrol.wait`, which is only legal while neither is produced by the immediately preceding kernel in the stream (per CUDA: the launch trigger "provides no memory visibility guarantee itself"). Production satisfies this -- both are built during per-forward metadata prep -- but two call sites could quietly break it, so: - the DSA backend now asserts `lengths.dtype == torch.int32` instead of calling `.to(torch.int32)`, which would place a cast kernel exactly there; - the unit test no longer launches `plan_topk_v2` back to back with the transform. Also renamed `TopKMode::INDICE` to `INDICES`. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` -- 234/234 pass on B200. The no-page-table mode is validated directly against `torch.topk` across every dispatch template and boundary (`test_topk_v2_output_indices`), and the paged mode is still validated by inverting the output through the page table (`test_topk_v2`, `test_topk_v2_ragged`), so both modes keep full coverage. ## Benchmarking and Profiling No kernel-algorithm change on the paged path, so throughput is unchanged for the common shapes. The wins are structural: one fewer fill kernel per layer, one fewer branch per output element in the transform loop, and short rows in a mixed-length long-context batch no longer sit blocked on the persistent cluster pool. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31958299936](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958299936)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32233055438](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233055438)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache] Split the host-memory budget across co-located ranks
signal.text: ## Motivation Every HiCache host-pool sizing guard checks its requested size against `psutil.virtual_memory().available`, which reports machine-wide free memory. Co-located ranks each see the same number, so every rank concludes its pool fits and the host ends up oversubscribed by the number of ranks it holds (8x for single-node TP8). The guard passes, and the pinned-host allocation later OOMs instead of failing fast with the intended `ValueError`. ## Modifications - Add `host_memory_budget_bytes()` in `pool_host/base.py`: subtract `HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES` from available host memory once, then divide by the number of ranks sharing the machine. - Derive that count in `ranks_per_host()` as `world_size // nnodes`: the launcher slices ranks uniformly across nodes (resolution asserts divisibility), so the co-located rank count is a config fact and needs no hostname collective — a collective here would have to be issued the same number of times on every rank, and ranks build different numbers of host pools. - Route all six sizing guards (`HostKVCache` base, `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool`, `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool`, `DSAIndexerPoolHost`, and the mamba/mha pools) through the helper. Single-rank behavior is unchanged. - Unit tests (`test_mem_pool_host.py`): the budget is split across co-located ranks, the reserve is subtracted once before the split rather than per rank, and `ranks_per_host` divides world size by node count. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: this only changes host-pool sizing guards, not model forward paths. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32291671532](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291671532)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32291671297](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291671297)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix weight checking for AITER-shuffled block FP8 weights
signal.text: ## Motivation This ports #34016 from `sglang-miles` to `main` following maintainer feedback. AITER pre-shuffles block-FP8 weights on ROCm for optimized inference kernels. The weight checker was treating the shuffled physical layout as the original logical layout during dequantization, causing false weight-update mismatches even though inference was correct. AITER rotary `cos_cache` and `sin_cache` buffers were also missing from the checker's existing derived-buffer skip patterns. ## Modifications - Mark dense and MoE block-FP8 parameters after AITER layout shuffling. - Propagate the layout metadata into the weight checker. - Restore the logical FP8 layout before checker dequantization, checksum, and ULP comparison. - Skip AITER rotary `cos_cache` and `sin_cache` buffers during weight checking. - Add unit tests for layout restoration, metadata propagation, and rotary-cache handling. - Register the weight-checker unit tests for AMD CI. The layout conversion is only applied to weights explicitly marked as AITER-shuffled. NVIDIA and other unshuffled paths retain the existing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on AMD MI355 with the Miles [DeepSeek V4 four-layer E2E test](https://github.com/radixark/miles/blob/main/tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_deepseek_v4_flash_4layer_ci.py). Both rollout runs passed, and all checked FP8 weights reported `num_exceed=0`. Weight-checker unit tests: - New focused tests: 6 passed - Full unit suite: 64 passed, 1 skipped because NVIDIA DeepGEMM is unavailable on ROCm This PR does not modify model forward computation or inference kernels. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The only inference-path change is setting metadata during weight loading. Layout restoration runs exclusively when the weight checker is enabled and does not affect normal inference performance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32053738759](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32053738759)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32053738308](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32053738308)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: Xinyu-Kang

signal.title: feat(mem_cache): semantic KV cache reuse via a pluggable fuzzy-match radix backend
signal.text: ## Motivation Exact prefix matching cannot reuse KV across prompts that share meaning but not leading tokens: paraphrased questions over the same document, RAG prompts with reordered context, multi-user workloads hitting the same knowledge base. This PR adds opt-in **semantic KV cache reuse** following the `|exact|fuzzy|miss|` prompt decomposition from the fuzzy prefix matching design discussion (Draft_Prefix_Matching.md, @ibifrost): when the radix tree covers only a prefix, a pluggable `FuzzyMatchProvider` may nominate donor KV from a previously finished request, which is copied into recipient-owned slots with RoPE position correction before the forward pass. Design goals, per maintainer guidance (@hzh0425): keep the default path untouched, register the feature as a radix-cache backend, keep `model_runner` changes minimal. ## Modifications - **New `FuzzyRadixCache(RadixCache)`** registered as radix-cache backend `fuzzy_match` (flexkv pattern). All fuzzy behavior lives in the backend: provider match on exact-miss, donor validation + pinning (lock refs via a TreeNode-id registry), realization-slot pre-allocation with clean exact-only fallback, donor registration on request finish. - **Core `RadixCache`/`BasePrefixCache` changes = two seams:** `MatchResult.fuzzy_matched_len` (new trailing field) and a no-op `_on_finished_insert` hook between the finished-request insert and duplicate-slot freeing. - **`FuzzyKVRealizer`** collaborator does pre-forward donor-KV realization (V copy; K reverse-RoPE at donor positions + apply at target positions; per-layer zero-out mask). `model_runner.py` gains only orchestration: a gated `maybe_init_fuzzy_kv_realizer()` and one delegate call in `_forward_raw` beside the deferred-mamba hook (outside CUDA-graph capture/replay, covers all extend branches). - **`ReverseRotaryEmbedding` / `get_reverse_rope` / `reverse_rotary_emb`** additions to `layers/rotary_embedding` (native path; no CUDA kernel exists for the reverse direction). - **`SemanticEmbedding` provider** (default): implemented by the [`semblend`](https://github.com/WorldFlowAI/semblend) package ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/semblend/), Apache-2.0), installed via the new extra `pip install "sglang[fuzzy-semantic]"`. SemBlend is an open-source library for semantic KV-cache donor discovery and reuse planning: it embeds prompts (MiniLM ONNX), maintains the donor index, aligns donor and recipient token chunks (N:M), scores reuse quality against configurable gates, and emits the reuse plan — donor span, positions, and the per-layer mask — that this PR's realization path consumes. Keeping that pipeline in a package keeps SGLang's tree free of the embedding/ANN stack while the reuse-planning algorithms iterate. Lazy import + hard version gate at startup with an actionable error. The `FuzzyMatchProvider` interface is public so custom providers can plug in. - **Observability:** prefill batch log shows `#fuzzy-token: N` when fuzzy reuse fired (previously realized reuse showed as `#cached-token: 0`). - **Config surface:** selecting the backend enables the feature; five `--fuzzy-*` flags (provider, threshold, min-reuse-ratio, min-match-length, model-arch). Provider-internal tuning stays in config defaults. - **Docs:** end-to-end call chain with explicit lock/alloc/RoPE ownership in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/fuzzy_match/README.md` (requested in review of the experimental branch). - **Tests:** 21 CPU unit tests (`test_fuzzy_match_providers.py`, `test_fuzzy_radix_cache.py`), semblend faked via sys.modules — no new CI dependency. Cover pool-accounting failure modes: stale-donor and kv-length-mismatch fallbacks (leak-checked), donor pin/release lifecycle, donor-registration ordering vs duplicate freeing, node-registry maintenance, registry selection + unsupported-config rejection, and concurrent recipients pinning one donor. Not supported yet: MLA pools, EAGLE, multi-region reuse, hierarchical-cache interaction. ## Follow-on work This PR deliberately ships the minimal `|exact|fuzzy|miss|` pattern — one contiguous fuzzy span re-anchored at the exact-prefix boundary — because it reuses the existing inference pipeline with no structural changes. Planned follow-ups, in rough order: - **Multi-segment / multi-region reuse** (`|exact|miss|fuzzy|miss|fuzzy|...`), the realistic shape of RAG and multi-document workloads: the scheduler builds a segmented prefill plan of fresh spans plus donor-KV spans, and the attention backend consumes it via FlashInfer's `VariableBlockSparseAttentionWrapper` (per the design discussion, a better fit than `custom_mask`). Early prototypes on 64K multi-donor prompts show mean 7.65x TTFT speedup versus cold prefill with good quality — worth its own RFC once this foundation lands. - **True per-layer recompute** for masked layers (the current `layer_recompute_mask` is a zero-out signal); recompute is the cleaner long-term answer for quality. - **Donor-registration budgeting** (rate/dedup limits on donor indexing) to shrink the remaining enabled-but-idle overhead on dense short-request workloads. - **MLA-pool support** in the realization path. - **Hierarchical-cache (HiCache) interaction** — fuzzy donors resident in host tiers. ## Accuracy Tests All runs on THIS branch (A10G, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, fresh server per configuration, 2026-07-13). - **GSM8K few-shot (n=1000), fuzzy on vs off:** baseline accuracy 0.862 (invalid 0.001) vs fuzzy-on **0.865** (invalid 0.001) — no degradation (delta within batching noise). The provider's gates produced **zero fuzzy fires across all 1000 questions** (short, semantically dissimilar prompts never meet the reuse-ratio gate; the few-shot prefix hits the exact radix path), and zero pool leaks. This is the negative control: enabling the backend does not perturb workloads without semantic overlap. - **Warm-vs-cold A/B at 8K/16K** (cnn_dailymail + wikihow clusters, at **default flags**). ROUGE-L / token-F1 compare the warm (reused) answer against the cold answer for the same prompt; the measurement scale: identical-prompt reruns without any reuse score ~0.88/0.90 (batching-noise floor), exact-prefix radix reuse scores 0.94/0.96. | Overlap type | cache frac | cold→warm TTFT | ROUGE-L | token-F1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | exact (control) | — (radix) | 3264→44ms | 0.941 | 0.955 | | partial_60 | 0.88 | 3254→646ms (5.0x) | 0.547 | 0.587 | | partial_80 | 0.58 | 3257→1700ms (1.9x) | 0.449 | 0.490 | | paraphrase | 0.76 | 3262→1034ms (3.2x) | 0.478 | 0.525 | | diverse (negative) | 0.00 | 3262→3318ms (no fire) | 0.878 | 0.898 | A sweep at looser settings (threshold 0.50, min-match 1) produced the same hit rates and the same drift — on genuinely similar pairs the threshold does not change what a hit does, it changes which pairs hit (on GSM8K, defaults fire on 1 in 1000 requests; the diverse control never fires). Read: a fuzzy hit trades TTFT for output drift beyond the rerun-noise floor — reuse is quality-gated but **not lossless**; answers remain on-topic and grounded (samples in the raw results), and per-layer recompute (follow-on) is the path to closing the gap. Zero pool-consistency failures across all sweeps and both GSM8K runs. Experimental-branch reference @16K (n=1): PPL(warm)/PPL(cold) 0.9587. - Statement of semantics: reuse is quality-gated but not lossless; the layer mask is a zero-out signal, not per-layer recompute. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - **Reuse speedup (this branch, e2e smoke):** paraphrase variant realized 104/119 donor tokens with RoPE correction; only 15 tokens prefilled. Experimental-branch reference at 16K: cold TTFT 4548ms → warm 230ms (19.8x); donor registration runs off the hot path (async embed). [OPTIONAL: re-measure 16K TTFT pair on this branch] - **No-hit overhead (GSM8K n=1000, parallel 32, default flags):** 1249 → 1164 tok/s output throughput (~7%) and 127.3 → 136.8s wall on a worst-case-dense workload (a thousand short requests, every one indexed as a donor). The synchronous per-miss lookup cost is bounded by `fuzzy_min_suffix_tokens` (default 256): suffixes too short to amortize a semantic lookup never pay for one. The residual is the asynchronous donor-registration embedding, which amortizes on long-context workloads (fewer, larger requests); donor-registration budgeting is listed as follow-on. Without the suffix gate the same workload measured ~10-11%. The feature is opt-in per deployment. ## Reproduction ```bash pip install "sglang[fuzzy-semantic]" python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \ --radix-cache-backend fuzzy_match \ --fuzzy-model-arch qwen2.5-7b \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 2>&1 | tee server.log # paired paraphrase prompts -> look for: # "fuzzy match success", "[FUZZY] Realized", "#fuzzy-token:" grep -c "pool memory leak detected" server.log # expect 0 ``` ## Checklist / credits - Design + `FuzzyMatchProvider` framework: @ibifrost (Draft_Prefix_Matching.md); backend-registry direction: @hzh0425. Co-authored-by: Chenxin Wu <ibifrostki@gmail.com> Big thanks to @ibifrost and @hzh0425 for all of the hard work/advice/reviewing over the past several months. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32293607482](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32293607482)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32293607129](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32293607129)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] W4A8 MoE kernel for NVFP4 models on non-Blackwell GPUs (SM90)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ### Background NVFP4 quantized models like **GLM-5 (744B)** and **DeepSeek V3.2 (671B)** are becoming increasingly popular. On Blackwell GPUs with native FP4 hardware support, these models run great. However, on non-Blackwell GPUs like H20 (SM90), SGLang falls back to the **Marlin W4A16 path** — dequantizing FP4 weights to BF16 and using BF16 tensor cores. We've been running GLM-5-NVFP4 on 8×H20 (141GB HBM3, SM90) and did extensive benchmarking and kernel-level profiling. The results suggest there's a significant opportunity to improve decode performance on these GPUs. ### Current Performance: NVFP4 (W4A16) vs FP8 on 8×H20 **Decode (DP Attention, MTP enabled):** | Concurrency | NVFP4 (Marlin W4A16) | FP8 | Gap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 58.6 tok/s | 63.6 tok/s | FP8 9% faster | | 64 | 963 tok/s | 1,228 tok/s | FP8 28% faster | **Prefill:** | | NVFP4 | FP8 | Gap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Peak (32 conc) | 5,300 tok/s | 10,500 tok/s | FP8 ~2× faster | We initially expected NVFP4 decode to be faster than FP8 since FP4 weights are half the size (decode is conventionally considered bandwidth-bound). However, **FP8 is faster across the board**. ### Root Cause: Marlin Kernel Efficiency Our profiling shows the Marlin W4A16 kernel has very low memory bandwidth utilization on MoE workloads: - **Theoretical** (bandwidth-limited): NVFP4 should read ~100MB per layer (8 activated experts), taking ~28μs at 4TB/s. FP8 reads ~200MB, taking ~52μs. NVFP4 should be ~1.8× faster. - **Actual**: Marlin takes ~117μs/layer (24% bandwidth utilization), FP8 Triton takes ~72μs/layer (72% utilization). FP8 ends up **1.6× faster**. Meanwhile, FP8 Triton's fused_moe_kernel achieves much higher efficiency with a simpler pipeline (direct FP8 loads, post-MMA scaling, FP8 tensor cores). ### Why This Matters NVFP4 has a key advantage over FP8 for serving: **much smaller weight footprint → more KV cache space**. On our 8×H20 setup with DP Attention, NVFP4 weights leave ~37GB/GPU for KV cache vs ~17GB/GPU for FP8, enabling significantly more concurrent requests. A W4A8 kernel would let non-Blackwell deployments benefit from both the memory advantage and competitive compute performance. Models that would benefit: any NVFP4 quantized MoE model on SM90 GPUs (H20, H100, H200, etc.), including GLM-5 and DeepSeek V3.2. ### Environment - GPUs: 8× NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 141GB HBM3) - Model: GLM-5-NVFP4 (744B MoE, 256 experts, top-8) - SGLang with DP Attention (tp=8, dp=8) - MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding enabled ### Related resources _No response_

signal.title: fix(gemma4): quantize MTP bridge projections
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation The block-FP8 `gemma-4-31B-it-assistant` checkpoint gets a 0% draft-token acceptance rate, while the BF16 assistant gets approximately 65%. The checkpoint stores `pre_projection` and `post_projection` as block-FP8 weights with corresponding `weight_scale` tensors. However, these layers were constructed with `quant_config=None`, causing the FP8 weights to load without their block scales and corrupting the MTP activations. ## Modifications Pass the draft model's `quant_config` to the Gemma 4 MTP assistant's: - `pre_projection` - `post_projection` The assistant transformer trunk already receives the correct `quant_config`. This does not change BF16 behavior because `quant_config` remains `None` for unquantized checkpoints. ## Accuracy Tests Before the fix: - BF16 MTP acceptance rate: approximately 65% - FP8 MTP acceptance rate: 0% End-to-end acceptance results after the fix: 60% ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not needed. signal.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash expert parallelism (DeepEP) crashes on Hopper/SM90 — DeepGEMM MXFP4 MegaMoE is SM100-only; late failure + misleading error
signal.text: ## Summary Serving the **stock (MXFP4-expert) `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`** with **expert parallelism** (`--enable-expert-parallel` / `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`) crashes on **Hopper (SM90)**. It fails late — after a full weight load + MHC prewarm + at **decode CUDA-graph capture** — inside DeepGEMM's MXFP4 grouped GEMM, which asserts SM100: ``` Capture cuda graph failed: Assertion error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:57): ab.scalar_type() == kPackedFP4 and arch_major == 10 ``` `arch_major == 10` is SM100 (Blackwell). On SM90 the scheduler then dies (`Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization`). This is the same failure as the (still-unanswered) discussion #26564 — reported there on H20, sglang 0.5.12 / DeepEP 1.2.1. Filing as an issue because there's clearly standing demand and no tracking issue. ## Environment / reproduce - **Ours:** `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.15.post1`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (stock MXFP4 experts), 4×H100 (SM90), `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Weights load fine (`quant=fp8, fmt=e4m3`), MHC prewarm completes, then the crash above at decode-graph capture. CrashLoops indefinitely. - **#26564:** H20 (SM90), sglang 0.5.12, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto` — identical assertion. Full traceback path: `scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs → tp_worker.init_cuda_graphs → model_runner.init_decode_cuda_graph → decode_cuda_graph_runner.__init__ → capture → DeepGEMM fp8_paged_mqa/MegaMoE layout.hpp:57`. ## Root cause The EP path (DeepEP a2a) routes expert compute to **DeepGEMM's packed-FP4 MegaMoE** grouped GEMM, and that kernel is built for **SM100 only** (Blackwell has native FP4 tensor cores; Hopper does not). The **TP path avoids this** because it resolves MXFP4 experts to **Marlin**, which dequantizes 4-bit → bf16 in-kernel and runs on SM80/SM90 tensor cores — which is exactly why the current DeepSeek-V4 Hopper cookbook recipe is TP-only. So MXFP4 **expert parallelism is implicitly Blackwell-only** today, with no explicit guard. For reference, vLLM's default single-node EP keeps the MXFP4 experts on **Marlin** (all-gather/reduce-scatter around the same Marlin GEMM) and therefore runs this checkpoint under EP on H100. ## Two UX problems 1. **Fails ~8 min in, not at startup.** The incompatibility is knowable from `(device SM) + (MXFP4 experts) + (EP enabled)` before any weights load, but the error only surfaces at graph capture. 2. **The printed remediations are misleading.** "lower `--mem-fraction-static`", "reduce `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`", "disable decode CUDA graph" — none address an *architecture* requirement. Disabling the graph just relocates the same SM100-only kernel to eager decode. ## Working alternatives on Hopper today (for anyone stuck now, incl. #26564) - **EP:** use the FP8-converted checkpoint `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8` with `--enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend deepep`. FP8 grouped GEMM is Hopper-native; we've run TP8/DP8/EP8 + DeepEP-auto on 8×H100 with zero errors. - **Stock MXFP4:** run **TP + Marlin** (no EP) — the documented Hopper cookbook recipe. ## Proposed fixes 1. **Interim — fail fast.** At startup, when `SM < 100` **and** experts are packed-FP4 **and** EP/DeepEP is requested, raise a clear error naming the two alternatives above, instead of crashing at graph capture with arch-agnostic tuning hints. 2. **Real support — Hopper MXFP4 EP.** Route the DeepEP-dispatched grouped expert batches through a Hopper-capable MXFP4 grouped GEMM (**Marlin**, already used on the TP path, or the FlashInfer mxfp4 path from #24816) instead of DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE. Caveat: SM90 has no native FP4, so this is dequant-to-bf16 compute — a memory-footprint win, not FP4 throughput. Happy to contribute the fail-fast guard (#1) and to help wire the Marlin EP path (#2) — would appreciate a pointer on where the MoE-runner / DeepEP dispatch should select the Hopper kernel.

signal.title: [Feature] Optimize AR and DiT overlap for GLM-Image dynamic batching
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR adds AR/DiT overlap to accelerate GLM-Image generation. This reduces the 10-prompt, concurrency-4 benchmark duration from about 223.79 to 182.39s, an **end-to-end improvement of roughly 18.4%.** By default, the overlap mode is disabled, so the existing execution behavior is unchanged: `--ar-dit-overlap-mode off` Users can explicitly enable it with: `--ar-dit-overlap-mode on`. When enabled, the scheduler can prefetch AR outputs for the next compatible request batch while the current DiT requests are being executed sequentially. This helps keep the DiT device fed in 1-AR / 1-DiT separated deployments and reduces idle time under higher concurrency. GLM-Image supports AR/DiT separation with external AR serving and native grouped requests. The original execution pattern is: ```text AR(batch N) -> DiT(req 1) -> DiT(req 2) -> ... -> DiT(req N) -> next AR(batch) ``` This batches the AR stage correctly, but the **next AR batch is only dispatched after all DiT requests in the current batch finish.** In a 1 AR + 1 DiT deployment, DiT runs sequentially on one device and becomes the throughput bottleneck. If AR is not prefetched while DiT is running, the DiT device has to wait for the next AR batch, creating pipeline bubbles. This PR changes the execution pattern to overlap external AR prefetch with sequential DiT execution: ``` AR(batch N) -> DiT(req 1), while prefetching next AR batch -> DiT(req 2) -> ... -> consume prefetched requests ``` The goal is to keep the DiT device fed with prepared AR tokens and reduce idle time in the separated AR/DiT deployment. # Modifications - Add an explicit supports_async_ar_prefetch() pipeline capability. - Enable async AR prefetch only for GLM-Image with an external SRT encoder URL. - Add a GLM-Image-specific async AR prefetch path instead of using the generic grouped pipeline executor from a background thread. - Prefetch AR tokens on CPU while sequential DiT execution is running. - Prefer already-prefetched requests before falling back to normal dynamic dispatch. - Add unit coverage for grouped and single-request GLM-Image external AR prefetch paths. # Accuracy Tests | model | LongText-Bench ZH | |---|---:| | GLM-Image (Official) | 0.9788 | | GLM-Image (AR & Dit Overlap) | **0.9803** | And run unit test: ``` PYTHONPATH=python python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_glm_image_ar.py ``` Result: ``` Passed ``` # Speed Tests and Profiling Server start command ``` export HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT=25000 export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="25000-25199" export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="25200-25399" export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 sglang serve \ --model-path /nas/disk1/GLM-Image/vision_language_encoder/ \ --tokenizer-path /nas/disk1/GLM-Image/processor/ \ --port 8764 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --base-gpu-id 0 \ --tp-size 1 \ --enable-multimodal \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 8 \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --disable-fast-image-processor export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true export HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT=26000 export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="26000-26199" export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="26200-26399" export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 sglang serve \ --model-path /nas/disk1/GLM-Image/ \ --base-gpu-id 0 \ --num-gpus 1 \ --srt-encoder-url http://127.0.0.1:8764 \ --srt-encoder-timeout 100 \ --port 8898 \ --batching-mode dynamic \ --batching-max-size 4 \ --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics \ --ar-dit-overlap-mode on \ --host 0.0.0.0 ``` Before this PR ``` Benchmark duration: 223.79s Max request concurrency: 4 Successful requests: 10/10 signal.title: Fail fast for MXFP4 MegaMoE/DeepEP on non-SM100 GPUs
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes the late, misleading failure in #35557. Serving the stock MXFP4 `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with expert parallelism (`--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, i.e. MegaMoE) on **SM90 (Hopper)** crashes only at **decode CUDA-graph capture**, after a full weight load + MHC prewarm (~minutes): ``` Capture cuda graph failed: Assertion error (.../heuristics/.../layout.hpp:57): ab.scalar_type() == kPackedFP4 and arch_major == 10 ``` `arch_major == 10` is SM100. MegaMoE routes experts through DeepGEMM's packed-FP4 grouped GEMM, which is SM100-only; Hopper has no native FP4. The printed remedies (lower `--mem-fraction-static`, reduce `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`, disable the decode graph) don't apply to an architecture requirement — disabling the graph just moves the same kernel to eager decode. This has bitten more than one user (see #35557 and discussion #26564). ## Change Raise a clear error at MXFP4 quant-method construction — before weights load — when `use_mega_moe` is selected on a non-SM100 GPU, naming the two paths that **do** work on Hopper: - stock MXFP4 with **tensor parallelism** (Marlin backend; no `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`), or - the **FP8-converted** checkpoint (e.g. `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8`) for DP-attention + DeepEP. The guard is gated on `use_mega_moe`, so it is **inert** for: - the **FP8** MegaMoE path (DeepGEMM FP8 grouped GEMM runs on SM90), and - the non-MegaMoE **Marlin / FlashInfer** MXFP4 backends (which already gate on `is_sm90_supported()`). ## Notes / for review - This is an interim guard. The real fix is Hopper MXFP4 EP support (route the MegaMoE/DeepEP FP4 experts to the existing SM90 Marlin runner); I'm happy to work that separately and it would supersede this guard. Design discussion in #35557. - I could not run this on hardware (no local SM90 build); the change is a construction-time `raise`, and the placement mirrors the existing `is_sm90_supported()` checks in `mxfp4_marlin_moe.py`. A maintainer sanity-check on the hook point is welcome. - Minor: the guard fires for any non-SM100 GPU. SM120 would also fail the `arch_major == 10` assertion, so raising there is correct; if `is_sm100_supported()` is ever broadened to include SM120, this predicate should be revisited. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32291318181](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291318181)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32291317852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291317852)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Add configurable decode interval after prefill
signal.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation With DP attention, each rank schedules attention work locally while all ranks still participate in the same MoE collective. A rank with repeated chunked-prefill continuation work can therefore keep winning SGLang's prefill-first scheduling decision and starve decode work on peer ranks. In the AgentX workload this left requests waiting while the actual decode batch remained small. The DP-attention MLP-sync all-gather already exposes whether any rank selected an EXTEND batch. Use that globally synchronized signal to enforce a rank-consistent decode interval after prefill. ## Modifications - Add `--prefill-decode-interval N`, defaulting to `0` (disabled, so existing behavior is unchanged). - After an EXTEND batch, defer new prefill scheduling for the next `N` scheduler rounds so the running batch can decode. - Under DP attention, arm the interval from the existing globally synchronized `is_extend_in_batch` flag. Under non-DP scheduling, use the local forward mode. - Validate non-negative values and add focused scheduler/server-argument unit tests. No AIPerf source change is required. The benchmark prototype used the existing per-session routing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes batch selection cadence only; it does not change model math or sampling. - Added unit coverage for disabled, non-DP, globally synchronized DP, and decode/non-rearm behavior. - Added server-argument validation coverage. - `python -m py_compile` passed for all modified Python/test files. - The focused pytest command could not collect on the development VM because its base Python environment does not include `torch`/`numpy`; the new tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equivalent scheduler prototype was evaluated with full 3,600-second DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 AgentX runs on 8x B200 using TP8/DP8/EP8, DP attention, MTP3, and an interval of 16: | Concurrency | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | Cache hit | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 56 | 30.75532 | 23,559.05865 | 95.945% | | 84 | 23.24221 | 26,110.24296 | 94.703% | The c84 run completed 7,096 profiled requests with zero request errors. These results validate the equivalent prototype on SGLang v0.5.17; this PR ports the behavior onto current `main` using the existing global DP EXTEND flag. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32217562639](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217562639)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32217562470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217562470)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: dougyster

signal.title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` is an NCCL-symmetric-memory all-to-all engine with a fixed per-rank capacity. Fixed capacity means static communication shapes, which makes the MoE decode path CUDA-graph capturable under any topology — including multi-node, where legacy `low_latency` is not available as a graphable path. This PR adds it as a standalone backend `deepep_v2` alongside `deepep`; only expert-parallel dispatch/combine is replaced. Validated on Hopper (H20, H200) and Blackwell (B200 `sm_100`, B300 `sm_103`). ## Modifications - **`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** (new): the dispatcher. `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` selects the ElasticBuffer topology — **not** the legacy `normal/low_latency` split. Layout is chosen per batch by inference phase, not by comm mode: decode uses the expanded layout + masked GEMM (static shapes, graph-capturable, available under `hybrid` too), extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout. Single-shot `dispatch()/combine()` with a strict handle lifecycle; the guards run before the DeepEP import check so the module imports cleanly without DeepEP installed. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: masked-slab repack kernels. A fixed per-expert worker pool keeps the grid static (graph-safe); top-k weights are folded in-kernel; the scale copy takes the source pack-dim stride, which is what makes Blackwell's packed-UE8M0 (column-major) layout correct alongside Hopper's row-major fp32. - **`layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the FP8 adapter (masked decode / contiguous prefill, consuming DeepEP's 128-aligned psum directly as group offsets). `deep_gemm` is the only supported runner: deepep_v2 dispatches FP8 activations plus scales, and no other a2a backend targets a different runner family either. `--moe-runner-backend` is checked at startup, but the runner is chosen per layer by the quant method and several hard-select Triton regardless, so `MoeRunner` rejects the mismatch too — otherwise such a model would reach the permute registry and die on a bare assert after the weights are loaded. - **`layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`**: `get_moe_impl_class` resolves `deepep_v2` to `DeepEPMoE` like every other a2a backend — this is what makes the UE8M0 load-time weight requant apply on Blackwell. - **`server_args.py`, `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: the new flags; `ep_size` and `disable_shared_experts_fusion` are declared through the a2a passes, and the runner is validated against `resolved_view(...)` so a model declaration that restores an unsupported runner fails fast. Boot-time capacity check for the chunked-prefill budget. TBO/SBO and enforced shared-expert fusion are rejected at startup. - **`state_capturer/routed_experts.py`**: classify deepep_v2 as a scattered-a2a backend; otherwise `dp_rank > 0` reads unwritten buffer rows under `--enable-return-routed-experts`. - **No CI/Docker changes**: `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` already provides `ElasticBuffer`, so CI can exercise this backend as-is; it stays inert for every other configuration, fails fast when DeepEP is missing, and its unit tests need only Triton. ## Usage DeepEP v2 needs NCCL symmetric memory, which SGLang turns off by default (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` is set to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when the variable is unset), so an otherwise correct launch fails with `nccl.cu:104: Communicator does not support symmetric memory!`. Pass `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` (used for every benchmark here) or `--enable-symm-mem`, which also works but additionally enables NVLS and a 4 GB symmetric-memory prealloc. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` is the fixed per-rank buffer capacity. It must cover the per-rank chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size / dp_size` under DP attention), and that chunk must be a multiple of `page_size` — with `page_size=256, dp_size=8` the smallest usable pair is capacity 256 with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`. Smaller capacity is better for decode; prefill servers size it to their chunk budget and add `--disable-cuda-graph`. No extra install step: the pinned `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ships `ElasticBuffer` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`), so this backend runs on a stock environment. Re-validated on H20 x8 against that wheel with no source build and no code change -- `direct` GSM8K 0.970 / MMLU 0.890, `hybrid` 0.970 / 0.886, three-question gate passing in both modes. Earlier development used a DeepEP source build at `d4f41e4`; the packaged API is a superset of what the dispatcher calls. Multi-node: add `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid --enable-dp-lm-head --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1}`. Blackwell with a BF16 `wo_a` checkpoint: `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0`. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --ep 8 --enable-dp-attention`, `deep_gemm`, kv fp8. | | deepep_v2 `direct` | deepep_v2 `hybrid` | deepep | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 | | H20 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 | | B200 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | — | | B200 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | — | MMLU at 500 examples has a ~1.4pp standard error at this accuracy, which is wider than every gap in the table; repeat runs of one configuration spanned 0.884-0.896. These numbers show the absence of a systematic shift against the same-node `deepep` baseline, not a ranking. The three-question gate passes on every configuration above. Unit tests (CI, no DeepEP required): masked-slab repack including a production packed-UE8M0 scale and CUDA-graph capture/replay, handle-lifecycle guards, server-args resolution, capturer classification, plus a DP>1 routed-experts readback e2e. The three-question gate also passes on the multi-node configuration below. Earlier validation on the same dispatch path: needle retrieval across chunk boundaries and 8-way concurrent requests 24/24; prefill/decode disaggregation functional. ## Speed Tests | | deepep_v2 | deepep | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 | -0.9% | | H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 | +3.2% | | B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 | -2.8% | | B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 | +2.9% | Each backend pair was measured back-to-back on the same node, on torch 2.13 / sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, with the prefill cells interleaved so drift cannot bias one side. H20 prefill averages 4 samples per cell (sd 95 and 72), B200 prefill 2 per cell (sd 132 and 57); decode is one cell per side. Decode reproduces well across nodes -- deepep_v2 measured 8,385 / 8,403 / 8,429 tok/s on three different B200 nodes -- but the `deepep` side moved more, so the decode delta has landed between -0.9% and -2.8% across runs; read it as "a low single-digit percentage behind" rather than a precise figure. Prefill has been consistently ahead by roughly 3%. Multi-node (2x H20x8, TP16/EP16/DP16, `hybrid`, same protocol): **4,610 tok/s** decode with the masked-GEMM + CUDA-graph path over RDMA — a graphable cross-node decode path legacy `low_latency` does not provide — and **20,688 in_tok/s** prefill (two samples: 20,322 / 21,054). There is no same-fabric deepep baseline for this pair: DeepEP's NVSHMEM data plane does not complete across nodes on this RoCE setup, reproduced with DeepEP's own `test_internode.py` outside SGLang. Reproduction (5 rounds per boot, mean of the last 3; prefill flushes the radix cache before each round): ```bash # common: NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1, SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20, capacity 1024 # deepep_v2: --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct # deepep : --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency|normal --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype fp8 # (with SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024) NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --context-length 4096 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 $BACKEND_FLAGS \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 # decode # --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --disable-cuda-graph --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph # prefill # decode python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 128 # prefill (curl -s localhost:30000/flush_cache before each round) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 16 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (separate follow-up PR). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (above). - [x] Code style. ### Notes for reviewers - Prerequisites: none beyond the current pins -- `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` provides `ElasticBuffer`. NCCL symmetric memory must be on (see Usage). - Follow-ups: TBO/SBO comm-compute overlap (a PoC showed the naive two-phase split cannot overlap because `ElasticBuffer.dispatch` is host-blocking; it needs a `return_recv_hook`-style split in DeepEP), adapters for other MoE runners, documentation. Co-authored-by: jianxiongzhang <40026647+jianxiongzhang@users.noreply.github.com> <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32259471892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259471892)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32259470116](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259470116)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kimi K3] Select FlashInfer MXFP4 for SM107 auto MoE
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 packed-MXFP4 models automatically select the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE runner on SM100 and SM103, but the current exact-architecture gate excludes SM107. Consequently, `--moe-runner-backend auto` can fall through to BF16 weight materialization during model loading and exhaust device memory. This is a policy follow-up to #33997. It remains a draft until SGLang's stock FlashInfer artifacts are qualified for the SM107 SiTU MXFP4 path. ## Modifications - Extend Kimi-K3 packed-MXFP4 auto MoE selection from SM100/SM103 to exact SM107. - Preserve every explicit `--moe-runner-backend` choice. - Add unit coverage for the SM107 positive case, a neighboring-architecture negative case, non-MXFP4 input, registry wiring, and explicit backend choices. ## Accuracy Tests SM107 stock-artifact launch, numerics, and memory qualification is pending. This PR must remain in draft and must not merge until that qualification passes, with the pinned FlashInfer artifact/version updated if required. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Pending the same SM107 stock-artifact qualification. The intended comparison is `auto` against explicit `flashinfer_mxfp4`; this change should make those routes identical. ## Checklist - [x] Format the changed files with the repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add focused CPU unit coverage. - [x] No user-facing documentation change is required for this model-specific auto-selection extension. - [ ] Provide SM107 stock-artifact accuracy, memory, and performance results before marking ready. - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. ## Dependency / merge gate Do not merge until the stock FlashInfer artifacts used by SGLang are qualified for SM107 SiTU MXFP4, updating the pinned artifact/version if required. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32288065413](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32288065413)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32289143314](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32289143314)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [EAGLE] Prune draft-extend logits to selected rows
signal.text: ## Motivation During EAGLE draft extension under CUDA graph execution, the model computes full-vocabulary logits for every draft row even though the speculative worker only consumes selected per-request rows. The unnecessary LM-head rows increase graph time and temporary memory usage on the decode critical path. ## Modifications - Select the rows consumed by the speculative verifier before applying the LM head during draft-extend CUDA graph execution. - Keep the full six-row draft forward unchanged so hidden-state and speculative-state evolution remain identical. - Preserve the eager path and existing output contract while sizing the graph logits buffer for the selected rows. ## Accuracy Tests | Natural-acceptance metric | Baseline | Candidate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Completed requests | 112 / 112 | 112 / 112 | | Output length | 860 | 860 | | Mean acceptance length | 3.684250 | 3.652805 | | Acceptance rate | 0.536375 | 0.530488 | | CUDA graph enabled | Yes | Yes | | Queue / retractions / errors | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM-MHA, FlashInfer CuTeDSL MoE plus FlashInfer A2A for target and draft, NEXTN with 5 speculative steps and 6 draft tokens, online-NVFP4 draft weights, ReplaySSM circular history, Mamba `extra_buffer`, and CUDA graph tiers through batch 32. - Workload: one frozen 88,786-token input repeated as a 112-request cohort, 112 warmup requests with OSL 64, 112 measurement requests with exact OSL 860, temperature 0, fixed AL 4.8, and no request replenishment during the measured pure-generation interval. - Measurement gate: all four ranks must simultaneously report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no completion/drain row inside the selected interval. | Serving metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Stable rank intervals | 17 / 17 / 17 / 17 | 17 / 17 / 17 / 16 | — | | Mean context tokens/rank | 103,367.5 | 102,725.7 | -0.6209% | | Target-step host time | 29.688688 ms | 28.996720 ms | -0.691968 ms / -2.3307% | | Fixed-AL4.8 output tokens/s/GPU | 4,526.977 | 4,635.007 | +2.3864% | - To remove the small context difference, an independent exact-context match paired 40 windows at the same mean context of 102,342.4 tokens/rank and measured 4,542.499 to 4,653.987 output tokens/s/GPU (+2.4543%). - The final zero-resident-context drain row is excluded from both arms. | Nsight metric for draft-extend graph `10658` | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Graph time/GPU-step | 1.113471 ms | 0.974980 ms | -0.138491 ms / -12.44% | | Selected-row projection | 0.371574 ms | 0.296726 ms | -0.074848 ms | | Large output copy | 0.098430 ms | 0.017771 ms | -0.080659 ms | | Graph capture memory | 0.15 GB | 0.07 GB | -0.08 GB / -53.3% | - The Nsight capture contains 40 actual-B28 steps on every rank with CUDA graph enabled and queue depth 0. - Draft-decode graph `10637` still performs four full-vocabulary projections per target step by design; this optimization only owns draft-extend graph `10658`. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. - As a cross-engine diagnostic only, applying the measured within-SGL gain to the fixed-work authority gives 4,608.074 output tokens/s/GPU versus TRT-LLM at 4,791.788, or 96.166% with a 3.834% remaining gap; this does not replace a direct final integration comparison. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - signal.title: Fix multimodal draft embedding alignment
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35440. `forward_batch.mm_input_embeds` is consumed by EAGLE/MTP draft models, but the target forward can mutate the same tensor in place. Draft prefill also rotates each request's `input_ids` left by one without applying the same transform to the retained multimodal embeddings. The draft therefore receives corrupted and misaligned embeddings. ## Modifications - Snapshot fused multimodal embeddings before target execution for EAGLE-family speculative decoding only. - Shift the snapshot left within each request during draft prefill. Retain the final row for the existing per-request tail-token replacement. - Add registered CPU tests for in-place target mutation and mixed-length batch alignment. ## Validation - `pre-commit` on all changed files: passed. - CPU unit test: 2 passed. - Qwen3.5-27B BF16 + NEXTN/EAGLE on one H200, eager prefill: 512/512 image requests succeeded at concurrency 16; average speculative acceptance length was 2.02. - The same model with breakable prefill CUDA graph: target capture completed, scheduler logs confirmed `cuda graph: True`, and 64/64 image requests succeeded at concurrency 16. - Full GSM8K (1319 examples, temperature 0, top-p 0.95, max 4096): 97.35% accuracy, 99.70% stop-rate, 0 errors. The four truncated prompts are text-only model loops; native non-speculative replay reproduced three of the four, and the changed code is not reached for text-only requests. ## Related work #27647 and #27846 fixed per-request final-row replacement for batched multimodal draft prefill. This PR preserves that replacement and fixes the remaining snapshot ownership and prefix-row alignment problems. The implementation was written independently against current `main`; no code was copied or cherry-picked from those PRs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32223946498](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32223946498)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32223946212](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32223946212)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sglang-miles] RDT/NIXL weight sync support for Ray scheduler actors
signal.text: ## What sglang-side support for **RDT (Ray Direct Transport / NIXL) weight sync** — lets the [miles](https://github.com/radixark/miles) trainer push RL weights to rollout engines via a zero-copy RDMA pull instead of NCCL broadcast. Paired with the miles-side PR (radixark/miles#1313), which has the perf write-up. ## Changes - **`ray/scheduler_actor.py`** — add `pull_weights()`, which uses `ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref` to RDMA pre-sharded weight buckets directly into the model's `param.data` buffers (no intermediate receive buffers / copies). - **`ray/engine.py` + `ray/data_parallel_controller.py`** — register `SchedulerActor`s as **detached** named actors with the http **port** baked into the name, so the trainer (a different Ray job) can discover them via `list_named_actors` even when several engines share a node; raise `max_concurrency` so a concurrent `pull_weights` is not starved while `run_event_loop` blocks; set `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` so the absolute GPU id from `get_accelerator_ids()` stays valid. - **`server_args.py`** — add `enable_engine_info_bootstrap` to start the engine-info bootstrap server and register per-rank parallelism config **without** the mooncake/verbs P2P transfer-engine seeding. - **`entrypoints/engine.py` + `model_executor/model_runner.py`** — honor `enable_engine_info_bootstrap`; make the P2P transfer-engine memory registration non-fatal so EFA/verbs clusters where it fails don't crash the scheduler (RDT only needs the parallelism config). - **`model_loader/loader.py`** — make `post_load_weights` public so the RDT path can invoke it. - **`pyproject.toml`** — require `ray>=2.55.1` (`ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref`). ## Notes Targeting the `sglang-miles` integration branch; rebased onto current `sglang-miles` (#28001, #29339). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32286981791](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32286981791)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32286980991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32286980991)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
