signal.title: [GDN] Validate FlashInfer Cake CP prefill on Blackwell
signal.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer [#4539](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4539) replaces the SM100/SM103 CP-selected GDN prefill implementation with the Cake backend while preserving the public `chunk_gated_delta_rule` API and its `use_cp="auto"` policy. SGLang already calls that public API; this PR makes the auto policy explicit and adds an SGLang-level route/contract test for the new backend. This PR depends on FlashInfer #4539 and a subsequent FlashInfer release. It intentionally does not pin SGLang production dependencies to an unreleased Git commit; the new test skips when the installed FlashInfer build does not yet expose the Cake route. ## Modifications - Pass `use_cp="auto"` explicitly from `FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`. - Add an SM100/SM103 BF16 GQA generic-tail test through the real SGLang fixture and `FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`. - Require the test invocation to enter Cake exactly once and make the legacy SM100 non-CP route fatal. - Compare output and selected final-state rows against the same FlashInfer revision with `use_cp=False` at `atol=rtol=1e-2`. - Verify Q/K/V/gate/beta/cu-seqlens/cache indices and unselected state rows are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.3, driver 580.167.08: - Targeted SGLang pytest: `1 passed, 7 deselected` (Slurm job `518335`; the test executed rather than skipping). - Candidate route: FlashInfer #4539 Cake path; external/non-CP fallback is fatal. - The SGLang route test compares #4539 Cake against the same candidate revision with `use_cp=False`; output and selected final state match at `atol=rtol=1e-2`. - The benchmark runner independently repeats that numerical comparison on B=1, L=65 and enforces exact input and unselected-state immutability for every timed row. - Maximum observed absolute output error: `2.44140625e-4`. - Maximum observed absolute selected-state error: `3.90625e-3`. - Both candidate and baseline preserve all input tensors and unselected state rows exactly. Adapter evidence JSON SHA-256: `0dfe9da69166585bcfd176f32cadc688aaf7794e29d75d08429ac3c7e1a97c58`; evidence-manifest SHA-256: `df1f8b4d8ab7508e2288fc14a41be1e32a16b8ce5e8f5d8890804b44e200e3ee`. ### Model-level GSM8K On the same GB300, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` was evaluated on the same 200 GSM8K questions with 5-shot completion prompts, one request at a time, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=512`. Radix caching was disabled in both arms because FlashInfer CP prefill does not yet support the state-checkpoint outputs needed by SGLang's radix state tracking. | Prefill arm | GSM8K exact match | Difference vs. Triton | |---|---:|---:| | FlashInfer #4539 Cake | 178/200 (0.890) | 0.000 | | Triton control | 178/200 (0.890) | — | For the Cake arm, the live dispatcher must report `extend=FlashInferGDNKernel`, produce SM103 Cake cubins in a job-unique empty workspace, and contain zero non-CP fallback warnings. The Triton arm must report `extend=TritonGDNKernel` and produce no Cake cubins. Both arms must exceed the predeclared 0.80 accuracy threshold. This is an accuracy comparison, not an end-to-end speed claim: decode uses Triton in both arms and dominates the sequential evaluation latency. GSM8K Slurm job: `518440`; result JSON SHA-256: `82523bca3fd65c13031cb15a53ccd1486d3671c28d46cc8582a37e746ed3570e`; evidence-manifest SHA-256: `3c5d92df3f25c5cbf4fac24c59cc4691eecfd6bd1603010aeff49f5c33060703`; dataset SHA-256: `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.3, driver 580.167.08. These are SGLang adapter-level prefill calls (`FlashInferGDNKernel.extend`) with BF16 Q/K/V/state, Hq=Hk=2, Hv=8, D=128. Each row uses an exact shape cell present in the original PR4078 benchmark set. The BF16 SGLang input/state profile is stated separately and is not presented as PR4078's dtype profile; no additional shape rows are included. | Batch | Sequence lengths | #4539 Cake (ms) | Current upstream CP (ms) | Speedup | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | `[2048]` | 0.442594 | 0.436882 | 0.987x | | 1 | `[8192]` | 0.445762 | 0.463090 | 1.039x | | 4 | `[2048, 2048, 2048, 2048]` | 0.443410 | 0.461602 | 1.041x | Geometric-mean speedup: **1.022x**. The B=1, L=2048 row is a measured 1.3% regression; the other two rows improve by 3.9% and 4.1%, respectively. Method: same-process ABBA paired samples using Cake `bench_gpu_time_interleaved` (`bench_gpu_time`), required CUPTI GPU activity timing, cold-L2 flush before each sample, 20 ms warmup and 100 ms measurement budget per arm, and a steady-state SM clock gate. The rows collected 422, 342, and 392 samples per arm at 2070/2070 MHz in Slurm job `518335`. During timed rows, both candidate and baseline non-CP paths were fatal, so every measured call used the intended CP route; the dedicated correctness case intentionally invoked the candidate revision's non-CP path as its numerical reference. Commits: - SGLang: `5fc7baa6dd458f37fdf50d9ad4817ad17365e05e` - FlashInfer candidate: `59da61dd534f74ea3acf8ada60c4a3935e2a8df9` - Current upstream FlashInfer baseline: `05e5d927399d62a2479c430ad3e167738254d760` - Cake timing harness: `25536d8f0acd0eb4503d9fd6b46509b9ac76a115` ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the [formatting guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add a real SGLang route/contract test. - [x] Provide correctness and paired GPU performance results. - [x] Bind the final model-level GSM8K result. ## Review and Merge Process This remains a draft until FlashInfer #4539 is merged and available in an SGLang-supported FlashInfer release. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32286382201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32286382201)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32286381900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32286381900)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Qwen3.5][MTP] Preserve online NVFP4 draft quantization for mixed checkpoints
signal.text: ## Motivation When a mixed ModelOpt checkpoint is used with an explicitly configured `nvfp4_online` speculative draft model, checkpoint detection currently overwrites the explicit draft quantization choice with `modelopt_mixed`. This prevents the MTP draft MoE from using the intended load-time NVFP4 conversion and FlashInfer CuTeDSL execution path. ## Modifications - Preserve an explicitly selected `nvfp4_online` draft quantization mode for both `modelopt_fp4` and `modelopt_mixed` checkpoints. - Keep the existing default behavior unchanged: when the user does not explicitly select draft quantization, the draft model still inherits the target model quantization. - Do not change the speculative decoding algorithm or automatically enable online NVFP4 on unsupported configurations. ## Accuracy Tests - The Blackwell production serving validation completed 112/112 identical requests with HTTP 200, fixed input length 88,786 tokens, exact output length 860 tokens, all four ranks at achieved batch 28, all CUDA graph captures enabled, zero queueing/retractions/errors, and natural mean acceptance length 4.79792. - This path is explicitly opt-in and limited by the existing SM100+ and FlashInfer MoE backend checks. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs in DP4, fixed ISL 88,786, exact OSL 860, 112 identical requests, MTP with 6 draft tokens, TRTLLM-MHA split 1, ReplaySSM circular history, and no request replenishment during the pure-generation measurement window. - Patch-level result with the same candidate command: before this change, checkpoint detection overwrites the explicit `nvfp4_online` draft setting with `modelopt_mixed`, which creates an incompatible draft runner/dispatcher combination and fails before serving; after this change, the command completes 112/112 requests. Because the unpatched control does not reach the benchmark, there is no patch-only throughput ratio. - The throughput numbers below compare two valid end-to-end draft backend configurations and are not an apple-to-apple attribution of the three-line compatibility fix. - Valid legacy baseline command; orchestration-only and identical arguments are omitted: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4> --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep ``` - Candidate command enabled by this fix: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4> --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --speculative-moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-quantization nvfp4_online ``` - Full configuration change used by the throughput experiment: ```diff --- baseline +++ candidate - --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep + --speculative-moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --speculative-moe-a2a-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-quantization nvfp4_online ``` | Valid configuration | Natural mean acceptance length | Target-step time (ms) | Output tokens/s/GPU | Configuration-level change | SGL/TRT ratio | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | DeepGEMM + DeepEP draft baseline | 4.80208 | 31.13983 | 4,317.890 | — | 90.1891% | | FlashInfer CuTeDSL + FlashInfer A2A + online-NVFP4 draft | 4.79792 | 30.71904 | 4,373.238 | +1.282% | 91.3452% | | TRT-LLM reference | 4.8 (forced) | 28.07256 | 4,787.594 | Reference | 100% | - Relative to the legacy configuration, profiling of the complete candidate tuple removes approximately 1.3672 ms/target-step of draft DeepGEMM work and 0.4218 ms/target-step of draft DeepEP communication; overlap limits the end-to-end gain, so these times are not added arithmetically. - The measured +1.282% belongs to the full runner, A2A backend, and draft-quantization tuple. This PR only preserves the explicit quantization request so that tuple can start; it does not establish an online-NVFP4-only or same-backend speedup. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is measured only from the all-rank fixed-B28 pure-generation interval after the final prefill and before the first request completion; it is not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Support Intern-S2-Mobius FP8
signal.text: ## Motivation `internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8` is now public, but it does not load on current SGLang. The serialized FP8 config lists `.linear_attn` parents as exact `modules_to_not_convert` entries, while SGLang treats ignored-layer names as prefixes and consequently skips quantized child projections. Strict loading then also needs to map the checkpoint's fused expert scale tensors and allow omitted KV-cache scales. The existing Intern-S2-Mobius cookbook only exposes the BF16 checkpoint. ## Modifications - Preserve FP8 quantization for Mobius linear-attention qkv/z and output projections while retaining the checkpoint's child exclusions. - Load `gate_up_proj_scale_inv` and `down_proj_scale_inv` into the fused expert scale parameters. - Treat Mobius `attn.k_scale` and `attn.v_scale` as optional while still loading them when present. - Add the FP8 checkpoint to the cookbook selector with verified 1xH200 TP=1 high-throughput and NEXTN recipes. B200 recipes remain explicitly unverified. - Separate the existing BF16 benchmark claims from the new FP8 launch verification. No unit test is added: this is a serialized-checkpoint integration path, and a mock loader test would only restate the configured parameter mappings. The real checkpoint path is covered by the end-to-end gate below. ## Accuracy Tests Verified commit `59c8810358` on 1xH200 with checkpoint revision `ea369586a687b1f31d29c8b10868acf2cb8e2889`: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \ --context-length 262144 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \ --model internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-threads 64 ``` | Examples | Accuracy | Stop rate | Truncated | Error | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1319 | **96.82%** | **100.00%** | 0.00% | 0.00% | All 1319 prediction records reported `finish_reason=stop`. The documented NEXTN recipe also passed live smoke tests: - Text: `15% of 240` returned `36`, `finish_reason=stop`. - Vision: the standard tiger image returned `tiger`, `finish_reason=stop`, with 70 image tokens. - A 292-token bounded generation stopped normally; telemetry reported accept length 4.00 and accept rate 1.00 with decode CUDA graphs enabled. Local validation passed: changed-file `pre-commit`, `py_compile`, cookbook config consistency, `git diff --check`, and `mint validate`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No FP8 speed benchmark is claimed in this PR. The cookbook explicitly keeps the existing speed tables scoped to BF16. For capacity context, the high-throughput server loaded 34.22 GB of FP8 model weights. The NEXTN target+draft process used about 94 GB on H200 with the documented settings. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Not applicable; checkpoint integration is covered by the full e2e gate.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Accuracy provided; speed is explicitly out of scope.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: feat(sgl-router): --default-top-k / --default-top-p to set fleet-wide sampling defaults
signal.text: The router forwards requests to the engine, so sampling defaults are normally the engine's job (`generation_config.json` + `--sampling-defaults model`), which requires editing the checkpoint. These flags let an operator set a fleet-wide default `top_k` / `top_p` **at the router** instead. ## Behavior Mirrors the existing `--max-output-tokens` injection: the value is injected into the forwarded `/v1/chat/completions` body **only when the request omits the field** (absent or explicit `null`), so a **client-supplied `top_k` / `top_p` always wins**. Unset (the default) forwards the body untouched — **no behavior change**. - Per-model config, validated at startup: `top_p` in `(0, 1]`, `top_k >= 1`. - Implemented in `build_outgoing_body` alongside the `rid` / `input_ids` / `max_tokens` injections; `RequestProbe` peeks `top_k`/`top_p` to decide fill-if-absent via the new `default_when_absent` helper. - Scope: the `/v1/chat/completions` handler (the only route the router rewrites). ## Usage ``` --default-top-k 1000 --default-top-p 0.95 ``` ## Tests - `default_when_absent`: fills only when missing; client value wins; `null` treated as absent. - `build_outgoing_body` injects both values. - CLI flags reach `ModelConfig` and reject out-of-range values. Verified on a CPU devbox against the sgl-router CI checks: `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo +nightly fmt -- --check` all clean; full `cargo test` green (lib 955, bin 3, component 57, proxy 118 — 0 failed). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32283354838](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32283354838)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32283354394](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32283354394)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Support MiniMax H3 on Ascend NPU's
signal.text: ## Motivation Extend the native MiniMax-H3 pipeline introduced in [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275) to Ascend NPU. MiniMax-H3 packs real multimodal tokens together with sequence-parallel alignment padding. Its attention path is therefore variable-length even when request batch size is one: the real-token segment and the alignment-padding segment must remain isolated. ## Scope and related work - [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275) provides the upstream MiniMax-H3 model and pipeline implementation that this PR extends. - [#33366](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33366) is the related XPU enablement PR. This PR does not include XPU backend code; shared paths use `current_platform` so the Ascend changes remain isolated and existing CUDA/ROCm behavior is preserved. - Experimental NPU RoPE, gate, and standalone SwiGLU kernel/registry paths were removed after benchmarking. The VAE reuses the existing runtime NPU SwiGLU implementation where gated SiLU is required. ## Bug fixes and upstream root causes During rebases onto current `main`, this PR also fixes or preserves fixes for the following MiniMax-H3/Ascend regressions: - [#33667](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33667) added the packed Ulysses Q/K/V Triton relayout. Its launch can exceed Ascend's program/core limit for MiniMax-H3 sequence lengths, so NPU uses the portable destination-major packing fallback while CUDA/ROCm keep the fused path. - [#34085](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34085) refactored the shared diffusion/USP JIT fast paths. The USP merge-head eligibility check now requires a real CUDA platform, preventing `diffusion_usp_relayout` from invoking NVCC on NPU. - [#33827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33827) enabled Cache-DiT for MiniMax-H3 and exposed BCG's padded boundary form `[0, used, source_seq]`. Laser derives the real-token boundary from `cu_seqlens_host[1]`, rather than comparing it with `max_seqlen`, so alignment padding is still detected when `used != source_seq`. - [#34575](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34575) provides the FSDP2 custom-forward registration used by MiniMax-H3. This PR preserves that behavior for `encode_ids`, preventing FL2VA keyframe encoding from mixing sharded `DTensor` parameters with ordinary tensors. - [#34736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34736) unified component residency but removed automatic FSDP CPU offload for shardable text encoders. That made a two-NPU 950 H3 launch copy the complete 47.97 GB text encoder onto each NPU alongside the resident DiT and VAEs, reaching about 106 GB and failing during warmup. The loader restores FSDP2 CPU offload for shardable text encoders with explicit shard conditions and marks it for the new residency manager. - [#33927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33927) reports late MiniMax-H3 output loss when FFmpeg is unavailable. NPU Docker/CI now install FFmpeg, and startup fails early with an actionable error instead of losing the generated output during encoding. ## Modifications ### Ascend Flash Attention - Add `forward_varlen` using `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score` with the `TND` layout and actual packed-sequence lengths. - Preserve independent packed-sequence boundaries. - Repack strided Ulysses Q/K/V views with one allocation instead of three independent contiguous copies. - Preserve the segmented fallback for causal attention. ### Laser Attention - Enable `laser_attn` for MiniMax-H3. - Add variable-length handling so real tokens cannot attend alignment padding. - Run attention only for the real-token segment, retain padding rows for sequence-parallel shape alignment, and zero-fill their output instead of computing attention for them. - Preserve BF16 activation range when the FP16 Laser kernel is used by compensating the Q/K softmax scale and restoring the value/output scale. - Limit this BF16 compensation to MiniMax-H3's packed variable-length path; the existing dense Laser path keeps its previous behavior. ### NPU dependencies and media output - Install `attentions*.whl` alongside the `deep_ep` and `sgl_kernel_npu` wheels from the pinned `sgl-kernel-npu` release archive in both the NPU Docker image and NPU CI. - Scope the missing-`attentions` layer-normalization warning to NPU. Layer normalization falls back to its native implementation; explicitly selecting Laser Attention without the package raises an actionable import error. - Install `ffmpeg` in the NPU Docker and CI environments and fail MiniMax-H3 startup early when required media tools are absent, preventing the late output loss reported in [#33927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33927). - Keep these dependency checks and warnings isolated from CUDA, ROCm, XPU, MUSA, and CPU. ### Ascend platform integration - Use `current_platform` for shared memory residency, RNG, autocast, and denoising dispatch. - Add NPU support to component offload/cache-release handling while preserving CUDA/ROCm behavior. - Keep Qwen3-VL position IDs and rotary embeddings on the execution device only on NPU. - Avoid enabling Ascend-specific behavior on XPU, MUSA, or CPU. - Add the validated eight-NPU TP2 + SP4 launch command and a four-NPU TP2 + SP2 variant to the MiniMax-H3 cookbook. Both commands list the benchmarked Cache-DiT configuration and pass `--dit-cpu-offload false` to keep the DiT resident; the cookbook records 55.07 s and 103.57 s end-to-end latency respectively. ### FL2VA keyframe encoding - Register `MiniMaxH3Qwen3VLEncoder.encode_ids` as an FSDP2 forward method when text-encoder CPU offload is active. - Ensure the root FSDP hooks materialize non-layer parameters, including the Qwen3-VL vision `Conv3d` patch embedding, before image-conditioned encoding. - Prevent the `aten.convolution` mixed `torch.Tensor`/`DTensor` failure observed by FL2VA requests. - Keep the change platform-independent and limited to FSDP-wrapped encoders that expose `encode_ids`; non-FSDP execution is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Validated end-to-end 5-second MiniMax-H3 T2VA generation with both Ascend Flash Attention and Laser Attention on 8 Ascend NPUs. Image-conditioned FL2VA was also validated with Laser Attention after the FSDP2 custom-forward fix. Server startup: ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 \ HCCL_BUFFSIZE=256 sglang serve \ --model-path ./weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --num-gpus 8 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 4 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --port 30088 ``` For a four-NPU host, use TP2 + SP2: ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 \ HCCL_BUFFSIZE=256 sglang serve \ --model-path ./weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --num-gpus 4 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 2 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --port 30088 ``` Use `--attention-backend fa` to validate the Ascend Flash Attention path. T2VA request: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30088/v1/videos \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3", "prompt": "At night, while their owner sleeps in a bedroom, three cats march in loudly playing tiny brass instruments, then abruptly file out.", "seconds": 5, "task": "t2va", "conditions": [], "target": { "short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0 }, "num_outputs_per_prompt": 1, "num_inference_steps": 50, "flow_shift": 12.0, "audio_flow_shift": 3.0, "seed": 1101 }' ``` Result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fd97552-b6ce-446c-b8d2-c26f61f7c91f FL2VA request: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30088/v1/videos \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3", "prompt": "The supplied frame continues with calm, natural motion and synchronized ambient sound.", "seconds": 5, "task": "fl2va", "conditions": [ { "type": "image", "uri": "./Forest.jpg", "role": "keyframe", "frame_index": 0 } ], "target": { "short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "auto", "duration_seconds": 5.0 }, "num_outputs_per_prompt": 1, "num_inference_steps": 50, "flow_shift": 12.0, "audio_flow_shift": 3.0, "seed": 2101 }' ``` Forest.jpg Result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cad1f72-86f4-45c2-bc70-5f8d4831ef97 ## Speed Tests and Profiling The Ascend FA path performs one packed `TND` attention operation using actual sequence lengths. For strided Ulysses tensors, Q/K/V are repacked through one allocation. Laser Attention computes only the real-token segment and zero-fills alignment-padding outputs, avoiding the previous short-segment fallback calculation. FA vs Laser Attention on T2VA: | Attention backend | Topology | End-to-end generation time | Speedup vs. 8-NPU FA | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ascend Flash Attention | 8 NPUs, TP2 + SP4 | 69.51 s | 1.00× | | Laser Attention | 8 NPUs, TP2 + SP4 | 55.07 s | 1.26× | | Laser Attention | 4 NPUs, TP2 + SP2 | 103.57 s | — | On the same eight-NPU topology, Laser Attention reduced end-to-end generation time by 20.8% compared with Ascend Flash Attention. The attention measurements use the same 5-second T2VA request at 1344×768, 124 frames, 24 FPS, 50 inference steps, and seed 1101. The launch commands list the measured Cache-DiT configuration explicitly: `FN=2`, `BN=1`, `WARMUP=4`, `RDT=0.4`, `MC=4`, TaylorSeer enabled, and TaylorSeer order 2. They also pass `--dit-cpu-offload false` so the transformer remains resident on the NPUs; allowing the automatic CPU-offload policy reduces peak device memory but adds transfer latency. Experimental NPU RoPE, SwiGLU, and gate kernels were disabled; they are not present in the final PR. Laser Attention performance: T2VA: FL2VA: ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: TP/PP Consensus checker
signal.text: ## Motivation We have spent a lot of time in investigation into PP/TP divergence issues. The most difficult problems is that, when PP/TP divergence happens (e.g. the server hangs), you will have the stacktrace, but it is not the real time-point which divergence happens. Think of a case. A PP/TP divergence may happen silently, forr example, the kv cache available memory size differs because of a software bug. The server continue to process requests. When a single request is accepted in TP0 but rejected in TP1, the batch size diverges, and then the server hangs. However, the request is just a victim, not the trigger. We have to find the trigger request to figure out why this happens. This PR introduces a **consensus checker**, which checks for early divergence. There are two ways to use the consensus checker. 1. (Prefered) Using `@rank_consensus_checker` decorator. This decorator checks that `check_prefetch_progress` is called at **every rank** with **identical parameters and results**. If this assertion breaks, the server will abort. ```py @rank_consensus(same_params=True, same_results=True) def check_prefetch_progress(self, req_id: str) -> bool: ... ``` You can also check consensus of one of the parameters or one field of a parameter, like `rank_consensus(same_params=["len(foo)", "operation.req_id"])`. it internally calls `assert_same`. 2. Call `rank_consensus_checker.assert_same`. You can alternatively call `rank_consensus_checker.assert_same` programmatically in a function. The function takes a string, which must be same over all ranks. Both `@rank_consensus` and `assert_same` must be called in the scheduler thread. Here is an example that divergence is detected. The results of `check_prefetch_progress` differ in PP0 and PP1. ## Modifications 1. Add a environment variable `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER`, which enables the consensus checker. **Default to false**. 2. Add `rank_consensus_checker.py`. It simply creates a background thread. When `assert_same` is called, it pushes a message to a queue. The background thread consumes the queue of events, and compares events with other ranks. Unless divergence, all ranks must have the same sequence of events. 3. Add `@rank_consenus` to a few functions in hicache code. This work is in progress. Feel free to talk to me if you have better idea, e.g. more convenient decorator, better naming, which code to add the decorator, etc. ## Test ### Effectiveness With rank consensus checker enabled, we could detect PP divergence with L3 in a few minutes. The problem is fixed after patching #27010. Use the following command to reproduce this. ```sh nohup env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1 \ sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --tp-size=1 \ --pp-size=2 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=$((64*1024)) \ --hicache-ratio=2 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "128gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' \ > sglang.log 2>&1 & python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \ --num-clients=32 \ --num-rounds=10 \ --disable-auto-run \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --enable-round-barrier \ --request-rate 1 ``` ### Performance Tested 3 groups: - A: Baseline (4a5d7d3c). - B: This PR, with consensus checker **disabled** - C: This PR, with consensus checker **enabled** Conconlusion: There is no overhead when then checker is disabled compared the baseline. Testing commands: ```sh nohup env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1 \ sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=$((64*1024)) \ --hicache-ratio=2 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "128gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' \ > sglang.log 2>&1 & python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \ --num-clients=32 \ --num-rounds=10 \ --disable-auto-run \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --enable-round-barrier \ --request-rate 1 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [DSA] Page-aware move_kv_cache for the DSA indexer cache (fix page_size>1 corruption)
signal.text: ## Motivation `IndexKeyCache.move` (reached from `DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache`) moves the DSA indexer cache with a whole-row copy per token: ```python for index_k in self.buffer: # PAGE-indexed: (num_pages, page_size*(...)) index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] # tgt/src are per-TOKEN locations ``` The buffer is **page-indexed**. Dim-0 is the page. Inside one page row, the `page_size` fp8 keys come first as one block, then a block of `page_size` fp32 scales. But `tgt_loc/src_loc` are **token** locations. Using them on dim-0 is only right when `page_size == 1`. At `page_size == 64` the token locations go up to `size`, which is far past `num_pages ≈ size/64`, so the copy hits the **wrong page row, or goes out of bounds**. This is not a small numeric error. An out-of-bounds row index crashes or trips a device assert, and a wrong-page write scrambles the indexer cache. Either way DSA top-k selection breaks. ## Why CUDA has not hit this This move only runs on the **`topk>1`** path, through `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache`. CUDA DSA runs EAGLE/MTP with **`topk == 1`** (the linear chain), so the path never executes there. `page_size == 64` is normal on CUDA DSA, but the buggy move never runs, which is why nothing has broken so far even though the bug is not ROCm specific. That is also why the test below needs no GPU: there is no end-to-end repro to ship until `topk>1` drafting is enabled on DSA. ## Modifications Map each token location to its `(page, offset)` and move both of its pieces, the fp8 key and the fp32 scale, through `as_strided` views over the two blocks in a page row: ```python sc = hd // pool.quant_block_size * 4 # scale bytes per token, same formula as _buffer_shape fp8 = index_k.as_strided((num_pages, ps, hd), (row_stride, hd, 1), base) scale = index_k.as_strided((num_pages, ps, sc), (row_stride, sc, 1), base + ps*hd) fp8[tgt_page, tgt_off] = fp8[src_page, src_off] # the right side gathers into a new tensor scale[tgt_page, tgt_off] = scale[src_page, src_off] # before the write, so overlap is safe ``` This works for any page size and covers the old `page_size == 1` case, so the per-token row copy goes away. The base MLA `super().move_kv_cache` (token-indexed, already correct) is untouched, and so is the 0-row placeholder skip for skip-topk layers. > Rebased onto current `main`: the DSA index buffer now sits behind the `IndexKeyCache` facade, so the > fix lands in `IndexKeyCache.move` instead of `memory_pool.py`. That refactor copied the bug over > unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_move_kv_cache.py` — **3/3 pass**, no GPU needed. It builds the page-packed buffer by hand, gives each token a unique value in both its key and its scale, moves a set that crosses pages at varied offsets, and checks every moved token plus one untouched token. On `main` the `page_size == 64` case fails with `IndexError: index 66 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 4`. One case covers the scale width. `_buffer_shape` computes scale bytes as `index_head_dim // quant_block_size * 4`, which is 4 only while those two are equal. The test uses `quant_block_size=64` so the width is 8, and it fails if the view hard-codes 4. <details> <summary>How to reproduce</summary> ```bash # Unit tests, no GPU needed for the logic, but pass the devices anyway: importing sglang # pulls in aiter, which runs rocminfo at import time. docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_move_kv_cache.py -q' # Red on main: restore the old code first, then the page_size == 64 case fails. git checkout origin/main -- python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py # Show that the fixed path cannot be reached today: this refuses to start. python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --speculative-algorithm NGRAM --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 4 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 --port 30000 ``` </details> ## Please read before prioritising The code is wrong and the test proves it, but **nothing can reach it today**. Both callers need `speculative_eagle_topk > 1`, and `speculative_hook.py` rejects `topk>1` together with `page_size>1` unless the attention backend is `flashinfer/fa3/triton` (EAGLE) or `flashinfer` (NGRAM). DSA forces `backend="dsa"` with `page_size=64`, so it is in neither list. Confirmed by running it — NGRAM on GLM-5.2 refuses to start: ``` ValueError: speculative_eagle_topk(10) > 1 with page_size(64) > 1 is unstable and produces incorrect results for paged attention backends. This combination is only supported for the 'flashinfer' backend. ``` So this is groundwork for turning on `topk>1` tree drafting with DSA later, not a fix for something users hit now. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The fixed path is not reachable in any startable configuration (see below), and the change is a pure indexing correction with no extra work per moved token. ## AI assistance This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The AI helped with the rebase and conflict resolution, wrote the unit tests, and ran the measurements reported above. All code and results were reviewed and verified by the author on real hardware; the commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32282533018](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32282533018)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32282532789](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32282532789)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [ROCm] Fix EAGLE spec-decode verify silently sampling greedy on HIP
signal.text: ## Motivation On ROCm/HIP, EAGLE speculative decoding **always commits `argmax` (greedy) in verify**. It ignores `temperature` and `top_p`: ```python if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: target_predict = torch.argmax(...) # greedy ``` `_is_hip` is in that list because the sampling-verify ops (`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`, `top_k_renorm_prob`, `top_p_renorm_prob`) are only imported under `is_cuda()/is_musa()`. So **any EAGLE spec-decode run at `temperature>0` on ROCm decodes greedy**. On long reasoning output that turns into repetition loops. This is not model specific. ## Modifications 1. `eagle_utils.py` — move the check into a small `_verify_uses_greedy(...)` helper, which returns exactly the old answer on every non-HIP platform. Add a Triton top-p renorm (pivot binary search) and a HIP wrapper to stand in for the CUDA-only sgl_kernel ops, and guard the CUDA-only imports. HIP then goes through the pure-Triton `chain_speculative_sampling_triton`. 2. `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` — turn on `speculative_use_rejection_sampling` by default on HIP for EAGLE/EAGLE3 with topk==1, default accept thresholds, and non-deterministic mode, so users do not have to know about a flag. These conditions are a strict subset of the checks that raise just below, so turning it on can never break a config that used to work. ## Accuracy Tests Both sides were run on this branch with the same settings. Only the patch differs. GLM-5.2-FP8, 8x MI355X, NEXTN spec decode (`num_steps=1, eagle_topk=1, draft_tokens=2`), GPQA-Diamond 198 questions, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=98304`. | | old code | this PR | |---|---|---| | **GPQA-Diamond** | **0.702 ± 0.033** | **0.904 ± 0.021** | | answers that used up the whole token budget | **78/198 (39.4%)** | **5/198 (2.5%)** | | mean response length | 134,921 chars | 7,860 chars | | accuracy on answers that did finish | 0.9333 | 0.9223 | **+20.2 points, about 5.2 sigma.** The cause is not model quality. On the questions where the old code finishes, it scores 0.9333, which matches the patched build. It loses because **39.4% of its answers never finish**: greedy verify at `temperature>0` falls into repetition loops and burns the whole budget without giving an answer. You can also see it in wall-clock time (about 2x) and in a first attempt that died because requests went past the default 1800s per-request timeout. A probe on a non-greedy batch confirms which branch runs: old code takes `GREEDY(argmax)`, this PR takes `SAMPLING`. The same run shows the `speculative_hook.py` half working, with the server logging `enabling speculative_use_rejection_sampling by default` and no error. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a correctness fix; the sampling path costs the same. Throughput under NEXTN spec decode on GSM8K n=200: 740-771 tok/s before, 764 tok/s after. **GSM8K cannot show this bug** because it runs greedy, so argmax is already the right answer there. It is only a no-regression check: 0.945-0.960 old vs 0.940 patched at n=200, throughput 740-771 vs 764 tok/s. ## Known gaps (pre-existing, not regressions) On HIP, EAGLE topk==1 with `--enable-deterministic-inference` or non-default accept thresholds is left alone on purpose, because rejection sampling really is incompatible there. HIP **tree drafting** (topk>1) still uses greedy, because the Triton chain sampler only handles chains. `_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip` decides whether to run the top-k sort with `bool((top_ks < vocab).any())`, which is a device sync on every verify step. Passing `sampling_info.need_top_k_sampling` and `need_top_p_sampling` (what the CUDA branch already uses) would remove it. That measured well under 0.5% of a decode step, so I left it out to keep this PR a pure bug fix whose numbers match the code. <details> <summary>How to reproduce</summary> Image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`, `/data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8`. Use FP8, **not** MXFP4: on that image `quark.py` imports a name its `overrides.py` does not have, so the server dies while loading weights. ```bash # Unit tests. Pass the GPU devices even for CPU-only tests: importing sglang pulls in aiter, # which runs rocminfo at import time. docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py \ test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py -q' # Serve with spec decode python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --context-length 163840 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --port 30000 # GPQA-Diamond. lm-eval pinned at b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476, # task gpqa_diamond_cot_n_shot. python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --tasks gpqa_diamond.yaml --output_path "$RESULTS" --log_samples \ --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:30000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,\ eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=64,timeout=7200,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=163840" \ --limit 198 --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=98304,temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95" ``` `--limit 198` takes one permutation per question (`process_docs` uses `n_repeats=2`). You need `HF_TOKEN`, the dataset is gated. lm-eval has to fall back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty, or every graded answer from a thinking model is an empty string. Two things to watch when probing the branch. Gate the probe on `not sampling_info.is_all_greedy`: server warmup sends a greedy request, so a plain one-shot probe tells you nothing. And do not use output diversity as a test: the old code still returns 8 out of 8 different completions at `temperature=1.0`, because the bonus token goes through the normal sampler. </details> ## AI assistance This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The AI helped with the rebase and conflict resolution, wrote the unit tests, and ran the measurements reported above. All code and results were reviewed and verified by the author on real hardware; the commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32282530690](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32282530690)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32282530462](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32282530462)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [GLM-5.2] Keep GlmMoeDsa MoE e_score_correction_bias in fp32
signal.text: ## Motivation GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`) keeps `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32. The values sit in a narrow band at a large offset: measured `[+6.817, +7.063]`, so a range of 0.246. At that magnitude bf16 can only step by 0.03125. But `MoEGate.__init__` allocates the parameter as **bf16** when a `quant_config` is present. So the values are lost when the weights load: 238 different biases become 8. `noaux_tc` uses this bias to pick experts, so top-k routing changes for almost every token. The CUDA grouped-topk paths keep the bias in fp32. Only the aiter path casts it down. ## Modifications 1. `models/deepseek_v2.py` — skip both bf16 downcasts for `GlmMoeDsa`, so the parameter stays fp32. The substring matches the main model and the NextN draft head. 2. `layers/moe/topk.py` — in the aiter `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` path, keep a bias that is **already fp32** in fp32 instead of casting it to the gating dtype. This checks the dtype, not the model name, so a bias that arrives as bf16 behaves exactly as before. You need both. Without (2) the fp32 parameter is cast back down at the aiter call. ## Accuracy Tests **The routing measurement is what this PR rests on.** I added a probe to `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` that routes the *same real* `gating_output` twice: once with the true fp32 bias, once with the bf16 version. Over 400 MoE calls / 203k tokens on GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8: | build | bias values (fp32 / bf16) | tokens that pick a different top-8 | |---|---|---| | old code | **8 / 8** | 0.00% | | this PR | **224 / 8** | **98.50%** | The `fp32=8` on the first row is the bug itself. The values are already gone before the kernel runs. So if you only probe the old code you see 0% and think nothing is wrong. **Accuracy benchmarks do not show this, and that is expected.** MoE experts overlap in what they do, so sending a token to a different expert does not have to change the answer: | eval | old code | this PR | |---|---|---| | GSM8K (1319) | 0.941 | 0.947 | | GPQA-Diamond (396, no spec decode) | 0.8333 ± 0.0188 | 0.8182 ± 0.0194 | Both gaps are smaller than the error bars, and GSM8K is already near its ceiling (~94%) for this model. Please judge this as a routing correctness fix, not by a benchmark number. Biases centred near zero are fine (Kimi-K3 keeps 644 of 896 values), which is why the fix is scoped instead of applied everywhere. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Keeping fp32 means `gating_output` is cast up for the aiter call. I measured the call: 16.5 us before, 21.0 us after. The **+4.5 us is flat** and does not grow with token count, so it is the cost of launching the cast, not bandwidth. Across 75 MoE layers that is 338 us per forward, about 1.2% of a 29 ms decode step. That is an upper bound, because decode runs under CUDA graphs. End-to-end GSM8K got no slower (643.9 → 699.3 tok/s at n=200, 947.1 → 970.0 at n=1319). <details> <summary>How to reproduce</summary> 8x MI355X, image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`, `/data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8`. Use FP8, **not** MXFP4: on that image `quark.py` imports a name that its `overrides.py` does not have, so the server dies while loading weights. FP8 is in the same `("fp8","compressed_tensors","quark")` tuple, so it hits the same code. ```bash # Unit tests. Pass the GPU devices even for CPU-only tests: importing sglang pulls in aiter, # which runs rocminfo at import time. docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_glmmoedsa_correction_bias_fp32.py -q' # Serve python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 30000 # GPQA-Diamond, used for the no-regression number above. # lm-eval pinned at b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476, task gpqa_diamond_cot_n_shot. python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --tasks gpqa_diamond.yaml --output_path "$RESULTS" --log_samples \ --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:30000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,\ eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=64,timeout=7200,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=163840" \ --limit 198 --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=98304,temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95" ``` You need `HF_TOKEN`, the dataset is gated. lm-eval has to fall back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty, or every graded answer from a thinking model is an empty string. For the routing probe, add a one-shot comparison right before the `aiter_biased_grouped_topk(...)` call and send any short workload. **Run it with this PR applied.** On the old code it prints `fp32=8 bf16=8` and 0% divergence, for the reason above. </details> ## AI assistance This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The AI helped with the rebase and conflict resolution, wrote the unit tests, and ran the measurements reported above. All code and results were reviewed and verified by the author on real hardware; the commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32282528583](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32282528583)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32282528274](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32282528274)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: Migrates the Qwen3.6 cookbook page to the **config-driven Deployment/Playground engine** (as for DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen3.5) and adds **measured speed benchmarks**. The legacy `qwen36-deployment.jsx` generator is removed. ## Config — `configs/qwen/qwen3.6.jsx` (44 cells) `h100/h200/b200/b300` × `{35B-A3B (MoE), 27B (Dense)}` × `{bf16, fp8, +nvfp4 on Blackwell}` × `{low-latency, high-throughput}`, plus **Xeon `balanced`** (27B/35B-A3B × bf16/fp8). low-latency = MTP/EAGLE + mamba radix-cache v2; high-throughput = MTP off; Xeon = spec unsupported → single `balanced` recipe (`--device cpu`, tp 3/6). GPU cells tp=1 single-node. ## Faithfulness - Cells reproduce the generator command **verbatim** — verified by executing `generateCommand()` across the matrix: **42/44 exact**. Parsers (`--reasoning-parser`/`--tool-call-parser`) omitted (Playground-only; DSv4 convention). - The 2 non-verbatim cells are **b300 35B-A3B NVFP4**, adding `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: the generator's default moe runner crashes on that model on 0.5.16, and this is exactly how b300 was measured. - Bench = `bench_serving` random isl 8192 / osl 1024, `--random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 64 --flush-cache`; LL @ conc 1+16, HT @ conc 1024+4096. `tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = output_throughput / tp × (isl+osl)/osl`. ## Coverage — 32/44 measured - Measured: **B200 (12) @ 0.5.15, H200 (8) + B300 (12) @ 0.5.16**. - Pending (render "pending"): **H100 (8)** — no 8×H100 capacity this run; **Xeon (4)** — no CPU box (Deploy command shown, no speed). - Blackwell NVFP4 version note: b200 on 0.5.15 (default moe runner works → plain command), b300 on 0.5.16 (needs the flag) — **each cell matches its own bench**. ## Follow-ups - Bench H100 (8) once capacity frees. - Re-bench b200 35B-A3B NVFP4 on 0.5.16 with `flashinfer_cutlass` to unify the Blackwell backend. - Apply the +13% mem0.92 tune to h200 35B-A3B bf16 HT (clean conc 1024+4096 re-bench). signal.title: Fix replicated (TP1) shared expert being summed by collectives that skip the MoE all-reduce
signal.text: ## Motivation The invariant, stated once: **a replicated (TP1) shared expert must never sit inside a tensor that a collective SUMs.** A TP-sharded shared expert produces a genuine per-rank partial, so reducing over it is correct; a replicated one holds the identical full value on every rank, so any group SUM scales it by the group size — silently, once per layer. `DeepseekV2MoE` encodes this by adding the shared output *after* its own post-experts all-reduce. That guard only covers the reduction it performs itself. `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` lets a caller defer, replace, or absorb that reduction, and **every such caller inherits the invariant**. This PR fixes the two reachable callers that did not honour it: 1. the prefill-CP combine (`mlp_reduce_scatter`), on `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` and `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`; 2. `fuse_mlp_allreduce`, which does not remove the all-reduce but *defers* it into the next layer — a plain TP bug, no CP involved. Under DSA prefill context parallelism with `moe_a2a_backend=none`, a **replicated (TP1) shared expert is counted `cp_size` times instead of once, in every MoE layer**. `dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states` SUMs the MoE output across the CP group. That is correct for the routed experts — their per-rank outputs are genuine partial sums — but wrong for a TP1 shared expert, where every rank holds the identical full value. `DeepseekV2MoE` already guards against exactly this for its own reduction: ```python if self.tp_size > 1 and not should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(is_tp_path=True): final_hidden_states = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(final_hidden_states) # TP1 shared experts are replicated, so add them after all-reduce to # avoid summing the same shared output once per TP rank. if self._shared_expert_tp1: final_hidden_states += shared_output ``` But under CP that internal all-reduce is **skipped** (`mlp_reduce_scatter=True`, see `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce`) and the cross-rank sum happens later in the CP combine — outside the reach of that guard. The existing hoist that would have prevented this, `_do_shared_local`, is gated on `_use_tp_moe_gather`, which is `not _use_cp and ...` — so it never engages on the CP path: ```python _do_shared_local = ( _SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL and _use_tp_moe_gather # == not _use_cp and ... and getattr(self.mlp, "shared_experts", None) is not None and getattr(self.mlp, "_shared_expert_tp1", False) ) ``` Both CP MoE paths are affected: the eager path (`dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states`) and the TBO path (`op_cp_combine_a` → `attn_cp_overlap_reduce_scatter_tensor`). ### When it triggers Only when the shared expert is replicated on the `moe_a2a_backend=none` CP path, i.e. `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1` or `should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`. Neither is the default, which is why CI has not caught it. There is currently no CI coverage for CP-v1 on HIP at all. ### Which CP flavors can actually reach this `_deepseek_family_overrides` forces `moe_a2a_backend=deepep` for the **zigzag** DSA CP strategy and for **MLA CP**, and deepep takes the EP combine branch instead of the CP reduce-scatter. So only **`interleave` DSA CP with `moe_a2a_backend=none`** reaches the bug today, on both the DSv4 layer and the DSv2 layer. The new predicate still admits `mla_use_prefill_cp` so the guard survives if that override is relaxed; that arm is currently dead code and is **not** claimed as tested. ## Modifications - Add `cp_requires_shared_expert_hoist()` to `communicator_dsa_cp.py`, documenting the invariant next to the collective that depends on it. - Extend `_do_shared_local` to the CP path in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`, and make it **unconditional** there — deliberately not gated on `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL`, since correctness must not depend on a perf env var. The shared expert is a per-token MLP, so computing it on this rank's local rows before the gather is identical to computing it on the gathered buffer and keeping this rank's slice. - Apply the same hoist to the TBO CP path (`op_cp_gather_a` / `op_cp_moe` / `op_cp_combine_b`), mirroring what `op_gather_a` / `op_combine_b` already do for DP. - **Extend the hoist to `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`**, which reaches the same CP combine via `DSACPLayerCommunicator.postprocess_layer` -> `dsa_cp_reduce_scatter_hidden_states`. This covers `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (it subclasses `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`, so it uses this layer) and `deepseek_nextn`. - Close two latent gaps that would have made the hoist itself unsound: - `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal_dual_stream` ignored `skip_shared_experts` entirely, so on the capture-mode path the caller's hoisted add and the MoE's own add would *both* land. - `dsv2_flashinfer_moe_dual_stream_graph` cannot express "skip the shared expert", so `forward` now falls back to `forward_normal` when the caller hoisted it. A perf downgrade, confined to a configuration that would otherwise be numerically wrong. - Unit tests encoding the invariant. The `getattr` in the new helper is kept deliberately: a dense layer's `mlp` has no `shared_experts` attribute, and it cannot simply be pre-initialized to `None` because three sites in `deepseek_v2.py` branch on `hasattr(self, "shared_experts")` (lines 869, 1051, 1533 — the last one gates an early return). ### 2. `fuse_mlp_allreduce` defers the all-reduce past the guard Under fusion the decoder tags its output with `_sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion` and the **next** layer's `prepare_attn` performs the all-reduce as part of its residual+layernorm. By then the replicated shared output is already inside the tensor, so it is summed `tp_size` times. The guard is still there; it just no longer guards anything. Fixed by declining the fusion when the layer's mlp owns a replicated shared expert — a perf downgrade strictly confined to configurations that would otherwise be numerically wrong. Applies to `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` and `LagunaDecoderLayer`, the two decoders that both publish `fuse_mlp_allreduce` and can own a replicated shared expert. `glm4_moe_lite` assigns `_shared_expert_tp1 = False` and never reassigns it, so it is unaffected. Reachable with `moe_a2a_backend=none` (anything else makes `mlp_mode` SCATTERED, which disables fusion) + `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1` + no DP attention + `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` on ROCm or `--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` on sm90/sm100. `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion` is asserted off when `attn_cp_size > 1`, so this is disjoint from the CP path above. `has_replicated_shared_expert()` moves the predicate next to `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` in `layers/moe/utils.py`, where the skip reasons that create the hazard are enumerated; `cp_requires_shared_expert_hoist()` keeps its CP-specific docstring and delegates. It also learns the second attribute spelling — `DeepseekV2MoE` says `shared_experts`, `LagunaMoE` says `shared_expert`. ## Accuracy results MI355X, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark`, TP8, greedy, 53 **token-exact** prompt lengths from 56 to 2052 (sent as `input_ids` so no BOS/template shifts the count). Each arm is compared against its **own** non-CP reference at the same TP. | arm | top-1 match | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | TP4 no CP vs TP8 no CP (noise floor) | 51/53 (96%) | 0.098 | | **cp=4, before** | 16/53 (30%) | **1.524** | | **cp=8, before** | 7/53 (13%) | **2.834** | | cp=8, `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=0` (workaround) | 48/53 (91%) | 0.087 | | **cp=8, after this PR** | **50/53 (94%)** | **0.086** | Mean top-1 logprob: `-0.870` no CP, `-2.394` at cp=4, `-3.705` at cp=8, `-0.893` after the fix. The error growing with `cp_size` (2.83 nats at cp=8 vs 1.52 at cp=4, on a matched TP control that itself differs by only 0.098) is the signature of the per-rank duplication. After the fix, CP sits inside the same noise band as simply changing TP. The 3 remaining mismatches are lengths where the non-CP reference is itself run-to-run unstable. Two hypotheses were tested and excluded before landing on this one: batch padding to `cp_align_size` (CP still diverged at 9/11 lengths needing no padding), and DSA top-k selection (at these lengths `seq_len < index_topk=1024`, so top-k is a no-op). ### CP-v2 (`SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=1`) is cured by the same change CP-v2 goes through the same `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`, so it carries the identical double-count. At n=64, TP8, cp=8 (the only length CP-v2 currently runs at cp=8 on HIP, for unrelated reasons): | arm | top-1 token | logprob | |---|---|---| | non-CP TP8 reference | 566 | -0.908 | | CP-v2, unpatched | 201 | -3.302 | | CP-v2, after this PR | 566 | -1.325 | One fix, both CP implementations. To be precise about what is *not* claimed: after the fix CP-v2 is at 25/32 top-1 / mean |Δlogprob| 0.147, still above the 50/53 / 0.071 non-CP noise floor, whereas CP-v1 lands *at* the noise floor (50/53 / 0.086). That CP-v2 residual is a separate v2-specific defect (the HIP dsv4 backend never calls `apply_cp_reindex` under v2), not a shortfall of this fix. ### `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` coverage (GLM-5.1-FP8, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) 8x MI355X, `GLM-5.1-FP8` (78 layers, `n_shared_experts=1`), TP8, DSA prefill CP `interleave`, `attn_cp_size=8`, `moe_a2a_backend=none`, greedy, the same 53 token-exact prompt lengths. Each arm is compared against a **non-CP arm with the same `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1` setting**. | arm | top-1 match | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | no CP, TP1=1 vs no CP, TP1=0 (sharding-only noise floor) | 47/53 | 0.044 | | **CP, TP1=1, before** | 0/53 | **2.189** | | **CP, TP1=1, after this PR** | 3/53 | **0.926** | | CP, TP1=0 (shared expert TP-sharded, bug unreachable — bisection control) | 2/53 | 1.016 | The shared-expert component of the error goes **2.189 -> 0.926**, landing on the **1.016** of the arm where the shared expert is TP-sharded and this bug cannot occur. That is the whole of this defect. **Honest caveat:** the ~1.0 nat that remains in *both* CP arms is a **separate, pre-existing defect** in DSA prefill CP for this model on ROCm — it is present with a TP-sharded shared expert, so nothing in this PR can explain or fix it. This PR does not address it and does not claim to. (`SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=0` above is a bisection control, not a production setting.) ### `fuse_mlp_allreduce` (GLM-5.1-FP8, no CP) 8x MI355X, TP8, **no CP**, `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1`, `moe_a2a_backend=none`, greedy, the same 53 token-exact prompt lengths, against the same build with fusion off. | arm | top-1 match | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | noise floor (TP1=1 vs TP1=0, no fusion) | 47/53 | 0.044 | | **`fuse_mlp_allreduce` on, before** | 0/53 | **2.591** | | **`fuse_mlp_allreduce` on, after this PR** | 49/53 | **0.060** | The fix lands at the noise floor. On how the arms force fusion: they publish `fuse_mlp_allreduce` through a **test-only env gate** rather than `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, so the deferred reduction lands on the exact `moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` branch of `prepare_attn`. Fused and unfused are then mathematically identical *except* for where the shared output is added, which isolates this defect. Using the real flag was tried first and is unusable as a control: on this model and image the aiter fused AR+RMSNorm kernel in `_gather_hidden_states_and_residual` is independently lossy by ~2.45 nats, which swamps the signal. That is a separate issue and is not touched here. ### End-to-end in the deployment stack (PD-disagg + DSpark + HiCache + CP) DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, 1P1D PD-disaggregation over mori, TP8, prefill CP interleave cp=8, HiCache L2 (dram, ratio 3), unified radix tree on, DSpark speculative decoding, AgentX trace replay, 940 s at concurrency 16. Both arms on the same two nodes, differing only by the `deepseek_v4.py` overlay. | | unpatched | patched | |---|---|---| | requests completed / errors | 418 / **0** | 475 / **0** | | output throughput | 430 tok/s | 508 tok/s | | e2e p50 | 8,993 ms | 6,363 ms | | ITL p50 | 25 ms | 16 ms | | interactivity p50 | 40 tok/s | 61 tok/s | | prefix cache hit | 95.5% | 96.1% | | DSpark accept length | 1.55 – 1.95 | 2.36 – 2.60 | The point of this run is that the fix survives the full deployment stack with zero request errors, not the throughput delta. **Accept length is deliberately not offered as a quality metric here**: DSpark self-drafts, so a degenerate target model can be *easier* to predict from itself — on a different (synthetic-corpus) workload the unpatched CP arm scored the *highest* accept length of all arms. What is worth noting is only that the patched arm's 2.36–2.60 sits inside the known-good non-CP DSpark band (2.16 smoke / 2.45 AgentX) while the unpatched arm's does not. ## Adjacent gap, deliberately not fixed here `mlp_reduce_scatter` on the **DP** path is a third caller of the same invariant: with DP attention + `moe_a2a_backend=none` + reduce-scatterv (or max-len padding), `_scatter_hidden_states` SUMs across the TP group after the MoE's own all-reduce was skipped. `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` does hoist the shared expert there — but only when `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL` is set, i.e. a *perf* env var currently doubles as the correctness guard. `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` has no equivalent hoist at all. Reported rather than patched: I have not been able to validate a fix for it on hardware, and this PR's rule is that nothing lands unmeasured. ## Checklist - [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (black/isort applied to touched files) - [x] `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py` + `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_replicated_shared_expert_invariant.py` — 31 passed, 18 subtests - [x] Accuracy validated end-to-end on 8xMI355X: DSv4 layer on DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark; DSv2 layer and the fusion fix on GLM-5.1-FP8 Related: #34142 (CP-v1 interleave shard-pitch fix, still unmerged) and #35510 (the CP-v2 counterpart — note that one is a hardening change, not a live-bug fix: v2's per-rank padding rounds a one-row shard up to `cp_size` rows and `pad_local_rows`' `torch.cat` launders the stride, so the pitch anomaly is currently unreachable there). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32270851433](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32270851433)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32270851217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32270851217)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [XPU CI] Guardian bot: auto-disable PR on 2-run XPU regression (draft)
signal.text: ## Summary Draft — putting this up so it can be reviewed / iterated on tomorrow. Adds a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/xpu-ci-guardian.yml`) that watches `PR Test (XPU)` on `main`. When the last two consecutive runs on `main` fail, it opens a **draft** PR that inserts `disabled="..."` on the `register_xpu_ci(...)` marker for each failing test file and pings the XPU CI owner. A separate job auto-closes any open guardian PR once `main` goes green again. ## Design - **Watch** — schedule every 30 min + manual `workflow_dispatch` with a `dry_run` toggle. - **Detect (2-run rule)** — only acts when the last two runs on `main` both failed, so single flakes handled by `enable_retry` in `run_suite.py` don't trigger it. Also filters known infra-flake log patterns (`UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`, `Server failed to start`, `XPU out of memory`). - **Diagnose** — extracts `test/registered/**/*.py` paths from the failing job's `--log-failed`. - **Unblock (scope-limited)** — inserts `disabled="auto-disabled by xpu-ci-guardian: run <id>"` into the file's `register_xpu_ci(...)`. Never touches kernel code, test bodies, `run_suite.py`, or per-method `@unittest.skipIf`. Skips files that are already disabled and files that don't call `register_xpu_ci`. - **Dedup** — at most one open guardian PR at a time via the `xpu-ci-guardian` label. - **PR body** — lists failing files with the last 5 commits on each, so the reviewer can jump straight to the probable culprit (as PR #33431 was in the current fire). - **Sweep** — companion job closes any open guardian PR when the next main run is green. - **Never auto-merges** — PR opens as a draft and only a human can promote / merge it. ## Required secrets on the fork's Actions - `GITHUB_TOKEN` (default; read-only for detection). - `BOT_PR_TOKEN` — fine-grained PAT with `contents:write` on `arathi-hlab/sglang` and `pull-requests:write` on `sgl-project/sglang`. ## Enablement checklist (before turning it on) - [ ] Merge (or land into the fork only, if we decide it shouldn't live upstream). - [ ] Add `BOT_PR_TOKEN` secret on the fork. - [ ] Manually run once with `dry_run=true` and inspect the workflow's outputs. - [ ] Manually run once with `dry_run=false` against a known-failing history to confirm the PR body/format looks right. - [ ] Add the `xpu-ci-guardian` label to the label set on `sgl-project/sglang`. ## Explicitly out of scope for this bot - Auto-generating actual code / kernel fixes (LLM-authored kernel patches are wrong often enough that reviewing them costs more than writing them from scratch). - Deep classification (e.g. distinguishing correctness vs. accuracy assertions). The bot just disables; the human writes the fix. - Alerting for non-XPU CI. This is scoped narrowly on purpose. ## Test plan - [ ] Run the workflow manually with `dry_run=true` — the `detect` job should classify the current XPU state and set `act` correctly without opening any PR. - [ ] Run with `dry_run=false` on a synthetic branch where I forcibly log two failing runs, and confirm the PR opens with the right title / labels / reviewer. - [ ] Trigger `sweep-when-green` manually after a subsequent green run — it should close the previously-opened guardian PR. - [ ] Confirm the guardian PR does NOT open a second time while another is open (dedup by `xpu-ci-guardian` label). ## Not included yet (defer to follow-up) - Slack notification hook — trivial to add via `slackapi/slack-github-action` when a channel + token are chosen. - Nightly weekly-summary email of caught regressions. --- 🤖 Draft raised now so it can be reviewed tomorrow morning; happy to iterate on scope / triggers / notification medium. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32281257858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32281257858)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32281257526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32281257526)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
