signal.title: [AMD] Drop redundant FP8 bpreshuffle scale transpose via fused AR kernel
signal.text: Dependent on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4478, merged but need aiter update. ## Motivation On gfx95 (MI35x, ROCm >= 7.2) the gfx95 bpreshuffle FP8 block-scale GEMM consumes the per-group activation scale in a **column-major** layout, whereas the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group-FP8-quant kernel emits it **row-major**. To bridge the two, the fused-quant path in `layernorm.py` currently runs an explicit post-kernel transpose (`materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`, i.e. `scale.t().contiguous().t()`) on every eligible layer. That `.contiguous()` launches an extra copy kernel per fused-quant call — pure overhead in the decode-latency-bound regime where the model is dominated by many small kernel launches. aiter's fused kernel already has a compile-time `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` template (ROCm/aiter#3652) that can write the scale directly in the column-major layout the bpreshuffle GEMM wants, at zero extra cost (it only changes the store-index math). This PR plumbs that flag through so the fused kernel emits the transposed scale itself, and drops the redundant post-kernel transpose on the fused-success paths. The emitted layout is byte-for-byte identical to what `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` produced (column-major storage `(num_groups, M)` viewed as `(M, num_groups)`, stride `(1, M)`), so this is a numerics-preserving change. This is FP8-only. The MXFP4 path uses a different kernel (`custom_fused_ar_rms_mxfp4_quant`) and is untouched. **Dependency:** requires the paired aiter change that forwards `transpose_scale` through `custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / `fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / the ops stub to the (already capable) C++ op, plus a bundled-aiter pin bump. Without it, the fused-kernel call falls back (the flag is ignored / raises and is caught), so this PR should land together with / after the aiter bump. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/distributed/communication_op.py`: add a `transpose_scale` kwarg to `tensor_model_parallel_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it to the group coordinator. - `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: add `transpose_scale` to `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it into the `ca_comm.custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` call. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`: pass `transpose_scale=use_bpreshuffle` to both fused per-group-quant calls (the `keep_bf16=False` attention path and the `keep_bf16=True` GDN emit_bf16 path), and remove the now-redundant `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` on the two fused-success return paths. - The two separate-per-group-quant **fallback** paths intentionally keep `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`: `per_1x128_quant`'s own `transpose_scale` byte-shuffles the scale into a different physical arrangement, not the column-major layout this GEMM consumes. - The FP8 linear consumer (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`) is unchanged: the scale layout reaching it is identical, and its own `materialize` call becomes an idempotent no-op (`.contiguous()` short-circuits on an already-column-major tensor). ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4 (MI35x), `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, gsm8k (1319 questions): | Metric | Reference (with transpose) | This PR (fused transpose_scale) | |---|---|---| | Accuracy | 0.947 | **0.955** | | Invalid | 0.008 | 0.008 | Within run-to-run noise (marginally higher) — the change is numerics-preserving. ## Benchmarking and Profiling **Kernel-level confirmation (conc4 profile, IL8192/OL1024, 8 steps):** the fused kernel template flipped `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` false→true (`allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group<…Lb0ELb0E>` → `<…Lb0ELb1E>`, 354 calls; `local_device_load_rmsnorm_quant_per_group_naive` Lb0→Lb1, 59 calls). The removed transpose copy (`elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<…nocast>`) dropped from **960 → 547 = −413**, exactly `354 + 59` (one `.contiguous()` per fused-quant call). Total GPU kernel launches: 11555 → 11142. **End-to-end (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, IL8192/OL1024, num_prompts = concurrency × 10):** | Concurrency | Output tok/s (before → after) | Δ throughput | Median TPOT ms (before → after) | Δ TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 438.8 → 443.1 | +0.98% | 8.44 → 8.41 | −0.37% | | 8 | 744.7 → 754.0 | +1.25% | 9.67 → 9.54 | −1.30% | | 16 | 1058.3 → 1071.4 | +1.24% | 13.53 → 13.30 | −1.67% | | 32 | 1525.8 → 1536.3 | +0.69% | 18.05 → 17.97 | −0.42% | | 64 | 1960.7 → 1973.7 | +0.66% | 27.27 → 27.09 | −0.65% | | 128 | 2615.1 → 2621.7 | +0.25% | 38.42 → 38.38 | −0.09% | Output-throughput geomean **+0.84%**; decode TPOT consistently lower across the sweep. A small but clean, zero-risk reduction — the benefit is the removal of ~per-layer kernel launches in the decode path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: feat(cake_gemm): add Cake batch DeepGEMM FP8 backend
signal.text: ## Real-weight correctness and E2E performance Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324), all 163 real FP8 safetensors shards. Both modes ran sequentially on the same 4x NVIDIA GB300 node with TP4/EP4 and identical settings. `native` is SGLang's integration-free packed-scale DeepGEMM path; `cake` enables this PR through FlashInfer's public batch DeepGEMM API. | Correctness | Native | Cake | Comparison | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Greedy prompts | 3 | 3 | same prompts | | Output tokens | 48 | 48 | **48/48 token IDs exact** | | Finish reasons | 3 | 3 | **3/3 exact** | | Non-finite output logprobs | 0 | 0 | **pass** | | Maximum output-token logprob absolute difference | — | — | **0.0** | | Round: 64 requests, input 16, output 128, concurrency 8 | Native output tok/s | Cake output tok/s | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0 | 42.407477 | 43.249187 | **1.019849x** | | 1 | 42.596189 | 43.690664 | **1.025694x** | | 2 | 43.402560 | 43.461728 | **1.001363x** | | Three-round median | Native | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Duration | 192.317675 s | 188.487675 s | **1.020320x** | | Request throughput | 0.332783 req/s | 0.339545 req/s | **1.020320x** | | Output throughput | 42.596189 tok/s | 43.461728 tok/s | **1.020320x** | | Total throughput | 47.920712 tok/s | 48.894444 tok/s | **1.020320x** | | Mean E2E latency | 24,036.562 ms | 23,558.187 ms | **1.020306x** | | Median E2E latency | 24,030.345 ms | 23,506.908 ms | **1.022267x** | | Mean TTFT | 484.798 ms | 479.128 ms | **1.011834x** | | Median TTFT | 507.402 ms | 508.436 ms | **0.997966x** | | Mean TPOT | 185.447 ms | 181.402 ms | **1.022301x** | | Median TPOT | 185.522 ms | 181.394 ms | **1.022760x** | | Output-throughput CV | 1.008% | 0.415% | — | Model load, server startup, kernel JIT, and 16 warmup requests are outside the measured request window. The old `1.85x` result was invalid: its reference arm used a slower wrapper route and produced only about `21.7 tok/s`. The corrected no-integration native packed-scale baseline produces `42.5962 tok/s` at the median. The limited model-level gain is expected from GPU attribution. In a profiled real-serving step, the two target native DeepGEMM kernels used `467.127 ms`, versus `415.951 ms` for Cake (`1.12303x`), but represented only `1.9853%` of native GPU kernel time. Amdahl's law predicts `1.00218x` for that isolated share and an infinite-kernel-speedup ceiling of `1.02025x`; the measured `1.02032x` E2E point estimate is therefore at the scale of the workload's maximum leverage and round-to-round variation, not a 1.85x model acceleration. ## Real-weight GSM8K capability The integration-free native route and Cake route were run sequentially on the same 4x GB300 node against all 1,319 questions from the public GSM8K test split. Both used the same real `DeepSeek-V3-0324` checkpoint, five-shot prompts, greedy decoding (`temperature=0`, `top_p=1`), a 512-token cap, and client parallelism 200. Model load, server startup, JIT, and the 8-question warmup are excluded from the reported evaluation latency. | Capability metric | Native packed DeepGEMM | Cake | Comparison | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Last-number exact-match accuracy | 1240/1319 (**94.0106%**) | 1239/1319 (**93.9348%**) | **-1 question / -0.0758 pp** | | Invalid answers | 0 | 0 | **equal** | | Correctness classification agreement | — | — | **1308/1319 (99.1660%)** | | Parsed final-answer agreement | — | — | **1307/1319 (99.0902%)** | | Complete generated-text agreement | — | — | **915/1319 (69.3707%)** | | Native-only correct / Cake-only correct | 6 | 5 | net **-1** for Cake | | Full GSM8K evaluation | Native packed DeepGEMM | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Benchmark latency | 947.236 s | 936.829 s | **1.011109x** | | Output throughput | 141.409 tok/s | 142.630 tok/s | **1.008635x** | | Full client wall time | 967.225 s | 957.133 s | **1.010544x** | The one-question accuracy delta is accompanied by bidirectional answer changes (6 native-only correct, 5 Cake-only correct), zero invalid outputs, and 99.17% agreement on per-question correctness. Complete generated text is not expected to be byte-identical across the two numerical routes, so the capability comparison uses the benchmark's last-number exact-match metric rather than token identity. ## Reproduction ```bash MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V3-0324 CORPUS_PATH=/path/to/fixed-128-row-corpus.json COMMON_SERVER_ARGS=( --trust-remote-code --tp 4 --ep 4 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --disable-shared-experts-fusion --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --disable-flashinfer-autotune --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 256 --context-length 2048 --max-running-requests 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --random-seed 42 --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":32}' ) # Run the modes sequentially on the same 4-GPU node. Use port 30000 for native and 32000 for Cake. PORT=30000 python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}" \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path "$CORPUS_PATH" \ --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \ --num-prompts 64 \ --random-input-len 16 \ --random-output-len 128 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 8 \ --seed 42 \ --disable-tqdm ``` For the full capability run, start each mode with `--max-running-requests 200`, then run: ```bash MODE=native # repeat with MODE=cake and a separately started server PORT=30000 # use the port assigned to MODE python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port "$PORT" \ --data-path /path/to/gsm8k-test.jsonl \ --num-shots 5 \ --num-questions 1319 \ --max-new-tokens 512 \ --temperature 0.0 \ --top-p 1.0 \ --parallel 200 \ --result-file "results/${MODE}.jsonl" \ --raw-result-file "results/${MODE}-raw.jsonl" ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32247257012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32247257012)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32247256883](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32247256883)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Refactor] New EPD
signal.text: ## Motivation The EPD encoder had grown into a single 4464-line `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py` that owned the FastAPI application, the DP launcher, the request scheduler, CPU preprocessing, the GPU forward, and both transfer backends at the same time. That coupling caused three concrete problems: **1. Duplicated orchestration.** HTTP non-DP and DP workers each maintained their own copy of encode scheduling, batch/direct branching, backend detection, metadata publication, embedding staging, send scheduling, error handling, resource release and metrics updates. On top of that: - single-request and batch encode had two separate implementations; - Mooncake, ZMQ-to-scheduler and ZMQ-to-tokenizer each carried near-identical send logic; - `send` and `release` were tightly coupled, and embedding cleanup was scattered across the normal, error and timeout branches. **2. Unsafe resource lifetimes.** Because `send` implicitly released embeddings and cleanup lived in several places, concurrent encode / send / release had no ordering guarantee: a release racing an in-flight forward could tear down state that a pending send still needed, and a failed encode could leave a `send` waiting forever. **3. No layer to build on.** There was no protocol-neutral home for scheduling, so gRPC could not reuse the HTTP backend topology, and neither the CPU preprocessing nor the HTTP layer could be replaced by a Rust implementation. This PR restructures the encoder into a package with explicit layers and unifies everything after `receive` into a single pipeline, while keeping the external HTTP/gRPC surface unchanged. ## Modifications ## 2. One inference lifecycle for every path Everything after `receive` now follows a single chain, identically for HTTP non-DP and for DP workers: ``` receive (protocol-specific entry point) → execute_encode_pipeline → MMEncoder.encode / batch_encode → acquire encode ref → preprocess → publish metadata → model forward → stage embedding → release encode ref → delivery.send → release_request ``` - `encode()` becomes a batch-of-one call into `batch_encode()`, so there is no second encode implementation. `EncoderScheduler` only decides *whether* requests coalesce into a batch. - `execute_encode_pipeline()` owns metrics and tracing, direct-vs-batched dispatch, metadata publication, the `MMEncoder` call, final metadata sync, the ZMQ synchronous send or the Mooncake metadata response, and resource release on the normal, error and timeout paths. - `ReqState` holds the whole per-request lifecycle: `embedding_data`, `embedding_ready`, `active_encodes`, `active_sends`, `release_requested`, `preserve_metadata_on_release`, `lifecycle_condition`, driven by `_acquire_encode_ref()` / `_release_encode_ref()`. The resulting guarantees: - a release issued during encode cannot delete request state early; - a release waits until `active_sends == 0`; - once a release is requested, new sends are rejected; - a shared embedding is freed only after all destinations have finished; - a failed encode still stages the error, so a waiting `send` can never block forever. - `EncoderDelivery` isolates the backend differences. The previous `ZmqSchedulerDelivery` and `ZmqTokenizerDelivery` collapse into one `ZmqDelivery` parameterized by `cleanup_receive_state`; `self.transfer_backend` / `self.use_mooncake` are cached on `MMEncoder` instead of re-reading `server_args.encoder_transfer_backend` all over the code. - `embedding_to_send.pop()`, `discard_embedding()`, handler-`finally` cleanup, the Mooncake callback cleanup and the ZMQ rendezvous cleanup all collapse into `release_request()`. - Mooncake marks an embedding ready **only after the CUDA stream is synchronized**, so an RDMA read can no longer observe a GPU buffer whose write has not landed. Global-cache embeddings keep their existing per-send registration semantics. ### 3. Metadata is published right after preprocess Every backend publishes embedding shape, dtype and size as soon as preprocessing completes — before the forward runs. At that point `ReqState.embedding_data` holds a metadata placeholder; the real embedding is staged and validated afterwards, which is what sets `embedding_ready`. For Mooncake non-DP this lets the receiver call `/scheduler_receive_meta_data`, then allocate and register its landing buffer **in parallel with the encoder forward**; the RDMA transfer itself still waits for `embedding_ready`. ZMQ publishes the same metadata today, but has no early consumer yet. ### 4. Preprocessing metadata consolidated `EncoderPreprocessResult` returns `mm_inputs`, `grid_thw` and `token_counts` together. Grid normalization and patch/token counting move out of `MMEncoder` into `EncoderPreprocessor`, so `process_mm_items` parses the grid exactly once and the direct, cache, Mooncake and batch paths reuse the same result. `slice_embedding` and `_encode_missing` no longer recompute token counts from the grid. ### 5. Receiver: one embedding pool for both backends - `EmbeddingPool` absorbs `MooncakeEmbeddingPool` and gains `try_stage` / `release_on_gc`. When `SGLANG_EMBEDDING_POOL_SIZE_MB` is set explicitly, `zmq_to_scheduler` also keeps received embeddings resident in the GPU pool: zero-copy per-modality views, slot lifetime bound to `mm_inputs` garbage collection, and a `PENDING` retry when the pool is full. **Default behaviour is unchanged** — the 4096 MB default still applies to Mooncake only. - RDMA buffer release becomes an ownership transfer to the receiving thread, which removes an up-to-1800 s `join` block on the scheduler main thread. - `WaitingMMRequestBase` (ABC) unifies `recv_embedding`; the backend differences shrink to three abstract methods — `send_encode_request`, `_extract_embedding_from_buffer`, `_prepare_embedding_buffer`. Seven separate failure paths merge into `_fail_and_release`, and the classes are renamed off "Image" into the `Zmq` / `Grpc` / `RDMA` families. - Dead code on the `zmq_to_tokenizer` path is removed. ## EPD performance results ### Common workload - 4 random 1080p JPEG images per request - Random input length 1024, output length 64 - Temperature 0, request rate `inf` - Radix cache and MM global cache disabled - Paired values below are `main/new_epd` ## Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ### Test setup - One 8×H20 node - Encoder TP1 on GPU 0–1; Language TP1 on GPU 2 - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.60 - `single`: client concurrency 1, scheduler max batch 1, 8 requests per round - `batch`: client concurrency 4, scheduler max batch 4, 16 requests per round - Each case used 2 warmup requests followed by 3 measured rounds - Results are the median of the 3 rounds - `zmq_to_scheduler` used a 4096 MB embedding pool ### Results | Encoder DP | Path | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | single | Tokenizer | 0.288/0.294 | 3058/2976 | 6.774/6.783 | | 1 | single | Scheduler | 0.293/0.362 | 2990/2331 | 6.786/6.775 | | 1 | single | Mooncake | 0.368/0.403 | 2280/2047 | 6.783/6.778 | | 1 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.447/0.448 | 7095/7076 | 19.498/19.452 | | 1 | batch | Scheduler | 0.436/0.519 | 7476/5945 | 19.439/18.077 | | 1 | batch | Mooncake | 0.525/0.566 | 5860/5352 | 19.421/19.429 | | 2 | single | Tokenizer | 0.282/0.297 | 3122/2934 | 6.780/6.776 | | 2 | single | Scheduler* | 0.334/0.362 | 2556/2343 | 6.777/6.776 | | 2 | single | Mooncake | 0.366/0.402 | 2299/2058 | 6.784/6.779 | | 2 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.488/0.487 | 6369/6367 | 28.541/28.516 | | 2 | batch | Scheduler* | 0.478/0.582 | 6708/5121 | 26.301/27.547 | | 2 | batch | Mooncake | 0.591/0.636 | 4975/4574 | 28.569/26.525 | \* For DP2 Scheduler, main used two independent TP1/DP1 Encoders, while new_epd used one internal TP1/DP2 Encoder. ## Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 ### Test setup - Two 8×H20 nodes - Language TP8 and Encoder deployed on separate nodes - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.70 - `DP4`: one TP1/DP4 Encoder process and one Encoder URL - `4×DP1`: four independent TP1/DP1 Encoders and four Encoder URLs - Concurrency 1: 16 warmup and 16 measured requests - Concurrency 8/32: 32 warmup and 64 measured requests - Results below use the second measured round - Scheduler embedding pool: 4096 MB ### Configurations | Client concurrency / scheduler max batch | Encoder layout | Encoder URLs | |---|---|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | 1 | | 8/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | 4 | ### Results | Concurrency / max batch | Layout | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | Tokenizer | 0.555/0.532 | 1438/1444 | 5.227/5.521 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Scheduler | 0.536/0.554 | 1470/1388 | 5.287/5.357 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Mooncake | 0.579/0.634 | 1315/1216 | 5.550/5.468 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.487/1.495 | 4179/4183 | 18.838/18.889 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.543 | —/3864 | —/19.014 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/1.761 | —/3339 | —/19.010 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.568/1.651 | 3398/2815 | 18.652/33.909 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.358/1.464 | 4323/4158 | 19.737/19.054 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 1.865/1.910 | 2965/2718 | 20.067/18.725 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.605/1.687 | 12621/11471 | 85.097/97.416 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.585 | —/13857 | —/96.598 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/2.246 | —/7814 | —/95.164 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.683/1.603 | 11529/12062 | 112.268/122.776 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.341/1.389 | 16667/13518 | 108.282/108.752 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.126/2.310 | 8433/7584 | 109.113/95.207 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.625/1.656 | 12093/11577 | 96.304/93.734 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.551/1.607 | 12602/13285 | 115.445/96.704 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.101/2.112 | 8615/8826 | 100.019/69.134 | `—` denotes an unsupported main DP4 combination. ### Known limitations in `main` - `main` does not support the `zmq_to_scheduler` path with Encoder DP enabled. - On the Mooncake path, enabling Encoder DP while running the Language service with TP greater than 1 causes request routing and embedding-lifecycle errors. These combinations were therefore not included as valid `main/new_epd` performance pairs. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Fix hybrid decode CUDA graph WAR event timing
signal.text:
## Summary Hybrid linear-attention (Mambaish) decode graphs continue reading shared recurrent state during CUDA graph replay. Publish the WAR read-done event after replay so the overlap scheduler cannot overwrite that state while the graph is still consuming it. ### Before ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as Decode graph runner participant G as GPU stream participant S as Overlap scheduler R->>G: Load shared Mamba state R->>G: Record read-done event R->>G: Replay CUDA graph S->>G: Wait for read-done G-->>S: Event completes before replay S->>G: Reuse / overwrite shared state Note over G: Replay is still reading the state
Race, hang, or invalid output ``` ### After ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as Decode graph runner participant G as GPU stream participant S as Overlap scheduler R->>G: Load shared Mamba state R->>G: Replay CUDA graph R->>G: Record read-done event S->>G: Wait for read-done G-->>S: Event completes after replay S->>G: Safely reuse / overwrite shared state ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30826570586](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30826570586) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30826565355](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30826565355)

signal.title: [MLX] Windowed per-request KV cache for sliding-window layers
signal.text: > Stacked on #30050 (un-merged): the first commit here is that PR's head; > review only the last commit. Will rebase once #30050 merges. ## Motivation Follow-up promised in #30050. That PR ran gpt-oss sliding-window layers by storing **full** KV history and applying the window at read time (banded mask at prefill, trailing-window truncation at decode). Numerically exact, but sliding layers paid full-context memory. This PR makes sliding-window layers keep only the trailing `window` tokens on the per-request KV path (`--disable-radix-cache`, the configuration the gpt-oss e2e tests run) via a new `WindowedAttentionKVCache`. Measured per-request KV for gpt-oss-20b geometry (24 layers, 12 sliding, window=128, 8 KV heads x 64 head_dim, bf16): | sequence | full-history | windowed | saving | |---|---|---|---| | <= 4096 (preallocated) | 192.0 MiB | 102.0 MiB | 46.9% | | 4096 prompt + 4000 decode | 384.0 MiB | 198.0 MiB | 48.4% | | 8192 prompt + 192 decode | 768.0 MiB | 390.0 MiB | 49.2% | (Numbers are decode steady state. While a prefill chunk is in flight a windowed layer's transient buffer is `window + max(chunk, window)` — the kept prefix plus the chunk — so with the default 4096-token chunked prefill the per-layer peak is ~4224 slots regardless of prompt length: no saving while prefilling a <= 4k prompt, roughly half from the second chunk onwards, and the buffer shrinks to `2*window` on the first decode step.) ## Modifications - `WindowedAttentionKVCache` (attention_kv_cache.py): fixed-size, temporal-order buffer. Decode appends in place into a `2*window` buffer and compacts the trailing window into a fresh buffer when full (amortised O(1) per token); prefill chunks normalise the kept prefix to `min(local, window)` on every `update_and_fetch`, so the returned length is deterministic. `offset` stays absolute (RoPE positions, decode bookkeeping); `make_mask` clamps the mask offset to the kept prefix, mirroring mlx_lm `RotatingKVCache.make_mask`, so mask width always equals returned key length. Oversized prefill-chunk buffers shrink back to `2*window` on the first decode step. Requesting a full-context mask after history has been dropped raises. - `MlxModelRunner`: `_new_native_cache` builds windowed caches for layers in `get_layer_window_sizes(model)` **only when `disable_radix_cache` is set**; the pool/radix path keeps #30050's full-history semantics because (a) `_sync_new_kv_to_pool` / `_sync_decode_kv_to_pool` slice per-request caches at absolute offsets, and (b) radix prefix reuse at match point P needs sliding KV for [P-window, P), which windowed storage no longer has. Pool-side memory work is tracked separately. - `_acquire_cache` resets reused caches via a new `reset()` (both cache classes) instead of poking `offset`. - `MLXAttentionWrapper._batched_decode` is unchanged: its trailing-window slice and locally rebuilt padding mask are already correct for both cache kinds (the windowed buffer is temporal, holds >= min(offset, window) tokens, and reports absolute offsets). Docstring updated. ## Test - New `test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/mlx/test_windowed_kv_cache.py` (15 tests): bit-exact equivalence of windowed storage vs the trailing slice of full-history storage across chunk patterns and compaction boundaries (including chunk > 2*window and buffer shrink after oversized chunks); mask width == returned key length on every chunk; clamped mask == trailing columns of the full banded mask; tiny-gpt-oss chunked prefill and 2*window greedy decode produce identical tokens windowed vs full-history; wrapper batched decode over windowed caches matches the full-KV banded reference at 1e-5 for 12 consecutive steps across the compaction boundary; runner wiring (windowed only on the per-request path, all-contiguous otherwise, reset on reuse). - Existing MLX suites stay green: test_sliding_window_attention (24), test_mlx_runner_pool_contract, test_runner_init_contract, test_scheduler_mixin. - Apple Silicon (M-series 24 GB), real weights, all at final code state: - gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8 reference correctness: PASS — token-for-token vs unpatched mlx_lm greedy (>128-token prompts, windowed path active), plus batched-vs-solo decode isolation - gpt-oss serving smoke (--disable-radix-cache): PASS — 3/3 incl. the >128-token needle prompt - gpt-oss steady-state compaction e2e: PASS — 94-token prompt + 420 greedy decode steps crossing the 2*window=256 compaction boundary three times; output character-identical to full-history storage (#30050 head) for all 420 tokens. (Both storage schemes diverge from unpatched mlx_lm at the same token ~150 steps in — a pre-existing batched-wrapper vs container numeric effect, independent of the storage change.) - qwen2_moe (Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B 4bit) serving regression: PASS — 3/3 on the default radix/pool path; windowed path correctly inactive for non-SWA models - qwen3_moe (Qwen3-30B-A3B 4bit) serving regression: PASS — 3/3 cc @yeahdongcn <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #30195520973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30195520973)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #30195520860](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30195520860)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Align deterministic DSpark target verify with Triton decode
signal.text: ## Motivation Addresses #35150. Deterministic top-k-1 DSpark target verification used Triton extend attention, while ordinary decoding used Triton decode attention. This change aligns those attention paths for static linear verification. ## Modifications - Build one causal decode row for each target-verify token. - Reuse Triton decode attention in eager and CUDA Graph target verification. - Restrict the path to CUDA deterministic DSpark target workers with top-k 1 and without custom or ragged masks, MLA, DCP, sliding-window attention, unified KV translation, or encoder-decoder attention. ## Accuracy Tests - `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, Black, and the repository Ruff rules passed. - Focused GPU probe: target-verify output exactly matched sequential decode (`unequal=0`, `max_abs=0.0`); eager and CUDA Graph `kv_indptr`, `kv_indices`, and KV splits matched. - Qwen3.8-27B DSpark, 96-token greedy request: - eager forced reject: `spec_accept_rate=0.0` - full CUDA Graph forced reject: `spec_accept_rate=0.0` - normal DSpark: `spec_accept_rate=0.484375` (31/64 drafts accepted) - all three Candidate B runs produced output-ID SHA256 `5fc99930b4c8f106a1267003582448c2f9bfe1f17c4db52839924cfc8e830fa1` The SHA above compares the three Candidate B runs; it is not a Base-model oracle comparison. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run; this PR targets deterministic correctness.

signal.title: [Kimi] Enable GB300 TP4 and GB200/GB300 TP16 SP collectives
signal.text: ## Summary Build on #35061 to enable tuned Kimi K3 sequence-parallel collectives for: - GB300 DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16, where attention TP is a derived node-local subgroup of full TP16. - GB200 and GB300 attention-TP16 / EP16 across four nodes in one NVL72 segment. ## Relationship to #35061 #35061 now provides the generic infrastructure this change previously carried locally: - topology/VMM-based multinode CustomAllReduceV2 admission; - SM100 world-size-16 communicator configuration; - dispatch priority over symmetric-memory PyNccl; and - capability coverage for world-size-16 MNNVL groups. Those overlapping server-policy, environment, and communicator changes have been removed from this PR. This PR still contributes K3-specific functionality not covered by #35061: 1. Derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-AR policy instead of unconditionally setting `use_custom_allreduce=False`. Capability selection still happens independently for each process group, and explicit `--disable-custom-all-reduce` remains respected. 2. K3 SP dispatch admits world size 16 on SM100 and SM103. 3. Correctness-checked, exact-device GB200 and GB300 `world=16,H=7168` RS/AG tuning tables are added. 4. Pull/direct K3 strategies no longer require push-workspace capacity. Larger RS buckets select measured pull candidates, so every push bucket fits the default 256 KiB world-16 workspace without forcing generic TP16 all-reduce thresholds. Ordinary TP16 all-reduce behavior is owned by #35061 and its generic SM100 heuristics; this PR does not override it. ## Changes ### Attention process group - Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy. - Leave final communicator selection to the topology and allocator capability checks from #35061. - Add focused CPU coverage for the derived-group option. ### K3 world-16 support - Enable K3 SP on SM100/SM103 when an exact-device table is available. - Add GB200 and GB300 `world=16,H=7168` reduce-scatter/all-gather tables. - Keep untuned attention-residual fusion entries on the existing `separate` path. - Check push workspace only in the push entry points; pull RS and direct AG use dedicated symmetric tensors. - Add exact-device table lookup and default-workspace-envelope tests. - Add one-time dispatch/fallback diagnostics. ## World-16 tuning and correctness Both devices were tuned on four 4-GPU nodes in one NVL72 segment over global-token buckets 16 through 16384. - Every measured push/pull/direct candidate was checked against NCCL before timing. - BF16 comparison used `rtol=2e-2`, `atol=5e-2` for rank-16 reduction-order differences. - Every selected custom bucket was faster than NCCL. - Attention-residual fusion was not part of the sweep and remains `separate`. - Production selection excludes push candidates above the generic world-16 256 KiB per-rank workspace. ### GB200 (SM100) Tuning run on four GB200 nodes in one NVL72 segment: | Operation | Tokens | NCCL | Selected custom | Strategy | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:| | Reduce-scatter | 512 | 98.892 us | 20.753 us | pull | 4.76x | | All-gather | 512 | 57.287 us | 16.904 us | direct | 3.39x | | Reduce-scatter | 8192 | 271.825 us | 172.092 us | pull | 1.58x | | All-gather | 8192 | 212.818 us | 171.805 us | direct | 1.24x | | Reduce-scatter | 16384 | 371.195 us | 330.806 us | pull | 1.12x | | All-gather | 16384 | 371.271 us | 334.210 us | direct | 1.11x | An independent graph-validation run captured and replayed every production-table RS+AG pair using the default CustomAllReduceV2 workspace. All 11 buckets matched NCCL; no forced workspace environment override was used. ### GB300 (SM103) | Operation | Tokens | NCCL | Selected custom | Strategy | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:| | Reduce-scatter | 512 | 105.371 us | 20.828 us | pull | 5.06x | | All-gather | 512 | 57.081 us | 16.824 us | direct | 3.39x | | Reduce-scatter | 8192 | 265.358 us | 171.723 us | pull | 1.55x | | All-gather | 8192 | 224.534 us | 171.736 us | direct | 1.31x | The original GB300 production table was checked under CUDA graph capture/replay at every bucket. The default-workspace table selects already-measured/correctness-checked pull candidates at 512 and 1024 tokens. ## Nsight dispatch validation ### GB300 DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16 Exactly 92 custom TP4 RS/AG pairs replaced NCCL per decode step: - NCCL RS over ten steps: 930 -> 10. - NCCL AG: 940 -> 20. - Custom RS: 0 -> 920. - Custom AG: 0 -> 920. - RS median: 16.014 -> 6.853 us (`-57.2%`). - AG median: 16.508 -> 7.179 us (`-56.5%`). - Full decode graph: 43.365 -> 40.259 ms (`-7.16%`). ### GB300 attention-TP16 / EP16 Over ten rank-0 decode steps: - 920 custom RS launches. - 920 custom direct AG launches. - Zero NCCL RS launches. - Eight SP collectives in the aligned four-layer window: 369.731 -> 137.872 us (`-62.71%`). ## Serving validation caveat The serving numbers below are matched stock/custom A/B validation using the pinned public SGLang container, public InferenceX commit, and fixed workload, not official cookbook results: - ISL 8192, OSL 1024, concurrency 512, 2048 requests. - Output throughput: 2872.99 -> 3029.28 tok/s (`+5.44%`). - Median TPOT: 117.64 -> 109.69 ms (`-6.76%`). - Median ITL: 55.33 -> 48.60 ms (`-12.16%`). ## Checks - Rebased onto `upstream/main` at `574274660f`. - Changed-file pre-commit suite passed, including clang-format. - Python syntax compilation and JSON parsing passed. - Push-workspace-envelope checks passed for both device tables. - Added CPU tests for derived attention-TP policy and exact GB200/GB300 dispatch lookup. - GB200: all candidates correctness-checked before timing; all 11 production buckets passed CUDA graph capture/replay against NCCL with the default workspace. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32252871443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32252871443)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32252871139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32252871139)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Support same-GPU data parallelism via --gpu-id-step 0
signal.text: ## Motivation Implements the proposal in #31891. Short-input prefill-only serving (embeddings, scoring) is CPU-bound at saturation: on an RTX A6000 a tuned single Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B replica tops out around 800 req/s with GPU SM-active at only ~33%. Colocating multiple replicas on one GPU reclaims that idle capacity — the pattern the SGLang-Omni team documented for TTS ([same-GPU DP with CUDA MPS](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/basic_usage/same_gpu_dp.html)), Snowflake ships for embedding inference, and roadmap #15344 tracks as *"Multi-replica execution per single GPU (DP-style)"* (citing arXiv 2512.07846: multiple worker processes parallelize CPU-side overhead). sglang is nearly there natively: `--dp-size N` already launches N schedulers behind the built-in DP load balancer, and the GPU assignment arithmetic (`base_gpu_id += tp_size * pp_size * gpu_id_step`) already colocates all workers on the base GPU at `gpu_id_step=0` — but validation rejects step 0, and two more things stand between "starts" and "is actually faster" (measured below): colocated startup races, and the shared tokenizer frontend. ## Modifications - `server_args.py`: allow `--gpu-id-step 0` as the explicit same-GPU DP opt-in. Validation lives in a `_check_same_gpu_dp()` helper (same shape as the neighboring `_check_two_batch_overlap`): step 0 requires `dp_size > 1`, `tp_size == pp_size == 1` (whole-replica colocation only), and `--max-total-tokens` — colocated workers each profile the *remaining free* memory at startup, so pools must be declared, not profiled (the same mitigation the Omni guide arrived at; with the cap, both workers get identical pools instead of 161k/85k-style asymmetry). - `data_parallel_controller.py`: start colocated workers sequentially (per-worker ready-event gate). Concurrent colocated startups race each other's memory profiling and CUDA graph capture; the multi-GPU path keeps the concurrent launch. - Depends on the multi-tokenizer `BatchEmbeddingOutput` repack fix (split into its own PR: #31892): the recommended `--tokenizer-worker-num` pairing crashes without it. - `--gpu-id-step` help text documents the new value. CUDA MPS stays external (daemon lifecycle is deployment, not server code); without MPS colocated workers share the GPU by ordinary time-slicing, which works but leaves throughput on the table. ## Accuracy Tests - Unit (CPU, `test/registered/unit/test_same_gpu_dp_args.py`, `base-a-test-cpu`) — **6 passed**: accepts the valid combination, keeps the default unchanged, rejects negative step, and rejects step 0 without `dp_size>1` / with TP or PP / without a token cap. - E2E (GPU, `test/registered/prefill_only/test_same_gpu_dp_embedding.py`, `1-gpu-small`): launches the recommended combination (`--dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 --max-total-tokens 32768 --tokenizer-worker-num 2`), checks `/server_info` reports the colocated topology, and runs single and batch embeddings through the built-in round-robin balancer — this also exercises the repack fix on every response. Functional only; CI runners have no MPS daemon. - Guard tests pass (`test_server_args_cli_metadata`, `test_legacy_global_ratchet`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling A6000, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 50-token token-exact inputs, saturation (`--request-rate inf`), seeded, radix cache flushed per run, equal total server cores across arms; MPS unless noted. External orchestration study (per-replica clients, own port each; mean of 3 fresh-server repetitions at 2048 prompts per replica, range in parentheses): ```text single 1x mf=0.80 816.2 req/s (84.9) 1.00x 2 full servers 2x mf=0.40 1283.9 req/s (27.1) 1.57x 3 full servers 3x mf=0.26 1490.4 req/s (166.5) 1.83x 2 full servers, no MPS 1135.6 req/s (30.2) 1.39x (time-slicing) ``` (A short scout pass had shown DP2 at 1.92x; sustained windows flatten it to 1.57x — short-window numbers are upper bounds.) Native path enabled by this PR (one endpoint, built-in round-robin, c=128; same-session paired runs): ```text --dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 749.0 req/s 0.93x (shared single tokenizer frontend caps throughput) --dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 --tokenizer-worker-num 2 1367.8 req/s 1.70x ``` Per-process CPU sampling attributes the remaining sub-linear behavior to per-worker CPU isolation, not IPC: at saturation one scheduler pegs at ~97% while the other is held at ~73% by core contention with the tokenizer workers on the shared cpuset — the split is stable across `--load-balance-method` choices and snapshots, the router/main process sits at 17%, and a detokenizer-bypass stack recovered only +1.9%, ruling out dispatch imbalance, router funnel, and detokenizer relay respectively. External orchestration sidesteps this by pinning each full server to its own core block. A deployment note applies (give colocated DP a generous cpuset); per-DP-worker CPU affinity closes it natively and is submitted as a stacked follow-up (`--dp-cpu-affinity`, +3.1% mean and ~3x variance reduction in paired A/B; branch ready, will be submitted once this PR settles). The dp2-without-extra-tokenizers number is kept deliberately: it shows the colocation mechanism alone is not enough for CPU-bound workloads, which is why the recommended `--tokenizer-worker-num` pairing (and its prerequisite repack fix) matter. ## H200 Reproduction (2026-07-12) Repeated on 2x NVIDIA H200 NVL (driver 580.159.03), same model/scenario/protocol, three repetitions: - **External arms**: single 573.0 -> DP2+MPS 908.3 (1.59x) -> DP3+MPS 1507.1 (2.63x, best; conservative min/max ratio 2.33x) -> DP2 time-slicing 1038.6 (1.81x). The colocation gain and the equal-mem-fraction KV asymmetry both reproduce. One honest divergence: at DP2 the MPS-over-time-slicing margin did **not** reproduce on this shared-tenant host (overlapping/inverted distributions) — that margin is host-dependent; the A6000 figure stays A6000-scoped. - **Native path (this PR), 3x3 Latin square, fixed `--max-total-tokens 262144`, 4096 prompts, c=128**: shared frontend 489.2 -> `--tokenizer-worker-num 2` 911.4 req/s, paired ratios **1.583x / 2.134x / 1.899x (3/3 positive)** — the recommended pairing's contribution reproduces strongly on datacenter hardware. Native tw2 throughput matched the external two-server arm's scale on this host (different client protocol, so stated as scale-match, not a ratio). Full protocol, integrity gates, and raw artifacts: `bench_v2/results/h200/` (native/report.md). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #29818045605](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29818045605)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29818045323](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29818045323)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Split TRTLLM MHA decode batches by KV sequence length
signal.text: ## Motivation TRTLLM-GEN decode attention can pay a large tail-latency tax when requests in the same batch have very different KV sequence lengths. On GB300, a matched mixed-context profile attributed `8.377 ms` of a `9.822 ms` decode-step delta to attention, with `7.601 ms` coming from the main SM100 variable-sequence FMHA kernel. At BS44/rank on a 148-SM GB300, the unsplit launch has only one KV CTA per request and selects the persistent kernel. Long requests then form the tail of the shared wave. Splitting a fixed-query-length batch into length-sorted groups increases CTA parallelism and prevents the longest requests from delaying the short groups. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS`, with default `1` preserving the existing single-call behavior. - For values above one, sort requests by KV length, form equal-count groups, gather their query/page-table/length metadata, invoke TRTLLM MHA per group, and scatter outputs back to request order. - Reuse the same helper for ordinary fixed-query decode and frozen-KV MTP target verification, including NVFP4 KV-cache scaling. - Validate the split count and cap it at the request count. The ragged-query path is unchanged. - Extend two existing TRTLLM-MHA test cases to cover split eager decode and frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph replay; no new test method or module is added. The refreshed commit is rebased onto current upstream `main@f019f0b064`. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation on `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.985** (197/200) | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | Acceptance was generated naturally; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. Targeted GB300 correctness coverage on the refreshed upstream commit: - existing eager dense-decode case with two sequence-length groups; - existing frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph case with two groups; - `2 passed`, covering `5` subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Feature isolation: no split versus two groups Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, TRTLLM MHA, NEXTN draft length 6, BS44/rank on GB300: | Workload | Splits=1 | Splits=2 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mixed ISL decode iteration | 57.485 ms | 51.639 ms | **-10.17%** | | Uniform 92k, exact matched points | 49.907 ms | 50.008 ms | +0.20% | | q_len=1 attention micro | 0.757 ms | 0.637 ms | **-15.9%** | | q_len=6 attention micro | 1.066 ms | 0.711 ms | **-33.3%** | The mixed run held batch size, average context, request count, and draft settings constant. Length splitting closed `75.5%` of the isolated mixed-ISL attention tax without a material steady-state regression on uniform lengths. ### Production split-count tuning AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. Exact-shape matching used each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. | Metric | Split-3 | Split-4 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape output TPS/User | 67.352353 | 70.623070 | **+4.8561%** | | Strict matched TPS/running request | — | — | **+1.82848%** | | ITL | — | — | **-4.0306%** | | Full decode duration | — | — | **-3.6644%** | Both arms had CUDA graph fraction `1.0` and zero retractions. This second table is split-count tuning enabled by the PR, not an additional additive estimate on top of the no-split comparison. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The opt-in setting is documented inline at its declaration. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is 135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets the model run on a consumer GPU, so the remaining barriers are the checkpoint download, host memory, and bytes streamed per layer. This adds a pre-quantized GGUF transformer path. The validated Q4_K_M DiT is 17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB. It complements online `kitchen_int8`: GGUF avoids first downloading and pinning the complete BF16 DiT, while `kitchen_int8` remains the faster compute-oriented path. ## Interface `--model-path` continues to provide the pipeline components and `--transformer-weights-path` selects the GGUF DiT. The loader accepts a local file, `owner/repo/path/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` when that suffix matches exactly one file. Repositories containing multiple variants require the full file path. ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --transformer-weights-path \ leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/minimax_h3_fl2va-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --port 30010 ``` `--quantization gguf` is intentionally rejected: quantization is encoded in the checkpoint and the file path is the selector. ## Implementation - Reuses SRT's GGUF file detection, Hub resolver, quantization type sets, and CUDA dequantization helper. Diffusion no longer carries duplicate download resolution, GGML support tables, or dequantization shape logic. - Keeps a small diffusion-specific header reader because model construction needs each tensor's exact logical and packed shape before parameters exist. Packed tensors stay mmap-backed until the generic loader copies their TP shard, which avoids cloning the complete 17.5 GiB checkpoint during load. - Uses dequantization followed by native GEMM for DiT linears. SRT's fused MMVQ/MMQ path is optimized for low-token LLM inference and regresses normal diffusion sequence lengths. - Supports block-aligned tensor parallel row/column/merged linear slicing. Incompatible TP degrees fail during model construction. - Supports both the original MiniMax-H3 timestep MLP and pruned community checkpoints containing an unquantized `adaln_t_table` curve. - Fails before download for conflicting or unsupported configurations: non-CUDA, FSDP for the GGUF component, LoRA, another `--quantization`, SVDQuant, and the separate MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache/online paths. - Keeps `quality=high` fail-closed when replacement transformer weights are supplied. F32/F16/BF16 tensors use the ordinary linear path. Quantized tensors must be 2D `.weight` matrices and have valid GGML block alignment; malformed, corrupt, opposite-endian, or unsupported files fail at load. ## Validation ### Automated - Changed-files pre-commit: passed. - Focused remote NVIDIA suite: **163 passed, 2 subtests passed**. - Coverage includes header corruption/endianness/BF16 handling, Hub resolution and ambiguity, type selection, CPU-offload loading, pre-download guards, quality admission, pruned curve interpolation, and TP row/column/merged slicing. ### Kernel selection On H200 with the real H3 Q4_K QKV matrix `(21504, 5376)`, fused MMVQ is useful only at one or two tokens. At 256 and 2048 tokens, SRT MMQ took 2.60 ms and 20.61 ms versus 0.37 ms and 0.91 ms for dequantize + GEMM. The final diffusion adapter therefore keeps the native-GEMM path. ### End to end 1x H200, FL2VA Q4_K_M, layerwise-offloaded DiT/text encoder, fixed seed, 1344x768, 107 frames, 2 inference steps: | Revision | Warmup | Generation | Peak GPU | Output | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Original PR dense-dequant path | 12.67 s | 10.11 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | | Refactored SRT-reuse path | 12.64 s | 10.13 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | The two MP4 files are byte-identical (same SHA-256; PSNR infinite, SSIM 1.0). The refactored loader constructed the 17.49 GiB DiT in about 1 second versus about 19 seconds in the original PR run because packed values are no longer cloned wholesale during iteration. The pruned `unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF` FL2VA Q4_K checkpoint also completed server warmup and a real 1344x768, 107-frame video + AAC request on H200; its loaded DiT size was 10.72 GiB. The original RTX 5090 measurements remain valid: 39.0 s denoise and 26.3 GiB peak with `dit,text_encoder` offload; adding VAE offload lowered peak to 19.6 GiB and increased VAE decode from 9.5 s to 57.2 s. Not yet validated end to end: `ref2va`, quantization types other than the listed Q4 variants, and multi-GPU GGUF. TP packed slicing is unit-tested, but a requested 2x H100 validation box remained in infrastructure provisioning and is not reported as a successful run. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update CLI, quantization, compatibility, and MiniMax-H3 documentation. - [x] Run real checkpoint and end-to-end NVIDIA validation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32256244219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256244219)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32256243954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256243954)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][DSV4] unified_kv: SWA per-request ring runtime accounting
signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30315 (pool **sizing** for `unified_kv`), complementary to #29168 (unified-KV **HiSparse device pool**). This PR adds the **runtime accounting** so the scheduler and allocator treat the unified SWA pool as a **fixed per-request ring** instead of a linearly-consumed token pool. On the unified path SWA/compress state is addressed by `state_slot (== req_pool_idx)` inside the DSV4 kernels; the paged SWA indices / `full_to_swa_index_mapping` are never consumed. Accounting SWA as a linear token pool therefore over-throttles admission and decode retract, even though the real bound is concurrency (`num_req_slots`). > Stacked on #30315 — the first commits belong to that PR; review only the last commit (`SWA per-request ring runtime accounting`). Will rebase onto `main` once #30315 merges. The unified HiSparse C4 device pool is **not** in this PR (that is #29168); this PR only forwards `swa_ring_cost_tokens` through the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper. ## Modifications All changes are gated on `get_kvcache()._unified_kv`; the non-unified (fp8) path is unchanged. - **`swa.py`** — account SWA as a fixed per-request ring slot (`swa_ring_cost_tokens`) bounded by `num_req_slots` (via `req_to_token_pool`), not linear token consumption. `available_size` / `swa_available_size` / `new_pages_available` / `alloc_extend` / `alloc_decode` take the unified branch and skip the vestigial paged SWA allocator + mapping. - **`schedule_policy.py`** — `rem_swa_tokens` / `_swa_budget_for_req` use the ring-based `swa_available_size` and charge exactly one fixed ring slot per request; skip the linear SWA clamp and the double-charge on chunked continuations. - **`schedule_batch.py`** — unified-KV `check_decode_mem` diagnostic (`[SWA-BOTTLENECK]`, throttled). - **`hisparse.py`** — forward `swa_ring_cost_tokens` through the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper (device pool itself is #29168). - **`model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py`** — wire `req_to_token_pool` into the SWA allocator. ## Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv`, TP8 / DP8, ROCm** (with #29168 for `--enable-hisparse`). Server reaches ready and unified ring accounting engages: ``` [SWA-BOOKKEEPING] unified ring accounting enabled: num_slots=129, swa_ring_size=128, ring_cost_tokens=256, unified_swa_pages=16512 | legacy paged size_swa=... (bypassed) Unified-KV: reconciling swa_max_total_num_tokens ... -> ... (fixed per-request SWA ring capacity) ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269391353](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269391353)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269390749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269390749)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [kernel] One rmsnorm kernel for every hidden size, tuned from Python
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Three rmsnorm kernels (`rmsnorm.cuh`, `fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh`, `rmsnorm_hf.cuh`) with three hand-written dispatches covered a fraction of the hidden sizes SGLang serves. `_is_supported_rmsnorm_hidden_size` admitted only multiples of 256 (512 above 8192); fused-add only multiples of 16 up to 8192. **1536, 2304, 2560 — Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-30B, Gemma — all fell back to `forward_native`.** The HF-semantics variant was a separate file only because the flag could not be threaded through, and reaching it cost a `.contiguous()` copy. ## Modifications **One kernel.** `kFusedAdd` and `kCastXBeforeOutMul` become template flags. A tile may over-cover its row: `in_bound` predicates the surplus lanes and folds away entirely when the row divides the tile, so **any even hidden size up to 16384** works. The launcher takes an arbitrary row stride and checks alignment at runtime, which drops the `.contiguous()`. **Schedule moves to Python.** `(vec_size, num_threads, copy_mode)` are the trailing template arguments; C++ only validates them. Retuning now costs one JIT compile per configuration instead of invalidating every module built from the file. Parameterizing by thread count rather than unroll makes padded tiles expressible, and they sometimes win — 5120 gains 17% at batch 1 from a tile that idles 17% of its lanes. **Weight staging (`CopyMode`)**, the one new idea, is taken from [flashinfer's CuTe DSL rmsnorm](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.15.post1/flashinfer/norm/kernels/rmsnorm.py) — credited in the file header. RMSNorm reads its row twice, so something must survive the reduction; flashinfer parks the *input* tile in smem to keep it out of registers. Applying the same trick to the *weight* tile frees `kUnroll` vectors of register file: | config | unroll | registers | cp.async | TMA | |---|---|---|---|---| | rmsnorm 12288, 256t | 6 | 87 | **64** | **64** | | rmsnorm 16384, 128t | 16 | 254 | 154 | 168 | | fused_add 12288, 256t | 6 | 102 | **64** | **63** | 12288/256t crossing 64 registers doubles occupancy, 2 → 4 blocks/SM. `cp.async` fills the tile on SM80+; a single `cp.async.bulk` under `elect.sync` on SM90+. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_rmsnorm.py` + `test_fused_add_rmsnorm.py`: **2587 passed** - A correctness matrix over both kernels x bf16/fp16 x both semantics x padded and exact tiles x warp and CTA traits x block sizes from 16 to 1024: **2160 comparisons, 0 over tolerance**, and all three copy modes **bit-identical** to each other (1296 tensor pairs via `torch.equal`) - `sm_80` and `sm_90` cross-compiles of every schedule the Python side emits; TMA is correctly rejected below sm90 (`Feature 'elect' requires .target sm_90`) - End to end on B200: **Qwen3-8B gsm8k 0.927** (300 examples, TMA path live at dim=4096), Qwen3-0.6B 0.635 ## Benchmarking and Profiling B200, bf16, vs the best configuration found by an exhaustive sweep of the previous kernel: | dim | bs=1024 | bs=4096 | bs=8192 | |---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 0.97x | **1.04x** | 1.01x | | 8192 | **1.08x** | **1.04x** | **1.03x** | | 12288 | **1.03x** | **1.05x** | **1.03x** | | 16384 | 1.01x | **1.07x** | **1.04x** | 16384 at batch 8192 lands at 83.9 us, **matching flashinfer for the first time** (previously 3.6% behind). Small batches keep the existing lead — 3072 is 1.78x flashinfer at batch 4. Staging is worth 1.29x (cp.async) / 1.31x (TMA) over the register path at dim=12288, batch 8192, and nothing below unroll 4. The win is proportional to **unroll**, not to hidden size: 16384's best shapes use many threads and low unroll, so they gain least. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269415529](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269415529)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269415074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269415074)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD]DSV4 Fix KV pool sizing for the unified_kv backend
signal.text: ## Motivation The DSV4 `unified_kv` backend has a different physical KV layout than the fp8 path, but `DSV4PoolConfigurator` sized both identically. Under `unified_kv` this over-allocates memory (and can OOM), because: - KV is stored in **bf16 over the full latent** (`attn_head_dim * 2` bytes), not the fp8(nope) + bf16(rope) + scale 584-byte cell. - SWA and the c4/c128 compress-states are **fixed per-request rings** (`num_req_slots * ring_size`), independent of `full_token`, so they must be fixed biases rather than per-token terms. ## Modifications All changes are gated on the same `is_unified_kv_triton()` / `_unified_kv` switch the pool itself uses, so sizing and allocation cannot drift apart. **No behavior change on the non-unified (fp8) path.** ### Pool sizing (`pool_configurator.py`) - Use bf16 full-latent bytes for the per-token coeff on the unified path (`_get_bytes_per_full_token`). - Exclude SWA from the per-token coeff and account for it as a fixed bias (`_fixed_swa_bytes`), inflated for the speculative draft worker the same way as the coeff. - Move the **c4 compress-state (attn + indexer)** off the per-token coeff and size it as a request-scoped fixed bias (`_fixed_c4_state_bytes` / `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`), finalized once `max_running_requests` is known — mirroring the c128 state pool. Subtract it from the token budget and log `c4_state_fixed`. - Factor the `max_running_requests`-per-worker resolution into a shared helper (`_resolve_max_running_requests_per_worker`) reused by the c128 state, SWA ring, and c4 state fixed-byte terms. - Log the SWA ring and c4-state fixed biases alongside the existing c128 fixed bias. ### Memory pool (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`) - Clamp `c4_state_pool_size` up to `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size` as a safety net (mirrors the c128 clamp). ### SWA idle accounting on the unified ring - `model_runner`: reconcile `swa_max_total_num_tokens` down to the allocator ring capacity (`swa_available_size`) so the idle pool-leak invariant matches the fixed per-request SWA ring (gated on unified_kv; no real buffer is resized). - `invariant_checker`: skip the SWA token-pool leak invariant on the unified ring — its `available` is non-binding and cached radix prefixes report a spurious `swa_evictable`, so `available + evictable + protected == total` does not hold; ring slots are still covered by the `req_to_token` leak check. - `pool_stats_observer`: zero `swa_evictable` on the unified ring so `swa_num_used` / `swa_token_usage` stay coherent (cached prefixes hold no ring slot). ### Review-fix follow-ups - Detect unified-KV via the canonical `get_kvcache()._unified_kv` (the previous `getattr(alloc, "_unified", ...)` was always `False` on the wrapped allocators — thanks @amd-danli103). Applied consistently in `invariant_checker`, `pool_stats_observer`, and `schedule_batch`. - Unwrap `logical_attn_allocator` in the `_check_kv_page_invariants` sub-allocator probe so the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper reaches its inner full/swa allocators. - `schedule_policy`: align the `add_one_req` SWA admission gate (`>=` -> `>`) with `add_one_req_ignore_eos` so an exact-fit request is admitted. ## Accuracy / Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv` + EAGLE MTP (speculative), TP8 / DP8, ROCm**. <details> <summary>Server launch command</summary> ```bash export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=false export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS=true export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=false export SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS_TRITON=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_OPT_FP4_MOE_K_ALIGN=128 export SGLANG_DSV4_INDEXER_K_CACHE_PRESHUFFLE=1 export SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY=false export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --tp 8 \ --dp 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-cache-report \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --max-running-request 2048 \ --page-size 256 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --port 30001 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --enable-prefill-delayer ``` </details> <details> <summary>Client / bench_serving command</summary> ```bash NUM_PROMPT=2048 INPUT_LEN=50 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --dataset-name random \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompt ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --max-concurrency ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --random-input $((INPUT_LEN * 1024)) \ --random-output 1024 \ --port 30001 ``` </details> ### Pool sizing (startup) `unified=True`, `bytes_per_full_token=9064` (spec-inflated), `c128_state_fixed=7.83 GB`, `swa_ring_fixed=1.99 GB`, `c4_state_fixed=1.21 GB` — matches the bf16 layout + request-scoped fixed rings. Non-unified (fp8) path logs/sizes are unchanged. | full_token | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | capacity | 8, 898, 560 | 12,047,104 | ### Stress (`bench_serving`, random) 1800 prompts × 51200-token input, 500-token output, concurrency 1800 (92.16M input tokens). - **1800 / 1800 requests completed, 0 crashes / 0 pool-leak errors** across the full run. - Peak `full token usage` 0.96 (previously the saturation zone that tripped idle/leak asserts). - Peak concurrent requests 1800. - MTP accept length 3.07; total token throughput 44,415 tok/s. ### Throughput (8k in / 1k out, concurrency 1024) | config | Total token throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before | 4523.21 | 89981.16 | 130.75 | | apply PR | 4559.63 | 90483.00 | 129.75 | ### GSM8K (5-shot,) **accuracy 0.950, invalid 0.000** — confirms the sizing / SWA-accounting changes do not affect correctness. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269389637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269389637)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269389057](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269389057)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSV4] unified_kv: isolate C4 compress state per request
signal.text: ## Motivation On the `unified_kv` path the DSV4 **C4 compress state** is addressed through the full→SWA mapping: ``` state_loc = (swa_loc // swa_page_size) * c4_ring_size + swa_loc % c4_ring_size ``` `swa_loc` is derived from `req_to_token`, so **two requests sharing a radix prefix resolve the same prefix positions to the same SWA slot, and therefore to the same C4 state row**. The C4 overlap state is per-request — it carries that request's running compress window — so this aliases one request's state onto another's. The same hazard exists within a single request across a slot reuse: a freshly allocated `req_pool_idx` inherits whatever the previous occupant left in its ring rows. C128 already avoids this by addressing state request-scoped. This PR gives C4 the same contract: ``` state_loc = req_pool_idx * c4_ring_size + position % c4_ring_size ``` a pure function of `(req slot, logical position)`, which cannot alias across requests. > **Stacked on #30315 and #31040.** The first 8 files in this diff belong to those two PRs; this PR's own change is the last 12 files (`+332/-43`, commit `fix(dsv4): isolate unified C4 compress state per request`). It has to be stacked: it rewrites `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`, which #30315 introduces. Will rebase onto `main` once those merge. > > To review this PR alone: > ``` > git diff yuttian1/dsv4-unified-kv-swa-ring...yuttian1/dsv4-unified-c4-per-request-ring > ``` ## Modifications Everything is gated on `compress_ratio == 4 and token_to_kv_pool._unified_kv`. **C128 and the non-unified (full→SWA) C4 path are untouched.** **Sizing and lifecycle** - **`pool_configurator.py`** — `_unified_c4_state_pool_size` becomes exactly `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size`, replacing the page-derived upper bound that the old addressing needed. - **`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`** — new `clear_c4_req_states(req_pool_indices)`, which resets the ring rows of the given slots (kv half → `0`, score half → `-inf`). Also documents why C4 needs no MTP-reject cleanup. - **`allocation.py`, `disaggregation/decode.py`** — call `clear_c4_req_states` for **newly allocated slots only**. A chunked continuation reuses its slot and must keep the state its previous chunk captured, so `newly_allocated` is captured *before* `alloc`. **Addressing** - **`compressor.py`, `compressor_v2.py`** — compute `use_req_ring` and thread it into the plan kwargs. - **`compress_hip.py`** — four `self.ratio == 128` guards in `CompressorHip.compress_extend_paged` / `compress_decode_paged` become `ratio == 128 or (ratio == 4 and _unified_kv)`, taking the existing `translate_from_req_position_to_state_loc` branch. - **`kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/c_plan.cuh`** — `compute_c128_loc` → `compute_req_ring_loc`, now also taken under `use_req_ring` (with `RuntimeCheck(!use_req_ring || compress_ratio == 4)`). Under `use_req_ring` the ring row is `position % ring_size`, so the extra "tail of the SWA page" write the overlap path emitted for full→SWA addressing is dropped. - **`kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/attn.py`, `compress.py`** — plumb `use_req_ring` through the Triton kernel and the plan entry points (XPU signatures unchanged). ## Accuracy Tests This is a correctness fix, not a numerics change: the compressed state values are identical, only the row they live in changes. Two tests pin the new address contract. **New — `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py`** (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): - pool size is the exact request-ring product; - `clear_c4_req_states` resets only the selected rings and leaves C128 alone; - `alloc_req_slots` clears new slots but **not** reused ones. **Extended — `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py`**: new `test_unified_request_ring_plans_ignore_full_to_state` runs the real prefill and decode plan kernels with a deliberately degenerate `full_to_state`, and asserts the emitted read pages / write locs are exactly `req_pool_idx * ring_size + position % ring_size`, and that two requests never land on the same row. Both run green on ROCm (MI355X): ``` test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py 3 passed test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py 35 passed ``` Plus the neighbouring suites, unchanged: ``` test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py, test_pool_configurator.py, test_hisparse_pool_configurator.py, test_prefill_adder.py -> 66 passed, 22 subtests passed ``` No end-to-end serving accuracy run is attached yet — the `unified_kv` path needs DeepSeek-V4-Pro on ROCm, which upstream CI cannot reach. Happy to attach one if a reviewer wants it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected throughput impact: the same number of state rows is written, and `_unified_c4_state_pool_size` gets *smaller* (exact product instead of a page-derived upper bound), so the C4 pool allocation shrinks slightly. ## Notes for reviewers This is the upstream port of an internal fix. Four hunks from the internal version are **intentionally omitted** because they depend on a SWA-HiCache offload line that is not upstream (`_swa_offload_page_stride`, `_restore_state_windows`, `capture_c4_state_windows_unified`): the `swa_component.py` and `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` changes, and the two HiCache capture helpers in `compress_hip.py`. When that line lands, the HiCache-side C4 restore will need a follow-up to use the same request-scoped address contract. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32269391591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269391591)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32269391311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32269391311)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
