signal.title: [Simulator] Add high-fidelity CPU-based inference simulator
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces SGLang Simulator, a CPU-based inference simulator for evaluating SGLang scheduling, latency, throughput, and prefix-cache behavior without loading model weights or executing model kernels. It is a current-main rework of the simulator prototype in [#22250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22250), while retaining SGLang v0.5.16 as the tested compatibility floor. Large-scale inference configuration studies are expensive to run directly on accelerators. SGLang Simulator reuses the real SGLang scheduler, radix cache, hierarchical cache, and request lifecycle, while replacing model-forward execution with a latency predictor. It supports measured traces, synthetic workloads, and both in-process and HTTP serving workflows. ## What This PR Adds - Add `tools/sglang-simulator` as a monorepo component. - Reuse the SGLang scheduler, cache allocator, radix cache, hierarchical cache, and request lifecycle with dummy model weights and a minimal KV allocation. - Add three forward-latency predictors: - AIConfigurator; - an sklearn-compatible ML predictor; - batch-composition replay. - Support Random, ShareGPT, and timestamped Autobench workloads. - Support direct Python execution through `SGLangBenchmarkRunner`. - Support server and benchmark-client execution through the HTTP serving path. - Collect request, latency, throughput, prefix-cache, cache-tier, and predictor metrics. - Add reusable example configurations, workloads, tokenizer assets, and replay fixtures. - Add compatibility checks for SGLang launch and serving APIs. - Run the simulator regression suite from CPU PR CI when `tools/sglang-simulator` changes. ## Simulation Modes The simulator provides two execution modes: - `OFFLINE`: advances a logical clock without sleeping, intended for fast configuration and workload studies. - `BLOCKING`: sleeps for predicted forward latency and visible L2-to-L1 load latency, intended for serving-path and timing-semantics validation. Replay replaces model-forward latency only. CPU preprocessing and postprocessing overhead remain enabled by default. For `OFFLINE` runs, latency, throughput, and duration should be read from the server-side simulator metrics rather than benchmark-client wall-clock time. ## Accuracy Validation The following results compare simulator output with measured serving traces. Latency, throughput, and duration values are absolute percentage errors. Prefix reuse is reported as absolute percentage-point error. The `SGLang baseline` column identifies the version used by the real service that produced the measurement trace. | Model | SGLang baseline | Hardware | Predictor / coverage | TTFT | TPOT | ITL | Input throughput | Duration | Prefix reuse | |:---|:---:|:---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3-8B | v0.5.9 | H20 | AIConfigurator; no-cache, L1, and L2 cases | 2.38–4.15% | 1.64–4.05% | 1.78–4.07% | 1.41–2.40% | 1.39–2.33% | 0.00–0.04 pp | | Qwen3-32B-FP8 | v0.5.9 | H20 | AIConfigurator; no-cache, L1, and L2 cases | 2.40–3.05% | 0.58–1.11% | 0.52–1.02% | 0.52–1.13% | 0.51–1.12% | 0.00–0.04 pp | | GLM-5.1-FP8 | v0.5.11 | GPU | ML; L1 and L2 cases | 5.27% | N/A | N/A | 1.11% | 1.08% | 0.028 pp | | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | v0.5.11 | GPU | ML; L1 and L2 cases | 6.12% | N/A | N/A | 0.23% | 0.22% | 0.048 pp | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | v0.5.16 | GPU | ML; L1 case | 0.786–1.343% | N/A | N/A | 0.000212% | 0.000212% | 0.000 pp | TPOT and ITL are not applicable to the GLM-5.1-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash validation traces because they use one-token outputs(Prefill-Decode Disaggregation). Prefix-cache accuracy is particularly sensitive to `max_total_tokens`. This value determines simulated device KV-cache capacity and also affects hierarchical host-cache sizing and eviction behavior. For deployment-faithful comparisons, use the `max_total_num_tokens` value reported by the real SGLang server startup log as the simulator's `--max-total-tokens` value. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32238508466](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32238508466)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32238508226](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32238508226)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Support Kimi-K3 ModelOpt mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint
signal.text: ## Motivation The official [nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4) checkpoint is a ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint: - routed MoE experts use NVFP4 with SiTU (`beta=4`, `linear_beta=25`); - supported attention projections use weight-only `FP8_PB_WO` with 128x128 block scales. Current `main` cannot serve this checkpoint with the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend. It rejects gated `situ` during startup, and it does not instantiate/load the checkpoint's block-FP8 attention scales. The K3 fused-front also needs to pass its row-strided FP32 router output through the stride-aware precomputed-routing interface. ## Modifications - Add gated `ActivationType.Situ` support to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP4 runner. - Pass the model-provided SiTU coefficients as GEMM1 alpha/beta and keep the W13 up-dequant scale inside the SiTU activation, avoiding double application through `g1_scale_c`. - Route K3 SiTU fused-front output through SGLang's stride-aware FP32 precomputed-routing path while keeping fused-front enabled. - Dispatch ModelOpt `FP8_PB_WO` layers to SGLang's native serialized block-FP8 linear method with dynamic activation quantization and 128x128 weight blocks. - Load ModelOpt's logical 4-D block scales into SGLang's 2-D `weight_scale_inv` parameters, including fused MLA projections and TP-sharded KDA projections. - Dequantize the FP8 MLA `kv_b` weight before K3's post-load absorption. - Dequantize only K3's small `f_a`/`f_b`/`b` projections once after loading into BF16 buffers for the existing fused tiny-GEMM path; the main KDA projections remain on native block-FP8 GEMMs. - Compile the KDA recompute kernel for the BF16 activation/parameter dtype rather than the serialized FP8 weight dtype. - Add regression coverage for the SiTU scale contract, `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch, block-scale dequantization, and the fused B/F_a path. ## Accuracy Tests Validated the released checkpoint on 8x GB300 with TP8: - GSM8K-200: **197/200 = 0.985** - `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` - `trtllm_mla` prefill and decode attention backends - fused-front enabled - K3 all-reduce fusion enabled - prefill CUDA Graph enabled; decode CUDA Graph enabled for batch sizes 1/2/4 - concurrency 4 - no fused-front-disable environment workaround Both raw completion and chat-completion smoke tests produced coherent, correct answers before the evaluation. The validation used the final patch contents in this PR. The branch was then rebased onto `eafbe2cb6f` from `main`; the intervening upstream commits do not touch this PR's files. Targeted checks: - 13/13 ModelOpt NVFP4 SiTU scale tests passed. - The ModelOpt mixed `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch test passed. - The K3 B/F_a fused-path tests passed, including CUDA Graph replay and block-FP8 dequantization. - Black, Python 3.12 `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed on the changed files. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not measured. This PR is a correctness and checkpoint-compatibility change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32202731802](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32202731802)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32202731542](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32202731542)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Add LLaDA2.2 Block Routing MoE support
signal.text: ## Motivation LLaDA2.2 uses block routing in its MoE router: each diffusion block first chooses a capacity-limited set of candidate experts, and each token then selects its top-k experts from that block-local expert set. This PR adds the SGLang serving-side implementation for that routing mode so LLaDA2 checkpoints that expose `expert_capacity` / `block_size` in their config can run through the native LLaDA2 model path. The default LLaDA2 routing path is unchanged. Block routing is enabled only when the model config has `expert_capacity`. ## Modifications - Add a two-phase Triton block top-k router in `python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py`: - Phase 1 (`_block_aggregation_kernel`): computes block-level expert scores via max aggregation over tokens in the block, then selects `expert_capacity` allowed experts using a threshold + cumsum approach with index-based tie-breaking. - Phase 2 (`_token_topk_kernel`): each token selects its top-k experts from only the block-allowed set; weights are normalized via row-max rescaling with a uniform fallback for near-zero scores. - Wire block routing through the existing `Llada2MoeBlock` by conditionally calling `block_topk_triton` when `expert_capacity` and `block_size` are present in model config, constructing `StandardTopKOutput` for downstream compatibility. - Add a manual unit test (`test/manual/layers/moe/test_block_topk_triton.py`) comparing the Triton kernel against a pure PyTorch reference for: - Small and large expert counts (16 to 256 experts); - Various capacity constraints (tight capacity, full capacity, production-like); - Edge cases: `top_k=1` (no normalization path), `block_size=1` (per-token degenerate case); - Stress test with 256 tokens. ## Checklist - [x] Triton kernel implementation with two-phase block routing - [x] Unit tests (7 cases, all passing on GPU) - [x] End-to-end serving verification with block routing active Co-authored with @R00Kie-Liu, @AsaHIXx, @utdawn, @SolarisAdams. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32267286104](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32267286104)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32267285858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32267285858)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Add process-local in-memory KV indexer and Router integration
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR supersedes #32662 with a smaller, dependency-free milestone for the KV Indexer proposed in #31458. The Indexer is an experimental metadata-only service that tracks which SGLang worker may reuse each content-addressed KV-cache block. KV data remains owned by the workers. The end-to-end path is: ```text SGLang worker └─ ZMQ component-aware KV events └─ kv-indexer-bridge └─ gRPC └─ process-local in-memory indexer └─ MatchExternalKvPrefix └─ experimental sgl-router ``` This revision removes Redis, Dragonfly, and Redis Cluster from the architecture. Placement metadata is held in one Indexer process and is intentionally soft state. That makes the core event → index → prefix-query path smaller, easier to run, and directly testable without an external database. Related: - RFC: #31458 - Previous KV Indexer PR: #32662 - KV-event correctness fixes: #32537, #32514 ## Scope and failure model The process-local backend is protected by an `RwLock` and bounded request work. It supports concurrent reads and serialized placement mutations in one server process. It is not a distributed or persistent store. - Run exactly one Indexer process for a deployment. - Restarting the Indexer loses all placement metadata. - There is no missed-event replay, restart fencing, worker liveness TTL, or cross-process replication in this milestone. - A disconnected Bridge reconnects transport but cannot recover events emitted while it was absent. A batch the Indexer sheds, or refuses as oversized, costs those events and a reconnect rather than terminating the Bridge. - A prefix hit only improves worker choice, so the Router degrades rather than failing when the Indexer cannot answer. An empty result, a rejection from either admission bound, a query that exceeds its deadline, and an unreachable Indexer all become no signal: the Router selects by minimum active load and logs at `WARN`. An Indexer outage therefore costs cache affinity rather than availability. Only a rejected RPC — the Router and the Indexer disagreeing on the request contract — still fails the request with `503`, because degrading would hide that disagreement from every request. An endpoint the Router could never dial is rejected at startup instead of failing every later query. The Router's local radix tree is used only when no Indexer endpoint is configured. These constraints are explicit. This PR establishes a validated single-process soft-state baseline; persistence and recovery belong in follow-up work. ## What changed ### Process-local memory backend - Replace the Redis backend with an in-process component-aware placement map. - Track `(block hash, worker, tier)` placement snapshots and worker cache specs. - Support FULL, SWA, and MAMBA reusable-prefix semantics. - Bound prefix scanning and request hash counts to keep work predictable. - Remove Redis features, scripts, configuration, and integration requirements. ### Admission and resource protection - Bound concurrent prefix queries in the Indexer. - Shed queries whose caller deadline has already expired before backend work. - Bound concurrent external Indexer queries in the Router. - Add configurable Router timeout and max-inflight controls. - Rate-limit rejection logs with doubling cadence to avoid log storms. ### Experimental Router integration ```bash sgl-router \ --model-id <model> \ --tokenizer-path <tokenizer> \ --worker-urls <worker URLs...> \ --policy cache_aware_zmq \ --kv-indexer-endpoint http://<indexer>:50061 \ --kv-indexer-query-timeout-ms 100 \ --kv-indexer-query-max-inflight 32 ``` For each eligible request, the Router hashes normalized request tokens into the same ordered block chain, calls `MatchExternalKvPrefix`, intersects returned addresses with current routing candidates, and selects among the best reusable prefix holders using active load. ### Component-aware prefix matching The bridge accepts the gated `component_types` field from SGLang KV events and stores a component snapshot for each placement. A versioned `WorkerCacheSpec` describes which components and tiers are reusable. - **FULL** must be present contiguously on every matched block. - **SWA** must cover the configured trailing window at the candidate boundary, or form an unbroken run from the prompt head. - **MAMBA** must be present on the candidate boundary block. Component-aware placements without a valid worker cache spec fail closed. Legacy whole-block events continue to use contiguous-prefix matching. ### Crate layout `sgl-kv-indexer` lives inside the Router workspace, at `experimental/sgl-router/sgl-kv-indexer`, as a workspace member. Both crates share one lockfile, one toolchain, and one CI workflow. Membership also means Cargo unifies features across the workspace, so the Indexer pins the same narrow `zeromq` feature set as the Router (`tokio-runtime`, `tcp-transport`): adding it neither enlarges the Router binary nor widens its license surface. ## Validation ### Current process-local backend: two machines, 15 Workers One host runs a single Indexer (`prefix_query_max_inflight=32`) and the experimental Router (`--policy cache_aware_zmq`, `--kv-indexer-query-timeout-ms 100`). Two further hosts run 8 + 7 GPUs, giving 15 independent Workers each with its own Bridge, page size 64. Both component profiles were driven end to end: FULL+SWA (`gpt-oss-20b-bf16`) and FULL+MAMBA (`Qwen3.5-27B-FP8`). This is a Worker-density claim, not a host-count claim. #### Placement and prefix correctness | check | FULL+SWA | FULL+MAMBA | | --- | --- | --- | | expected blocks == Unified Tree cached blocks == Indexer prefix result | 15/15 | 15/15 | | unique prefix routed by the Router to its exact holder | 15/15 | 15/15 | | shared prefix routed to a holder from the shared set | pass | pass | Prefix sizes differ per Worker by construction (SWA 104–118 blocks, MAMBA 13–41). FULL+SWA routing was verified before and after churn. #### Event replay against indexed state The raw ZMQ event stream from both hosts (`BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` / `AllBlocksCleared`, including `component_types`) was replayed independently and compared with the Indexer's `MatchExternalKv` snapshot, hash by hash and mask by mask. | scenario | stored events | removals | AllBlocksCleared | distinct blocks | Workers exactly equal | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | FULL+SWA, seed and selective flush | 3,135 | 0 | 24 | 1,665 | 15/15 | | FULL+SWA, after 15 min churn | 101,475 | 2,353 | 54 | 28,416 | 15/15 | | FULL+MAMBA, seed | 405 | 0 | 15 | 405 | 15/15 | | FULL+MAMBA, after 5 min churn | 268,603 | 4,286 | 54 | 97,511 | 15/15 | The churn rows cover eviction: caches were driven past capacity, so blocks were removed and later re-stored. The MAMBA seed row also matched the expected mask distribution, exactly one FULL|MAMBA checkpoint block per sequence and FULL only elsewhere. #### Cache churn Concurrent generation, prefix reuse and capacity-exceeding requests across all 15 Workers, starting from a fresh `AllBlocksCleared` so both sides share one origin. | profile | duration | requests | fresh / reuse / evicting | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | FULL+SWA | 15 min, 30 threads | 815 | 387 / 246 / 182 | | FULL+MAMBA | 5 min, 15 threads | 3,984 | 1,626 / 1,380 / 978 | Workers run `max_running_requests=1`, so the SWA churn saturated them and 111 client calls hit their read timeout; correctness is judged from the event stream, not from client success. #### Selective flush Flushing one Worker, then all 8 Workers of one host: flushed placements dropped to zero, untouched Workers kept their exact block counts, and the replayed event state still equalled the Indexer state for 15/15 Workers. Verified for both profiles. #### MAMBA checkpoint boundary Four probes per Worker, 15/15 passing: a query ending on the checkpoint block returns the full prefix with the correct sole holder; including the trailing partial page returns the same; one block short of the checkpoint returns 0; the first block alone returns 0. Sweeping all truncation points for a 17-block prefix, cuts 1–16 return 0 and cuts 17–18 return 17. #### Query capacity and admission Capacity was measured against the Indexer alone, with no GPUs: 15 synthetic Workers holding 118-block FULL+SWA prefix chains, loaded through 15 real Bridge processes, then queried by an increasing number of independent client processes (16 threads each, co-located, 224-core host). Sweeping the process count is what separates a driver limit from the server's: queries from a single Python process are capped by its own interpreter, so one process cannot measure this server. | client processes | in-flight callers | accepted qps | p50 ms | p99 ms | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 16 | 1,554 | 7.6 | 41.9 | 0 | | 2 | 32 | 3,441 | 6.8 | 38.5 | 0 | | 4 | 64 | 7,559 | 5.6 | 37.6 | 0 | | 8 | 128 | 19,422 | 4.5 | 28.7 | 0 | | 16 | 256 | 83,347 | 2.8 | 7.7 | 0 | | 32 | 512 | 158,810 | 3.0 | 8.2 | 0 | | 48 | 768 | 217,604 | 3.2 | 9.1 | 12 | | 64 | 1,024 | 241,816 | 3.8 | 11.4 | 350 | | 96 | 1,536 | 244,557 | 4.8 | 17.7 | 609,498 | The original string-encoding run served roughly 245k prefix queries per second at 118 blocks. Latency falls as clients are added rather than rising, up to saturation, confirming that the low-process rows measure the driver. The query-size sweep was re-run after changing hashes from decimal `string` to packed `sfixed64`. This is a direct-parent A/B: commit `8e5fcd4054` versus `39b5bdeaaa`, both release builds, with the same 15 Workers x 1,024-block state, 15-second stages, and the original saturation process count for each size. | blocks per query | approx tokens | client processes | string qps | packed qps | change | p99 ms (string -> packed) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 64 | 128 | 429,141 | 369,186 | -14.0% | 14.2 -> 16.6 | | 8 | 512 | 96 | 396,532 | 364,880 | -8.0% | 10.3 -> 13.2 | | 32 | 2,048 | 128 | 362,378 | 355,003 | -2.0% | 14.1 -> 15.4 | | 118 | 7,552 | 64 | 243,462 | 301,617 | +23.9% | 10.9 -> 9.0 | | 256 | 16,384 | 64 | 182,357 | 267,709 | +46.8% | 14.4 -> 10.1 | | 512 | 32,768 | 64 | 121,948 | 218,857 | +79.5% | 21.5 -> 12.2 | | 1,024 | 65,536 | 64 | 74,310 | 143,859 | +93.6% | 37.4 -> 16.0 | A least-squares fit of per-request cost gives 2.54 us fixed + 10.79 ns/block for strings and 2.70 us fixed + 4.06 ns/block for packed hashes: the length-dependent cost falls 62.4%. Short-query throughput is 2-14% lower; this commit also adds a 64-stream per-connection bound, so the gRPC A/B does not isolate encoding from that transport admission change at extreme concurrency. Long-prefix throughput and latency improve substantially. The in-memory state footprint improves too. With identical state (15 Workers x 16,384 unique FULL+SWA blocks, 245,760 blocks total), loaded-minus-idle PSS falls from 120.6 MiB to 90.2 MiB (-25.2%) and RSS from 121.1 MiB to 90.8 MiB (-25.1%). The first and last Worker's full 16,384-block matches were verified after load. In the earlier string-encoding run, a query missing its first hash beat a fully matching query by 6.8% at 118 blocks and 13.5% at 1,024. That showed tree scan depth was only 6-12% of the old per-block cost; moving and decoding the hash list dominated, which is consistent with the packed-encoding improvement. **The inflight bound rejects as designed.** With `prefix_query_max_inflight=32`, rejections begin at ~768 concurrent callers and grow from there. At 1,536 callers the excess is shed while accepted throughput holds near 245k qps and p99 stays at 17.7 ms, so the bound caps the tail instead of letting queueing delay grow without limit. **Deadline shedding is demonstrated.** 5,119 of 5,120 requests carrying a 1 ms deadline were shed as `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` before backend work; one completed before expiry. Shedding protects the Indexer, not the caller: like an admission rejection, a shed query reaches the Router as no signal, so the request is still routed, by minimum active load. **Concurrent event ingestion is free at realistic event rates.** In the original string-encoding run, 15 Bridges applying ~150 event batches/s returned 249,491 qps against a 248,681 qps idle baseline at 118 blocks, so applies and prefix queries did not contend measurably. Taken together: at the tested load points, the current packed implementation serves 144k-369k queries/s across 1-1,024 blocks and does not reject below ~700 concurrent in-flight queries. Neither protection is expected to engage at realistic Router query rates; both bound the tail, not the normal path. **Router under Worker saturation.** With every Worker at capacity during churn, 16 concurrent end-to-end chat requests all exceeded the 30 s client timeout. The Indexer saw zero errors in the same window and routing returned to 15/15 once churn stopped, so this is Worker saturation rather than Router or Indexer behaviour. This is the scale claim for the process-local backend in this PR. A current 4/8-machine memory-backend result is intentionally not claimed. ### Event-pipeline evidence from the previous Redis-backed build Before the backend replacement, the same component-event schema, Bridge decode path, Unified Tree semantics, and prefix rules were validated at larger scale: | deployment | phase | workers | Tree = Indexer = expected | raw event replay = indexed state | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 machines | FULL+MAMBA | 32 | 32/32 | 32/32 | | 4 machines | FULL+SWA | 32 | 32/32 | 32/32 | | 8 machines | FULL+MAMBA | 63 | 63/63 | 63/63 | | 8 machines | FULL+SWA | 62 | 62/62 | 62/62 | The 4-machine run also completed 15 minutes of churn with 4,224 checkpointed Tree/Indexer alignment checks and zero failures. These results support event production, Bridge decoding, component replacement, and holder attribution at scale; they are not presented as 4/8-machine validation of the new memory backend. ### Code and build gates - One workspace gate over both crates: format, Clippy with warnings denied, release build, and **659 release tests** (107 Indexer, 552 Router), plus the tokenizer parity test run separately. - `cargo deny` clean for advisories, bans, licenses, and sources. - Repository pre-commit checks passed. - Both Router images built from the final source: the release image's distroless entrypoint passed a `--help` smoke test, and the k8s e2e image runs `sgl-router` with its tokenizer fixture in place. ## Test coverage The branch includes: - memory-backend placement, tier, clear, and component-transition tests; - FULL, SWA, MAMBA, and legacy prefix-rule tests; - deadline, request-size, and max-inflight admission tests; - gRPC validation, wire-contract, and client endpoint-validation tests; - Bridge decoding and component-snapshot coverage; - Router policy, fallback, degradation, configuration, and concurrency tests; - process-local memory integration tests. ## Current limitations - **Component metadata depends on #32514, which is not yet merged.** The `component_types` field on `BlockStored` and the `--enable-kv-events-component-types` option come from that PR. - Metadata is process-local soft state and is lost on restart. - Exactly one Indexer process is supported per deployment. - No replay/reconciliation, liveness filtering, persistence, failover, or network-partition recovery is claimed. Bridge reconnect restores transport only; events missed while a Bridge was absent are not recovered, and this was not exercised. - `KV_INDEXER_WORKER_ADDRESS` must match the Router worker URL byte-for-byte. - Prefix scans are capped at 2,048 blocks (~131k tokens). A longer request is truncated rather than rejected, so it is matched on its first 2,048 blocks only. - Worker density was validated at 15 Workers against one Indexer; higher densities only on the previous Redis-backed build. ## Checklist - [x] Format and lint code according to repository conventions. - [x] Add unit, contract, integration, and Router tests. - [x] Update architecture, configuration, and limitation documentation. - [x] Validate the final process-local backend on two machines. - [x] Build and smoke-test the final Router Docker image. - [ ] Confirm the updated PR CI is green. cc: @isytwu @TianDi101 Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32263847233](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32263847233)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32263847053](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32263847053)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [UnifiedTree] feat: support runtime attach/detach
signal.text: ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache.attach_storage_backend` / `detach_storage_backend` were stubs that always returned `False`, so the `/hicache/storage-backend` admin API only worked with `HiRadixCache`. This implements them for the unified tree. Preceding fix for #35081. Supersedes #35240 (same feature, developed in parallel). ## Modifications **`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py` (new).** `StorageAttachment` owns the storage backend lifecycle: policy validation, extra-config parsing, controller attach, the ordered teardown, and `apply_runtime_config()`. Keeping it beside the tree rather than inside it leaves `UnifiedRadixCache` on cache logic and gives the three entry points — startup, the admin API, and the atexit hook — one implementation. `UnifiedRadixCache` goes from 2764 to 2520 lines. `apply_runtime_config()` is the single point where storage turns on, which is why the hash backfill below lives there rather than in `attach()`. **Hash-chain backfill (correctness).** Page hashes chain off the parent's last hash, and `_add_new_node` only computes them when storage is enabled. A node built before attach therefore has no hash, and hashing its children against it restarts the chain mid-sequence — the resulting L3 keys claim to encode a full prefix but only encode a suffix, so an unrelated request starting with those tokens loads KV computed under a different prefix, silently. Reproduced end-to-end with `--page-size 64` and explicit `input_ids` (P, R, Q are 128 tokens each): request `P+R` with storage off, attach, request `P+R+Q`, flush, then request `Q+S`. | | L3 hit for the `Q`-prefixed request | |---|---| | without backfill | **128 tokens** — loaded KV computed after `P+R` | | with backfill | **0** — correctly misses | | control: same sequence after its own backup | 128 in both, so L3 itself is healthy | `UnifiedTreeCore.backfill_missing_hash_values()` walks parent-before-child so each node hashes against an already-filled parent. **`cache_controller.py`.** The storage control queues are now initialized to `None` in `__init__` instead of only existing after `_start_storage_threads()`, so a detach on a server that never attached is a clean no-op rather than an `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Tests Output stability is asserted throughout: every scenario re-runs fixed prompts and compares them byte-for-byte against a baseline captured before any attach. ## Tests **15-scenario attach/detach state machine**, run in one server process, asserting per step that the HTTP result is as expected, the server stays healthy, output is unchanged, and `GET /hicache/storage-backend` reflects reality: - traffic → attach → traffic → detach → traffic - attach → traffic → detach - attach → attach (same backend → 200, policies updated; different backend → 400, state unchanged) - attach → detach → detach; detach before any attach - attach/detach cycled 5× with traffic in between - interleaved traffic/attach/traffic/attach/traffic/detach/traffic/detach/traffic - L3 actually used when attached (960 tokens) and unused when detached (0) - invalid policies rejected without changing state - attach onto a warm tree, then extend an existing prefix (the backfill path) - **attach/detach hammered under concurrent traffic**: 16 ops → `[200, 400×15]`, every 400 a `not idle` refusal, state never half-applied, no output drift - **8× attach + real L3 traffic + detach**: L3 hit count constant at 960 across rounds, which is the observable proof that host pages come back (the scheduler's invariant checker guards the device pool but not the host pool) Result: **157 PASS / 0 FAIL on 1 GPU and again under `--tp-size 2`** (48 attaches, repeatedly creating and destroying the prefetch gloo groups; no traceback, SIGQUIT, leak or NCCL/gloo anomaly after server ready). **Unit tests** — `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` pins the contract that a backfilled hash chain is identical to one hashed from the start. Verified by mutation: stubbing `backfill_missing_hash_values` to `return 0` turns two cases red; restoring it turns them green. Full file: 1046 passed, 0 failed. **Registered e2e** — `test_hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach.py` now covers both implementations via a subclass, so the existing HiRadixCache coverage is retained rather than switched over. 2 passed. ## Notes `HiRadixCache` has the same unhashed-node issue and the same non-idempotent detach when no backend was ever attached. Both are left alone here to keep this PR scoped to the unified tree. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32210047237](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210047237)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32213695558](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32213695558)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion][Refactor] Refactor and unify RoPE execution for DiT models using RotaryEmbedding based on CustomOp
signal.text: ## Motivation Currently, DiT models across SGLang call various ad-hoc functions to apply Rotary Position Embeddings. The choice of function depends on the target hardware device, argument types, and model-specific configurations. Furthermore, internal branches within these functions often perform device type checks again, leading to code fragmentation and duplication. To clean up and unify this behavior, this PR leverages SGLang's existing `CustomOp` mechanism to enhance the core `RotaryEmbedding` class located in `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`. This abstraction allows models to invoke RoPE through a single, unified interface without writing device-specific handling inside model code, significantly simplifying codebase maintainability and cross-platform execution. ## Modifications This PR is a continuation of [PR #31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453). Modified 5 key files to implement unified RoPE dispatch and propagate complex frequencies: ### 1. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py` - Updated `get_freqs_cis()` to return both standard `cos_sin_cache` tuples (`freqs_cis`) and pre-calculated complex frequency tuples (`freqs_complex`). - Propagated `freqs_complex` through `_prepare_cond_kwargs` and pipeline stages. - Added Sequence Parallelism sharding for `img_complex` via `shard_rotary_emb_for_sp()`, enabling pre-computed complex frequencies to be passed directly to the Qwen Image DiT model. ### 2. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py` - Implemented `forward_npu`, `forward_cuda`, and `forward_native` backend methods inside the `RotaryEmbedding`. - Extended signatures to flexibly accept any RoPE inputs: `complex_freqs`, `cos`/`sin`, or 2D `cos_sin_cache`. - Integrated unified dispatching across lower-level implementations: - `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` (for complex multiplication). - `_apply_rotary_emb` (for standard PyTorch RoPE). - `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` (for optimized CUDA execution). - Standardized tensor dimension expectations: `query` and `key` as 4D `[batch, seq_len, num_heads, head_size]`, `complex_freqs` as 3D `[num_tokens, 1, head_size // 2]`, and `cos`/`sin` as 2D `[num_tokens, head_size // 2]`. ### 3. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/layernorm.py` - Added optional `freqs_complex` parameter to `apply_qk_norm_rope` and `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. - Replaced FlashInfer calls in the fallback path with the unified `RotaryEmbedding`. - Preserved the existing CUDA fused QK-Norm + RoPE kernel (`fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`) to ensure zero performance regression on CUDA. ### 4. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py` - Refactored `SelfAttention.forward` to implement the usage of `RotaryEmbedding`. ### 5. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py` - Updated `QwenImageCrossAttention` to extract `freqs_complex` from `cross_attention_kwargs`. - Passed `img_complex` and `txt_complex` into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`, enabling Qwen Image DiT cross-attention layers to leverage complex RoPE. ### 6. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/glm_image.py` - Updated `GlmImageAttention` with `RotaryEmbedding` class usage. - Replaced the `_apply_rotary_emb` and `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` functions with `self.rotary_emb()` call . ### 7. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py` - Updated `FluxAttention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 8. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py` - Updated `Flux2Attention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 9. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/joy_image.py` - Updated `MMDoubleStreamBlock` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ## Accuracy Tests The changes were tested on openmoss/MOVA-360p, GLM-Image, black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev, unsloth/FLUX.2-dev, jd-opensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit-Diffusers, nv-community/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image and MusePublic/Qwen-image models. ### Mova video generation (the same as before changes): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/396ce85d-df45-432a-a7bf-6d87b1fdb6ee ### QwenImage image generation (the same as before changes): ### Flux image generation (the same as before changes): ### Flux2 image generation (the same as before changes): ### JoyImage image generation (the same as before changes): ### Cosmos3 image generation (the same as before changes): ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### For MOVA testing and profiling were used listed below commands: ### 1. SGLang Server Launch Command ```bash sglang serve --model-path $(pwd)/mova_video_360p --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --num-gpus 4 --ring-degree 1 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode memory --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode server --vae-tiling --vae-sp ``` ### 2. signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Gemma 4 multimodal models currently build their vision and audio components and load their weights even for text-only serving. This increases memory usage and model load time. It also causes SGLang to treat the model as multimodal and disable the prefill CUDA graph because breakable CUDA graphs are incompatible with multimodal models. This PR makes Gemma 4 multimodal loading opt-in with `--enable-multimodal`, matching Llama 4 and Gemma 3. > On a DGX Spark with TP1, text-only mode increased the default static memory fraction from `0.8115` to `0.8880` and reduced memory used by model weights. Together, these changes increased the KV cache capacity from 265,062 to 326,684 tokens, an increase of 61,622 tokens or 23.2%. ## Modifications - Default `gemma4_mm` and `gemma4_unified` to text-only mode. - Build and load vision and audio components only when `--enable-multimodal` is set. - Update Gemma 4 deployment documentation with the new default and flag. - Enable multimodal mode explicitly in the existing Gemma 4 MMMU eval configurations. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This PR does not change model computation. The registered Gemma 4 MMMU eval configurations now pass `--enable-multimodal` explicitly and keep their existing thresholds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This PR only skips multimodal component construction and weight loading during text-only serving. The inference path is unchanged when multimodal mode is enabled. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https:// docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Add FlashInfer prefill context parallelism
signal.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer did not support CP-v2 prefill, so dense MHA/GQA models could not use the existing zigzag context-parallel strategy with the FlashInfer attention backend. ## Modifications - Add FlashInfer dispatch to the CP strategy and implement CP-aware paged prefill metadata/execution. - Materialize full KV state before each local FlashInfer attention invocation while preserving zigzag query sharding. - Validate supported configurations: CP-v2, zigzag, dense MHA/GQA, replicated dense MLP weights, and disabled prefill CUDA graphs. - Replicate Qwen3 dense MLP weights when `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` is selected so TP collectives do not mix different CP token shards. - Add two-GPU synthetic MHA/GQA coverage, configuration/metadata rejection tests, and Qwen3-0.6B TP2-vs-CP2 server correctness with prefix reuse. ## Accuracy Tests Pinned image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:6f91b6bbe3a02da260341b1ee36e8df647e26e8a71d7e74799824e7009f2e2e2` ```text python -m pytest -q test/registered/cp/test_flashinfer_prefill_cp.py 5 passed, 32 subtests passed in 224.17s ``` Qwen3-0.6B output tokens and top-logprob values matched TP2 within the test tolerance, including radix-prefix reuse. Formatting and repository checks also passed: - Black - isort - Ruff (`F401,F821,UP037`) - `scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Environment: - 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 - Driver 580.95.05 - Ubuntu 22.04.5 - CUDA 13.0.1 - FlashInfer attention, Qwen3-0.6B, batch size 1, output length 1 - Five measured samples per mode and input length CP command additionally used `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=1 --attn-cp-size 2 --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag`. | Input tokens | TP2 mean latency | CP2 mean latency | TP2 throughput | CP2 throughput | CP speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2,048 | 70.75 ms | 47.16 ms | 28,959 tok/s | 43,512 tok/s | **1.50×** | | 8,192 | 282.40 ms | 194.41 ms | 29,009 tok/s | 42,139 tok/s | **1.45×** | <details> <summary>Nsight Compute result</summary> A replay-safe, Qwen-shaped FlashInfer attention invocation was profiled with Nsight Compute 2025.3.1 using container-only `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` (not privileged mode). | Metric | Value | |---|---:| | Attention kernel duration | 54.53 µs | | SM throughput | 30.01% peak | | DRAM throughput | 11.84% peak | | Tensor pipeline activity | 30.01% peak | | Achieved / theoretical occupancy | 14.35% / 16.67% | | Registers per thread | 245 | | Shared memory per block | 50,256 bytes | | L1 / L2 sector hit rate | 1.98% / 88.46% | NCU classified the kernel as latency/occupancy limited rather than DRAM-bandwidth limited. Register and shared-memory pressure limit residency, while NCU also identified math-pipe throttling, workload imbalance, and inefficient global-load sector utilization. These findings concern the upstream FlashInfer kernel; the end-to-end SGLang path already shows the speedups above. A direct distributed NCU replay was not used for conclusions because replay pauses one rank while another waits in NCCL collectives. The focused profile isolates the attention kernel and avoids that replay artifact. </details> ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit tools. - [x] Add unit and two-GPU integration tests. - [x] Documentation is not required for this backend implementation change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32265859094](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265859094)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32265858544](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265858544)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: `batch_is_full` latched during final chunked-prefill pass starves waiting queue until a running request finishes (self-healing variant of #28530 / #22518)
signal.text: ## Summary With `--max-running-requests 4` and chunked prefill enabled, 4 concurrent cold prompts result in only 3 running requests; the 4th waits in the queue until one of the running requests **finishes decoding entirely**, even though all resource pools are nearly empty. Root cause: `running_batch.batch_is_full` is latched `True` during the final chunked-prefill pass and is never re-evaluated on the steady-state decode path. This is the same stale-flag family as #28530 and #22518 (and the ordering issue in #14872), but triggered by a different, much more common path: **normal generation traffic with chunked prefill**. Unlike #28530 it does not permanently deadlock — it self-heals when a running request completes — so it presents as a latency / throughput cliff rather than a hang, which is likely why it hasn't been reported. ## Environment - sglang v0.5.17 (`lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image, pulled 2026-08) - Model: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (hybrid GDN / linear-attention architecture), `--trust-remote-code` - Single GPU, Docker (WSL2 backend) - Relevant flags: ``` --max-running-requests 4 --cuda-graph-max-bs 4 --max-mamba-cache-size 24 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --context-length 262144 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph ``` ## Symptom 4 concurrent requests with unique ~3100-token prompts (staggered 0/0.2/0.4/0.8s): - **Observed**: 3 requests run, the 4th stays in the waiting queue. Decode-phase queue events show it is only admitted after one of the 3 finishes. In the original production-like scenario (longer prompts), the queued request waited **~4.5 minutes** while the server was otherwise idle-capable. - **Resource headroom at the moment of starvation**: KV pool 382,958 tokens with ≤4% used; mamba state pool 16/24 slots used. No limit is anywhere near reached. - **Self-healing**: as soon as one running request completes its decode, the queued request is admitted immediately — no restart needed (unlike #28530). ## Root cause In `Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw()` (v0.5.17, `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`): 1. During the pass where the last chunked-prefill continuation finishes, the in-flight `chunked_req` occupies the last allocatable slot, so one of the admission paths (in our trace L3204: `len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs)`) sets `running_batch.batch_is_full = True`. 2. The batch then transitions to steady-state decode. On the decode path, `batch_is_full` is only reset when the batch shrinks / becomes empty / retracts — none of which happens while all requests are mid-decode. 3. Every subsequent scheduler pass hits the early return (`if (running_batch.batch_is_full or len(self.waiting_queue) == 0) and self.chunked_req is None`), so the waiting queue is starved until a running request finishes and the batch rebuild path finally clears the flag. I diffed v0.5.17 against `main` (fetched 2026-08-19): all 14 read/write sites of `batch_is_full` are equivalent — the bug is still present on main. ## Minimal reproduction ```python import concurrent.futures as cf, random, string, time, urllib.request, json URL = "http://localhost:8004/v1/chat/completions" # server port MODEL = "Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4" # any model + chunked prefill should work def rand_text(n): return "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " ", k=n)) def call(idx, delay): time.sleep(delay) t0 = time.time() prompt = f"[{time.time()}-{idx}] " + rand_text(4200) + "\nSummarize the above." body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": 400, "temperature": 0.7, "stream": False} req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r: resp = json.load(r) print(f"req{idx}: total={time.time()-t0:.1f}s usage={resp.get('usage')}", flush=True) if __name__ == "__main__": with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex: list(ex.map(call, range(4), [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8])) ``` Expected: 4 requests admitted (4 slots available, ~3100-token prompts each needing 2 chunked passes at 2048). Observed: 3 admitted, 1 queued until first completion. ## Proposed fix Re-evaluate fullness at the top of every `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw()` pass: ```python # FIX(qwen38-queue-starvation): batch_is_full can be latched True during # the final chunked-prefill pass (the in-flight chunked continuation # occupies the last allocatable slot) and is never reset on the decode # path, starving waiting requests until a running request finishes. # Re-evaluate fullness every pass; the allocatable-reqs guard below and # the budget gates in add_one_req still protect all real resources. running_batch.batch_is_full = False ``` placed immediately before the early-return check: ```python if ( running_batch.batch_is_full or len(self.waiting_queue) == 0 ) and self.chunked_req is None: ``` Rationale: `batch_is_full` is a per-pass admission hint, but it is persisted on the long-lived `ScheduleBatch` object, so a stale value survives across scheduler passes. The flag is re-derived inside the pass anyway (L3138 / L3204 / L3209 / L3246), and `PrefillAdder` budget gates enforce all real resource limits, so an unconditional reset cannot over-admit. ## Verification (same repro script) - Before: 3 running + 1 queued; 4th request delayed ~4s in the minimal repro (~4.5 min in the original longer-prompt scenario). - After: all 4 requests admitted immediately, completed uniformly in 8.3–9.2s, **zero** decode-phase queue events. - No regression observed in mixed prefill/decode steady state over extended runs. ## Related - #28530 — NO_TOKEN rejection latches `batch_is_full`, permanent deadlock (page_size > 1) - #22518 — embedding server deadlock, stale `batch_is_full` after first full batch - #14872 — NO_TOKEN set after preemption check, preemption never triggers All share the same underlying defect: `batch_is_full` is sticky state with incomplete reset coverage. A per-pass re-evaluation fixes this whole family of triggers; alternatively each set site could be paired with a guaranteed reset, but that is more invasive.

signal.title: [diffusion] Guard unsupported quantized component checkpoints
signal.text: ## Summary - add one fail-closed admission boundary for native auxiliary component loaders that only materialize plain state dicts - reject detected top-level, nested text-config, and compressed-tensors quantization metadata before model construction or large weight reads - apply the boundary to connectors/duration heads, bridges, diffusion decoders, sound tokenizers, spatial upsamplers, and vocoders - keep the local PE model on its Transformers `from_pretrained` path, where compatible quantization formats remain model-specific - use one documentation contract across the overview, CLI, compatibility matrix, and quantization guide ## Motivation #35184 makes independent component repository routing generic and safely routes supported quantized VAEs. The remaining raw-state native loaders still had no common quantization admission rule, so a quantized component repo could be interpreted as a dense module or fail only after allocating/loading weights. Path routing and quantized materialization are separate capabilities. This PR does not add a generic per-component quantization knob: such a knob would overstate support until each loader has a matching backend. Existing transformer, native encoder, VAE, PE/Transformers, and upstream AutoModel quantization paths remain unchanged. ## Validation - all pre-commit hooks pass - focused unit coverage added for metadata layouts and early rejection order - runtime tests left to CI <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32258969645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258969645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32258969397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258969397)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(diffusion): add OmniDreams autoregressive video world model
signal.text: ## Motivation Add OmniDreams, a 2B distilled autoregressive driving-video world model (Cosmos-Predict2.5-based), to `multimodal_gen`. Given a first frame + a per-frame HD-map control signal, it rolls out a temporally-coherent driving video via 2-step Self-Forcing flow-match denoising over a rolling block KV cache. Served both one-shot (HTTP `/v1/videos`) and realtime (WebSocket `/v1/realtime_video/generate`). Related issue: #27214. ## What changed - Added the OmniDreams pipeline: flat-checkpoint DiT loading, AR rollout with `BlockKVCache` (sink + rolling window), per-chunk HD-map conditioning, and seam-free Wan VAE decode. 38 files. - Added realtime generation through the shared `RealtimeModelAdapter` base, with per-chunk HD-map control events and incremental frame output. - Kept the default runtime in pure PyTorch / BF16 (no custom CUDA extensions). - Added optional acceleration paths that degrade gracefully: - **FP8 GEMM**: `sgl_kernel.fp8_scaled_mm` for the MLP linears (56/284); falls back to `torch._scaled_mm` when sgl_kernel is unavailable. - **SageAttention-3**: `sageattn3_blackwell` direct call for self-attention (FP4/FP8); falls back to PyTorch SDPA when sageattn3 is not built. - **Breakable CUDA graph**: `make_breakable_attention_forward` installed on `OmniDreamsAttention.forward` (break at attention, capture the rest). `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` also enables Full CG for the fixed-shape VAE decode stage. - **torch.compile**: the DiT is compile-ready (`_compile_conditions`); the base `DenoisingStage` handles compilation via `--enable-torch-compile`. - Refactored for conciseness: unified offline/realtime AR chunk body via `_run_ar_chunk` + `_ARChunkCtx` (−458 LOC); removed dead cross-view attention, `shift_t_freqs`, SP post-process no-op, and Phase annotations. ## Compatibility - Default path: BF16 + PyTorch SDPA (no sgl_kernel / sageattn3 / BCG required). - FP8 GEMM activates only when sgl_kernel is importable on a CUDA device; otherwise falls back to `torch._scaled_mm`. - SageAttention-3 activates only when `sageattn3` is importable; otherwise SDPA. Not a runtime dependency for the default path. - BCG is opt-in via `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`; transparent pass-through when disabled. - WanVAE `clear_encode_cache` (scoped encoder-only reset) is backward-compatible: standalone encoders are unaffected (no live decoder cache). ## Validation - Unit tests: 19 passed (construction, RoPE, BlockKVCache, scheduler, DiT forward, AR rollout, config, state-dict key fixture, num_chunks math). 4 GPU tests fail on tiny arch (head_dim=12 triggers Triton RoPE power-of-2 constraint — not a production issue; real model uses head_dim=128). - E2E on RTX 6000D (sm_120a, 85GB): | Config | 13f Total | 100f Total | Peak VRAM | |---|---|---|---| | Eager bf16 + sage3 | 8.34s | 36.64s | 46.2 GB | | fp8 + BCG | 8.18s | 35.79s | 46.9 GB | - FP8 vs BF16 numerical consistency: **bit-identical** output (13f, same seed, per-frame max_diff=0.0000). FP8 swaps 56 MLP linears; attention stays bf16. - Full CG decode saves 0.4s at 100f (14.30→13.90s, −2.8%). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32265071574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265071574)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32265071434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32265071434)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix MoE MORI Accuracy Issue
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a bug where MoE models served with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` produce garbage output (0/10 on known-answer accuracy), while the exact same model/config with `--moe-a2a-backend none` is correct (10/10). This reproduces on: - Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8) - Hy3-preview / Hunyuan (`HYV3ForCausalLM`, 192 experts, top-8, with shared experts) It reproduces at single node (where MoRI runs its IntraNode kernel) and at multi-node (InterNode/RDMA kernel), so it is not tied to a specific transport. ### Root Cause After the experts run, `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` / `HYV3MoEFused` apply a post-experts all-reduce (`moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce` / `moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`), gated by `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`. That all-reduce is correct for backends whose experts return a partial result per rank. But MoRI's `combine` already all-to-all-reduces each token's expert outputs back to the source rank — the routed output is already complete and replicated across the group, exactly like the `flashinfer` and `pplx` dispatchers, which are already excluded from the post-experts all-reduce. Because `mori` was not in the skip list, the extra all-reduce re-reduces an already-complete result, summing it `ep_size`/`tp_size`× and destroying the output. We confirmed this directly by dumping per-rank MoE tensors on the failing server: the routed MoE output is identical across all ranks (already reduced by MoRI combine), and the post-experts `final_out` equals `Σ_ranks(routed)` (i.e. `ep_size × routed`), the fingerprint of the erroneous re-reduce. A reference-trajectory comparison against a correct HuggingFace forward on the same prompt showed layer-0 attention matching (cosine ≈ 1.0) but the trajectory diverging starting at the first MoE layer's output — isolating the defect to the post-experts reduce, not to MoRI's dispatch/GEMM/combine (which produce numerically correct values). ### Specific to Hunyuan 3 `HYV3MoEFused` adds a shared expert (`shared_mlp`, built with `reduce_results=False`) to the routed output before the all-reduce. Under MoRI, the routed output is already full/replicated (must not be reduced again), but the shared output is still a TP/EP partial (still needs reducing). So simply skipping the blanket all-reduce fixes the routed part but leaves `shared` at a fraction (`1/group_size`), which still corrupts the sum. The fix reduces only the shared partial over the same group(s) the blanket reduce would have used, then adds it to the already-full routed output. Qwen3 has no shared experts, so it needs only the skip. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py` — `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`: add an `is_mori()` skip alongside the existing `is_flashinfer()` / `is_pplx()` skips (same "combine already reduces to source rank" rationale). This alone fully fixes models without shared experts (e.g. Qwen3). - `python/sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py` — in both `_forward_single_stream` and `_forward_dual_stream`, for the MoRI path only, reduce the shared-expert partial over the EP/TP group before adding it to the already-full routed output; plus the `get_moe_a2a_backend` import. Required for Hunyuan/Hy3 and any MoRI model with shared experts. Both changes are gated on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()`, so `none`, `flashinfer`, `deepep`, and `pplx` behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy = greedy known-answer probe (10 factual prompts, temperature 0). Baseline `mori` is the unpatched image; `none` is the reference-correct control. ### Probe Test | Model | Nodes | Geometry | Backend | Before Fix | After Fix | |-------|:-----:|----------|---------|:--------:|:--------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | - Qwen3: clean PASS at 1/2/4 nodes (0/10 degenerate). - Hy3: all answers correct at 1/2/4 nodes. At multi-node the probe's separate degenerate-tail heuristic flags 3–4/10 (the base model repeats after answering), but the correct `none` reference shows the same 2–4/10 — i.e. it's a base-model/prompt artifact, not a regression from this fix. - Controls: `--moe-a2a-backend none` remains 10/10 (unchanged), confirming the fix is scoped to MoRI. Both single-node (MoRI IntraNode) and multi-node (MoRI InterNode/RDMA) paths verified. ### GSM8K (exact-match, 40 problems, 5-shot) | Model | Nodes | Geometry | none (control) | mori (before fix) | mori (after fix) | |-------|:-----:|----------|:--------------:|:-----------------:|:----------------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 87.5% (35/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 90.0% (36/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 85.0% (34/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 92.5% (37/40) | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 77.5% (31/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 80.0% (32/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 80.0% (32/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 80.0% (32/40) | - Before the fix, mori is broken at every scale (Qwen3 0%, Hy3 0–2.5%), consistent with the garbage output on the known-answer probe. - After the fix, mori tracks the none reference at every scale: Qwen3 lands at or slightly above none (within noise at N=40), and Hy3 matches the reference closely (exactly equal at 1 and 4 nodes: 31/40 and 32/40). - The absolute score reflects each base model's own capability (Hy3-preview is a preview model, so its ceiling is lower); the fix restores reference-equivalent accuracy on the MoRI path rather than changing model quality. - Single-node exercises MoRI's IntraNode kernel; 2-node and 4-node exercise MoRI's InterNode (RDMA) kernel. Scored offline against the staged GSM8K test split via final-integer exact-match. ### Test Environment - Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm700-mi30x-20260728` (SGLang upstream `main` @ `84cdfde`, version `0.5.16.dev20260728`), 8× MI300 per node, pure TP (`tp==ep`), `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. - Hy3 runs also apply an orthogonal, environment-specific workaround for AITER's `biased_grouped_topk` on ROCm (falls back to the reference impl when `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output=True`); this is unrelated to the all-reduce fix. ## Follow Up - Other MoRI models with shared experts (beyond Hunyuan) would need the same shared-expert handling in their model file; consider factoring the "reduce shared partial only" step into a shared helper. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32264685472](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32264685472)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32264685079](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32264685079)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: NIXL EP can be built with different top-k index types. signal.title: fix: clean up metrics server processes
signal.text: ## Summary - gracefully terminate metrics test servers before falling back to a process-tree kill - wait for the fallback kill to reap remaining processes ## Root cause The metrics test used the fire-and-forget `kill_process_tree(process.pid)` cleanup path. In [job 95963112642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32215766590/job/95963112642), the launcher and a GPU-owning child process remained alive after the test, so the next test waited for GPU idle until the 30-minute job timeout. Use the existing `terminate_and_kill_process_tree` helper so the server can release its CUDA context gracefully, with a 60-second wait for forced cleanup if needed. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py` - `python3 -m py_compile test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py` - Full GPU test not run locally; it requires the CI GPU runner. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32263095187](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32263095187)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32263094990](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32263094990)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] NSA optimization roadmap
signal.text: ### Attention algorithm [Link to original table](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1u_AaRCEp2xWO3lxBkXJOgzFm4PG9P-88U6M-Dfa-svI/edit?usp=sharing) The parts highlighted in blue is work that has been done or in progress. To summarize: - Use MHA for short context lengths, as suggested in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/DeepSeek_V3_2.pdf - Below context lengths 2K, sparse attention is the same as non-sparse attention and we can skip the logits computation and directly generates the indices for sparse MLA kernel or use MHA when possible - The current flashmla_decode kernel is not well optimized on B200. So a separate dequant kernel + flashmla_sparse_bf16 works better for prefill + fp8 kvcache if the kv cache is not too long compared to the q sequence length. The heuristics will need to be updated after new optimizations to either the prefill or decode kernels, making it a bit hard to use in practice. Detailed analysis is [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1u_AaRCEp2xWO3lxBkXJOgzFm4PG9P-88U6M-Dfa-svI/edit?gid=1552909022#gid=1552909022) ### Kernel optimizations - FP8 per tensor sparse MLA kernel from trtllm - More optimizations to flashmla_decode on B200 - Adaptive MHA attention pathway #11892 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/12788 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/12964 - Layernorm optimization #12044 - quantize_k_cache_fast (curr: 3 kernel, 6us). No need to cat, but pass in two separate tensors. - Optimize `torch.cat([q_nope, q_rope])` by either writing a fast triton/cuda kernel or using torch.compile. It's used for prefill/decode but the prefill one is much bigger and has more room for optimizations. The trtllm kernel supports separate `q_nope` and `q_rope`, but flashmla doesn't. #12215 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13022 - DeepGeMM fp8_mqa_logits optimizations https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13402 ### Indexer optimizations - [Decode] Optimize dual stream in Indexer https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13546 - [Decode] Move deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata to init time, similar to attention kernel metadata compute - [Prefill] Optimize _get_topk_ragged where there are a lot of small kernels. Try multi-stream, torch.compile, and add new kernels when necessary. - [MTP] Enable nextn = 2/4 in deep_gemm.fp8_paged_mqa_logits, which is faster than the current implementation which uses the kernel with nextn = 1 regardless of mtp size. ### Min latency optimizations - Enable TP in Attention

signal.title: │ DFlash2 selector crashes with quantized target lm_head (NVFP4 W4A4): RuntimeError requires dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head │
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary DFlash2 speculative decoding (`--speculative-algorithm DFLASH`) crashes on the first request when the target model has a **quantized `lm_head` (NVFP4 W4A4)**: ```text RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head. ``` This currently blocks DFlash2 from being used with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`. ## Environment * **SGLang:** main @ `c14312a66420b75ca9a11bf1817c4db1fa26b097` (PR #35371) * **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` * **GPU:** RTX PRO 6000 96GB, SM120, CUDA 13.0.3 * **Target:** `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` * MLP + `lm_head`: dynamic NVFP4 W4A4, group size 16 * Attention weights: FP8 * **Draft:** `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` * **TP:** 1 * **Draft tokens:** 8 ## Reproduction ```bash docker run --gpus all lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \ --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 \ --tp 1 ``` The server starts successfully and the DFlash2 draft runner initializes correctly, but the **first `/v1/chat/completions` request crashes**. ## Root Cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py`, `compute_candidates` directly requires the target `lm_head` to be dense FP16/BF16/FP32. This is separate from `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head`, which already supports quantized heads through: ```python lm_head.quant_method.apply(...) ``` DFlash2's selector does not use that path. This also explains why **DSpark works with the same NVFP4 target**: DSpark has its own dense `lm_head`, while DFlash2 borrows the target model's `lm_head`. So this is not a simple `DSpark → DFlash2` configuration change. ## What I Tried I ported the quantized-head selector approach from: https://github.com/r0b0tlab/qwen38-27b-nvfp4-sm121-sglang Their patch replaces the unconditional `raise` with a chunked `lm_head.quant_method.apply(...)` path. That approach reportedly works with their **W4A16** NVFP4 checkpoint. However, with the **RadixArk W4A4** checkpoint, the patch still fails. The W4A4 activation quantization in the `lm_head` appears to prevent the same `quant_method.apply` path from working, but I have not narrowed down the exact failure yet. ## Questions 1. Is a **W4A4 quantized `lm_head`** intended to be supported by the DFlash2 selector? 2. If yes, does the selector need a dedicated W4A4 dequantization/quantized matmul path? 3. If no, should the RuntimeError explicitly state that DFlash2 requires a dense target `lm_head`? 4. Should the DFlash2 documentation/model compatibility requirements explicitly mention this limitation? ## Related * DFlash2 merge: #35371 * Working W4A16 patch: https://github.com/r0b0tlab/qwen38-27b-nvfp4-sm121-sglang * vLLM DFlash2 PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52816 ### Related resources _No response_

signal.title: [AMD] Fuse quantized in_proj layers in Qwen3.5
signal.text: ## Motivation In Qwen3.5 GDN layers the input projection is issued as two separate GEMMs, `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`. Both read the same activation, so on checkpoints that quantize both to the *same* scheme they can be served by one wider GEMM. Keeping them apart costs an extra kernel launch, an extra activation-quantization pass and an extra epilogue per GDN layer per decode step — overhead that is a significant share of decode time at low-to-mid concurrency. This became actionable with the AMD Qwen3.5 MXFP4+AttnFP8 "V2" line, which quantizes `in_proj_ba` to FP8; on V2 all four shards resolve to one scheme and the merge is eligible. ## Modifications - **`qwen3_5.py`**: add `create_qkvzba_proj()`, which builds a single `in_proj_qkvzba` from the four shards (`qkv`, `z`, `b`, `a`) via `MergedColumnParallelLinear`, with N padded 10304 → 10368 for alignment. Gated by `SGLANG_GDN_FUSE_QKVZBA` (default **off**). The merge is attempted only when all four checkpoint shards resolve to the same quantization scheme; a mismatch raises `ValueError`, which is caught and falls back to the existing separate projections. Mixed-precision checkpoints are therefore untouched — on V1, where `in_proj_a/b` stay bf16, the model loads exactly as before. - **`triton_gdn_fused_proj.py`**: parameterize the split/reshape/cat kernel by `QKVZ_STRIDE` / `BA_STRIDE` rather than deriving the row stride from logical widths, so it can read column slices of a wider, padded projection. - No `communicator.py` change, and `_forward_input_proj_fused_quant_amd` is untouched: the merged GEMM is dispatched at the top of `_forward_input_proj`, where `_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear` handles a plain tensor and a fused-AR tuple alike, so one branch covers both entry paths. - **test**: cover the fused split/reshape/cat kernel both for dense inputs and for column slices of a wider projection, which is what the merge produces. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k 5-shot, **full 1319** questions, `lm_eval` `local-chat-completions` with `--apply_chat_template` against `/v1/chat/completions`, server run with `--reasoning-parser qwen3` and `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`. Checkpoint: AMD Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2 (PR#4 revision), 2× MI355X, TP=2. | `SGLANG_GDN_FUSE_QKVZBA` | strict-match | flexible-extract | | --- | --- | --- | | `0` (separate, today's behaviour) | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | | `1` (merged) | **0.9773 ± 0.0041** | **0.9765 ± 0.0042** | The merged arm is 0.6 pp higher, well inside the ±0.4–0.5 pp standard error of each measurement, i.e. the two arms are statistically indistinguishable. No accuracy regression. Note for anyone reproducing: Qwen3.5 V2 is a thinking model. Grading it on `/v1/completions` scores the raw `<think>` text and yields a spurious ~0.82–0.83 for *both* arms; the chat + thinking-off recipe above is the one that reflects real quality. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `bench_serving`, random dataset, OSL 1024, `--random-range-ratio 0.8`, `--num-prompts 10×cc`, `request_rate=inf` with `--max-concurrency`, seed 0. Same checkpoint/hardware as above. Server: `--attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 16 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --disable-radix-cache --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion --enable-dense-fp8` (effective `mem_fraction_static` 0.578, `max_running_requests` 636); the 1k regime adds `--enable-mixed-chunk`. TPOT figures are medians. **8k context (ISL 8192, OSL 1024)** | cc | prompts | TPOT separate (ms) | TPOT merged (ms) | ΔTPOT | total tok/s separate | merged | Δ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 40 | 8.84 | 8.60 | **−2.71%** | 3845.6 | 3954.6 | +2.83% | | 8 | 80 | 11.72 | 11.38 | **−2.90%** | 5782.4 | 5964.7 | +3.15% | | 16 | 160 | 16.57 | 16.15 | **−2.53%** | 8299.6 | 8511.3 | +2.55% | | 32 | 320 | 25.34 | 24.78 | **−2.21%** | 10930.6 | 11136.7 | +1.89% | | 64 | 640 | 40.49 | 39.92 | **−1.41%** | 13903.8 | 14095.0 | +1.38% | **1k context (ISL 1024, OSL 1024)** | cc | prompts | TPOT separate (ms) | TPOT merged (ms) | ΔTPOT | total tok/s separate | merged | Δ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 40 | 8.06 | 7.85 | **−2.61%** | 950.1 | 976.2 | +2.75% | | 8 | 80 | 10.11 | 9.80 | **−3.07%** | 1532.4 | 1579.4 | +3.07% | | 16 | 160 | 13.06 | 12.72 | **−2.60%** | 2409.1 | 2475.6 | +2.76% | | 32 | 320 | 17.91 | 17.52 | **−2.18%** | 3498.6 | 3571.2 | +2.07% | | 64 | 640 | 24.81 | 24.51 | **−1.21%** | 5065.3 | 5132.7 | +1.33% | All 20 cells (2 regimes × 5 concurrencies × 2 arms) favour the merged arm on both TPOT and throughput; tok/s columns are total input+output throughput, and output-only moves by the same percentage.
