signal.title: [Bug] TP>1 LoRA tensor hot-load reuses one-shot ForkingPickler FDs and crashes schedulers
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug is present in the latest release source (`0.5.12.post1`). - [x] A minimal reproducible demo and environment information are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] This issue is written in English. ### Describe the bug `load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` is not safe with tensor parallelism greater than one when the payload is produced by SGLang's `MultiprocessingSerializer`. The serializer uses `ForkingPickler`, so CPU tensor storages are represented by one-shot `multiprocessing.resource_sharer` file-descriptor handles. SGLang serializes the tensor dictionary once, broadcasts the same request to every TP scheduler, and every TP worker independently deserializes the same string. The first consumer removes each handle from the resource-sharer cache; the remaining consumers raise `EOFError`. Relevant `0.5.12.post1` source: - [`Engine.load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` serializes once](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py#L1100-L1120) - [`Scheduler.recv_requests` broadcasts the same request to the TP group](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L1656-L1765) - [Every TP worker calls `MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L188-L204) - [`MultiprocessingSerializer` uses `ForkingPickler`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py#L2234-L2273) This is not a generic Python `resource_sharer` bug: its server deliberately does `self._cache.pop(key)`, so each registered FD is single-use. The issue is broadcasting one single-consumer payload to multiple consumers. Observed end-to-end with an actual SGLang server: - Qwen3-0.6B, 8x H20, `tp_size=8` - rank-16 q/k/v/o LoRA, 224 bf16 CPU tensors (8.75 MiB) - server and serializer shared the same multiprocessing parent/authkey, matching the SGLang `Engine`/embedded-server topology - the HTTP load disconnected after 222 ms - seven schedulers raised `EOFError` - SGLang then received `SIGQUIT` and the server exited - successful loads: **0/1** Using a plain pickle + base64 payload for the same tensor dictionary succeeded for load, one-token generation with the adapter, and unload: **3/3 at TP8**. At TP1, the multiprocessing path is valid and useful. In the same benchmark its warm serialization + HTTP load time was 46.31 ms versus 96.89 ms for inline pickle, so a fix should ideally preserve the optimization for the single-consumer case. ### Reproduction The following latest-release repro isolates the exact payload property used by the TP broadcast. It requires no model or GPU: ```python import multiprocessing as mp import torch from sglang.srt.utils import MultiprocessingSerializer def consume(index, payload, start, results): start.wait() try: restored = MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize(payload) results.put((index, "ok", restored["w"].numel())) except BaseException as exc: results.put((index, type(exc).__name__, str(exc))) if __name__ == "__main__": ctx = mp.get_context("spawn") tensors = {"w": torch.zeros(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16)} payload = MultiprocessingSerializer.serialize(tensors, output_str=True) start = ctx.Event() results = ctx.Queue() workers = [ ctx.Process(target=consume, args=(i, payload, start, results)) for i in range(8) ] for worker in workers: worker.start() start.set() output = sorted(results.get(timeout=30) for _ in workers) for worker in workers: worker.join() print(output) ``` On `sglang==0.5.12.post1`, the result is one success and seven failures: ```text (one worker) ok (seven workers) EOFError ``` The resource-sharer thread also prints seven instances of: ```text send, close = self._cache.pop(key) KeyError: 1 ``` Expected behavior: all eight TP workers load the adapter and the server remains healthy. Potential fixes: 1. Short-term: use an inline pickle/byte payload when `tp_size > 1`, while retaining `MultiprocessingSerializer` for TP1. 2. Performance-preserving: extend the request to carry one independently serialized payload per TP rank, so every rank receives its own FD handles. 3. Alternatively, deserialize once on the leader and explicitly broadcast/copy the tensor contents to the remaining ranks. A downstream workaround using the first approach is being developed in [Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL#227](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL/pull/227). ### Environment Latest-release serializer reproduction: ```text Python: 3.12.0 CUDA available: True GPU: 8x NVIDIA H20 (compute capability 9.0) CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: 12.9 CUDA driver: 535.247.01 PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu128 sglang: 0.5.12.post1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.1 (not used by the CPU-only reproduction) flashinfer_python: 0.6.7.post3 triton: 3.5.1 transformers: 5.3.0 numpy: 2.3.5 fastapi: 0.141.1 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 pyzmq: 27.1.0 ulimit -n: 1000000 ``` The full TP8 server reproduction used the same machine and Python environment with the image's compatible `sglang==0.5.10.post1`. Inspection of `0.5.12.post1` at commit `5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584` confirms that the serialize-once, TP-broadcast, deserialize-per-rank path remains unchanged.

signal.title: [Model] Add deepseek v3 bidirectional embedding
signal.text: ## Motivation Add native SGLang support for **`ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-10B-A1.8B-0826`**, a text-embedding model built on the **DeepSeek-V3 MoE (MLA)** backbone but run with **encoder-style (bidirectional) attention** and mean pooling. Its HF checkpoint declares `architectures=["DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel"]` with `is_causal=false`. DeepSeek uses MLA, whose absorbed attention kernels are causal-only, so bidirectional support requires routing through the non-absorbed MHA prefill path. This is one of a pair of PRs adding the Giga-Embeddings models; the Qwen3 sibling (`Qwen3BidirectionalModel`) is submitted separately. ## Modifications Driven entirely by the checkpoint's own `is_causal=False` (default `True` leaves the causal path unchanged). Since embedding models are **prefill-only**, they are served through `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA`'s non-absorbed MHA prefill path (`attn_mha`), which is a standard `RadixAttention` that honors `attn_type`. - **`models/deepseek_v2.py`**: set `attn_mha` to `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` when `config.is_causal is False` (the absorbed `attn_mqa` decode path stays causal and is unused for embeddings). - **`models/deepseek_v2_embedding.py`** (new): `DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel` subclasses `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` to reuse all MoE/MLA weight loading, replacing the logits path with `Pooler(MEAN, normalize=True)`. - **`configs/model_config.py`**: register the arch as **MLA** (so an MLA KV pool is allocated, not MHA) and as a non-generation embedding model. - **`configs/embedding_model_spec.py`**: register as a bidirectional, mean-pooling embedding architecture (auto-enables embedding mode). - **`server_args.py` / `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: for this architecture, force **`--attention-backend triton`**, `--disable-cuda-graph`, `--disable-radix-cache`, `--chunked-prefill-size -1`. Rationale (all verified below): only Triton honors `ENCODER_ONLY` on the MLA MHA prefill (flashinfer silently runs causal); CUDA-graph capture pins the absorbed causal-only MLA kernel; and prefix/split-prefill reuse is invalid under bidirectional attention. This mirrors the existing HRM-Text handling. Serving is fully automatic: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-10B-A1.8B-0826 \ --is-embedding --trust-remote-code ``` ## Accuracy Tests Reference = HF `AutoModel` (`trust_remote_code`, `is_causal=False`), mean-pool over non-padding tokens + L2 normalize. (The remote checkpoint stores per-expert MoE weights; the reference loads them fused.) SGLang served with the out-of-the-box command above. | Backend | min cosine vs HF (batched & single) | Result | |---|---|---| | triton (default / forced) | 0.996 | ✅ PASS | | flashinfer (auto-overridden → triton) | 0.996 | ✅ PASS (after override) | Retrieval sanity (query → documents): `Paris` 0.68 ≫ `mitochondria` 0.16 ≫ `photosynthesis` 0.05. Single-request and batched outputs agree. **Regressions caught during testing (all fixed in this PR):** - Without the MLA registration, startup crashed (`'MHATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'set_mla_kv_buffer'`) — an MHA KV pool was allocated for an MLA model. - With the `flashinfer` backend, the MLA prefill ran **causal** and produced wrong embeddings (min cosine ~0.35). Forcing Triton restores parity; verified that launching with `--attention-backend flashinfer` logs the override to `triton` and yields min cosine 0.9964. A unit test guards the capability adjustment (triton force + CUDA-graph/radix/chunked disable). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No changes to existing DeepSeek code paths (the bidirectional branch is gated on `is_causal=False`, which no existing checkpoint sets). The new path is prefill-only embedding. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v3_bidirectional_embedding_registration.py`; also updated `test_embedding_model_spec.py`). - [x] Update documentation (`docs/docs/supported-models/embedding_models.mdx`). - [x] Provide accuracy results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32260138562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32260138562)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32260137952](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32260137952)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Add qwen3 bidirectional embedding
signal.text: ## Motivation Add native SGLang support for **`ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-3B-0826`**, a text-embedding model built on the Qwen3 backbone but run with **encoder-style (bidirectional) attention** and mean pooling. Its HF checkpoint declares `architectures=["Qwen3BidirectionalModel"]` with `is_causal=false`; without native support it falls back to the Transformers backend (and, more importantly, SGLang has no bidirectional-attention path wired for Qwen3). This is one of a pair of PRs adding the Giga-Embeddings models; the DeepSeek-V3 sibling (`DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel`) is submitted separately. ## Modifications The whole change is driven by the checkpoint's own `is_causal=False` flag (default `True` keeps the existing causal path byte-for-byte identical). It mirrors the merged `Lfm2BidirectionalModel` / `gemma3_causal.py` patterns. - **`models/qwen3.py`**: thread an `attn_type` through `Qwen3Attention` / `Qwen3DecoderLayer`, selected from `config.is_causal` → `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` when bidirectional, else `AttentionType.DECODER` (unchanged default). - **`models/qwen3_embedding.py`**: add `Qwen3BidirectionalModel` (reuses the existing bare-backbone embedding wrapper; `Pooler(MEAN, normalize=True)`), registered via the `EntryClass` list. - **`configs/model_config.py`**: classify `Qwen3BidirectionalModel` as a non-generation (embedding) architecture. - **`configs/embedding_model_spec.py`**: register it as a bidirectional, mean-pooling embedding architecture (auto-enables embedding mode). - **`server_args.py`**: for this architecture, force `--disable-cuda-graph`, `--disable-radix-cache`, `--chunked-prefill-size -1`. Bidirectional attention over the whole prompt makes prefix/split-prefill reuse invalid, and — verified below — the captured prefill CUDA graph corrupts the non-causal attention. This mirrors the existing HRM-Text / EmbeddingGemma handling. Serving is fully automatic: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-3B-0826 \ --is-embedding --trust-remote-code ``` ## Accuracy Tests Reference = HF `AutoModel` (`trust_remote_code`, `is_causal=False`), mean-pool over non-padding tokens + L2 normalize. SGLang served with the out-of-the-box command above (auto-guards applied). Cosine similarity, per text: | Backend | min cosine vs HF (batched & single) | Result | |---|---|---| | triton | 0.997 | ✅ PASS | | flashinfer | 0.9965 | ✅ PASS | | torch_native | 0.9976 | ✅ PASS | Retrieval sanity (query → documents): `Paris` 0.68 ≫ `mitochondria` 0.10 ≫ `photosynthesis` 0.01. Single-request and batched outputs agree (no cross-sequence leakage). > Note: `fa3` could not be validated on the test GPU (RTX 5090, SM120 — fa3 requires SM 80–90). It is a regular-attention backend that honors `ENCODER_ONLY`, so it is expected to pass on Hopper; a maintainer with Hopper hardware may want to confirm. **Regression caught during testing:** with the prefill CUDA graph enabled, embeddings were wrong and batch-size-dependent (min cosine ~0.18). Disabling CUDA graph (as this PR does) restores parity. A unit test guards the capability adjustment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No changes to existing code paths (the causal Qwen3 path is unchanged). The new path is prefill-only embedding; no decode/CUDA-graph impact on existing models. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_bidirectional_embedding_registration.py`; also updated `test_embedding_model_spec.py` and `test_qwen3_embedding_registration.py` for the extended registry). - [x] Update documentation (`docs/docs/supported-models/embedding_models.mdx`). - [x] Provide accuracy results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32259721331](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259721331)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32259720337](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32259720337)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(dsv4): Support DeepSeek V4(C4A C128A, SWA with C4A Indexer/State) with FlexKV
signal.text: ## Summary Add DeepSeek V4 support to the redesigned mainline FlexKV integration. - register c4, c128, and c4-indexer KV pools through FlexKV multi-group layouts - persist the C4 attention and indexer compress states as SWA-page sidecars - compose FlexKV I/O with `UnifiedRadixCache` for hybrid SWA bookkeeping - save exact sidecar snapshots at both prefill and final committed boundaries - propagate DP/CP/PP coordinates using the current mainline parallel-state APIs This is adapted to the current `FlexKVConnector` / radix-cache registry design; it does not reintroduce the older `BaseKVConnector` and `ExtendedRadixCache` abstractions. ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 DSA attention reads both restored KV tensors and runtime `kv_score` compress states. FlexKV previously persisted the main KV pools but not those state buffers. After a GPU cache flush, a FlexKV hit could therefore restore byte-correct KV while DSA consumed stale scores. The state buffers share the SWA physical-page mapping, so this change registers SWA KV and the two C4 state groups on FlexKV's dedicated SWA channel and supplies the translated SWA slot mapping on load and store. Host lookup is SWA-aware and only reports a reusable hit when the matching prefix also owns its sidecars. State snapshots are prefix-boundary specific. Storing only the final `prompt + output` leaf leaves no valid sidecar at the prompt boundary and causes a strict SWA-aware R2 lookup to return zero. The hybrid wrapper now stores the non-chunked prefill boundary as well as the final committed boundary. The two asynchronous stores use independent tracking keys, and reset drains connector I/O before inner-cache slots are released. ## Configuration `swa_multi_group` is tri-state in the paired FlexKV configuration: - omitted or `true`: store and restore SWA KV plus the attention/indexer compress states - `false`: store and restore SWA KV only The paired FlexKV implementation is `taco-project/FlexKV` commit `60ace11a8834b4497631ec8f35af9a7e6fa2bdd0` on `merge/dpskv4-to-main`. ## Current limitations - DeepSeek V4 unified-KV layout is not supported yet. - `--enable-hisparse` has an independent device-page mapping and fails explicitly for now. - Other hybrid SWA models and Mamba/SSM pools are not covered by this integration. ## Validation - Ruff on the changed Python files - Black formatting check - Python bytecode compilation and `git diff --check` - focused behavioral checks for prefill/final store tracking and reset ordering - FlexKV heterogeneous SWA/state layout and configuration tests The local macOS environment does not contain SGLang's full runtime dependency set, so the registered pytest module could not be collected there. GPU end-to-end validation remains required; this PR stays draft until R1 emits a prefill-boundary PUT and R2 performs real main plus sidecar H2D with baseline accuracy. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32244711456](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244711456)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32244711291](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32244711291)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: jianan-gu

signal.title: [mem_cache] SWA radix cache: evict branch tail sliding window last
signal.text: ## Motivation `SWARadixCache.evict()` walks the SWA LRU list without any notion of where a branch ends, so it can tombstone (or delete) a node that sits inside the last `sliding_window_size` tokens of a branch. Because `_match_prefix_helper` can only stop at a node that has `sliding_window_size` **consecutive non-tombstone** tokens in front of it (the `match_len_since_tombstone` check), tombstoning a single node inside that trailing window makes the *entire* branch unmatchable: the reusable prefix collapses from tens of thousands of tokens to 0, while the branch's full KV stays allocated in the full pool until full-side LRU reclaims it. This is a cliff, not a gradual degradation — the tail window is the only part of a branch whose SWA KV is load-bearing for reuse. Idle branches are hit first. `_match_post_processor` uses `reset_node_and_parents_mru`, which makes root-side nodes least-recently-used *within* a branch, but ordering *across* branches is still by last access time. A request that is parked in a tool call has its whole branch older than any active branch, so its tail nodes are evicted before the root-side nodes of busy branches — the opposite of what we want. Impact: agentic / multi-turn tool-calling workloads on SWA models (e.g. window 128) with a small SWA pool re-prefill their whole history when they come back from a tool call, even though (a) their full KV is still cached and (b) decode only needs the last `sliding_window_size` SWA tokens. Reproduction sketch (window = 4, two branches sharing an 8-token prefix): ``` shared(8) -> tail1(4) # branch 1, parked in a tool call shared(8) -> other(8) # branch 2, just matched ``` `evict(swa_num_tokens=4)` picks `tail1` (the LRU node) and deletes it, so `match_prefix(branch1)` can no longer return the branch. Tombstoning the 8-token `shared` internal node instead frees 2x more SWA tokens *and* keeps branch 1 fully matchable, because 4 (== window) non-tombstone tokens still follow the tombstone. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/swa_radix_cache.py`: - The SWA eviction loop now skips a candidate whose nearest branch end is less than one page-aligned window away, and retries those nodes only once no other candidate is left. This is a **deprioritization, not a reservation** — the eviction target is still met when the SWA pool is genuinely exhausted, and `swa_evictable_size_` accounting plus the scheduler contract are unchanged, so there is no new OOM / retract risk. - New `_is_swa_branch_tail()` computes the shortest token distance from a candidate down to the nearest branch end, where a branch end is a leaf **or** the node right before an existing tombstone (both are valid stop points for `_match_prefix_helper`). The walk is pruned by the window size, so it visits at most the tail of the branch rather than the whole subtree, and it is iterative so a long chunked-prefill chain cannot exhaust the recursion limit. - New `_swa_tail_size()` factors out the `ceil(window / page) * page` formula that `_maybe_split_leaf_for_swa_lock()` already used, so both paths agree on page alignment. Cost of the deprioritized set is `#branch_ends * sliding_window_size` (128 tokens per branch for a 128-token window), negligible against a few hundred K SWA slots. ### Scope: legacy `SWARadixCache` only `unified_cache/components/swa_component.py` has a parallel SWA eviction walk with the same shape — `_evict_device_next_node()` scans the SWA LRU from the tail via `get_lru_no_lock()` / `get_prev_no_lock()`, tombstones internal nodes inline and cascade-deletes leaves (see `unified_cache/components/README.md`) — so it has the same blind spot. This PR intentionally changes only the legacy `SWARadixCache` to keep the diff reviewable: the unified walk is cursor-based (`cursor_begin` / `cursor_next`, plus the `enable_session_radix_cache` path), so skipping a candidate there also needs cursor-recovery semantics rather than the plain `get_prev_no_lock` step used here. Happy to port it in a follow-up, or to fold it into this PR if maintainers would rather land both paths together — please say which you prefer. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — this only changes which cache entry is evicted first, not any model output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not included yet. I do not have a GPU environment attached right now, so the SWA unit tests have not been executed and I have no workload numbers to report. Both are being added to this PR: - unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_unittest.py` covering (1) the branch tail surviving and the prefix staying fully reusable, (2) the previous behavior as a regression baseline, (3) the fallback pass still meeting the eviction target when only tails remain, and (4) `page_size` equal to, below and above the window; - cache hit rate / TTFT / SWA eviction counts for a tool-calling workload under SWA pool pressure. Review feedback on the approach in the meantime is very welcome — in particular whether maintainers would prefer this gated behind a `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_*` env flag (as with `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_SPLIT_LEAF_ON_INSERT`) rather than being on by default. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32258596774](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258596774)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32258594151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258594151)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [4/N] elastic-ep: Scale at DP-attention replica granularity
signal.text: ## Summary This PR follows the Elastic EP CUDA graph recapture PR [#33723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33723) and removes the scale-up topology restriction `dp_size == tp_size == ep_size`. Scale-up now admits complete DP-attention replicas. For example, with fixed `attn_tp_size=2`, a deployment can scale from **DP2/TP4 to DP3/TP6 to DP4/TP8**, adding two physical EP ranks and one logical DP replica per step. The scale API continues to use physical EP sizes. The scheduler, DP controller, and tokenizer use the corresponding logical DP size. ## Changes - Derive the replica width as `attn_tp_size * attn_cp_size` and track the live DP size as `elastic_ep_size / replica_width`. - Size scheduler workers, DPC capacity, joiner offsets, and tokenizer routing in logical DP units. - Keep scale targets and Mooncake/NIXL membership in physical EP-rank units. - Admit and health-check complete replicas instead of individual ranks. - Create fixed attention and DCP groups for joiners using their global rank offset; only Mooncake WORLD grows during scale-up. - Handle the newly exercised MLP synchronization, empty embedding batch, and DCP KV-padding paths. ## Configuration Primary and joiner groups must use the same fixed topology: ```text attn_tp_size attn_cp_size dcp_size moe_dense_tp_size=1 ``` The target EP size must be divisible by `attn_tp_size * attn_cp_size`. ## Known Limitations - Attention TP, attention CP, and DCP sizes cannot change during scale-up. - This PR does not negotiate topology between the primary and joiners. - `moe_dense_tp_size == attn_tp_size` cold launch is outside this PR; `moe_dense_tp_size=1` remains required. - The scale-direction and recovery limitations of the existing Elastic EP scale-up path are unchanged. ## Test Plan The eight-GPU test adds one complete two-rank attention replica per step: | Stage | Physical topology | Logical DP size | | --- | --- | ---: | | Launch | DP2 / TP4 / EP4 | 2 | | First scale | DP3 / TP6 / EP6 | 3 | | Second scale | DP4 / TP8 / EP8 | 4 | It uses fixed `attn_tp_size=2`, `dcp_size=2`, `attn_cp_size=1`, and `moe_dense_tp_size=1`. ```bash python -m pytest -v -s \ "test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUpDP2TP4ToDP4TP8::test_scale_up_on_demand" ``` Validated results: - Eager DP2/TP4 -> DP3/TP6 -> DP4/TP8: passed, GSM8K **63.28%**. - FULL decode CUDA graphs on the same topology: passed, GSM8K **64.45%**. - Existing width-one EP4/DP4 -> EP5/DP5 -> EP6/DP6: passed, GSM8K **64.06%**. - Existing width-one EP4/DP4 -> EP5/DP5 with CUDA graphs: passed, GSM8K **62.50%**. - Focused topology, process-group, utility, and embedding tests: **37 passed**. ## References - [PR #33723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33723) - CUDA graph recapture after scale-up - [PR #30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - runtime EP scale-up - [[RFC] Elastic EP Scale](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32258348897](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258348897)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32258348632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32258348632)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Docs] PaddleOCR-VL: say which stage of the pipeline this serves, show real output
signal.text: Follow-up to #35318, which added the PaddleOCR-VL cookbook. ### What was wrong The intro now states the boundary explicitly, and connects it to something a reader actually needs: the reason the model is prompt-conditioned rather than instruction-following is precisely that the caller — the pipeline — already knows whether a crop is a table, a formula or a chart. ### Also in this PR - The two "Example Output" accordions said "Pending update". They now carry verbatim server output. - The OCR example pointed at `https://example.com/your_page.png`, so it could not be run. It now points at a real public page from the PaddleOCR repo, and the shown output is that page's actual output. - New note: `Table Recognition:` answers in OTSL-style cell tokens (`<fcel>` per cell, `<nl>` per row), not HTML. Easy to get wrong when writing a caller, and nothing on the page said so. ### How the outputs were captured One H200, `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL`, served with the recipe this cookbook generates (`--context-length 16384 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --enable-mixed-chunk --num-continuous-decode-steps 2`, native image processor, breakable prefill CUDA graph active, 2 preprocessing workers), `temperature=0`. The multi-page block is abridged where marked; nothing shown is edited or synthesized. Docs only — no code changes, no test impact. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32220166479](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32220166479)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32220382186](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32220382186)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [KDA] Route Kimi-Linear through native Cake kernels
signal.text: Depends on #34299 for the checkpoint-capable KDA serving surface and on FlashInfer [#4535](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4535) for native `lower_bound=None` kernels. ## Summary - Auto-select BF16 recurrent state and native Cake prefill/decode for Kimi-Linear-48B's D128 equal-head contract at TP-local H4/H8/H16/H32 (TP8/TP4/TP2/TP1). - Feed packed Q/K/V, raw gate, and row-strided beta views directly to FlashInfer without `contiguous()` staging or state gather/scatter copies. - Preserve the native prefill route under breakable CUDA Graph padding by slicing only the live token prefix as storage-sharing row views. - Keep admission fail-closed and retain structured per-layer route events and aggregate counters. Per-event JSON logging remains an explicit diagnostic opt-in. ## Validation - B200 and B300 each pass 85 focused unit tests, 12 GPU decode integrations, and seven GPU prefill integrations, including bounded rows, H4/H8/H16/H32 unbounded routes, checkpoints, packed rows, graph padding, and exact-identity inputs. - The exact final FlashInfer source passes 48 decode and 15 prefill GPU rows per architecture. Six representative launches per target pass warmup, synccheck, and memcheck with zero errors. - A final-source B200 recurrence diagnostic forces old and new decode variants over graph batches 128/136, active batches 1/32/111/128/136, indexed noncompact state, inactive rows, and 256 sequential updates per case. The new two-warp output and recurrent state are bitwise equal to both one-warp variants across all 1,536 updates, with maximum difference `0.0`. - The full-model TP8/local-H4 audit completes every request. Its isolated diagnostic arm records 7,840 prefill and 59,840 decode Cake successes with zero fallback, fatal outcomes, or copied inputs. - Serving performance is faster than FLA, but final inference qualification remains open: Cake scores `0.875` on the 200-example five-shot GSM8K arm and does not clear the strict `>0.88` threshold; FLA scores `0.905`. ## Kimi-Linear-48B TP8/local-H4 serving The performance audit uses one eight-B200 node and independent `Cake, FLA, FLA, Cake` services. Each arm receives 32 workload-shaped warmups followed by 64 measured requests at nominal 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, and cache flush. Values are two-replicate geometric means except peak memory and accuracy. | Metric | Cake | FLA Triton | Cake / FLA or delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Throughput | 27,863.85 token/s | 26,833.37 token/s | `1.0384x` (+3.84%) | | Mean TTFT | 115.913 ms | 134.673 ms | -13.93% | | Median TTFT | 113.900 ms | 137.567 ms | -17.20% | | Mean TPOT | 6.708 ms | 7.035 ms | -4.64% | | Median TPOT | 6.874 ms | 6.730 ms | +2.13% | | Peak memory across 8 GPUs | 1,366,768 MiB | 1,388,112 MiB | -1.54% | | Five-shot GSM8K accuracy | 0.875 (fails `>0.88`) | 0.905 (passes) | -0.030 | The concurrency-32 performance arm reaches at most 28 live requests and replays at padded batch 32, so its throughput delta is not attributed to two-warp grouping. The 128-thread accuracy arm reaches the two-warp band, but the forced-variant trajectory excludes that selector change as the score-miss cause. Cake/FLA stop on configured token `163586` for 197/199 of 200 accuracy responses; the remaining 3/1 responses validly reach the 512-token cap. The Cake accuracy miss remains explicit and is not treated as a passing serving result.

signal.title: Fix Grok-2 nightly: derive image-understanding capability from is_multimodal
signal.text: ## Motivation The `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-grok2` suite has been failing since #32914 merged. `xai-org/grok-2` never finishes startup: ``` [2026-08-05 08:28:43] INFO: 127.0.0.1:56094 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request [2026-08-05 08:28:43] Initialization failed. warmup error: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py", line 2281, in _execute_server_warmup assert res.status_code == 200, f"{res.text}" AssertionError: {"object":"error","message":"Model only supports text input; received unsupported content type 'image_url'.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400} [2026-08-05 08:28:43] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=5123, include_parent=True, pid=5123 ... Exception: Server process exited with code -9. Check server logs for errors. ``` Root cause: `ModelConfig` derives two modality flags from two independent heuristics with no enforced relationship between them. `is_multimodal` is `False` for grok-2. #23383 made that correct on purpose — grok-2's HF config (`model_type="git"`) auto-populates a `vision_config` in `__post_init__`, so the sub-config heuristic is gated behind `model_impl == TRANSFORMERS`. The architecture is `Grok1ForCausalLM`, which is not in `multimodal_model_archs` (only `Grok1VForCausalLM` / `Grok1AForCausalLM` are). `is_image_understandable_model` was missed by that fix and still keyed on the raw `hasattr(hf_config, "vision_config")`, so it is `True` for grok-2. That value reaches `/model_info` as `has_image_understanding`, which the warmup reads back as `is_vlm` and uses to build a `/v1/chat/completions` request carrying an `image_url` part. #32914 then added `_validate_media_content`, which rejects media input based on `is_multimodal`. The server now answers its own warmup request with a 400, the warmup assertion fires, `kill_process_tree` takes the process down, and `popen_launch_server` reports exit `-9`. Before #32914 the same bogus image request was sent, but the non-multimodal path silently dropped the media parts and returned 200, so the wrong flag went unnoticed. `/model_info` has also been advertising a capability grok-2 does not have. ## Modifications Derive `is_image_understandable_model` from `is_multimodal` instead of re-deriving it from `enable_multimodal` plus the `vision_config` attribute: ```diff + # Gated on `is_multimodal` because this flag is advertised via /model_info + # and drives the VLM warmup request, while the OpenAI serving layer rejects + # media input for models that are not `is_multimodal`. A text-only model + # with an auto-populated `vision_config` (see above) would otherwise warm up + # with an image request that its own serving layer answers with 400. # TODO: requires further polishing - self.is_image_understandable_model = enable_multimodal and hasattr( + self.is_image_understandable_model = self.is_multimodal and hasattr( self.hf_config, "vision_config" ) ``` Image understanding is logically a refinement of `is_multimodal` — a model the engine does not run in multimodal mode cannot consume image input. Expressing it as a derivation rather than a parallel heuristic makes the two values unable to diverge by construction, which is why no change is needed in the warmup or in `_validate_media_content`. Scope and risk: - Since `is_multimodal = enable_multimodal and (...)`, `is_multimodal` implies `enable_multimodal`. The new condition is therefore strictly stronger than the old one and can only flip `True` → `False`, never the reverse. - The models that flip are exactly those with a `vision_config` that are neither registered as a multimodal arch nor detected through a sub-config. Those load a text-only model class with no vision tower and no multimodal processor, and `_validate_media_content` rejects images for them, so `has_image_understanding: true` was factually wrong. Real VLMs keep `is_multimodal == True` and a `vision_config`, so their value is unchanged. - `is_image_understandable_model` has exactly two consumers in the SRT engine: the `/model_info` payload (`http_server.py`) and the warmup gate that reads it back from `/model_info`. The identically named symbols under `multimodal_gen/` belong to the separate image-generation runtime and are untouched. This continues the decision already made in #23383 (stop trusting an auto-populated `vision_config` for grok-2) by applying it to the flag that PR missed. Alternatives considered and rejected: relaxing `_validate_media_content` would forward images into a model with no vision encoder, turning a clean 400 into a deeper failure for real users; making the warmup tolerate a 400 would leave `/model_info` advertising a capability the model lacks and would suppress genuine VLM warmup regressions, which is what the warmup exists to catch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32014813022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32014813022)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32014812645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32014812645)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [GDN] Route Qwen TP4 decode and verify rows through Cake
signal.text: ## Summary - lazily load the optional public FlashInfer Cake GDN decode package on SM100/SM103 - fail closed on unsupported dtype, layout, shape, stride, state-pool, or graph-capture combinations - preserve caller-stream and CUDA graph semantics with preallocated workspace/state and cached FP32 dt bias - route the actual Qwen3-Next TP4 BF16 decode and verify rows through the promoted tile16 full-warp kernels ## Qualification - rebased onto current SGLang main b814a7e812fb9367d994af307085bd30de329f96 - B200/SM100, job 3752127 on umbriel-b200-037: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including actual TP4 eager and CUDA Graph paths - GB300/SM103, job 510532 on nvl72d093-T03: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including the same paths - exact route IDs: cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_t1.tile16_fullwarp and cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_verify_t4.tile16_fullwarp - exact TP4 shapes: B=4,T=1,H=4,HV=8 and B=2/3/5/8,T=4,H=4,HV=8; adjacent B=4,T=4 and every unmeasured layout fail closed - same-environment cold-L2 CUPTI kernel A/B versus live FlashInfer 8044d94bf9: - B200 T1 0.003296 vs 0.003472 ms (1.053x), T4 0.006400 vs 0.006944 ms (1.085x), geometric mean 1.069x - GB300 T1 0.003040 vs 0.003296 ms (1.084x), T4 0.006304 vs 0.006736 ms (1.069x), geometric mean 1.076x - correctness uses fixed BF16 atol=rtol=1e-2; dual-arch public ABI/stream/graph and sanitizer gates pass - exact Qwen3-Next 80B FP8 TP4/MTP model replay, four GB300s, job 3137824: 4/4 tests pass; cache-hit KL 0.0007701/0.0017106 versus the fixed 0.0035 ceiling; all four TP ranks record the Cake T4 route during CUDA Graph capture - attributed serving ABBA, four GB300s, job 3137849: all eight measured 128-request rounds complete; four-round median output/total throughput 1.000280x, mean/median TPOT 1.003214x/1.005037x, and mean TTFT 0.987693x versus FlashInfer (the ~1.25% TTFT regression is retained explicitly) Current-head real-model evidence is recorded below. Review and merge are intentionally deferred in this evidence-only phase. ## Current-head decision evidence This replay uses FlashInfer #4581 head `4215a24cb` and supersedes the earlier `45b60f98` jobs/comment. Review and merge are intentionally deferred. ### Environment and attribution - real Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 weights, revision `c5f5f263bdd5cc134092897864e8905d8fe7b928` - four NVIDIA GB300 CC 10.3 GPUs on healthy replacement nodes; SGLang `ee8378ad4`, Torch `2.13.0a0+nv26.07`, CUDA 13.3 - `sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1+cu130`, `sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post3`, `apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11` - source-matched FlashInfer JIT in both arms; the released image AOT package is removed equally. Candidate phases route all four TP ranks through Cake; baseline phases route none ### Accuracy and model behavior Both arm orders run the full 1,319-row GSM8K file with five fixed exemplars, so 1,314 answers are scored, plus decode/prefill cache-hit KL and prefix-cache branching: | Job / order | FlashInfer | Cake | Paired delta | FlashInfer KL | Cake KL | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---| | `516222`, baseline → Cake | 1256/1314 (0.955860) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -8 / -0.608828 pp | 0.00136385 / 0.00157485 | 0.00134804 / 0.00159145 | | `516345`, Cake → baseline | 1249/1314 (0.950533) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -1 / -0.076104 pp | 0.00078810 / 0.00255420 | 0.00073162 / 0.00252816 | All four tests pass in every arm, all scores exceed the fixed `0.93` gate, and every KL value is below `0.0035`. Cake's exact score reproduces across node and order, but exact no-drop is false. The baseline itself varies by seven answers, so the first paired eight-answer delta cannot be assigned wholly to Cake. ### Uninstrumented E2E A/B Job `516223` uses baseline/Cake/Cake/baseline order, counterbalanced workload order, eight rounds per arm/workload, and 20,000 deterministic round-bootstrap resamples. Every request completes. | Workload | Metric | FlashInfer | Cake | Speedup (95% CI) | Decision | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | 128 prompts, 512 in / 256 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1231.754012 tok/s | 1237.596662 tok/s | 1.004743x [0.998292, 1.020776] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 839.608126 ms | 832.389779 ms | 1.008672x [0.999705, 1.020929] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 6.216159 ms | 6.113625 ms | 1.016771x [1.001588, 1.026764] | speedup | | 64 prompts, 128 in / 1024 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1403.321505 tok/s | 1412.172752 tok/s | 1.006307x [0.994657, 1.042125] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 2834.498442 ms | 2840.753832 ms | 0.997798x [0.986704, 1.034864] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 5.561249 ms | 5.532944 ms | 1.005116x [0.993362, 1.016897] | indistinguishable | Dynamic B2/B3/B5 coverage removes the former statistically resolved decode-heavy throughput regression. Balanced mean TPOT has a resolved gain, and both aggregate-throughput point estimates are positive, but both throughput confidence intervals cross 1.0. Therefore this head passes the fixed model correctness gates but does not establish exact GSM8K no-drop or a general statistically resolved E2E throughput speedup. ## Dependencies - FlashInfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4581 Supersedes #35328 because repository rules prohibit force-pushing its protected head branch after rebase. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32210997206](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210997206)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32210997060](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210997060)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode. - [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration. - [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure. - [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code. - [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters. --- ## Summary Under a long-prefill workload with: - DeepSeek-V4-Pro - TP=8 - DP=8 - DP Attention enabled - chunked prefill enabled - PrefillDelayer enabled - one 8-GPU node an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes: ### Healthy synchronized state - Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s - DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep - `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait` - average running requests is ~8.5 ### Pathological LOW state - Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s - within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks - the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk - `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay` - average running requests collapses to ~0.15 - residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s. Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency: - throughput: ~48–68k tok/s - avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9 - residual batches: ~11–14% Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress. The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898. --- ## Environment ```text SGLang version : 0.5.14 commit : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb git log -1 : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246) git describe : v0.5.14 remote : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git local patches : no tracked-file modifications ``` The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree. Hardware / topology: ```text 1 node 8 × NVIDIA B30Z TP = 8 DP = 8 DP Attention = enabled MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE ``` Relevant server configuration: ```bash --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --chunked-prefill-size 131072 ``` With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is: ```text 131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens ``` Relevant MegaMoE cap: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512 ``` Workload: ```text input length : 60000 output length : 1 max concurrency : 16 num prompts : 160 ignore_eos : true seed : 1 ``` The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as: ```text 16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder ``` The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline. --- ## Reproduction behavior Representative post-reboot runs: | Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% | | LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% | | LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% | | good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% | | mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% | | LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% | The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise. A host reboot did not eliminate the problem. --- ## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence Using the per-rank counter: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"} ``` I computed: ```text progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) ``` Results: | Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k | | LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k | | LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 | The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately: ```text 16384 tokens ``` which is exactly one effective prefill chunk. `realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution. ### Metric-cadence validation I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk. Across all ranks: ```text jump interval p50 = 1.397 s jump interval p95 = 1.535 s min interval = 0.401 s ``` Jump-size distribution: ```text 16384 ×112 (one full chunk) 11264 ×8 (tail chunks) 256 ×3 (small startup fragments) 32768 ×0 (no two-chunk merge observed) ``` Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run. --- ## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload. | Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% | | mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% | | LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% | The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run: ```text 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 ``` All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s. Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state. Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch. --- ## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs From: ```text sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total ``` healthy runs eventually converge to sustained: ```text input_estimation="all" output_reason="no_wait" ``` while LOW runs remain dominated by: ```text input_estimation="mixed" output_reason="delay" ``` In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state. In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime. I use: ```text all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay) ``` only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode. The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model. --- ## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled. | Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s | | 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s | | 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s | | 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s | | 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s | | 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s | Mean throughput: ```text 58,980 tok/s CV = 12.88% ``` The important mechanism difference is: ```text PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5 PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15 PrefillDelayer OFF : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9 ``` Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime. This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above. --- ## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to: ```text 2 requests/s, fixed interval ``` while keeping concurrency=16. This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful. Representative results: ```text burst: 94,630 tok/s ramp : 53,449 tok/s burst: 64,016 tok/s ramp : LOW again ``` The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state. This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase. Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration. --- ## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes. ### 1. #29898 — missing locally The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch: ```python prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0 if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1: ... output_reason="delay" else: ... output_reason="wait_timeout" ``` but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true: ```python if slot_condition or queue_condition: ... next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count() return _NegotiateOutput( output_allow=False, output_reason="delay", ... ) ``` with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound. This confirms that the local tree predates #29898. However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`. Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse. --- ### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths: ```text add_one_req_ignore_eos() -> negotiation after budget/admission checks add_one_req() -> negotiation at the beginning of the function ``` The dispatch condition is: ```python if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True): return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req) ``` This reproduction has: ```text ignore_eos = true radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false ``` so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`. In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with: ```python if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and ( not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill( local_prefillable=True, running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(), max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs, max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests, waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len, ) ): return AddReqResult.OTHER ``` before later request / chunk / admission checks. Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics. This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal. That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger. --- ### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present The local scheduler already contains an early guard: ```python if ( self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0 and self.chunked_req is None ... ): ``` but the later waiting-queue loop still contains: ```python if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs): self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True ``` while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses: ```python min( pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs, req_to_token_pool.available_size(), ) ``` where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`. This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295. I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor. --- ### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization. With the current settings: ```text disable_overlap_schedule = false SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false ``` PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path. Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround. If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further. --- ### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills. The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match. It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior. --- ## Current interpretation The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence: ```text formal workload begins ↓ DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts ↓ within the first few seconds, per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount ↓ PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states ↓ mixed/delay persists ↓ under-filled / residual batches increase ↓ running concurrency collapses ↓ LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining ``` One causal distinction is still unresolved: ### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer: ```text same/similar forward opportunity ↓ one rank completes later ↓ prefill progress diverges ↓ Delayer subsequently observes mixed ``` ### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities: ```text scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges ↓ Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions ↓ those ranks do less forward work ↓ prefill progress diverges ``` I am instrumenting: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"} ``` together with: ```text sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category} ``` using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`. The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state. The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between: ```text Δprefill_progress and Δcompleted_forward_execution_time ``` over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence. Roughly: ```text ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower → rank likely completed less forward work → supports scheduler/readiness-side cause ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher → rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress → supports execution-duration-side cause ``` This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above. --- ## Why I think this deserves a separate issue I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together: ```text DP Attention + PrefillDelayer + chunked long-prefill workload + same deterministic configuration + healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state + LOW dominated by mixed/delay + avg running collapsing near zero + rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk + request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction ``` #29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug. The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode. --- ## Questions for maintainers 1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer? 2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks? 3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state? 4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`? 5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing? --- ## Additional data available I retained: - per-run server logs - per-rank Prefill batch logs - `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces - 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures - per-rank `realtime_tokens_total` - PrefillDelayer outcome counters - queue/running-request counters - host/GPU telemetry - good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

signal.title: [AMD][Fix] Route MoRI through the Qwen MoE all-to-all path
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving **Qwen3.5 MoE** (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` on MI355X/ROCm (DP=1 / TP=2, EP=2) produced near-zero accuracy — gsm8k **0.006**. The Qwen2/Qwen3 MoE gates key on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`, which recognises **only** pure DeepEP. MoRI is a DeepEP-class backend and needs the same per-rank EP expert layout, so under MoRI the block silently fell through to the plain-TP path: - the shared expert stayed sharded by TP=2, so each token computed only one shared-expert shard and lost the other half of the contribution; - `can_fuse_shared_expert` still allowed the fusion, placing the shared expert in a **global** slot that the per-rank EP layers never allocate; - the block never entered `_forward_deepep()`, so the routed experts never went through the MoRI dispatch/combine at all. The corrupted first token then poisons everything generated after it. This PR is the correctness follow-up to #31793 (which only disabled the global-slot shared-expert fusion to get MoRI past the init crash). ## Modifications Add `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()` alongside the existing `is_deepep()` at the four gates in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`: `can_fuse_shared_expert` (`:153`), the shared-expert TP override (`:328`), the EP layout branch (`:347`), and the forward dispatch (`:563`). MoRI now uses the correct per-rank EP expert layout, replicates the shared expert per rank (`tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`), enters `_forward_deepep()`, and each token receives the full shared-expert output. The remaining DeepEP-class backends (Mooncake, PPLX) are deliberately **not** included — they have no Qwen MoE coverage to validate against, so `is_mori()` keeps the change byte-identical to `main` for the CUDA-side backends this PR does not exercise. A CPU unit test in `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` pins that `can_fuse_shared_expert` refuses for both `deepep` and `mori`, and still fuses on plain TP. ## Two earlier changes have been removed from this PR On-hardware re-validation no longer shows either of the two bugs they targeted. ### Decode CUDA graph disable (`server_args.py`) — removed MoRI normal mode **is** CUDA-graph safe, as @Duyi-Wang said. `mori_cpp.build_args` returns an args struct whose values (input/indices pointers, `curRankNumToken`, and the preallocated shmem buffer pointers) are snapshotted per graph node by `hipModuleLaunchKernel`, and every comm buffer has fixed capacity and a stable address. The earlier "serial gsm8k 1.000 eager → 0.000 graph" reading was a misattribution of the routing bug above. With the routing gates reverted, gsm8k is **0.000 in both eager and graph** — no code state produces the eager/graph split that motivated the guard: | routing gates | decode CUDA graph | gsm8k (40q serial) | |---|---|---| | broken (`is_deepep()` only) | on | 0.000 (invalid 0.625) | | broken (`is_deepep()` only) | **off (eager)** | **0.000** (invalid 0.600) | | fixed (this PR) | on | 0.967 (60q) | The clincher: the eager number this PR originally reported (**0.935** @ parallel 200) matches the graph number measured now (**0.932** @ parallel 200) — at 2.2x the throughput. If graph replay were misrouting experts, accuracy would collapse, not match to three decimals. Disabling the decode graph also costs spec-decode acceptance, which is what regressed `test/registered/amd/test_moriep_small.py::TestMTP::test_gsm8k` (2.51 against a 2.8 bar; passes on `main` at 3.0077). Reproduced independently on Qwen3.5 with EAGLE MTP — same server, only the graph flag differs: | decode CUDA graph | accept length | |---|---| | on | **3.47 – 3.59** | | off | 2.59 – 2.91 | ### AITER eager-metadata buffer capacity (`aiter_backend.py`) — removed The `Target sizes: [111] / Tensor sizes: [112]` crash no longer reproduces, and the sizing change did not fix the remaining high-concurrency fault: with it applied, Qwen3.5 + MTP at 64 running requests still dies with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N`, and it does so exactly when the log shows `mamba usage: 1.00` — linear-attention state pool exhaustion, not `kv_indptr` overflow. That is a separate bug and is tracked outside this PR. ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, 2x MI355X, TP2 / EP2, `--moe-a2a-backend mori` (deepep_mode normal), aiter attention, fp8 KV cache, decode CUDA graph **on**: | Questions | Parallel | Accuracy | |---|---|---| | — | — | 0.006 (before fix) | | 60 | 30 | 0.967 | | 400 | 64 | 0.925 | | 1000 | 200 | **0.932** | With EAGLE MTP (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), 200 questions / parallel 30: accuracy **0.935**, accept length **~3.5**. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GSM8K 1000 questions / parallel 200, same config: **1552.6 tok/s** output throughput (vs 691 tok/s with the decode graph disabled). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32085415106](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085415106)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32085414973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085414973)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(sgl-kernel): route below-SM90 GPUs to sm90 build in load_utils
signal.text: ## Problem `_load_architecture_specific_ops()` routes only `compute_capability == 90` to the `sm90/` directory; every other GPU falls into the `sm100/` branch. However, the sm90 artifact is the compatibility build: `ENABLE_BELOW_SM90` (default ON on x86_64) appends `compute_80`/`compute_89` gencode (and `compute_87` on aarch64) to the shared `SGL_KERNEL_CUDA_FLAGS` used by `common_ops_sm90_build` (see `python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt`). Below-SM90 GPUs (sm_80/86/87/89, e.g. L40S / RTX 4090) are therefore sent to the wrong directory and fail to `import sgl_kernel` whenever the sm100 artifact does not carry below-SM90 gencode — reproduced on an sm_89 GPU with CUDA 12.1 and sglang-kernel 0.4.5, where import failed until cc=89 was routed to the sm90 directory. This currently happens to work on recent x86_64 wheels only because both builds share the same flags and the sm100 artifact incidentally contains sm_89 cubins; any divergence of the two builds' flag sets (or a wheel built with `ENABLE_BELOW_SM90=OFF`) breaks below-SM90 users immediately. ## Fix Route every GPU with `compute_capability < 100` to the sm90 build. cc >= 100 and the no-GPU path are unchanged. `variant_name` now reports the actual cc instead of hardcoding "SM90". Note: sm_89 is **not** a subset of sm_90 (Ada 8.x vs Hopper 9.x) — this works because the sm90 artifact is compiled with below-SM90 gencode, not because sm90 cubins run on sm89. ## Test - `python -m py_compile` passes. - Verified on an sm_89 GPU: `import sgl_kernel` succeeds with cc=89 routed to the sm90 directory. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32255261048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255261048)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32255260792](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255260792)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] MXFP4 MoE on gfx942 through aiter's Triton kernels
signal.text: ## Motivation MXFP4 MoE cannot run on CDNA3, which is what Kimi-K3 needs. `aiter.fused_moe` has no gfx942 a4w4 path and dies in the activation quantiser with `fused_dynamic_mx_quant_moe_sort_hip: not support output type: fp4x2` — the `fp4x2` branch in `csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu` is behind `#if defined(__Float4_e2m1fn_x2)`, which is not defined on CDNA3, and `hsa/gfx942/f4gemm/*.csv` is empty. There is no non-aiter escape either: the generic Triton MoE runner (`moe_runner/triton.py`, what `MoeRunnerBackend.TRITON` selects when `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is unset) has no MXFP4 support at all. So on gfx942 MXFP4 MoE either aborts or has no path. ## Modifications `moe_runner/aiter_mxfp4_triton.py` routes gfx942 MXFP4 MoE through aiter's *Triton* MXFP4 GEMMs, which lower `tl.dot_scaled` onto the bf16 MFMA CDNA3 has always had. `moe_runner/mxfp4_situ_fused.py` adds a SiTU variant of aiter's fused gated epilogue so the routed experts keep their activation fused into the GEMM; `ACT_SITU=False` is the upstream SwiGLU epilogue unchanged. **No patched aiter is required.** `arch_info.is_fp4_avail()` still excludes gfx942, but it is asserted only in aiter's GEMM entry points, never in `fused_moe_mxfp4`, and it was never a capability probe. The one thing a stock aiter lacks is a tile config — there is no `configs/moe/gfx942-MOE-MX_FP4.json`, and the fallback is a 256x256x64 tile sized for CDNA4's 160 KB LDS that does not compile against CDNA3's 64 KB. `_moe_config()` carries the gfx942 table and defers to aiter's the moment aiter ships one. Everything here is behind `use_triton_mxfp4_moe()`, which is False on every arch but gfx942 and on any build where the Triton kernels do not import, so no other MoE path changes. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/moe/test_aiter_mxfp4_triton_moe.py` checks both new kernels against an fp32 reference that dequantizes the same MXFP4 bytes and runs the MoE in plain torch: | case | coverage | | --- | --- | | both epilogues | SwiGLU (upstream) and SiTU (Kimi-K3), incl. the tanh soft-clips | | both routed-weight placements | `apply_router_weight_on_input` on/off | | expert parallelism | `num_global = 2 x local`; the dropped `-1` rows are what make the fused reduce's masked load load-bearing | | tile shapes | 1 / 16 / 512 tokens — either side of the small/medium config boundary | | gate | `SGLANG_AITER_MXFP4_TRITON` override, no GPU needed | | activation | rel L2 vs fp32 reference | | --- | --- | | SiTU | 2.5e-3 – 2.8e-3 | | SwiGLU | 3.8e-3 – 4.2e-3 | | EP rank 1 (half the experts dropped) | 2.5e-3 | | router weight on input | 2.9e-3 | Tolerance is 1e-2 — the bf16 floor, since the fp4 weights are exact on both sides. 6 tests / 7 subtests green on gfx942 against a stock aiter. Registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (isort / black 26.1.0 / ruff `F401,F821,UP037`) - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32255063349](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255063349)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32255062985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32255062985)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
