signal.title: [AMD] perf: fuse Kimi-K2.5 MLA projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation During Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 graph decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed MLA key projection, rotary embedding, and KV-cache write are launched separately on the latency-critical path even though they share operands. Fusing these operations reduces decode launch overhead and improves long-context serving performance. ## Modifications - Fuse the absorbed MXFP4 `w_kc` projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write into one AITER grid using `fused_fp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`. - Add `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE`, enabled by default. - Restrict the fast path to ROCm gfx95/AITER graph decode with MXFP4 `w_kc`. - Validate the fused kernel's shape requirements before dispatch: - `kv_lora_rank` must be a power of two. - `qk_rope_head_dim` must be a power of two and at least 2. - `qk_nope_head_dim` must be a power of two between 32 and 256. - Retain the existing split path for unsupported configurations, including DSA, DCP, optimized LoRA execution, and active `kv_b_proj` LoRAs. - Carry the fusion decision from `forward_absorb_prepare` to `forward_absorb_core` through `RocmMlaProjectionFusionPlan`. - Add CPU unit coverage for backend, graph-decode, and kernel-shape gating. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests Hardware and model: - 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) - Model: `Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4` - TP=4 - AITER prefill and decode attention - AITER MoE and all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache - Full GSM8K test set: 1,319 questions, 8-shot, maximum 512 new tokens - Project accuracy threshold: 0.92 | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Status | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | Fusion disabled | 0.925 | 0.000 | PASS | | Fusion enabled | 0.930 | 0.000 | PASS | The fused path preserved accuracy and remained above the existing 0.92 threshold. Focused unit tests: ```text 2 passed, 5 subtests passed ``` The tests cover the AITER graph-decode gate and reject unsupported non-power-of-two or out-of-range shapes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The A/B benchmark follows the Kimi-K2.5 ROCm recipe. Configuration: - 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) - Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4, TP=4 - AITER prefill/decode attention and MoE - AITER all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 16 - Breakable prefill graph and full decode graph - Maximum concurrency: 4 - ISL: 8,192 - OSL: 1,024 - 20 measured requests after warmup - Identical seed and generated workload for both arms - The only A/B feature change was `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE=0/1` | Metric | Fusion disabled | Fusion enabled | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Output throughput | 428.77 tok/s | 433.33 tok/s | +1.06% | | Total token throughput | 3,861.04 tok/s | 3,902.11 tok/s | +1.06% | | Median TPOT | 8.81 ms | 8.68 ms | -1.48% | | Median end-to-end latency | 8,455.36 ms | 8,328.59 ms | -1.50% | | Median TTFT | 246.43 ms | 247.99 ms | +0.63% | The fusion improves decode-sensitive throughput, TPOT, and end-to-end latency for the 8k/1k workload. The small TTFT variation is expected because this optimization targets graph decode rather than prefill. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: route decode wo_a bf16 batched matmul to aiter batched_gemm_bf16
signal.text: # [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: route decode wo_a bf16 batched matmul to aiter `batched_gemm_bf16` ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm decode path, the MLA output-absorb (`wo_a`) bf16 GEMM runs `torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", o, wo_a)`, which dispatches to a **rocBLAS/Tensile `Cijk_*` batched GEMM** — one of the larger kernels in the DSV4 decode attention region. aiter ships a tuned `batched_gemm_bf16` for exactly this shape, and the reference ATOM stack uses it for the same op. This PR routes the einsum to `batched_gemm_bf16` on gfx95, behind a new opt-in env flag, with an einsum fallback. **What this change is:** a 1:1 kernel replacement that aligns the sglang decode `wo_a` op with the kernel the reference stack uses. The trace confirms the replacement; in raw GPU time the aiter kernel is **at parity** with the Tensile kernel (see Validation). End-to-end this shows a **marginal (~2-3% total tok/s)** effect in repeated pure-TP runs — this is an ATOM-alignment / kernel-parity change, **not** a large throughput win. ## Motivation Attributing the DSV4 decode attention region kernel-by-kernel (torch-profiler External-id + enclosing python stack) shows the `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_*_MT16x16x1024` Tensile kernel is launched by `aten::bmm` from the `wo_a` bf16 einsum. The same logical op in the reference stack is aiter's `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel`. Routing sglang to that kernel matches the reference kernel choice for this op. ## What changed - `deepseek_v4.py`: new module helper `_apply_wo_a_bf16_matmul(o, wo_a, is_decode)`. Eligibility (opt-in flag `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM`, the global `SGLANG_USE_AITER` switch, HIP, and gfx95) is folded into `_wo_a_aiter_gemm_eligible(...)` and evaluated **once at module import** into `_wo_a_aiter_batched_gemm_enabled`; the aiter kernel is **pre-imported** into `_wo_a_batched_gemm_bf16` at import as well. This keeps the per-token decode critical path free of `EnvBool.get()` and function-local imports. - On the decode path, when enabled and not runtime-disabled, it calls aiter `batched_gemm_bf16` (`Y[i] = X[i] @ W[i]^T`): `XQ = o.transpose(0,1)` `[G,T,D]`, `WQ = wo_a` `[G,R,D]` -> `[G,T,R]` -> transpose back to `[T,G,R]`. Otherwise (prefill, any gate off, or after a failure) it uses the einsum. The `wo_a` else-branch calls this helper, passing `forward_batch.forward_mode.is_decode()`. - Restricted to **decode** — the kernel was benchmarked/validated for decode; prefill keeps the einsum. - Gated on the global `SGLANG_USE_AITER` switch, so the reroute cannot activate when aiter is disabled even if the opt-in flag is set. - **Two-stage fallback** — an import failure disables the reroute at module load (logged once); a kernel that imports but raises at runtime flips a process-global and falls back to the einsum for the rest of the process (logged once), instead of retrying/re-logging on every layer/token. - `environ.py`: new `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM = EnvBool(False)`. No behavior change unless the flag is set. CUDA, non-gfx95, and prefill paths are untouched. ## Validation (MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8) **Numerics** — model-free bit-check of `batched_gemm_bf16` vs the einsum across `T/G/D/R` shapes: max relative error <= 5e-4 (bf16 rounding; mostly exactly 0.0). The unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_wo_a_bf16.py` (registered on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) exercises the aiter kernel on-device and covers static eligibility, dispatch/prefill gating, the runtime-failure fallback, and the numerics check. **Accuracy** — 5-shot GSM8K, 1319 questions, `--parallel 1319`, cuda-graph on: einsum (flag off) 0.952 / aiter (flag on) 0.946 — same 0.946-0.952 fp4-MoE run-to-run band, no regression. **Coherence** — server generates correctly with the flag on (`capital of France is` -> "Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin."). **Kernel swap (trace-confirmed, same scope)** — total GPU time for all launches of the kernel in the profiled decode window, flag off vs on: - off: `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_*_MT16x16x1024` 2.04 ms x244 - on: `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel_*` 2.07 ms x244 (aiter); `Cijk` drops 248->4 launches So the kernel is replaced 1:1 (~8.4 us vs ~8.5 us per launch) — the aiter kernel is at **parity** in raw GPU time, marginally higher, within noise. The trace demonstrates *kernel replacement*, not a kernel-time reduction. **Profiling** Before After **Throughput** (DSV4-Pro fp4, MI355X, TP8, **pure-TP eager**, `random` ISL 512 / OSL 1024, N=4 reps/point, fixed seed; flag off (einsum) vs on (aiter)): Output tok/s (mean / p50 / pop-std): | conc | off (mean / p50 / std) | on (mean / p50 / std) | d mean | d p50 | |------|------------------------|-----------------------|--------|-------| | 4 | 36.0 / 36.0 / 0.00 | 36.0 / 36.0 / 0.00 | +0.00% | +0.00% | | 32 | 288.0 / 288.0 / 0.00 | 294.0 / 288.0 / 10.39 | +2.08% | +0.00% | | 64 | 576.0 / 576.0 / 0.00 | 576.0 / 576.0 / 0.00 | +0.00% | +0.00% | Total tok/s (mean / p50) — output tok/s is quantized to fixed steps in this harness and hides sub-step movement: | conc | off (mean / p50) | on (mean / p50) | d mean | d p50 | |------|------------------|-----------------|--------|-------| | 4 | 52.0 / 52.0 | 53.3 / 53.3 | +2.53% | +2.48% | | 32 | 416.7 / 417.0 | 425.5 / 426.0 | +2.12% | +2.16% | | 64 | 817.2 / 817.5 | 842.8 / 842.8 | +3.13% | +3.10% | Reading: on the quantized output-tok/s metric the off/on bands overlap at every concurrency (the lone conc=32 outlier is +2.08% mean but d p50 = 0 with std 10.4 — within run-to-run variance). On total tok/s there is a consistent, small **+2-3%**. Under DP-attention / high concurrency it is expected to be ~neutral (comm-bound). Honest framing: kernel-parity / ATOM-alignment change with a marginal (~2-3%) end-to-end effect, not a confirmed output-tok/s win. **DeepSeek-V4-Pro GPTQ** — not available in this environment, so not tested (documented as an environment limitation). The reroute is dtype-agnostic for correctness: `wo_a` is a bf16 batched matmul (`o` and `wo_a` are bf16 regardless of the MoE quant scheme), so the einsum-vs-aiter swap is numerically identical across fp4/GPTQ; the fp4 GSM8K accuracy plus the model-free bit-check cover the numerical contract. ## How to enable ``` SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 ``` Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on gfx95 (MI355X). Applies to the decode path only. ## Checklist - [x] Numerically validated (bf16-equivalent vs einsum; on-device unit test) - [x] Coherent end-to-end on MI355X TP8 - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved - [x] Opt-in (default off); CUDA / non-gfx95 / prefill unchanged - [x] Flag + kernel cached at module import (no per-token `EnvBool.get()` / import) - [x] Repeated-run A/B (mean / p50 / std), reframed as kernel-parity + marginal effect --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #32097452107](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32097452107) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32097451926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32097451926)

signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4 MI355X: eliminate bpreshuffle fp8-scale relayout copy in dense w8a8 linear
signal.text: ## Summary On MI355X (gfx950) the CK bpreshuffle w8a8 blockscale GEMM consumes the per-group activation scale in **column-major** `[num_groups, tokens]` layout. `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` quantizes the activation row-major and then relays the scale out with `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` = `.t().contiguous().t()` — a real relayout **copy per dense w8a8 GEMM** (the MLA q/kv/o projections and MoE), one of the larger ELEWISE deltas in the DeepSeek-V4 MI355X decode breakdown. `aiter_per1x128_quant` already supports `transpose_scale=True`, which emits the exact `[num_groups, tokens]` byte-order directly. This PR asks for that and reinterprets the strides with a zero-copy view, removing the copy on the fresh-quant path. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`** — in the fresh-quant branch of `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`, pass `transpose_scale=emit_bpreshuffle_scale` to `aiter_per1x128_quant` and consume the result via the shared `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` helper (the `as_strided((1, M))` metadata repair that landed on main in #31727) instead of `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`. Guarded `M >= 2`; the M==1 single-row case keeps the materialize path, which for a contiguous `[1, G]` input is a **no-op view** anyway (the `[1, G]` and `[G, 1]` byte orders coincide, so `.t().contiguous().t()` shares storage and launches no copy kernel). Bit-identical output; removes one relayout copy on the M>=2 path. The pre-existing Triton row-major-view branch is routed through the same helper too, so the transposed-scale repair lives in one documented place rather than as duplicated inline `as_strided` expressions. ## Tests - **CPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_scale.py`) — the shared-helper stride/no-copy contract, and the `M == 1` materialize fallback: values intact on the natural `(G, 1)` stride (the no-op-view layout, not `(1, 1)`), sharing storage. - **MI35X GPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_dense_linear_mi35x.py`, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) — exercises the **real** kernels: (1) `aiter_per1x128_quant` with `transpose_scale` True vs False, asserting identical quantized bytes, equal scale values, the `(1, M)` stride (M>=2) / `(G, 1)` no-op (M==1), and zero-copy sharing; (2) end-to-end `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` new path vs the original path (forced by patching quant→row-major + relayout→materialize), asserting **bit-identical** GEMM output over M ∈ {1, 2, 8, 16} (M==1 exercises the materialize fallback), and **spying the GEMM dispatch to assert the CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` path is taken (not Triton)** so a future tuned-shape-list change can't silently void the coverage. This is the direct real-path evidence the fabricated-layout CPU test could not provide. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP8. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260731`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch. Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. **Correctness:** GEMM output bit-identical vs the materialize path (`gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, max-abs-diff 0.0). ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 2 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.941 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.947 | Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise); the bit-identical correctness check above is the primary guarantee. ### Perf (random 8k/1k, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, seed 42, num-prompts = conc×10) — preliminary **Single-shot, one run per arm — preliminary, not an established speedup.** The Δ below (≈ 0.9–2.0%) is not yet backed by repeated A/B runs, so I'm presenting it as directional rather than a confirmed win; the trend (larger at lower concurrency, i.e. more launch/latency-bound) is consistent with removing a per-GEMM relayout copy but isn't proven by these numbers alone. The correctness/no-regression guarantee is the **bit-identical GEMM output** check above. Happy to add repeated-run A/B (mean/p50/variance) if a throughput claim is wanted. | conc | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | ΔTPOT | baseline total tok/s | patched total tok/s | Δtot | |-----:|:------------------:|:-----------------:|:-----:|:--------------------:|:-------------------:|:----:| | 16 | 19.48 | 19.10 | −2.0% | 6500.2 | 6613.0 | +1.7% | | 32 | 24.63 | 24.22 | −1.7% | 9685.3 | 9821.3 | +1.4% | | 64 | 35.03 | 34.60 | −1.2% | 12819.0 | 12935.7 | +0.9% | Coherent, zero dropped requests. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32115420885](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32115420885)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32115420264](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32115420264)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(moe): support Llama4 NVFP4 router input weights on SM120
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34192. Llama 4 constructs its MoE layers with `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. For ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120/SM121, SGLang selects the FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner, which previously rejected this configuration during server warmup. For top-1 routing, the required semantics can be implemented exactly by multiplying each token's hidden states by its router weight before activation quantization and passing unit final scales to CUTLASS. This follows the existing pattern in the AITER MoE runner. The fix remains intentionally restricted to top-1 routing. With top-k greater than one, each selected expert would require a differently scaled copy of the input. ## Modifications - Add top-1 router-weight pre-scaling to the common FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE execution path. - Replace the kernel's output-side router scaling with float32 unit `token_final_scales` when pre-scaling is active. - Normalize all `token_final_scales` passed through this CUTLASS path to float32, as required by the binding. - Remove the ModelOpt NVFP4 and FlashInfer CUTLASS assertions that rejected `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. - Preserve explicit rejection for: - top-k greater than one; - activations already quantized before dispatch, including the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 all-gather path. - Add focused CPU unit tests covering: - top-1 activation pre-scaling; - float32 unit final scales; - preservation of expert IDs; - top-k greater than one rejection; - pre-quantized dispatch rejection. The normal `apply_router_weight_on_input=False` path is unchanged apart from enforcing the CUTLASS binding's float32 scale requirement. ## Accuracy Tests Added: ```text test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py ``` The tests compare the transformed hidden states and final scales against the expected top-1 formulation and verify that unsupported configurations fail explicitly. Local validation: ```text python -m py_compile \ python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py \ python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py \ test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py ``` Result: passed. All commit-time pre-commit checks passed, including Python AST validation, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, and registered-test validation. The focused pytest test could not be executed in the local development environment because PyTorch is not installed. No real-checkpoint accuracy test was run for this checkout. The equivalent patch and its SM120/SM121 validation evidence are documented in #34192. That validation used dummy weights for end-to-end liveness, so it is not claimed as a model-accuracy result. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed test or profiling was run for this checkout. The equivalent patch validation documented in #34192 completed both SM120 scenarios without errors and did not show a decode throughput regression. Those results used dummy weights and a separate validated build, so they are included only as prior evidence, not as performance results for this commit. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: [Bug] TypeError in set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs during NEXTN TARGET_VERIFY — mamba_next_track_idx is None (hybrid-mamba + speculative decoding + lazy buffer mode)
signal.text: **Env:** SGLang 0.5.14 (pip wheel) · model: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 · GPU: 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB each) · NEXTN speculative decoding enabled **Crash:** \`TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer\` at \`schedule_batch.py:1594\` in \`set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs()\` during TARGET_VERIFY. **Mechanism (from reading v0.5.14 source):** \`Req.mamba_next_track_idx\` initializes to \`None\` (schedule_batch.py:790) and is only assigned in the extend path — an assignment that lazy buffer mode skips (line ~2325, deferring to \`mamba_lazy_prealloc_at_boundary\` in \`prepare_for_decode\`). NEXTN's TARGET_VERIFY builds the track-index tensor (line 1589+) before any decode step has run for a fresh request, so the tensor build receives \`None\`. **Workaround (running stably on my machine):** for req in batch.reqs: if req.mamba_next_track_idx is None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = 0 placed immediately before the torch.tensor build. Zero is the semantically correct initial ping-pong slot per the field's own comment ("0 or 1"). A maintainer may prefer initializing at the source instead. **Context:** the same architectural class (hybrid-recurrent state index reaching a spec-decode kernel unset/unbounded) has three known instances in vLLM (vllm#43559, vllm#50021) — SGLang fails loudly with this TypeError where vLLM's analogues fault in-kernel. Downstream discussion: noonghunna/club-3090#803.

signal.title: [PD] Deferred decode-side KV release for the NIXL backend
signal.text: ## Motivation #35049 added env-gated **deferred decode-side KV release** — on abort, hold an in-flight request's KV pages/req-slot until the prefill confirms its transfer drained (or a timeout fires), so a still-landing write can't corrupt the next request that reuses those pages. It wired the prefill ack for **mooncake only**. Two reasons NIXL needs it: 1. **There is a latent footgun today.** The decode side is backend-agnostic, so enabling `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` on a NIXL deployment *already* holds pages (`NixlKVManager(CommonKVManager)`, `NixlKVReceiver(CommonKVReceiver)` inherit the abort/tracker machinery). But NIXL never sends `ABORT_ACK` and had no path to receive one, so `is_abort_release_safe` is never satisfied and **every abort waits out the full timeout** — safe (holding is the safe direction), but fully degraded, pinning KV and back-pressuring new requests under abort load. 2. **The hazard is arguably worse than mooncake's.** NIXL transfers are inherently asynchronous — `agent.transfer(handle)` posts and returns, and the worker polls `check_xfer_state(handle)` for `DONE` — so there is always a real in-flight window. Mooncake's *default* path is the synchronous `batch_transfer_sync`. `nixl/conn.py::_handle_abort_notification` even carried a `TODO` for exactly this mechanism. ## Modifications **Shared (`common/conn.py`)** — one ack implementation for both backends: - Hoist `_prefill_unique_rank`, `_send_abort_ack`, `_maybe_ack_drained_abort` and the `_deferred_ack_targets` map from `MooncakeKVManager` to `CommonKVManager`; add `register_deferred_ack_target()` documenting the mark-`Failed`-first ordering. Mooncake behavior is unchanged (now inherited). `CommonKVSender.clear()` already drops held targets, so NIXL gets that cleanup for free. **NIXL (`nixl/conn.py`)**: - `_handle_abort_notification`: parse the return address the decode already sends (`_send_abort_notification` has always included ip/port — NIXL just ignored it), register the held ack **after** the status flip for an active room, and ack a concluded room immediately. It never acks an active room from the bootstrap thread: a chunk dequeued but not yet counted would race the ack. - `transfer_worker`: ack at the skip site (nothing was written for the aborted room) and after the existing `while handles: check_xfer_state == DONE` barrier (writes have landed). NIXL's drain point is actually *cleaner* than mooncake's — no sibling-future hazard. Deliberately **no** ack on the exception path: that barrier bails on the first `ERR`, so sibling handles may still be writing; the room falls back to the decode timeout. **Closing two ack-stranding windows (both backends — both were present in #35049):** Previously the ack was driven only by worker visits, so two sequences left a registered target that nobody ever acked, falling back to the decode timeout (safe, but losing the fast path exactly when you want it): 1. the owning worker could pass its `Failed` skip point *between* the status flip and the target registration (ack attempt a no-op, then the target lands and strands); 2. a room whose enqueued chunks had all drained with no further chunk coming (`is_last_chunk` unseen) is never revisited by the worker at all. The root cause was that `outstanding == 0` was not a quiescence predicate: chunks were counted *after* the `Failed` status check, so a chunk could be dequeued and about to write while the counter still read 0 — which is why the ack could not safely be sent from the bootstrap thread. Now chunks are **counted at dequeue, before the status check**, so a chunk either writes (counted) or skips (uncounted), never both, and `Failed and outstanding == 0` genuinely means nothing can still write. With that predicate the abort path attempts the ack once after registering, covering both windows. Counting slightly earlier is strictly more conservative for the existing `poll()` Success hold and teardown condition (increments/decrements still pair). - Decode: generalize the staging-only ZMQ thread into a decode **listener** that also handles `ABORT_ACK`, started when staging *or* deferred release is enabled. A dedicated thread ingests acks even while the decode is idle — NIXL notifs would **not**, since the decode agent runs with `num_threads=0` and only drains notifs inside a live receiver's `poll()`, which early-returns once `conclude_state` is set on abort. Off by default; when disabled, both backends behave exactly as before. ## Tests New `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`: ack held until outstanding drains, fires at most once, unregistered-room no-op, rank formula matches the Success-sync formula, abort-notification registration (active / concluded / feature-off / legacy 2-frame abort / non-ABORT passthrough), and per-rank ack aggregation. Existing NIXL fixtures that build a manager via `object.__new__` now set `enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = False` (they cover the legacy no-ack behavior). Verified in the `lmsysorg/sglang` container on a CPU VM: ``` test_nixl_deferred_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_nixl_backend_basic Ran 43 tests OK test_deferred_decode_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_decode_queue_cleanup Ran 6 tests OK test_nixl_sender_failure_cleanup Ran 1 test OK test_disaggregation_wire Ran 23 tests OK test_kv_transfer_replica_metric Ran 3 tests OK ``` (The mooncake-side suites are included deliberately: the dequeue-counting change touches shared worker logic.) ## Not covered / follow-ups - **No live NIXL PD run.** The state machine and wiring are unit-tested; an end-to-end abort-mid-transfer run on a real NIXL deployment (and the fast-ack-vs-timeout ratio) is not yet measured. Same gap as #35049's, which validated on mooncake. - Multi-node / TP>1 dummy-rank fan-out unvalidated (the `len(bootstrap_infos)` denominator is dummy-proof by construction, but untested where the real multi-queue concurrency lives). - The mamba/state path (`maybe_send_extra`) is not routed through drain-aware waiting on either backend — carried over from #35049. ## Checklist - [x] Format with pre-commit (black/isort) - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A — abort-path correctness; no kernel/throughput impact, no-op when disabled) - [x] Code style Related: #35049, #32564, #27372 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32218714755](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32218714755)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32218714578](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32218714578)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(cache): deduplicate shared SWA slots before free
signal.text: ## Problem `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` allows several full-cache locations to reference the same sliding-window slot. `free_swa()` expands the full locations and forwards every mapped value to the underlying allocator without deduplication. When a shared slot appears more than once, it is returned to the free pool repeatedly. The available count exceeds the pool capacity and hybrid-model generation aborts at the allocator invariant: ```text assert self.swa_attn_allocator.available_size() <= self.swa_attn_allocator.size ``` This reproduced on 4x MI350X with Inkling-Small LoRA after 32/256 responses. ## Fix Deduplicate the positive mapped SWA indices before calling the non-idempotent child allocator. Mapping entries are still cleared for every full location. ## Validation - [x] Added a focused regression where two full locations share one SWA slot; one free restores exactly the configured capacity. - [x] Full `test_swa_unittest.py`: 12 passed, 15 subtests passed. - [x] Pre-commit passed on both changed files. - [x] 4x MI350X Inkling-Small native LoRA completed two rollouts and four train steps when combined with the Miles ROCm launcher/API fallbacks; Ray job succeeded. - [ ] Maintainer-triggered CUDA CI. - [ ] Maintainer-triggered AMD CI. This remains draft pending owner review and independent CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32237348266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237348266)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32237347959](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237347959)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [XPU] Add diffusion server test config for Intel XPU B60
signal.text: ## Motivation **Let the `multimodal_gen` diffusion server tests run on Intel XPU with correct expectations.** The diffusion server tests compare generated images against committed ground-truth images and check stage timings against committed perf baselines. Both sets of reference values are CUDA-derived, and neither is reachable from XPU today: - `get_consistency_platform()` has no XPU branch, so an XPU run silently falls through to the `h100` thresholds. - `BASELINE_CONFIG` composes per-platform perf overrides for Ascend and MUSA, but there is no XPU entry. The image mismatch is not a correctness bug. XPU seeds its initial latent noise from a different RNG stream than CUDA, so the pixels cannot match bit-for-bit: the image stays semantically identical (CLIP remains high) while `ssim` / `psnr` / `mean_abs_diff` degrade. Comparing XPU output against CUDA thresholds therefore fails on a difference that carries no signal. This PR adds XPU as a first-class platform in both registries, following the existing Ascend and MUSA pattern. ## Modifications Purely additive: 4 files, 56 insertions, 0 deletions. - **`test/test_utils.py`** — register `intel_xpu_b60` in `CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD_FILE_BY_PLATFORM`, add the `intelxpub60` alias, and add the `current_platform.is_xpu()` branch to `get_consistency_platform()`. - **`test/server/consistency_thresholds/intel_xpu_b60.json`** — XPU consistency thresholds for `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` and `fsdp-inference`. - **`test/server/xpu/perf_baselines_xpu.json`** — XPU perf baselines for `fsdp-inference`, measured on Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.71 GiB per card). - **`test/server/testcase_configs.py`** — chain the XPU baseline file into `BASELINE_CONFIG`, alongside the existing Ascend and MUSA `.update()` calls. No CUDA path changes: both new files are read only when the resolved platform is XPU, and the two registry additions are new keys. ## Thresholds | case | clip | ssim | psnr | mean_abs_diff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `fsdp-inference` | 0.97 | 0.6 | 11.0 | 37.0 | | `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` | 0.98 | 0.79 | 15.7 | 17.2 | Only these two cases were measured on XPU hardware. Every other case still inherits from `h100.json`; that is called out in the `_comment` field of the threshold file so the remaining cases can be triaged the same way rather than being assumed correct. ## Dependency Blocked on #33320, which adds `CustomOp.forward_xpu`. `dispatch_forward()` already returns `self.forward_xpu` on XPU, but the base-class method does not exist yet, so any `multimodal_gen` `CustomOp` raises `AttributeError` on XPU before these test configs are reached. This PR is the test-configuration half; #33320 is the runtime half. ## Accuracy Tests Verified on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.7 GiB per card): ``` python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_2_gpu.py::TestDiffusionServerTwoGpu::test_diffusion_generation[fsdp-inference] ``` Model `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo`. Passes end to end in ~157 s, including the consistency check against the thresholds above. Measured CLIP 0.9779 (passes); SSIM 0.6609 / PSNR 12.0434 / mean-abs-diff 33.3489, which fail the H100 thresholds and pass the XPU ones. XPU output is deterministic across 4 runs (identical md5). The perf baselines are single-host measurements, not an averaged multi-run distribution, so they are starting reference values rather than tight regression bounds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — no new test case is introduced; this PR adds the platform configuration that existing diffusion server tests read on XPU. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing behaviour change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). cc: @siju-samuel @rbabukv <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32237906482](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237906482)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32237906272](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237906272)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Perf] Fuse prefill norm/act quantization for NVFP4 W4A4 hybrid models (Qwen3.5 family)
signal.text: > Rebased onto `main` after #34859 merged: the SiLU+FP4-quant base fusion landed with the model support, so this PR is now a single commit with the three remaining fusions (attention-layer SiLU coverage, post-LN+FP4-quant, gated-norm+FP8-quant). ## Motivation For Qwen3.5-family hybrid (GDN + attention) models served with a mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, prefill spends a measurable share of GPU time in standalone norm / activation / quantization glue kernels: every projection input is normalized, written to HBM in bf16, then re-read and quantized by a separate kernel. Kernel-level tracing against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same model showed the GEMM/attention/GDN families at parity while SGLang lost time exclusively in this glue (vLLM fuses norm+quant and act+quant via torch.compile). This PR removes the extra round-trips with three targeted fusions (all bit-equivalent up to FP4/FP8 rounding ties, each with a kill switch): 1. **SiLU+mul + NVFP4 quant** for dense MLPs: replaces `act_and_mul` + the standalone per-block FP4 quantize with FlashInfer's `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` (single-group form), handing `down_proj` a prequantized `(fp4, swizzled_scale)` tuple through the existing `_accepts_prequantized_fp4` path. Enabled for both GDN-layer and attention-layer MLPs. 2. **Post-attention GemmaRMSNorm + NVFP4 quant**: FlashInfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` fuses the residual-add, the norm, and the `gate_up` input quant into one kernel. Gemma's `(1 + w)` scaling is folded into a precomputed weight; the swizzled block-scale is exposed as the 2D `(m_padded, K/16)` view so the cuDNN mm_fp4 backend's shape validation also passes. 3. **GDN gated RMSNorm + static-FP8 quant**: adds an fp8-store epilogue to the `fla` `layernorm_gated` Triton kernel (skips the bf16 intermediate write entirely) and teaches `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` to accept a prequantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple for `out_proj` (explicit opt-in attribute, mirroring the fp4 path). Kill switches: `SGLANG_DISABLE_SILU_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_POST_LN_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GATED_NORM_FP8_QUANT_FUSION=1`. ## Benchmark RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), Qwen3.5-family 27B hybrid GDN model, mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, TP1, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --disable-radix-cache`, flashinfer 0.6.17. Workload: `bench_serving`, random 8192-in / 1024-out, bs=1, 5 prompts, seed 1234, warmup pass then measured pass; both lanes in one session on the same GPU, base commit 5c9ee86d90. ### TTFT (8k prefill) | | main | main + this PR | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | TTFT mean | 674.8 ms | **640.1 ms** | **−34.7 ms (−5.1%)** | | TTFT median | 665.3 ms | **631.3 ms** | **−34.0 ms (−5.1%)** | ### Decode (unchanged, sanity check) | | main | main + this PR | |---|---|---| | output tok/s (bs=1) | 68.7 | 69.1 | | ITL median | 13.92 ms | 13.86 ms | Per-kernel effect at the 8k prefill step (torch profiler, per forward): the standalone `act_and_mul` (~8.6 ms), the gate_up-input `quantize_with_block_size` pass (~6.7 ms), the down-input `cvt_fp16_to_fp4` pass, and the out_proj `static_quant_fp8` launches (128/forward) are removed or absorbed into the producing kernel; the gated-norm epilogue also skips its 100 MB bf16 intermediate write per layer. The fusions auto-enable only when the touched projections use the matching ModelOpt linear method (NVFP4 W4A4 for 1–2, per-tensor static FP8 for 3), so other checkpoints and quant modes keep their current control flow. ### Accuracy GSM8K via `sglang.test.run_eval` (full test set, 1319 examples, same server flags as above): | | score | |---|---| | fusions **off** (all kill switches set) | 0.9635 | | fusions **on** (this PR default) | 0.9658 | Also verified layer-count wiring at startup (64/64 layers log each fusion) and bit-exact residual propagation (fused kernels update the residual identically to `fused_add_rmsnorm`). ### Data provenance The RTX PRO 6000 tables above were measured with **all three fusions of this PR** applied directly on `main` @ 5c9ee86d90 (commit a452f1ef8c, fusion content byte-equivalent to this branch's net diff), before stacking on #34859. The full stacked branch (#34859 + conflict resolution + these fusions, i.e. this PR's head) was additionally validated end-to-end on an H200 with the FP8 checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, dynamic activation), where these fusions by design stay inactive (`fused_lines=0` in server logs) — confirming zero intrusion on non-W4A4 deployments: **H200, full stacked branch vs `main` @ 8922bb98e2, 4096-in/1024-out, seed 1234, same GPU back-to-back** | bs | main (tok/s) | stacked (tok/s) | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 95.9 | 95.8 | ±0 | | 8 | 607.1 | 623.0 | +2.6% | | 16 | 988.3 | 1013.4 | +2.5% | | 64 | 1468.5 | 1486.6 | +1.2% | (gains here come from #34859's model-side changes; this PR's fusions are inactive on FP8-dynamic) | accuracy | main | stacked | |---|---|---| | GSM8K (1319) | 0.9665 | 0.9642 | | AIME25 (30) | 25/30 | 25/30 | A matching bs-sweep + GSM8K + AIME25 matrix for the NVFP4 checkpoint on SM120 is queued (blocked on machine availability) and will be posted in a comment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32237563518](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237563518)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32237563270](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32237563270)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Overlap prefill DP-rank bootstrap queries
signal.text: ## Motivation Decode admission synchronously queried the prefill bootstrap server for DP-rank routing at the result-consumption point. This HTTP round trip was on the scheduler critical path even though pending bootstrap rooms were already known before request intake and while the previous decode graph could still be in flight. This change is functionally independent of #35070 and is based directly on upstream `main`. For production validation, it was tested with #35070 enabled; the performance numbers below are the additional increment over that PREBUILT-enabled baseline, not a code dependency on #35070. ## Modifications - Submit the authoritative batched prefill DP-rank query through the existing KV-manager executor once, at the top of each decode scheduler iteration before request intake. - Consume the future at the original resolution point, preserving same-cycle receiver initialization and bootstrap-server routing authority. - Preserve FIFO behavior and the existing synchronous retry/error fallback. - Cancel owned futures during queue cleanup. - Add one focused case to the existing decode queue cleanup test. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.995** | | Mean speculative acceptance length | 4.519494 | | Acceptance rate | 0.704089 | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | The evaluation used natural model output; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. Removing the redundant second prefetch does not change the authoritative result-consumption, retry, or receiver-initialization path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. The clean PREBUILT A/B uses each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. Output TPS/User is `output_sequence_length / full_decode_duration`, with exact request-shape matching. | Metric | PREBUILT baseline | Top-only prefetch | Additional change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape Output TPS/User | 83.560918 | 84.695096 | **+1.357308%** | Both jobs completed successfully with zero request errors, zero retractions, and no CUDA-graph fallback. The exact-shape comparison contains 7,870 common shapes and 8,088 matched requests. Instrumentation showed that the upper prefetch had a mean `17.35 ms` lead, was ready at the consume point in `69.8%` of observations, and reduced residual synchronous wait from `1.140 ms` to `0.265 ms`. The removed lower call had only about `0.8 ms` of lead and mostly observed futures already submitted by the upper call, so keeping it added control-flow complexity without preserving additional measured throughput. Targeted production-container unit coverage passed before the production A/B. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: [Bug] Ranks sharing one `ssd_offload_path` collide on Mooncake bucket files → L3 cache broken
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug **Summary.** `MooncakeStore` passes one `ssd_offload_path` to every rank's embedded Mooncake client, but Mooncake's `LOCAL_DISK` (bucket) tier assumes **one client per directory**. A shared directory silently corrupts KV data and makes cross-restart recovery ambiguous. A fix already exists in #31926, but it has no tracking issue and its CI is blocked on the `run-ci` label — this issue is the tracking issue + rationale. **Environment.** SGLang `main`; Mooncake `main`; DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MLA), TP8, HiCache L3 → Mooncake bucket backend. **Root cause** (Mooncake `mooncake-store/src/storage_backend.cpp`): - bucket id = `(time_gen() << 12) | 0`, seeded once at construction (`time_gen()` is whole-second), then plain `fetch_add` — time is never re-read. - filename = `<storage_path>/<bucket_id>.bucket` — no rank/client component; opened `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, no `O_EXCL`. - Two ranks constructed in the same second → identical id sequences → identical filenames → the second `O_TRUNC` silently truncates the first → later reads return wrong KV bytes, no error. - With dp-attention, `tp_rank` is attention-group-local (0 on every DP rank when `attn_tp_size==1`), so `tp_rank` alone collapses ranks onto one dir — `dp_rank` is required. **Impact.** - Silent KV corruption in any shared-path multi-rank deploy. Production repro in #31926: 8 clients, same second, mutual truncation within minutes. - On restart, each rank's Mooncake `Init()` adopts the whole directory (no owner tag), so all ranks re-register all keys; the master keeps an arbitrary first-claim → dangling references when one rank later evicts a shared file. **Fix + coupling.** - #31926 gives each rank `ssd_offload_path/rank_{dp}_{tp}_{pp}/` (unchanged when `storage_config is None`) and adds `dp_rank` to `HiCacheStorageConfig`. Its CI is red only because the `run-ci` gate exits before any test runs. - The per-rank layout is also the precondition for Mooncake's per-directory recovery/ownership model — its restart re-adoption binds identity to a per-`storage_path` marker (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2306) — so the SGLang and Mooncake sides should land jointly. **Ask.** 1. Apply the CI label so #31926 (or equivalent per-rank namespacing) can be tested and merged. 2. Confirm one-storage-location-per-client as the supported model, make the per-rank path the HiCache+Mooncake default, and document it. ### Reproduction See #31926 ### Environment See #31926

signal.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signal.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signal.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signal.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32236976842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32236976842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32236976735](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32236976735)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] /v1/responses endpoint does not support PD disaggregation
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Summary The `/v1/responses` endpoint does not support PD disaggregation. The `ResponsesRequest` protocol is missing the bootstrap and DP routing fields that `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` already include, and `serving_responses.py` does not pass these fields when constructing `GenerateReqInput`. As a result, the endpoint cannot function in any PD disaggregated deployment. ### Expected Behavior `/v1/responses` should accept and propagate the same PD disaggregation body parameters as `/v1/chat/completions`, so it can be used in PD disaggregated deployments. ### Reproduction prefill： ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 8 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend=mooncake \ --disaggregation-ib-device xx ``` decode： ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 8 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend=mooncake \ --disaggregation-ib-device xx ``` ``` curl http://<host>:<port>/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "input": "Tell me a three sentence bedtime story about a unicorn." }' ``` ### Environment sglang:v0.5.16

signal.title: [Mooncake] Fix silent SSD offload corruption when TP/PP ranks share ssd_offload_path
signal.text: ## Motivation Each scheduler rank embeds its own `MooncakeDistributedStore` client, and `MooncakeStore.__init__ `passes all of them the same ssd_offload_path. Mooncake's SSD tier assumes one client per storage location, and a shared directory corrupts silently: - bucket ids are generated per process (`timestamp<<12` seed with a plain atomic increment, `mooncake-store/src/storage_backend.cpp`) - after a restart every client resumes from the same scanned max_bucket_id, making filename collisions deterministic - bucket files are opened with `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, so a collision truncates another rank's bucket and subsequent reads return wrong KV bytes with no error ## Modifications Give every rank a private subdirectory `ssd_offload_path/rank_<dp_rank>_<tp_rank>_<pp_rank>` (created before setup()). The suffix mirrors the per-rank key convention already used in this file (mha_suffix). When storage_config is None the path is used as-is, unchanged from today. The dp_rank component is required, not cosmetic: with dp-attention, `HiCacheController` reports the attention-group-local rank as tp_rank, which is 0 on every DP rank when attn_tp_size == 1 (e.g. tp8/dp8 DeepSeek), so tp_rank alone collapses all ranks onto one directory. We hit exactly this in a production deployment: 8 clients started in the same second shared one seed and truncated each other's buckets within minutes. `HiCacheStorageConfig` gains a `dp_rank` field (default 0) populated from the dp_rank the controller already computes. Note for existing SSD-offload deployments: previously offloaded buckets at the directory root are orphaned by the layout change (a one-time cache loss, recomputed on miss - not corruption). They can be deleted. ## Accuracy Tests N/A - no change to model outputs (client-side storage path handling only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A - one os.makedirs at engine startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31714157632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31714157632)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31714157430](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31714157430)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Fall back to cpu_tensor when host-pool retraction cannot fit
signal.text: ## Motivation `resolve_decode_retraction_backup`, added in #34801, picks the PD decode retraction backend on capability alone — mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, priority preemption, pool class. Whether the host pool fits never comes up, and it has to: `host_pool` mirrors the device KV pool 1:1 on every scheduler, while the only capacity check sits downstream in `pool_host/base.py`, well past the point of no return. On a GB300 tray that check can never pass. Four Blackwell Ultra GPUs hold 1110 GiB of HBM against 955 GiB of Grace LPDDR5X, so a KV pool sized to fill HBM cannot be mirrored into host RAM — a hybrid-SWA model at TP4 wants 1059.80 GB against ~854 GB free: ``` ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 117.76 GB but only have 98.90 GB free. ``` No workload or freed page cache gets there, and any node whose HBM rivals its DRAM lands the same way. An inferred default that cannot be satisfied should step aside; one asked for by name should still fail loudly. ## Modifications The inferred choice degrades to `cpu_tensor` with a warning naming both figures. Explicit `host_pool` still hard-fails, since the gate sits inside the `backend is None` branch. The budget reads `available` — what `HostKVCache.__init__` itself gates on. `_agree_across_ranks` all-reduces MIN over the world CPU group, shaped after `sync_fixed_hicache_size`, so no rank diverges. Reaching it needs a rank-uniform predicate, which splits the eligibility test: mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, and priority preemption come from the config bags and gate the estimate, while `supports_host_pool` is per-rank and only picks the backend. Prefill, embedding, and non-PD servers skip the estimate entirely. Three sizing fixes: - `_local_scheduler_count` mirrors the launcher's `pp_size_per_node * tp_size_per_node` plus the classic-DP replica factor. `tp_size // nnodes` undercounts past `pp_size > 1` and can reach zero. Reads `configured_tp_size()` / `configured_pp_size()`, which don't assert before process-group init. - MTP/EAGLE draft pools count, since the mirror packs them into its own `layer_num`. - `_kv_pool_bytes` takes both `get_kv_size_bytes` shapes. It tests for the `(k, v)` pair rather than the scalar: MLA returns `numpy.int64`, which `isinstance(size, int)` misses. `hicache_ratio` keys off the pre-fallback verdict, so the gate cannot enlarge the pool it just rejected. Deliberately not keyed off "a host pool gets built anyway", which would cut 2.0 to 1.0 for hierarchical-cache users on the decode-radix-cache path. The gate and the normalisation cover different cases — reverting the normalisation alone on 4×GB300: | Configuration | Normalisation | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | non-PD MLA | reverted | starts — the gate excludes it | | non-PD MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | | PD decode MLA | reverted | crashes in `_kv_pool_bytes` | | PD decode MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | The estimate is a lower bound; the per-rank gate stays authoritative. Page round-up and SIDECAR draft pools are unmodelled, because reproducing host-pool sizing here would go stale quietly. That belongs in a shared sizing helper, along with the scalar/tuple split and the unified pools — they return `(0, 0)` while subclassing MHA/SWA, so they would leave the gate inert rather than loud. Unreachable today: `--enable-unified-memory` with PD is MLA hybrid-Mamba only. ## Accuracy Tests Outputs are untouched — this resolves startup configuration, not the retraction path. `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_capacity.py` is new and CPU-registered, covering the PP and DP rank arithmetic, fits and doesn't-fit, the reserve, draft-pool accounting, both accessor shapes, the scope, and the ratio invariant driven through the resolver itself. Each fix was mutation-checked by reverting it: | Reverted | Result | | --- | --- | | ratio keyed off the post-fallback backend | 1 failure, `AssertionError: 2.0 != 1.0` | | reduction re-gated on the per-rank predicate | 2 failures, `_agree_across_ranks` called 0 times | | shape normalisation | 3 failures | | config-uniform gate | 2 failures | 166 tests pass across that file, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, and `test_server_args.py`; 20/20 under the `unittest` runner; pre-commit clean. On 4×GB300, a hybrid-SWA PD decode server falls back with identical figures on all four ranks and no deadlock, an MLA server starts clean both non-PD and PD decode, and a plain non-PD server never reaches the estimate. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The gate runs once per scheduler at startup, only for a config-eligible decode server, and the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No flag, default, or documented behaviour moves — an inferred default that used to crash now degrades with a warning. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32201835433](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201835433)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32201835245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201835245)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [ROCm] Use the AITER sparse-MLA kernel for DSA prefill and decode
signal.text: Enable with `--dsa-prefill-backend aiter --dsa-decode-backend aiter` (both flags are required; passing only one skips the ROCm default path). The default is unchanged. ## What this does On ROCm, DSA attention currently runs on TileLang for both prefill and decode. This PR adds an `aiter` backend that routes both phases to the AITER sparse-MLA kernel `mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen1_gqaratio16_ps` with fp8 Q and fp8 KV. Sparse DSA prefill is structurally a very wide decode: the chunk is handed to `mla_decode_fwd` as `num_tokens` sequences of length 1 (`max_seqlen_q = 1`), so one kernel serves both phases and no separate prefill kernel is needed. Notable details: - Q must be fp8, or AITER dispatches `mla_a16w8_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1_ps` instead, which is 4.2x slower. fp8 Q comes from `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, whose gate in `forward_mla.py` previously tested `dsa_backend == "tilelang"` literally. It is now a set of backends that want fp8 Q. - CUDA-only DSA backends now fall back to `tilelang` on ROCm with a warning instead of raising `ImportError: flashmla_ops`. The ROCm default is only applied when *both* backend flags are unset, so passing one previously made the other fall through to `flashmla_kv`. ## Results GLM-5.2 FP4, MI355X (gfx950) TP4, 8192 in / 1024 out, concurrency 64. Kernel time from a rocprof trace: | | TileLang | this PR | |---|---|---| | Prefill MLA, per 8192-token step | 320.2 ms | **143.7 ms** | | Prefill GPU busy, whole window | 728.4 ms | **564.8 ms** (-22.5%) | | Decode MLA, per iteration | 3.12 ms | **1.86 ms** | Everything else is unchanged within noise: MoE GEMM, dense GEMM and all-reduce all move by less than 1%. ## Correctness `python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200` -> **0.945**. ## Scope ROCm only, and only when both DSA backends are set to `aiter`. CUDA backends (`flashmla_*`, `flashinfer_sparse_mla`, `trtllm`) and the ROCm default (`tilelang`) are untouched; the default remains `tilelang/tilelang`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->_Not run yet_<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
