signal.title: [Feature] Add a tiered AdaLN cache manager for MiniMax-H3
signal.text: ## Summary MiniMax-H3 can avoid keeping the 24.2 GiB of `adaln_proj` checkpoint weights resident by rebuilding AdaLN outputs online. With TP=2, the resident path uses approximately 12.3 GiB per card for those weights. The current online implementation instead keeps a fixed GPU slab of historical timestep plans. This works well for repeated schedules, but it wastes GPU memory and evicts all plans when the schedule working set changes. This issue proposes a tiered cache manager: 1. Keep only the current request's AdaLN working set on GPU. 2. Keep complete, bounded schedule entries in pinned CPU memory. 3. Use online rebuild for CPU misses and high-churn workloads. 4. Keep precomputed sidecars as the preferred path for fixed production schedules. The design must preserve exact timestep-plan matching and the current numerical contract. Approximate timestep merging is out of scope. ## Motivation The cache key is the exact FP32 timestep plan used by a denoise step. A request can produce a different key when any of the following changes: - `num_inference_steps` - video or audio `sigmas` - `flow_shift` or `audio_flow_shift` - condition noise augmentation - task or reference modality layout In a typical 8-step request, only seven plans are needed. The default rebuild slab reserves 64 plans at the maximum width, even when most of that capacity is unused. When capacity is exceeded, the current implementation resets the slab, so returning to a recently used schedule requires rebuilding it from the checkpoint again. The default 64-plan, width-4 slab is approximately 2.31 GiB per card. The T2VA measurements below used the supported width-2 setting, which reduces that fixed slab to approximately 1.16 GiB per card. ## Measurements Environment: 2 x H200, MiniMax-H3 FL2VA, 1344 x 768, 4 seconds, 8 steps, TP=2/Ulysses=1. ### End-to-end measurements | Configuration | AdaLN prepare | E2E | GPU AdaLN working memory | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 64-plan online slab, warm hit | ~0.2 ms | ~19.0 s | ~1.16 GiB/card | | 7-plan request-sized slab, warm hit | ~0.2 ms | ~19.0 s | ~0.13 GiB/card | | 7-plan slab, new schedule | ~2.4 s | ~21.4 s | ~0.13 GiB/card | | Fixed 8-step sidecar, warm hit | ~0.02 ms | ~19.25 s | ~0.13 GiB/card | | Resident AdaLN weights, warm | N/A | ~19.0 s | +~12.3 GiB/card | The 7-plan slab is a temporary request-sized approximation, not the proposed final dynamic implementation. It demonstrates that reducing the slab capacity does not regress warm-request latency. ### CPU backing transfer cost Pinned host-to-device and device-to-host copies were measured at approximately 51 GiB/s: | Schedule working set | H2D | D2H | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 120 MiB (T2VA) | 2.28 ms | 2.29 ms | | 185 MiB (FL2VA) | 3.51 ms | 3.53 ms | | 231 MiB (widest ref2va) | 4.39 ms | 4.40 ms | This is substantially cheaper than rebuilding a schedule from checkpoint weights, which currently takes roughly 2.4-3.0 seconds. Nsight profiling shows that cold rebuild time is dominated by reading roughly 24.3 GiB of AdaLN checkpoint weights into GPU memory. The projection GEMMs are not the dominant cost. ### Raw request results The following values are taken from the server perf dumps generated during the experiment. The sequence for the online runs was `flow_shift = [12, 12, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 12]`, with `audio_flow_shift=3`, 8 inference steps, and the same prompt, resolution, duration, and seed for every request. The first request includes one-time server/kernel warm-up and is reported separately. | Run | Schedule | AdaLN prepare | Denoising | Decoding | E2E | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Online, 64 plans, request 0 | 12 (cold start) | 3037.0 ms | 21427.9 ms | 3466.6 ms | 25206.1 ms | | Online, 64 plans, request 1 | 12 (GPU hit) | 0.2 ms | 16847.6 ms | 2021.8 ms | 18948.3 ms | | Online, 64 plans, requests 2-10 | 4-13 (new schedules) | 2888.4-3044.2 ms | 19793.6-20209.3 ms | 2021.4-2027.6 ms | 21894.5-22335.3 ms | | Online, 64 plans, request 11 | 12 (GPU hit) | 0.2 ms | 17009.5 ms | 2021.3 ms | 19106.7 ms | | Online, 7 plans, request 0 | 12 (cold start) | 2745.5 ms | 21355.7 ms | 2755.7 ms | 24764.7 ms | | Online, 7 plans, request 1 | 12 (GPU hit) | 0.2 ms | 16859.2 ms | 2022.4 ms | 18966.7 ms | | Online, 7 plans, requests 2-10 | 4-13 (new schedules) | 2309.6-2424.1 ms | 19236.3-19334.9 ms | 2020.1-2122.1 ms | 21350.8-21457.9 ms | | Online, 7 plans, request 11 | 12 (evicted, rebuild) | 2363.5 ms | 19240.2 ms | 2128.2 ms | 21502.3 ms | | Resident AdaLN weights, request 1 | 12 (warm) | 0.02 ms | 16920.2 ms | 2027.9 ms | 19025.7 ms | | Fixed sidecar, request 1 | 12 (sidecar hit) | 0.02 ms | 17136.6 ms | 2029.3 ms | 19246.2 ms | The return-to-12 result is the direct eviction evidence: the 64-plan run still had the original schedule available, while the 7-plan run had replaced its entire GPU working set and paid another rebuild. ### Raw memory observations The perf dumps reported the following allocated-memory checkpoints per card: | Configuration | Before forward | Peak after forward | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Online, 64 plans, warm | 51949.1 MiB | 54888.1 MiB | | Online, 7 plans, warm | 50895.4 MiB | 53834.3 MiB | | Resident weights, warm | 63191.6 MiB | 66131.5 MiB | | Fixed sidecar, warm | 50895.6 MiB | 53834.5 MiB | The 7-plan workspace reduced allocated memory by approximately 1054 MiB per card relative to the 64-plan T2VA run, without a measurable warm-hit regression. The resident-weight comparison was run in a separate server process; its latency is useful as a reference, but the memory values should be interpreted as process-level observations rather than an isolated AdaLN allocation measurement. ### Accuracy and transfer checks - The audited AdaLN comparison checked 470,367,744 output elements at TP1 and TP2 with zero mismatches. - Online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs produced matching MP4 MD5 values for both cold and cached cases at TP1 and TP2. - Pinned CPU/GPU transfer microbenchmarks measured 2.28 ms H2D for 120 MiB, 3.51 ms for 185 MiB, and 4.39 ms for 231 MiB. D2H measured 2.29 ms, 3.53 ms, and 4.40 ms respectively. - The fixed sidecar accepted the exact `flow_shift=12` schedule and rejected `flow_shift=4` with `MiniMax H3 AdaLN cache does not cover the request timestep plan`. ### Nsight cold-rebuild profile A TP1 cold-rebuild capture covered 8455.9 ms. Within that range: | Activity | Count/bytes | GPU or API time | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Host-to-device checkpoint copies | 249 copies, 26,078,740,624 bytes | 7258.2 ms | | Main AdaLN projection GEMM kernel | 2450 launches | 296.9 ms | | BF16 output copy kernels | 2400 launches | 7.9 ms | | `cudaMemcpyAsync` host API calls | 397 calls | 7349.7 ms | The capture confirms that checkpoint movement, rather than AdaLN projection compute, dominates an online cold miss. ## Proposed design ### GPU tier - Allocate stable GPU buffers once per worker, sized for the configured maximum request working set. - Reuse the same tensor pointers across requests to preserve CUDA graph and breakable-CUDA-graph assumptions. - Populate the buffers with the current request's complete schedule only. - Do not retain old schedules in the GPU tier after a request is admitted. The exact dynamic allocation policy still needs to account for graph capture. A first implementation may use a deployment-configured upper bound per task (`t2va`, `fl2va`, or `ref2va`) while keeping the active logical length request local. ### CPU tier - Use the complete schedule, including task/modality and exact FP32 plan bits, as the cache key. - Store the complete projected AdaLN output for that schedule in pinned CPU memory. - Bound the cache by bytes and/or number of schedules. - Use LRU eviction and expose hit, miss, admission, eviction, and transfer counters. - Copy a CPU hit into the GPU working set asynchronously before denoising. The CPU tier should cache complete schedules rather than individual plans. A partial plan hit still causes the current rebuild path to scan all AdaLN layers, so plan-level LRU would retain complexity without avoiding the expensive miss. ### Miss and admission policy - On a CPU miss, rebuild the complete schedule from checkpoint weights. - Optionally admit the resulting schedule into CPU memory only after a second use, or when the configured admission budget allows it. - If the workload has a low CPU hit rate or exceeds the CPU byte budget, fall back to online rebuild without retaining the result. - A fixed schedule can bypass the manager entirely and use a precomputed sidecar. ## Layout considerations The current GPU tensor layout is effectively `[plan, timestep, layer, feature]`. Forward accesses are layer-oriented, so slicing one layer across multiple timesteps is non-contiguous for plans longer than one timestep and can force a materialization during `reshape`. The manager should evaluate a layer-contiguous backing layout, for example `[plan, layer, timestep, feature]`, or pre-materialized request-local views. Any layout change must be checked against: - exact BF16 output equality; - TP1 and TP2 behavior; - CUDA graph pointer stability; - per-step denoising latency; - sidecar compatibility. ## Scope ### In scope - A bounded CPU pinned-memory schedule cache. - Request-local GPU working-set management. - Exact schedule key construction and collision-free lookup. - Metrics and perf-dump visibility for each tier. - TP1/TP2 accuracy and end-to-end benchmarks. ### Out of scope - Approximate timestep matching or schedule interpolation. - Changing timestep embedding math or scheduler semantics. - Changing AdaLN numerical precision or TP sharding. - Replacing the existing fixed-schedule sidecar format in the first phase. ## Acceptance criteria - A repeated schedule served from CPU backing avoids checkpoint rebuild and adds no more than 10 ms to AdaLN preparation for the measured H3 working-set sizes. - A CPU miss has the same numerical output as the existing online rebuild path. - GPU memory for an 8-step T2VA request is within the request working-set size, rather than the default 64-plan slab size. - A schedule that is not present in a sidecar fails closed with an actionable error. - Capacity eviction and failed rebuilds leave no partially published cache hit. - TP1 and TP2 outputs remain bit-identical for the audited AdaLN output set and end-to-end media checks. - CUDA graph and breakable-CUDA-graph replay continue to work with the manager enabled, or the manager explicitly disables graph replay with a documented reason. ## Suggested implementation phases 1. Refactor the cache into a request-local GPU workspace with stable pointers; retain the existing online rebuild path as the miss handler. 2. Add a standalone pinned CPU schedule store and benchmark `A -> B -> A` and high-churn sequences before integrating it into request admission. 3. Integrate CPU hits, asynchronous copies, byte-bounded LRU eviction, and metrics. 4. Benchmark the current layout against a layer-contiguous layout. 5. Add TP1/TP2 accuracy tests, sidecar compatibility tests, reset/retry tests, and end-to-end workload benchmarks. ## Open questions - Should CPU entries be shared across workers or kept per TP replica? - Should a schedule be admitted on first use or only after a second use? - What byte budget is appropriate for H200 and lower-memory deployments? - Which graph modes require a fixed maximum workspace versus an eager fallback? - Should the manager be enabled by default, or initially behind an experimental server flag?

signal.title: Fix Qwen3.5 GDN multi-item scoring
signal.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.5 hybrid models use recurrent GDN layers alongside full-attention layers. Multi-item scoring already gives the full-attention layers an item-branching mask, but the GDN prefill path previously processed the packed suffix as one continuous recurrent sequence. As a result, later items could inherit convolution and SSM state from earlier items. Fixes #31969. ## Modifications - Add a read-only final-state mode to the Triton chunk gated-delta-rule path while preserving in-place updates by default. - Build GDN-specific MIS metadata once per forward for compact query and item segments. - Run GDN MIS prefill in two phases: compute each request query once, then branch every item from the query-end convolution and SSM states. - Keep item recurrence read-only against the request SSM pool and use unique cloned convolution slots per item. - Reject unsupported combinations, including non-Triton GDN prefill, page-major layout, cached prefixes, non-prefill requests, and hybrid linear backends without MIS support. - Add kernel, causal-convolution, backend, metadata, validation, and Qwen3.5 end-to-end coverage. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on one NVIDIA H20 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` in BF16, FlashInfer full attention, and Triton linear-attention prefill. - Qwen3.5 MIS end-to-end: 3 tests passed, covering empty queries, concurrent requests, varied item counts and lengths, and sibling modification/reordering. - Focused recurrent, causal-convolution, GDN backend, metadata, and validation suite: 27 tests passed with 46 subtests. - Full recurrent and causal-convolution test files: 275 tests passed. - Multi-item scores match per-item MIS scoring with `atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2`. - Formatting, import checks, spelling, syntax compilation, CI registration validation, and whitespace checks passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Single H20, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, query length 120, item length 180, 10 items per request, 10 warmup requests, followed by three 60-second runs. CUDA graph, radix cache, and chunked prefill were disabled in both modes. | Mode | Items/s/GPU | P50 latency | P99 latency | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Independent pointwise scoring | 52.80 | 189.06 ms | 195.25 ms | | Multi-item scoring | 62.75 | 158.74 ms | 167.21 ms | This is an 18.84% throughput increase, with P50 latency reduced by 16.04% and P99 latency reduced by 14.36%. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with the repository formatters and static checks. - [x] Add unit and end-to-end tests. - [x] Documentation is not required because this does not change the public API or Score API schema. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. 2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers. 3. Trigger the required CI tests. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32088388694](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32088388694)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32224764451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224764451)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: refactor(kernels): split zero-KV fixup by alignment
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This is a follow-up to #32890, which introduced the TRT-LLM ragged attention zero-KV fixup path. That path clears `out` and sets `lse` to `-inf` for sequences whose KV length is zero. The original fix already handles potentially misaligned rows by checking alignment inside the device helper before using vectorized `float4` stores. Per @nvpohanh's suggestion, this PR avoids the device-side if/else by compiling separate aligned and scalar store paths, then choosing the appropriate specialization from the host launcher. This keeps the aligned vectorized fast path while routing potentially misaligned layouts, such as TP cases where `lse` row stride is not a 16-byte multiple, to scalar stores. ## Modifications - Compile the zero-KV fixup kernel with independent store-mode template parameters for `out` and `lse`. - Dispatch four host-side variants: vector/vector, vector/scalar, scalar/vector, and scalar/scalar. - Include both base pointer alignment and row-stride alignment in the host predicates. This covers contiguous tensors with non-zero PyTorch `storage_offset`. - Preserve the existing public Python/JIT wrapper API. - Add a registered CUDA unit test for: - contiguous tensors with non-zero storage offsets; - mixed-alignment layouts where `out` can remain vectorized while `lse` uses scalar stores. ## Accuracy Tests Added: ```bash test/registered/kernels/test_fixup_zero_kv.py ``` Local checks run: ```bash git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/private/tmp/sglang_pycache python3 -m py_compile test/registered/kernels/test_fixup_zero_kv.py ``` Not run locally: ```bash python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/test_fixup_zero_kv.py -q ``` The local Python environment does not have `pytest` installed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Added a dedicated microbenchmark for this PR: ```bash python3 test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_fixup_zero_kv.py ``` It is also registered in the CUDA kernel benchmark suite and can be run through: ```bash python3 test/run_suite.py --hw cuda \ --suite base-b-kernel-benchmark-test-1-gpu-large \ --continue-on-error ``` The benchmark exercises the four host-dispatched specializations introduced here: | mode | `out` store | `lse` store | coverage | |---|---:|---:|---| | `vec_vec` | vectorized | vectorized | fully 16-byte aligned fast path | | `vec_scalar` | vectorized | scalar | TP-like layouts where `lse` row stride is not 16-byte aligned | | `scalar_vec` | scalar | vectorized | non-zero storage offset / misaligned `out` base pointer | | `scalar_scalar` | scalar | scalar | both buffers potentially misaligned | Shapes covered: `(max_seq_len, batch_size) = (32, 32), (128, 32), (512, 16)`. The benchmark is intentionally a kernel microbenchmark so it isolates the zero-KV fixup cost instead of hiding it inside a full model run. I did not post local timing numbers because this workstation cannot run the CUDA benchmark (`nvidia-smi` is unavailable and the local Python env does not have `torch`). Light local validation completed: ```bash PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/sglang-pr33881-pycache \ python3 -m py_compile \ test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_fixup_zero_kv.py \ test/registered/kernels/test_fixup_zero_kv.py git diff --check ``` Expected perf behavior: the fully aligned `vec_vec` path preserves the existing vectorized fast path, while mixed-alignment cases avoid the previous device-side per-row alignment branch by selecting the scalar/vector specialization once in the host launcher. ## Microbenchmark ## Microbenchmark **GPU:** GB200 | **dtype:** fp16 signal.title: [NVIDIA][comm] Merge EP+MoE-TP post-experts all-reduces into one _TP reduction
signal.text: ## Problem statement With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, the post-experts reduction requires two all-reduces over orthogonal groups (`_MOE_EP` then `_MOE_TP`). The allreduce fusion gate was skipping *both* once `fuse_mlp_allreduce` was published, then Observed as GSM8k accuracy 0.012 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` with silently returning under-reduced activations with no error. Observed as GSM8k accuracy 0.012 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` with the fused residual+LN kernel reduced over only `_MOE_EP` (2 of 4 peers) — silently returning under-reduced activations with no error ## Motivation Under hybrid MoE EP+TP (`moe_ep_size > 1` **and** `moe_tp_size > 1`), allreduce fusion silently produces under-reduced activations. There is no error — the model just returns garbage. Reproduced on `main`, 4×GB200: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tp-size 4 --ep-size 2 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Where is capital city of France? Answer in one short word." } ], "chat_template_kwargs": { "enable_thinking": false }, "max_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0 }' ``` The completion is garbage unless `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` is passed. `--ep-size 4` and `--ep-size 1` are both fine. ### Root cause With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, the post-experts reduction spans **two** disjoint groups (`Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward_normal`): ``` moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce -> _MOE_EP moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce -> _MOE_TP ``` `_MOE_EP × _MOE_TP` is an orthogonal decomposition of the TP world (`moe_tp_size = tp_size // moe_ep_size // moe_dp_size`), so both reductions are needed to cover all 4 ranks. When the decoder publishes `fuse_mlp_allreduce`, `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` skips **both** of them — it keys off `should_skip_mlp_all_reduce()`, which does not distinguish the EP path from the TP path. The reduction is then supposed to be absorbed by the next layer's fused residual+RMSNorm, but that kernel reduces over a **single** group: the MoE fusion workspace, which `ensure_workspace_initialized()` rendezvouses on `_MOE_EP` when `moe_ep_size > 1`. Net effect: the MoE output is reduced over 2 of the 4 required ranks. `--ep-size 4` (`moe_tp_size == 1`) and `--ep-size 1` (`moe_ep_size == 1`) are unaffected, because there a single group already covers every peer. This is pre-existing on `main` and independent of any in-flight FlashInfer work. It was surfaced while reviewing #30700 (thanks @mmangkad for the hybrid EP+TP question that led here). ### Graph illustration ## Why hybrid EP+TP specifically With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, `moe_tp_size = 4 // 2 // 1 = 2`, and the MoE output needs reducing over two orthogonal subgroups that together tile the TP world: ``` rank: 0 1 2 3 ep_rank: 0 0 1 1 <- which expert shard it holds tp_rank: 0 1 0 1 <- which FFN shard it holds _MOE_EP: {0,2} {1,3} _MOE_TP: {0,1} {2,3} ``` output needs reducing over two orthogonal subgroups that together tile the TP world: ``` rank: 0 1 2 3 ep_rank: 0 0 1 1 <- which expert shard it holds tp_rank: 0 1 0 1 <- which FFN shard it holds _MOE_EP: {0,2} {1,3} _MOE_TP: {0,1} {2,3} ``` Either reduction alone covers 2 of the 4 ranks; both are required. ``` layer N (MoE output) | layer N+1 ----------------------------------------------|------------------------ main experts --> [EP skipped] [TP skipped] -----|--> fused AR + RMSNorm | workspace group = _MOE_EP | sums {0,2} only -> WRONG this PR experts --> AR(_MOE_EP) --> AR(_MOE_TP) ----|--> RMSNorm {0,2} {0,1} | all 4 ranks summed -> ok ``` Publishing `fuse_mlp_allreduce` makes `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` drop **both** reductions, because it keys off that flag without distinguishing the EP path from the TP path. The next layer's fused residual+LN then reduces over a single group — the MoE fusion workspace, which `ensure_workspace_initialized()` rendezvouses on `_MOE_EP` when `moe_ep_size > 1`. Half the peers never contribute, and the result is wrong without any error. No other configuration breaks, because no other configuration has two distinct subgroups: ``` ep_size=1 -> moe_tp_size == tp_size, _MOE_TP *is* _TP (parallel_state.py:2483) ep_size=4 -> moe_ep_size == tp_size, _MOE_EP *is* _TP (parallel_state.py:2454) ep_size=2 -> neither aliases _TP -> the only broken case ## Modifications `LayerCommunicator.should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer()` now returns `False` when `moe_ep_size > 1 and moe_tp_size > 1`. Fusion is only valid when one group covers every peer of the reduction, which is not the case here. Both post-experts all-reduces then run inline as usual. The guard sits before the backend-specific checks, so it covers the aiter fusion branch too — that path reduces over a single group for the same reason. Attention-side fusion is untouched: it uses the attention-TP workspace (`use_attn_tp_group=True`) whose group spans the full TP world, and it is gated on `apply_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` alone, not on `fuse_mlp_allreduce`. New unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py` (CPU, 3 cases): hybrid EP+TP must not fuse; pure-TP and pure-EP must still fuse. The hybrid case fails on pre-fix code and passes on the fix; the other two guard against the gate degrading to always-off. After fix: ``` {"id":"0dc05777d22f4efdbbba2ba896d4d196","object":"chat.completion","created":1785440815,"model":"nvidia/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-NVFP4","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Paris","reasoning_content":null,"tool_calls":null},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","matched_stop":151645}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":25,"total_tokens":27,"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens_details":null,"reasoning_tokens":0},"metadata":{"weight_version":"default"}} ``` ## Accuracy Tests - `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2` on 4×GB200 with Qwen3-30B-A3B: garbage before, correct completions after, **without** `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion`. - `--ep-size 4` and `--ep-size 1` re-checked for no regression. - `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py` — 3 passed. GSM8k: ``` on GB200 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1316 --parallel 1316 reference: (--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4) Accuracy: 0.743 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 18.692 s Output throughput: 17213.786 token/s before fix: (--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2) Accuracy: 0.012 Invalid: 0.014 Latency: 37.922 s Output throughput: 17453.860 token/s after fix: (--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2) Accuracy: 0.777 Invalid: 0.003 Latency: 17.508 s Output throughput: 16609.659 token/s ``` Also support DSV4: ``` python -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 --ep-size 2 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 ``` gsm8k: ``` python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1316 --parallel 1316 Accuracy: 0.954 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 90.583 s ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31798534381](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31798534381)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31798534097](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31798534097)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
signal.text: ## Problem Partition 0 of `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x-rocm720` (`test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py`) has failed on every scheduled run since 2026-08-16 12:08 UTC. Example: [job 95552260420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32083881457/job/95552260420). The empty-batch guard added in #34474 reads `hidden_states.shape[0]` immediately after `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs()`. When the fused AR+quant path is active that call returns a tuple — `(bf16, fp8, scale)` in the GatedDeltaNet layer, `(fp8, scale)` in the plain attention layer — so the guard raises during decode CUDA-graph capture and the server dies at startup: ``` File "python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 806, in forward if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` The scheduler child dying takes the process tree with it, which the test surfaces as the less obvious `Server process exited with code -9`. Only the `fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant` variant is affected; the `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control variant stays on the tensor path. ## Fix Read the row count off the tuple's first element, using the same inline form `glm4_moe.py` already uses for this situation. Applied at both guard sites. This is behavior-preserving. `prepare_attn()` returns early on `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0` *before* the fusion branch, so a tuple can only appear when the count is already `> 0`; the tuple path therefore behaves exactly as it did before #34474, while the tensor path keeps the empty-batch guard. Both sites are patched because `keep_bf16=False` still yields a tuple, just the 2-element form. `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.forward_prepare_native()` / `.forward_prepare_fused_gate()` both open with `isinstance(hidden_states, tuple)`, and `_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear()` has a dedicated `len(...) == 2` branch that only this path produces. Supersedes #35250, which diagnosed the same bug but patched the GatedDeltaNet site only. ## Verification Reproduced and fixed end-to-end on an 8x MI350X node following the CI flow exactly — same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`), same `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, same `run_suite.py` invocation. Before, at the failing scheduled-run SHA `91144797c`: the `AttributeError` above, byte-for-byte the CI signature. After: | Variant | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | Threshold | Status | | ------- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------- | ------ | | fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant | 0,1,2,3 | 0.951 | 0.009 | 53.66 | 4067.56 | 0.94 | PASS | | disable-fused-ar-quant-opt-out | 4,5,6,7 | 0.940 | 0.009 | 53.85 | 4010.65 | 0.94 | PASS | On CI, partition 0 is green on both [run 32203488998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203488998) and [run 32227220289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227220289), with accuracy matching the last pre-regression baseline ([run 31916881653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653): 0.949 / 0.943). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No new test: `test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py` already covers this path and is the test that was red. No user-facing behavior change, and no before-number to benchmark since the server did not start.

signal.title: [Fix] LLaVA-hf checkpoints: five sequential fixes for Transformers-fallback vision-tower loading
signal.text: ## Summary Five sequential fixes that let `llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf` reach model.forward on the current transformers release. Each was surfaced by the next after the prior was applied; all are localized. A sixth blocker (a multimodal-scheduler mismatch, `items_offset` handed as `None` to `_count_mm_tokens_in_extend`) is a different subsystem — not in scope for this PR, will follow up separately. ### 1. `TransformersBase.__init__` — guard `vocab_size` lookup for vision encoders The initializer dereferences the input embeddings unconditionally as the `getattr()` default: ```python self.vocab_size = getattr( self.text_config, "vocab_size", self.model.get_input_embeddings().num_embeddings, ) ``` Python 3 evaluates the default eagerly, so `self.model.get_input_embeddings().num_embeddings` fires even when `text_config.vocab_size` is set. For a vision-only backbone (e.g. `CLIPVisionModel` routed through the fallback as the vision tower of a native LLaVA impl), `get_input_embeddings()` returns the patch-embedding `Conv2d`, which has no `num_embeddings`: ``` AttributeError: 'Conv2d' object has no attribute 'num_embeddings' ``` **Fix:** restructure the lookup so the fallback only runs when actually needed, and treats a non-`nn.Embedding` input-embedding module as "no vocab" (vision case). `input_embeddings` is now computed once and reused for the subsequent `embed_scale` probe. ### 2. `LlavaForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` — accept HF's `"default"` select strategy `load_weights` guards on `vision_feature_select_strategy` (decides whether to bump `image_feature_len` for a leading CLS token). It accepted `"patch"` / `"full"` / `"cls_patch"` and raised on anything else. HF's own `LlavaConfig` — used by every `llava-hf/*` checkpoint — sets this to `"default"` (equivalent to `"patch"`: take all patch tokens after CLS, no length bump): ``` ValueError: Unexpected select feature: default ``` The sibling `get_image_feature` paths on the same class already treat `"default"` as an alias for `"patch"`. This is a stale gap in one location, not a semantic change. ### 3. `LlavaForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` — strip legacy `vision_model.` wrapper `llava-hf/*` checkpoints serialize the vision tower under `vision_tower.vision_model.*` — the historical HF nesting for `CLIPVisionModel.vision_model = CLIPVisionTransformer(...)`. transformers ≥ 5.6 flattens that layout: `CLIPVisionModel.named_children()` returns `embeddings`, `pre_layrnorm`, `encoder`, `post_layernorm` directly, and the `vision_model` wrapper is gone. When SGLang's native LLaVA impl routes the vision tower through the Transformers fallback (`_get_sgl_model_cls(vision_config, AutoModel)` → `TransformersForCausalLM`), the fallback wraps that same flattened HF class, so `self.model` has no `vision_model` submodule. After the LLaVA dispatcher strips `vision_tower.`, the residual names still lead with `vision_model.` and the loader trips at descend time: ``` ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.vision_model' in TransformersForCausalLM. ``` **Fix:** strip the residual `vision_model.` prefix at the LLaVA dispatcher — the same place other post-`vision_tower` renames belong. Sibling model `llavavid.py` already carries this rewrite in its projector-weight map for the same reason (see the `transformers 5.6.0` comment there); this is the base-class counterpart. ### 4. `TransformersBase.replace_vocab_embed_class` — skip non-`nn.Embedding` input embeddings `replace_vocab_embed_class` swaps the model's input embedding with a `VocabParallelEmbedding` sized to `self.vocab_size`. That is correct for language-model backbones (`nn.Embedding`, `num_embeddings == vocab_size`), but wrong for vision encoders: HF vision models return the patch-embedding `Conv2d` from `get_input_embeddings()`, which is a pixel→patch projection, not a lookup. Compounding it, HF's `LlavaConfig.__init__` copies `text_config.vocab_size` onto `vision_config`, so a plain `CLIPVisionConfig()` has no `vocab_size` but the `LlavaConfig`-nested one carries `vocab_size = 32000`. The result: - `self.vocab_size` resolves to 32000 (from `vision_config.vocab_size`) - `new_module = VocabParallelEmbedding(32000, 1024)` replaces the `Conv2d` - weight load of `vision_tower.vision_model.embeddings.patch_embedding.weight` (shape `[1024, 3, 14, 14]`) into the `VocabParallelEmbedding` trips its shape guard: ``` AssertionError: self.org_vocab_size=32000 self.use_presharded_weights=False loaded_weight.shape[output_dim]=1024 ``` Even if the guard didn't fire, forward would break: a `Conv2d(pixels→patches)` cannot be an `nn.Embedding` lookup. **Fix:** bail out early when the input embedding is not an `nn.Embedding` subclass — vision encoders keep their `Conv2d` patch embedding untouched. Text models (`nn.Embedding` + optional `embed_scale` subclasses) are unchanged. ### 5. `LlavaForConditionalGeneration.__init__` + `_infer_image_aspect_ratio` — use configured aspect ratio, drop LLaVA-Onevision fallback The initializer injects LLaVA-Onevision-shaped defaults when the HF config is missing `image_aspect_ratio` or `image_grid_pinpoints`: ```python if not hasattr(self.config, "image_aspect_ratio"): self.config.image_aspect_ratio = "anyres" if not hasattr(self.config, "image_grid_pinpoints"): self.config.image_grid_pinpoints = [ [96, 96], [224, 224], [384, 384], [512, 512], [768, 768], [1024, 1024], ] ``` `llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf` sets neither, so it gets forced into an anyres regime with LLaVA-Onevision pinpoints. `pad_input_ids` then computes an anyres grid via `get_anyres_image_grid_shape` and passes it to `unpad_image_shape`, which trips a `ZeroDivisionError` (or an `ast.literal_eval(None)` with a `None`-pinpoints default). Compounding it, the base-class helper that decides the branch has the same LLaVA-Onevision bias: ```python @staticmethod def _infer_image_aspect_ratio(mm_items): ... return "anyres" # single-image fallback ``` Two changes, same root cause: - `_infer_image_aspect_ratio` becomes an instance method whose single-image fallback returns `self.image_aspect_ratio` instead of hard-coding `"anyres"`. Each subclass now propagates its own configured aspect ratio; processor-supplied per-item overrides still win. - Missing-config defaults switch to `"pad"` and pinpoints `None`, the correct behavior for LLaVA-1.5-style single-grid checkpoints. Real anyres models (LLaVA-Onevision, LLaVA-NeXT) set both fields explicitly on their HF config, so the `hasattr` guards leave them untouched. ## Test plan - [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for both files. - [x] `llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf` (TP=1, `intel_xpu` attention backend, `mem-fraction-static=0.80`) — on `main`, scheduler init dies at `AttributeError: 'Conv2d' object has no attribute 'num_embeddings'` before weight load; with fix 1 it progresses to the strategy-alias `ValueError`; fix 2 to the `vision_model.` descend `ValueError`; fix 3 to the `VocabParallelEmbedding` shape assertion; fix 4 to the anyres `ZeroDivisionError`; with all five fixes the server boots end-to-end (`Load weight end`, `KV Cache is allocated`, `Uvicorn running`), `/model_info` returns 200, `pad_input_ids` completes, and control reaches `model.forward` before the next-distinct blocker (see below). - [ ] Not yet reaching output: a further `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object` fires in `mm_schedule._count_mm_tokens_in_extend` (`items_offset` is `None`). Distinct subsystem — multimodal-scheduler expects a `[(start, end), ...]` list that the LLaVA `pad_input_ids` path isn't populating on this route. Follow-up separately. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32227380720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227380720)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32227380550](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227380550)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Inference Support Mamba 2 and 1
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add SGLang support for the **Mamba family of pure state-space models**, none of which could be served before — they crashed at startup or fell through to attention code paths they don't fit. This PR covers both generations: - **Mamba2 (SSD):** `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1` - **Mamba-1 (selective-scan):** `tiiuae/falcon-mamba-7b` / `-instruct`, `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`, and the raw `state-spaces/mamba-{130m,790m,2.8b}` checkpoints Root causes addressed: these configs have no `num_attention_heads`/`head_dim`, so shape derivation tripped before any weights loaded; the pure-SSM path routed through the paged decoder KV cache (an SSM keeps none); Mamba2 checkpoints use `backbone.*` names with no `max_position_embeddings`; and the raw state-spaces configs carry no `model_type`/`architectures`, so `AutoConfig` rejected them outright. ## Modifications - **New models:** `Mamba2ForCausalLM` (`models/mamba2.py`), `FalconMambaForCausalLM` (`models/falcon_mamba.py`), `MambaForCausalLM` (`models/mamba.py`) — pre-norm mixer decoder layers, no MLP; weight loaders remap `backbone.* → model.*`, `embeddings/embedding. → embed_tokens`, `norm_f → norm` (Mamba2 also `A_log → A`; Mamba-1 keeps `A_log`). - **New Mamba-1 mixer** (`layers/attention/mamba/mamba1.py`, `MambaMixer1`): causal conv over intermediate channels, `x_proj`/`dt_proj` selection, optional Falcon weightless RMSNorm on `B`/`C`/`dt`. Decode reuses `selective_state_update`; prefill uses a portable per-timestep selective scan (works off-CUDA, e.g. XPU). - **Reuse of the Mamba2 backend for Mamba-1:** express the full-rank Mamba-1 state on the Mamba2 head layout (`num_heads = intermediate_size`, `head_dim = 1`) via `Mamba2StateShape.create_mamba1`, so it rides the existing attention backend and memory pool unchanged. - **Config/wiring (gated, additive):** `AttentionArch.SSM`; `PURE_SSM_ARCHITECTURES` / `PURE_MAMBA1_ARCHITECTURES` with `_is_pure_mamba2` / `_is_pure_mamba1` flags; KV-less handling (`head_dim = 0`) in `model_config.py`; cache-param build in `hybrid_arch.py`; SSM backend selection in `attention_backend_setup.py`; forward-metadata guard in `eager_runner.py`. - **Raw-checkpoint support:** `_try_load_raw_mamba_config` pre-`AutoConfig` hook in `utils/hf_transformers/config.py` builds a `MambaConfig` from the minimal `d_model`/`n_layer`/`ssm_cfg` config. - **Conv dtype fix** for fp32 checkpoints (`SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE` mismatch); CPU unit test for Mamba2 weight remapping; docs entry. All changes are gated behind the SSM arch/flag; existing MLA/MHA models keep their original code paths. ## Accuracy Tests | Model | Task | Metric | SGLang (Intel XPU) | |---|---|---|---| | Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1 | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, greedy) | flexible / strict | 0.4579 / 0.4488 | | falcon-mamba-7b | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot) | flexible / strict | 0.5140 / 0.5095 | | falcon-mamba-7b-instruct | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, chat) | flexible / strict | 0.5883 / 0.5534 | | state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | piqa (1000, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.649 / 0.637 (≈ published 0.64) | | state-spaces/mamba-130m (raw) | hellaswag (limit-50, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.34 / 0.48 | | state-spaces/mamba-790m, 2.8b (raw) | — | greedy generation | coherent | All models load with 0 real skipped params. Stock server commands run unchanged (raw checkpoints need `--tokenizer-path EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b`, a deployment flag). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Adds new models with no change to existing code paths or their speed. Serving on Intel XPU (2× Arc Pro B60): Mamba-Codestral ~36 concurrent sequences / ~220 tok/s decode (tp-size 2); Falcon-Mamba ~42 / ~200 tok/s (tp-size 1). Pure SSM models report a zero-byte KV cache, so concurrency is bounded by `--max-total-tokens` / Mamba state-cache slots rather than KV memory. Mamba-1 prefill uses a per-token selective scan (no in-tree chunked-scan kernel yet), so prefill throughput is low — a Triton Mamba-1 scan kernel is the natural follow-up. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32132432442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132432442)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32132432386](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132432386)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Add MiniCPM-SALA support
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add native serving support for MiniCPM-SALA checkpoints, which interleave MiniCPM sparse softmax-attention layers with constant-decay Lightning linear-attention layers. The implementation integrates the model with SGLang's existing attention, linear-attention, CUDA graph, and memory-pool infrastructure. It also replaces the serving-time dependency on the original out-of-tree block-table extension with SGLang JIT kernels. ## Modifications - Add `MiniCPMHybridConfig` and register both `MiniCPMForCausalLM` and `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. - Normalize mixer aliases and repeat mixer patterns to the configured layer count. - Parse both flattened and legacy nested sparse-attention configuration. - Describe Lightning state using the existing `Mamba2CacheParams` and linear-attention model registry. - Extend the MiniCPM model with SALA mixer support. - Add Lightning QKV projection, optional Q/K normalization, RoPE, output normalization and gating, configurable attention scaling, and checkpoint-compatible weight loading. - Reuse the in-tree Lightning backend and `seg_la` kernels instead of introducing a model-specific linear-attention backend or external dependency. - Generalize the shared Lightning backend to read the linear KV-head count, layerwise decay mode, and per-layer attention scale from the model config. - Add `minicpm_flashattn` and `minicpm_flashinfer` sparse-attention backends. - Compose with `FlashAttentionBackend` for dense metadata and CUDA graph state. - Keep FlashInfer support as a composed decode path rather than duplicating its wrapper management. - Select FA4 automatically on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Support dense/sparse prefill and decode, CUDA graph capture/replay, K1/K2 key compression, sparse top-k selection, and optional fused TileLang kernels. - Add JIT-compiled CUDA block-table kernels. - Use v2 for prefill and v3 for the optimized decode layout, with automatic v2 fallback for unsupported v3 shapes. - Cache compiled modules by top-k, head-group count, and block size. - Attach the MiniCPM compressed cache to the existing `ReqToTokenPool`. - Reserve and account for K1/K2 capacity without introducing a model-specific pool subclass. - Route extend/decode allocation, rollback, request release, streaming-session cleanup, allocator reset, and pool statistics through generic no-op auxiliary-cache hooks. - Add MiniCPM model overrides and developer controls. - Default sparse SALA models to `minicpm_flashattn`, or `minicpm_flashinfer` on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Disable radix caching only for configs that actually contain sparse or Lightning layers. - Reject unsupported sparse-attention PD disaggregation early. - Add `SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSE_TOPK`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_SPLIT_STAGE1`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_DENSE_AS_SPARSE`, and `SGLANG_MINICPM_FORCE_DENSE` environment switches. - Add CPU and CUDA coverage for configuration defaults, model overrides, Lightning dispatch, compressed-cache lifecycle, sparse metadata, block-table kernels, and compression kernels. ## Accuracy Tests The following CPU regression suite passes on the final rebased branch: ```text 112 passed, 8 subtests passed ``` It covers: - MiniCPM config parsing, mixer selection, Lightning cache shape, scaling, and idle batches. - Sparse metadata construction, CUDA graph padding, and dense/sparse batch accounting. - K1/K2 allocation boundaries, reuse, rollback, cleanup, and streaming-session release. - Backend defaults, force-dense remapping, radix-cache gating, and unsupported PD disaggregation. CUDA correctness tests are included for: - v2/v3 block-table outputs against a PyTorch reference. - Sparse key compression against a PyTorch reference. End-to-end checkpoint output accuracy has not yet been recorded on the final rebased branch and should be added before merge. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/bench_get_block_table.py` benchmarks the v2 prefill and v3 decode block-table kernels across token counts. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Benchmark] Add optional steady-state window for serving metrics
signal.text: ## Motivation The serving benchmark currently calculates metrics over the entire benchmark duration. This includes the initial request ramp-up and final drain phases, where request concurrency is lower. As a result, throughput and other aggregate metrics may not accurately represent performance under sustained load. This PR adds an optional continuous steady-state measurement window and applies it consistently across serving benchmark metrics. ## Modifications - Add the `--steady-state-concurrency-ratio` option to `bench_serving`. - Define the steady-state concurrency threshold as: ```text ceil(observed peak concurrency × steady-state-concurrency-ratio) ``` The minimum steady-state concurrency is calculated as: ceil(observed peak concurrency × steady-state-concurrency-ratio) The measurement window: Starts when active request concurrency first reaches the threshold. Ends when concurrency falls below the threshold for the last time. Remains continuous, so temporary concurrency drops inside the window are retained. For example: python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --steady-state-concurrency-ratio 0.8 \ ... The accepted range is (0, 1]. ## Metrics calculated within the window When steady-state measurement is enabled: - Successful requests and request throughput use requests completed within the window. - Input token throughput uses successful requests started within the window. - Output token throughput uses output tokens generated within the window. - Total token throughput combines input and output tokens measured within the window. - TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and E2E latency statistics use requests completed within the window. - Average and peak concurrency are restricted to the window. - Peak output token throughput only uses one-second buckets inside the window. - Cache statistics use requests started within the window. - Throughput plots are restricted to the same window. Output token timestamps are reconstructed using request start time, TTFT, and ITL. Since a streaming chunk may contain multiple tokens, timestamp events are weighted using the server-reported output token count. Output metadata The benchmark output additionally reports: - Steady-state duration (s) - Steady-state min concurrency In JSONL output: - duration represents the actual metric measurement duration. - benchmark_duration preserves the complete benchmark runtime. - steady_state_duration records the steady-state window duration. - steady_state_concurrency_threshold records the calculated concurrency threshold. Backward compatibility Steady-state measurement is disabled by default. When --steady-state-concurrency-ratio is not specified, all metrics retain the original full-benchmark behavior, including: - The original measurement duration. - The original throughput calculations. - The original latency sample selection. - The original peak throughput and concurrency calculations. - The original cache statistics. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32233981401](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233981401)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32233981201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32233981201)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache] Support DCP with DSpark
signal.text: ## Motivation DCP + HiCache + DSpark is currently rejected during server argument validation. Removing that guard exposed a draft HiCache sidecar sizing bug: draft indices inherit the target cache's DCP-wide logical index space, while the draft host pool was sized from only the target's physical per-rank rows. Once L1 eviction reached the uncovered range, the draft host transfer failed with `CUDA error: invalid argument`. ## Modifications - Allow DSPARK with HiCache when `--dcp-size > 1`, while retaining the guard for other speculative algorithms. - Size full draft HiCache sidecar pools from the target host pool's logical capacity. - Apply the same logical-capacity sizing to the legacy draft HiCache path. - Add a regression test for DCP-expanded draft sidecar sizing. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on RunPod node 5 with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs using a Kimi-K3 target and RadixArk Kimi-K3 DSpark draft model, TP8/DCP8, A2A, HiCache L2, and the normal CUDA graph path. - Eviction stress test: 64 requests x 16,384 input tokens, concurrency 48. - Result: 64/64 successful; 1,048,576 input tokens and 512 output tokens processed in 52.00 seconds. - Post-run `/health_generate`: HTTP 200. - No scheduler exceptions or CUDA errors after the fix. - `test_server_args.py`: 144 passed, 15 subtests passed. - `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: 4 passed. [TODO] more advanced tests involving DeepSWE ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a capacity/correctness fix rather than a kernel-path performance change. The eviction stress test above observed approximately 20,164 input tokens/s. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No documentation change needed; this enables an existing flag combination.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32096782129](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32096782129)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32190324962](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190324962)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix ROCm VAE Conv2D fast path breaking spatial-parallel decode
signal.text: ## Motivation On ROCm, running the Wan VAE decode with spatial-shard parallel decode (`--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel`) crashes as soon as the decoding stage starts: ``` RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (39) must match the size of tensor b (43) at non-singleton dimension 3 # under torch.compile the same failure surfaces during tracing: # Attempting to broadcast a dimension of length 43 at -2! ... [1, 384, 1, 43, 160] vs [1, 384, 1, 39, 160] ``` The trigger is `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1` (equivalently `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D=1`), which enables the ROCm Conv3D→Conv2D VAE fast path. `RocmPlatform._replace_conv3d_with_conv2d` monkey-patches `forward` on every `nn.Conv3d` subclass that carries a `_padding` attribute. That predicate also matches `SpatialParallelCausalConv3d` and `SpatialParallelConv3d`, whose `_padding` intentionally carries **no height padding** — the missing rows come from the halo exchange with the neighbouring rank, and the output is trimmed afterwards. Replacing their `forward` outright discards both the halo exchange and the output trim, so every 3×3×3 conv silently loses two rows of height while the 1×1×1 `conv_shortcut` (kernel is not 3-D, so it is never patched) keeps its own. In `residual_block_forward` the two paths then disagree at `return x + h`: ``` local shard height 45 -> conv_in 43 -> conv1 41 -> conv2 39 (halo dropped) local shard height 45 -> conv_shortcut 43 (1x1x1, unpatched) => x + h ==> 39 vs 43 ``` Single-GPU decode is unaffected because plain `WanCausalConv3d._padding` does carry real height padding. `torch.compile` is not involved — the failure reproduces identically with `--enable-torch-compile false`. ## Modifications - `runtime/layers/parallel_conv.py`: add `_halo_conv_forward` to `SpatialParallelCausalConv3d` and `SpatialParallelConv3d`. It is the inner conv applied to the already halo-exchanged input, and it is the documented override point for platform fast paths. Both classes now pass `self._halo_conv_forward` to `_spatial_parallel_conv_forward` instead of `super().forward`. - `runtime/platforms/rocm.py`: for spatial-parallel convs, install the Conv2D decomposition into `_halo_conv_forward` instead of clobbering `forward`, so the halo exchange and output trim stay in place and the optimization is preserved rather than disabled. A spatial-parallel conv with no such hook, or with a non-`zeros` `padding_mode`, is now skipped rather than silently corrupted. Non-parallel `CausalConv3d` modules keep the existing `forward` patch unchanged. - `runtime/layers/parallel_conv.py`: generalize `_maybe_contiguous_for_sp_gather`. It previously only handled channels-last inputs, so the Conv2D decomposition's permuted-view output reached NCCL non-contiguous and failed with `Tensors must be contiguous` in `gather_and_trim_height`. It now materializes any non-contiguous input. - Logging now reports the two patch kinds separately: `patched N CausalConv3d + M spatial-parallel halo kernels`. ## Benchmarking and Profiling Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 720p, MI355, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1`. Before this PR, 2-GPU spatial-parallel decode does not run at all, so there is no before/after latency to compare — the table records that the failing configurations now complete. | Config | Before | After | |---|---|---| | 2 GPU CFG-parallel, eager | crash: `39` vs `43` | 7.00 s | | 2 GPU CFG-parallel, `--enable-torch-compile true` | crash during Dynamo tracing | 179.63 s (includes cold compile) | | 2 GPU CFG-parallel, 193 frames, 8 steps, torch.compile (full workload) | crash | 114.23 s end-to-end, decoding stage 4.49 s | ## Accuracy Tests Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 720p, 25 frames, 8 steps, seed 42, MI355. Frames decoded from the saved mp4 and compared pixel-wise. | Comparison | MAE | Max abs diff | PSNR | |---|---|---|---| | 1-GPU reference vs 2-GPU spatial-parallel (this PR, Conv2D fast path) | 0.9277 | 12 / 255 | 45.57 dB | | 1-GPU reference vs 2-GPU spatial-parallel (Conv3D reference path) | 0.9366 | 12 / 255 | 45.52 dB | `python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_spatial_parallel_decode.py` — 18 passed, 12 subtests passed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: perf(kimi-k3): fork side streams after the main-stream kernel, not before
signal.text: A captured decode graph was using **98 distinct GPU streams** at bs=1. Under CUDA-graph capture, the branch that enqueues its first kernel after `alt.wait_stream(cur)` keeps the main chain's graph-internal stream; a region that launches its side kernels first hands that stream away, so the main chain is assigned a fresh internal stream -- once per layer. Two sites did that, and both are fixed by moving the region's main-stream kernel above the `with torch.cuda.stream(alt)` block: * `_ep_front_overlap` -- gate + top-k on the side stream, latent down-proj on the main one * `forward_qkvbfg_fused` -- the tiny `[f_a|b]` + `f_b` GEMVs on the side stream, the wide `[q,k,v,g]` GEMM on the main one Same kernels, same dependencies, same overlap, same numerics; only the enqueue order changes. ### Measured 8xB300, tp8, `flashinfer_mxfp4`, AR fusion on, `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`, at `b5607ec5a` (before #32699 / #32764 landed): | | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | distinct GPU streams, bs=1 decode graph | 98 | **29** | | decode latency (3x2000 tokens after a warm-up run) | 8.902 ms/tok | **8.832 ms/tok** | | GSM8K 1319q | 0.955 | 0.950 | The latency runs carry no profiler and vary by +/-0.07% within a config, so the 0.8% gain is outside the noise -- 69 fewer graph-internal streams also means less scheduling work. The GSM8K difference is 6-7 questions, inside the +/-0.6pp standard error of a 1319-question run, and a statement reorder cannot change the arithmetic. The mechanism reproduces standalone in a few dozen lines: capture N fork/join diamonds and count the streams a replay reports -- side-first gives `N+2`, main-first a constant 4. ### Not in scope The remaining 29 are the MLA output-gate overlap, whose region stays open across the whole attention core. That costs one stream per MLA layer no matter how the fork is ordered (a dedicated stream, an in-place join, an event-only join, and a persistent fork were all measured at 29-30), and closing the region early gives back the streams but loses the overlap's 1.5% decode latency. Folding `g_proj` into the qkv-a GEMM the way the KDA layers already fuse `[q,k,v,gate]` would settle it; left for a follow-up. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01WQiAHF7ykPjyaJ1sfhZikw <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #30446581036](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30446581036)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #30446580784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30446580784)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(sgl-model-gateway): parse prefilled Qwen3 reasoning
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35148. When `qwen3` reasoning parsing is configured only in `sgl-model-gateway`, Qwen3.8 responses can contain a prefilled reasoning segment from the chat template. The gateway parser starts in the wrong state, so the reasoning is returned in `content` and `reasoning_content` remains null instead of separating the thinking and final answer. ## Modifications - Upgrade `reasoning-parser` from `1.0.0` to `1.3.0`. - Initialize the non-streaming parser per request, including reset and prefilled-thinking state. - Initialize each streaming parser per choice with the tokenizer's `ThinkingToggle`, `ThinkingKeyName`, and `think_in_prefill` settings. - Respect explicit `enable_thinking` / `thinking` request overrides. - Add unit regressions for Qwen3.8 prefilled `</think>` parsing in streaming and non-streaming paths. ## Accuracy Tests Added parser unit tests covering: - Qwen3 prefilled reasoning in the non-streaming path. - Qwen3 prefilled reasoning and closing `</think>` transition in the streaming path. - Thinking-toggle defaults and request-key resolution. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a reasoning-parser correctness fix and does not change an inference kernel or performance-critical model computation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32102419923](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32102419923)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32102419296](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32102419296)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [docs] Add a fused-kernels page for SGLang Diffusion
signal.text: ## Motivation Following the [`ops/diffusion` reorganization](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35114), the fused kernels that replace eager elementwise chains — adaLN modulate, residual gating, QK-norm, RoPE, norm epilogues, VAE layout kernels — have no user-facing page. The package `README.md` added in that PR is a selection matrix aimed at kernel authors, so there is nowhere to point someone who asks what is already fused, whether it changes their output, or how to turn on the parts that do. This adds that page, in the spirit of Sol-Engine's [kernel techniques](https://nvlabs.github.io/Sana/Sol-Engine/docs/techniques/kernel/) page but following this site's conventions. ## Modifications New page `docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx`, registered under **Performance Optimization** and cross-linked from the overview's output-preserving lever table. Contents: - **The two numerical contracts.** Bit-exact fusions mount unconditionally and still verify themselves against the live eager chain on first sight, falling back permanently on mismatch. Fusions that differ from eager at half-precision rounding level mount only for `quality="high"`, at batch boundaries, all-or-nothing per transformer. The page explains why the distinction is not pedantic: multi-step denoising turns a per-step rounding difference into visible quality loss. - **How to opt into the request-gated set** — `--quality high` on the CLI, and the `quality` field on the OpenAI-compatible endpoints — plus the list of families that mount. - **An inventory by operator domain** (normalization, adaLN modulation, RoPE/QK-norm, activation, attention, data movement): what each of the 34 registered operators replaces, on which backend, under which contract. - **Coverage by model**, since these kernels target a specific eager chain in a specific model rather than being general-purpose operators. - **How to query the registry** and pin a backend, and the import contract (import from the package, predicate-plus-kernel pairs, lazy resolution). Docs-only; no code changes. ## Accuracy Every table row is derived from the merged tree rather than written from memory: - the operator list, backends and capability sets come from the registry's `_SPECS` in `ops/diffusion/__init__.py` (34 operator ids across 38 implementations); - the model-coverage table comes from the actual import sites under `multimodal_gen/runtime/models`; - `--quality` and the OpenAI `quality` field were traced to `SamplingParams.quality` / `_runtime_sampling_quality` before being documented; - both Python snippets were executed against the live registry: ``` diffusion ops: 34 KernelBackend.TRITON norm.rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact:fused_scale_residual_rmsnorm_scale_shift_bitexact [CUDA] KernelBackend.CUTE_DSL norm.scale_residual_norm_cutedsl:fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift [CUDA] KernelBackend.FLYDSL norm.fused_residual_norm_flydsl:flydsl_fused_residual_norm_scale_shift [HIP] select_kernel -> KernelBackend.CUTE_DSL KernelSpec has load(): True ``` Relative links resolve to existing pages, `docs.json` parses, the page is reachable from the navigation, and headings follow the sentence-case rule in `docs/AGENTS.md`. The Mintlify CLI needs Node ≥ 20.17 and this machine has 18, so `mint broken-links` was replaced with an equivalent scripted check. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). — N/A: docs only. - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed. — N/A: docs only. - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and would like to remove yourself as a reviewer, please leave a comment with `/unassign` and click on `Re-request review`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32214261614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32214261614)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32214261534](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32214261534)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix dummy initialization of inverse weight scales
signal.text: ## Summary - Initialize floating-point `weight_scale_inv` tensors to the neutral value `1.0` when loading dummy weights. - Preserve randomized dummy initialization for regular floating-point weights. ## Problem The dummy loader randomized every floating-point tensor into a small interval around zero. Inverse weight scales must be positive, and DeepGEMM paths that convert them to UE8M0 additionally require power-of-two inputs. DSV4 FP4 expert and FP8 attention post-load processing therefore aborted in `transform_sf_into_required_layout` before the server could start. This complements #33500, which fixed serialized MXFP4 scale placeholders stored as raw integer UE8M0 bytes. The affected DSV4 paths here expose floating-point inverse scales, so the integer-placeholder fix does not cover them. ## Fix Use `1.0` for floating-point state-dict entries whose names end in `weight_scale_inv`. It is a neutral, valid inverse scale for the post-load transforms. Real checkpoint loading is unchanged. ## Validation - Full pre-commit suite passed. - A TP4 DSV4 DSpark dummy startup completed target and draft weight loading and post-processing without the DeepGEMM scale-layout assertion. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32232930988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232930988)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32232930566](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232930566)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [docs] add a ComfyUI section for every diffusion cookbook page
signal.text: ## Summary Whether a model can be driven from ComfyUI was not answerable from its cookbook page — a reader had to go read the plugin source. All 18 diffusion pages now end with a `Run in ComfyUI` section. The per-model facts live in one shared component (`docs/src/snippets/diffusion/comfyui-support.jsx`) rather than eighteen copies of prose, because they derive from a single source of truth in the plugin: a model has an integrated mode only if it appears in `executor_class_dict`. Prose per page would drift the moment the plugin gains or loses an executor. It also means changing the wording later is a one-file edit instead of eighteen. Three shapes fall out of that table: | | Server mode | Integrated mode | |---|---|---| | FLUX, Z-Image, Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit | generic image node | executor + reference workflow | | MiniMax-H3 | dedicated `SGLDiffusion Generate H3` node | not available — packed video+audio in one pass, no audio branch in KSampler | | everything else | generic image / video node | not available, stated explicitly | Only H3 is marked as run end to end against a live server; the others state the mechanism without claiming per-model verification. Enforcement so this does not rot: - `cookbook-add-model` now requires the section when adding a diffusion page. - `cookbook-review-pr` flags a missing section, inline prose instead of the component, and — the one that would actually mislead readers — a model-specific key without matching plugin support. ## Test plan - [x] Purely additive: 21 files, 236 insertions, **0 deletions**. - [x] Section number derived per page from its existing headings, so no renumbering and no broken anchors (pages end at 4, 5, 6, or 9 today). - [x] Every `model` key used resolves in the component's table; the four integrated-mode keys match `executor_class_dict` exactly (`flux`, `lumina2`, `qwen_image`, `qwen_image_edit`). - [x] Image/video classification taken from each page's own `DiffusionModelTags`, not guessed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32225195095](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225195095)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32225194878](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225194878)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signal.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash Download the tested FP4/FP8 GGUF from [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash). The benchmark used the immutable model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP4-FP8-native.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32232779018](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232779018)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32232778712](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232778712)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
