signal.title: feat(cake_vsa): add Cake Stage-2 backend for FastWan VSA
signal.text: ## Motivation FastWan's video sparse attention currently runs Stage 2 through the `vsa` package only. FlashInfer [#4593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4593) adds a Cake source backend that consumes FastWan's direct per-head top-k metadata on SM100/SM103. This PR makes that backend available as an explicit SGLang opt-in while preserving `vsa` as the default. This is a video-diffusion workload, not an LLM reasoning workload, so GSM8K is not applicable. Validation uses [`FastVideo/FastWan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastWan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers) and the VBench `subject_consistency` prompt `a person swimming in ocean`. ## Modifications - add `stage2_backend` (`vsa` or `cake`) and optional zero-based `cake_step_indices` to the existing VSA backend configuration - preserve the compressed-attention branch and pass its direct per-head `torch.topk` metadata to FlashInfer - sort selected KV block ids to preserve native VSA's traversal and BF16 accumulation order - cache the Cake wrapper and fixed `q2k_num` metadata per transformer layer - fail closed for unsupported devices, dtypes, batches, and head dimensions; selected Cake steps never silently fall back - expose the live generation duration while the generation timer context is active The validated FastWan configuration is: ```json {"VSA_sparsity": 0.8, "stage2_backend": "cake", "cake_step_indices": [1, 2]} ``` ## Accuracy NVIDIA B300, BF16, seed 42, 61 frames at 480x832, three denoising steps, guidance scale 3.0, and VSA sparsity 0.8. Applying Cake to all three denoising steps missed the conservative per-frame SSIM gate (`0.914666 < 0.92`). A four-route accuracy sweep isolated the first step, and the explicit `[1, 2]` route passed every frame without relaxing any threshold. | Check | Cake step indices `[1, 2]` | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | Frames passing all gates | 61/61 | 61/61 | | Minimum per-frame PSNR | 35.466198 dB | >= 24 dB | | Minimum per-frame SSIM | 0.978827 | >= 0.92 | | Maximum per-frame MAE | 1.635058 | <= 10 | | Final latent cosine similarity | 0.999255 | reported | | Final latent MAE | 0.018273 | reported | | Baseline repeat max error | 0 | deterministic | | Cake repeat max error | 0 | deterministic | The real-shape backend smoke also passed BF16 `atol=rtol=1e-2` with maximum absolute error `0.0009765625`, one observed Cake route, and zero generic device, host, or floating-point workspace bytes. ## Performance The full-model test alternates both `vsa, cake, cake, vsa` and `cake, vsa, vsa, cake`. Each block has one warmup and five measured requests, for 20 measured requests per backend. Both order-specific ratios are above `1.0x`; the table reports the geometric mean of the two sequence medians. No fixed overhead is added or subtracted. | FastWan 61x480x832 boundary | Native `vsa==0.0.4` | Cake `[1, 2]` | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Synchronized client generation | 1.478475 s | 1.470300 s | **1.005560x** | | Inference worker before output transport | 1225.263790 ms | 1220.807151 ms | **1.003651x** | The client boundary covers request dispatch through the synchronized response, including 61-frame materialization and transport. The worker boundary ends after model forward and before output transport; it is included to isolate the inference path from frame-return overhead. The narrower public-wrapper replay uses cold-L2 CUPTI timing and includes SGLang tiling/untile, compressed attention, dynamic top-k, Stage 2, gate fusion, and the FlashInfer wrapper call. | Near-E2E VSA workload | Native `vsa==0.0.4` | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Model-card 61x448x832, S=23,296 | 3.906334 ms | 3.799102 ms | **1.028226x** | | SGLang default 61x480x832, real/padded S=24,960/26,624 | 4.516563 ms | 4.393202 ms | **1.028080x** | ## Validation - `ruff format --check`: 4 files formatted - focused unit tests: 7 passed - real B300 FastWan shape smoke: correctness, strict Cake route, and zero generic workspaces passed - full FastWan ABBA/BAAB correctness and performance crossover: passed Depends on https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4593 and is tracked by https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32232671225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232671225)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32232670929](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32232670929)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Speculative] Fix DSpark base logits for quantized target lm_head
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving a **quantized** target model with a DSpark draft fails at startup (both eager and CUDA-graph capture) with: ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (7x5120 and 2560x248320) ``` Reproduced on `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` drafting `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (RTX 5090, sglang 0.5.17 and current main). **Root cause**: DSpark dense drafts share the target's `lm_head` (`attach_shared_modules`). When the target is quantized, `lm_head.weight` is stored in a packed layout — e.g. NVFP4 stores `[vocab, 2560]` for a 5120-hidden target (5120 × 4 bit = 2560 bytes/row, with separate per-block `weight_scale`). `compute_base_logits` performs a raw `torch.matmul(hidden, weight.T)` against the packed layout, which is invalid for any quantized packing. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/dspark.py` — `DSparkDraftMixin.compute_base_logits`: - When `weight.shape[1] != hidden.shape[-1]` (packed layout), route through `lm_head.quant_method.apply(lm_head, hidden, bias)` — mirroring `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head` so the quant method's dequantize path applies. - Raise a clear `ValueError` when the lm_head is packed but carries no applicable quant method. - Unquantized targets keep the existing dense matmul path unchanged. ## Tests New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/models/test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py` (3 cases, all passing locally): 1. packed weight routes through `quant_method.apply` (call verified via mock, returns expected logits) 2. unquantized weight still uses the dense matmul path 3. packed weight without a quant method raises `ValueError` ``` test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_packed_weight_routes_to_quant_method PASSED test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_packed_weight_without_quant_method_raises PASSED test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_unquantized_weight_uses_matmul PASSED ``` ## End-to-end validation With this patch, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` + `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` boots to `ready to roll` on an RTX 5090 (previously crashed at CUDA graph capture). Single-stream bench (random ISL 1024 / OSL 512, 20 prompts): 131.41 output tok/s, accept len 2.89/8. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32206503048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206503048)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32206502903](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206502903)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Validate MiniMax-H3 quality=high on B300
signal.text: ## 0x0. What this PR does Video generation does not need distillation, a different solver, or model surgery to get fast. Keep the weights and the math untouched, be rigorous about *computing less*, and MiniMax-H3 goes from 41.19 s to 11.16 s for a 5-second 1344x768 clip with audio on 8x B300 — with the quality argument written down, gated, and byte-reproducible. Concretely, this PR: - admits the strict 8x B300 TP1/Ulysses8 deployment for MiniMax-H3 request-scoped `quality="high"` - gives each validated deployment its own audited Cache-DiT schedule: 4xH200 keeps the conservative `(4, 0.04, 1)`; **8xB300 ships `(4, 0.08, 3)`**, selected by a parameter sweep on the sglang-native prompt set and gated on LPIPS plus a consecutive-frame temporal review - makes Sol-Attn dense guard steps use the platform-selected FlashAttention implementation (FA4 on Blackwell) and preserves packed-document boundaries on sparse steps - lets the common BCG fail-closed path run before H3 arms Cache-DiT input preservation - documents the protocol, limitations, results, and comparison figure in the cookbook ![MiniMax-H3 B300 quality and latency comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16f604256169b1e9889a3ab4f297883f3f84c15d/docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/assets/minimax-h3-b300-quality-high.png) ## 0x1. Results first Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (SM103). Workload: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA T2VA, 1344x768, 124 frames @24 fps, 50 sigma points, video/audio flow shifts 12/3, sglang-native prompts (cookbook example + two benchmark presets), seeds 0/1/2. Latency is the median of three requests after one warmup. This air-cooled node sits on its 1100 W power cap and its sustained-clock regime drifts intraday (~20% on step time), so only same-session ratios are comparable — every row below was measured back-to-back in one session: | Arm | Median latency | Speedup vs Diffusers | LPIPS mean / max vs SGLang lossless | Decision | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Diffusers BF16 dense + Ulysses8 | 41.19 s | 1.00x | 0.347 / 0.465 | baseline | | SGLang lossless | 23.03 s | 1.79x | 0.000 / 0.000 | exact default | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.04, 1) | 16.45 s | 2.50x | 0.101 / 0.129 | superseded on B300 | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.08, 3) | **11.16 s** | **3.69x** | 0.293 / 0.399 | **admitted** | The admitted path is 2.06x faster than SGLang lossless, and its LPIPS distance (0.293 / 0.399) sits below the distance that already separates the two reference implementations from each other (0.347 / 0.465). Side-by-side frames match the lossless output in content, staging, and lighting on all three prompts. ## 0x2. Where the speedup comes from The 0.08 residual threshold works as an adaptive brake: it sleeps on easy content and forces full computation the moment the trajectory drifts, leaving 21 of 49 full video-tower steps on this prompt set. The conservative 0.04 is too sensitive here (33 full steps on the same prompt, 16.45 s). The consecutive-cache cap barely binds at this threshold — cap 1 at the same threshold is strictly slower at equal quality (11.60 s, LPIPS 0.289 / 0.401) — so cap 3 is used. The schedule is deterministic: fresh server launches on the real `quality="high"` code path reproduce the audited sweep outputs byte-for-byte (md5-verified on all three prompts), so the quality gate transfers exactly to the shipped code. Measured on top of the admitted schedule but not enabled here: SubBlock sparse attention (#34148) composes with Cache-DiT and reaches 10.37 s, and passed a 6/6 production-style serving validation on six unseen prompts. Its blk64 kernel needed two separate fixes, both now proposed upstream in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4533 (open, not merged): a deterministic SM103 scheduling hang, and an intermittent CTA wedge — roughly 1 request in 25 — that turned out to be a named-barrier id collision in the kernel's correction warpgroup. With both applied, 100 consecutive requests ran clean and per-request output md5s became deterministic. That last result revises this arm's quality numbers rather than confirming them: the pre-fix kernel silently produced a differing output on roughly one request in six, so the LPIPS figures behind the 10.37 s arm were measured on a nondeterministic kernel and need re-taking before sparse can default. Latency is unaffected. NVFP4 was evaluated and rejected (LPIPS 0.53+ under the same-seed gate even MLP-only, for at most 6% latency). ## 0x3. Sweep and rejected candidates Every line below was measured, not guessed: - threshold 0.04 with cap 1 (the H200 schedule): 33 full steps, 16.45 s — superseded - wider thresholds: 0.24 never triggers the brake and reaches LPIPS max 0.596 — rejected - cache cap 4: LPIPS max 0.53+ — rejected - warmup 3: no end-to-end win, quality drops — rejected - cached audio tower: audio drift leaks into the video tower through the dual-tower bridge — rejected - TaylorSeer order 1: no measurable gain — rejected - `--minimax-h3-adaln-online` with Cache-DiT: corrupted outputs — disqualified - generic Sol-Attn on SM103: slower than dense cuDNN-SDPA — rejected - FA4 attention backend: 4-15% slower per kernel than cuDNN-SDPA at H3 shapes, end-to-end tie — not adopted ## 0x4. Quality protocol Two gates, both must pass. Gate one: frame-aligned LPIPS (AlexNet) at 1 fps against the bit-exact SGLang lossless output — LPIPS measures same-seed trajectory drift, not absolute quality, so the yardstick is stated explicitly: the two reference implementations already sit 0.347 / 0.465 apart, and drift below that line is treated as insignificant. Gate two: human review of consecutive 4 fps frames against a temporal-artifact taxonomy (flicker, coherence, boundaries, mosaic/static regions, ghosting, broken motion, major blur). ## 0x5. Reproducibility and validation - benchmark source rebased onto `41cd5a718`; Diffusers baseline `bb56997d4`, BF16 eager dense, lossless ContextParallel Ulysses8 only - `PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` -> `25 passed, 1 skipped` on the current head - pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file - fresh-launch byte-exact smoke on 8x B300: three prompts, md5 match against the audited sweep outputs, no environment overrides ## 0x6. Risk and rollback The high-quality admission stays fail-closed to the exact B300 device name/capability, topology, task, shape, schedule, flow shifts, eager mode, and native dense attention. The per-deployment schedule map only distinguishes between already-admitted profiles; H200 behavior is unchanged. Removing the B300 deployment branch restores the previous H200-only admission without touching the lossless default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31934159311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934159311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31934158406](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934158406)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [ROCm] Direct-write a8w8 bmm output to eliminate o_proj transpose copy
signal.text: This PR removes a redundant memory copy in the per-channel FP8 attention output path on AMD gfx95 (validated on MI355X with Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4). By emitting the absorbed a8w8 BMM output already in the layout the o_proj epilogue needs, the downstream `flatten` becomes a free view instead of a transpose copy, improving throughput by up to ~3.3% with no accuracy change. ## Motivation For per-channel FP8 `kv_b_proj` on gfx95, the absorbed value BMM (`batched_gemm_a8w8_a_per_token_group_prequant_w_per_batched_tensor_quant`) writes its output in `(heads, tokens, vdim)` layout (`YQ=None, transpose_bm=False`). The o_proj epilogue then runs `attn_output.transpose(0, 1).flatten(1, 2)`, where the `.transpose(0, 1)` forces a full memory copy — visible in the profile as a standalone `direct_copy_kernel bf16`. ## Change Preallocate `_bmm_buf` in `(tokens, heads, vdim)` layout and pass `YQ=_bmm_buf, transpose_bm=True` so the GEMM writes directly in the final layout. The downstream `flatten(1, 2)` is then a free view — the transpose copy is gone. This mirrors the existing uint8 / MXFP4 `_bmm_buf` fast path directly above it. No numerical change (identical values, different write layout). ## Accuracy test Results (MI355X / gfx950, Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4) **Accuracy (GSM8K)** — neutral, within run-to-run noise: Results (MI355X / gfx950, Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4) | parallel | 100 | 300 | 600 | 1200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | original | 0.951 | 0.953 | 0.942 | 0.950 | | direct_write | 0.946 | 0.947 | 0.950 | 0.951 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Throughput / GPU (tok/s)** — consistent improvement: Results (MI355X / gfx950, Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4) | Conc | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | original | 906.82 | 1491.25 | 2128.38 | 2955.05 | 3925.4 | 5048.96 | | direct_write | 936.7 | 1522.67 | 2199.21 | 2990.27 | 3989.75 | 5112.88 | | Δ | +3.30% | +2.11% | +3.33% | +1.19% | +1.64% | +1.27% | original profiling: direct_write profiling: ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [HiSparse] HiCache as the plugin logical KV pool
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> A compatible implementation of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32314. HiSparse enables high-concurrency long-context decode for Sparse Attention models. Today the KV that is *not* in that hot set can live in exactly one place — a private pinned host pool owned by the coordinator. That single choice carries two structural drawbacks: 1. **The radix cache must be off** (`--disable-radix-cache` is required), so shared-prefix and multi-turn workloads get no prefix reuse at all; 2. **The regular GPU KV pool is bypassed**, so HBM that could hold hot KV goes unused. This PR names the axis those drawbacks live on — *where a token's attention KV is while it is not in the hot working set* — and makes it a **pluggable backing** resolved from the cache configuration, so `--enable-hisparse` remains the only switch users write: | radix cache | hierarchical cache | write policy | resolved backing | |---|---|---|---| | off | – | – | `private_host` (today's behaviour, bit-for-bit) | | on | on | `write_back` | `hicache` (new) | | on | off | – | rejected at startup, naming both legal recipes | | on | on | other | rejected at startup, requires `write_back` | ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> `--enable-hisparse` off (default) is untouched; the private-host backing is behaviour-preserving. - **`managers/hisparse_protocol.py`** (new): the coordinator interface both backings answer, so call sites never learn which one they got. Paths a single backing has stay off the protocol (PD direct-to-host, DeepSeek V4, shared-index prefetch key on `coordinator.backing` and talk to the concrete class), so the protocol never grows a member with one real implementation. - **`managers/hisparse_hicache_coordinator.py`** (new): the HiCache backing. Admission (expanded indexer pages + temp device buffer, then early tree-lock release so the prefix becomes evictable), eviction application at the one controlled point between two forwards, hybrid indexer page table, swap-in, finish/retract release. - **`managers/hisparse_hicache_admission.py`** (new): the admission ledger and per-round quota. Pure integer arithmetic, no tensors, so it is unit-testable on CPU. - **`mem_cache/sparsity/factory.py`**: `HiSparseBacking` + `resolve_hisparse_backing` (pure, no torch, so startup validation can import it), the coordinator factory, and one sizing helper. - **`kernels/jit/csrc/hisparse.cuh` / `kernels/ops/kvcache/hisparse.py`**: the existing fused swap-in kernel gains two compile-time flags — a third *pass-through* source (`req_to_token >= 0` means the pool still owns the position, so emit its slot with no copy and no buffer slot) and a late-bound host base+row-stride (HiCache attaches its host tier after CUDA-graph capture, and its `page_first` rows are `layer_num` cells apart). The all-false private-host instantiation stays byte-identical. - **`layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`**: the indexer's page table becomes backing-aware (evicted prefix pages resolve to request-private expanded pages), including an in-place substitution into the graph-static buffer after the metadata kernels rebuild it. - **`mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py` / `unified_radix_cache.py`**: eviction hooks (a `NamedTuple` of two callables, not a monkey-patch), a copy-less-drop veto for data backing a live request, and the early-lock-release bookkeeping on the finish path. - **Scheduler / budget**: admission-aware future-token reservation and a quota gate that keeps a candidate queued rather than letting it run standard and pin its whole prefix on device. - **Capacity model**: `hisparse_indexer_expansion_ratio` is the single source for both the reserved memory and the allocated `index_buf_size`, so they cannot drift. For the HiCache backing the total is `2 + hicache_ratio`: one pool for the base region (a KV page id doubles as its indexer page id) plus `1 + hicache_ratio` for the expanded region, which holds a copy of every admitted prefix and is bounded by the two tiers those prefixes can live in. `1 + hicache_ratio` is the natural misreading, and it silently halves admission depth. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> DSv3.2 FP8, 4x GB200, `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 4`, `temperature=0`. - **gsm8k** (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 200 questions, parallel 64, `--temperature 0`): | shots (prompt) | Baseline | HiSparse `hicache` | |---|---|---| | 32-shot (~5K) | 0.980 | 0.980 | | 128-shot (~19K) | 0.990 | **0.995** | ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Setup: DSv3.2 FP8 (KV cache `fp8_e4m3`, auto-selected for DSA on SM10x), 4x GB200, `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 4`, `--max-total-tokens 60000`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.95`. Host budget equalized at 2x the device pool on both backings (`host_to_device_ratio: 2` / `--hicache-ratio 2`). Three numbers per workload: end-to-end output throughput (client wall clock, includes prefill), the server-reported decode-phase `gen throughput` summed over the 4 DP ranks, and the peak concurrent requests per DP rank. | Workload | Metric | Baseline | HiSparse `private_host` | HiSparse `hicache` | |---|---|---|---|---| | 32 x unique 30.8K, out 512 | output tok/s (e2e) | 139.2 | 182.1 | **217.6** | | | gen tok/s (decode, Σ4 ranks) | 227 | 399 | **563** | | | max running-req / rank | 1 | 3 | **4** | | 64 x unique 30.8K, out 1024 (working set ~9.8x pool) | output tok/s (e2e) | 168.8 | 233.0 | **309.8** | | | gen tok/s (decode, Σ4 ranks) | 223 | 394 | **557** | | | max running-req / rank | 1 | 3 | **4** | | 64 x shared 26K + unique 15K (~42K, near pool cap), out 1024 | output tok/s (e2e) | 227.1 | 182.5 | **260.4** | | | gen tok/s (decode, Σ4 ranks) | 221 | 313 | **335** | | | max running-req / rank | 2 | 2 | **3** | <details> <summary>Server launch commands</summary> Common prefix (all three configs): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <DeepSeek-V3.2, FP8> \ --tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 4 \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 --max-total-tokens 60000 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \ --moe-runner-backend triton --disable-flashinfer-autotune ``` Baseline: common prefix only. HiSparse, `private_host` backing (radix cache must be off; explicit `--max-running-requests` required — the per-request tables are sized by the req-slot count): ```bash --enable-hisparse --disable-radix-cache \ --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 2048, "device_buffer_size": 4096, "host_to_device_ratio": 2}' \ --max-running-requests 64 ``` HiSparse, `hicache` backing: ```bash --enable-hisparse \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_back --hicache-ratio 2 \ --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 2048}' \ --max-running-requests 64 ``` </details> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Feature] MXFP4 KV Cache Decode for DSV4 on Hopper
signal.text: ## Summary MXFP4 KV cache for DeepSeek V4 on Hopper (SM90/H20), end to end: codec + memory pool + fused decode attention kernel + backend integration. The decode kernel is a JIT-compiled port of the FlashMLA three-stage split-KV design (scheduler metadata kernel + persistent WGMMA main kernel + combine kernel), covering all 44 layers (SWA + C4/C128 + attn_sink) in one call. The PR is self-contained: the kernel and its vendored dependencies live under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/` and compile at first use via `load_jit` — no sgl-kernel wheel changes required. ## MXFP4 Layout (368 B/token) ``` [224 B packed E2M1 | 14 B E8M0 + 2 B pad | 128 B BF16 RoPE] ``` - E2M1 (4-bit FP: 1S+2E+1M) nope data, block-size 32 (14 groups) - E8M0 8-bit exponent-only scale per group (dequantized in-register via `bits << 23`) - BF16 RoPE (unquantized) - Row-major contiguous, no page tail padding; no global scale needed (unlike NVFP4) - 16-byte-aligned row (368 B = 16×23) enables 128-bit loads; the NVFP4 reference's 380 B is only 4-byte aligned Memory capacity gain vs FP8: ~+37% full-token capacity (bytes/token 7705 → 5609; the NVFP4 reference gains +31.75%). ## Decode Kernel (`kernels/jit/csrc/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90/`) FlashMLA-style fused split-KV decode for MXFP4: 1. **Scheduler metadata kernel** — 1 CTA × 1 thread computes per-SM split assignments with device-side length clamping (CUDA-graph safe: runs inside the captured graph, re-executes with replayed top-k lengths) 2. **Persistent main kernel** — 384 threads (3 warp groups: producer dequant→SMEM, QK+PV local, PV remote), WGMMA 64×64×16 / 64×256×16; E8M0 block-32 dequant via bit-shift, E2M1 via LUT+PRMT (4 instructions per 16 elements) 3. **Combine kernel** — merges split-K partials with PDL (programmatic dependent launch) Entry point: `entry.cuh` (TVM-FFI single translation unit, explicit instantiations for h_q 64/128). Python wrapper: `kernels/ops/attention/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90.py` (FlashMLASchedMeta, per-geometry scratch reuse, C++-side stream resolution via `TVMFFIEnvGetStream`). ### Vendored dependencies (provenance) | Component | Source | |---|---| | `params.h`, `defines.h`, `utils.h`, `flashmla_utils.h`, `kerutils/`, `combine` | FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 | | `config.h`, `dequant.h`, `layout.h`, `components/helpers.h`, splitkv skeleton | SGLang reference PR #31269 (NVFP4) | | `splitkv_mla.cuh` (MXFP4 variant), `entry.cuh` | This PR | CUTLASS/CUTE headers come from the JIT build's `extra_dependencies=["cutlass"]` (pinned cutlass @ 147f5673, matching the reference PR). `kerutils` includes were converted to relative paths during vendoring. ## Changes - **Codec** (`srt/layers/attention/dsv4/mxfp4_k_cache.py`): quantize/dequant for the 368 B row (Triton), paged variants - **Compressor** (`compressor_v2.py`): `_forward_mxfp4` covering all 44 layers (C0/C4/C128), decode-plan boundary semantics - **Memory pool**: parameterized enablement via `--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4` (env alias with deprecation warning); pool sizing/accounting unified - **Startup guards**: HiSparse + MXFP4 combination rejected at init (incompatible sparse layout); DeepseekV4 + fp4_e2m1 on non-SM90 fails fast with a clear error - **Backend** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`): `_forward_mxfp4_decode_flashmla` — one fused call per layer; scheduler metadata shared per geometry across layers, re-created during CUDA-graph capture (top-k lengths are replayed device inputs) - **Tests**: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` (17 kernel cases: C0/C4/C128 × flash/profiling geometries, graph replay + length clamping, invalid contracts, scheduler-refresh regressions) + `test_mxfp4_k_cache.py` (5 codec cases) + `test_dsv4_hisparse_pool.py` (3 pool-guard cases) + `test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (3 restored cases); benchmark in `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` - **E2E**: `test/registered/kernels/e2e/test_mxfp4_dsv4_e2e.py` — 8-GPU H200 server + gsm8k, exercising pool configurator → compressor → CUDA-graph capture (CI stage extra-b) - Removed the first-generation standalone JIT kernel (`mxfp4_decode.cuh` + `_forward_mxfp4_decode`) superseded by the FlashMLA port ## Validation - Kernel SASS was byte-identical to the AOT (cmake) build of the same sources at port time; the subsequent refactors (V32 path removal, aligned 128-bit row loads) are instruction-level changes covered by the same unit suite - Unit: 28/28 kernel + codec + pool-guard tests pass; 8-GPU e2e integration test passes locally - End-to-end on 8×H20 (TP8, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), FP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) vs MXFP4 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4`), identical server flags otherwise: | Metric | FP8 baseline | MXFP4 (this PR) | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | Decode throughput (server-side, 4k×256, conc 32) | 1013 tok/s | 980 tok/s | −3.3% | | GSM8K (1319, greedy, max_tokens 1024; truncated samples excluded) | 96.89% | 96.89% | 0.0pt | | AIME25 (480 = 30×16, greedy, max_tokens 32768; 73 truncated samples excluded from both) | 99.57% pass@1 | 99.78% pass@1 | +0.2pt | ## Known gaps / follow-ups - Small-batch (b≤8) kernel-level latency vs FP8: +8–12% (kernel-inherent scheduling granularity; end-to-end TPOT already within 5%) - Prefill-path throughput: −6.8% vs FP8 (out of scope for this PR; triton-based MXFP4 prefill) - Deep-context + high-concurrency decode (64 concurrent, 8k ctx, no rolling prefill): decode TPOT +17% vs FP8 (33.1 vs 28.3 ms); end-to-end 8k→8k throughput on par (1677 vs 1652 tok/s). One full AIME25 eval run showed −44% throughput vs FP8, but four controlled reruns (5-question replica, rolling short-prompt, 8k×8k fixed) could not reproduce it and measured MXFP4 at parity or faster — attributed to environment, not the kernel. - sm_90a-only (Hopper); no SM100 support (non-SM90 + fp4_e2m1 is rejected at startup) - HiSparse (sparse KV cache) not supported with MXFP4 — rejected at startup ## References - PR #31269 — NVFP4 KV cache for DSV4 in sgl-kernel (reference implementation for the FlashMLA three-stage decode) - FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 — scheduler/combine kernels and kerutils - This PR takes the jit_kernel approach (JIT CUDA via TVM-FFI) instead of AOT CUTLASS in sgl-kernel, keeping the PR self-contained --- **Status**: Ready for review — kernel + integration complete, end-to-end validated on 8×H20. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32231903565](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231903565)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32231903211](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231903211)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] support distributed inference pipeline for GLM-Image
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds GLM-Image distributed serving: the public head batches external AR generation and dispatches each AR-complete request to an independent batch-1 denoiser that runs request preparation, DiT, and VAE decoding. ## Modifications - Add GLM-Image distributed mode for a head configured with `--srt-encoder-url` and `--denoiser-urls`, with encoder and decoder URL lists omitted. - Group compatible text-to-image requests by resolution and send one batched `/generate` call to the external AR server. Batch capacity is measured in output slots, consistent with #30683. - Run the blocking external AR request on a dedicated executor so AR generation overlaps with active denoiser work. - Assign generated prior tokens and usage to each request, then dispatch AR-complete requests across connected denoisers with one active request per worker. - Run glyph/text preparation, sequential batch-1 DiT inference, and VAE decoding on each distributed denoiser. `num_outputs_per_prompt > 1` is processed sequentially and regrouped into the original response. - Transfer only request metadata and CPU prior-token IDs over ZMQ; this mode bypasses Mooncake/RDMA and does not transfer latent or embedding tensors. - Return each completed request immediately to the head, which preserves client ordering, seeds, output paths, output saving, and image URL registration. - Track denoiser connectivity, stop dispatching to disconnected workers, and reclaim request state and worker capacity after timeouts. - Preserve the existing encoder ? denoiser ? decoder disaggregation path when GLM distributed mode is not enabled. - Validate per-role TP/SP/CFG/DP device requirements and disable only auto-enabled CFG parallelism when incompatible with the worker device count. - Document the topology, deployment commands, limitations, and measured NVIDIA and Ascend results. ## Deployment ### Run 14 independent Cache-DiT denoisers The denoisers keep DiT weights resident on NPU to avoid CPU-to-NPU weight transfers; this requires sufficient device memory. ~~~bash #!/bin/bash DISAGG_SERVER="tcp://127.0.0.1:19655" MODEL_PATH="zai-org/GLM-Image" BASE_MASTER_PORT=29005 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true worker_pids=() cleanup() { trap - EXIT if ((${#worker_pids[@]})); then kill "${worker_pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true wait "${worker_pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true fi } trap cleanup EXIT trap 'exit 130' INT trap 'exit 143' TERM for i in $(seq 2 15); do scheduler_port=$((19001 + i)) master_port=$((BASE_MASTER_PORT + i)) sglang serve \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --disagg-role denoiser \ --disagg-server-addr "$DISAGG_SERVER" \ --srt-encoder-url http://127.0.0.1:30020 \ --scheduler-port "$scheduler_port" \ --master-port "$master_port" \ --num-gpus 1 \ --base-gpu-id "$i" \ --denoiser-sp 1 \ --cfg-parallel-size 1 \ --batching-max-size 1 \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --attention-backend fa & worker_pids+=("$!") done # Stop all denoisers if any worker exits or fails during startup. wait -n "${worker_pids[@]}" ~~~ ### Run the AR server ~~~bash sglang serve \ --model-path zai-org/GLM-Image/vision_language_encoder/ \ --tokenizer-path zai-org/GLM-Image/processor/ \ --enable-multimodal \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 28 \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --disable-fast-image-processor \ --tp-size 2 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30020 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 ~~~ ### Run the public head ~~~bash sglang serve \ --model-path zai-org/GLM-Image \ --disagg-role server \ --srt-encoder-url http://127.0.0.1:30020 \ --srt-encoder-timeout 300 \ --denoiser-urls "tcp://127.0.0.1:19003;tcp://127.0.0.1:19004;tcp://127.0.0.1:19005;tcp://127.0.0.1:19006;tcp://127.0.0.1:19007;tcp://127.0.0.1:19008;tcp://127.0.0.1:19009;tcp://127.0.0.1:19010;tcp://127.0.0.1:19011;tcp://127.0.0.1:19012;tcp://127.0.0.1:19013;tcp://127.0.0.1:19014;tcp://127.0.0.1:19015;tcp://127.0.0.1:19016" \ --batching-mode dynamic \ --batching-max-size 28 \ --batching-delay-ms 30 \ --enable-batching-metrics \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30052 \ --scheduler-port 19655 \ --output-path ./outputs ~~~ ### Run the benchmark Tested on [longtext-bench.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29779516/longtext-bench.zip). ~~~bash python fetch_images.py \ --base-url http://localhost:30052/v1 \ --model GLM-Image-distributed-test \ --output-dir generated_images \ --max-concurrency 56 ~~~ ## Limitations - GLM distributed mode is text-to-image only; non-string prompts and image-conditioned requests are rejected. - In-flight jobs are not replayed if a denoiser disconnects. - Distributed-denoiser `RequestMetrics` are not propagated back to the head; median request E2E latency and peak memory below are reconstructed from server logs. ## Results All runs use 1280?1280 output, 30 denoising steps, and Cache-DiT. Configurations are ordered from lowest to highest throughput. The tables retain the sustained-throughput and batch-relative latency values from the original performance summary. Median request E2E latency and peak memory are reconstructed from server logs after excluding the initial BS2 warm-up where applicable. Median request E2E is measured from request arrival. Batch-relative latency is measured from batch/AR dispatch and excludes pre-dispatch waiting; for non-batched configurations, it is approximately the request latency. ### 8-GPU NVIDIA comparison | Metric | No Batch + No External AR *(baseline)* | No Batch + External AR | Monolithic Batch (8 GPUs) + External AR | Disaggregated (7 denoisers) + External AR | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Sustained throughput (img/s)** | **0.018** | **0.09** | **0.24** | **0.37** | | **Throughput improvement (baseline = 1)** | **1.0** | **5.0** | **13.3** | **20.6** | | Median request E2E latency (s) | 55.22 | 10.83 | 134.30 | 72.07 | | Batch-relative latency (s) | ~56 | ~11 | ~80 | ~55 | | Latency improvement | 1.0 | **5.1** | *0.7* | ~1.0 | | Peak GPU memory (MB) | 46,698 | 27,296 | 27,982 | 28,046 per denoiser | - Using these sustained-throughput values, seven-denoiser disaggregation is 1.54 faster than monolithic batching and 20.6 faster than the local-AR baseline. ### 16-NPU Ascend comparison | Metric | No Batch + Local AR *(baseline)* | No Batch + External AR | Monolithic Batch (28) + External AR | Disaggregated (7 denoisers) + External AR | Disaggregated (14 denoisers) + External AR | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Sustained throughput (img/s)** | **0.0087** | **0.0435** | **0.20** | **0.41** | **0.74** | | **Throughput improvement (baseline = 1)** | **1.00** | **5.0** | **23.0** | **47.1** | **85.1** | | Median request E2E latency (s) | 122.18 | 22.96 | 141.82 | 69.57 | 73.56 | | Batch-relative latency (s) | ~115 | ~23 | ~90 | ~52 | ~37 | | Latency improvement | 1.00 | **5.0** | 1.28 | 2.2 | **3.1** | | Peak NPU memory (MB) | 48,228 | 28,302 | 28,332 | 28,316 per denoiser | 28,566 per denoiser | - Using these sustained-throughput values, 14-denoiser disaggregation is 3.70 faster than monolithic batching, 1.80 faster than seven-denoiser disaggregation, and 85.1 faster than the local-AR baseline. - The 14-denoiser request E2E latency range is 57.25-129.25 s; median request E2E latency is 73.56 s. ### Methodology - The initial BS2 client warm-up is excluded from every affected median request E2E calculation. - Sustained throughput and batch-relative latency values are retained from the original performance summary. - For batched configurations, batch-relative latency is measured from batch/AR dispatch; median request E2E is measured from request arrival and includes pre-dispatch waiting. - Incomplete trailing BS28 groups are excluded from server-log latency calculations. - Peak memory is the runtime-reported diffusion process or denoiser value; it is not aggregate cluster memory. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-style). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Responses] Fix multimodal Kimi-K3 /v1/responses returning 400 "texts cannot be empty"
signal.text: …mpty' <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation A `/v1/responses` request against a **multimodal Kimi-K3** deployment fails immediately: ```json {"error":{"message":"texts cannot be empty and tokenizer must be initialized","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":400}} ``` The equivalent /v1/chat/completions request with the same messages and tools works, so the bug is specific to the /v1/responses path for multimodal Kimi-K3. ## Why The kimi_k3 custom encoder produces a usable prompt_ids (via apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, ...)) but leaves prompt == "" — the only prompt = decode(prompt_ids) assignment lives in the prompt_ids is None branch, which kimi_k3 never enters. OpenAIServingResponses._make_request forwarded that empty prompt as text on the multimodal branch, producing GenerateReqInput(text=""). In TokenizerManager.generate_request, input_ids is None and input_text is empty, so control reaches _tokenize_texts(""), which raises the error above. serving_chat._convert_to_internal_request already special-cases this (elif is_multimodal and self.chat_encoding_spec == "kimi_k3": prompt_kwargs = {"input_ids": ...}); the responses path was missing the same guard. A text-only Kimi-K3 deployment (is_multimodal == False) takes the else branch and uses prompt_ids, so it is unaffected — which is why the bug only surfaces for multimodal Kimi-K3. Fixes #35460 ## Modifications - python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py: - test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py: add ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel or model-forward change; this only fixes which prompt field the responses path hands to the engine. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32231404454](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231404454)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32231403957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231403957)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix M-RoPE positions when an extend reaches past the precomputed mm table
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35482. A continuation of a held request (a session extension via `session_params: {id, rid}`) can have an extend window that reaches past the mm input's precomputed `mrope_positions` table. The extend branch of `ForwardBatch._compute_mrope_positions` sliced that table without checking coverage: a partially covered window silently truncated to the overlapping columns, producing a wrong-width `(3, N)` position tensor that crashes the whole engine in the batch loader (`torch._foreach_copy_` size mismatch, all TP schedulers exit). The `numel() == 0` guard only caught the fully uncovered case, and its fallback returned a single-column tensor for a multi-token extend, which hits the same crash. Instrumented crash batch on Qwen3.8-27B (tp4, BF16), text-only session continuation: ``` extend_lens=[50] prefix_lens=[896] -> sliced mrope width (3, 2) copy mismatch dst=(3, 50) src=(3, 2) RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (50) must match the size of tensor b (2) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` On GDN hybrids the window is widened further because the continuation resumes from the last mamba state checkpoint (`prefix_lens` snaps down to a multiple of `mamba_track_interval`), making the overrun easy to hit, but the defect is reachable by any M-RoPE model served with sessions. We reproduced the engine death 6/6 times across native and streaming session modes, with and without prefill CUDA graphs, with multimodal and text-only continuations. ## Modifications In the extend branch, when the sliced window is narrower than `extend_seq_len`, fill the uncovered span with sequential positions continuing from `mrope_position_delta`, the same rule the decode path applies. The span past the table is text after the last mm item, for which sequential positions are the correct M-RoPE assignment. This replaces the `numel() == 0` fallback and covers the fully uncovered case with correct width. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on the reproduction pod (Qwen3.8-27B, tp4, BF16, 32k context): - The 6/6-fatal reproduction now completes: the rid-chained continuation answers correctly (turn 2 "Say one word." -> "Book", stop matched `<|im_end|>`). - Two 16-turn multimodal session conversations (one native, one streaming mode), growing to 26 images, completed with coherent, history-aware answers: turn 5 correctly recalls the book cover shown at turn 1, turn 12 retrieves content from the start of the conversation, turn 14 summarizes the full browse. This checks that the filled-in positions are semantically right, not merely shape-compatible. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Session-continuation TTFT on the fixed build stays flat with depth: 16 turns growing 2 -> 26 images, TTFT 212ms (turn 1) -> 178ms (turn 16, ~24k resident tokens) in native session mode, 181 -> 176ms in streaming mode. The identical conversation served statelessly on the same pod rises to 440ms (radix-cached) / 1259ms (uncached tail layout) at turn 16. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Happy to add a unit test for `_compute_mrope_positions` partial coverage if maintainers can point at the preferred harness for `ForwardBatch`-level tests. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32231303625](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231303625)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32231303546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231303546)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Make HiSparse's logical KV pool a pluggable backing, and add the HiCa…
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> A compatible implementation of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32314. HiSparse enables high-concurrency long-context decode for Sparse Attention models. Today the KV that is *not* in that hot set can live in exactly one place — a private pinned host pool owned by the coordinator. That single choice carries two structural drawbacks: 1. **The radix cache must be off** (`--disable-radix-cache` is required), so shared-prefix and multi-turn workloads get no prefix reuse at all; 2. **The regular GPU KV pool is bypassed**, so HBM that could hold hot KV goes unused. This PR names the axis those drawbacks live on — *where a token's attention KV is while it is not in the hot working set* — and makes it a **pluggable backing** resolved from the cache configuration, so `--enable-hisparse` remains the only switch users write: | radix cache | hierarchical cache | write policy | resolved backing | |---|---|---|---| | off | – | – | `private_host` (today's behaviour, bit-for-bit) | | on | on | `write_back` | `hicache` (new) | | on | off | – | rejected at startup, naming both legal recipes | | on | on | other | rejected at startup, requires `write_back` | ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> `--enable-hisparse` off (default) is untouched; the private-host backing is behaviour-preserving. - **`managers/hisparse_protocol.py`** (new): the coordinator interface both backings answer, so call sites never learn which one they got. Paths a single backing has stay off the protocol (PD direct-to-host, DeepSeek V4, shared-index prefetch key on `coordinator.backing` and talk to the concrete class), so the protocol never grows a member with one real implementation. - **`managers/hisparse_hicache_coordinator.py`** (new): the HiCache backing. Admission (expanded indexer pages + temp device buffer, then early tree-lock release so the prefix becomes evictable), eviction application at the one controlled point between two forwards, hybrid indexer page table, swap-in, finish/retract release. - **`managers/hisparse_hicache_admission.py`** (new): the admission ledger and per-round quota. Pure integer arithmetic, no tensors, so it is unit-testable on CPU. - **`mem_cache/sparsity/factory.py`**: `HiSparseBacking` + `resolve_hisparse_backing` (pure, no torch, so startup validation can import it), the coordinator factory, and one sizing helper. - **`kernels/jit/csrc/hisparse.cuh` / `kernels/ops/kvcache/hisparse.py`**: the existing fused swap-in kernel gains two compile-time flags — a third *pass-through* source (`req_to_token >= 0` means the pool still owns the position, so emit its slot with no copy and no buffer slot) and a late-bound host base+row-stride (HiCache attaches its host tier after CUDA-graph capture, and its `page_first` rows are `layer_num` cells apart). The all-false private-host instantiation stays byte-identical. - **`layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`**: the indexer's page table becomes backing-aware (evicted prefix pages resolve to request-private expanded pages), including an in-place substitution into the graph-static buffer after the metadata kernels rebuild it. - **`mem_cache/unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py` / `unified_radix_cache.py`**: eviction hooks (a `NamedTuple` of two callables, not a monkey-patch), a copy-less-drop veto for data backing a live request, and the early-lock-release bookkeeping on the finish path. - **Scheduler / budget**: admission-aware future-token reservation and a quota gate that keeps a candidate queued rather than letting it run standard and pin its whole prefix on device. - **Capacity model**: `hisparse_indexer_expansion_ratio` is the single source for both the reserved memory and the allocated `index_buf_size`, so they cannot drift. For the HiCache backing the total is `2 + hicache_ratio`: one pool for the base region (a KV page id doubles as its indexer page id) plus `1 + hicache_ratio` for the expanded region, which holds a copy of every admitted prefix and is bounded by the two tiers those prefixes can live in. `1 + hicache_ratio` is the natural misreading, and it silently halves admission depth. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> DSv3.2 FP8, 4x GB200, `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 4`, `temperature=0`. - **gsm8k** (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 200 questions, parallel 64, `--temperature 0`): | shots (prompt) | Baseline | HiSparse `hicache` | |---|---|---| | 32-shot (~5K) | 0.980 | 0.980 | | 128-shot (~19K) | 0.990 | **0.995** | ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Setup: DSv3.2 FP8 (KV cache `fp8_e4m3`, auto-selected for DSA on SM10x), 4x GB200, `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 4`, `--max-total-tokens 60000`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.95`. Host budget equalized at 2x the device pool on both backings (`host_to_device_ratio: 2` / `--hicache-ratio 2`). Three numbers per workload: end-to-end output throughput (client wall clock, includes prefill), the server-reported decode-phase `gen throughput` summed over the 4 DP ranks, and the peak concurrent requests per DP rank. | Workload | Metric | Baseline | HiSparse `private_host` | HiSparse `hicache` | |---|---|---|---|---| | 32 x unique 30.8K, out 512 | output tok/s (e2e) | 139.2 | 182.1 | **217.6** | | | gen tok/s (decode, Σ4 ranks) | 227 | 399 | **563** | | | max running-req / rank | 1 | 3 | **4** | | 64 x unique 30.8K, out 1024 (working set ~9.8x pool) | output tok/s (e2e) | 168.8 | 233.0 | **309.8** | | | gen tok/s (decode, Σ4 ranks) | 223 | 394 | **557** | | | max running-req / rank | 1 | 3 | **4** | | 64 x shared 26K + unique 15K (~42K, near pool cap), out 1024 | output tok/s (e2e) | 227.1 | 182.5 | **260.4** | | | gen tok/s (decode, Σ4 ranks) | 221 | 313 | **335** | | | max running-req / rank | 2 | 2 | **3** | <details> <summary>Server launch commands</summary> Common prefix (all three configs): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <DeepSeek-V3.2, FP8> \ --tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 4 \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 --max-total-tokens 60000 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \ --moe-runner-backend triton --disable-flashinfer-autotune ``` Baseline: common prefix only. HiSparse, `private_host` backing (radix cache must be off; explicit `--max-running-requests` required — the per-request tables are sized by the req-slot count): ```bash --enable-hisparse --disable-radix-cache \ --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 2048, "device_buffer_size": 4096, "host_to_device_ratio": 2}' \ --max-running-requests 64 ``` HiSparse, `hicache` backing: ```bash --enable-hisparse \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_back --hicache-ratio 2 \ --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 2048}' \ --max-running-requests 64 ``` </details> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bug] Session continuation crashes the engine on M-RoPE models: unguarded partial slice of the mm-input M-RoPE position table
signal.text:
## Summary Extending a session (`/generate` with `session_params: {id, rid}`) on a Qwen3.5-family model kills the whole engine on the second request. The scheduler process raises inside the static buffer loader: ``` File ".../model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py", line 52, in _foreach_copy torch._foreach_copy_(group_dsts, group_srcs) RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1842) must match the size of tensor b (1816) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` All TP schedulers exit (`Scheduler hit an exception` -> SIGQUIT -> `kill_process_tree`), taking every in-flight request down with them. ## Reproduction matrix (4/4 crash) | session mode | prefill CUDA graphs | second request | result | |---|---|---|---| | native | on (default) | text + 2 images | engine dies | | streaming (`--enable-streaming-session`) | on | text + 2 images | engine dies | | native | `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` | text + 2 images | engine dies (same copy, via `eager_runner.load_batch`) | | native | off | **text only** | engine dies | The text-only reproduction rules out multimodal payloads; the eager reproduction rules out the CUDA-graph runners (the failing copy is the shared `cuda_graph_buffer_registry.fill_from`, used by the eager path too). Turn 1 through the session path works normally. Plain stateless traffic on the same pod is completely healthy (we ran 48-request multimodal ladders up to 26 images / 23.6k tokens with the mamba radix cache giving correct prefix reuse). ## Setup - Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid GDN + full-attention, M-RoPE) - sglang 0.5.17 (image `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` pulled 2026-08-18), BF16, tp 4, `--context-length 32768`, `--trust-remote-code` ## Minimal reproduction Run against a server started with `--enable-streaming-session` (or without; native sessions crash identically). One image on turn 1, a text-only rid-chained turn 2, and the engine dies: ```python import base64, json, urllib.request BASE = "http://localhost:30000" def post(path, body): req = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}{path}", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) def gen(sid, rid, text, images=None): sp = {"id": sid} if rid is None else {"id": sid, "rid": rid} body = {"text": text, "session_params": sp, "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 30, "stop": ["<|im_end|>"]}, "stream": True} if images: body["image_data"] = images final, meta = "", {} with post("/generate", body) as r: for raw in r: line = raw.decode().strip() if not line.startswith("data:") or line[5:].strip() == "[DONE]": continue ch = json.loads(line[5:].strip()) final = ch.get("text", final) meta = ch.get("meta_info", meta) return final, meta img = "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(open("any.jpg", "rb").read()).decode() sid = json.loads(post("/open_session", {"capacity_of_str_len": 262144}).read()) t1 = ("<|im_start|>user
<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>What is this?<|im_end|>
" "<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

") reply, meta = gen(sid, None, t1, [img]) print("turn 1 ok:", reply[:40]) t2 = ("<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
Say one word.<|im_end|>
" "<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

") gen(sid, meta["id"], t2) # engine dies here; subsequent requests get connection refused ``` ## Diagnosis (instrumented, root cause confirmed) The failing tensor is `ForwardBatch.mrope_positions`. We instrumented `_grouped_foreach_copy_` and `_compute_mrope_positions` on the repro pod and caught the crash batch directly. Text-only continuation of a session whose turn 1 carried one image: ``` [XA-DEBUG] mrope extend_lens=[50] prefix_lens=[896] widths=[(3, 2)] [XA-DEBUG] copy mismatch dst=(3, 50) src=(3, 2) dtype=torch.int64 RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (50) must match the size of tensor b (2) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` The mechanism is in `ForwardBatch._compute_mrope_positions` (extend branch): ```python mrope_positions = mm_input.mrope_positions[ :, extend_prefix_len : extend_prefix_len + extend_seq_len ] if mrope_positions.numel() == 0: mrope_positions = self._expand_mrope_from_input(...) ``` For a session continuation, `mm_input` is the session's original multimodal input, whose precomputed `mrope_positions` table covers only the original prompt (~898 columns here). The continuation's extend window `[896 : 896+50]` runs past the end of that table, and the slice **silently truncates** to the 2 overlapping columns. The `numel() == 0` guard only catches the fully-out-of-range case; a partially-out-of-range window sails through as a wrong-width tensor and explodes in the batch loader, killing the engine. The multimodal variant (turn 2 adds 2 new images, delta = 1816 tokens) is the same misalignment, with a hybrid-model amplifier visible in the logged numbers: ``` [XA-DEBUG] mrope extend_lens=[1843] prefix_lens=[1792] widths=[(3, 1816)] [XA-DEBUG] copy mismatch dst=(3, 1843) src=(3, 1816) dtype=torch.int64 ``` `prefix_lens` snapped down to 1792 = 7 x 256 (`mamba_track_interval`): on a GDN hybrid the continuation resumes from the last mamba state checkpoint, which widens the extend window past the raw delta. The M-RoPE table ends at column 3608, so the slice `[:, 1792 : 1792 + 1843]` truncates to 1816 columns against an 1843-token extend. The checkpoint snap-down makes hybrids especially prone to the overrun, but the unguarded partial slice is the root defect and is reachable by any M-RoPE model served with sessions. Models without M-RoPE never take this path, which matches production experience: the identical session protocol (including rewind) has served a gemma-4 pod for weeks without issue. The bug is the intersection sessions x M-RoPE models, not sessions in general. ## Suggested fix shape In the extend branch, treat a partially-covered window the same as an uncovered one: when `mm_input.mrope_positions.shape[1] < extend_prefix_len + extend_seq_len`, recompute positions for the uncovered span (sequential positions continuing from `mrope_position_delta`, as the existing fallback does) instead of slicing short. Alternatively, extend the session's mm-input position table at continuation enqueue. We have a live repro pod and can validate a patch and follow up with a PR. Secondary observation, likely worth its own issue: a per-request accounting error inside the scheduler takes down the entire engine rather than failing the request.

signal.title: [speculative] Support DFlash speculative decoding under PD disaggregation
signal.text: ## Motivation DFlash speculative decoding does not engage on the decode side under PD disaggregation. Before this change, `SpeculativeAlgorithm.build_disagg_draft_input()` handles EAGLE and DSpark but has no DFLASH branch. For DFLASH it returns `None`, so `decode_schedule_batch_mixin.py` takes the non-speculative fallback: `spec_info` is not assigned, the last target token is relayed through the non-speculative path, and DFlash draft decoding never starts. No explicit error is raised. Thanks to @moehanabi for identifying this issue in #28390 and proposing the original fix direction. ## Changes - Add the missing `is_dflash()` dispatch to `SpeculativeAlgorithm.build_disagg_draft_input()`. - Reuse the existing upstream `build_dflash_family_disagg_draft_input()` helper unchanged. - Add a registered 2-GPU PD accuracy test with prefill on GPU 0 and decode on GPU 1. - Use Llama-3.1-8B and its matching DFlash draft for the registered GSM8K test. - Set `SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1` on both PD sides because the draft checkpoint has a shorter configured context length than the target checkpoint. The runtime change is intentionally limited to the missing DFLASH dispatch. ## Validation ### Static checks The current diff passed: - Python compilation - Black - isort - `git diff --check` ### Current-head 4P+4D PD smoke test The current PR source was used for a local 4P+4D PD smoke test without modifying any PR source files. The test configuration was: - Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and a matching DFlash draft - Prefill TP=4 - Decode TP=4 - Mooncake/RDMA transfer - DFlash block size 8 - Greedy and non-greedy sampling - Sequential and 16-way concurrent requests | Check | Result | |---|---:| | Greedy sequential request | 1/1 | | Non-greedy sequential request | 1/1 | | Greedy concurrent requests | 16/16 | | Non-greedy concurrent requests | 16/16 | | Total requests | 34/34 | | Router health | HTTP 200 | | Prefill health | HTTP 200 | | Decode health | HTTP 200 | | Bootstrap health | HTTP 200 | The decode log reported: ```text accept len: 2.31 accept rate: 0.19 #transfer-req: 5 cuda graph: True ``` This confirms that the decode side constructed DFlash draft input, DFlash speculative decoding engaged instead of taking the non-speculative fallback, PD transfer was active, and CUDA Graph execution remained enabled. No `KVTransferError`, Mooncake failure, NCCL timeout/error, CUDA error, watchdog failure, rank exit, traceback, or segmentation fault was observed. ### Registered-test configuration The registered test uses one prefill GPU and one decode GPU with Llama-3.1-8B and its matching DFlash draft. In an earlier local 200-example GSM8K run, this configuration scored: | Configuration | GSM8K score | Time | |---|---:|---:| | Llama-3.1-8B + DFlash, 1P1D | 0.77 | 103s | This is above the registered-test threshold of 0.74. ### Earlier accuracy evidence Before the latest branch update, an additional 80-example GPQA-diamond comparison was run with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and a matching DFlash draft using `max_tokens=8192`, `temperature=0`, and 16 client threads. | Setup | GPQA | Output tok/s | Wall time | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Single-node, no speculative decoding | 0.750 | 1324 | 339.1s | | Single-node, MTP | 0.750 | 1227 | 375.5s | | Single-node, DFlash | 0.7625 | 1364 | 339.5s | | Two-node PD, DFlash | 0.738 | 1344 | 330.4s | The PD result differs from the non-speculative single-node reference by one answer out of 80. This sample is too small to establish an accuracy regression, and no measurable loss was observed in this run. `KVTransferError` remained zero throughout the 80-question evaluation. The observed PD output throughput was approximately 1.5% lower than the single-node DFlash reference. This is a single comparison rather than a repeated performance benchmark, so it should not be interpreted as a precise performance estimate. ## Scope This PR only adds the missing DFLASH dispatch for PD decode and its registered coverage. It does not change: - DFlash acceptance logic - Speculative sampling behavior - KV-transfer implementation - TP synchronization - The shared DFlash PD input-construction helper ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the contribution guide. - [x] Add registered GPU test coverage. - [x] Provide accuracy and runtime validation results. - [ ] Run the registered GitHub GPU test after the `run-ci` label is added. - [ ] Update documentation if requested by maintainers.

signal.title: [diffusion][model] Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting
signal.text:
# Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting ## Motivation The initial LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B port covered text-to-video. The released checkpoint also ships refiner weights and supports image-to-video and text-to-image, so a deployment today exercises only part of what the model can do. This PR closes that gap. Related issue: #32336 Upstream PR: #32341 ## Design One pipeline serves every task. `task_type` becomes `TI2V`, which makes the input image optional, so the request decides: `image_path` gives image-to-video, omitting it gives text-to-video, `num_frames=1` gives a still. The checkpoint leaves little choice here — `model_index.json` declares a single pipeline class and the registry resolves a single config, so a second class would be unreachable without an extra CLI flag on every image-to-video request. Conditioning uses the frame twice: as visual context for the Qwen3-VL encoder, and as a clean latent pinned to the head of the diffusion latent and rewritten after every scheduler step. The DiT forward signature is untouched. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. It loads from the checkpoint's `refiner/` subfolder by redirecting only the weight path, so the component keeps its `transformer_2` identity and still resolves the transformer loader. Its second pass rebuilds text conditioning without vision tokens because the refiner DiT has no image-conditioning path, drives both posterior samples and the noise draw from one seeded generator, and rejects single-frame requests. Prompt rewriting runs as a stage against an externally served vision language model over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, rather than pulling another 27B model into the diffusion worker. Set `rewriter_url` and free-text prompts get expanded and mapped to JSON in two turns; structured captions pass through untouched, and leaving the URL unset skips the stage. ## Verification Checked against the reference diffusers implementation on the same hardware, checkpoint, seed, and parameters. Cross-GPU comparison is not meaningful for this model — identical code and seed on an H100 and a 5090 produce visibly different motion — so every comparison below is same-hardware. ### Prompts and inputs The DiT consumes a structured JSON caption rather than a plain sentence, so the prompt below is the caption itself. Every run in this section uses seed 42 and the same caption for its task, so a reviewer can reproduce any clip from the served model. ```bash sglang serve --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b --num-gpus 1 ```

They are running towards the camera, which tracks backward to maintain their position in the frame. The background features a blurred cityscape and a bridge over a river, creating a sense of depth and urban vitality. The atmosphere is energetic and futuristic, blending organic nature with advanced technology.", "camera_movement_description": "The camera executes a smooth, continuous backward tracking shot, moving parallel to the subjects' forward motion to keep them centered in the frame. There is a subtle, rhythmic vertical bobbing motion synchronized with the cadence of the runners' footsteps, adding a visceral sense of speed and physical exertion. the rewriter expands it and maps it to the structured form before denoising. | Task | Prompt | | --- | --- | | T2V | a red fox trotting through fresh snow at dawn, breath visible in the cold air | | TI2V | the two runners speed up dramatically, petals swirling behind them | | T2I | a glass of iced tea on a windowsill, afternoon sunlight | T2V https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c847d6a1-0b45-46f1-be56-e052b8c51b08 TI2V https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eba3ab2-57de-4129-9a0d-e79d5024aeef T2I Unit tests: ``` python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lingbot_video_moe.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_lingbot_video_moe_i2v.py ``` ## Inference speed Seed 42, 40 base steps, guidance_scale 3.0, flow shift 3.0, fps 24, structured JSON captions. Every sglang number is the second or later run of that task on a resident server, so autotune is warm; for scale, a cold first request costs 0.890 s/step against a warm 0.700 for T2V on H100. sglang numbers are per-stage wall time from the server log. Reference numbers come from its own denoising-loop timer and exclude text encoding and VAE decode. Base pass, 320x192, 121 frames: | Runtime | Hardware | s/step | Denoise | Decode | Text encode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang T2V | H100 80GB | 0.700 | 28.0 s | 0.96 s | 0.13 s | | sglang TI2V | H100 80GB | 0.705 | 28.2 s | 0.96 s | 0.19 s | | reference T2V | H100 80GB | 0.95 | 38 s | -- | -- | | reference TI2V | H100 80GB | 0.95 | 38 s | -- | -- | | sglang T2V | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.96 s | 0.12 s | | sglang TI2V | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.97 s | 0.19 s | Text to image, 832x480, single frame: | Runtime | Hardware | s/step | Denoise | Decode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang | H100 80GB | 0.198 | 7.9 s | 0.06 s | | reference | H100 80GB | 0.30 | 12 s | -- | | sglang | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.22 s | Across 16 requests all three tasks land on the same 2.122 s/step on the 5090, because layerwise offload streams the whole DiT from host memory every step and the loop is bound by that transfer rather than by sequence length: a single 832x480 frame carries 1560 tokens against 7440 for the 121-frame clip and still costs the same. On H100 without offload the three tasks separate as expected, 0.700 / 0.705 / 0.198. Refiner, 49 frames, 8 refiner steps, t_thresh 0.85, sigma tail 2: | Runtime | Hardware | Refiner res | Base denoise | Upscale | Refine s/step | Refine total | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang | H100 80GB, offload | 1920x1088 | 87.2 s | 5.8 s | 20.18 | 163.2 s | | sglang | 5090 32GB, offload | 640x384 | 86.5 s | 1.2 s | 2.17 | 17.6 s | | reference | H100 80GB, 8-way FSDP | 1920x1088 | 121 s | -- | -- | 210 s | Both sglang refiner rows keep layerwise offload on so the two DiTs share one card, which is why their base denoise sits near the 5090 figure rather than the 28 s an H100 reaches without offload. Refiner cost then tracks the refiner resolution rather than the hardware: 1920x1088 is 8.5x the pixels of 640x384 and costs 9.3x per step. Image conditioning, condition frame preprocessing plus a single-frame VAE encode: | Hardware | Resolution | Time | | --- | --- | --- | | H100 80GB | 320x192 | 0.30 s | | 5090 32GB | 320x192 | 0.02 s to 0.06 s | | 5090 32GB | 832x480 | 0.22 s | --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32230061210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32230061210) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32230060988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32230060988)
