signal.title: [diffusion][Model] Support MAGI-2-preview
signal.text: ## Motivation Relate #35011 Adds native support for [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview), SandAI's 114B MoE model that generates a video and its synchronized stereo soundtrack in one denoising trajectory. About 6B parameters are active per token. Audio is not a second pass over finished video: video and audio latents share one packed sequence and one denoise loop. Text-to-video and image+text-to-video are both supported. The checkpoint ships two DiTs. A preview model denoises the clip, and a refiner then takes that result to 1920x1088; the words "preview" and "refiner" below always mean those two. Serving it today means standing up a second stack. The reference implementation launches under `torchrun`, depends on SandAI's own kernels ([MagiAttention](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiAttention), [MagiCompiler](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiCompiler), FlashAttention 3) and so ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview), and its checkpoint has no `model_index.json`. This PR builds it against SGLang's own layers so it is served like every other family in `sglang.multimodal_gen`. ## Modifications ### New code Four pieces the tree did not already have. Everything else goes through existing machinery. - **Multi-head MoE** (`runtime/layers/moe_multihead.py`). MAGI-2 routes 12 independent heads over 256 experts each, top-6, where the tree's MoE assumes one routing head. Viewing tokens as `[N * 12, 256]` instead of `[N, 12, 256]` makes it a standard MoE with `hidden_size=256` and `num_experts=3072`, so srt's Triton `fused_experts` runs unmodified. A rank owns `(12 / ep_size) * 256` of those, and `moe_align_block_size` runs 1024 threads while indexing `prefix[num_experts]`, so anything past 1023 takes an illegal memory access; the experts run in balanced head chunks that fit, which is one call at `ep_size >= 4` and is what lets 1, 2 and 3 work at all. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and `gemm1_clamp_limit`. - **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed through, along with `window_size`. - **Block-window local attention** (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. The same mask is also expressed as token-range pairs for MagiAttention's `flex_flash_attn_func`, which is used when that package is importable and is 1.78x faster on the refiner's shape; without it the `flex_attention` path runs unchanged. - **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288, mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly stochastic. ### Reused from the tree Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them: - **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them. - **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. `ep_size` defaults to the world size and can be set below it through `--pipeline-config-path`, which is how 8 ranks run. - **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work without model-specific code. - `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts. ### Structure Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`. Two orderings matter and are easy to break in review: Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs **after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis, and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding. The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile, residency and warmup still come from the base stage. ### Parallelism `--num-gpus` must divide every Ulysses head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA key/value heads. The preview's 12 MoE heads are sharded by `ep_size` instead and are checked against that. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2, 4 or 8 and preview-only also admits 3, 6 and 12. All four axes are checked in `validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a collective. 8 GPUs divides every Ulysses axis but not the preview's 12 MoE heads, so it needs an explicit `ep_size` of 4: two expert-parallel groups of 4 ranks, each holding all 12 heads. The reference instead pads the head axis to 16 and gives the spare ranks zero-weight experts; this PR needs no padding and leaves no rank idle. `--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance. Expert parallelism is also what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. Below 4 ranks the expert weights need `--dit-layerwise-offload` to fit at all. ### Deliberate divergences from the reference Both are marked at the site in the code. **The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length, which the two-stage tier does not have to spare. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the rotary. **Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, and is not needed: an `ep_size` below the world size reaches 8 ranks without it, as described under Parallelism. ### Docs `docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility matrix. ### Known limitations - Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise. 1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16. - 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration. - `--enable-torch-compile` must be paired with `--regional-compile`. On its own it compiles the whole transformer, and inductor autotuning then fails on the multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`). With `--regional-compile` the expert GEMMs stay out of the compiled region and both DiTs compile per block. Compile is also rank-count dependent: it pays at 4 ranks and loses at 8, where the preview pass measures 335s compiled against 184s eager. - 1 GPU passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview DiT, which casts the whole state dict to the device before layerwise offload can take over. - 2 GPUs needs `--dit-layerwise-offload`; the expert weights are 217 GB. - `ep_size` has no CLI flag, so the 8-rank launch needs `--pipeline-config-path` with `{"ep_size": 4}`. - `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below. - FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded. - The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is unset. ## Accuracy Tests ### Side-by-side with the reference implementation Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording. **Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the climax. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67 **Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the conditioning image. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d **Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at his feet — plus its conditioning still. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964 The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. This PR runs SGLang's own attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate divergences. The clips are the thing to look at. ### Prompt coverage Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English: - Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe - Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20 - Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38 - Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc - Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e - 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9 - Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b - Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23 All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps, 249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the lake clip is continuous and low-frequency. ### Unit tests 59 unit tests, 51 of which need no GPU: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder, packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in, sequence bucketing, the expert-axis sharding predicate, and which submodules the regional-compile conditions select. The remaining 8 need CUDA and are skipped without it: the mHC mixing kernel against an FP32 reference, and the block-window mask against a dense `scaled_dot_product_attention` reference. They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up and they run in the existing suite with no CI change: ``` python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit ``` The full 1080p path needs at least two cards and minutes per clip, so it is not in the suite. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative comparisons, not as sizing targets. They are eager-mode figures; the compiled configuration and the comparison against the reference are in Benchmark below. **One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:** text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under 0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to encode — and measures 741s. **Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat, which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in the host page cache. **Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses 124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer, so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup rather than left for a user to discover. **Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text + reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where the first three share a prompt length: - rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s - using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, since dynamo guards a captured int by value and would recompile per prompt length even at a fixed shape. `dynamic=True` is not an alternative; it costs 26s per clip. ## Benchmark Same box, same weights, same seed 42, same 1920x1088 two-stage tier at 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, 4 ranks on each side. This PR runs `--enable-torch-compile --regional-compile`. Nine clips per side, discarding each process's first clip while its graphs are still building. One clip is 249 frames at 25 fps — just under 10 seconds of 1920x1088 video with its synchronized stereo audio, generated together in one denoising trajectory. 10 seconds is the only duration the model was trained for, so the figures below do not scale with a requested length. Weight loading is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. | | reference | this PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | preview denoise (100 steps) | 277.7s | 286.6s | | refiner denoise (5 steps) | 46.1s | 41.9s | | decode (video and audio) | 8.9s | 7.8s | | **one clip, end to end** | **344.9s** | **349.3s** | **At 4 ranks this PR is 1.3% slower** — 4.4s on a 345s clip, which is larger than the spread between runs. The refiner and the decode are faster; preview denoise is 8.9s slower and is where the difference sits. Stage times do not sum to the end-to-end row on either side, because the two implementations synchronize at different points, so the end-to-end row is the one to compare. ### Across topologies Same clip, same seed, each column at that rank count's best configuration. Two steady clips per arm on one 8-GPU box, so this is a narrower measurement than the nine-clip table above; the 4-rank column reproduces its 349.3s within the noise floor, which is what makes the columns comparable: | | 2 ranks | 4 ranks | 8 ranks | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `ep_size` | 2 | 4 (default) | 4 | | compile | regional | regional | **none** | | offload | layerwise | none | none | | preview denoise (100 steps) | 590.4s | 286.9s | 183.9s | | refiner denoise (5 steps) | 79.4s | 41.3s | 31.6s | | decode (video and audio) | 7.1s | 8.8s | 12.2s | | **one clip, end to end** | **689.0s** | **348.2s** | **253.5s** | | peak memory | 132208 MiB | 85274 MiB | 126572 MiB | | GPU-seconds per clip | 1378 | 1393 | 2028 | 8 ranks is 1.37x faster per clip and spends 46% more GPU-time to get there, so it buys latency rather than throughput, and two concurrent 4-rank deployments beat one 8-rank deployment on total output. 2 and 4 ranks cost the same GPU-seconds, so the 2-rank arm trades latency for hardware at no efficiency loss. Decode moves the wrong way with rank count, so every latency gain comes from denoise. The 8-rank arm runs eager deliberately: compiled, its preview pass measures 335.4s against 183.9s, which is the only configuration in this PR where `--regional-compile` is a loss. 1 rank passes validation but runs out of memory while loading the preview DiT. The reference was not re-run at 8 ranks, so none of these are head-to-head; its published 8-rank timings use head padding and a different step budget. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bugfix] Kimi-K3: fix vision-DP rank-local indexing into global grid_thws_host
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving Kimi-K3 with vision-DP sharding (observed on `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8` with DSPARK speculative decoding, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`), the first `/v1/chat/completions` request that carries **two or more images with different geometries** kills the scheduler: ``` ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids ``` The request returns 500 and the server never recovers — every subsequent request fails until the container is restarted. Single-image requests, and multi-image requests whose images share one NaViT grid, are unaffected — which is how this survives typical smoke tests. ## Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`, `materialize_item_features(image_indices)` receives the **global** image indices assigned to this vision-DP rank, but the deferred-preprocessing block indexes `grid_thws_host` — a global tensor with one row per image in the batch — with the rank-**local** enumerate positions: ```python expected_grids = grid_thws_host[indices] # local idx into global tensor ... patch_counts = [int(grid_thws_host[index].prod().item()) for index in indices] # same bug ``` On any rank whose assigned images are not the global prefix `[0..k)`, the expected grids and patch split counts are read from the wrong rows. If the wrongly-read row happens to hold a different grid, the `torch.equal` sanity check fires and raises, taking the scheduler down. (The non-DP path passes `list(range(len(items)))`, where local == global, so it never triggers.) ## Fix Translate the local enumerate positions through the closure's `image_indices` before indexing `grid_thws_host`, in both the expected-grid comparison and the `patch_counts` split. No numeric effect on correct batches — the check now compares each produced grid against the row it was actually produced from. ## Accuracy Tests Deterministic repro: one chat completion with two images, 504×504 and 1344×756 (different NaViT grids), against a TP8/DCP8 B300 deployment. - **Before:** request returns 500, scheduler dead (`/health` times out until restart) — reproduced 2/2. - **After:** request returns 200 (14.8s cold) with a correct description of both images; `/health` stays 200; subsequent multimodal and text traffic unaffected. Model outputs for previously-working requests are unchanged: the patch only affects index bookkeeping inside a validation check, not any computed feature. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — two list-indexing expressions inside the deferred-preprocessing validation branch; no hot-path change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black/codespell clean; ruff `F401,F821,UP037` and isort report zero *new* findings vs the base revision of this file) - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (The fixed code is a closure inside `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`'s image-feature path, so it cannot be exercised without constructing the model; the failure mode — call sites passing rank-local indices — is only reachable under multi-GPU vision-DP. Validated with the deterministic E2E repro above instead. There is currently no registered NVIDIA K3 e2e suite to extend (`test_kimi_k25.py` uses `kimi_k25.py`, not this file); if maintainers want a registered regression, I'm happy to contribute an `8-gpu-models` K3 case that sends one two-image heterogeneous-grid chat completion and asserts the server survives — pending confirmation the CI runners can host K3 weights.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## CI First-time external contribution from a fork, so I cannot initiate CI myself — could a maintainer or authorized contributor kick it off with `/tag-and-rerun-ci`? I'll follow up with `/rerun-failed-ci` on any flaky stages after that. Happy to address review feedback quickly. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32229955738](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32229955738)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32229955253](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32229955253)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CI] Trim the base-c 4-gpu-h100 stage from 5 shards to 4
signal.text: `base-c-test-4-gpu-h100` runs its shards serially (`max_parallel = 5 // 3 = 1`), so cutting `est_time` is a linear wall-clock win. **5470s / 16 files -> 3572s / 13 files, 5 shards -> 3.** Nothing is dropped from CI. Most of it is placement: several tests sat on the 4-GPU runner without needing four GPUs. - `test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` -> `base-b`/`1-gpu-small`, dropping its `4-gpu-b200` and `4-gpu-gb300` registrations. Collectives are faked and every arch branch is `patch.object`-mocked, so the three runners ran identical mocks. - `test_hicache_storage_3fs_backend.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Max `--tp-size` is 2 and both configs are H100. - `test_disaggregation_unified_memory.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Its two classes are prefill tp1 on GPU 0 plus decode at `decode_base_gpu_id=1`, i.e. two GPUs; the two classes left in `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py` need three (prefill tp2/pp2 plus `decode_base_gpu_id=2`). The shared parity base class stays in the latter and is imported. Four PD tests already run on `2-gpu-large` with the same `PDDisaggregationServerBase` fixture. - `test_pp_gemma4.py` (new) -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`, taking `TestGemma4PPAccuracy` and `TestGemma4PLEPPAccuracy` out of `test_pp_single_node.py`. Both are tp1/pp2; the four classes left behind are tp2/pp2. Both already carry `@unittest.skipIf(is_in_amd_ci())`, so no AMD registration moves. - The two `*AllocFail` classes and three DeepEP crossings move to new `*_extra.py` files on `extra-b`. Dead code removed (594 lines, no CI time since none of it ran): - `test_deepep_small.py::TestNoGatherdBuffer`, skipped as "covered in test_deepep_large.py" -- verified: `test_deepep_large.py::TestDeepseek` runs the same dp-attention + DeepEP + `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` + `--enable-dp-lm-head` combination. - `test_deepep_small.py::TestMTP`, skipped as "covered in TestMTPWithTBO". That claim was inaccurate -- it is tp4/dp2 while `TestMTPWithTBO` is tp4/dp4 -- so removing it does drop the dp2 + MTP combination rather than a duplicate. - `test/registered/rl/test_release_memory_occupation.py`, carrying `disabled="Temporarily disabled - needs investigation"` since 2026-05-26. Nothing imports it, and the sibling `test_multi_instance_release_memory_occupation.py` is self-contained. All moved classes keep their bodies byte-for-byte; the only edit is renaming the PD parity base class so it can be imported. `base-b-test-2-gpu-large` absorbs the three moves at 6701s -> 8121s, which raises it from 5 shards to 7 and its `max_parallel` from 1 to 2, cutting its serial waves from 5 to 4. `base-b-test-1-gpu-small` stays at 8 shards. Reviewer note: the DeepEP split takes **attention-TP + TBO off the per-commit path**; every other dimension there keeps a representative. The two new `2-gpu-large` `est_time` values (900s, 220s) are estimates split from the parent files -- the live partition model will correct them. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208152940](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208152940)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208152857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208152857)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Question: unit mismatch in evict_from_tree_cache for SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator?
signal.text: ## Potential Issue Looking at the current main branch code in `common.py`: ```python # common.py evict_from_tree_cache if isinstance(allocator, SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator): full_available_size = allocator.full_available_size() # ← what unit? swa_available_size = allocator.swa_available_size() if full_available_size < num_tokens or swa_available_size < num_tokens: full_num_tokens = max(0, num_tokens - full_available_size) swa_num_tokens = max(0, num_tokens - swa_available_size) tree_cache.evict( EvictParams(num_tokens=full_num_tokens, swa_num_tokens=swa_num_tokens) ) ``` `full_available_size()` for DSA (DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool -> Hisparse allocator -> SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator) eventually calls `self.full_attn_allocator.available_size()` which returns `self.free_slots.numel()` — the number of free **pages** (slots) in the C4 pool. However, `num_tokens` from the callers (`alloc_token_slots` -> `batch.extend_num_tokens`) appears to be in **tokens**. For DSA models, the C4 pool has ~4096 physical pages. Each page stores multiple compressed tokens. Even when the C4 allocator reports ~4000 free pages, a prefill batch requesting e.g. 3000 tokens would see `4000 < 3000 = False` — and Full eviction would never trigger. For non-DSA models with smaller `page_size` (e.g. 16), the unit mismatch is less severe because pages and tokens are closer in magnitude, which might explain why this hasn't been noticed before. ## Question Is `full_available_size()` intended to return pages or tokens? Should `num_tokens` be divided by `page_size` before comparison, or should `full_available_size()` be multiplied by `page_size`? Or are we misunderstanding the DSA allocator architecture? Any clarification would be greatly appreciated. Happy to submit a PR if this is indeed a mismatch. ## Environment - SGLang version: v0.5.x - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash - TP=8, H100, page_size=64, max_total_tokens=16384

signal.title: feat(mamba): add strict FlashInfer SSD and Cake prefill backends
signal.text: ## Summary - add strict opt-in `flashinfer_ssd` and `cake` Mamba SSD prefill backends while preserving the existing `flashinfer` default - project Nemotron-H logical C256 metadata onto the physical C128 domain supported by both source-level SSDCombined backends - preserve unified Mamba radix caching by inserting logical checkpoint boundaries into packed metadata and storing compact Cake checkpoint states in the main prefill pass - consume Cake checkpoints directly when resuming cached suffixes; retain replay only for the original CuTe route - keep backend routing strict: selecting Cake never falls back to Triton or CuTe ## Radix-cache correctness The packed-boundary unit case uses sequence lengths `[72, 312]` with an absolute checkpoint at token 200. Same-backend split-prefix/suffix output and final-state parity passes, and Cake checkpoint state agrees with the original CuTe prefix at BF16 `atol=rtol=1e-2` with maximum absolute error `0.015625`. `nvidia/Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K` revision `20acad0a529d386e3c7115b8635d482f9023e1b9`, BF16, TP2, 2x GB300, full GSM8K test set (1,319 questions), 8 train-set CoT exemplars, greedy decoding, 512 output-token cap, last-number exact match. Dataset SHA256: `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. | Cache-on run | Backend | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Matched run | Existing `flashinfer` | 785 / 1,319 | 59.5148% | 0 | | Matched run | Original `flashinfer_ssd` / CuTe | 770 / 1,319 | 58.3776% | 1 | | Matched run | Cake | 751 / 1,319 | 56.9371% | 0 | | Independent repeat | Cake | 766 / 1,319 | 58.0743% | 0 | Before checkpoint support, the cache-on CuTe and Cake routes each scored 92 / 1,319 (6.9750%). The repaired Cake repeat is within 4 questions (0.3033 percentage points) of the matched CuTe run and is consistent with the prior cache-off Cake result of 762 / 1,319 (57.7710%). Server state confirms `disable_radix_cache=False`, `uses_mamba_radix_cache=True`, and the unified Mamba cache pool; there is no Cake replay or fallback path. ## Performance Three-run medians after warmup and cache flush, fixed token counts; every reported Cake row is faster: | Baseline | Workload | Baseline | Cake | Speedup | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Existing `flashinfer` | TTFT, input 4096 / output 1 / concurrency 1 | 50.717 ms | 37.159 ms | 1.3648x | | Existing `flashinfer` | Total throughput, input 2048 / output 8 / concurrency 16 | 84,140.9 tok/s | 126,098.0 tok/s | 1.4987x | | Original `flashinfer_ssd` | TTFT, input 4096 / output 1 / concurrency 1 | 40.640 ms | 37.159 ms | 1.0937x | | Original `flashinfer_ssd` | Total throughput, input 2048 / output 8 / concurrency 16 | 121,311.7 tok/s | 126,098.0 tok/s | 1.0395x | The new routes remain opt-in because the established production route still has the highest matched-run task accuracy. This PR restores radix-cache safety; it does not change the default backend. Depends on https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4576 and is tracked by https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254.
signal.author: yyihuang

signal.title: [SM120] DeepSeek-V4: DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer +FP4 MoE+ page-split
signal.text: **Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x. It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend. ## Split out of this PR Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have their own PRs: - #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix) - #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent) **This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once it lands. The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread 0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to reproduce them as written. ## What is in it 1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. 2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer. 3. **Page-split dirty mask** — `_split_kv_pages_to_64` re-laid out the whole SWA KV pool (~105 MB/layer) every decode step; now only the pages this step's top-k references are split (CUDA-graph safe, bit-identical). 4. **DeepGEMM FP4 MoE on SM120** — probe the block-scale entry point (DeepGEMM#324) instead of hard-disabling DeepGEMM at `sm==120`, plus the contiguous grouped-GEMM prefill path, the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant fix, and the swiglu-clamp fallback for TP>=2 shapes. 5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory request from the device budget instead of a fixed 128 KB. Non-SM120 architectures are unchanged: every behavioural change is either gated on `is_sm120_supported()` or is a fix that only engages where the previous code was wrong (the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant and the shared-memory cap). ## E2E benefit "main" is marlin MoE + the torch paged-MQA fallback, because that is the only SM120 path on `14bd315d` that starts: the default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` + TileLang indexer) dies in the TileLang JIT for `sm_120a` (TileLang ships nvcc 13.3, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` has CUDA 13.0 headers), and `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` raises `AttributeError: module 'sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper' has no attribute 'get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor'` (SM120 disables `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` while the runner stays selectable). Both sides then run identical server args, only the tree differs: TP4, marlin MoE, CUTLASS FP8, chunked prefill 8192, `--disable-radix-cache`, and no speculative decoding except where the tables say otherwise. 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, OSL 256, `--warmup-requests 0` so every measured request is a real prefill. TTFT is a median. **Single request (BS=1)** — 3 sequential requests, median. TTFT: | ISL | main | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | 8K | 1124 ms | 899 ms | −20% | | 32K | 4540 ms | 3585 ms | −21% | | 128K | 20107 ms | 15481 ms | −23% | TPOT, without and with MTP-2 (EAGLE, 2 steps / 3 draft tokens) on both sides: | ISL | main | this PR | | main + MTP-2 | this PR + MTP-2 | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8K | 36.1 ms | 10.5 ms | **3.4x** | 13.6 ms | 6.0 ms | 2.3x | | 32K | 35.8 ms | 10.7 ms | **3.3x** | 12.6 ms | 5.7 ms | 2.2x | | 128K | 36.1 ms | 11.9 ms | **3.0x** | 13.4 ms | 6.8 ms | 2.0x | Accepted length is within 0.2 of each other on the two sides at every context length, so the MTP gain comes from the decode path itself, not from better speculation. **Concurrent (ISL 8K)** — `--num-prompts BS --max-concurrency BS`: | BS | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | | output tok/s main | output tok/s this PR | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 3574 ms | 2826 ms | −21% | 42.9 ms | 16.8 ms | 2.6x | 71 | 147 | | 8 | 5660 ms | 4530 ms | −20% | 51.9 ms | 24.3 ms | 2.1x | 108 | 191 | | 16 | 10482 ms | 8365 ms | −20% | 71.6 ms | 40.9 ms | 1.8x | 143 | 219 | TTFT holds at −20% across batch sizes; the decode multiple decays with batch (3.4x at BS1, 1.8x at BS16) because what this PR removes is per-step fixed cost, which amortises as the batch grows. Speculative decoding amortises it the same way. GSM8K (50 questions) is 0.980 on main and 0.960 on this PR at 8K — one question apart. All tables are without prefill context parallelism, which is upstream code this PR does not touch. <details> <summary>Recipes</summary> Common to both: `--fp8-gemm-backend cutlass --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32`, plus `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. **Prefill-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`. **Decode-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. </details> ## Dependencies - FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (SM120 sparse-MLA kernels) and sglang-kernel 0.4.5 — both are what `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` currently ships. - DeepGEMM at or after deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#324 for the FP4 MoE backend. The `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` indexer path additionally needs DeepGEMM's attention host-gates to accept SM120 (a 3-line arch gate, not yet upstream in sgl-project/DeepGEMM); without it, keep the TileLang indexer default. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant.py` (9 cases, registered for CI) covers the fused swiglu-clamp + silu_mul + fp8-quant kernel against a reference. GSM8K numbers are from `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`. Reviewed and validated with @ormandj (conflict resolution) and @moxcat (inference-mode buffer fix, now #35116) on 2x and 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Re-validated after the split on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (the pinned version), this tree plus #35116: GSM8K-50 1.000 with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, 0.960 with MTP-2; ISL 8K BS1 TTFT 116/88 ms, TPOT 12.8/7.3 ms. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32228739222](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32228739222)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32228738944](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32228738944)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Scale the req_to_token row headroom by attn_dcp_size
signal.text: Under DCP the allocator is built with `page_size * attn_dcp_size` (`_build_token_to_kv_pool_allocator`), and a row is rounded up by the allocator's page -- but the headroom was sized from the scheduled page size alone, so near the context limit the rounded write lands in the neighbor row. `attn_dcp_size` is 1 without DCP, so nothing changes there. Stacks on #35401. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32220549165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32220549165)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32220548927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32220548927)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Pass Anthropic thinking history as reasoning_content for custom chat encoders
signal.text: ## Motivation Run Kimi-K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` and talk to it on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` on. Any agentic client sends assistant `thinking` blocks back in history — the Messages API requires it for tool-use turns — and a few turns in, raw XTML channel markers show up in visible assistant text: ``` turn 3 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|<|sep|>Something is very strange. […]' turn 4 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|' ``` Turns 1-2 are fine, then every turn after that is corrupted — it never recovers. Drop the `thinking` blocks from the replayed history and it never happens at all, so the problem is how prior reasoning gets fed back, not the reasoning parser. **Root cause.** K3 ships no Jinja chat template, so SGLang renders it through the checkpoint's own XTML encoder. That encoder frames the `think` / `response` / `tools` channels itself and wants prior reasoning in an assistant `reasoning_content` field. The Anthropic adapter never used it — instead it wrapped prior thinking in the reasoning detector's markers and spliced that into assistant **content**. Here is what the two forms actually render to, straight from the K3 tokenizer: ``` # before — think channel empty, reasoning nested inside the response channel <|open|>think<|sep|><|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR <|close|>think<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> # after <|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> ``` Every replayed turn taught the model the same lesson: think channel empty, think block sitting inside the response channel. Two turns of that and it starts writing `<|open|>think<|sep|>` as ordinary response text. None of this is K3-specific. All four Python chat encoders that bypass `apply_chat_template` frame their own reasoning channel and read `reasoning_content`, so the splice was wrong for every one of them. ## Modifications - **`entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`** — adds `spec_owns_reasoning_history(spec)`, right under `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` so the contract sits with the specs it describes. It covers the whole custom-encoder family (`spec is not None`) rather than listing specs, so whoever adds the fifth one gets the safe default for free. An encoder that ignores the field drops history — what the splice path already does for models with no reasoning detector — instead of leaking. - **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`** — `supports_native_reasoning_history()`, a one-line delegate. - **`entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`** — `_convert_assistant_thinking_blocks` now returns `(reasoning_content, text)`. Custom encoders get the history in the field, everyone else keeps the splice untouched. `redacted_thinking` still raises before the branch, and the best-effort drop for detector-less models survives. Nothing needed a schema change: `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` already declared `reasoning_content`, and messages are dumped without `exclude_none`, so it flows straight through. `wrap_reasoning_history` has exactly one production caller, so that is the whole mechanism. `dsv4`/`dsv32` also land on their official multi-turn contract now instead of bypassing it. Jinja-path models stay on the splice on purpose — their markers (`<think>`, `[THINK]`, `◁think▷`) really do live in the content stream, so it reproduces what the model emitted anyway. ## Test Plan ### Live server Same deployment before and after — `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on 2x4 GB300, TP8, DSPARK spec-decode — same scripts, `temperature=0`: | run | main | with the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | 12-turn tool loop, streaming `/v1/messages` | leaks turns 3-12, all ten of them | clean, and the loop converges at turn 9 | | 8-turn tool loop, non-streaming | leaks turns 3-8 | clean | | 6 concurrent sessions x 5 turns | all six leak, every one first at turn 3 | none leak | | thinking dropped from replayed history | clean | clean | | `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | clean | clean | | reasoning passed as `reasoning_content` on `/v1/chat/completions` | clean | clean | | thinking-only history turn, and a turn with two thinking blocks | clean | clean | | `redacted_thinking` history | 400 | 400 | On main the onset is turn 3 every single time, and it never recovers — the `thinking` block stops appearing at all from there on and the markers move into `text`. That is also why the loop never converges: each turn re-reads its own corrupted history and re-diagnoses the same phantom problem. With the fix, `thinking` comes back on essentially every turn and the model finishes the task. Asked what it had just been thinking, the model quoted the injected reasoning back — the history really does land in the think channel rather than being quietly dropped. Prompt rendering was also diffed against the real K3 tokenizer for a thinking + text + tool_use turn. ### Unit tests `anthropic/test_serving.py` — 61/61. Two new cases: history reaches a channel-framing encoder as `reasoning_content` and never through the wrap path, and a thinking-only turn keeps its reasoning across the empty-content placeholder branch. Both go red against pre-fix code, and the existing wrap-path test still covers the default encoder. `openai/test_serving_chat.py` — 111/111. Two more: the real `OpenAIServingChat` predicate across all four specs plus `None`, and a guard that parses the literals `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` can return and checks them against the tuple the capability test iterates. Add an encoder without classifying it and CI fails. Mutation-checked, so it is not passing vacuously. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32228328048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32228328048)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32228327601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32228327601)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: bound FlashInfer DeepSeek routing shapes
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang's `fused_topk_deepseek` dispatch guard admitted grouped shapes outside the executable FlashInfer NoAuxTc boundary. Those shapes can fail in the native backend instead of using SGLang's generic Triton grouped router. This also provides a safe integration boundary for the Cake backend in [FlashInfer #4587](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4587), tracked by [FlashInfer #4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254). ## Modifications - Centralize the FlashInfer DeepSeek router shape predicate. - Preserve the existing power-of-two expert policy and source API top-k/group constraint. - Match the executable grouped boundary: `G<=8`, `topk_group<=4`, `E<=256`, `2<=E/G<=32`, and `(E/G)*topk_group<=128`. - Route valid out-of-contract grouped shapes to the existing Triton fallback. - Add accepted/rejected boundary tests and fail-closed GPU fallback tests. ## Accuracy Tests NVIDIA B200, SM100, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0: ```bash python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_topk_deepseek.py ``` Result: `146 passed` in 29.86s. The file covers the in-contract FlashInfer/Cake route and verifies three legal out-of-contract grouped shapes against the PyTorch reference while monkeypatching FlashInfer to fail if called. A 24-layer synthetic DeepSeek-V3 service run exercised the production `E=256, G=8, topk_group=4, topk=8` route in baseline/Cake/Cake/baseline order. Three correctness cases with input lengths 7, 31, and 127 produced exact output token IDs and output log probabilities within `atol=1e-4`. A fail-closed route observer recorded `selected_backend=default` for both baseline arms and `selected_backend=cake` for both candidate arms. Evidence SHA256: `55d673ec330854143ddd57e21bce681d158a7e49b4cbf2332f893d953604957c`. A real DeepSeek-V3-0324 run at revision `e9b33add` used four GB300s, TP4/EP4, and default/Cake/Cake/default order. Each arm evaluated the same 200 official GSM8K test questions with the fixed five-shot prompt, temperature 0, and zero invalid answers. Both default runs scored 193/200 (96.5%); both Cake runs scored 191/200 (95.5%). The paired two-question difference is not statistically significant (two-sided exact McNemar p=0.754 and 0.727 for the two Cake arms versus the first default arm), but exact generated-text parity is not claimed for this FP8 full-model run. ```bash python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --backend srt --data-path <official-test.jsonl> \ --num-shots 5 --num-questions 200 --max-new-tokens 512 \ --temperature 0 --top-p 1 --parallel 16 ``` The fail-closed CUDA observer captured only `deepseek_v3_topk_kernel` in both default arms and only `kernel_cake_deepseek_routing_grouped_k8g4_f32_f32` in both Cake arms. The separate launch audit returned exact expert IDs and routing weights within `atol=rtol=1e-4` in every arm. Evidence SHA256: `ad36974732243993c6d84a2a8ee3430b6e21e87979abaddefcc8b55eea33fc16`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The B200 synthetic service run used two warmups and five measured requests per server (10 samples per arm after ABBA aggregation). The full-model operation mix dominates the microsecond router, so small client-wall variations are reported rather than filtered out. | Workload | Client wall / throughput | E2E latency | TTFT | TPOT | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | decode b1, I256/O64 | 0.9970x | 0.9969x | 0.9882x | 1.0012x | | decode b16, I256/O64 | 1.0001x | 0.9957x | 1.0107x | 1.0022x | | decode b64, I128/O32 | 0.9972x | 1.0255x | 1.0136x | 1.0956x | The real-model serving arm used 128 fixed 512-input/128-output requests at concurrency 16: ```bash python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 \ --random-range-ratio 1 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 16 --seed 42 ``` | Real DeepSeek-V3 GB300 metric | Default median | Cake median | Cake speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | GSM8K wall latency | 275.259 s | 283.131 s | 0.9722x | | GSM8K output throughput | 71.734 token/s | 71.115 token/s | 0.9914x | | Serving request throughput | 0.54063 req/s | 0.54117 req/s | 1.0010x | | Serving output throughput | 69.2005 token/s | 69.2693 token/s | 1.0010x | | Mean E2E latency | 28045.81 ms | 28029.82 ms | 1.0006x | | Mean TTFT | 2326.10 ms | 2335.58 ms | 0.9959x | | Mean TPOT | 202.517 ms | 202.317 ms | 1.0010x | The linked current FlashInfer source benchmark uses CUPTI cold-L2 timing for one complete routing invocation. On B200 all 15 contract rows pass correctness and improve over the default backend by 1.0194--1.2101x. On GB300 all 15 rows improve by 1.2665--1.5738x. B200 synccheck and memcheck pass with PDL disabled and enabled, both with zero errors. ## Checklist - [x] Targeted pre-commit passed for both modified files. - [x] Added unit and GPU correctness tests. - [x] Verified a real SGLang service selects Cake rather than merely importing it. - [x] Preserved the existing in-contract fast path and fail-closed out-of-contract fallback. - [x] Followed the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32227976057](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227976057)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32227975940](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227975940)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Extend Qwen3-VL EAGLE3 draft support
signal.text: ## Motivation Extend Qwen3-VL EAGLE3 draft model support to include draft models that ship with `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` as their `architectures` field (vLLM-style class name; e.g. [AngelSlim/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct_eagle3](https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct_eagle3) ). The canonical SGLang arch name for these drafts is `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3`, so currently any draft published with the `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` alias fails to load because the model registry has no entry for that name. ## Modifications - In `model_config._config_draft_model`, normalize the `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` alias to `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` for draft models. signal.title: [diffusion] ComfyUI: add a MiniMax-H3 node and a generic extra-fields passthrough
signal.text: ## Summary The ComfyUI plugin's executors cover flux / qwen_image / zimage — all image models — so there was no route to MiniMax-H3 from ComfyUI. H3 does not fit the executor route. It denoises a packed video+audio sequence in one pass and routes conditioning by task (`t2va` / `fl2va` / `ref2va`), while ComfyUI's KSampler drives a single latent tensor and has no audio branch. Rebuilding that inside ComfyUI would duplicate the visual/audio/reference conditioning stages the server already runs, so this wires H3 through the server route instead. Two changes: - **`generate_video` gains `extra_fields`.** The video request schema already accepts unknown fields, so the client only needed a way to reach a model's own request surface. `extra_fields` is merged last, so a model-specific field wins over a generic default of the same name. No further change to this client is needed for the next model that adds request fields. - **`SGLDiffusionGenerateH3`** builds H3's `task` / `conditions` / `target` shape from ComfyUI-native inputs. Keyframes carry a `frame_index`; references keep request order because the prompt addresses them positionally per modality; local paths become `file://` URIs while remote URLs pass through unchanged. Output dimensions are read from the response, because H3 aligns the canvas server-side and `short_edge` alone cannot reconstruct it. ## Test plan - [x] 9 new tests drive the real node through the real client and mock only HTTP, so a change on either side of the payload contract fails. They cover the three task shapes, keyframe frame-index mapping, modality ordering for prompt tags, remote-URL passthrough, the server-resolved canvas, the task/conditioning validation errors, and `extra_fields` precedence. - [x] Run on a plain checkout and on an H200 box: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/test/test_h3_request.py --import-mode=importlib` **Not covered:** an end-to-end run against a live H3 server. The tests pin the request shape against the documented contract and the shape used by the existing H3 CI case, but nothing here has generated a video through ComfyUI yet. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32221182305](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32221182305)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32221181823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32221181823)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Warm PaddleOCR-VL with a page-sized image, not a 32x32 one
signal.text: ### The gap `_get_vlm_warmup_image_base64` already treats warmup image size as something worth choosing per model: Kimi K2.5 gets 512x512 to compile MoonViT position interpolation, Kimi K3 gets 448x448 to match its native patch grid, and the docstring says why — *"This keeps one-time vision setup work out of the first external image request."* PaddleOCR-VL falls through to the 32x32 minimum. Measured against what it actually serves: | warmup image | ViT patches | image tokens | |---|---|---| | current minimum, 32x32 | **4** | 1 | | Kimi K3, 448x448 | 1024 | 256 | | Kimi K2.5, 512x512 | 1296 | 324 | | **a real page** (checkpoint default budget) | **~5184** | ~1296 | Three orders of magnitude below the serving shape, so nothing shape-dependent in the packed vision path is warm when the first page arrives. ### The symptom While measuring this model against vLLM I ran four independent server instances × three rounds. Within every instance the first round came out low and the next two recovered, and the model's run-to-run spread was 4.7% against vLLM's 1.6% on the same host and workload. That pattern is a warmup tail, not noise. Being straight about what is and isn't measured here: the coverage gap in the table is measured, and the variance is measured. The first-request improvement is not — I no longer have the H200 that produced those numbers. So this is proposed on the mechanism plus the precedent already in this function, and I'm happy to attach a before/after TTFT once a box frees up if a reviewer wants that before merging. ### Implementation notes - The image is generated (stdlib `zlib` + `struct`, ~15 lines) instead of checked in as a third kilobyte-long base64 literal, so the next model to need one costs a single call. - Verified by executing the real function over every branch: PaddleOCR-VL (by architecture and by `model_type`) gets a decodable 1008x1008 truecolor PNG, and **Kimi K2.5, Kimi K3 and the default path return byte-identical bytes to before**. No other model's startup cost moves. - Truecolor rather than grayscale, since image processors assume three channels. - Tests cover the size for the new branch, the token arithmetic behind the choice, and the generated PNG's chunk structure and CRCs. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32225952459](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225952459)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32225952326](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225952326)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix three logger calls that drop their record and print a logging error
signal.text: ## Motivation Three logging calls pass an extra positional argument to a format string that has no `%`-placeholder. `logging` only formats the message when a handler emits it, so the failure surfaces as a handler error rather than at the call site: the record is dropped and `--- Logging error ---` plus a `TypeError` goes to stderr. ``` --- Logging error --- Traceback (most recent call last): ... File ".../logging/__init__.py", line 368, in getMessage msg = msg % self.args TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting Message: 'Custom quick allreduce:' Arguments: ('Invalid quantization level: FOO. Supported levels: ...',) ``` | file | line | call | |---|---|---| | `srt/distributed/device_communicators/quick_all_reduce.py` | 178 | `logger.warning("Custom quick allreduce:", f"Invalid quantization level: ...")` | | `srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py` | 32 | `logger.debug("Function {} has already been called.", fn.__name__)` | | `test/nightly_bench_utils.py` | 75 | `logger.error("Some trace files are None", f"{trace_files=}")` | `quick_all_reduce.py` is the one that matters in practice. It is the warning that lists the accepted values of `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION`, and it is reached exactly when a user has set an invalid one — so the message that would tell them what to set is the message that gets swallowed, and the code then `return`s silently. `npu/utils.py` is a second variant: the format string uses `{}` while `logging` interpolates with `%`, so the placeholder is never filled and the extra argument triggers the same `TypeError`. It's reachable through the `@_call_once` decorator at line 89. ## Modifications The two multi-argument calls become single strings; the `{}` one becomes `%s`, which is what `logging` interpolates. No control flow, log levels or message wording change. ## Accuracy Test Ran the three calls through a real `logging` handler before and after. Before, nothing reaches the handler and the traceback above goes to stderr. After: ``` DEBUG:x:Function npu_init has already been called. WARNING:x:Custom quick allreduce: Invalid quantization level: FOO. Supported levels: ['NONE', 'FP', 'INT8'] ERROR:x:Some trace files are None: [None, None] ``` with stderr empty. No unit test added: two of the three sites need ROCm and Ascend NPU hardware to reach, which I don't have here, so any test I wrote for them would be one I couldn't run. The sites were found by walking the AST for logging calls whose first argument is a placeholder-free string literal with further positional arguments; that sweep reports no remaining matches in `python/sglang/srt` after this change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci) — see the note above on why hardware-gated sites are verified by reproduction rather than a test. - [ ] Update documentation as needed, including docstrings or example tutorials. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32226980638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32226980638)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32226980496](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32226980496)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix registered HiCache host pointer aliases
signal.text: ## Motivation Registered HiCache host allocations can have different CPU and GPU virtual addresses. This is observable on MI355X, where `hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is false. Passing the CPU VA to a custom kernel causes a GPU memory fault even though runtime copy APIs can still accept that address. The affected paths include AOT/JIT HiCache transfers, Mamba transfers, HiSparse copies, and host-pool pointer tables. CPU-side storage and disaggregation metadata must continue to expose the original CPU VA. ## Modifications - Add a target-device-aware `get_device_accessible_ptr` AOT API using `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` / `hipHostGetDevicePointer`. - Resolve direct registered-host tensor operands at AOT and JIT kernel launch boundaries while preserving the caller's current device. - Build CUDA/ROCm host-pool kernel pointer tables from device-accessible aliases for MHA, MLA, K-only, DSV4 paged/state, and DSA pools. - Keep raw CPU addresses for unregister, contiguous-buffer metadata, page metadata, and storage/disaggregation consumers. - Preserve unpinned, NPU, and MUSA pointer behavior. - Add registered-mmap regressions for pointer domains, AOT/JIT transfers, and CUDA graph capture/replay. ## Accuracy Tests ROCm 7.2 / MI355X (`gfx950`), Docker image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260813`: - Fresh ROCm AOT build: passed. - `test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: `15 passed`. - `test_transfer_mamba.py`: `16 passed`. - `test_hisparse.py`: `16 passed, 2 skipped`. - `test_mem_pool_host.py`: `9 passed`. - Registered-mmap post-rebase regressions: `3 passed`. - Native HIP runtime comparison: alias matches `hipHostGetDevicePointer`; wrong-device input is rejected; current device is restored. - Repository pre-commit hooks over the rebased PR diff: passed. CUDA validation in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130` (compile-only because this host has no NVIDIA GPU): - HiCache, Mamba, and HiSparse JIT modules compiled and loaded for SM90. - Modified AOT `transfer.cu` and `common_extension.cc` translation units compiled for SM90. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This is a correctness fix for registered-host pointer address domains; it does not change kernel bodies or transfer algorithms. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change required.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Correctness results above; no performance-sensitive algorithm change.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32218201039](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32218201039)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32218200911](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32218200911)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: DSpark support DeepEP & MegaMoE
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Reference：https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30513 DSpark speculative decoding with DP attention previously only supported the built-in TP MoE backend (`moe_a2a_backend='none'`). This prevented running DSpark together with all-to-all expert-parallel dispatchers such as DeepEP and MegaMoE, which are needed for efficient large-scale expert-parallel deployments. This PR enables DSpark to run with `moe_a2a_backend='deepep'` and `moe_a2a_backend='megamoe'` under DP attention, and fixes the draft-path token metadata / MoE backend selection issues that surfaced once these backends were enabled. ## Modifications - **`arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`**: Relax the DSpark + DP-attention validation from `moe_a2a_backend='none'` only to a whitelist of `'none'` (built-in TP MoE), `'deepep'` and `'megamoe'`. Any other A2A backend still raises, since the remaining `MoeA2ABackend` values are unverified with DSpark. The existing `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static` requirement for non-`none` backends is unchanged. - **`speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py`**: Populate `num_token_non_padded` / `num_token_non_padded_cpu` for both the idle batch (zeros) and the draft forward batch (actual draft-block token count), so the DP MoE path receives correct token metadata during draft forwarding. - **`speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py`**: Rework `_draft_context` into a `contextmanager` backed by an `ExitStack` that layers in `speculative_moe_backend_context()` and `speculative_moe_a2a_backend_context()` (temporarily switching to the configured speculative MoE runner / A2A backend and disabling FP4 allgather for unquantized MTP layers). Idle-decode participation for MoE draft models is now wrapped in this context so it uses the correct MoE backend. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] [CI] Fix ROCm aiter attention backend rejecting grouped-query attention
signal.text: ## Motivation `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd-rocm720` fails at server startup for `cosmos3_nano_t2v` (and `cosmos3_nano_t2i` in the sibling shard): [run 32009315390 / job 95325370019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32009315390/job/95325370019) ``` RuntimeError: Server exited early (code 1). ... File ".../runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py", line 132, in __init__ raise NotImplementedError( NotImplementedError: AITer backend does not support Grouped Query Attention yet. [Error while loading customized transformer, falling back to native version] ... AttributeError: module diffusers has no attribute Cosmos3OmniTransformer ``` On ROCm the diffusion server defaults to the `aiter` attention backend, and `AITerImpl.__init__` rejected any `num_kv_heads != num_heads`. Cosmos3's cross-attention is GQA (`num_attention_heads=32`, `num_key_value_heads=8`), so `Cosmos3CrossAttention` → `USPAttention` → `AITerImpl` raised at construction. The component loader swallowed that, fell back to loading the transformer through native diffusers, and died there with the misleading `AttributeError` above. Net effect: the whole 1-GPU AMD diffusion shard is red on a Cosmos3 case that has nothing to do with attention support. The guard is stale. `aiter.flash_attn_func` documents and implements MQA/GQA by broadcasting KV heads internally; only the FP8 FMHA ASM kernel (`fmha_fwd_hd128_fp8_gfx950`) is MHA-only, and that was already gated separately by `_can_use_fmha_fp8_prefill`. This failure is unrelated to #34424 — it reproduces on `main`. ## Modifications - `runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py` - Replace the blanket `NotImplementedError` with a `num_heads % num_kv_heads` divisibility check, and store `num_heads` / `num_kv_heads` / `is_gqa` on the impl (other backends, e.g. `flash_attn.py`, already just store and forward). - Under `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_AITER_FP8_ATTN=1`, a GQA layer now short-circuits to BF16 before the per-tensor quantization instead of quantizing q/k/v and then discarding the result inside `_can_use_fmha_fp8_prefill`; it warns once at construction instead of per forward. - Pass `softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale` to `aiter.flash_attn_func` in the BF16 path. It was silently dropped, so the kernel always used its `head_dim**-0.5` default. That matches `USPAttention`'s default scale, so nothing changes numerically today, but any layer passing a custom scale was computing the wrong attention. - `test/unit/test_aiter_attention_gqa.py` (new): GQA/MQA head counts are accepted, indivisible counts are rejected, `num_kv_heads=None` defaults to MHA, and the GQA forward matches `scaled_dot_product_attention(enable_gqa=True)`. Auto-discovered by the `unit` suite (`_discover_unit_tests()`), skipped where `aiter` is unavailable. ## Regression origin The `NotImplementedError` guard has been in `aiter.py` since the first diffusion commit (7bc1dae095, #12484, 2025-11-06) and was never revisited. ROCm started defaulting to the `aiter` backend in 4bf06635fc (#13760, 2025-12-19), and Cosmos3's GQA cross-attention landed in c317beda99 (#24994, 2026-05-27). What turned this into a red AMD shard is **9450696aa5 (#26963, 2026-06-03)**, which added `cosmos3_nano_t2v` to `ONE_GPU_CASES`. signal.title: [AMD][bugfix] Add moe_ep_size/moe_tp_size to the allreduce-fusion gate test stub
signal.text: ## Motivation `TestAiterAllreduceFusionGate` in `test/registered/ops/test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd.py` has been erroring on every AMD run since 2026-08-12. The hybrid EP+TP guard added in #30700 (commit `c7c03ec53`, 2026-08-11) reads two new fields at the very top of `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer`: ```python parallel = get_parallel() if parallel.moe_ep_size > 1 and parallel.moe_tp_size > 1: return False ``` The AMD gate test stubs `get_parallel()` with a `SimpleNamespace` that only carries `tp_size`, so every one of the 7 gate cases now raises: ``` AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'moe_ep_size' ``` Because the guard sits before every other branch, all 7 cases fail; CI's failfast only surfaces the first one (`test_dense_tp_fuses`). This is a test-stub gap only. The aiter fused all-reduce + RMSNorm kernel itself is fine: the three GPU subtests (`test_fused_ar_rms_benchmark`, `test_fused_ar_rms_multi_hidden_dim`, `test_fused_ar_rms_residual_accuracy`) pass. Scheduled ROCm 7.2 runs on `main`, shard 3 — the guard landed at 2026-08-11T23:46Z: | run date | shard 3 | | --- | --- | | 08-09, 08-10, 08-11 17:46 | success | | 08-12 12:21 onward (every run) | failure | ## Modifications Add `moe_ep_size=1` and `moe_tp_size=1` to the `get_parallel()` stub. Both being 1 means no MoE EP and no MoE TP, so the hybrid EP+TP guard stays inactive and the aiter branch is what decides — which is what all 7 existing cases are written to exercise. No existing assertion changes meaning. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — test-only change, no kernel or model forward code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149134311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149134025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134025)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
