signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix multimodal state in streaming sessions
signal.text: # [Bugfix] Fix multimodal state in streaming sessions ## Motivation Appending multimodal turns to a `StreamingSession` currently carries three non-canonical pieces of state into the next request: 1. Page-local M-RoPE positions and deltas are concatenated. On the second Qwen3-VL image turn, the delta becomes shape `(2, 1)`, and decode later sees `[3, 2]` positions for a `[3, 1]` buffer. 2. Multimodal offsets are shifted by the padded prefix length instead of the cumulative unpadded prefix used by model-specific padding. 3. Scheduler-side padding rewrites `origin_input_ids`, but the session's carried `full_untruncated_fill_ids` can retain the raw multimodal token IDs. Since this rewrite can preserve length, `Req._refresh_fill_ids()` cannot detect the stale values. This can drop visual embeddings from later turns. ## Modifications - Add a streaming-session-specific multimodal preparation path that merges all accumulated MM items, regenerates canonical padded IDs from cumulative unpadded IDs, and synchronizes the fill-ID array. - Force M-RoPE recomputation through the active model processor after a multimodal streaming append, and invalidate the repeated delta cache. - Shift newly appended MM offsets using the cumulative unpadded prefix length. - Add deterministic Qwen3-VL regression coverage for page composition, M-RoPE prefix stability, cumulative repadding, fill-ID synchronization, offsets, and delta-cache invalidation. The new behavior is restricted to `session.streaming`; ordinary requests and non-streaming sessions keep their existing preparation path. ## Accuracy Tests Environment: - SGLang base commit: `3b4fac5b99670f3e8bcb5bc9ecf04b821e7b8de5` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, snapshot `0c351dd01ed87e9c1b53cbc748cba10e6187ff3b` - GPU: NVIDIA H20-3e - TP1, chunked prefill 2048, CUDA graphs disabled Production-source server on the final rebased commit, without monkeypatching: | Pages | Arrival | Greedy generation | B0/B1 output IDs | Intermediate output | B1 cached/prompt | |---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:| | 16 | 250 ms/page | forced 32 tokens | exact | 0 | 1291/1387 | The same patch was also swept at 4/8/16/20 pages immediately before the final rebase; every bucket produced 32 exact output IDs and zero intermediate output. CPU tests (7 multimodal + 4 token-share + 5 streaming-session): ```text 16 passed ``` The tested files also pass all configured pre-commit hooks, including isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, AST checks, and registered-test validation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling In one observed run with 16 pages arriving every 250 ms, measured from final-page arrival to the first generated token: | Path | Time | |---|---:| | One-shot B0 | 243.825 ms | | StreamingSession B1 | 50.053 ms | This is a 79.5% reduction. B1 reuses 1291/1387 prompt tokens (93.1%). The full paced wall time changes from 3993.825 ms to 3800.230 ms because the fixed 3.75 s page-arrival window dominates this synthetic workload. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Added CPU unit and regression tests. - [x] Added real-weight accuracy results. - [x] Added latency and prompt-cache measurements. - [x] No user-facing API change; documentation update is not required. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31023923905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31023923905)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31023923257](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31023923257)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: perf: fix overlap scheduling and all-reduce fusion for NVIDIA Confidential Computing(CC) on Blackwell
signal.text: ## Motivation Two fixes so SGLang runs efficiently under **NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC)**, where the GPU operates behind a bounce buffer: 1. **Per-step D2H result readback stalls the scheduler.** Under CC, `cudaMemcpyAsync` (D2H) is forced synchronous — it blocks at issue — so the per-step readback of `next_token_ids` / logprobs serializes onto the scheduler's critical path and kills decode overlap. 2. **FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion disables itself.** `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` allocates a symmetric-memory (cuMulticast) workspace whose preflight fails under CC, so the fusion silently falls back off — even though the fusion kernels themselves are multicast-free. Both paths are gated on `is_confidential_compute()` (NVML, overridable via `SGLANG_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE`); **off-CC behavior is unchanged.** ## Modifications **`cc: async device->host result-readback worker`** - New `python/sglang/srt/managers/async_d2h_copy_worker.py` (`AsyncD2HCopyWorker`): runs the per-step D2H copy on a dedicated thread with its own CUDA stream, off the scheduler's critical path, so overlap is preserved. Wired into `scheduler.py` / `managers/utils.py`; only routed through the worker when CC is detected. - Adds `is_confidential_compute()` to `srt/utils/common.py`. **`cc(fix): enable FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion under Confidential Computing`** (`layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`) - FlashInfer now auto-selects a multicast-free IPC workspace under CC, so SGLang reuses the normal off-CC fusion path: `_resolve_backend` forces the `trtllm` backend under CC (SM100 "auto" defaults to `mnnvl`, which needs NVLink multicast), the symmetric-memory preflight is skipped, and the workspace stays a normal `AllReduceFusionWorkspace`. Enabled by default whenever CC is detected. ## Accuracy Tests With CC on: ``` |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9348|± |0.0068| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9606|± |0.0054| ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (all hooks pass). - [x] Added unit tests (`test/registered/core/test_async_d2h_copy_worker.py`). - [ ] Documentation update — n/a. - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmark — n/a (no output change; CC-hardware benchmark pending). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31763733100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31763733100)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31763732864](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31763732864)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [FlashInfer v0.6.18] add FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 mode
signal.text: ## Motivation @humansand Add an opt-in W4A16 compute mode for FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE and dense linear layers: weights remain NVFP4 while activations and outputs stay BF16. Registered tests cover online-quantized Nemotron MoE accuracy, serialized ModelOpt Qwen3 dense+MoE disk-reload invariance, and the existing dense W4A4 numerical path. Dependency: - This PR depends on **FlashInfer 0.6.18**. Its [`release-v0.6.18`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/tree/release-v0.6.18) branch contains CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE W4A16 support, SiTU support, the invocation-workspace lifetime fix, and the SM100/SM103 dense W4A16 GEMM from [#4466](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4466). - SGLang's pinned FlashInfer package and CI image must be updated to 0.6.18 before merge. This integration intentionally has no compatibility fallback for earlier FlashInfer APIs. - Historical MoE validation used the 20260817 nightly plus the workspace fix. Final dense+MoE reload validation used [`nightly-v0.6.18-20260818`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/nightly-v0.6.18-20260818) source at `0751be928d24187bd39a0dde45ce96418bc03ddf`, which contains #4466. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16` (default `false`). - Select `CuteDslMoEWrapper(quant_mode="w4a16")`, pass raw BF16 activations, and omit GEMM1/GEMM2 activation scales. - Reuse the existing packed NVFP4 weights and CuTe MMA-layout block scales, but construct weight-only decode alphas for both online-quantized and serialized ModelOpt weights. - Keep serialized ModelOpt NVFP4 dense layers in the existing `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod`. When the environment variable and `--fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` are both selected, its registered `fp4_gemm` compiler boundary dispatches to FlashInfer `mm_bf16_fp4`; otherwise the existing W4A4 `mm_fp4` route is unchanged. - Prepare dense W4A16 weights through `prepare_bf16_fp4_weights`, preserve loader-owned source scales for disk reload, and keep stable prepared scale/alpha bindings for decode CUDA graphs. Reuse the existing NVFP4_AWQ pre-scale operation before BF16 GEMM. - Recognize prepared W4A16 state in the generic quantized LM-head guard, and keep DeepSeek's W4A4-only GEMM+SwiGLU fusion disabled for W4A16. - Support the standard CuTe DSL v2 paths with no A2A or FlashInfer A2A on SM100-family GPUs (SM100/SM103). Keep FlashInfer A2A dispatch in BF16 by suppressing automatic NVFP4 dispatch and rejecting an explicit NVFP4-dispatch configuration; the existing DeepEP masked path remains W4A4-only. Both registered accuracy/reload tests exercise FlashInfer A2A, and the serving benchmark compares no A2A with FlashInfer A2A. - Preserve the configured finalize mode for ReLU2. For gated/SwiGLU W4A16, disable fused finalize and use FlashInfer's two-stage finalize path. - Register nightly `4-gpu-b200` end-to-end coverage for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8` with online NVFP4 expert-weight quantization. - Add a separate registered TP4/DP4/EP4 case with DP attention and FlashInfer A2A for serialized `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`: dense and MoE layers use W4A16, and two same-checkpoint disk reloads across weight/CUDA-graph release and resume must preserve deterministic decode text and token IDs exactly, with token logprobs within `1e-4`. This remains alongside the existing per-token NVFP4 CuTe DSL case. ## Accuracy Tests Environment: - MoE accuracy image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682` (`sha256:fa8774dd128600a09fd6d46670b06fb69a55dac8a3881e50ccf0916a45eb39af`) -
